Mahāparinibbānasuttaṃ

Tipiṭaka 3
← Previous: Mahānidānasuttaṃ Home Next: Mahāsudassanasuttaṃ →
131
<p n="131" rend="bodytext"><hi rend="paranum">131</hi><hi rend="dot">.</hi> Evaṃ <pb ed="T" n="2.0085"/><pb ed="M" n="2.0061"/><pb ed="V" n="2.0056"/> me <pb ed="P" n="2.0072"/> sutaṃ – ekaṃ samayaṃ bhagavā rājagahe viharati gijjhakūṭe pabbate. Tena kho pana samayena rājā māgadho ajātasattu vedehiputto vajjī abhiyātukāmo hoti. So evamāha – ‘‘ahaṃ hime vajjī evaṃmahiddhike evaṃmahānubhāve ucchecchāmi <note>ucchejjāmi (syā. pī.), ucchijjāmi (ka.)</note> vajjī, vināsessāmi vajjī, anayabyasanaṃ āpādessāmi vajjī’’ti <note>āpādessāmi vajjīti (sabbattha) a. ni. 7.22 passitabbaṃ</note>.</p>
Thus have I heard. On one occasion the Blessed One was dwelling at Rājagaha on Mount Vulture Peak.

Now at that time the Magadhan King Ajātasattu, the son of Queen Vedehi, desired to wage war against the Vajjis.

He said: ‘I will strike the Vajjis who are so powerful and strong, I will cut them off and destroy them, I will bring them to ruin and destruction!’
<p n="131" rend="bodytext"><hi rend="paranum">131</hi><hi rend="dot">.</hi><hi rend="bold">Evaṃ</hi><pb ed="P" n="2.0516"/><pb ed="V" n="2.0095"/><pb ed="M" n="2.0106"/><hi rend="bold">me suta</hi>nti mahāparinibbānasuttaṃ. Tatrāyamanupubbapadavaṇṇanā – <hi rend="bold">gijjhakūṭe</hi>ti gijjhā tassa kūṭesu vasiṃsu, gijjhasadisaṃ vā tassa kūṭaṃ atthīti gijjhakūṭo, tasmiṃ gijjhakūṭe. <hi rend="bold">Abhiyātukāmo</hi>ti abhibhavanatthāya yātukāmo. <hi rend="bold">Vajjī</hi>ti vajjirājāno. <hi rend="bold">Evaṃmahiddhike</hi>ti evaṃ mahatiyā rājiddhiyā samannāgate, etena nesaṃ samaggabhāvaṃ kathesi. <hi rend="bold">Evaṃmahānubhāve</hi>ti evaṃ mahantena ānubhāvena samannāgate, etena nesaṃ hatthisippādīsu katasikkhataṃ kathesi, yaṃ sandhāya vuttaṃ – ‘‘sikkhitā vatime licchavikumārakā, susikkhitā vatime licchavikumārakā, yatra hi nāma sukhumena tāḷacchiggalena asanaṃ atipātayissanti poṅkhānupoṅkhaṃ avirādhita’’nti (saṃ. ni. 5.1115). <hi rend="bold">Ucchecchāmī</hi>ti ucchindissāmi. <hi rend="bold">Vināsessāmī</hi>ti nāsessāmi, adassanaṃ pāpessāmi. <hi rend="bold">Anayabyasana</hi>nti ettha na ayoti anayo, avaḍḍhiyā etaṃ nāmaṃ. Hitañca sukhañca viyassati vikkhipatīti byasanaṃ, ñātipārijuññādīnaṃ etaṃ nāmaṃ. <hi rend="bold">Āpādessāmī</hi>ti pāpayissāmi.</p> <p rend="bodytext">Iti kira so ṭhānanisajjādīsu imaṃ yuddhakathameva katheti, gamanasajjā hothāti evaṃ balakāyaṃ āṇāpeti. Kasmā? Gaṅgāyaṃ kira ekaṃ paṭṭanagāmaṃ nissāya aḍḍhayojanaṃ ajātasattuno āṇā, aḍḍhayojanaṃ licchavīnaṃ. Ettha pana āṇāpavattiṭṭhānaṃ hotīti attho. Tatrāpi ca pabbatapādato mahagghabhaṇḍaṃ otarati. Taṃ sutvā – ‘‘ajja yāmi, sve yāmī’’ti ajātasattuno saṃvidahantasseva licchavirājāno samaggā sammodamānā puretaraṃ gantvā sabbaṃ gaṇhanti. Ajātasattu pacchā āgantvā taṃ pavattiṃ ñatvā <pb ed="P" n="2.0517"/> kujjhitvā gacchati. Te punasaṃvaccharepi tatheva karonti. Atha so balavāghātajāto tadā evamakāsi.</p> <pb ed="P" n="2.0517"/> <p rend="bodytext">Tato cintesi – ‘‘gaṇena saddhiṃ yuddhaṃ nāma bhāriyaṃ, ekopi moghappahāro nāma natthi, ekena kho pana paṇḍitena saddhiṃ mantetvā karonto nipparādho hoti, paṇḍito ca satthārā sadiso <pb ed="V" n="2.0096"/> natthi, satthā ca avidūre dhuravihāre vasati, handāhaṃ pesetvā pucchāmi <pb ed="M" n="2.0107"/>. Sace me gatena koci attho bhavissati, satthā tuṇhī bhavissati, anatthe pana sati kiṃ rañño tattha gamanenāti vakkhatī’’ti. So vassakārabrāhmaṇaṃ pesesi. Brāhmaṇo gantvā bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesi. Tena vuttaṃ – <hi rend="bold">‘‘atha kho rājā…pe… āpādessāmī’’</hi>ti.</p> <pb ed="V" n="2.0096"/> <pb ed="M" n="2.0107"/> <hi rend="bold">‘‘atha kho rājā…pe… āpādessāmī’’</hi> <p rend="subhead">Rājaaparihāniyadhammavaṇṇanā</p>
131. Thus.

I have heard that the *Mahāparinibbānasuttaṃ* [says] this.

Here follows a word-by-word explanation: *gijjhakūṭe* means: vultures dwelt on its peaks; or, *gijjhasadisaṃ* (similar to vultures) exists on its peak; therefore, *gijjhakūṭo*, on that Vulture Peak.

*abhiyātukāmo* means: *yātukāmo* (desiring to travel) for the sake of overpowering *abhibhavanatthāya*.

*vajjī* means: the Vajjian kings *vajjirājāno*.

*evaṃmahiddhike* means: *evaṃ* thus, possessed of great royal power *mahatiyā rājiddhiyā samannāgate*; by this *etena*, he related their unity *samaggabhāvaṃ kathesi*.

*evaṃmahānubhāve* means: *evaṃ*, thus, possessed of great majesty *mahantena ānubhāvena samannāgate*; by this *etena* he related their skill in elephant-lore, etc. *hatthisippādīsu katasikkhataṃ kathesi*, which, intending what, was said: “Skilled indeed are these Licchavi princes, very skilled are these Licchavi princes, since they will cause an arrow to pass through a very fine hole in a palm tree, point after point, without missing” (S.N. 5.1115).

*ucchecchāmī* means: I will cut off *ucchindissāmi*.

*vināsessāmī* means: I will destroy *nāsessāmi*, I will cause disappearance *adassanaṃ pāpessāmi*.

*anayabyasana* means: here, *na ayoti anayo*, *avaḍḍhiyā etaṃ nāmaṃ* (this is a name for decline).

*hitañca sukhañca viyassati vikkhipatīti byasanaṃ*, *ñātipārijuññādīnaṃ etaṃ nāmaṃ* (this is a name for the loss of relatives, etc.).

*āpādessāmī* means: I will cause to reach *pāpayissāmi*.

Thus, it is said, he only told war stories, on occasions such as sitting and lying down, etc. *ṭhānanisajjādīsu imaṃ yuddhakathameva katheti*, he ordered the army thus: “Be prepared to march!” *gamanasajjā hothāti evaṃ balakāyaṃ āṇāpeti*.

Why? On the Ganges, relying on one village with a landing place, was half a *yojana* under the authority of Ajātasattu *aḍḍhayojanaṃ ajātasattuno āṇā*, and half a *yojana* under that of the Licchavis *aḍḍhayojanaṃ licchavīnaṃ*.

Here, however *ettha pana*, *āṇāpavattiṭṭhānaṃ hotīti attho* the meaning is that there is a place where authority is exercised.

And there also *tatrāpi ca*, valuable merchandise descends from the foot of the mountain *pabbatapādato mahagghabhaṇḍaṃ otarati*.

Having heard that *taṃ sutvā* – “Today I will go, tomorrow I will go” *‘‘ajja yāmi, sve yāmī’’ti*, even while Ajātasattu was delaying *ajātasattuno saṃvidahantasseva*, the Licchavi kings, united *licchavirājāno samaggā*, rejoicing *sammodamānā*, going ahead *puretaraṃ gantvā*, took everything *sabbaṃ gaṇhanti*.

Ajātasattu, coming afterwards *ajātasattu pacchā āgantvā*, having learned that course of events *taṃ pavattiṃ ñatvā*, became angry and left *kujjhitvā gacchati*.

They did likewise the following year *te punasaṃvaccharepi tatheva karonti*.

Then he *atha so balavāghātajāto tadā evamakāsi*, born of violent attacks, did thus *evamakāsi*.

Then he thought *tato cintesi* - “War with a multitude is a heavy matter *gaṇena saddhiṃ yuddhaṃ nāma bhāriyaṃ*, there is not even one futile blow *ekopi moghappahāro nāma natthi*; but doing [something] having deliberated with one wise man is free from fault *ekena kho pana paṇḍitena saddhiṃ mantetvā karonto nipparādho hoti*, and a wise man is like a teacher *paṇḍito ca satthārā sadiso*, there is no [teacher] *natthi*, and the teacher lives not far away at Dhuravihāra *satthā ca avidūre dhuravihāre vasati*, come now, I will send [someone] and ask [him] *handāhaṃ pesetvā pucchāmi*.

If there will be some benefit from my going *sace me gatena koci attho bhavissati*, the teacher will remain silent *satthā tuṇhī bhavissati*, but if there is no benefit *anatthe pana sati*, he will say: ‘What is the use of the king going there?’ *kiṃ rañño tattha gamanenāti vakkhatī’’ti*.

He sent the Brahmin Vassakāra *so vassakārabrāhmaṇaṃ pesesi*.

The Brahmin, going *brāhmaṇo gantvā*, reported this matter to the Blessed One *bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesi*.

By him it was said *tena vuttaṃ* – “Then, indeed, the king… pe… I will cause [them] to reach [misfortune]” *‘‘atha kho rājā…pe… āpādessāmī’’ti*.

“Then, indeed, the king… pe… I will cause [them] to reach [misfortune]” *‘‘atha kho rājā…pe… āpādessāmī’’*.
Explanation of the *dharma* for non-decline of kings *rājaaparihāniyadhammavaṇṇanā*.
132
<p n="132" rend="bodytext"><hi rend="paranum">132</hi><hi rend="dot">.</hi> Atha kho rājā māgadho ajātasattu vedehiputto vassakāraṃ brāhmaṇaṃ magadhamahāmattaṃ āmantesi – ‘‘ehi tvaṃ, brāhmaṇa, yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkama; upasaṅkamitvā mama vacanena bhagavato pāde sirasā vandāhi, appābādhaṃ appātaṅkaṃ lahuṭṭhānaṃ balaṃ phāsuvihāraṃ puccha – ‘rājā, bhante, māgadho ajātasattu vedehiputto bhagavato pāde sirasā vandati, appābādhaṃ appātaṅkaṃ lahuṭṭhānaṃ balaṃ phāsuvihāraṃ pucchatī’ti. Evañca vadehi – ‘rājā, bhante, māgadho ajātasattu vedehiputto vajjī abhiyātukāmo. So evamāha – ‘‘ahaṃ hime vajjī evaṃmahiddhike evaṃmahānubhāve ucchecchāmi vajjī, vināsessāmi vajjī, anayabyasanaṃ <pb ed="P" n="2.0073"/> āpādessāmī’’’ti. Yathā te bhagavā byākaroti, taṃ sādhukaṃ uggahetvā mama āroceyyāsi. Na hi tathāgatā vitathaṃ bhaṇantī’’ti.</p> <p rend="subhead">Vassakārabrāhmaṇo</p>
Then King Ajātaśatru (Ajātasattu), the son of Queen Vaidehī, of Magadha, addressed the Brahmin Vassakāra, the chief minister of Magadha: "Come, Brahmin, go to the Blessed One (Bhagavā); having gone, bow in my name with your head to the Blessed One’s feet (bhagavato pāde sirasā vandāhi), ask whether he is free from illness and affliction (appābādhaṃ appātaṅkaṃ), is healthy, strong, and living in comfort (lahuṭṭhānaṃ balaṃ phāsuvihāraṃ), saying, ‘King Ajātaśatru (Ajātasattu), the son of Queen Vaidehī, of Magadha, bows in reverence with his head to the Blessed One’s feet and asks whether he is free from illness and affliction, is healthy, strong, and living in comfort.’"

And say this: ‘Venerable sir, King Ajātaśatru (Ajātasattu), the son of Queen Vaidehī, of Magadha, desires to march against the Vajjis (vajjī abhiyātukāmo).’

He said this: "I will uproot the Vajjis (vajjī), so mighty and powerful, I will destroy the Vajjis, I will bring ruin and calamity upon them!"

"However the Blessed One (Bhagavā) answers you, having grasped it well (sādhukaṃ uggahetvā), report it to me."

"For the Tathāgatas do not speak falsehood (na hi tathāgatā vitathaṃ bhaṇantī)."

Vassakāra the Brahmin
133
<p n="133" rend="bodytext"><hi rend="paranum">133</hi><hi rend="dot">.</hi> ‘‘Evaṃ, bho’’ti kho vassakāro brāhmaṇo magadhamahāmatto rañño māgadhassa ajātasattussa vedehiputtassa paṭissutvā bhaddāni bhaddāni yānāni yojetvā bhaddaṃ bhaddaṃ yānaṃ abhiruhitvā <pb ed="T" n="2.0086"/> bhaddehi bhaddehi yānehi rājagahamhā niyyāsi, yena gijjhakūṭo pabbato tena pāyāsi. Yāvatikā yānassa bhūmi, yānena gantvā, yānā paccorohitvā pattikova yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavatā saddhiṃ sammodi. Sammodanīyaṃ kathaṃ sāraṇīyaṃ vītisāretvā <pb ed="V" n="2.0057"/> ekamantaṃ <pb ed="M" n="2.0062"/> nisīdi. Ekamantaṃ nisinno kho vassakāro brāhmaṇo magadhamahāmatto bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – ‘‘rājā, bho gotama, māgadho ajātasattu vedehiputto bhoto gotamassa pāde sirasā vandati, appābādhaṃ appātaṅkaṃ lahuṭṭhānaṃ balaṃ phāsuvihāraṃ pucchati. Rājā <note>evañca vadeti rājā (ka.)</note>, bho gotama, māgadho ajātasattu vedehiputto vajjī abhiyātukāmo. So evamāha – ‘ahaṃ hime vajjī evaṃmahiddhike evaṃmahānubhāve ucchecchāmi vajjī, vināsessāmi vajjī, anayabyasanaṃ āpādessāmī’’’ti.</p> <p rend="subhead">Rājaaparihāniyadhammā</p>
133. “So be it, sir,” replied the brahmin Vassakāra, the chief minister of Magadha, to King Ajātasattu Vedehiputta of Magadha. He then had auspicious carriages harnessed, mounted an auspicious carriage, and departed from Rājagaha in those auspicious carriages, heading towards Vulture Peak Mountain (Gijjhakūṭa Pabbata).

As far as the ground was suitable for carriages, he traveled by carriage; then, dismounting from the carriage, he proceeded on foot to where the Blessed One (Bhagavā) was. Having approached, he exchanged courteous greetings with the Blessed One.

After exchanging polite conversation and greetings, he sat down to one side.

Seated to one side, the brahmin Vassakāra, the chief minister of Magadha, said to the Blessed One: “King Ajātasattu Vedehiputta of Magadha, reverently bows with his head at the feet of the esteemed Gotama, and inquires about [your] well-being, freedom from illness, lightness of body, strength, and ease of dwelling."

"The king," he noted, "also says: 'The King, revered Gotama, Ajātasattu Vedehiputta of Magadha, desires to attack the Vajjis.'"

He further said: “He declares: ‘I will utterly destroy the Vajjis, who are so mighty and powerful! I will annihilate the Vajjis! I will bring ruin and disaster upon the Vajjis!’”

Qualities that do not lead to decline for a king (Rājaaparihāniyadhammā).
134
<p n="134" rend="bodytext"><hi rend="paranum">134</hi><hi rend="dot">.</hi> Tena kho pana samayena āyasmā ānando bhagavato piṭṭhito ṭhito hoti bhagavantaṃ bījayamāno <note>vījayamāno (sī.), vījiyamāno (syā.)</note>. Atha kho bhagavā āyasmantaṃ ānandaṃ āmantesi – ‘‘kinti te, ānanda, sutaṃ, ‘vajjī abhiṇhaṃ sannipātā sannipātabahulā’ti? ‘‘Sutaṃ metaṃ, bhante – ‘vajjī abhiṇhaṃ sannipātā sannipātabahulā’’ti. ‘‘Yāvakīvañca, ānanda, vajjī abhiṇhaṃ sannipātā sannipātabahulā bhavissanti, vuddhiyeva, ānanda, vajjīnaṃ <pb ed="T" n="2.0087"/> pāṭikaṅkhā, no parihāni.</p> <p rend="bodytext">‘‘Kinti te, ānanda, sutaṃ <pb ed="P" n="2.0074"/>, ‘vajjī samaggā sannipatanti, samaggā vuṭṭhahanti, samaggā vajjikaraṇīyāni karontī’ti? ‘‘Sutaṃ metaṃ, bhante – ‘vajjī samaggā sannipatanti, samaggā vuṭṭhahanti, samaggā vajjikaraṇīyāni karontī’’ti. ‘‘Yāvakīvañca, ānanda, vajjī samaggā sannipatissanti, samaggā vuṭṭhahissanti, samaggā vajjikaraṇīyāni karissanti, vuddhiyeva, ānanda, vajjīnaṃ pāṭikaṅkhā, no parihāni.</p> <pb ed="P" n="2.0074"/> <p rend="bodytext">‘‘Kinti te, ānanda, sutaṃ, ‘vajjī apaññattaṃ na paññapenti, paññattaṃ na samucchindanti, yathāpaññatte porāṇe vajjidhamme samādāya vattantī’’’ti? ‘‘Sutaṃ metaṃ, bhante – ‘vajjī apaññattaṃ na paññapenti, paññattaṃ na samucchindanti, yathāpaññatte porāṇe vajjidhamme samādāya vattantī’’’ti. ‘‘Yāvakīvañca, ānanda, ‘‘vajjī apaññattaṃ na paññapessanti, paññattaṃ na samucchindissanti, yathāpaññatte porāṇe vajjidhamme samādāya vattissanti, vuddhiyeva, ānanda, vajjīnaṃ pāṭikaṅkhā, no parihāni.</p> <p rend="bodytext">‘‘Kinti <pb ed="M" n="2.0063"/> te, ānanda, sutaṃ, ‘vajjī ye te vajjīnaṃ vajjimahallakā, te sakkaronti garuṃ karonti <note>garukaronti (sī. syā. pī.)</note> mānenti pūjenti, tesañca sotabbaṃ maññantī’’’ti? ‘‘Sutaṃ metaṃ, bhante – ‘vajjī ye <pb ed="V" n="2.0058"/> te vajjīnaṃ vajjimahallakā, te sakkaronti garuṃ karonti mānenti pūjenti, tesañca sotabbaṃ maññantī’’’ti. ‘‘Yāvakīvañca, ānanda, vajjī ye te vajjīnaṃ vajjimahallakā <pb ed="T" n="2.0088"/>, te sakkarissanti garuṃ karissanti mānessanti pūjessanti, tesañca sotabbaṃ maññissanti, vuddhiyeva, ānanda, vajjīnaṃ pāṭikaṅkhā, no parihāni.</p> <pb ed="M" n="2.0063"/> <note>garukaronti (sī. syā. pī.)</note> <pb ed="V" n="2.0058"/> <pb ed="T" n="2.0088"/> <p rend="bodytext">‘‘Kinti te, ānanda, sutaṃ, ‘vajjī yā tā kulitthiyo kulakumāriyo, tā na okkassa pasayha vāsentī’’’ti? ‘‘Sutaṃ metaṃ, bhante – ‘vajjī yā tā kulitthiyo kulakumāriyo tā na okkassa pasayha vāsentī’’’ti. ‘‘Yāvakīvañca, ānanda, vajjī yā tā kulitthiyo kulakumāriyo, tā na okkassa pasayha vāsessanti, vuddhiyeva, ānanda, vajjīnaṃ pāṭikaṅkhā, no parihāni.</p> <p rend="centre">‘‘Kinti te, ānanda, sutaṃ, ‘vajjī yāni tāni</p> <p rend="bodytext">Vajjīnaṃ vajjicetiyāni abbhantarāni ceva bāhirāni ca, tāni sakkaronti garuṃ karonti mānenti pūjenti, tesañca dinnapubbaṃ katapubbaṃ dhammikaṃ baliṃ no parihāpentī’’’ti? ‘‘Sutaṃ <pb ed="P" n="2.0075"/> metaṃ, bhante – ‘vajjī yāni tāni vajjīnaṃ vajjicetiyāni abbhantarāni ceva bāhirāni ca, tāni sakkaronti garuṃ karonti mānenti pūjenti tesañca dinnapubbaṃ katapubbaṃ dhammikaṃ baliṃ no parihāpentī’’’ti. ‘‘Yāvakīvañca, ānanda, vajjī yāni tāni vajjīnaṃ vajjicetiyāni abbhantarāni ceva bāhirāni ca, tāni sakkarissanti garuṃ karissanti mānessanti pūjessanti, tesañca dinnapubbaṃ katapubbaṃ dhammikaṃ baliṃ no parihāpessanti, vuddhiyeva, ānanda, vajjīnaṃ pāṭikaṅkhā, no parihāni.</p> <pb ed="P" n="2.0075"/> <p rend="bodytext">‘‘Kinti te, ānanda, sutaṃ, ‘vajjīnaṃ arahantesu dhammikā rakkhāvaraṇagutti susaṃvihitā, kinti anāgatā ca arahanto vijitaṃ āgaccheyyuṃ, āgatā ca arahanto vijite phāsu vihareyyu’’’nti? ‘‘Sutaṃ metaṃ, bhante ‘vajjīnaṃ arahantesu dhammikā rakkhāvaraṇagutti susaṃvihitā kinti anāgatā ca arahanto <pb ed="T" n="2.0089"/> vijitaṃ āgaccheyyuṃ, āgatā ca arahanto vijite phāsu vihareyyu’’’nti. ‘‘Yāvakīvañca, ānanda, vajjīnaṃ arahantesu dhammikā rakkhāvaraṇagutti susaṃvihitā bhavissati, kinti anāgatā ca arahanto vijitaṃ <pb ed="M" n="2.0064"/> āgaccheyyuṃ, āgatā ca arahanto vijite phāsu vihareyyunti. Vuddhiyeva, ānanda, vajjīnaṃ pāṭikaṅkhā, no parihānī’’ti.</p> <pb ed="T" n="2.0089"/> <pb ed="M" n="2.0064"/>
At that time the Venerable Ānanda was standing behind the Blessed One, fanning him.

Then the Blessed One addressed the Venerable Ānanda, "Have you heard, Ānanda, that the Vajjis meet frequently and their gatherings are well-attended?"

"I have heard this, venerable sir: that the Vajjis meet frequently and their gatherings are well-attended."

"Ānanda, as long as the Vajjis meet frequently and their gatherings are well-attended, growth is surely to be expected for the Vajjis, not decline."

"Have you heard, Ānanda, that the Vajjis meet in harmony, adjourn in harmony, and conduct their Vajjian business in harmony?"

"I have heard this, venerable sir: that the Vajjis meet in harmony, adjourn in harmony, and conduct their Vajjian business in harmony."

"Ānanda, as long as the Vajjis meet in harmony, adjourn in harmony, and conduct their Vajjian business in harmony, growth is surely to be expected for the Vajjis, not decline."

"Have you heard, Ānanda, that the Vajjis neither enact what has not been enacted, nor abolish what has been enacted, but proceed in accordance with the ancient Vajjian laws as enacted?"

"I have heard this, venerable sir: that the Vajjis neither enact what has not been enacted, nor abolish what has been enacted, but proceed in accordance with the ancient Vajjian laws as enacted."

"Ānanda, as long as the Vajjis neither enact what has not been enacted, nor abolish what has been enacted, but proceed in accordance with the ancient Vajjian laws as enacted, growth is surely to be expected for the Vajjis, not decline."

"Have you heard, Ānanda, that the Vajjis honor, respect, venerate, and pay homage to those Vajjian elders of the Vajjis, and consider them worth listening to?"

"I have heard this, venerable sir: that the Vajjis honor, respect, venerate, and pay homage to those Vajjian elders of the Vajjis, and consider them worth listening to."

"Ānanda, as long as the Vajjis will honor, respect, venerate, and pay homage to those Vajjian elders of the Vajjis, and consider them worth listening to, growth is surely to be expected for the Vajjis, not decline."

"Have you heard, Ānanda, that the Vajjis do not abduct and detain by force women and girls of good families?"

"I have heard this, venerable sir: that the Vajjis do not abduct and detain by force women and girls of good families."

"Ānanda, as long as the Vajjis do not abduct and detain by force women and girls of good families, growth is surely to be expected for the Vajjis, not decline."

"Have you heard, Ānanda, that the Vajjis honor, respect, venerate, and pay homage to those Vajjian shrines of the Vajjis, both internal and external, and do not neglect the rightful offerings given and made to them in the past?"

"I have heard this, venerable sir: that the Vajjis honor, respect, venerate, and pay homage to those Vajjian shrines of the Vajjis, both internal and external, and do not neglect the rightful offerings given and made to them in the past."

"Ānanda, as long as the Vajjis will honor, respect, venerate, and pay homage to those Vajjian shrines of the Vajjis, both internal and external, and will not neglect the rightful offerings given and made to them in the past, growth is surely to be expected for the Vajjis, not decline."

"Have you heard, Ānanda, that righteous protection, defense, and guarding have been well established among the Vajjis for the *arhats*, so that *arhats* who have not come might come to the realm, and *arhats* who have come might live comfortably in the realm?"

"I have heard this, venerable sir: that righteous protection, defense, and guarding have been well established among the Vajjis for the *arhats*, so that *arhats* who have not come might come to the realm, and *arhats* who have come might live comfortably in the realm."

"Ānanda, as long as righteous protection, defense, and guarding will be well established among the Vajjis for the *arhats*, so that *arhats* who have not come might come to the realm, and *arhats* who have come might live comfortably in the realm, growth is surely to be expected for the Vajjis, not decline."

<p n="134" rend="bodytext"><hi rend="paranum">134</hi><hi rend="dot">.</hi><hi rend="bold">Bhagavantaṃ bījayamāno</hi>ti thero vattasīse ṭhatvā bhagavantaṃ bījati, bhagavato pana sītaṃ vā uṇhaṃ vā natthi. Bhagavā brāhmaṇassa vacanaṃ sutvā tena saddhiṃ amantetvā therena saddhiṃ mantetukāmo <hi rend="bold">kinti te, ānanda, suta</hi>ntiādimāha. <hi rend="bold">Abhiṇhaṃ sannipātā</hi>ti divasassa tikkhattuṃ sannipatantāpi antarantarā sannipatantāpi abhiṇhaṃ sannipātāva. <hi rend="bold">Sannipātabahulā</hi>ti hiyyopi sannipatimhā, purimadivasampi sannipatimhā, puna ajja kimatthaṃ sannipatitā homāti vosānaṃ anāpajjantā sannipātabahulā nāma honti. <hi rend="bold">Yāvakīvañcā</hi>ti yattakaṃ kālaṃ. <hi rend="bold">Vuddhiyeva, ānanda, vajjīnaṃ pāṭikaṅkhā, no parihānī</hi>ti – abhiṇhaṃ asannipatantā hi disāvidisāsu āgataṃ sāsanaṃ na suṇanti, tato – ‘‘asukagāmasīmā vā nigamasīmā vā ākulā, asukaṭṭhāne corā vā pariyuṭṭhitā’’ti na jānanti, corāpi ‘‘pamattā rājāno’’ti ñatvā gāmanigamādīni paharantā janapadaṃ nāsenti. Evaṃ rājūnaṃ parihāni hoti. Abhiṇhaṃ sannipatantā pana taṃ taṃ pavattiṃ suṇanti, tato balaṃ pesetvā amittamaddanaṃ karonti, corāpi – ‘‘appamattā rājāno, na sakkā amhehi vaggabandhehi vicaritu’’nti bhijjitvā palāyanti. Evaṃ rājūnaṃ vuddhi hoti. Tena vuttaṃ – ‘‘vuddhiyeva, ānanda, vajjīnaṃ pāṭikaṅkhā no parihānī’’ti. Tattha <hi rend="bold">pāṭikaṅkhā</hi>ti icchitabbā, avassaṃ bhavissatīti evaṃ daṭṭhabbāti attho.</p> <p rend="bodytext"><hi rend="bold">Samaggā</hi>tiādīsu sannipātabheriyā niggatāya – ‘‘ajja me kiccaṃ atthi, maṅgalaṃ atthī’’ti vikkhepaṃ <pb ed="P" n="2.0518"/> karontā na samaggā sannipatanti nāma. Bherisaddaṃ pana sutvāva bhuñjantāpi alaṅkariyamānāpi vatthāni nivāsentāpi aḍḍhabhuttā vā aḍḍhālaṅkatā vā vatthaṃ nivāsayamānā vā sannipatantā samaggā sannipatanti nāma. Sannipatitā pana cintetvā mantetvā kattabbaṃ katvā ekatova avuṭṭhahantā <pb ed="M" n="2.0108"/> na samaggā vuṭṭhahanti nāma. Evaṃ vuṭṭhitesu hi ye paṭhamaṃ gacchanti, tesaṃ evaṃ hoti – ‘‘amhehi bāhirakathāva sutā, idāni vinicchayakathā bhavissatī’’ti. Ekato vuṭṭhahantā pana samaggā vuṭṭhahanti nāma. Apica – ‘‘asukaṭṭhānesu gāmasīmā <pb ed="V" n="2.0097"/> vā nigamasīmā vā ākulā, corā pariyuṭṭhitā’’ti sutvā – ‘‘ko gantvā imaṃ amittamaddanaṃ karissatī’’ti vutte – ‘‘ahaṃ paṭhamaṃ, ahaṃ paṭhama’’nti vatvā gacchantāpi samaggā vuṭṭhahanti nāma. Ekassa pana kammante osīdamāne sesā rājāno puttabhātaro pesetvā tassa kammantaṃ upatthambhayamānāpi, āgantukarājānaṃ – ‘‘asukassa gehaṃ gacchatu, asukassa gehaṃ gacchatū’’ti avatvā sabbe ekato saṅgaṇhantāpi, ekassa maṅgale vā roge vā aññasmiṃ vā pana tādise sukhadukkhe uppanne sabbe tattha sahāyabhāvaṃ gacchantāpi samaggā vajjikaraṇīyāni karonti nāma.</p> <hi rend="bold">Samaggā</hi> <pb ed="P" n="2.0518"/> <pb ed="M" n="2.0108"/> <pb ed="V" n="2.0097"/> <p rend="bodytext"><hi rend="bold">Apaññatta</hi>ntiādīsu pubbe akataṃ suṅkaṃ vā baliṃ vā daṇḍaṃ vā āharāpentā apaññattaṃ paññapenti nāma. Porāṇapaveṇiyā āgatameva pana anāharāpentā paññattaṃ samucchindanti nāma. Coroti gahetvā dassite avicinitvāva chejjabhejjaṃ anusāsentā porāṇaṃ vajjidhammaṃ samādāya na vattanti nāma. Tesaṃ apaññattaṃ paññapentānaṃ abhinavasuṅkādīhi pīḷitā manussā – ‘‘atiupaddutamha, ko imesaṃ vijite vasissatī’’ti paccantaṃ pavisitvā corā vā corasahāyā vā hutvā janapadaṃ paharanti. Paññattaṃ samucchindantānaṃ paveṇīāgatāni suṅkādīni agaṇhantānaṃ koso parihāyati. Tato hatthiassabalakāyaorodhādayo yathānibaddhaṃ vaṭṭaṃ alabhamānā thāmena balena parihāyanti. Te neva yuddhakkhamā honti, na pāricariyakkhamā. Porāṇaṃ vajjidhammaṃ samādāya avattantānaṃ vijite manussā – ‘‘amhākaṃ puttaṃ pitaraṃ bhātaraṃ acoraṃyeva coroti <pb ed="P" n="2.0519"/> katvā chindiṃsu bhindiṃsū’’ti kujjhitvā paccantaṃ pavisitvā corā vā corasahāyā vā hutvā janapadaṃ paharanti, evaṃ rājūnaṃ parihāni hoti, paññattaṃ paññapentānaṃ pana ‘‘paveṇīāgatameva rājāno karontī’’ti manussā haṭṭhatuṭṭhā kasivāṇijjādike kammante sampādenti. Paññattaṃ asamucchindantānaṃ paveṇīāgatāni suṅkādīni gaṇhantānaṃ <pb ed="M" n="2.0109"/> koso vaḍḍhati, tato hatthiassabalakāyaorodhādayo yathānibaddhaṃ vaṭṭaṃ labhamānā thāmabalasampannā yuddhakkhamā ceva pāricariyakkhamā ca honti.</p> <hi rend="bold">Apaññatta</hi> <pb ed="P" n="2.0519"/> <pb ed="M" n="2.0109"/> <p rend="bodytext"><hi rend="bold">Porāṇaṃ vajjidhamma</hi>nti ettha pubbe kira vajjirājāno ‘‘ayaṃ coro’’ti ānetvā dassite ‘‘gaṇhatha naṃ cora’’nti avatvā vinicchayamahāmattānaṃ denti. Te vinicchinitvā sace acoro hoti, vissajjenti. Sace coro, attanā kiñci avatvā vohārikānaṃ denti. Tepi acoro ce, vissajjenti. Coro ce, suttadharānaṃ denti. Tepi vinicchinitvā acoro ce, vissajjenti. Coro ce, aṭṭhakulikānaṃ denti. Tepi tatheva katvā senāpatissa, senāpati uparājassa, uparājā rañño, rājā vinicchinitvā acoro ce, vissajjeti. Sace <pb ed="V" n="2.0098"/> pana coro hoti, paveṇīpotthakaṃ vācāpeti. Tattha – ‘‘yena idaṃ nāma kataṃ, tassa ayaṃ nāma daṇḍo’’ti likhitaṃ. Rājā tassa kiriyaṃ tena samānetvā tadanucchavikaṃ daṇḍaṃ karoti. Iti etaṃ porāṇaṃ vajjidhammaṃ samādāya vattantānaṃ manussā na ujjhāyanti, ‘‘rājāno porāṇapaveṇiyā kammaṃ karonti, etesaṃ doso natthi, amhākaṃyeva doso’’ti appamattā kammante karonti. Evaṃ rājūnaṃ vuddhi hoti. Tena vuttaṃ – ‘‘vuddhiyeva, ānanda, vajjīnaṃ pāṭikaṅkhā, no parihānī’’ti.</p> <hi rend="bold">Porāṇaṃ vajjidhamma</hi> <pb ed="V" n="2.0098"/> <p rend="bodytext"><hi rend="bold">Sakkarontī</hi>ti yaṃkiñci tesaṃ sakkāraṃ karontā sundarameva karonti. <hi rend="bold">Garuṃ karontī</hi>ti garubhāvaṃ paccupaṭṭhapetvāva karonti. <hi rend="bold">Mānentī</hi>ti manena piyāyanti. <hi rend="bold">Pūjentī</hi>ti nipaccakāraṃ dassenti. <hi rend="bold">Sotabbaṃ maññantī</hi>ti divasassa dve tayo vāre upaṭṭhānaṃ gantvā tesaṃ kathaṃ sotabbaṃ saddhātabbaṃ maññanti. Tattha ye evaṃ mahallakānaṃ rājūnaṃ sakkārādīni na karonti, ovādatthāya ca nesaṃ upaṭṭhānaṃ na gacchanti, te tehi vissaṭṭhā anovadiyamānā kīḷāpasutā rajjato parihāyanti. Ye pana tathā paṭipajjanti, tesaṃ mahallakarājāno – ‘‘idaṃ kātabbaṃ, idaṃ na kātabba’’nti <pb ed="P" n="2.0520"/> porāṇaṃ paveṇiṃ ācikkhanti. Saṅgāmaṃ patvāpi – ‘‘evaṃ pavisitabbaṃ, evaṃ nikkhamitabba’’nti upāyaṃ dassenti. Te tehi ovadiyamānā yathāovādaṃ paṭipajjantā sakkonti rājappaveṇiṃ sandhāretuṃ. Tena vuttaṃ – ‘‘vuddhiyeva, ānanda, vajjīnaṃ pāṭikaṅkhā, no parihānī’’ti.</p> <hi rend="bold">Sakkarontī</hi> <hi rend="bold">Garuṃ karontī</hi> <hi rend="bold">Mānentī</hi> <hi rend="bold">Pūjentī</hi> <hi rend="bold">Sotabbaṃ maññantī</hi> <pb ed="P" n="2.0520"/> <p rend="bodytext"><hi rend="bold">Kulitthiyo</hi>ti <pb ed="M" n="2.0110"/> kulagharaṇiyo. <hi rend="bold">Kulakumāriyo</hi>ti anividdhā tāsaṃ dhītaro. <hi rend="bold">Okkassa pasayhā</hi>ti ettha ‘‘okkassā’’ti vā ‘‘pasayhā’’ti vā pasayhākārassevetaṃ nāmaṃ. ‘‘Ukkassā’’tipi paṭhanti. Tattha <hi rend="bold">okkassā</hi>ti avakassitvā ākaḍḍhitvā. <hi rend="bold">Pasayhā</hi>ti abhibhavitvā ajjhottharitvāti ayaṃ vacanattho. Evañhi karontānaṃ vijite manussā – ‘‘amhākaṃ gehe puttamātaropi, kheḷasiṅghāṇikādīni mukhena apanetvā saṃvaḍḍhitadhītaropi ime rājāno balakkārena gahetvā attano ghare vāsentī’’ti kupitā paccantaṃ pavisitvā corā vā corasahāyā vā hutvā janapadaṃ paharanti. Evaṃ akarontānaṃ pana vijite manussā appossukkā sakāni kammāni karontā rājakosaṃ vaḍḍhenti. Evamettha vuddhihāniyo veditabbā.</p> <hi rend="bold">Kulitthiyo</hi> <pb ed="M" n="2.0110"/> <hi rend="bold">Kulakumāriyo</hi> <hi rend="bold">Okkassa pasayhā</hi> <hi rend="bold">okkassā</hi> <hi rend="bold">Pasayhā</hi> <p rend="bodytext"><hi rend="bold">Vajjīnaṃ vajjicetiyānī</hi>ti vajjirājūnaṃ vajjiraṭṭhe cittīkataṭṭhena cetiyānīti laddhanāmāni yakkhaṭṭhānāni. <hi rend="bold">Abbhantarānī</hi>ti antonagare ṭhitāni. Bāhirānīti bahinagare ṭhitāni <pb ed="V" n="2.0099"/>. <hi rend="bold">Dinnapubba</hi>nti pubbe dinnaṃ. <hi rend="bold">Katapubba</hi>nti pubbe kataṃ. <hi rend="bold">No parihāpessantī</hi>ti aparihāpetvā yathāpavattameva karissanti dhammikaṃ baliṃ parihāpentānañhi devatā ārakkhaṃ susaṃvihitaṃ na karonti, anuppannaṃ dukkhaṃ janetuṃ asakkontāpi uppannaṃ kāsasīsarogādiṃ vaḍḍhenti, saṅgāme patte sahāyā na honti. Aparihāpentānaṃ pana ārakkhaṃ susaṃvihitaṃ karonti, anuppannaṃ sukhaṃ uppādetuṃ asakkontāpi uppannaṃ kāsasīsarogādiṃ hananti, saṅgāmasīse sahāyā hontīti evamettha vuddhihāniyo veditabbā.</p> <hi rend="bold">Vajjīnaṃ vajjicetiyānī</hi> <hi rend="bold">Abbhantarānī</hi> <pb ed="V" n="2.0099"/> <hi rend="bold">Dinnapubba</hi> <hi rend="bold">Katapubba</hi> <hi rend="bold">No parihāpessantī</hi> <p rend="bodytext"><hi rend="bold">Dhammikā rakkhāvaraṇaguttī</hi>ti ettha rakkhā eva yathā anicchitaṃ na gacchati, evaṃ āvaraṇato āvaraṇaṃ. Yathā icchitaṃ na vinassati, evaṃ gopāyanato gutti. Tattha balakāyena parivāretvā rakkhaṇaṃ pabbajitānaṃ dhammikā rakkhāvaraṇagutti <pb ed="P" n="2.0521"/> nāma na hoti. Yathā pana vihārassa upavane rukkhe na chindanti, vājikā vajjhaṃ na karonti, pokkharaṇīsu macche na gaṇhanti, evaṃ karaṇaṃ dhammikā rakkhāvaraṇagutti nāma. <hi rend="bold">Kinti anāgatā cā</hi>ti iminā pana nesaṃ evaṃ paccupaṭṭhitacittasantānoti cittappavattiṃ pucchati.</p> <hi rend="bold">Dhammikā rakkhāvaraṇaguttī</hi> <pb ed="P" n="2.0521"/> <hi rend="bold">Kinti anāgatā cā</hi> <p rend="bodytext">Tattha <pb ed="M" n="2.0111"/> ye anāgatānaṃ arahantānaṃ āgamanaṃ na icchanti, te assaddhā honti appasannā. Pabbajite ca sampatte paccuggamanaṃ na karonti, gantvā na passanti, paṭisanthāraṃ na karonti, pañhaṃ na pucchanti, dhammaṃ na suṇanti, dānaṃ na denti, anumodanaṃ na suṇanti, nivāsanaṭṭhānaṃ na saṃvidahanti. Atha nesaṃ avaṇṇo abbhuggacchati – ‘‘asuko nāma rājā assaddho appasanno, pabbajite sampatte paccuggamanaṃ na karoti…pe… nivāsanaṭṭhānaṃ na saṃvidahatī’’ti. Taṃ sutvā pabbajitā tassa nagaradvārena na gacchanti, gacchantāpi nagaraṃ na pavisanti. Evaṃ anāgatānaṃ arahantānaṃ anāgamanameva hoti. Āgatānampi phāsuvihāre asati yepi ajānitvā āgatā, te – ‘‘vasissāmāti tāva cintetvā āgatamhā, imesaṃ pana rājūnaṃ iminā nīhārena ko vasissatī’’ti nikkhamitvā gacchanti. Evaṃ anāgatesu anāgacchantesu, āgatesu dukkhaṃ viharantesu so deso pabbajitānaṃ anāvāso hoti. Tato devatārakkhā na hoti, devatārakkhāya asati amanussā okāsaṃ labhanti. Amanussā ussannā anuppannaṃ byādhiṃ uppādenti, sīlavantānaṃ dassanapañhāpucchanādivatthukassa puññassa anāgamo hoti. Vipariyāyena pana yathāvuttakaṇhapakkhaviparītassa sukkapakkhassa sambhavo hotīti evamettha vuddhihāniyo veditabbā.</p> <pb ed="M" n="2.0111"/>
134. When the venerable one was fanning the Blessed One, the venerable one stood at the head of the couch and fanned the Blessed One, but the Blessed One felt neither cold nor heat.

Having heard the words of the Brahmin, the Blessed One, without conferring with him, desiring to confer with the venerable one, said, “What have you heard, Ānanda?” and so on.

“Frequent assemblies” means even those who assemble three times a day, and even those who assemble intermittently, they are indeed frequent assemblies.

“Abounding in assemblies” means yesterday we assembled, the day before yesterday we assembled, again today why have we assembled?—not reaching a conclusion, they are said to be abounding in assemblies.

"As long as" means for that much time.

“Growth indeed, Ānanda, is to be expected for the Vajjis, not decline”—indeed, those who do not frequently assemble do not hear the teaching that has come from various directions; therefore, they do not know, "Such and such a village boundary or town boundary is disturbed, robbers have surrounded such and such a place"; even the robbers, knowing, "The kings are negligent," attacking the villages and towns, destroy the country.
Thus there is decline for the kings.

But those who frequently assemble hear this and that news, therefore sending forces, they suppress the enemy; even the robbers, "The kings are not negligent, it is not possible for us to wander about with bands of followers," scattering, they flee.
Thus there is growth for the kings.

Therefore it was said, “Growth indeed, Ānanda, is to be expected for the Vajjis, not decline.”

There, "to be expected" means it should be desired, it will certainly be, thus it should be seen, [this is] the meaning.

In "harmonious" and so on, when the assembly drum has been sounded—"Today I have business, I have a festival"—making an exception, those who are doing [those things] are not said to assemble harmoniously.

But having heard the sound of the drum, even those who are eating, even those who are adorning themselves, even those who are putting on clothes, either half-eaten or half-adorned or putting on clothes, those who assemble are said to assemble harmoniously.

But those who have assembled, having thought, having conferred, having done what needs to be done, rising up alone, are not said to rise up harmoniously.

Indeed, when they have risen up thus, those who go first, it occurs to them thus: "We have heard only external talk, now there will be talk of judgment."

But those who rise up together, those who are harmonious are said to rise up harmoniously.

Moreover, having heard, "In such and such places the village boundary or the town boundary is disturbed, robbers have surrounded [it]"—"Who, going, will suppress this enemy?"—when [this] has been said, "I first, I first," saying [this], even those who are going are said to rise up harmoniously.

Moreover, when the work of one is failing, even though the remaining kings, sons and brothers, sending [help], support his work, even though they all gather together a visiting king, not saying, "Let him go to such and such's house, let him go to such and such's house," even though they all gather together, even though all go there in companionship when happiness or suffering or another such thing has arisen for one, they are said to do the Vajjian duties harmoniously.

Harmonious

When in "un-enacted" and so on, exacting a tax or tribute or penalty that was not done before, they are said to enact the un-enacted.

But not exacting what has come by ancient tradition, they are said to abolish the enacted.

Having seized someone as a thief and having shown [him], not investigating, but instructing about what should be cut off and what should be broken, not undertaking the ancient Vajjian custom, they are not said to proceed.

For those who enact the un-enacted, oppressed by new taxes and so on, people [think], "We are extremely oppressed, who will live in their conquered territory?" and entering the border region, becoming either robbers or companions of robbers, they attack the country.

For those who abolish the enacted, not taking the taxes and so on that have come by tradition, the treasury declines.

Then elephants, horses, armies, women of the court, and so on, not obtaining the regular allowance, decline in strength and power.

They are fit neither for war nor for attendance.

For those who, not undertaking the ancient Vajjian custom, proceed, in the conquered territory, people, "Having made our son, father, brother, even though not a thief, [they say] 'He is a thief!' and they cut [him] off, they break [him]," being angry, entering the border region, becoming either robbers or companions of robbers, they attack the country, thus there is decline for the kings; but for those who enact the enacted, "The kings do only what has come by tradition," people, being delighted and pleased, accomplish the works such as agriculture and trade.

For those who do not abolish the enacted, taking the taxes and so on that have come by tradition, the treasury increases, then elephants, horses, armies, women of the court, and so on, obtaining the regular allowance, being endowed with strength and power, are fit both for war and for attendance.

Un-enacted

In "ancient Vajjian custom," formerly, indeed, the Vajjian kings, having brought someone, [saying], "This is a thief," when he had been shown, without saying, "Seize him, [he is] a thief," they hand [him] over to the ministers of judgment.

They, having judged, if he is not a thief, release [him].If [he] is a thief, without saying anything himself, they give [him] to the *vohārika*s.

If those also [determine that he] is not a thief, they release [him].

If [he] is a thief, they give [him] to the *suttadhara*s.

If those also, having investigated, [determine that he] is not a thief, they release [him].

If [he] is a thief, they give [him] to the *aṭṭhakulika*s.

If those also, having done likewise, [give him] to the commander, the commander to the sub-king, the sub-king to the king, [and] the king, having investigated, [determines that he] is not a thief, [he] releases [him].

If, however, [he] is a thief, he orders the book of customs to be read.

There, it is written: “By whomever this deed was done, for him this is the punishment.”

The king, comparing his deed with that, inflicts a punishment appropriate to it.

Thus, people do not complain of those who, having adopted this ancient custom of the Vajjis, conduct [themselves accordingly], [saying,] “The kings perform [their] actions according to ancient custom; there is no fault in them, the fault is only in us.” Being mindful, they perform [their] work.

Thus, there is growth for the kings.

Therefore it was said: “Growth alone, Ānanda, is to be expected for the Vajjis, not decline.”

Ancient Vajjian custom.

"They venerate" means that whatever veneration they perform for them, they perform it beautifully.

"They respect" means they perform [it] only after having established an attitude of reverence.

"They honor" means they please with [their] minds.

"They worship" means they show reverence.

"They think [one] should listen" means that, having gone to [their] presence two or three times a day, they think one should listen to their words and have faith.

There, those who do not perform acts of veneration and so forth for these elderly kings, and do not go to their presence for instruction, being separated from them, not being instructed, given to play, decline from [their] kingdom.

Those, however, who conduct themselves in that way, to them the elderly kings explain the ancient tradition, [saying,] “This should be done, this should not be done."

Even having reached a battle, they show a means [of escape, saying,] “Thus should [one] enter, thus should [one] exit.”

Those who, being instructed by them, conduct themselves according to [their] instruction, are able to maintain the royal lineage.

Therefore it was said: “Growth alone, Ānanda, is to be expected for the Vajjis, not decline.”

They venerate, they respect, they honor, they worship, they think [one] should listen.

"Women of good families" means women of noble households.

"Girls of good families" means unmarried daughters of those [families].

"By force to Okkassa" means here that either “to Okkassā” or “by force” is a name for an act of force.

They also read “Ukkassā”.

There, “Okkassā” means having drawn [them] away, having pulled [them].

“By force” means having overcome, having overwhelmed; this is the meaning of the word.

For when they do thus, the people in the conquered territory [think:] "These kings, having forcibly taken away even our daughters who were raised after removing the spit and snot and so forth from [their] mouths, cause [them] to live in their own houses." Being angered, having entered the border region, either as thieves or as friends of thieves, they strike the countryside.

When, however, they do not do thus, the people in the conquered territory, being unconcerned, performing their own tasks, increase the royal treasury.

Thus, growth and decline should be understood here.

Women of good families, girls of good families, by force to Okkassa, to Okkassā, by force.

"The Vajjis’ *vajji-cetiya*s" means the *yakṣa*-shrines in the Vajjis’ territory of the Vajjis that have obtained the name *cetiya* by reason of [their] being made prominent.

"Inner ones" means those situated in the inner city.

"Outer ones" means those situated outside the city.
0099"/>.
“*Dinnapubba*” means previously given.
“*Katapubba*” means previously done.
“They will not diminish it” means without causing it to diminish, they will perform the customary and righteous offering. Because deities do not protect and properly arrange the guard for those who diminish the righteous offering (*dhārmikaṃ baliṃ*), even though they are unable to generate suffering that has not arisen, they increase coughs, headaches, and other diseases that have arisen. When battles occur, they are not allies.
But for those who do not diminish it, they protect and properly arrange the guard. Even though they are unable to generate happiness that has not arisen, they destroy coughs, headaches, and other diseases that have arisen. They are allies in battle. Thus, in this regard, growth and decline should be understood.
The *Vajjīs'* inner *Vajji* shrines.
0099"/> "*Dinnapubba*," "*Katapubba*," "they will not diminish it." The righteous protection, guard, and defense (*dhārmikā rakkhāvaraṇaguttī*) here, protection itself is such that what is not desired does not go, thus from covering to covering.
Just as what is desired does not perish, thus protection from concealment.
There, having surrounded [them] with a troop, the righteous protection, guard, and defense of the renunciates.
0521"/> is not called.
Just as, moreover, in a monastery's park, they do not cut down trees, the *vājika*s do not kill the condemned, in the ponds they do not catch fish, thus, that doing is called righteous protection, guard, and defense.
"*Kinti anāgatā cā*" means by this, he asks about the mental activity of those whose minds are thus established.
The righteous protection, guard, and defense.
0521"/> "*Kinti anāgatā cā*" There <pb ed="m" n="2.
0111"/> Those who do not desire the arrival of future *arhat*s, they are faithless and unappeased.
And when renunciates arrive, they do not go out to meet them, having gone, they do not see them, they do not make a respectful reception, they do not ask questions, they do not listen to the Dharma, they do not give a gift, they do not rejoice in approval, they do not arrange a dwelling place.
Then ill-repute goes out for them – “So-and-so, by name, is a king, faithless and unappeased, he does not go out to meet renunciates who have arrived…pe…he does not arrange a dwelling place.”
Having heard that, the renunciates do not go by the gate of that city, even going, they do not enter the city.
Thus, for future *arhat*s, there is just non-arrival.
Even for those who have arrived, when there is no comfortable dwelling, those who have arrived without knowing – “We came, thinking ‘we will dwell’, but with this policy of these kings, who will dwell?” – having left, they go.
Thus, when those who are not coming are not coming, when those who have come dwell in suffering, that place is uninhabitable for renunciates.
From that, there is no protection by deities. When there is no protection by deities, non-humans obtain an opportunity.
Non-humans, being rampant, generate a disease that has not arisen. The non-arrival of merit for the virtuous, whose object is seeing, questioning, asking questions, and so forth.
By the opposite, moreover, the arising of the bright fortnight, which is the opposite of the aforementioned dark fortnight, occurs. Thus, in this regard, growth and decline should be understood.
135
<p n="135" rend="bodytext"><hi rend="paranum">135</hi><hi rend="dot">.</hi> Atha <pb ed="V" n="2.0059"/> kho bhagavā vassakāraṃ brāhmaṇaṃ magadhamahāmattaṃ āmantesi – ‘‘ekamidāhaṃ, brāhmaṇa, samayaṃ vesāliyaṃ viharāmi sārandade <note>sānandare (ka.)</note> cetiye. Tatrāhaṃ vajjīnaṃ ime satta aparihāniye dhamme desesiṃ. Yāvakīvañca, brāhmaṇa, ime satta aparihāniyā dhammā vajjīsu ṭhassanti, imesu ca sattasu aparihāniyesu dhammesu vajjī sandississanti, vuddhiyeva, brāhmaṇa, vajjīnaṃ pāṭikaṅkhā, no parihānī’’ti.</p> <p rend="bodytext">Evaṃ vutte, vassakāro brāhmaṇo magadhamahāmatto bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – ‘‘ekamekenapi, bho gotama, aparihāniyena dhammena samannāgatānaṃ vajjīnaṃ vuddhiyeva pāṭikaṅkhā, no parihāni <pb ed="P" n="2.0076"/>. Ko pana vādo sattahi aparihāniyehi dhammehi. Akaraṇīyāva <note>akaraṇīyā ca (syā. ka.)</note>, bho gotama, vajjī <note>vajjīnaṃ (ka.)</note> raññā māgadhena ajātasattunā vedehiputtena yadidaṃ yuddhassa, aññatra upalāpanāya aññatra mithubhedā. Handa ca dāni mayaṃ, bho gotama, gacchāma <pb ed="T" n="2.0090"/>, bahukiccā mayaṃ bahukaraṇīyā’’ti. ‘‘Yassadāni tvaṃ, brāhmaṇa, kālaṃ maññasī’’ti. Atha kho vassakāro brāhmaṇo magadhamahāmatto bhagavato bhāsitaṃ abhinanditvā anumoditvā uṭṭhāyāsanā pakkāmi.</p> <pb ed="P" n="2.0076"/> <note>akaraṇīyā ca (syā. ka.)</note> <note>vajjīnaṃ (ka.)</note> <pb ed="T" n="2.0090"/> <p rend="subhead">Bhikkhuaparihāniyadhammā</p>
135. Then the Blessed One addressed Vassakāra the Brahmin, the chief minister of Magadha, "Once, Brahmin, I was staying near Vesālī at the Sārandada shrine. There I taught the Vajjis these seven principles for preventing decline. As long as these seven principles that prevent decline endure among the Vajjis, and the Vajjis adhere to these seven principles, their growth is to be expected, not their decline."

When this was said, Vassakāra the Brahmin, the chief minister of Magadha, said this to the Blessed One: "Even with one of these principles, Master Gotama, the growth of the Vajjis is to be expected, not their decline. What then of all seven principles for preventing decline? The Vajjis cannot be overcome in battle by Ajātasattu, King of Magadha, the son of Vedehi, except through deception or sowing discord. And now, Master Gotama, we must depart, as we have many duties and much to do." "Then do, Brahmin, what you think it is now time to do."

Then Vassakāra the Brahmin, the chief minister of Magadha, delighting in and approving of the Blessed One’s words, got up from his seat and departed.

The bhikkhu's principles for preventing decline.
<p n="135" rend="bodytext"><hi rend="paranum">135</hi><hi rend="dot">.</hi><hi rend="bold">Ekamidāha</hi>nti idaṃ bhagavā pubbe vajjīnaṃ imassa vajjisattakassa desitabhāvappakāsanatthamāha <pb ed="V" n="2.0100"/>. Tattha <hi rend="bold">sārandade cetiye</hi>ti evaṃnāmake vihāre. Anuppanne kira buddhe tattha sārandadassa yakkhassa nivāsanaṭṭhānaṃ cetiyaṃ ahosi. Athettha bhagavato vihāraṃ kārāpesuṃ, so sārandade cetiye katattā sārandadacetiyantveva saṅkhyaṃ gato.</p> <p rend="bodytext"><hi rend="bold">Akaraṇīyā</hi>ti akātabbā, aggahetabbāti attho. <hi rend="bold">Yadida</hi>nti <pb ed="P" n="2.0522"/> nipātamattaṃ. <hi rend="bold">Yuddhassā</hi>ti karaṇatthe sāmivacanaṃ, abhimukhayuddhena gahetuṃ na sakkāti attho. <hi rend="bold">Aññatra upalāpanāyā</hi>ti ṭhapetvā upalāpanaṃ. Upalāpanā nāma – ‘‘alaṃ vivādena, idāni samaggā homā’’ti hatthiassarathahiraññasuvaṇṇādīni pesetvā saṅgahakaraṇaṃ. Evañhi saṅgahaṃ katvā kevalaṃ vissāsena sakkā gaṇhitunti attho. <hi rend="bold">Aññatra mithubhedāyā</hi>ti ṭhapetvā mithubhedaṃ. Iminā aññamaññabhedaṃ katvāpi sakkā ete gahetunti <pb ed="M" n="2.0112"/> dasseti. Idaṃ brāhmaṇo bhagavato kathāya nayaṃ labhitvā āha.</p> <hi rend="bold">Akaraṇīyā</hi> <hi rend="bold">Yadida</hi> <pb ed="P" n="2.0522"/> <hi rend="bold">Yuddhassā</hi> <hi rend="bold">Aññatra upalāpanāyā</hi> <hi rend="bold">Aññatra mithubhedāyā</hi> <pb ed="M" n="2.0112"/> <p rend="bodytext">Kiṃ pana bhagavā brāhmaṇassa imāya kathāya nayalābhaṃ na jānātīti? Āma, jānāti. Jānanto kasmā kathesīti? Anukampāya. Evaṃ kirassa ahosi – ‘‘mayā akathitepi katipāhena gantvā sabbe gaṇhissati, kathite pana samagge bhindanto tīhi saṃvaccharehi gaṇhissati, ettakampi jīvitameva varaṃ, ettakañhi jīvantā attano patiṭṭhānabhūtaṃ puññaṃ karissantī’’ti.</p> <p rend="bodytext"><hi rend="bold">Abhinanditvā</hi>ti cittena abhinanditvā. <hi rend="bold">Anumoditvā</hi>ti ‘‘yāva subhāsitañcidaṃ bhotā gotamenā’’ti vācāya anumoditvā. <hi rend="bold">Pakkāmī</hi>ti rañño santikaṃ gato. Tato naṃ rājā – ‘‘kiṃ ācariya, bhagavā avacā’’ti pucchi. So – ‘‘yathā bho samaṇassa gotamassa vacanaṃ na sakkā vajjī kenaci gahetuṃ, api ca upalāpanāya vā mithubhedena vā sakkā’’ti āha. Tato naṃ rājā – ‘‘upalāpanāya amhākaṃ hatthiassādayo nassissanti, bhedeneva te gahessāmi, kiṃ karomā’’ti pucchi. Tena hi, mahārāja, tumhe vajjiṃ ārabbha parisati kathaṃ samuṭṭhāpetha. Tato ahaṃ – ‘‘kiṃ te mahārāja tehi, attano santakehi kasivāṇijjādīni katvā jīvantu ete rājāno’’ti vatvā pakkamissāmi. Tato tumhe – ‘‘kinnu kho bho esa brāhmaṇo vajjiṃ ārabbha pavattaṃ kathaṃ paṭibāhatī’’ti vadeyyātha, divasabhāge cāhaṃ tesaṃ paṇṇākāraṃ pesessāmi, tampi gāhāpetvā tumhepi mama dosaṃ āropetvā bandhanatālanādīni akatvāva kevalaṃ khuramuṇḍaṃ maṃ katvā nagarā nīharāpetha. Athāhaṃ – ‘‘mayā te nagare pākāro parikhā ca kāritā, ahaṃ kira dubbalaṭṭhānañca uttānagambhīraṭṭhānañca jānāmi, na cirasseva dāni <pb ed="V" n="2.0101"/> ujuṃ karissāmī’’ti <pb ed="P" n="2.0523"/> vakkhāmi. Taṃ sutvā tumhe – ‘‘gacchatū’’ti vadeyyāthāti. Rājā sabbaṃ akāsi.</p> <hi rend="bold">Abhinanditvā</hi> <hi rend="bold">Anumoditvā</hi> <hi rend="bold">Pakkāmī</hi> <pb ed="V" n="2.0101"/> <pb ed="P" n="2.0523"/> <p rend="bodytext">Licchavī tassa nikkhamanaṃ sutvā – ‘‘saṭho brāhmaṇo, mā tassa gaṅgaṃ uttarituṃ adatthā’’ti āhaṃsu. Tatra ekaccehi – ‘‘amhe ārabbha kathitattā kira so evaṃ kato’’ti vutte ‘‘tena hi, bhaṇe, etū’’ti bhaṇiṃsu. So gantvā licchavī disvā ‘‘kiṃ āgatatthā’’ti pucchito taṃ pavattiṃ ārocesi, licchavino – ‘‘appamattakena nāma evaṃ garuṃ daṇḍaṃ kātuṃ na yutta’’nti <pb ed="M" n="2.0113"/> vatvā – ‘‘kiṃ te tatra ṭhānantara’’nti pucchiṃsu. ‘‘Vinicchayāmaccohamasmī’’ti. Tadeva te ṭhānantaraṃ hotūti. So suṭṭhutaraṃ vinicchayaṃ karoti, rājakumārā tassa santike sippaṃ uggaṇhanti.</p> <pb ed="M" n="2.0113"/> <p rend="bodytext">So patiṭṭhitaguṇo hutvā ekadivasaṃ ekaṃ licchaviṃ gahetvā ekamantaṃ gantvā – dārakā kasantīti pucchi. Āma, kasanti. Dve goṇe yojetvāti? Āma, dve goṇe yojetvāti. Ettakaṃ vatvā nivatto. Tato taṃ añño – ‘‘kiṃ ācariyo āhā’’ti pucchitvā tena vuttaṃ asaddahanto ‘‘na me esa yathābhūtaṃ kathetī’’ti tena saddhiṃ bhijji. Brāhmaṇo aññasmiṃ divase ekaṃ licchaviṃ ekamantaṃ netvā – ‘‘kena byañjanena bhuttosī’’ti pucchitvā nivatto. Tampi añño pucchitvā asaddahanto tatheva bhijji. Brāhmaṇo aparampi divasaṃ ekaṃ licchaviṃ ekamantaṃ netvā – ‘‘atiduggatosi kirā’’ti pucchi. Ko evamāhāti pucchito asuko nāma licchavīti. Aparampi ekamantaṃ netvā – ‘‘tvaṃ kira bhīrukajātiko’’ti pucchi. Ko evamāhāti? Asuko nāma licchavīti. Evaṃ aññena akathitameva aññassa kathento tīhi saṃvaccharehi te rājāno aññamaññaṃ bhinditvā yathā dve ekamaggena na gacchanti, tathā katvā sannipātabheriṃ carāpesi. Licchavino – ‘‘issarā sannipatantu, sūrā sannipatantū’’ti vatvā na sannipatiṃsu.</p> <p rend="bodytext">Brāhmaṇo – ‘‘ayaṃ dāni kālo, sīghaṃ āgacchatū’’ti rañño sāsanaṃ pesesi. Rājā sutvāva balabheriṃ carāpetvā nikkhami. Vesālikā sutvā – ‘‘rañño gaṅgaṃ uttarituṃ na dassāmā’’ti bheriṃ carāpesuṃ. Tampi sutvā – ‘‘gacchantu sūrarājāno’’tiādīni vatvā na <pb ed="P" n="2.0524"/> sannipatiṃsu. ‘‘Nagarappavesanaṃ na dassāma, dvārāni pidahitvā ṭhassāmā’’ti bheriṃ carāpesuṃ. Ekopi na sannipati. Yathāvivaṭeheva dvārehi pavisitvā sabbe anayabyasanaṃ pāpetvā gato.</p> <pb ed="P" n="2.0524"/> <p rend="subhead">Bhikkhuaparihāniyadhammavaṇṇanā</p>
135. *ekamidāha*nti: The Blessed One said this to reveal that he had previously taught this to the Vajjis regarding this group of Vajjis.

There, *sārandade cetiye*ti: In the monastery named Sārandada. It is said that before the Buddha arose, the *cetiya* was the dwelling place of the *yakṣa* Sārandada. Then, there they had a monastery built for the Blessed One, so it was named Sārandadacetiya because it was made in the Sārandada *cetiya*.

*akaraṇīyā*ti: Unsuitable, improper, is the meaning.

*yadida*nti: Just a particle.

*yuddhassā*ti: It is a word expressing ownership in the sense of instrumentality, the meaning is that it is not possible to seize them by direct warfare.

*aññatra upalāpanāyā*ti: Except by appeasement. Appeasement is this: "Enough of quarreling, let us now be harmonious," sending elephants, horses, chariots, gold, silver, etc., and making reconciliation. For by making reconciliation in this way, it is possible to seize them merely by trust, is the meaning.

*aññatra mithubhedāyā*ti: Except by causing dissension. By causing mutual dissension in this way, it is possible to seize them, this is what it shows. The *brāhmaṇa* said this after gaining insight into the Blessed One's teaching.

*akaraṇīyā*, *yadida*, *yuddhassā*, *aññatra upalāpanāyā*, *aññatra mithubhedāyā*

Why then did the Blessed One not know of this *brāhmaṇa*'s gain of insight into the teaching by this statement? Yes, he knows.

Knowing, why did he speak? Out of compassion.

It was like this for him: "Even if I do not speak, after a few days, having gone, he will seize all of them; but if I speak, while he is destroying those who are harmonious, he will seize them in three years. Even that much life is better, for living that long they will do merit that is the foundation for themselves."

*abhinanditvā*ti: Having rejoiced with his mind.

*anumoditvā*ti: Having expressed approval with his voice, saying, "How well spoken this is by Master Gotama!"

*pakkāmī*ti: He went to the presence of the king.

Then the king asked him, "O teacher, what did the Blessed One say?"

He said, "It is not possible to seize the Vajjis by any means, just as the word of the *śramaṇa* Gotama is; but it is possible by appeasement or by causing dissension."

Then the king asked him, "By appeasement our elephants, horses, etc., will be destroyed; I will seize them only by dissension; what should I do?"

"In that case, great king, how should you instigate a speech concerning the Vajjis in the assembly?"

Then I will say, "What is the use of those kings to you, great king? Let those kings live by doing agriculture, trade, etc., with their own possessions," and I will leave.

Then you should say, "What is this? This *brāhmaṇa*, having taken the Vajjis as his object, is preventing the arisen speech!" And in the daytime I will send them a tribute; having had that accepted, you too, having imputed blame to me, without doing imprisonment, beating, etc., just having made me with a shorn head, have me led out of the city.

Then I will say, "The rampart and the moat in that city were made by me; I know both the weak places and the shallow and deep places; now, without delay, I will make them straight."

Having heard that, you should say, "Go away!"

The king did everything.

*abhinanditvā*, *anumoditvā*, *pakkāmī*

The Licchavis, having heard of his departure, said, "The *brāhmaṇa* is a cheat; do not give him passage to cross the Gaṅgā!"

There, some said, "It was because he spoke concerning us that he was made so." "In that case, come, sir!" they said.Having gone, seeing the Licchavis, when asked, "Why have you come?" he announced that matter. The Licchavis said, "It is not proper to inflict such a heavy punishment for a trifle." Having said this, they asked, "What is your position there?"

"I am a judge."

"May that be your position."

He judges very well. The princes learn crafts near him.

</p>
Having become one of established qualities, one day, having taken a Licchavi, having gone to one side, he asked: "Are the boys plowing?"

"Yes, they are plowing."

"Are they yoking two oxen?" "Yes, they are yoking two oxen."

Having said this much, he returned.

Then another, having asked him, "What did the teacher say?" disbelieving what was said by him, [saying,] "He does not tell me the truth," broke with him.

A *brāhmaṇa*, on another day, having led a Licchavi to one side, having asked, "With what seasoning have you eaten?" he returned.

Another, having asked him, disbelieving, likewise broke [with him].

A *brāhmaṇa*, again on another day, having led a Licchavi to one side, asked: "You are very poor, I hear?"

When asked, "Who says this?" [he replied,] "So-and-so, a Licchavi."

Again, having led [another] to one side: "You are timid by nature, I hear?" he asked.

"Who says this?" "So-and-so, a Licchavi."

In this way, telling to another what was not said by another, after three years, having caused those kings to break with each other, just as two do not go on one road, having done so, he had the drum of assembly paraded.

The Licchavis, saying, "The lords should assemble, the heroes should assemble," did not assemble.

</p>
The *brāhmaṇa* sent a message to the king, "Now is the time, let him come quickly."

The king, having heard, immediately had the drum of strength paraded, and went out.

The Vesalians, having heard, had a drum paraded, [saying,] "We will not allow the king to cross the Gaṅgā."

Having heard that too, having spoken words beginning with "Let the hero-kings go," they did not assemble.

"We will not allow entrance into the city; having closed the doors, we will stand firm," they had a drum paraded.

Not even one assembled.

Having entered through the very open doors, having brought all to misfortune and ruin, he departed.

</p>
Description of the conditions for non-decline for monks.
136
<p n="136" rend="bodytext"><hi rend="paranum">136</hi><hi rend="dot">.</hi> Atha kho bhagavā acirapakkante vassakāre brāhmaṇe magadhamahāmatte āyasmantaṃ ānandaṃ āmantesi – ‘‘gaccha tvaṃ, ānanda, yāvatikā bhikkhū rājagahaṃ upanissāya viharanti, te sabbe upaṭṭhānasālāyaṃ sannipātehī’’ti. ‘‘Evaṃ, bhante’’ti kho āyasmā ānando bhagavato paṭissutvā yāvatikā bhikkhū rājagahaṃ upanissāya viharanti, te sabbe upaṭṭhānasālāyaṃ sannipātetvā yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṃ abhivādetvā ekamantaṃ aṭṭhāsi. Ekamantaṃ ṭhito kho āyasmā ānando bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – ‘‘sannipatito, bhante, bhikkhusaṅgho, yassadāni, bhante, bhagavā kālaṃ maññatī’’ti.</p> <p rend="bodytext">Atha <pb ed="M" n="2.0065"/> kho bhagavā uṭṭhāyāsanā yena upaṭṭhānasālā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā paññatte āsane nisīdi. Nisajja kho bhagavā bhikkhū āmantesi – ‘‘satta vo, bhikkhave, aparihāniye dhamme desessāmi, taṃ suṇātha, sādhukaṃ manasikarotha, bhāsissāmī’’ti. ‘‘Evaṃ, bhante’’ti kho te bhikkhū bhagavato paccassosuṃ. Bhagavā etadavoca –</p> <pb ed="M" n="2.0065"/> <p rend="bodytext">‘‘Yāvakīvañca <pb ed="V" n="2.0060"/>, bhikkhave, bhikkhū abhiṇhaṃ sannipātā sannipātabahulā bhavissanti, vuddhiyeva, bhikkhave, bhikkhūnaṃ pāṭikaṅkhā, no parihāni.</p> <pb ed="V" n="2.0060"/> <p rend="bodytext">‘‘Yāvakīvañca, bhikkhave, bhikkhū samaggā sannipatissanti, samaggā vuṭṭhahissanti, samaggā saṅghakaraṇīyāni <pb ed="T" n="2.0091"/> karissanti <pb ed="P" n="2.0077"/>, vuddhiyeva, bhikkhave, bhikkhūnaṃ pāṭikaṅkhā, no parihāni.</p> <pb ed="T" n="2.0091"/> <pb ed="P" n="2.0077"/> <p rend="bodytext">‘‘Yāvakīvañca, bhikkhave, bhikkhū apaññattaṃ na paññapessanti, paññattaṃ na samucchindissanti, yathāpaññattesu sikkhāpadesu samādāya vattissanti, vuddhiyeva, bhikkhave, bhikkhūnaṃ pāṭikaṅkhā, no parihāni.</p> <p rend="bodytext">‘‘Yāvakīvañca, bhikkhave, bhikkhū ye te bhikkhū therā rattaññū cirapabbajitā saṅghapitaro saṅghapariṇāyakā, te sakkarissanti garuṃ karissanti mānessanti pūjessanti, tesañca sotabbaṃ maññissanti, vuddhiyeva, bhikkhave, bhikkhūnaṃ pāṭikaṅkhā, no parihāni.</p> <p rend="bodytext">‘‘Yāvakīvañca, bhikkhave, bhikkhū uppannāya taṇhāya ponobbhavikāya na vasaṃ gacchissanti, vuddhiyeva, bhikkhave, bhikkhūnaṃ pāṭikaṅkhā, no parihāni.</p> <p rend="bodytext">‘‘Yāvakīvañca, bhikkhave, bhikkhū āraññakesu senāsanesu sāpekkhā bhavissanti, vuddhiyeva, bhikkhave, bhikkhūnaṃ pāṭikaṅkhā, no parihāni.</p> <p rend="bodytext">‘‘Yāvakīvañca, bhikkhave, bhikkhū paccattaññeva satiṃ upaṭṭhapessanti – ‘kinti anāgatā ca pesalā sabrahmacārī āgaccheyyuṃ, āgatā ca pesalā sabrahmacārī phāsu <note>phāsuṃ (sī. syā. pī.)</note> vihareyyu’nti. Vuddhiyeva, bhikkhave, bhikkhūnaṃ pāṭikaṅkhā, no parihāni.</p> <note>phāsuṃ (sī. syā. pī.)</note> <p rend="bodytext">‘‘Yāvakīvañca, bhikkhave, ime satta aparihāniyā dhammā bhikkhūsu ṭhassanti, imesu ca sattasu aparihāniyesu dhammesu bhikkhū sandississanti, vuddhiyeva, bhikkhave, bhikkhūnaṃ pāṭikaṅkhā, no parihāni.</p>
136. Then, soon after the departure of the brahmin Vassakāra, the chief minister of Magadha, the Blessed One addressed the Venerable Ānanda: "Go, Ānanda, assemble in the assembly hall all the monks who dwell in dependence on Rājagaha."

"So be it, Lord," the Venerable Ānanda replied to the Blessed One. Having gathered all the monks who dwelt in dependence on Rājagaha in the assembly hall, he approached the Blessed One. Having approached, bowed down to the Blessed One, and stood to one side.

Standing to one side, the Venerable Ānanda said to the Blessed One: "The Saṅgha of monks is assembled, Lord. Now is the time, Lord, for the Blessed One to do as he sees fit."

Then the Blessed One rose from his seat and went to the assembly hall. Having arrived, he sat down on the seat that was prepared.

Having sat down, the Blessed One addressed the monks: "Monks, I will teach you seven conditions leading to no decline ( *aparihāṇiya dhamma*). Listen to them, pay close attention, and I will speak."

"So be it, Lord," those monks replied to the Blessed One.

The Blessed One said this:

"As long as the monks hold frequent and well-attended assemblies, their growth is to be expected, not their decline.

As long as the monks meet in harmony, adjourn in harmony, and conduct the business of the Saṅgha in harmony, their growth is to be expected, not their decline.

As long as the monks do not enact what has not been enacted, nor abolish what has been enacted, but conduct themselves in accordance with the training rules as they have been enacted, their growth is to be expected, not their decline.

As long as the monks honor, respect, venerate, and esteem the elder monks who are experienced, long ordained, fathers of the Saṅgha, and leaders of the Saṅgha, and consider them worth listening to, their growth is to be expected, not their decline.

As long as the monks do not come under the sway of craving that leads to renewed existence, their growth is to be expected, not their decline.

As long as the monks find satisfaction in secluded forest dwellings, their growth is to be expected, not their decline.

As long as the monks maintain mindfulness within themselves, thinking, ‘May virtuous *sabrahmacārī* companions who have not yet come, come; and may the virtuous *sabrahmacārī* companions who have already come live in comfort,’ their growth is to be expected, not their decline.

As long as these seven conditions leading to no decline endure among the monks, and the monks are known for these seven conditions leading to no decline, their growth is to be expected, not their decline."
<p n="136" rend="bodytext"><hi rend="paranum">136</hi><hi rend="dot">.</hi><hi rend="bold">Atha</hi><pb ed="V" n="2.0102"/><hi rend="bold">kho bhagavā acirapakkante</hi>tiādimhi <hi rend="bold">sannipātetvā</hi>ti dūravihāresu iddhimante pesetvā santikavihāresu sayaṃ gantvā – ‘‘sannipatatha, āyasmanto; bhagavā vo sannipātaṃ icchatī’’ti sannipātetvā. <hi rend="bold">Aparihāniye</hi>ti <pb ed="M" n="2.0114"/> aparihānikare, vuddhihetubhūteti attho. <hi rend="bold">Dhamme desessāmī</hi>ti candasahassaṃ sūriyasahassaṃ uṭṭhapento viya catukuṭṭake gehe anto teladīpasahassaṃ ujjālento viya pākaṭe katvā kathayissāmīti.</p> <p rend="bodytext">Tattha <hi rend="bold">abhiṇhaṃ sannipātā</hi>ti idaṃ vajjisattake vuttasadisameva. Idhāpi ca abhiṇhaṃ asannipatitā disāsu āgatasāsanaṃ na suṇanti. Tato – ‘‘asukavihārasīmā ākulā, uposathapavāraṇā ṭhitā, asukasmiṃ ṭhāne bhikkhū vejjakammadūtakammādīni karonti, viññattibahulā pupphadānādīhi jīvikaṃ kappentī’’tiādīni na jānanti, pāpabhikkhūpi ‘‘pamatto bhikkhusaṅgho’’ti ñatvā rāsibhūtā sāsanaṃ osakkāpenti. Abhiṇhaṃ sannipatitā pana taṃ taṃ pavattiṃ suṇanti, tato bhikkhusaṅghaṃ pesetvā sīmaṃ ujuṃ karonti, uposathapavāraṇādayo pavattāpenti, micchājīvānaṃ ussannaṭṭhāne ariyavaṃsake pesetvā ariyavaṃsaṃ kathāpenti, pāpabhikkhūnaṃ vinayadharehi niggahaṃ kārāpenti, pāpabhikkhūpi ‘‘appamatto bhikkhusaṅgho, na sakkā amhehi vaggabandhena vicaritu’’nti bhijjitvā palāyanti. Evamettha hānivuddhiyo veditabbā.</p> <hi rend="bold">abhiṇhaṃ sannipātā</hi> <p rend="bodytext"><hi rend="bold">Samaggā</hi>tiādīsu cetiyapaṭijagganatthaṃ vā bodhigehauposathāgāracchādanatthaṃ vā katikavattaṃ vā ṭhapetukāmatāya ovādaṃ vā dātukāmatāya – ‘‘saṅgho sannipatatū’’ti bheriyā vā ghaṇṭiyā vā ākoṭitāya – ‘‘mayhaṃ cīvarakammaṃ atthi, mayhaṃ patto pacitabbo, mayhaṃ navakammaṃ atthī’’ti vikkhepaṃ karontā na samaggā sannipatanti nāma. Sabbaṃ pana taṃ kammaṃ ṭhapetvā – ‘‘ahaṃ purimataraṃ, ahaṃ purimatara’’nti ekappahāreneva sannipatantā samaggā sannipatanti nāma. Sannipatitā pana cintetvā mantetvā kattabbaṃ <pb ed="P" n="2.0525"/> katvā ekato avuṭṭhahantā samaggā na vuṭṭhahanti nāma. Evaṃ vuṭṭhitesu hi ye paṭhamaṃ gacchanti, tesaṃ evaṃ hoti – ‘‘amhehi bāhirakathāva sutā, idāni vinicchayakathā bhavissatī’’ti. Ekappahāreneva vuṭṭhahantā pana samaggā vuṭṭhahanti nāma. Apica ‘‘asukaṭṭhāne vihārasīmā ākulā, uposathapavāraṇā ṭhitā, asukaṭṭhāne vejjakammādikārakā pāpabhikkhū ussannā’’ti sutvā – ‘‘ko gantvā <pb ed="M" n="2.0115"/> tesaṃ niggahaṃ karissatī’’ti <pb ed="V" n="2.0103"/> vutte – ‘‘ahaṃ paṭhamaṃ, ahaṃ paṭhama’’nti vatvā gacchantāpi samaggā vuṭṭhahanti nāma.</p> <hi rend="bold">Samaggā</hi> <pb ed="P" n="2.0525"/> <pb ed="M" n="2.0115"/> <pb ed="V" n="2.0103"/> <p rend="bodytext">Āgantukaṃ pana disvā – ‘‘imaṃ pariveṇaṃ yāhi, etaṃ pariveṇaṃ yāhi, ayaṃ ko’’ti avatvā sabbe vattaṃ karontāpi, jiṇṇapattacīvarakaṃ disvā tassa bhikkhācāravattena pattacīvaraṃ pariyesamānāpi, gilānassa gilānabhesajjaṃ pariyesamānāpi, gilānameva anāthaṃ – ‘‘asukapariveṇaṃ yāhi, asukapariveṇaṃ yāhī’’ti avatvā attano attano pariveṇe paṭijaggantāpi, eko oliyamānako gantho hoti, paññavantaṃ bhikkhuṃ saṅgaṇhitvā tena taṃ ganthaṃ ukkhipāpentāpi samaggā saṅghaṃ karaṇīyāni karonti nāma.</p> <p rend="bodytext"><hi rend="bold">Apaññatta</hi>ntiādīsu navaṃ adhammikaṃ katikavattaṃ vā sikkhāpadaṃ vā bandhantā apaññattaṃ paññapenti nāma, purāṇasanthatavatthusmiṃ sāvatthiyaṃ bhikkhū viya. Uddhammaṃ ubbinayaṃ sāsanaṃ dīpentā paññattaṃ samucchindanti nāma, vassasataparinibbute bhagavati vesālikā vajjiputtakā viya. Khuddānukhuddakā pana āpattiyo sañcicca vītikkamantā yathāpaññattesu sikkhāpadesu samādāya na vattanti nāma, assajipunabbasukā viya. Navaṃ pana katikavattaṃ vā sikkhāpadaṃ vā abandhantā, dhammavinayato sāsanaṃ dīpentā, khuddānukhuddakāni sikkhāpadāni asamūhanantā apaññattaṃ na paññapenti, paññattaṃ na samucchindanti, yathāpaññattesu sikkhāpadesu samādāya vattanti nāma, āyasmā upaseno viya, āyasmā yaso kākaṇḍakaputto viya ca.</p> <hi rend="bold">Apaññatta</hi> <p rend="indent">‘‘Suṇātu, me āvuso saṅgho, santamhākaṃ sikkhāpadāni gihigatāni, gihinopi jānanti, ‘idaṃ vo samaṇānaṃ sakyaputtiyānaṃ kappati, idaṃ vo na kappatī’ti. Sace hi mayaṃ khuddānukhuddakāni sikkhāpadāni <pb ed="P" n="2.0526"/> samūhanissāma, bhavissanti vattāro – ‘dhūmakālikaṃ samaṇena gotamena sāvakānaṃ sikkhāpadaṃ paññattaṃ, yāvimesaṃ satthā aṭṭhāsi, tāvime sikkhāpadesu sikkhiṃsu. Yato imesaṃ satthā parinibbuto, na dānime sikkhāpadesu sikkhantī’ti. Yadi saṅghassa pattakallaṃ, saṅgho apaññattaṃ <pb ed="M" n="2.0116"/> na paññapeyya, paññattaṃ na samucchindeyya, yathāpaññattesu sikkhāpadesu samādāya vatteyyā’’ti (cuḷava. 442) –</p> <pb ed="P" n="2.0526"/> <pb ed="M" n="2.0116"/> <p rend="bodytext">Imaṃ tantiṃ ṭhapayanto āyasmā mahākassapo viya ca. <hi rend="bold">Vuddhiyevā</hi>ti sīlādīhi guṇehi vuḍḍhiyeva, no parihāni.</p> <hi rend="bold">Vuddhiyevā</hi> <p rend="bodytext"><hi rend="bold">Therā</hi>ti <pb ed="V" n="2.0104"/> thirabhāvappattā therakārakehi guṇehi samannāgatā. Bahū rattiyo jānantīti <hi rend="bold">rattaññū.</hi> Ciraṃ pabbajitānaṃ etesanti <hi rend="bold">cirapabbajitā.</hi> Saṅghassa pituṭṭhāne ṭhitāti <hi rend="bold">saṅghapitaro. </hi> Pituṭṭhāne ṭhitattā saṅghaṃ parinenti pubbaṅgamā hutvā tīsu sikkhāsu pavattentīti <hi rend="bold">saṅghapariṇāyakā.</hi></p> <hi rend="bold">Therā</hi> <pb ed="V" n="2.0104"/> <hi rend="bold">rattaññū.</hi> <hi rend="bold">cirapabbajitā.</hi> <hi rend="bold">saṅghapitaro. </hi> <hi rend="bold">saṅghapariṇāyakā.</hi> <p rend="bodytext">Ye tesaṃ sakkārādīni na karonti, ovādatthāya dve tayo vāre upaṭṭhānaṃ na gacchanti, tepi tesaṃ ovādaṃ na denti, paveṇīkathaṃ na kathenti, sārabhūtaṃ dhammapariyāyaṃ na sikkhāpenti. Te tehi vissaṭṭhā sīlādīhi dhammakkhandhehi sattahi ca ariyadhanehīti evamādīhi guṇehi parihāyanti. Ye pana tesaṃ sakkārādīni karonti, upaṭṭhānaṃ gacchanti, tepi tesaṃ ovādaṃ denti. ‘‘Evaṃ te abhikkamitabbaṃ, evaṃ te paṭikkamitabbaṃ, evaṃ te ālokitabbaṃ, evaṃ te vilokitabbaṃ, evaṃ te samiñjitabbaṃ, evaṃ te pasāritabbaṃ, evaṃ te saṅghāṭipattacīvaraṃ dhāretabba’’nti paveṇīkathaṃ kathenti, sārabhūtaṃ dhammapariyāyaṃ sikkhāpenti, terasahi dhutaṅgehi dasahi kathāvatthūhi anusāsanti. Te tesaṃ ovāde ṭhatvā sīlādīhi guṇehi vaḍḍhamānā sāmaññatthaṃ anupāpuṇanti. Evamettha hānivuddhiyo veditabbā.</p> <p rend="bodytext">Punabbhavadānaṃ punabbhavo, punabbhavo sīlamassāti ponobbhavikā, punabbhavadāyikāti attho, tasmā <hi rend="bold">ponobbhavikāya. Na vasaṃ gacchantī</hi>ti ettha ye catunnaṃ paccayānaṃ kāraṇā upaṭṭhākānaṃ padānupadikā hutvā gāmato gāmaṃ vicaranti, te tassā taṇhāya vasaṃ gacchanti nāma, itare na gacchanti <pb ed="P" n="2.0527"/> nāma. Tattha hānivuddhiyo pākaṭāyeva.</p> <hi rend="bold">ponobbhavikāya. Na vasaṃ gacchantī</hi> <pb ed="P" n="2.0527"/> <p rend="bodytext"><hi rend="bold">Āraññakesū</hi>ti pañcadhanusatikapacchimesu. <hi rend="bold">Sāpekkhā</hi>ti sataṇhā sālayā. Gāmantasenāsanesu hi jhānaṃ appetvāpi tato vuṭṭhitamattova itthipurisadārikādisaddaṃ suṇāti, yenassa adhigatavisesopi hāyatiyeva. Araññe pana niddāyitvā paṭibuddhamatto sīhabyagghamorādīnaṃ saddaṃ <pb ed="M" n="2.0117"/> suṇāti, yena āraññakaṃ pītiṃ labhitvā tameva sammasanto aggaphale patiṭṭhāti. Iti bhagavā gāmantasenāsane jhānaṃ appetvā nisinnabhikkhuno araññe niddāyantameva pasaṃsati. Tasmā tameva atthavasaṃ paṭicca – ‘‘āraññakesu senāsanesu sāpekkhā bhavissantī’’ti āha.</p> <hi rend="bold">Āraññakesū</hi> <hi rend="bold">Sāpekkhā</hi> <pb ed="M" n="2.0117"/> <p rend="bodytext"><hi rend="bold">Paccattaññeva satiṃ upaṭṭhapessantī</hi>ti attanāva attano abbhantare satiṃ upaṭṭhapessanti. <hi rend="bold">Pesalā</hi>ti piyasīlā. Idhāpi sabrahmacārīnaṃ āgamanaṃ anicchantā nevāsikā assaddhā honti appasannā <pb ed="V" n="2.0105"/>. Sampattabhikkhūnaṃ paccuggamanapattacīvarappaṭiggahaṇaāsanapaññāpanatālavaṇṭaggahaṇādīni na karonti, atha nesaṃ avaṇṇo uggacchati – ‘‘asukavihāravāsino bhikkhū assaddhā appasannā vihāraṃ paviṭṭhānaṃ vattapaṭivattaṃ na karontī’’ti. Taṃ sutvā pabbajitā vihāradvārena gacchantāpi vihāraṃ na pavisanti. Evaṃ anāgatānaṃ anāgamanameva hoti. Āgatānaṃ pana phāsuvihāre asati yepi ajānitvā āgatā, te – ‘‘vasissāmāti tāva cintetvā āgatāmha, imesaṃ pana nevāsikānaṃ iminā nīhārena ko vasissatī’’ti nikkhamitvā gacchanti. Evaṃ so vihāro aññesaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ anāvāsova hoti. Tato nevāsikā sīlavantānaṃ dassanaṃ alabhantā kaṅkhāvinodanaṃ vā ācārasikkhāpakaṃ vā madhuradhammassavanaṃ vā na labhanti, tesaṃ neva aggahitadhammaggahaṇaṃ, na gahitasajjhāyakaraṇaṃ hoti. Iti nesaṃ hāniyeva hoti, na vuddhi.</p> <hi rend="bold">Paccattaññeva satiṃ upaṭṭhapessantī</hi> <hi rend="bold">Pesalā</hi> <pb ed="V" n="2.0105"/> <p rend="bodytext">Ye pana sabrahmacārīnaṃ āgamanaṃ icchanti, te saddhā honti pasannā, āgatānaṃ sabrahmacārīnaṃ paccuggamanādīni katvā senāsanaṃ paññapetvā denti, te gahetvā bhikkhācāraṃ pavisanti, kaṅkhaṃ vinodenti, madhuradhammassavanaṃ labhanti. Atha nesaṃ kittisaddo uggacchati – ‘‘asukavihārabhikkhū evaṃ saddhā pasannā vattasampannā saṅgāhakā’’ti. Taṃ sutvā bhikkhū dūratopi enti, tesaṃ nevāsikā vattaṃ karonti <pb ed="P" n="2.0528"/>, samīpaṃ āgantvā vuḍḍhataraṃ āgantukaṃ vanditvā nisīdanti, navakatarassa santike āsanaṃ gahetvā nisīdanti. Nisīditvā – ‘‘imasmiṃ vihāre vasissatha gamissathā’’ti pucchanti. ‘Gamissāmī’ti vutte – ‘‘sappāyaṃ senāsanaṃ, sulabhā bhikkhā’’tiādīni vatvā gantuṃ na denti. Vinayadharo ce hoti, tassa santike vinayaṃ sajjhāyanti. Suttantādidharo ce, tassa santike taṃ taṃ dhammaṃ sajjhāyanti. Āgantukānaṃ therānaṃ ovāde ṭhatvā saha paṭisambhidāhi arahattaṃ pāpuṇanti. Āgantukā ‘‘ekaṃ <pb ed="M" n="2.0118"/> dve divasāni vasissāmāti āgatāmha, imesaṃ pana sukhasaṃvāsatāya dasadvādasavassāni vasissāmā’’ti vattāro honti. Evamettha hānivuddhiyo veditabbā.</p> <pb ed="P" n="2.0528"/> <pb ed="M" n="2.0118"/>
136. Then, shortly after the Blessed One had departed… Having assembled [the monks], meaning having sent those with psychic powers to monasteries far away, and having gone to nearby monasteries himself, he assembled them, [saying]: “Assemble, venerable ones; the Blessed One desires a gathering of you.”

Aparīhāniye means “not declining,” meaning productive of growth, this is the meaning.

Dhamme desessāmī means, as if causing a thousand moons and a thousand suns to rise, as if lighting a thousand oil lamps inside a four-walled house, having made it clear, I will speak.

There, abhiṇhaṃ sannipātā means this is just like what was said regarding the Vajjis.

And here too, those who do not frequently assemble do not hear the teaching that has come to the (various) districts.

Therefore, [they] do not know the following: “The boundary of such and such a monastery is confused, the *uposatha* and *pavāraṇā* are not properly established, in such and such a place the monks are doing medical work, messenger work, etc., they maintain their livelihood through many requests, by means of flower offerings, etc.” Even the wicked monks, having known that “the Saṅgha of monks is negligent,” and having become numerous, push the Teaching aside.

But those who frequently assemble hear that and that event. Therefore, having sent a Saṅgha of monks, they straighten the boundary, they cause the *uposatha*, *pavāraṇā*, etc. to be maintained, having sent noble-lineage monks to the place where wrong livelihoods have arisen, they cause a noble-lineage talk to be given, they cause the wicked monks to be disciplined by Vinaya-holders. Even the wicked monks, [thinking,] “the Saṅgha of monks is not negligent, it is not possible for us to live with group-attachments,” having broken apart, they flee.

Thus, here, decline and growth should be understood.

Abhiṇhaṃ sannipātā samaggā means, in the case of those who wish to establish a custom regarding the restoration of *cetiya*s, or regarding the covering of the Bodhi-tree house, or the *uposatha* hall, or who wish to give advice: “Let the Saṅgha assemble!” [When] a drum or a bell has been struck, those who create distraction, [saying,] “I have robe-making work, my bowl must be cooked, I have new work,” are not called “assembling harmoniously.”

But having put aside all that work, those who assemble, [thinking,] “I [will be] earlier, I [will be] earlier,” with a single striking, are called “assembling harmoniously.”

But those who have assembled, having considered and deliberated what should be done, having done it, those who do not rise up from one place are not called “rising up harmoniously.”

For when they have risen up in this way, this is what happens to those who go first: “We have only heard outer talk, now there will be talk of resolution.”

But those who rise up with a single striking are called “rising up harmoniously.”

Moreover, having heard that “in such and such a place the boundary of the monastery is confused, the *uposatha* and *pavāraṇā* are not properly established, in such and such a place wicked monks who do medical work, etc. have arisen,” and [thinking,] “who will go and discipline them?” When [this] has been said, those who go, [saying,] “I [will go] first, I [will go] first,” are called “rising up harmoniously.”

Samaggā Having seen a newcomer, even those who, without saying, “Go to this dwelling, go to that dwelling, who is this?”, all do their duty, having seen an old, leaf-robe, even those who search for a bowl-robe with the alms-wandering duty for him, even those who search for medicine for a sick person, even those who, without saying to a sick, helpless person, “Go to such and such a dwelling, go to such and such a dwelling,” care for him in their own dwelling, even when there is a single, sinking book, having gathered a wise monk, even those who cause him to lift up that book, are called “doing the Saṅgha’s duties harmoniously.”

Apaññatta means, in the case of those who, in the ādi sūtras, binding a new, unlawful customary practice or training rule, enact what has not been enacted, like the monks in Savatthi regarding the old bedding-material.

Those who, illuminating the Teaching by means of what is not the Dharma and what is not the Vinaya, completely cut off what has been enacted are called the Vesālika Vajjiputtakas in the Blessed One’s hundredth year after his parinirvāṇa.

But those who, intentionally transgressing the minor and sub-minor offenses, without undertaking it, do not conduct themselves according to the training rules as they have been enacted, are called Assaji and Punabbasukā.

But those who, without binding a new customary practice or training rule, illuminating the Teaching according to the Dharma and Vinaya, without uprooting the minor and sub-minor training rules, do not enact what has not been enacted, do not completely cut off what has been enacted, undertaking the training rules as they have been enacted, conduct themselves [accordingly], are called the venerable Upasena, the venerable Yasa Kākaṇḍakaputta, and others.

Apaññatta “Let the Saṅgha listen to me, friends. Our training rules have gone to the householders, even the householders know, ‘this is suitable for you ascetics, Sakya-sons, this is not suitable for you.’

If we were to uproot the minor and sub-minor training rules, there will be speakers [saying]: ‘The ascetic Gotama enacted a smoke-time training rule for his disciples; as long as their teacher remained, they trained themselves in the training rules.

Since their teacher has attained parinirvāṇa, they no longer train themselves in the training rules.’

If it is agreeable to the Saṅgha, the Saṅgha should not enact what has not been enacted, should not completely cut off what has been enacted, should conduct themselves undertaking the training rules as they have been enacted,” (Culavagga 442) –

The venerable Mahākassapa also established this thread.

Vuddhiyevā means growth alone by means of the qualities beginning with morality, not decline.

Vuddhiyevā therā means those who have attained a stable state, who are endowed with qualities that make [one] a *thera*.
Knowing many nights, therefore, *rattaññū*.
These have been long ordained, therefore, *cirapabbajitā*.
Standing in the place of the Sangha's nourishment, therefore, *saṅghapitaro*.
Because they stand in the place of nourishment, they lead the Sangha, being foremost in setting forth the three trainings, therefore, *saṅghapariṇāyakā*.

*Theras*, *rattaññūs*, *cirapabbajitas*, *saṅghapitaros*, *saṅghapariṇāyakas*.

Those who do not show respect, etc., to them, do not approach to attend them for instruction two or three times, do not give them advice, do not tell traditional stories, do not teach the essence of the Dharma.
