They, separated from those, decline in qualities such as virtue, etc., the aggregates of the Dharma, and the seven noble riches.
But those who show respect, etc., to them, approach to attend them, give them advice.
"Thus you should go forward, thus you should go back, thus you should look, thus you should gaze, thus you should draw in, thus you should stretch out, thus you should wear the double-layered robe and bowl," they tell traditional stories, teach the essence of the Dharma, instruct with the thirteen ascetic practices and the ten topics of discussion.
They, standing in their advice, growing in qualities such as virtue, etc., attain the goal of the monastic life.
Thus, here, decline and growth should be understood.

Giving rebirth is rebirth; rebirth is their virtue, therefore, *ponobbhavikā*, the meaning is "giver of rebirth," therefore, to the *ponobbhavika*.
"They do not go to dependence," here, those who wander from village to village as attendants for the sake of the four requisites, they go to dependence on that craving, the others do not go.
There, decline and growth are evident.

To the *ponobbhavika*.
"They do not go to dependence."
"*Āraññakesū*" means in the westernmost places five-bow lengths away.
"*Sāpekkhā*" means with craving, with attachment.
For in village-bordering dwelling places, even if one puts aside meditation, as soon as one has arisen from it, one hears the sound of women, men, girls, etc., by which even the special attainment one has gained declines.
But in the forest, having slept and as soon as one has awoken, one hears the sound of lions, tigers, peacocks, etc., by which, having gained forest delight, contemplating just that, one is established in the highest fruit.
Thus, the Blessed One praises the monk sitting in a village-bordering dwelling place having put aside meditation, but only sleeping in the forest.
Therefore, relying on just that meaningfulness, he said, "In forest dwelling places and dwelling places, they will be dependent."

"*Āraññakesū*, *sāpekkhā*."
"*Paccattaññeva satiṃ upaṭṭhapessantī*" means they establish mindfulness within themselves, by themselves.
"*Pesalā*" means with beloved virtue.
Here too, unwilling to come near their fellow ব্রহ্মcarīs, the residents are faithless and displeased.
They do not do welcoming, taking bowls and robes, preparing seats, taking palm leaves, etc., for the monks who have arrived, but rather dispraise arises about them: "The monks residing in such-and-such a monastery are faithless and displeased, they do not do what is proper for those who have entered the monastery."
Having heard that, even going by the monastery gate, the ordained do not enter the monastery.
Thus, for those who have not come, there is just not coming.
But for those who have come, if there is no comfortable dwelling place, even those who have come unknowingly, "Thinking that we would live here, we have come, but who would live with such ill treatment from these residents?" they depart and leave.
Thus, that monastery is just uninhabitable for other monks.
Then the residents, not gaining a sight of virtuous ones, do not gain dispelling of doubt, teaching of conduct, or hearing of sweet Dharma; for them, there is neither grasping of ungrasped Dharma, nor doing recitation of what has been grasped.
Thus there is only decline for them, not growth.Maintaining mindfulness for oneself, they are skilled.

Moreover, those who desire the arrival of their fellow *brahmacārins*, they are faithful and pleased, and having made welcoming gestures and so forth for the arrived *brahmacārins*, they prepare a seat and give it. Taking it, they enter for alms, dispel doubt, and obtain the hearing of sweet *dharma*.

Then their sound of fame goes forth: "The *bhikṣus* of such-and-such *vihāra* are thus faithful, pleased, accomplished in duties, and receptive."

Having heard that, *bhikṣus* come even from afar, and the residents perform their duties for them, and having come near, they respectfully salute the elder newcomer and sit down; near the newer one, having taken a seat, they sit down.

Having sat down, they ask, "Will you dwell in this *vihāra*, or will you depart?"

If [one] says, "I will depart," they say, "The lodging is suitable, alms are easy to obtain," and so forth, and do not allow [him] to leave.

If he is a master of the *Vinaya*, they recite the *Vinaya* in his presence.

If he is a master of the *Sūtrānta* and so forth, they recite that *dharma* in his presence.

Having stood in the instruction of the elder newcomers, together with the *pratisaṃbhidās*, they attain *Arhatship*.

The newcomers say, "We have come [intending to] dwell one or two days, but due to the pleasant association with these [monks], we will dwell ten or twelve years," thus they are speakers.

Thus here, decrease and increase should be understood.
137
<p n="137" rend="bodytext"><hi rend="paranum">137</hi><hi rend="dot">.</hi> ‘‘Aparepi <pb ed="T" n="2.0092"/><pb ed="M" n="2.0066"/> vo, bhikkhave, satta aparihāniye dhamme desessāmi, taṃ suṇātha, sādhukaṃ <pb ed="V" n="2.0061"/> manasikarotha, bhāsissāmī’’ti. ‘‘Evaṃ, bhante’’ti kho te bhikkhū bhagavato paccassosuṃ. Bhagavā etadavoca –</p> <p rend="bodytext">‘‘Yāvakīvañca, bhikkhave, bhikkhū na kammārāmā bhavissanti <pb ed="P" n="2.0078"/> na kammaratā na kammārāmatamanuyuttā, vuddhiyeva, bhikkhave, bhikkhūnaṃ pāṭikaṅkhā, no parihāni.</p> <pb ed="P" n="2.0078"/> <p rend="bodytext">‘‘Yāvakīvañca, bhikkhave, bhikkhū na bhassārāmā bhavissanti na bhassaratā na bhassārāmatamanuyuttā, vuddhiyeva, bhikkhave, bhikkhūnaṃ pāṭikaṅkhā, no parihāni.</p> <p rend="bodytext">‘‘Yāvakīvañca, bhikkhave, bhikkhū na niddārāmā bhavissanti na niddāratā na niddārāmatamanuyuttā, vuddhiyeva, bhikkhave, bhikkhūnaṃ pāṭikaṅkhā, no parihāni.</p> <p rend="bodytext">‘‘Yāvakīvañca, bhikkhave, bhikkhū na saṅgaṇikārāmā bhavissanti na saṅgaṇikaratā na saṅgaṇikārāmatamanuyuttā, vuddhiyeva, bhikkhave, bhikkhūnaṃ pāṭikaṅkhā, no parihāni.</p> <p rend="bodytext">‘‘Yāvakīvañca, bhikkhave, bhikkhū na pāpicchā bhavissanti na pāpikānaṃ icchānaṃ vasaṃ gatā, vuddhiyeva, bhikkhave, bhikkhūnaṃ pāṭikaṅkhā, no parihāni.</p> <p rend="bodytext">‘‘Yāvakīvañca, bhikkhave, bhikkhū na pāpamittā bhavissanti na pāpasahāyā na pāpasampavaṅkā, vuddhiyeva, bhikkhave, bhikkhūnaṃ pāṭikaṅkhā, no parihāni.</p> <p rend="bodytext">‘‘Yāvakīvañca, bhikkhave, bhikkhū na oramattakena visesādhigamena antarāvosānaṃ āpajjissanti, vuddhiyeva, bhikkhave, bhikkhūnaṃ pāṭikaṅkhā, no parihāni.</p> <p rend="bodytext">‘‘Yāvakīvañca, bhikkhave, ime satta aparihāniyā dhammā bhikkhūsu <pb ed="T" n="2.0093"/> ṭhassanti, imesu ca sattasu aparihāniyesu dhammesu bhikkhū sandississanti, vuddhiyeva, bhikkhave, bhikkhūnaṃ pāṭikaṅkhā, no parihāni.</p> <pb ed="T" n="2.0093"/>
137. Furthermore, monks, I will teach you the seven conditions of non-decline (*aparihāṇiya dharma*). Listen to them, pay close attention, and bear them in mind."

"Yes, Lord," the monks replied to the Blessed One (*bhagavān*).

The Blessed One said: "As long as, monks, the monks are not delighted in activities (*kammārāmā*), are not fond of activities (*kammaratā*), and are not devoted to delighting in activities (*kammārāmatamanuyuttā*), growth (*vuddhi*) is to be expected for the monks, not decline (*parihāṇi*).

As long as, monks, the monks are not delighted in idle talk (*bhassārāmā*), are not fond of idle talk (*bhassaratā*), and are not devoted to delighting in idle talk (*bhassārāmatamanuyuttā*), growth (*vuddhi*) is to be expected for the monks, not decline (*parihāṇi*).

As long as, monks, the monks are not delighted in sleeping (*niddārāmā*), are not fond of sleeping (*niddāratā*), and are not devoted to delighting in sleeping (*niddārāmatamanuyuttā*), growth (*vuddhi*) is to be expected for the monks, not decline (*parihāṇi*).

As long as, monks, the monks are not delighted in company (*saṅgaṇikārāmā*), are not fond of company (*saṅgaṇikaratā*), and are not devoted to delighting in company (*saṅgaṇikārāmatamanuyuttā*), growth (*vuddhi*) is to be expected for the monks, not decline (*parihāṇi*).

As long as, monks, the monks are not of evil desires (*pāpicchā*), and are not under the control of evil desires (*pāpikānaṃ icchānaṃ vasaṃ gatā*), growth (*vuddhi*) is to be expected for the monks, not decline (*parihāṇi*).

As long as, monks, the monks do not have evil friends (*pāpamittā*), evil companions (*pāpasahāyā*), and evil comrades (*pāpasampavaṅkā*), growth (*vuddhi*) is to be expected for the monks, not decline (*parihāṇi*).

As long as, monks, the monks do not stop halfway with some trifling achievement (*oramattakena visesādhigamena antarāvosānaṃ āpajjissanti*), growth (*vuddhi*) is to be expected for the monks, not decline (*parihāṇi*).

As long as, monks, these seven conditions of non-decline (*aparihāṇiyā dhammā*) endure among the monks (*bhikkhūsu*), and the monks are known for these seven conditions of non-decline (*aparihāniyesu dhammesu*), growth (*vuddhi*) is to be expected for the monks, not decline (*parihāṇi*)."
<p n="137" rend="bodytext"><hi rend="paranum">137</hi><hi rend="dot">.</hi> Dutiyasattake kammaṃ ārāmo etesanti <hi rend="bold">kammārāmā</hi>ti. Kamme ratāti <hi rend="bold">kammaratā. Kammārāmatamanuyuttā</hi>ti yuttā payuttā anuyuttā. Tattha <hi rend="bold">kamma</hi>nti itikātabbakammaṃ vuccati. Seyyathidaṃ – cīvaravicāraṇaṃ, cīvarakaraṇaṃ, upatthambhanaṃ, sūcigharaṃ, pattatthavikaṃ, asaṃbaddhakaṃ, kāyabandhanaṃ, dhamakaraṇaṃ, ādhārakaṃ, pādakathalikaṃ, sammajjanīādīnaṃ karaṇanti. Ekacco hi etāni karonto sakaladivasaṃ etāneva karoti. Taṃ sandhāyesa paṭikkhepo. Yo pana etesaṃ karaṇavelāyameva etāni karoti, uddesavelāyaṃ uddesaṃ gaṇhāti, sajjhāyavelāyaṃ sajjhāyati, cetiyaṅgaṇavattavelāyaṃ <pb ed="V" n="2.0106"/> cetiyaṅgaṇavattaṃ karoti, manasikāravelāyaṃ manasikāraṃ karoti, na so kammārāmo nāma.</p> <p rend="bodytext"><hi rend="bold">Na bhassārāmā</hi>ti ettha yo itthivaṇṇapurisavaṇṇādivasena ālāpasallāpaṃ karontoyeva divasañca rattiñca vītināmeti, evarūpe bhasse pariyantakārī na hoti, ayaṃ bhassārāmo nāma. Yo pana rattindivaṃ dhammaṃ katheti, pañhaṃ vissajjeti, ayaṃ appabhassova bhasse pariyantakārīyeva. Kasmā? ‘‘Sannipatitānaṃ vo, bhikkhave, dvayaṃ karaṇīyaṃ – dhammī vā kathā, ariyo vā tuṇhībhāvo’’ti (ma. ni. 1.273) vuttattā.</p> <hi rend="bold">Na bhassārāmā</hi> <p rend="bodytext"><hi rend="bold">Na niddārāmā</hi>ti ettha yo gacchantopi nisinnopi nipannopi thinamiddhābhibhūto niddāyatiyeva, ayaṃ niddārāmo nāma. Yassa pana karajakāyagelaññena cittaṃ bhavaṅge otarati <pb ed="P" n="2.0529"/>, nāyaṃ niddārāmo. Tenevāha – ‘‘abhijānāmahaṃ aggivessana, gimhānaṃ pacchime māse pacchābhattaṃ piṇḍapātappaṭikkanto catugguṇaṃ saṅghāṭiṃ paññapetvā dakkhiṇena passena sato sampajāno niddaṃ okkamitā’’ti (ma. ni. 1.387).</p> <hi rend="bold">Na niddārāmā</hi> <pb ed="P" n="2.0529"/> <p rend="bodytext"><hi rend="bold">Na saṅgaṇikārāmā</hi>ti ettha yo ekassa dutiyo dvinnaṃ tatiyo tiṇṇaṃ catutthoti evaṃ saṃsaṭṭhova viharati, ekako assādaṃ na labhati, ayaṃ saṅgaṇikārāmo. Yo pana catūsu iriyāpathesu ekako assādaṃ labhati, nāyaṃ saṅgaṇikārāmoti veditabbo.</p> <hi rend="bold">Na saṅgaṇikārāmā</hi> <p rend="bodytext"><hi rend="bold">Na</hi><pb ed="M" n="2.0119"/><hi rend="bold">pāpicchā</hi>ti ettha asantasambhāvanāya icchāya samannāgatā dussīlā pāpicchā nāma.</p> <hi rend="bold">Na</hi> <pb ed="M" n="2.0119"/> <hi rend="bold">pāpicchā</hi> <p rend="bodytext"><hi rend="bold">Na pāpamittā</hi>dīsu pāpā mittā etesanti <hi rend="bold">pāpamittā. </hi> Catūsu iriyāpathesu saha ayanato pāpā sahāyā etesanti <hi rend="bold">pāpasahāyā.</hi> Tanninnatappoṇatappabbhāratāya pāpesu sampavaṅkāti <hi rend="bold">pāpasampavaṅkā.</hi></p> <hi rend="bold">Na pāpamittā</hi> <hi rend="bold">pāpamittā. </hi> <hi rend="bold">pāpasahāyā.</hi> <hi rend="bold">pāpasampavaṅkā.</hi> <p rend="bodytext"><hi rend="bold">Oramattakenā</hi>ti avaramattakena appamattakena. <hi rend="bold">Antarā</hi>ti arahattaṃ apatvāva etthantare. <hi rend="bold">Vosāna</hi>nti pariniṭṭhitabhāvaṃ – ‘‘alamettāvatā’’ti osakkanaṃ ṭhitakiccataṃ. Idaṃ vuttaṃ hoti – ‘‘yāva sīlapārisuddhimattena vā vipassanāmattena vā jhānamattena vā sotāpannabhāvamattena vā sakadāgāmibhāvamattena vā anāgāmibhāvamattena vā vosānaṃ na āpajjissanti, tāva vuddhiyeva bhikkhūnaṃ pāṭikaṅkhā, no parihānī’’ti.</p> <hi rend="bold">Oramattakenā</hi> <hi rend="bold">Antarā</hi> <hi rend="bold">Vosāna</hi>
137. In the second group, *kammārāmā* means those who delight in action, thinking, "Action is our garden."

*Kammaratā* means those who are fond of action.

*Kammārāmatamanuyuttā* means those who are engaged in being yoked, practiced, and applied to action.

There, *kamma* means that which should be done, that is, action is spoken of.

Specifically, these are: attending to robes (*cīvaravicāraṇa*), making robes (*cīvarakaraṇa*), supporting, a needle case (*sūcighara*), a bowl stand (*pattatthavika*), that which is unbound (*asaṃbaddhaka*), a body binding (*kāyabandhana*), making a water strainer (*dhama-karaṇa*), a stand (*ādhāraka*), a footstool (*pādakathalika*), making a broom (*sammajjanī*), and so on.

Someone who, while doing these, spends the entire day doing just these.

This is a refutation aimed at that.

However, one who at the time of doing these actions does them, at the time of learning, learns, at the time of reciting, recites, at the time of attending to the monastery courtyard, attends to the monastery courtyard, at the time of mental application, applies the mind, that one is not called *kammārāma*.

*Na bhassārāmā* means that one who, here, by way of talk with women, talk with men, and so forth, just spends the day and the night in idle chatter, in such idle talk, there is no limit-maker, this one is called *bhassārāma*.

However, one who speaks the Dharma day and night, answers questions, that one is of little idle talk and is a limit-maker in idle talk.

Why? Because it was said, "When you have gathered together, monks, two things should be done: either Dhamma talk or noble silence" (M.Ni. 1.273).

*Na bhassārāmā. Na niddārāmā* means that one who, here, whether going, sitting, or lying down, being overcome by sloth and torpor, just sleeps, this one is called *niddārāma*.

However, one whose mind falls into the life-continuum (*bhavaṅga*) due to bodily sickness, that one is not *niddārāma*.

Therefore, he said, "I recall, Aggivessana, in the last month of the hot season, on returning from my almsround, after my meal I lay out my outer robe folded in four, and lying down on my right side, I fall asleep mindful and fully aware" (M.Ni. 1.387).

*Na niddārāmā. Na saṅgaṇikārāmā* means that one who, here, one for one, a second for two, a third for three, a fourth for four, thus entangled, lives, not obtaining pleasure alone, this one is *saṅgaṇikārāma*.

However, one who in the four postures obtains pleasure alone, that one should be understood as not *saṅgaṇikārāma*.

*Na saṅgaṇikārāmā. Na pāpicchā* means that one who, here, is endowed with desire based on improper imagination, is immoral, that one is called *pāpicchā*.

*Na pāpicchā. Na pāpamittā* means that among the *pāpamittā* and so forth, the evil friends of these are the *pāpamittā*.

In the four postures, along with the going, the evil companions of these are the *pāpasahāyā*.

Due to their inclination, bent, and tendency toward that, they are inclined towards evil, they are *pāpasampavaṅkā*.

*Na pāpamittā. pāpamittā. pāpasahāyā. pāpasampavaṅkā.*

*Oramattakenā* means by inferior measure, by small measure.

*Antarā* means in the middle of this, before attaining Arhatship.

*Vosāna* means the state of being completely finished – "Enough, mendicants!" – the abandoning [of exertion], the task being established.

This was said: "As long as they do not reach completion by way of mere purity of virtue, by way of mere insight, by way of mere absorption, by way of mere stream-entry, by way of mere once-returning, or by way of mere non-returning, so long is growth alone to be expected of the monks, not decline."

*Oramattakenā antarā vosāna.*
138
<p n="138" rend="bodytext"><hi rend="paranum">138</hi><hi rend="dot">.</hi> ‘‘Aparepi vo, bhikkhave, satta aparihāniye dhamme desessāmi…pe… ‘‘yāvakīvañca, bhikkhave, bhikkhū saddhā bhavissanti…pe… hirimanā bhavissanti… ottappī bhavissanti… <pb ed="V" n="2.0062"/> bahussutā bhavissanti… <pb ed="P" n="2.0079"/> āraddhavīriyā bhavissanti… upaṭṭhitassatī <pb ed="M" n="2.0067"/> bhavissanti… paññavanto bhavissanti, vuddhiyeva, bhikkhave, bhikkhūnaṃ pāṭikaṅkhā, no parihāni. Yāvakīvañca, bhikkhave, ime satta aparihāniyā dhammā bhikkhūsu ṭhassanti, imesu ca sattasu aparihāniyesu dhammesu bhikkhū sandississanti, vuddhiyeva, bhikkhave, bhikkhūnaṃ pāṭikaṅkhā, no parihāni.</p>
“Furthermore, monks, I will teach you seven conditions that lead to no decline…pe… As long as the monks have faith (*śraddhā*)…pe… have a sense of shame (*hrīmanā*), have moral dread (*otāppī*), are very learned (*bahussutā*), have aroused vigor (*āraddhavīriyā*), have mindfulness established (*upaṭṭhitassatī*), and are wise (*prajñāvantah*), then monks, only growth is to be expected for the monks, not decline. As long as these seven conditions leading to no decline endure among the monks, and the monks are seen to possess these seven conditions leading to no decline, then monks, only growth is to be expected for the monks, not decline.
<p n="138" rend="bodytext"><hi rend="paranum">138</hi><hi rend="dot">.</hi> Tatiyasattake <pb ed="V" n="2.0107"/><hi rend="bold">saddhā</hi>ti saddhāsampannā. Tattha āgamanīyasaddhā, adhigamasaddhā, pasādasaddhā, okappanasaddhāti catubbidhā saddhā. Tattha <hi rend="bold">āgamanīyasaddhā</hi> sabbaññubodhisattānaṃ hoti. <hi rend="bold">Adhigamasaddhā</hi> ariyapuggalānaṃ. Buddho dhammo saṅghoti vutte pana pasādo <hi rend="bold">pasādasaddhā.</hi> Okappetvā pakappetvā pana saddahanaṃ <hi rend="bold">okappanasaddhā.</hi> Sā duvidhāpi idhādhippetā. Tāya hi saddhāya samannāgato saddhāvimutto, vakkalittherasadiso hoti. Tassa hi cetiyaṅgaṇavattaṃ vā, bodhiyaṅgaṇavattaṃ vā katameva hoti. Upajjhāyavattaācariyavattādīni sabbavattāni pūreti. <hi rend="bold">Hirimanā</hi>ti pāpajigucchanalakkhaṇāya hiriyā yuttacittā. <hi rend="bold">Ottappī</hi>ti pāpato bhāyanalakkhaṇena ottappena samannāgatā.</p> <p rend="bodytext"><hi rend="bold">Bahussutā</hi>ti ettha pana pariyattibahussuto, paṭivedhabahussutoti <pb ed="P" n="2.0530"/> dve bahussutā. <hi rend="bold">Pariyattī</hi>ti tīṇi piṭakāni. <hi rend="bold">Paṭivedho</hi>ti saccappaṭivedho. Imasmiṃ pana ṭhāne pariyatti adhippetā. Sā yena bahu sutā, so bahussuto. So panesa nissayamuccanako, parisupaṭṭhāko, bhikkhunovādako, sabbatthakabahussutoti catubbidho hoti. Tattha tayo bahussutā samantapāsādikāya vinayaṭṭhakathāya ovādavagge vuttanayena gahetabbā. Sabbatthakabahussutā pana ānandattherasadisā honti. Te idha adhippetā.</p> <hi rend="bold">Bahussutā</hi> <pb ed="P" n="2.0530"/> <hi rend="bold">Pariyattī</hi> <hi rend="bold">Paṭivedho</hi> <p rend="bodytext"><hi rend="bold">Āraddhavīriyā</hi>ti <pb ed="M" n="2.0120"/> yesaṃ kāyikañca cetasikañca vīriyaṃ āraddhaṃ hoti. Tattha ye kāyasaṅgaṇikaṃ vinodetvā catūsu iriyāpathesu aṭṭhaārabbhavatthuvasena ekakā honti, tesaṃ kāyikavīriyaṃ āraddhaṃ nāma hoti. Ye cittasaṅgāṇikaṃ vinodetvā aṭṭhasamāpattivasena ekakā honti, gamane uppannakilesassa ṭhānaṃ pāpuṇituṃ na denti, ṭhāne uppannakilesassa nisajjaṃ, nisajjāya uppannakilesassa sayanaṃ pāpuṇituṃ na denti, uppannuppannaṭṭhāneyeva kilese niggaṇhanti, tesaṃ cetasikavīriyaṃ āraddhaṃ nāma hoti.</p> <hi rend="bold">Āraddhavīriyā</hi> <pb ed="M" n="2.0120"/> <p rend="bodytext"><hi rend="bold">Upaṭṭhitassatī</hi>ti cirakatādīnaṃ saritā anussaritā mahāgatimbayaabhayattheradīghabhāṇaabhayattheratipiṭakacūḷābhayattherā viya. Mahāgatimbayaabhayatthero kira jātapañcamadivase maṅgalapāyāse tuṇḍaṃ pasārentaṃ vāyasaṃ disvā huṃ hunti saddamakāsi. Atha so therakāle – ‘‘kadā paṭṭhāya, bhante, sarathā’’ti bhikkhūhi pucchito ‘‘jātapañcamadivase katasaddato paṭṭhāya āvuso’’ti āha.</p> <hi rend="bold">Upaṭṭhitassatī</hi> <p rend="bodytext">Dīghabhāṇakaabhayattherassa jātanavamadivase mātā cumbissāmīti onatā tassā moḷi muccittha <pb ed="V" n="2.0108"/>. Tato tumbamattāni sumanapupphāni dārakassa ure patitvā dukkhaṃ janayiṃsu. So therakāle – ‘‘kadā paṭṭhāya, bhante, sarathā’’ti pucchito – ‘‘jātanavamadivasato paṭṭhāyā’’ti āha.</p> <pb ed="V" n="2.0108"/> <p rend="bodytext">Tipiṭakacūḷābhayatthero – ‘‘anurādhapure tīṇi dvārāni pidahāpetvā manussānaṃ ekena dvārena nikkhamanaṃ katvā – ‘tvaṃ kinnāmo, tvaṃ kinnāmo’ti pucchitvā sāyaṃ puna apucchitvāva tesaṃ nāmāni sampaṭicchāpetuṃ – ‘‘sakkā āvuso’’ti āha. Evarūpe bhikkhū sandhāya – ‘‘upaṭṭhitassatī’’ti vuttaṃ.</p> <p rend="bodytext"><hi rend="bold">Paññavanto</hi>ti pañcannaṃ khandhānaṃ udayabbayapariggāhikāya paññāya samannāgatā. Api ca dvīhipi etehi padehi vipassakānaṃ <pb ed="P" n="2.0531"/> bhikkhūnaṃ vipassanāsambhārabhūtā sammāsati ceva vipassanāpaññā ca kathitā.</p> <hi rend="bold">Paññavanto</hi> <pb ed="P" n="2.0531"/>
138. In the third *sattaka*, “*saddhā*” means possessing *saddhā*. There, *āgamanīyasaddhā*, *adhigamasaddhā*, *pasādasaddhā*, *okappanasaddhā* are the four kinds of *saddhā*. There, *āgamanīyasaddhā* is for the all-knowing bodhisattvas. *Adhigamasaddhā* is for the noble individuals (*āryapudgala*). When it is said, “Buddha, Dharma, Sangha,” the satisfaction is *pasādasaddhā*. But believing after deciding and determining is *okappanasaddhā*. Both of these are intended here. Endowed with that *saddhā*, one who is liberated by faith is like Vakkalitthera. For him, the duty to the *cetiya* courtyard or the *bodhi* courtyard, whichever it may be, is fulfilled. He fulfills all duties, such as the duty to the preceptor (*upādhyāya*), the duty to the teacher (*ācārya*), and so on. "*Hirimanā*" means having a mind endowed with *hirī*, which is characterized by abhorrence of evil. "*Ottappī*" means endowed with *ottappa*, which is characterized by fear of evil.

"*Bahussutā*" Here, however, there are two *bahussutā*: one who is learned in the texts (*pariyattibahussuto*) and one who is learned in realization (*paṭivedhabahussuto*). *Pariyatti* means the three baskets (*piṭaka*). *Paṭivedho* means the realization of the truth (*saccappaṭivedho*). But in this instance, *pariyatti* is intended. He by whom much is heard is *bahussuto*. But this one is of four kinds: one who abandons reliance, one who attends to the assembly, one who advises monks, and one who is a *sabbatthakabahussuto*. There, the three *bahussutā* should be understood in the manner stated in the chapter on advice (*ovādavagga*) in the *vinayaṭṭhakathā* called *Samantapāsādika*. But the *sabbatthakabahussutā* are like Ānandatthera. These are intended here.

"*Āraddhavīriyā*" Those whose bodily and mental *vīriya* is aroused. There, those who, having dispelled association with the body and being alone in the four postures, are solitary by way of the eight bases of endeavor, their bodily *vīriya* is said to be aroused. Those who, having dispelled mental association and being alone by way of the eight attainments, do not allow the defilement that has arisen while walking to reach the place, nor the defilement that has arisen in the place to reach sitting, nor the defilement that has arisen while sitting to reach lying down, but suppress the defilements in the very place where they have arisen, their mental *vīriya* is said to be aroused.

"*Upaṭṭhitassatī*" Like Mahāgatimbaya Abhayatthera, Dīghabhāṇa Abhayatthera, and Tipiṭaka Cūḷābhaya Thera, who remembered and recollected what had been done for a long time, etc. It is said that Mahāgatimbaya Abhayatthera, on the fifth day after his birth, saw a crow extending its beak into the auspicious milk-rice (*maṅgalapāyāsa*) and made a sound "hum, hum." Then, when he was an elder, when he was asked by the monks, "When did you become mindful, venerable sir?", he said, "From the time of making that sound on the fifth day after birth, friend."

On the ninth day after the birth of Dīghabhāṇaka Abhayatthera, when his mother bent down to kiss him, her crest (*moḷi*) came loose. Then, *sumana* flowers the size of gourds fell on the boy's chest, causing him pain. When he was an elder, when he was asked, "When did you become mindful, venerable sir?", he said, "From the ninth day after birth."

Tipiṭaka Cūḷābhaya Thera - Having had three gates closed in Anuradhapura and having made the people exit through one gate - "What is your name, what is your name?" Having asked, in the evening, without asking again, he was able to receive their names - "It is possible, friend," he said. Referring to such a monk, it is said, "*upaṭṭhitassatī*."
“Those who are wise” (paññavanto) means those who are endowed with wisdom (paññā) that discerns the arising and passing away of the five aggregates (pañca khandha).

Moreover, by these two lines, right mindfulness (sammāsati) and insight wisdom (vipassanāpaññā) which are the requisites for insight (vipassanā) of the monks (bhikkhūnaṃ) who practice insight (vipassakānaṃ) have been spoken of.

“Those who are wise” (paññavanto).
139
<p n="139" rend="bodytext"><hi rend="paranum">139</hi><hi rend="dot">.</hi> ‘‘Aparepi vo, bhikkhave, satta aparihāniye dhamme desessāmi, taṃ suṇātha, sādhukaṃ manasikarotha, bhāsissāmī’’ti. ‘‘Evaṃ, bhante’’ti kho te bhikkhū bhagavato paccassosuṃ. Bhagavā etadavoca –</p> <p rend="bodytext">‘‘Yāvakīvañca, bhikkhave, bhikkhu satisambojjhaṅgaṃ bhāvessanti…pe… dhammavicayasambojjhaṅgaṃ bhāvessanti… vīriyasambojjhaṅgaṃ bhāvessanti… pītisambojjhaṅgaṃ bhāvessanti… passaddhisambojjhaṅgaṃ bhāvessanti… samādhisambojjhaṅgaṃ bhāvessanti… upekkhāsambojjhaṅgaṃ bhāvessanti, vuddhiyeva <pb ed="T" n="2.0094"/>, bhikkhave, bhikkhūnaṃ pāṭikaṅkhā, no parihāni.</p> <pb ed="T" n="2.0094"/> <p rend="bodytext">‘‘Yāvakīvañca, bhikkhave, ime satta aparihāniyā dhammā bhikkhūsu ṭhassanti, imesu ca sattasu aparihāniyesu dhammesu bhikkhū sandississanti, vuddhiyeva, bhikkhave, bhikkhūnaṃ pāṭikaṅkhā no parihāni.</p>
139. "Furthermore, monks, I will teach you seven conditions that do not lead to decline. Listen, pay close attention, I will speak."

"As you say, lord," those monks responded to the Blessed One.

The Blessed One said this:

"As long as, monks, the monks cultivate mindfulness as a factor of enlightenment ( *satisambojjhaṅgaṃ bhāvessanti*)... discrimination of dharma as a factor of enlightenment ( *dhammavicayasambojjhaṅgaṃ bhāvessanti*)... energy as a factor of enlightenment ( *vīriyasambojjhaṅgaṃ bhāvessanti*)... joy as a factor of enlightenment ( *pītisambojjhaṅgaṃ bhāvessanti*)... tranquility as a factor of enlightenment ( *passaddhisambojjhaṅgaṃ bhāvessanti*)... concentration as a factor of enlightenment ( *samādhisambojjhaṅgaṃ bhāvessanti*)... equanimity as a factor of enlightenment ( *upekkhāsambojjhaṅgaṃ bhāvessanti*), surely growth, monks, is to be expected for the monks, not decline.

"As long as, monks, these seven conditions that do not lead to decline endure among the monks, and the monks are known for these seven conditions that do not lead to decline, surely growth, monks, is to be expected for the monks, not decline.
<p n="139" rend="bodytext"><hi rend="paranum">139</hi><hi rend="dot">.</hi> Catutthasattake satiyeva sambojjhaṅgo <hi rend="bold">satisambojjhaṅgo</hi>ti. Esa nayo sabbattha. Tattha upaṭṭhānalakkhaṇo satisambojjhaṅgo, pavicayalakkhaṇo dhammavicayasambojjhaṅgo, paggahalakkhaṇo vīriyasambojjhaṅgo, pharaṇalakkhaṇo <pb ed="M" n="2.0121"/> pītisambojjhaṅgo, upasamalakkhaṇo passaddhisambojjhaṅgo, avikkhepalakkhaṇo samādhisambojjhaṅgo, paṭisaṅkhānalakkhaṇo upekkhāsambojjhaṅgo. <hi rend="bold">Bhāvessantī</hi>ti satisambojjhaṅgaṃ catūhi kāraṇehi samuṭṭhāpentā, chahi kāraṇehi dhammavicayasambojjhaṅgaṃ samuṭṭhāpentā, navahi kāraṇehi vīriyasambojjhaṅgaṃ samuṭṭhāpentā, dasahi kāraṇehi pītisambojjhaṅgaṃ samuṭṭhāpentā, sattahi kāraṇehi passaddhisambojjhaṅgaṃ samuṭṭhāpentā, dasahi kāraṇehi samādhisambojjhaṅgaṃ samuṭṭhāpentā, pañcahi kāraṇehi upekkhāsambojjhaṅgaṃ samuṭṭhāpentā vaḍḍhessantīti attho. Iminā vipassanāmaggaphalasampayutte lokiyalokuttaramissake sambojjhaṅge kathesi.</p>
139. In the fourth week, mindfulness itself is the awakening factor, hence *satisambojjhaṅga*.

This method applies to all the other cases.

Therein, mindfulness (*satisambojjhaṅga*) has the characteristic of presence (*upaṭṭhānalakkhaṇo*); investigation of the Dhamma (*dhammavicayasambojjhaṅga*) has the characteristic of examination (*pavicayalakkhaṇo*); effort (*vīriyasambojjhaṅga*) has the characteristic of exertion (*paggahalakkhaṇo*); joy (*pītisambojjhaṅga*) has the characteristic of suffusion (*pharaṇalakkhaṇo*); tranquility (*passaddhisambojjhaṅga*) has the characteristic of calming (*upasamalakkhaṇo*); concentration (*samādhisambojjhaṅga*) has the characteristic of non-distraction (*avikkhepalakkhaṇo*); equanimity (*upekkhāsambojjhaṅga*) has the characteristic of reflection (*paṭisaṅkhānalakkhaṇo*).

"Developing" (*bhāvessantī*) means generating the mindfulness awakening factor (*satisambojjhaṅga*) through four causes, generating the investigation of the Dhamma awakening factor (*dhammavicayasambojjhaṅga*) through six causes, generating the effort awakening factor (*vīriyasambojjhaṅga*) through nine causes, generating the joy awakening factor (*pītisambojjhaṅga*) through ten causes, generating the tranquility awakening factor (*passaddhisambojjhaṅga*) through seven causes, generating the concentration awakening factor (*samādhisambojjhaṅga*) through ten causes, generating the equanimity awakening factor (*upekkhāsambojjhaṅga*) through five causes, they will increase them, this is the meaning.

In this way, he spoke of the awakening factors (*sambojjhaṅge*) associated with the path and fruition of insight (*vipassanāmaggaphalasampayutte*), mixed with the mundane and supramundane (*lokiyalokuttaramissake*).
140
<p n="140" rend="bodytext"><hi rend="paranum">140</hi><hi rend="dot">.</hi> ‘‘Aparepi vo, bhikkhave, satta aparihāniye dhamme desessāmi, taṃ suṇātha, sādhukaṃ manasikarotha, bhāsissāmī’’ti. ‘‘Evaṃ, bhante’’ti kho te bhikkhū bhagavato paccassosuṃ. Bhagavā etadavoca –</p> <p rend="bodytext">‘‘Yāvakīvañca, bhikkhave, bhikkhū aniccasaññaṃ bhāvessanti…pe… anattasaññaṃ bhāvessanti… asubhasaññaṃ bhāvessanti… ādīnavasaññaṃ bhāvessanti… pahānasaññaṃ bhāvessanti… virāgasaññaṃ bhāvessanti… nirodhasaññaṃ bhāvessanti, vuddhiyeva, bhikkhave, bhikkhūnaṃ pāṭikaṅkhā, no parihāni.</p> <p rend="bodytext">‘‘Yāvakīvañca <pb ed="P" n="2.0080"/>, bhikkhave, ime satta aparihāniyā dhammā bhikkhūsu ṭhassanti, imesu ca <pb ed="V" n="2.0063"/> sattasu aparihāniyesu dhammesu bhikkhū sandississanti, vuddhiyeva, bhikkhave, bhikkhūnaṃ pāṭikaṅkhā, no parihāni.</p> <pb ed="P" n="2.0080"/> <pb ed="V" n="2.0063"/>
“I will tell you another seven things conducive to welfare, monks. Listen and pay heed to what I shall say.”

“Very well, reverend Sir,” those monks replied to the Fortunate One.

The Fortunate One said this:

“As long as monks develop the perception of impermanence (*anিত্যsañjñāṃ bhāvessanti*)... of non-self (*anātmasaṃjñāṃ bhāvessanti*)... of impurity (*aśubhasaṃjñāṃ bhāvessanti*)... of danger (*ādīnavasaṃjñāṃ bhāvessanti*)... of overcoming (*prahāṇasaṃjñāṃ bhāvessanti*)... of dispassion (*virāgasaṃjñāṃ bhāvessanti*)... of cessation (*nirodhasaṃjñāṃ bhāvessanti*), they may be expected to prosper and not decline.

as long as the monks hold to these seven things and are seen to do so, they may be expected to prosper and not decline.
<p n="140" rend="bodytext"><hi rend="paranum">140</hi><hi rend="dot">.</hi> Pañcamasattake <hi rend="bold">aniccasaññā</hi>ti aniccānupassanāya saddhiṃ uppannasaññā. <hi rend="bold">Anattasaññā</hi>dīsupi eseva nayo. Imā satta lokiyavipassanāpi honti. ‘‘Etaṃ santaṃ, etaṃ paṇītaṃ, yadidaṃ sabbasaṅkhārasamatho virāgo nirodho’’ti (a. ni. 9.36) āgatavasenettha dve lokuttarāpi hontīti veditabbā.</p>
140. In the fifth heptad, *aniccasaññā* (perception of impermanence) means the perception that arises together with the contemplation of impermanence.

The same method applies to *anattasaññā* (perception of non-self) and so forth.

These seven are also mundane *vipassanā* (insight).

“This is peace, this is excellent, namely the calming of all formations (*sarvasaṃskārasamatha*), dispassion (*virāga*), cessation (*nirodha*)” (A.
N.
9.
36). It should be understood that here, based on what has come, there are two supramundane [insights] as well.
141
<p n="141" rend="bodytext"><hi rend="paranum">141</hi><hi rend="dot">.</hi> ‘‘Cha, vo bhikkhave, aparihāniye dhamme desessāmi, taṃ suṇātha, sādhukaṃ manasikarotha, bhāsissāmī’’ti. ‘‘Evaṃ, bhante’’ti kho te bhikkhū bhagavato paccassosuṃ. Bhagavā etadavoca –</p> <p rend="bodytext">‘‘Yāvakīvañca <pb ed="M" n="2.0068"/>, bhikkhave, bhikkhū mettaṃ kāyakammaṃ paccupaṭṭhāpessanti sabrahmacārīsu āvi ceva raho ca, vuddhiyeva, bhikkhave, bhikkhūnaṃ pāṭikaṅkhā, no parihāni.</p> <pb ed="M" n="2.0068"/> <p rend="bodytext">‘‘Yāvakīvañca, bhikkhave, bhikkhū mettaṃ vacīkammaṃ paccupaṭṭhāpessanti <pb ed="T" n="2.0095"/> …pe… mettaṃ manokammaṃ paccupaṭṭhāpessanti sabrahmacārīsu āvi ceva raho ca, vuddhiyeva, bhikkhave, bhikkhūnaṃ pāṭikaṅkhā, no parihāni.</p> <pb ed="T" n="2.0095"/> <p rend="bodytext">‘‘Yāvakīvañca, bhikkhave, bhikkhū, ye te lābhā dhammikā dhammaladdhā antamaso pattapariyāpannamattampi tathārūpehi lābhehi appaṭivibhattabhogī bhavissanti sīlavantehi sabrahmacārīhi sādhāraṇabhogī, vuddhiyeva, bhikkhave, bhikkhūnaṃ pāṭikaṅkhā, no parihāni.</p> <p rend="bodytext">‘‘Yāvakīvañca, bhikkhave, bhikkhū yāni kāni sīlāni akhaṇḍāni acchiddāni asabalāni akammāsāni bhujissāni viññūpasatthāni <note>viññuppasatthāni (sī.)</note> aparāmaṭṭhāni samādhisaṃvattanikāni tathārūpesu sīlesu sīlasāmaññagatā viharissanti sabrahmacārīhi āvi ceva raho ca, vuddhiyeva, bhikkhave, bhikkhūnaṃ pāṭikaṅkhā, no parihāni.</p> <note>viññuppasatthāni (sī.)</note> <p rend="bodytext">‘‘Yāvakīvañca, bhikkhave, bhikkhū yāyaṃ diṭṭhi ariyā niyyānikā, niyyāti takkarassa sammā dukkhakkhayāya, tathārūpāya diṭṭhiyā diṭṭhisāmaññagatā viharissanti sabrahmacārīhi āvi ceva raho ca, vuddhiyeva, bhikkhave, bhikkhūnaṃ pāṭikaṅkhā, no parihāni.</p> <p rend="bodytext">‘‘Yāvakīvañca <pb ed="P" n="2.0081"/>, bhikkhave, ime cha aparihāniyā dhammā bhikkhūsu ṭhassanti, imesu ca chasu aparihāniyesu dhammesu bhikkhū sandississanti, vuddhiyeva, bhikkhave, bhikkhūnaṃ pāṭikaṅkhā, no parihānī’’ti.</p> <pb ed="P" n="2.0081"/>
141. “Six further conditions leading to welfare I shall set forth, *bhikkhus*. Listen and pay heed to what I shall say.”

“As you say, lord,” the *bhikkhus* responded to the Blessed One.

The Blessed One said this:

“As long as the *bhikkhus* cultivate loving-kindness in their bodily actions (*kāyakamma*) towards their fellows in the holy life, both openly and in private, growth is to be expected for the *bhikkhus*, not decline.

“As long as the *bhikkhus* cultivate loving-kindness in their verbal actions (*vacīkamma*)… as long as the *bhikkhus* cultivate loving-kindness in their mental actions (*manokamma*) towards their fellows in the holy life, both openly and in private, growth is to be expected for the *bhikkhus*, not decline.

“As long as the *bhikkhus*, whatever rightful gains ( *lābhā dhammikā dhammaladdhā*) they receive—even if it is only the contents of their alms bowl (*pattapariyāpannamattampi*)—do not enjoy them without sharing (*appaṭivibhattabhogī*), but share them with their virtuous companions in the holy life (*sīlavantehi sabrahmacārīhi sādhāraṇabhogī*), growth is to be expected for the *bhikkhus*, not decline.

“As long as the *bhikkhus*—with reference to those rules of moral conduct (*sīlāni*) that are unbroken (*akhaṇḍāni*), without gaps (*acchiddāni*), unspotted (*asabalāni*), untainted (*akammāsāni*), liberating (*bhujissāni*), praised by the wise (*viññūpasatthāni*), untouched (by craving) (*aparāmaṭṭhāni*), conducive to concentration (*samādhisaṃvattanikāni*)—dwell, with their virtue in harmony with that of their companions in the holy life (*sīlasāmaññagatā*), both openly and in private, growth is to be expected for the *bhikkhus*, not decline.

“As long as the *bhikkhus*—with reference to that noble view (*diṭṭhi*) that leads outwards (*niyyānikā*), that leads those who act in accordance with it to the right ending of suffering (*dukkhakkhayāya*)—dwell, with their view in harmony with that of their companions in the holy life (*diṭṭhisāmaññagatā*), both openly and in private, growth is to be expected for the *bhikkhus*, not decline.

“As long as these six conditions leading to welfare (*aparihāniyā dhammā*) endure among the *bhikkhus*, and the *bhikkhus* are known for these six conditions, growth is to be expected for the *bhikkhus*, not decline.”
<p n="141" rend="bodytext"><hi rend="paranum">141</hi><hi rend="dot">.</hi> Chakke <hi rend="bold">mettaṃ kāyakamma</hi>nti mettacittena kattabbaṃ kāyakammaṃ. <hi rend="bold">Vacīkammamanokammesu</hi>pi eseva nayo. Imāni pana bhikkhūnaṃ vasena āgatāni gihīsupi labbhanti <pb ed="V" n="2.0109"/>. Bhikkhūnañhi mettacittena ābhisamācārikadhammapūraṇaṃ mettaṃ kāyakammaṃ nāma. Gihīnaṃ cetiyavandanatthāya bodhivandanatthāya saṅghanimantanatthāya gamanaṃ, gāmaṃ piṇḍāya paviṭṭhaṃ bhikkhuṃ disvā paccuggamanaṃ, pattappaṭiggahaṇaṃ, āsanapaññāpanaṃ, anugamananti evamādikaṃ mettaṃ kāyakammaṃ nāma.</p> <p rend="bodytext">Bhikkhūnaṃ mettacittena ācārapaññattisikkhāpadapaññāpanaṃ, kammaṭṭhānakathanaṃ, dhammadesanā, tepiṭakampi buddhavacanaṃ mettaṃ vacīkammaṃ nāma. Gihīnaṃ cetiyavandanatthāya gacchāma <pb ed="P" n="2.0532"/>, bodhivandanatthāya gacchāma, dhammassavanaṃ karissāma, dīpamālapupphapūjaṃ karissāma, tīṇi sucaritāni samādāya vattissāma, salākabhattādīni dassāma, vassavāsikaṃ dassāma, ajja saṅghassa cattāro paccaye dassāma, saṅghaṃ nimantetvā khādanīyādīni saṃvidahatha, āsanāni paññāpetha, pānīyaṃ upaṭṭhapetha, saṅghaṃ paccuggantvā ānetha, paññattāsane <pb ed="M" n="2.0122"/> nisīdāpetha, chandajātā ussāhajātā veyyāvaccaṃ karothātiādikathanakāle mettaṃ vacīkammaṃ nāma.</p> <pb ed="P" n="2.0532"/> <pb ed="M" n="2.0122"/> <p rend="bodytext">Bhikkhūnaṃ pātova uṭṭhāya sarīrappaṭijagganaṃ, cetiyaṅgaṇavattādīni ca katvā vivittāsane nisīditvā imasmiṃ vihāre bhikkhū sukhī hontu averā abyāpajjāti cintanaṃ mettaṃ manokammaṃ nāma. Gihīnaṃ ‘ayyā sukhī hontu, averā abyāpajjā’ti cintanaṃ mettaṃ manokammaṃ nāma.</p> <p rend="bodytext"><hi rend="bold">Āvi ceva raho cā</hi>ti sammukhā ca parammukhā ca. Tattha navakānaṃ cīvarakammādīsu sahāyabhāvagamanaṃ sammukhā mettaṃ kāyakammaṃ nāma. Therānaṃ pana pādadhovanavandanabījanadānādibhedaṃ sabbaṃ sāmīcikammaṃ sammukhā mettaṃ kāyakammaṃ nāma. Ubhayehipi dunnikkhittānaṃ dārubhaṇḍādīnaṃ tesu avamaññaṃ akatvā attanā dunnikkhittānaṃ viya paṭisāmanaṃ parammukhā mettaṃ kāyakammaṃ nāma.</p> <hi rend="bold">Āvi ceva raho cā</hi> <p rend="bodytext">Devatthero tissattheroti evaṃ paggayha vacanaṃ sammukhā mettaṃ vacīkammaṃ nāma. Vihāre asantaṃ pana paṭipucchantassa kuhiṃ amhākaṃ devatthero, kuhiṃ amhākaṃ tissatthero, kadā nu kho āgamissatīti evaṃ mamāyanavacanaṃ parammukhā mettaṃ vacīkammaṃ nāma.</p> <p rend="bodytext">Mettāsinehasiniddhāni pana nayanāni ummīletvā pasannena mukhena olokanaṃ sammukhā mettaṃ <pb ed="V" n="2.0110"/> manokammaṃ nāma. Devatthero tissatthero arogo hotu, appābādhoti samannāharaṇaṃ parammukhā mettaṃ manokammaṃ nāma.</p> <pb ed="V" n="2.0110"/> <p rend="bodytext"><hi rend="bold">Lābhā</hi>ti cīvarādayo laddhapaccayā. <hi rend="bold">Dhammikā</hi>ti kuhanādibhedaṃ micchājīvaṃ vajjetvā dhammena samena bhikkhācāravattena uppannā. <hi rend="bold">Antamaso pattapariyāpannamattampī</hi>ti pacchimakoṭiyā patte pariyāpannaṃ pattassa antogataṃ dvitikaṭacchubhikkhāmattampi <pb ed="P" n="2.0533"/>. <hi rend="bold">Appaṭivibhattabhogī</hi>ti ettha dve paṭivibhattā nāma – āmisappaṭivibhattañca, puggalappaṭivibhattañca. Tattha – ‘‘ettakaṃ dassāmi, ettakaṃ na dassāmī’’ti evaṃ cittena vibhajanaṃ <hi rend="bold">āmisappaṭivibhattaṃ</hi> nāma. ‘‘Asukassa dassāmi, asukassa na dassāmī’’ti evaṃ cittena vibhajanaṃ pana <hi rend="bold">puggalappaṭivibhattaṃ</hi> nāma. Tadubhayampi akatvā yo appaṭivibhattaṃ bhuñjati, ayaṃ <hi rend="bold">appaṭivibhattabhogī</hi> nāma.</p> <hi rend="bold">Lābhā</hi> <hi rend="bold">Dhammikā</hi> <hi rend="bold">Antamaso pattapariyāpannamattampī</hi> <pb ed="P" n="2.0533"/> <hi rend="bold">Appaṭivibhattabhogī</hi> <hi rend="bold">āmisappaṭivibhattaṃ</hi> <hi rend="bold">puggalappaṭivibhattaṃ</hi> <hi rend="bold">appaṭivibhattabhogī</hi> <p rend="bodytext"><hi rend="bold">Sīlavantehi</hi><pb ed="M" n="2.0123"/><hi rend="bold">sabrahmacārīhi sādhāraṇabhogī</hi>ti ettha sādhāraṇabhogino idaṃ lakkhaṇaṃ, yaṃ yaṃ paṇītaṃ labbhati, taṃ taṃ neva lābhena lābhaṃ nijigīsanatāmukhena gihīnaṃ deti, na attanā bhuñjati, paṭiggaṇhanto ca – ‘‘saṅghena sādhāraṇaṃ hotū’’ti gahetvā ghaṇṭiṃ paharitvā paribhuñjitabbaṃ saṅghasantakaṃ viya passati.</p> <hi rend="bold">Sīlavantehi</hi> <pb ed="M" n="2.0123"/> <hi rend="bold">sabrahmacārīhi sādhāraṇabhogī</hi> <p rend="bodytext">Imaṃ pana sāraṇīyadhammaṃ ko pūreti, ko na pūretīti? Dussīlo tāva na pūreti. Na hi tassa santakaṃ sīlavantā gaṇhanti. Parisuddhasīlo pana vattaṃ akhaṇḍento pūreti. Tatridaṃ vattaṃ – yo hi odissakaṃ katvā mātu vā pitu vā ācariyupajjhāyādīnaṃ vā deti, so dātabbaṃ deti, sāraṇīyadhammo panassa na hoti, palibodhajagganaṃ nāma hoti. Sāraṇīyadhammo hi muttapalibodhasseva vaṭṭati. Tena pana odissakaṃ dentena gilānagilānupaṭṭhākaāgantukagamikānañceva navapabbajitassa ca saṅghāṭipattaggahaṇaṃ ajānantassa dātabbaṃ. Etesaṃ datvā avasesaṃ therāsanato paṭṭhāya thokaṃ adatvā yo yattakaṃ gaṇhāti, tassa tattakaṃ dātabbaṃ. Avasiṭṭhe asati puna piṇḍāya caritvā therāsanato paṭṭhāya yaṃ yaṃ paṇītaṃ, taṃ datvā sesaṃ paribhuñjitabbaṃ. ‘‘Sīlavantehī’’ti vacanato dussīlassa adātumpi vaṭṭati.</p> <p rend="bodytext">Ayaṃ pana sāraṇīyadhammo susikkhitāya parisāya supūro hoti, no asikkhitāya parisāya. Susikkhitāya hi parisāya yo aññato labhati, so na gaṇhāti. Aññato alabhantopi pamāṇayuttameva gaṇhāti, nātirekaṃ. Ayaṃ pana sāraṇīyadhammo evaṃ punappunaṃ piṇḍāya caritvā laddhaṃ laddhaṃ dentassāpi dvādasahi vassehi pūrati, na tato oraṃ. Sace hi dvādasame <pb ed="V" n="2.0111"/> vasse sāraṇīyadhammapūrako piṇḍapātapūraṃ pattaṃ āsanasālāyaṃ ṭhapetvā nahāyituṃ gacchati saṅghatthero ca kasseso pattoti, ‘‘sāraṇīyadhammapūrakassā’’ti <pb ed="P" n="2.0534"/> vutte ‘‘āharatha na’’nti sabbaṃ piṇḍapātaṃ vicāretvā bhuñjitvā ca rittaṃ pattaṃ ṭhapeti, atha so bhikkhu rittaṃ pattaṃ disvā ‘‘mayhaṃ anavasesetvāva paribhuñjiṃsū’’ti domanassaṃ uppādeti, sāraṇīyadhammo bhijjati, puna dvādasavassāni pūretabbo hoti. Titthiyaparivāsasadiso hesa, sakiṃ khaṇḍe jāte puna pūretabbova. Yo pana – ‘‘lābhā vata <pb ed="M" n="2.0124"/> me, suladdhaṃ vata me, yassa me pattagataṃ anāpucchāva sabrahmacārī paribhuñjantī’’ti somanassaṃ janeti, tassa puṇṇo nāma hoti.</p> <pb ed="V" n="2.0111"/> <pb ed="P" n="2.0534"/> <pb ed="M" n="2.0124"/> <p rend="bodytext">Evaṃ pūritasāraṇīyadhammassa pana neva issā, na macchariyaṃ hoti. So manussānaṃ piyo hoti, sulabhapaccayo ca, pattagatamassa diyyamānampi na khīyati, bhājanīyabhaṇḍaṭṭhāne aggabhaṇḍaṃ labhati, bhaye vā chātake vā sampatte devatā ussukkaṃ āpajjanti.</p> <p rend="bodytext">Tatrimāni vatthūni – senagirivāsī tissatthero kira mahāgirigāmaṃ upanissāya viharati. Paññāsa mahātherā nāgadīpaṃ cetiyavandanatthāya gacchantā girigāme piṇḍāya caritvā kiñci aladdhā nikkhamiṃsu. Thero pana pavisanto te disvā pucchi – ‘‘laddhaṃ, bhante’’ti? Vicarimha āvusoti. So tesaṃ aladdhabhāvaṃ ñatvā āha – ‘‘bhante yāvāhaṃ āgacchāmi, tāva idheva hothā’’ti. Mayaṃ, āvuso, paññāsa janā pattatemanamattampi na labhimhāti. Bhante, nevāsikā nāma paṭibalā honti, alabhantāpi bhikkhācāramaggasabhāgaṃ jānantīti. Therā āgamesuṃ. Thero gāmaṃ pāvisi. Dhurageheyeva mahāupāsikā khīrabhattaṃ sajjetvā theraṃ olokayamānā ṭhitā. Atha therassa dvāraṃ sampattasseva pattaṃ pūretvā adāsi, so taṃ ādāya therānaṃ santikaṃ gantvā gaṇhatha, bhanteti, saṅghattheraṃ āha. Thero – ‘‘amhehi ettakehi kiñci na laddhaṃ, ayaṃ sīghameva gahetvā āgato, kiṃ nu kho’’ti sesānaṃ mukhaṃ olokesi. Thero olokanākāreneva ñatvā ‘‘bhante, dhammena samena laddhapiṇḍapāto, nikkukkuccā gaṇhathā’’tiādito paṭṭhāya sabbesaṃ yāvadatthaṃ datvā attanāpi yāvadatthaṃ bhuñji.</p> <p rend="bodytext">Atha naṃ bhattakiccāvasāne therā pucchiṃsu – ‘‘kadā, āvuso, lokuttaradhammaṃ paṭivijjhī’’ti? Natthi me, bhante, lokuttaradhammoti. Jhānalābhīsi, āvusoti? Etampi <pb ed="P" n="2.0535"/> me, bhante, natthīti. Nanu, āvuso, pāṭihāriyanti? Sāraṇīyadhammo me, bhante, pūrito, tassa me dhammassa pūritakālato paṭṭhāya sacepi bhikkhusatasahassaṃ hoti, pattagataṃ na khīyatīti. Te sutvā <pb ed="V" n="2.0112"/> – ‘‘sādhu sādhu sappurisa, anucchavikamidaṃ tuyha’’nti āhaṃsu. Idaṃ tāva – ‘‘pattagataṃ na khīyatī’’ti ettha vatthu.</p> <pb ed="P" n="2.0535"/> <pb ed="V" n="2.0112"/> <p rend="bodytext">Ayameva pana thero cetiyapabbate giribhaṇḍamahāpūjāya dānaṭṭhānaṃ gantvā imasmiṃ ṭhāne kiṃ varabhaṇḍanti pucchi. Dve sāṭakā, bhanteti. Ete mayhaṃ <pb ed="M" n="2.0125"/> pāpuṇissantīti. Taṃ sutvā amacco rañño ārocesi – ‘‘eko daharo evaṃ vadatī’’ti. Daharassa evaṃ cittaṃ, mahātherānaṃ pana sukhumasāṭakā vaṭṭantīti vatvā mahātherānaṃ dassāmīti ṭhapeti. Tassa bhikkhusaṅghe paṭipāṭiyā ṭhite dentassa matthake ṭhapitāpi te sāṭakā hatthaṃ nārohanti. Aññe ārohanti. Daharassa dānakāle pana hatthaṃ āruḷhā. So tassa hatthe pātetvā amaccassa mukhaṃ oloketvā daharaṃ nisīdāpetvā dānaṃ datvā saṅghaṃ vissajjetvā daharassa santike nisīditvā – ‘‘bhante, imaṃ dhammaṃ kadā paṭivijjhitthā’’ti āha. So pariyāyenāpi asantaṃ avadanto – ‘‘natthi mayhaṃ mahārāja lokuttaradhammo’’ti āha. Nanu, bhante, pubbe avacutthāti. Āma, mahārāja, sāraṇīyadhammapūrako ahaṃ, tassa me dhammassa pūritakālato paṭṭhāya bhājanīyabhaṇḍaṭṭhāne aggabhaṇḍaṃ pāpuṇātīti. ‘‘Sādhu sādhu, bhante, anucchavikamidaṃ tuyha’’nti vanditvā pakkāmi. Idaṃ – ‘‘bhājanīyabhaṇḍaṭṭhāne aggabhaṇḍaṃ pāpuṇātī’’ti ettha vatthu.</p> <pb ed="M" n="2.0125"/> <p rend="bodytext">Brāhmaṇatissabhaye pana bhātaragāmavāsino nāgattheriyā anārocetvāva palāyiṃsu. Therī paccūsasamaye – ‘‘ativiya appanigghoso gāmo, upadhāretha tāvā’’ti daharabhikkhuniyo āha. Tā gantvā sabbesaṃ gatabhāvaṃ ñatvā āgamma theriyā ārocesuṃ. Sā sutvā ‘‘mā tumhe tesaṃ gatabhāvaṃ cintayittha, attano uddesaparipucchāyonisomanasikāresuyeva yogaṃ karothā’’ti vatvā bhikkhācāravelāyaṃ pārupitvā attadvādasamā gāmadvāre nigrodhamūle aṭṭhāsi. Rukkhe adhivatthādevatā dvādasannampi bhikkhunīnaṃ piṇḍapātaṃ datvā ‘‘ayye, mā aññattha gacchatha, niccaṃ <pb ed="P" n="2.0536"/> idheva ethā’’ti āha. Theriyā pana kaniṭṭhabhātā nāgatthero nāma atthi, so – ‘‘mahantaṃ bhayaṃ, na sakkā idha yāpetuṃ, paratīraṃ gamissāmī’’ti attadvādasamova attano vasanaṭṭhānā nikkhanto theriṃ disvā gamissāmīti bhātaragāmaṃ āgato. Therī – ‘‘therā āgatā’’ti sutvā tesaṃ santikaṃ gantvā kiṃ ayyāti pucchi. So taṃ pavattiṃ ācikkhi. Sā – ‘‘ajja ekadivasaṃ vihāreyeva vasitvā sve gamissathā’’ti āha. Therā vihāraṃ agamaṃsu.</p> <pb ed="P" n="2.0536"/> <p rend="bodytext">Therī <pb ed="M" n="2.0126"/> punadivase rukkhamūle piṇḍāya caritvā theraṃ upasaṅkamitvā ‘‘imaṃ piṇḍapātaṃ paribhuñjathā’’ti āha. Thero – ‘‘vaṭṭissati therī’’ti vatvā tuṇhī aṭṭhāsi. Dhammiko tāta piṇḍapāto <pb ed="V" n="2.0113"/>, kukkuccaṃ akatvā paribhuñjathāti. ‘‘Vaṭṭissati therī’’ti. Sā pattaṃ gahetvā ākāse khipi. Patto ākāse aṭṭhāsi. Thero – ‘‘sattatālamatte ṭhitampi bhikkhunibhattameva therī’’ti vatvā – ‘‘bhayaṃ nāma sabbakālaṃ na hoti, bhaye vūpasante ariyavaṃsaṃ kathayamāno, ‘bho piṇḍapātika, bhikkhunibhattaṃ bhuñjitvā vītināmayitthā’ti cittena anuvadiyamāno santhambhetuṃ na sakkhissāmi, appamattā hotha theriyo’’ti maggaṃ āruhi.</p> <pb ed="M" n="2.0126"/> <pb ed="V" n="2.0113"/> <p rend="bodytext">Rukkhadevatāpi – ‘‘sace thero theriyā hatthato piṇḍapātaṃ paribhuñjissati, na naṃ nivattessāmi. Sace na paribhuñjissati, nivattessāmī’’ti cintayamānā ṭhatvā therassa gamanaṃ disvā rukkhā oruyha pattaṃ, bhante, dethāti pattaṃ gahetvā theraṃ rukkhamūlaṃyeva ānetvā āsanaṃ paññapetvā piṇḍapātaṃ datvā katabhattakiccaṃ paṭiññaṃ kāretvā dvādasa bhikkhuniyo dvādasa bhikkhū ca sattavassāni upaṭṭhahi. Idaṃ – ‘‘devatā ussukkaṃ āpajjantī’’ti ettha vatthu. Tatra hi therī sāraṇīyadhammapūrikā ahosi.</p> <p rend="bodytext"><hi rend="bold">Akhaṇḍānī</hi>tiādīsu yassa sattasu āpattikkhandhesu ādimhi vā ante vā sikkhāpadaṃ bhinnaṃ hoti, tassa sīlaṃ pariyante chinnasāṭako viya <hi rend="bold">khaṇḍaṃ</hi> nāma. Yassa pana vemajjhe bhinnaṃ, tassa majjhe chiddasāṭako viya <hi rend="bold">chiddaṃ</hi> nāma hoti. Yassa pana paṭipāṭiyā dve tīṇi bhinnāni, tassa piṭṭhiyaṃ vā kucchiyaṃ vā uṭṭhitena visabhāgavaṇṇena kāḷarattādīnaṃ aññataravaṇṇā gāvī viya <hi rend="bold">sabalaṃ</hi> nāma hoti. Yassa pana antarantarā visabhāgabinducitrā gāvī <pb ed="P" n="2.0537"/> viya <hi rend="bold">kammāsaṃ</hi> nāma hoti. Yassa pana sabbenasabbaṃ abhinnāni, tassa tāni sīlāni <hi rend="bold">akhaṇḍāni acchiddāni asabalāni akammāsāni</hi> nāma honti. Tāni panetāni taṇhādāsabyato mocetvā bhujissabhāvakaraṇato <hi rend="bold">bhujissāni.</hi> Buddhādīhi viññūhi pasatthattā <hi rend="bold">viññupasatthāni,</hi> taṇhādiṭṭhīhi aparāmaṭṭhattā – ‘‘idaṃ nāma tvaṃ āpannapubbo’’ti kenaci parāmaṭṭhuṃ asakkuṇeyyattā ca <hi rend="bold">aparāmaṭṭhāni,</hi> upacārasamādhiṃ vā appanāsamādhiṃ vā saṃvattayantīti <hi rend="bold">samādhisaṃvattanikānī</hi>ti vuccanti.</p> <hi rend="bold">Akhaṇḍānī</hi> <hi rend="bold">khaṇḍaṃ</hi> <hi rend="bold">chiddaṃ</hi> <hi rend="bold">sabalaṃ</hi> <pb ed="P" n="2.0537"/> <hi rend="bold">kammāsaṃ</hi> <hi rend="bold">akhaṇḍāni acchiddāni asabalāni akammāsāni</hi> <hi rend="bold">bhujissāni.</hi> <hi rend="bold">viññupasatthāni,</hi> <hi rend="bold">aparāmaṭṭhāni,</hi> <hi rend="bold">samādhisaṃvattanikānī</hi> <p rend="bodytext"><hi rend="bold">Sīlasāmaññagatā</hi><pb ed="M" n="2.0127"/><hi rend="bold">viharissantī</hi>ti tesu tesu disābhāgesu viharantehi bhikkhūhi saddhiṃ samānabhāvūpagatasīlā viharissanti. Sotāpannādīnañhi sīlaṃ samuddantarepi devalokepi vasantānaṃ aññesaṃ sotāpannādīnaṃ sīlena samānameva hoti, natthi maggasīle nānattaṃ. Taṃ sandhāyetaṃ vuttaṃ.</p> <hi rend="bold">Sīlasāmaññagatā</hi> <pb ed="M" n="2.0127"/> <hi rend="bold">viharissantī</hi> <p rend="bodytext"><hi rend="bold">Yāyaṃ</hi><pb ed="V" n="2.0114"/><hi rend="bold">diṭṭhī</hi>ti maggasampayuttā sammādiṭṭhi. <hi rend="bold">Ariyā</hi>ti niddosā. Niyyātīti <hi rend="bold">niyyānikā. Takkarassā</hi>ti yo tathākārī hoti. <hi rend="bold">Sabbadukkhakkhayāyā</hi>ti sabbadukkhakkhayatthaṃ. <hi rend="bold">Diṭṭhisāmaññagatā</hi>ti samānadiṭṭhibhāvaṃ upagatā hutvā viharissanti. <hi rend="bold">Vuddhiyevā</hi>ti evaṃ viharantānaṃ vuddhiyeva bhikkhūnaṃ pāṭikaṅkhā, no parihānīti.</p> <hi rend="bold">Yāyaṃ</hi> <pb ed="V" n="2.0114"/> <hi rend="bold">diṭṭhī</hi> <hi rend="bold">Ariyā</hi> <hi rend="bold">niyyānikā. Takkarassā</hi> <hi rend="bold">Sabbadukkhakkhayāyā</hi> <hi rend="bold">Diṭṭhisāmaññagatā</hi> <hi rend="bold">Vuddhiyevā</hi>
141. "Physical act of loving-kindness (*mettā kāyakamma*)" means a physical act that should be done with a mind of loving-kindness.

The same method applies to verbal and mental acts.

However, these [examples], which come from the perspective of monks, are also found in laypeople. For monks, fulfilling the duties of proper conduct with a mind of loving-kindness is called a physical act of loving-kindness. For laypeople, going to worship at a *cetiya*, going to worship the Bodhi tree, going to invite the *saṅgha*, going to greet a monk entering a village for alms, receiving his bowl, providing a seat, accompanying him, and so on, are called physical acts of loving-kindness.

For monks, teaching the rules of conduct (*ācārapaññatti-sikkhāpada-paññāpanaṃ*), telling about meditation subjects (*kammaṭṭhānakathanaṃ*), giving a Dhamma talk, and even the Buddha's words in the Tipiṭaka are called verbal acts of loving-kindness. For laypeople, saying, "We are going to worship at a *cetiya*, we are going to worship the Bodhi tree, we will listen to the Dhamma, we will offer lamps, garlands, and flowers, we will undertake the three kinds of good conduct, we will give tickets for food, etc., we will give robes for the rainy season, today we will give the four requisites to the *saṅgha*, having invited the *saṅgha*, prepare delicious foods, etc., provide seats, offer drinking water, go to greet the *saṅgha* and bring them in, have them seated on the prepared seats, be keen and enthusiastic, perform services," and so on, at the time of such speech, it is called a verbal act of loving-kindness.

For monks, rising early in the morning and taking care of the body, and after doing the duties of the *cetiya* compound, etc., sitting down in a secluded seat and thinking, "May the monks in this monastery be happy, free from enmity, free from affliction," is called a mental act of loving-kindness. For laypeople, thinking, "May the noble ones be happy, free from enmity, free from affliction," is called a mental act of loving-kindness.

"Openly and in secret (*āvi ceva raho ca*)” means in the presence and in the absence.

There, going to be a helper to new monks in robe-making, etc., is called a physical act of loving-kindness in the presence. For senior monks, all respectful acts, such as washing the feet, bowing, and giving seeds, etc., are called physical acts of loving-kindness in the presence. For both, not showing disrespect for poorly placed wooden items, etc., and tidying them up as if they were one's own poorly placed items is called a physical act of loving-kindness in the absence.

Speaking respectfully, "Devatthera, Tissatthera," is called a verbal act of loving-kindness in the presence. However, when asking about someone who is not in the monastery, "Where is our Devatthera? Where is our Tissatthera? When will he come?" Such words of affection are called verbal acts of loving-kindness in the absence.

Looking with eyes full of loving-kindness and affection, having opened [them] wide, with a serene face, is called a mental act of loving-kindness in the presence. Bringing to mind, "May Devatthera and Tissatthera be free from disease, free from affliction," is called a mental act of loving-kindness in the absence.

"Gains (*lābhā*)" means the requisites obtained, such as robes.

"Righteous (*dhammikā*)" means those that have arisen through righteous conduct, through an equal [and fair] alms-seeking life, avoiding deceit and wrong livelihood.

"Even as much as fills the bowl (*antamaso pattapariyāpannamattampī*)" means even as much as the second spoonful of alms that fills the bowl at the very edge, that is, what is contained within the bowl.

"Not sharing what has been obtained (*appaṭivibhattabhogī*)." Here, there are two kinds of sharing: sharing of material things and sharing with individuals. There, dividing with the mind, "I will give this much, I will not give this much," is called "sharing of material things (*āmisappaṭivibhattaṃ*)". Dividing with the mind, "I will give to so-and-so, I will not give to so-and-so," is called "sharing with individuals (*puggalappaṭivibhattaṃ*)". One who eats without doing either of these is called "not sharing what has been obtained (*appaṭivibhattabhogī*)".

"Gains," "righteous," "even as much as fills the bowl," "not sharing what has been obtained," "sharing of material things," "sharing with individuals," "not sharing what has been obtained."

"Sharing possessions in common with virtuous fellow practitioners (*sīlavantehi sabrahmacārīhi sādhāraṇabhogī*)." Here, this is the characteristic of sharing possessions in common: whatever is obtained that is excellent, he does not give that gain to laypeople out of a desire to conquer gain with gain, nor does he eat it himself, and when receiving it, he thinks, "May it be in common with the *saṅgha*," and having taken it, strikes the bell and sees it as something belonging to the *saṅgha* that should be used.

"With virtuous [monks]," "sharing possessions in common with fellow practitioners."

Now, who fulfills this Dhamma that causes affection, and who does not fulfill it? A person of poor moral character certainly does not fulfill it. Virtuous people do not accept what belongs to him. However, someone of perfectly pure morality fulfills it while keeping his duties unbroken.
Here the rule is: "This is what is meant: someone makes an *odissaka* gift to mother, father, teacher, preceptor, or others, that person gives what should be given, but for him, there is no *sāraṇīyadharma*, it is merely called a bond that causes delay.
The *sāraṇīyadharma* is suitable only for one who is free from the bonds [that cause delay].
Therefore, when giving the *odissaka*, one should give to the sick, those who attend to the sick, newcomers, travelers, and new monks who do not know how to acquire the *saṅghāṭī* robe and the bowl.
Having given to these, whatever remains, from the seat of the elders onward, one should not give a little bit; whoever takes as much as he needs, that much should be given to him.
When there is not enough left over, having gone again for alms and starting from the seat of the elders, whatever is excellent, having given that, the remainder should be used.
Because of the statement "to the virtuous," it is proper not to give even to the immoral.

Now, this *sāraṇīyadharma* is very fulfilling for an assembly that is well-trained, not for one that is untrained.
For an assembly that is well-trained, whoever obtains [something] from elsewhere does not take it.
Even if not obtaining [something] from elsewhere, he takes only what is appropriate, not more than that.
Now, this *sāraṇīyadharma*, by thus repeatedly going for alms, even for one giving whatever is obtained, is fulfilled in twelve years; not less than that.
If, indeed, in the twelfth year, one fulfilling the *sāraṇīyadharma*, having placed a bowl filled with alms in the alms hall and having gone to bathe, and if the elder of the *saṅgha* says, "Whose is this bowl?", saying "*sāraṇīyadharma*-fulfiller," if [someone] says, "Bring it here," having examined all the alms and having eaten and placed the empty bowl, then that *bhikkhu*, seeing the empty bowl, produces unhappiness, [thinking], "They have consumed [it] all without leaving anything for me," the *sāraṇīyadharma* is broken, and it must be fulfilled again for twelve years.
This is similar to the penance of the Tīrthikas; once a breach has occurred, it must be fulfilled again.
But whoever generates joy, [thinking], "It is a gain for me! It is a good gain for me! The co-religionists are consuming what is in my bowl without even asking me," for him, there is what is called "fullness."

Thus, for one who has fulfilled the *sāraṇīyadharma*, there is neither envy nor stinginess.
He is dear to human beings, and the requisites are easily obtained, and even when what is in his bowl is being given away, it does not diminish; in the place for things to be shared, he obtains the best thing; when fear or hunger has arisen, the deities quickly come to his aid.

Here are these stories: Tissatthera, dwelling in Senāgiri, lived depending on Mahāgirigāma.
Fifty great elders, going to Nāgadīpa for the purpose of venerating the *caitiya*, having gone for alms in Girigāma, departed without obtaining anything.
The elder, entering, having seen them, asked, "Did you obtain anything, *bhante*?" "We went around, *āvuso*."
He, having known their state of not having obtained [anything], said, " *Bhante*, until I return, stay right here."
"We, *āvuso*, fifty people, did not obtain even the amount to fill a bowl."
"*Bhante*, the inhabitants here are very capable; even without obtaining [anything], they know the sharing of the alms-path."
The elders waited.
The elder entered the village.
The great laywoman, in her own house, having prepared milk-rice and looking out for the elder, stood there.
Then, as the elder reached the door, having filled the bowl, she gave [it to him]; he, having taken that, having gone to the presence of the elders, said, "Take [this], *bhante*," [and] spoke to the elder of the *saṅgha*.
The elder—"We, so many, did not obtain anything; this one has quickly taken [something] and come, what is this?"—looked at the faces of the others.
The elder, having known by the manner of [their] looking, [said], " *Bhante*, the alms have been obtained by rightful means, take [it] without hesitation," and from the beginning, having given according to their needs to all, he himself also ate according to his need.

Then, at the end of the meal, the elders asked him, "When, *āvuso*, did you penetrate the supramundane Dharma?" "For me, *bhante*, there is no supramundane Dharma."
"Are you a gainer of *jhāna*, *āvuso*?" "That too, *bhante*, is not for me."
"Then, *āvuso*, [do you have] a miracle?" "*Sāraṇīyadharma* has been fulfilled by me, *bhante*; from the time of the fulfillment of that Dharma, even if there are one hundred thousand monks, what is in the bowl does not diminish."
They, having heard [that], said, "Good, good, good sir, this is fitting for you."
This is indeed the story here concerning "what is placed in the bowl does not diminish."
Then that elder, going to the alms-hall at Cetiyapabbata during the Giribhaṇḍa great-offering festival, asked, “What is a choice ware in this place?”

“Two cloaks, venerable sir.”

“These will accrue to me.”

Having heard that, the minister announced to the king, “A certain young man is saying thus.”

Such was the young man’s thought: “Fine cloaks are suitable for the great elders.” Having said, “I will give them to the great elders,” he placed them [there].

Though those cloaks were placed on the head of the one giving in the alms-line of the Sangha, they did not descend to his hand.

Others received [them].

But at the time of giving by the young man, they descended to his hand.

He, having made [the cloaks] fall into his hand, looked at the minister’s face, seated the young man, gave the gift, dismissed the Sangha, sat near the young man, and said, “Venerable sir, when did you penetrate this Dharma?”

He, not speaking untruth even by a pretext, said, “There is no supramundane Dharma for me, great king.”

“Surely, venerable sir, you spoke falsely before?”

“Yes, great king, I am one who fulfills the Dharma worthy of remembrance. From the time of the fulfillment of that Dharma for me, I attain the foremost ware in the place of worthy wares.”

“Good, good, venerable sir, this is fitting for you!” Having praised [him], he departed.

This is the story in regard to, “I attain the foremost ware in the place of worthy wares.”

Due to the fear of the Brāhmaṇa Tissa, the inhabitants of Bhātaragāma fled without even announcing it to the nun Nāgattherī.

At dawn, the nun said to the young nuns, “The village is exceedingly quiet. Investigate, at least.”

Those [nuns], having gone and learned the state of their having gone, came back and announced it to the nun.

She, having heard, said, “Do not think about their having gone. Just apply yourselves to the exercises of reciting the teaching, questioning, and wise attention.” Then, having robed herself at the time for the alms round, together with eleven others, she stood at the village gate, at the foot of a banyan tree.

The deity dwelling in the tree, having given alms food to the twelve nuns, said, “Venerable ladies, do not go elsewhere. Always come here.”

Now, the nun had a younger brother named the elder Nāga. He [thought], “There is great danger. It is not possible to live here. I will go to the far shore.” Together with eleven others, having left his dwelling place, [and thinking], “I will go after seeing the nun,” he came to Bhātaragāma.

The nun, having heard, “The elders have come,” went to their presence and asked, “What is it, venerable sirs?”

He told her that account.

She said, “Today, having stayed just one day in the monastery, tomorrow you may go.”

The elders went to the monastery.

The nun, on the following day, having gone for alms in the vicinity of a tree, approached the elder and said, “Partake of this alms food.”

The elder, saying, “The nun will subsist,” remained silent.

“This alms food is lawful, dear one. Partake without anxiety.”

“The nun will subsist.”

She, taking the bowl, threw it into the sky.

The bowl remained in the sky.

The elder, saying, “Even though she remains firm at a height of seven tālas, the nun is only taking what is given for alms,” then said, “Fear is not always present. When fear has subsided, while reciting the noble lineage, being chided by the mind, ‘O alms-mendicant, you lived having partaken of what was given for alms to a nun,’ I will not be able to steady myself. Be diligent, nuns!” [Then] he ascended the path.
"""0126"/> <pb ed="v" n="2.
0113"/>

A tree goddess [thought]: "If that venerable one eats the alms food from the hand of a nun, I will not turn him away.
If he does not eat, I will turn him away." Thinking this, she stood watching the venerable one's arrival. Seeing him, the tree spirit descended from the tree, took the bowl saying, "Venerable sir, give [me] the bowl!" Having brought the venerable one to the foot of the tree, having prepared a seat, and having given the alms food, having made him do the after-meal duties, she attended upon twelve nuns and twelve monks for seven years.
This is the story of ""the deity becoming zealous"".
There, that venerable one was a fulfiller of memorable qualities.

In ""unbroken,"" etc., if the *śikṣāpada* is broken at the beginning or the end in those seven aggregates of offenses, then his morality is called ""fragmented"" (*khaṇḍa*), like a torn cloth at the edge.
But when he has broken it in the middle (*vemajjhe*), it is called ""rent"" (*chidra*), like a cloth that is rent in the middle (*majjhe*).
When he has broken it twice or thrice in succession (*paṭipāṭiyā*), it is called ""blotched"" (*sabala*), like a cow whose body is some such color as black or red (*kāḷarattādi*) with a discrepant color appearing on the back or the belly (*piṭṭhiyaṃ vā kucchiyaṃ vā uṭṭhitena visabhāgavaṇṇena*).
When a cow with discrepant-spot-variegated drops [has them] in the inner-intervals (*antarāntarā visabhāgabinducitrā gāvī*), it is called ""spotted"" (*kammāsaṃ*).
When they are entirely unbroken (*sabbena sabbaṃ abhinnāni*), those ethical conducts are called ""unbroken"" (*akhaṇḍāni*), ""unperforated"" (*acchiddāni*), ""unblotched"" (*asabalāni*), ""unspotted"" (*akammāsāni*).
Those, having freed [one] from the bondage of craving (*taṇhādāsabyato mocetvā*), on account of making the state of being free, are ""free"" (*bhujissāni*).
Because they are praised by the wise ones, such as the Buddha, they are ""praised by the wise"" (*viññupasatthāni*); because they are untouched by craving and views, they are ""untouched"" (*aparāmaṭṭhāni*), because one cannot be touched by anyone saying, ""Your name is formerly an offender,"" and because they bring about either approximate concentration or fixed concentration, they are called ""conducive to concentration"" (*samādhisaṃvattanikāni*).

Unbroken, fragmented, rent, blotched,
spotted, unbroken, unperforated, unblotched, unspotted, free,
praised by the wise, untouched, conducive to concentration,

"""endowed with the commonality of ethical conduct"" (*sīlasāmaññagatā*)—they will dwell (viharissanti) in those various directional parts (*disābhāgesu*), with those monks who are dwelling, the ethical conducts that have approached a state of equality will dwell (*viharissanti*).
Indeed, the morality of stream-enterers and so forth is the same for other stream-enterers and so forth dwelling in the interior of the ocean and in the heaven realm; there is no difference in the morality of the path (*maggasīle nānattaṃ*).
This was said with reference to that.

Endowed with the commonality of ethical conduct,
they will dwell.

"""This insight"" (*yāyaṃ diṭṭhi*) means right view associated with the path.
"""Noble"" (*ariyā*) means faultless.
Because it leads out, it is ""leading out"" (*niyyānikā*).
"""Of such a nature"" (*takkarassā*) means one who is of such a nature.
"""For the destruction of all suffering"" (*sabbadukkhakkhayāyā*) means for the purpose of the destruction of all suffering.
"""Endowed with the commonality of insight"" (*diṭṭhisāmaññagatā*) means having approached a state of commonality of insight, they will dwell (*viharissanti*).
"""There is only growth"" (*vuddhiyevā*) means for those dwelling thus, growth alone is to be expected for the monks, not decline.

This insight,
noble, leading out, of such a nature, for the destruction of all suffering, endowed with the commonality of insight, there is only growth."""
142
<p n="142" rend="bodytext"><hi rend="paranum">142</hi><hi rend="dot">.</hi> Tatra <pb ed="V" n="2.0064"/> sudaṃ bhagavā rājagahe viharanto gijjhakūṭe pabbate etadeva bahulaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ dhammiṃ kathaṃ karoti – ‘‘iti sīlaṃ, iti samādhi, iti paññā. Sīlaparibhāvito samādhi mahapphalo hoti mahānisaṃso. Samādhiparibhāvitā paññā <pb ed="T" n="2.0096"/> mahapphalā hoti mahānisaṃsā. Paññāparibhāvitaṃ cittaṃ sammadeva āsavehi vimuccati, seyyathidaṃ – kāmāsavā, bhavāsavā, avijjāsavā’’ti.</p>
And then, it is said, the Blessed One, while dwelling at Rājagṛha on Vulture Peak Mountain (gijjhakūṭe pabbate), often gave this Dhamma talk to the monks (bhikkhūnaṃ): "Such is virtue (sīlaṃ); such is concentration (samādhi); such is wisdom (paññā)."

Concentration (samādhi) developed with virtue (sīlaparibhāvito) is of great fruit (mahapphalo) and great benefit (mahānisaṃso).

Wisdom (paññā) developed with concentration (samādhiparibhāvitā) is of great fruit (mahapphalā) and great benefit (mahānisaṃsā).

The mind (cittaṃ) developed with wisdom (paññāparibhāvitaṃ) is completely freed (vimuccati) from the taints (āsavehi), that is, the taint of sensual desire (kāmāsavā), the taint of becoming (bhavāsavā), and the taint of ignorance (avijjāsavā)."
<p n="142" rend="bodytext"><hi rend="paranum">142</hi><hi rend="dot">.</hi><hi rend="bold">Etadeva bahula</hi>nti āsannaparinibbānattā bhikkhu ovadanto punappunaṃ etaṃyeva dhammiṃ kathaṃ karoti. <hi rend="bold">Iti sīla</hi>nti evaṃ sīlaṃ, ettakaṃ sīlaṃ. Ettha catupārisuddhisīlaṃ <hi rend="bold">sīlaṃ</hi> cittekaggatā <hi rend="bold">samādhi,</hi> vipassanāpaññā <hi rend="bold">paññā</hi>ti veditabbā. <hi rend="bold">Sīlaparibhāvito</hi>ti ādīsu yasmiṃ sīle ṭhatvāva maggasamādhiṃ phalasamādhiṃ nibbattenti. Eso tena sīlena paribhāvito mahapphalo hoti, mahānisaṃso. Yamhi samādhimhi ṭhatvā maggapaññaṃ phalapaññaṃ nibbattenti, sā tena samādhinā paribhāvitā mahapphalā hoti, mahānisaṃsā. Yāya paññāya ṭhatvā maggacittaṃ phalacittaṃ nibbattenti, taṃ tāya paribhāvitaṃ <hi rend="bold">sammadeva āsavehi vimuccati.</hi></p> <p rend="bodytext"><hi rend="bold">Yathābhiranta</hi>nti buddhānaṃ anabhiratiparitassitaṃ nāma natthi, yathāruci yathāajjhāsayanti pana vuttaṃ hoti. <hi rend="bold">Āyāmā</hi>ti ehi yāma. ‘‘Ayāmā’’tipi pāṭho, gacchāmāti <pb ed="P" n="2.0538"/> attho. <hi rend="bold">Ānandā</hi>ti bhagavā santikāvacarattā theraṃ ālapati. Thero pana – ‘‘gaṇhathāvuso pattacīvarāni, bhagavā asukaṭṭhānaṃ gantukāmo’’ti bhikkhūnaṃ āroceti.</p> <hi rend="bold">Yathābhiranta</hi> <hi rend="bold">Āyāmā</hi> <pb ed="P" n="2.0538"/> <hi rend="bold">Ānandā</hi>
142. "Etadeva bahulaṃ" means, because he is near complete nirvāṇa, the monk, while advising, repeatedly makes this very teaching.

"Iti sīlaṃ" means thus is morality, this much is morality.

Here, morality (śīla) is to be understood as the fourfold purity of morality (catupārisuddhi-sīla), concentration (samādhi) is mental one-pointedness (cittekaggatā), and wisdom (paññā) is insight-wisdom (vipassanā-paññā).

"Śīlaparibhāvito" and so forth, [refers to] that morality (śīla) in which one stands and then brings about the concentration of the path (magga-samādhi) and the concentration of the fruit (phala-samādhi).

Because it is cultivated with that morality, it is of great fruit (mahāpphala) and great benefit (mahānisaṃsa).

The wisdom of the path (magga-paññā) and the wisdom of the fruit (phala-paññā) are brought about by standing in whichever concentration (samādhi) ; therefore, cultivated by that concentration (samādhi), it is of great fruit (mahapphalā) and great benefit (mahānisaṃsā).

By whichever wisdom (paññā) they stand and bring about the mind of the path (magga-citta) and the mind of the fruit (phala-citta), that, cultivated by that, is rightly released from the influxes (āsavehi vimuccati).

"Yathābhirantaṃ" means, for the Buddhas, there is no such thing as discontented distress; rather, it is said to be according to their liking (yathāruci) and according to their inclination (yathāajjhāsayanti).

"Āyāmā" means, come, let us go.

"Ayāmā" is also a reading; the meaning is "we go."

"Ānandā" means the Blessed One (bhagavā) addresses the elder (thera) because he is always in his presence.

Then the elder announces to the monks, "Take your bowl and robes (pattacīvarāni), the Blessed One (bhagavā) intends to go to such-and-such a place."
143
<p n="143" rend="bodytext"><hi rend="paranum">143</hi><hi rend="dot">.</hi> Atha <pb ed="M" n="2.0069"/> kho bhagavā rājagahe yathābhirantaṃ viharitvā āyasmantaṃ ānandaṃ āmantesi – ‘‘āyāmānanda, yena ambalaṭṭhikā tenupasaṅkamissāmā’’ti. ‘‘Evaṃ, bhante’’ti kho āyasmā ānando bhagavato paccassosi. Atha kho bhagavā mahatā bhikkhusaṅghena saddhiṃ yena ambalaṭṭhikā tadavasari. Tatra sudaṃ bhagavā ambalaṭṭhikāyaṃ viharati rājāgārake. Tatrāpi sudaṃ bhagavā ambalaṭṭhikāyaṃ viharanto rājāgārake etadeva bahulaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ dhammiṃ kathaṃ karoti – ‘‘iti sīlaṃ iti samādhi iti paññā. Sīlaparibhāvito samādhi mahapphalo hoti mahānisaṃso. Samādhiparibhāvitā paññā mahapphalā hoti mahānisaṃsā. Paññāparibhāvitaṃ cittaṃ sammadeva āsavehi vimuccati, seyyathidaṃ – kāmāsavā, bhavāsavā, avijjāsavā’’ti.</p>
Then, the Blessed One, having stayed near Rājagaha as long as he pleased, said to Venerable Ānanda, “Come, Ānanda, we will head for Ambalaṭṭhikā.”

“Very well, reverend Sir,” venerable Ānanda replied to the Fortunate One.

Then the Blessed One, together with a large *bhikkhu-saṅgha* went to Ambalaṭṭhikā.

There the Fortunate One lived near Ambalaṭṭhikā in the King’s Rest House.

While staying there near Ambalaṭṭhikā at the Royal Cottage, the Blessed One often gave this *dhamma* talk to the monks: “Such is virtue (*śīla*), such is concentration (*samādhi*), such is discernment (*prajñā*).

Great becomes the fruit, great is the gain of concentration (*samādhi*) when it is fully developed by virtuous conduct (*śīla-paribhāvito*);

great becomes the fruit, great is the gain of wisdom (*prajñā*) when it is fully developed by concentration (*samādhi-paribhāvitā*);

The mind nurtured with discernment (*prajñā-paribhāvitam*) is rightly released from the effluents (*āsavā*), i. e. , the effluent of sensuality (*kāmāsavā*), the effluent of becoming (*bhavāsavā*), the effluent of ignorance (*avijjāsavā*).”
144
<p n="144" rend="bodytext"><hi rend="paranum">144</hi><hi rend="dot">.</hi> Atha kho bhagavā ambalaṭṭhikāyaṃ yathābhirantaṃ viharitvā āyasmantaṃ ānandaṃ āmantesi – ‘‘āyāmānanda, yena nāḷandā tenupasaṅkamissāmā’’ti. ‘‘Evaṃ, bhante’’ti kho āyasmā ānando bhagavato paccassosi. Atha kho bhagavā mahatā bhikkhusaṅghena saddhiṃ yena nāḷandā tadavasari, tatra sudaṃ bhagavā nāḷandāyaṃ viharati pāvārikambavane <pb ed="T" n="2.0097"/>.</p> <p rend="subhead">Sāriputtasīhanādo</p>
144. Then the Blessed One, having stayed at Ambalaṭṭhikā as long as he pleased, addressed the Venerable Ānanda, "Come, Ānanda, let us go to Nāḷandā."

"So be it, venerable sir," the venerable Ānanda replied to the Fortunate One.

Then the Blessed One, together with a large *saṅgha* of monks, went to Nāḷandā. There he stayed near Nāḷandā at the Pāvārika mango grove.

The Lion's Roar of Śāriputra.
<p n="144" rend="bodytext"><hi rend="paranum">144</hi><hi rend="dot">.</hi><hi rend="bold">Ambalaṭṭhikāgamanaṃ</hi> uttānameva. <hi rend="bold">Atha kho āyasmā sāriputto</hi>tiādi (dī. ni. 3.141) <hi rend="bold">sampasādanīye</hi> vitthāritaṃ.</p> <p rend="subhead">Dussīlaādīnavavaṇṇanā</p>
144. *Ambalaṭṭhikāgamanaṃ* is straightforward.

*Atha kho āyasmā sāriputto* etc. (Dī. Ni. 3. 141) is extensively explained in the *Sampasādanīya*.

Explanation of the disadvantages of immorality etc.
145
<p n="145" rend="bodytext"><hi rend="paranum">145</hi><hi rend="dot">.</hi> Atha kho āyasmā sāriputto yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṃ abhivādetvā ekamantaṃ <pb ed="P" n="2.0082"/> nisīdi. Ekamantaṃ nisinno kho āyasmā sāriputto bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – ‘‘evaṃ pasanno ahaṃ, bhante, bhagavati; na cāhu na ca bhavissati na cetarahi vijjati añño samaṇo vā brāhmaṇo vā bhagavatā bhiyyobhiññataro yadidaṃ sambodhiya’’nti. ‘‘Uḷārā kho te ayaṃ, sāriputta, āsabhī vācā <note>āsabhivācā (syā.)</note> bhāsitā, ekaṃso gahito, sīhanādo nadito – ‘evaṃpasanno ahaṃ, bhante, bhagavati; na cāhu na ca bhavissati na cetarahi vijjati añño samaṇo vā brāhmaṇo vā bhagavatā bhiyyobhiññataro yadidaṃ sambodhiya’nti.</p> <p rend="bodytext">‘‘Kiṃ <pb ed="M" n="2.0070"/><pb ed="V" n="2.0065"/> te <note>kiṃ nu (syā. pī. ka.)</note>, sāriputta, ye te ahesuṃ atītamaddhānaṃ arahanto sammāsambuddhā, sabbe te bhagavanto cetasā ceto paricca viditā – ‘evaṃsīlā te bhagavanto ahesuṃ itipi, evaṃdhammā evaṃpaññā evaṃvihārī evaṃvimuttā te bhagavanto ahesuṃ itipī’’’ti? ‘‘No hetaṃ, bhante’’.</p> <pb ed="M" n="2.0070"/> <pb ed="V" n="2.0065"/> <note>kiṃ nu (syā. pī. ka.)</note> <p rend="bodytext">‘‘Kiṃ pana te <note>kiṃ pana (syā. pī. ka.)</note>, sāriputta, ye te bhavissanti anāgatamaddhānaṃ arahanto sammāsambuddhā, sabbe te bhagavanto cetasā ceto paricca viditā – ‘evaṃsīlā te bhagavanto bhavissanti itipi, evaṃdhammā evaṃpaññā evaṃvihārī evaṃvimuttā te bhagavanto bhavissanti itipī’’’ti? ‘‘No hetaṃ, bhante’’.</p> <note>kiṃ pana (syā. pī. ka.)</note> <p rend="bodytext">‘‘Kiṃ pana te, sāriputta, ahaṃ etarahi arahaṃ sammāsambuddho cetasā ceto paricca vidito – ‘‘evaṃsīlo bhagavā itipi <pb ed="T" n="2.0098"/>, evaṃdhammo evaṃpañño evaṃvihārī evaṃvimutto bhagavā itipī’’’ti? ‘‘No hetaṃ, bhante’’.</p> <pb ed="T" n="2.0098"/> <p rend="bodytext">‘‘Ettha ca hi te, sāriputta, atītānāgatapaccuppannesu arahantesu sammāsambuddhesu cetopariyañāṇaṃ <note>cetopariññāyañāṇaṃ (syā.), cetasā cetopariyāyañāṇaṃ (ka.)</note> natthi. Atha kiñcarahi te ayaṃ, sāriputta, uḷārā āsabhī <pb ed="P" n="2.0083"/> vācā bhāsitā, ekaṃso gahito, sīhanādo nadito – ‘evaṃpasanno ahaṃ, bhante, bhagavati; na cāhu na ca bhavissati na cetarahi vijjati añño samaṇo vā brāhmaṇo vā bhagavatā bhiyyobhiññataro yadidaṃ sambodhiya’’’nti?</p> <note>cetopariññāyañāṇaṃ (syā.), cetasā cetopariyāyañāṇaṃ (ka.)</note> <pb ed="P" n="2.0083"/>
145. Then venerable Śāriputra approached the Blessed One; having approached, prostrated himself before the Blessed One, and sat down to one side.

Sitting to one side, venerable Śāriputra said to the Blessed One: “I am confident in the Blessed One in this way, venerable sir; there has not been, nor will there be, nor is there at present another renunciate ( *śramaṇa*) or *brāhmaṇa* more greatly enlightened than the Blessed One, that is, with regard to perfect awakening (*sambodhi*).”

“Lofty indeed, Śāriputra, is the bull-like speech you have uttered, a definitive statement, a lion’s roar that you have roared: ‘I am confident in the Blessed One in this way, venerable sir; there has not been, nor will there be, nor is there at present another renunciate or *brāhmaṇa* more greatly enlightened than the Blessed One, that is, with regard to perfect awakening.’”
