“But Śāriputra, did you know, with your mind, encompassing with your mind [the minds of] all the worthy ones (*arhats*), the rightly self-awakened ones (*samyaksaṃbuddha*) who existed in the past, that ‘Those Blessed Ones were of such virtue (*śīla*), such was their teaching (*dharma*), such their wisdom (*prajñā*), such their conduct (*vihāra*), such their liberation (*vimukti*)’?” “No, venerable sir.”

“But Śāriputra, [do you know about] all the worthy ones, the rightly self-awakened ones who will exist in the future, that ‘Those Blessed Ones will be of such virtue, such will be their teaching, such their wisdom, such their conduct, such their liberation’?” “No, venerable sir.”

“But Śāriputra, do you know me, the worthy one, the rightly self-awakened one, existing at present, having encompassed [my mind] with [your] mind, that ‘The Blessed One is of such virtue, such is his teaching, such his wisdom, such his conduct, such his liberation’?” “No, venerable sir.”

“And here, Śāriputra, you do not have the knowledge of others' minds regarding the worthy ones, the rightly self-awakened ones, of the past, future, and present. So then, Śāriputra, how can it be that you have uttered this lofty, bull-like speech, a definitive statement, a lion’s roar that you have roared: ‘I am confident in the Blessed One in this way, venerable sir; there has not been, nor will there be, nor is there at present another renunciate or *brāhmaṇa* more greatly enlightened than the Blessed One, that is, with regard to perfect awakening’?”
146
<p n="146" rend="bodytext"><hi rend="paranum">146</hi><hi rend="dot">.</hi> ‘‘Na kho me, bhante, atītānāgatapaccuppannesu arahantesu sammāsambuddhesu cetopariyañāṇaṃ atthi, api ca me dhammanvayo vidito. Seyyathāpi, bhante, rañño paccantimaṃ nagaraṃ daḷhuddhāpaṃ daḷhapākāratoraṇaṃ ekadvāraṃ, tatrassa dovāriko paṇḍito viyatto medhāvī aññātānaṃ nivāretā ñātānaṃ pavesetā. So tassa nagarassa samantā anupariyāyapathaṃ <note>anucariyāyapathaṃ (syā.)</note> anukkamamāno na passeyya pākārasandhiṃ vā pākāravivaraṃ vā, antamaso biḷāranikkhamanamattampi. Tassa evamassa <note>na passeyya tassa evamassa (syā.)</note> – ‘ye kho keci oḷārikā pāṇā imaṃ nagaraṃ pavisanti vā nikkhamanti vā, sabbe te imināva dvārena pavisanti vā nikkhamanti vā’ti. Evameva kho me, bhante, dhammanvayo vidito – ‘ye te, bhante, ahesuṃ atītamaddhānaṃ <pb ed="T" n="2.0099"/> arahanto sammāsambuddhā <pb ed="M" n="2.0071"/>, sabbe te bhagavanto pañca nīvaraṇe pahāya cetaso upakkilese paññāya dubbalīkaraṇe catūsu satipaṭṭhānesu supatiṭṭhitacittā sattabojjhaṅge yathābhūtaṃ bhāvetvā anuttaraṃ sammāsambodhiṃ abhisambujjhiṃsu. Yepi te, bhante, bhavissanti anāgatamaddhānaṃ arahanto sammāsambuddhā <pb ed="V" n="2.0066"/>, sabbe te bhagavanto pañca nīvaraṇe pahāya cetaso upakkilese paññāya dubbalīkaraṇe catūsu satipaṭṭhānesu supatiṭṭhitacittā satta bojjhaṅge yathābhūtaṃ bhāvetvā anuttaraṃ sammāsambodhiṃ abhisambujjhissanti. Bhagavāpi, bhante, etarahi arahaṃ sammāsambuddho pañca nīvaraṇe pahāya cetaso upakkilese paññāya dubbalīkaraṇe catūsu satipaṭṭhānesu supatiṭṭhitacitto satta bojjhaṅge yathābhūtaṃ bhāvetvā anuttaraṃ sammāsambodhiṃ abhisambuddho’’’ti.</p>
146. “I do not have, venerable sir (bhante), any knowledge encompassing the minds of the *arhats* (*arahantesu*), the Perfectly Enlightened Ones (*sammāsambuddhesu*) of the past (*atītānāgata*), the future, and the present, but still I have understood this by inference from the Dhamma (*dhammanvayo vidito*).

“It’s as if, venerable sir (bhante), there were a royal frontier city (*rañño paccantimaṃ nagaraṃ*) with strong ramparts (*daḷhuddhāpaṃ*), strong walls and arches (*daḷhapākāratoraṇaṃ*), and a single gate (*ekadvāraṃ*). In it would be a gatekeeper (*dovāriko*) wise (*paṇḍito*), competent (*viyatto*), and intelligent (*medhāvī*) to keep out those he didn’t know (*aññātānaṃ nivāretā*) and to let in those he knew (*ñātānaṃ pavesetā*).

As he patrols the path (*anupariyāyapathaṃ*) that leads all around the fortress (*nagarassa samantā*), he does not perceive a hole or fissure (*pākārasandhiṃ vā pākāravivaraṃ vā*) in the ramparts even big enough to allow a cat (*biḷāra*) to slip through (*nikkhamanamattampi*).

The thought would occur to him: ‘Whatever large creatures (*oḷārikā pāṇā*) enter or leave this city (*imaṃ nagaraṃ pavisanti vā nikkhamanti vā*), all enter and leave through this one gate (*imināva dvārena pavisanti vā nikkhamanti vā*.’

In the same way, venerable sir (bhante), I have known the consistency of the Dhamma (*dhammanvayo vidito*): ‘All those who were worthy ones (*arahanto*), the rightly self-awakened ones (*sammāsambuddhā*) in the past (*atītamaddhānaṃ*) awoke to the unexcelled right self-awakening (*anuttaraṃ sammāsambodhiṃ abhisambujjhiṃsu*) after having abandoned the five hindrances (*pañca nīvaraṇe pahāya*)—those defilements of awareness (*cetaso upakkilese*) that weaken discernment (*paññāya dubbalīkaraṇe*)—having well-established their minds in the four establishings of mindfulness (*catūsu satipaṭṭhānesu supatiṭṭhitacittā*) and having developed, as they have come to be, the seven factors for awakening (*sattabojjhaṅge yathābhūtaṃ bhāvetvā*).

All those who will be worthy ones (*arahanto*), the rightly self-awakened ones (*sammāsambuddhā*) in the future (*anāgatamaddhānaṃ*) will awaken to the unexcelled right self-awakening (*anuttaraṃ sammāsambodhiṃ abhisambujjhissanti*) after having abandoned the five hindrances (*pañca nīvaraṇe pahāya*)—those defilements of awareness (*cetaso upakkilese*) that weaken discernment (*paññāya dubbalīkaraṇe*)—having well-established their minds in the four establishings of mindfulness (*catūsu satipaṭṭhānesu supatiṭṭhitacittā*) and having developed, as they have come to be, the seven factors for awakening (*satta bojjhaṅge yathābhūtaṃ bhāvetvā*).

And the Blessed One (*bhagavāpi*), venerable sir (bhante), being at present the worthy one (*arahaṃ*), the rightly self-awakened one (*sammāsambuddho*) has awakened to the unexcelled right self-awakening (*anuttaraṃ sammāsambodhiṃ abhisambuddho*) after having abandoned the five hindrances (*pañca nīvaraṇe pahāya*)—those defilements of awareness (*cetaso upakkilese*) that weaken discernment (*paññāya dubbalīkaraṇe*)—having well-established his mind in the four establishings of mindfulness (*catūsu satipaṭṭhānesu supatiṭṭhitacitto*) and having developed, as they have come to be, the seven factors for awakening (*satta bojjhaṅge yathābhūtaṃ bhāvetvā*).’”
147
<p n="147" rend="bodytext"><hi rend="paranum">147</hi><hi rend="dot">.</hi> Tatrapi sudaṃ bhagavā nāḷandāyaṃ viharanto pāvārikambavane <pb ed="P" n="2.0084"/> etadeva bahulaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ dhammiṃ kathaṃ karoti – ‘‘iti sīlaṃ, iti samādhi, iti paññā. Sīlaparibhāvito samādhi mahapphalo hoti mahānisaṃso. Samādhiparibhāvitā paññā mahapphalā hoti mahānisaṃsā. Paññāparibhāvitaṃ cittaṃ sammadeva āsavehi vimuccati, seyyathidaṃ – kāmāsavā, bhavāsavā, avijjāsavā’’ti.</p> <p rend="subhead">Dussīlaādīnavā</p>
147. Furthermore, the Blessed One, while dwelling at Nāḷandā in the Pāvārika mango grove, often gave this Dhamma talk to the monks: "Such is virtue (*śīla*), such is concentration (*samādhi*), such is wisdom (*prajñā*). Concentration (*samādhi*) developed by virtue (*śīla*) is of great fruit and benefit. Wisdom (*prajñā*) developed by concentration (*samādhi*) is of great fruit and benefit. The mind (*citta*) developed by wisdom (*prajñā*) is completely freed from the taints (*āsava*), namely, the taint of sensual desire (*kāmāsava*), the taint of becoming (*bhavāsava*), and the taint of ignorance (*avijjāsava*)."

The disadvantages of immorality (*dussīlaādīnavā*).
148
<p n="148" rend="bodytext"><hi rend="paranum">148</hi><hi rend="dot">.</hi> Atha kho bhagavā nāḷandāyaṃ yathābhirantaṃ viharitvā āyasmantaṃ ānandaṃ āmantesi – ‘‘āyāmānanda, yena pāṭaligāmo tenupasaṅkamissāmā’’ti. ‘‘Evaṃ, bhante’’ti kho āyasmā ānando bhagavato paccassosi <pb ed="T" n="2.0100"/>. Atha kho bhagavā mahatā bhikkhusaṅghena saddhiṃ yena pāṭaligāmo tadavasari. Assosuṃ kho pāṭaligāmikā upāsakā – ‘‘bhagavā kira pāṭaligāmaṃ anuppatto’’ti. Atha kho pāṭaligāmikā upāsakā yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkamiṃsu; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṃ abhivādetvā ekamantaṃ nisīdiṃsu. Ekamantaṃ nisinnā kho pāṭaligāmikā upāsakā bhagavantaṃ etadavocuṃ – ‘‘adhivāsetu no, bhante, bhagavā āvasathāgāra’’nti. Adhivāsesi bhagavā tuṇhībhāvena. Atha kho pāṭaligāmikā upāsakā bhagavato adhivāsanaṃ viditvā uṭṭhāyāsanā bhagavantaṃ abhivādetvā padakkhiṇaṃ katvā yena āvasathāgāraṃ tenupasaṅkamiṃsu; upasaṅkamitvā sabbasanthariṃ <pb ed="M" n="2.0072"/><note>sabbasantharitaṃ satthataṃ (syā.), sabbasanthariṃ santhataṃ (ka.)</note> āvasathāgāraṃ santharitvā āsanāni paññapetvā udakamaṇikaṃ patiṭṭhāpetvā telapadīpaṃ āropetvā yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkamiṃsu, upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṃ abhivādetvā ekamantaṃ aṭṭhaṃsu. Ekamantaṃ ṭhitā kho pāṭaligāmikā upāsakā bhagavantaṃ etadavocuṃ – ‘‘sabbasantharisanthataṃ <note>sabbasanthariṃ santhataṃ (sī. syā. pī. ka.)</note>, bhante, āvasathāgāraṃ, āsanāni paññattāni, udakamaṇiko patiṭṭhāpito, telapadīpo āropito; yassadāni, bhante, bhagavā kālaṃ maññatī’’ti. Atha <pb ed="P" n="2.0085"/> kho bhagavā sāyanhasamayaṃ <note>idaṃ padaṃ vinayamahāvagga na dissati</note>. Nivāsetvā pattacīvaramādāya saddhiṃ bhikkhusaṅghena yena āvasathāgāraṃ tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā pāde pakkhāletvā āvasathāgāraṃ pavisitvā <pb ed="V" n="2.0067"/> majjhimaṃ thambhaṃ nissāya puratthābhimukho <note>puratthimābhimukho (ka.)</note> nisīdi. Bhikkhusaṅghopi kho pāde pakkhāletvā āvasathāgāraṃ pavisitvā pacchimaṃ bhittiṃ <pb ed="T" n="2.0101"/> nissāya puratthābhimukho nisīdi bhagavantameva purakkhatvā. Pāṭaligāmikāpi kho upāsakā pāde pakkhāletvā āvasathāgāraṃ pavisitvā puratthimaṃ bhittiṃ nissāya pacchimābhimukhā nisīdiṃsu bhagavantameva purakkhatvā.</p>
And then the Blessed One, having stayed at Nāḷandā as long as he pleased, addressed the Venerable Ānanda, "Come, Ānanda, let us go to Pāṭaligāma."

"Yes, venerable sir," the Venerable Ānanda replied to the Blessed One.

Then the Blessed One, together with a large community of monks, arrived at Pāṭaligāma.

The lay followers of Pāṭaligāma heard, "The Blessed One, they say, has arrived at Pāṭaligāma."

Then the lay followers of Pāṭaligāma went to the Blessed One, and upon arriving, respectfully bowed down to him and sat down to one side.

As they were sitting to one side, the lay followers of Pāṭaligāma said to the Blessed One, "May the Blessed One accept our rest-house ( *āvasathāgāra*), venerable sir."

The Blessed One consented in silence.

Then the lay followers of Pāṭaligāma, knowing that the Blessed One had accepted, rose from their seats, respectfully bowed down to him, circumambulated him, and went to the rest-house. Having arrived, they spread felt rugs all over the rest-house, arranged seats, set out a water vessel, and lit an oil lamp. Then they went to the Blessed One, and upon arriving, respectfully bowed down to him and stood to one side.

Standing to one side, the lay followers of Pāṭaligāma said to the Blessed One, "The rest-house, venerable sir, is covered all over with felt rugs, the seats are arranged, the water vessel is set out, and the oil lamp is lit. Now is the time, venerable sir, for the Blessed One to do as he sees fit."

Then, in the evening, the Blessed One, having dressed, taking his bowl and robe, went to the rest-house together with the community of monks. Having arrived, he washed his feet, entered the rest-house, and sat down facing east, leaning against the central pillar (*stambha*).

The community of monks also washed their feet, entered the rest-house, and sat down facing east, leaning against the western wall, with the Blessed One in front of them.

The lay followers of Pāṭaligāma also washed their feet, entered the rest-house, and sat down facing west, leaning against the eastern wall, with the Blessed One in front of them.
<p n="148" rend="bodytext"><hi rend="paranum">148</hi><hi rend="dot">.</hi> Pāṭaligamane <pb ed="M" n="2.0128"/><hi rend="bold">āvasathāgāra</hi>nti āgantukānaṃ āvasathagehaṃ. Pāṭaligāme kira niccakālaṃ dvinnaṃ rājūnaṃ sahāyakā āgantvā kulāni gehato nīharitvā māsampi aḍḍhamāsampi vasanti. Te manussā niccupaddutā – ‘‘etesaṃ āgatakāle vasanaṭṭhānaṃ bhavissatī’’ti nagaramajjhe mahatiṃ sālaṃ karitvā tassā ekasmiṃ padese bhaṇḍapaṭisāmanaṭṭhānaṃ, ekasmiṃ padese nivāsaṭṭhānaṃ akaṃsu. Te – ‘‘bhagavā āgato’’ti sutvāva – ‘‘amhehi gantvāpi bhagavā ānetabbo siyā, so sayameva amhākaṃ vasanaṭṭhānaṃ sampatto, ajja bhagavantaṃ āvasathe maṅgalaṃ vadāpessāmā’’ti etadatthameva upasaṅkamantā. Tasmā evamāhaṃsu. <hi rend="bold">Yena āvasathāgāra</hi>nti te kira <pb ed="V" n="2.0115"/> – ‘‘buddhā nāma araññajjhāsayā araññārāmā antogāme vasituṃ iccheyyuṃ vā no vā’’ti bhagavato manaṃ ajānantā āvasathāgāraṃ appaṭijaggitvāva āgamaṃsu. Idāni bhagavato manaṃ ñatvā puretaraṃ gantvā paṭijaggissāmāti yenāvasathāgāraṃ, tenupasaṅkamiṃsu. <hi rend="bold">Sabbasanthari</hi>nti yathā sabbaṃ santhataṃ hoti, evaṃ santhariṃ.</p>
148.
In Pāṭaligamana, *āvasathāgāra* means a dwelling-house for guests.

It seems that in Pāṭaligāma, helpers of two kings would regularly come, remove families from their houses, and stay for a month or half a month.

Those constantly oppressed people thought, "In the future, there will be a dwelling place for them." Having built a large hall in the middle of the city, in one part of it they made a place for storing goods, and in one part a dwelling place.

They, having heard that the Blessed One has come, [thought,] "We should go and bring the Blessed One. He Himself has arrived at our dwelling place. Today, we will have the Blessed One pronounce a blessing in the rest house." Thus they approached for this very purpose.

Therefore, they said thus.

*Yena āvasathāgāra* means that they, thinking, "Indeed, Buddhas are those who dwell in the forest, who delight in forests [and] gardens. They may or may not wish to dwell within the village," not knowing the mind of the Blessed One, they did not prepare the rest house and left.

Now, knowing the mind of the Blessed One, they went ahead, thinking, "We will prepare it." So they approached the rest house.

*Sabbasanthari* means just as everything is spread out, so [it is] spread out.
149
<p n="149" rend="bodytext"><hi rend="paranum">149</hi><hi rend="dot">.</hi> Atha kho bhagavā pāṭaligāmike upāsake āmantesi – ‘‘pañcime, gahapatayo, ādīnavā dussīlassa sīlavipattiyā. Katame pañca? Idha, gahapatayo, dussīlo sīlavipanno pamādādhikaraṇaṃ mahatiṃ bhogajāniṃ nigacchati. Ayaṃ paṭhamo ādīnavo dussīlassa sīlavipattiyā.</p> <p rend="bodytext">‘‘Puna caparaṃ, gahapatayo, dussīlassa sīlavipannassa pāpako kittisaddo abbhuggacchati. Ayaṃ dutiyo ādīnavo dussīlassa sīlavipattiyā.</p> <p rend="bodytext">‘‘Puna caparaṃ, gahapatayo, dussīlo sīlavipanno yaññadeva parisaṃ upasaṅkamati – yadi khattiyaparisaṃ yadi brāhmaṇaparisaṃ yadi gahapatiparisaṃ yadi samaṇaparisaṃ – avisārado upasaṅkamati maṅkubhūto. Ayaṃ tatiyo ādīnavo dussīlassa sīlavipattiyā.</p> <p rend="bodytext">‘‘Puna caparaṃ, gahapatayo, dussīlo sīlavipanno sammūḷho kālaṅkaroti. Ayaṃ catuttho ādīnavo dussīlassa sīlavipattiyā.</p> <p rend="bodytext">‘‘Puna <pb ed="M" n="2.0073"/> caparaṃ, gahapatayo, dussīlo sīlavipanno kāyassa bhedā paraṃ maraṇā apāyaṃ duggatiṃ vinipātaṃ nirayaṃ upapajjati. Ayaṃ pañcamo ādīnavo dussīlassa sīlavipattiyā. Ime kho, gahapatayo, pañca ādīnavā dussīlassa sīlavipattiyā.</p> <pb ed="M" n="2.0073"/> <p rend="subhead">Sīlavantaānisaṃsa</p>
Then the Blessed One addressed the lay followers of Pāṭaligāma: "Householders, there are these five dangers for one of bad morality, of failure in virtue (śīla).

Which five? Here, householders, the immoral person, failing in virtue (śīla), through negligence incurs great loss of wealth (bhogajāniṃ).

This is the first danger for one lacking in virtue (śīla), for one who has lost his virtue (śīla).

Furthermore, householders, the bad reputation of the immoral person, failing in virtue (śīla), gets spread about.

This is the second danger for one lacking in virtue (śīla), for one who has lost his virtue (śīla).

Furthermore, householders, the immoral person, failing in virtue (śīla), whatever assembly he approaches—whether an assembly of nobles (khattiya), of Brahmins (brāhmaṇa), of householders (gahapati), or of ascetics (samaṇa)—he approaches it without confidence, abashed.

This is the third danger for one lacking in virtue (śīla), for one who has lost his virtue (śīla).

Furthermore, householders, the immoral person, failing in virtue (śīla), dies confused.

This is the fourth danger for one lacking in virtue (śīla), for one who has lost his virtue (śīla).

Furthermore, householders, the immoral person, failing in virtue (śīla), upon the breakup of the body, after death, reappears in a state of misery (apāya), in an unhappy destination (duggati), in the nether world (vinipāta), in hell (niraya).

This is the fifth danger for one lacking in virtue (śīla), for one who has lost his virtue (śīla).

These, householders, are the five dangers for one lacking in virtue (śīla), for one who has lost his virtue (śīla).

The advantages of the virtuous.
<p n="149" rend="bodytext"><hi rend="paranum">149</hi><hi rend="dot">.</hi><hi rend="bold">Dussīlo</hi>ti asīlo nissīlo. <hi rend="bold">Sīlavipanno</hi>ti vipannasīlo bhinnasaṃvaro. <hi rend="bold">Pamādādhikaraṇa</hi>nti pamādakāraṇā.</p> <p rend="bodytext">Idañca suttaṃ gahaṭṭhānaṃ vasena āgataṃ pabbajitānampi pana labbhateva. Gahaṭṭho hi yena yena sippaṭṭhānena jīvitaṃ kappeti – yadi kasiyā, yadi vaṇijjāya, pāṇātipātādivasena pamatto taṃ taṃ yathākālaṃ sampādetuṃ na sakkoti, athassa mūlampi vinassati. Māghātakāle pāṇātipātaṃ pana adinnādānādīni ca karonto daṇḍavasena mahatiṃ bhogajāniṃ nigacchati. Pabbajito dussīlo ca pamādakāraṇā sīlato buddhavacanato jhānato sattaariyadhanato ca jāniṃ nigacchati.</p> <p rend="bodytext">Gahaṭṭhassa – ‘‘asuko nāma asukakule jāto dussīlo pāpadhammo <pb ed="P" n="2.0539"/> pariccattaidhalokaparaloko salākabhattamattampi na detī’’ti catuparisamajjhe pāpako kittisaddo abbhuggacchati. Pabbajitassa vā – ‘‘asuko nāma nāsakkhi sīlaṃ rakkhituṃ, na buddhavacanaṃ uggahetuṃ, vejjakammādīhi <pb ed="M" n="2.0129"/> jīvati, chahi agāravehi samannāgato’’ti evaṃ abbhuggacchati.</p> <pb ed="P" n="2.0539"/> <pb ed="M" n="2.0129"/> <p rend="bodytext"><hi rend="bold">Avisārado</hi>ti gahaṭṭho tāva – ‘‘avassaṃ bahūnaṃ sannipātaṭṭhāne keci mama kammaṃ jānissanti, atha maṃ niggaṇhissantī’’ti vā, ‘‘rājakulassa vā dassantī’’ti sabhayo upasaṅkamati, maṅkubhūto pattakkhandho adhomukho aṅgulikena bhūmiṃ kasanto nisīdati, visārado hutvā kathetuṃ na sakkoti. Pabbajitopi – ‘‘bahū bhikkhū sannipatitā, avassaṃ koci mama kammaṃ jānissati, atha me uposathampi pavāraṇampi ṭhapetvā sāmaññato cāvetvā nikkaḍḍhissantī’’ti sabhayo upasaṅkamati, visārado hutvā kathetuṃ na sakkoti. Ekacco pana dussīlopi dappito viya vicarati, sopi ajjhāsayena maṅku hotiyeva.</p> <hi rend="bold">Avisārado</hi> <p rend="bodytext"><hi rend="bold">Sammūḷho kālaṅkarotī</hi>ti tassa hi maraṇamañce nipannassa dussīlakamme samādāya pavattitaṭṭhānaṃ āpāthamāgacchati, so ummīletvā idhalokaṃ passati, nimīletvā paralokaṃ passati <pb ed="V" n="2.0116"/>, tassa cattāro apāyā upaṭṭhahanti, sattisatena sīse pahariyamāno viya hoti. So – ‘‘vāretha, vārethā’’ti viravanto marati. Tena vuttaṃ – ‘‘sammūḷho kālaṃ karotī’’ti. Pañcamapadaṃ uttānameva.</p> <hi rend="bold">Sammūḷho kālaṅkarotī</hi> <pb ed="V" n="2.0116"/>
149. *Dussīlo* means one who is without virtue (*asīlo*) or completely without virtue (*nissīlo*).

*Sīlavipanno* means one who has lost virtue (*vipannasīlo*) or whose vows are broken (*bhinnasaṃvaro*).

*Pamādādhikaraṇa* means the cause of negligence (*pamādakāraṇā*).

This *sutta* comes in connection with householders, but it can also be applied to renunciates.

A householder (*gahaṭṭho*) lives his life by whatever skill (*sippaṭṭhānena*) – whether it be agriculture (*kasiyā*) or trade (*vaṇijjāya*). If, due to negligence (*pamatto*) on account of actions such as killing living beings (*pāṇātipātādivasena*), he is unable to accomplish those things at the right time (*yathākālaṃ sampādetuṃ na sakkoti*), then even his capital (*mūlampi*) is destroyed (*vinassati*).

At the time of drought (*māghātakāle*), if one engages in killing living beings (*pāṇātipātaṃ*), stealing what is not given (*adinnādānādīni*), etc. (*ca karonto*), due to punishment (*daṇḍavasena*), he incurs great loss of wealth (*mahatiṃ bhogajāniṃ nigacchati*).

A renunciate (*pabbajito*) who is immoral (*dussīlo*) and negligent (*pamādakāraṇā*) also incurs loss (*jāniṃ nigacchati*) with respect to virtue (*sīlato*), the Buddha's teachings (*buddhavacanato*), meditation (*jhānato*), and the seven noble riches (*sattaariyadhanato*).

For a householder (*gahaṭṭhassa*), the evil report (*pāpako kittisaddo*) arises in the midst of the four assemblies (*catuparisamajjhe*), saying, "So-and-so (*asuko nāma*), born in such-and-such a family (*asukakule jāto*), is immoral (*dussīlo*), of wicked nature (*pāpadhammo*), and does not give even a morsel of food (*salākabhattamattampi na detī*) to support this life or the next (*pariccattaidhalokaparaloko*)."

Or for a renunciate (*pabbajitassa vā*), the report arises, "So-and-so (*asuko nāma*) was not able to protect his virtue (*sīlaṃ rakkhituṃ*), nor to learn the Buddha's teachings (*buddhavacanaṃ uggahetuṃ*), and lives by medical practice (*vejjakammādīhi jīvati*), being endowed with six kinds of disrespect (*chahi agāravehi samannāgato*)."

*Avisārado* means, in the case of a householder (*gahaṭṭho*), that he approaches with fear (*sabhayo upasaṅkamati*), thinking (*iti*), "Certainly, in a gathering place (*sannipātaṭṭhāne*) of many (*bahūnaṃ*), some (*keci*) will know my actions (*mama kammaṃ jānissanti*), and then they will censure me (*maṃ niggaṇhissantī*)," or, "They will show me to the royal family (*rājakulassa vā dassantī*." He sits down (*nisīdati*) dejected (*maṅkubhūto*), with downcast eyes (*pattakkhandho adhomukho*), scratching the ground with his finger (*aṅgulikena bhūmiṃ kasanto*), and is unable to speak confidently (*visārado hutvā kathetuṃ na sakkoti*).

Or in the case of a renunciate (*pabbajitopi*), he approaches with fear (*sabhayo upasaṅkamati*), thinking (*iti*), "Many *bhikkhus* are assembled (*bahū bhikkhū sannipatitā*), and certainly someone (*koci*) will know my actions (*mama kammaṃ jānissati*), and then they will set aside my *uposatha* and *pavāraṇa*, and after removing me from the *sāmañña*, they will drive me out (*nikkaḍḍhissantī*)." He is unable to speak confidently (*visārado hutvā kathetuṃ na sakkoti*).

But some (*ekacco pana*) immoral ones (*dussīlopi*) behave as if they are proud (*dappito viya vicarati*); even he (*sopi*) becomes dejected (*maṅku hotiyeva*) through his intention (*ajjhāsayena*).

*Avisārado, sammūḷho kālaṅkarotī* means that for him (*tassa hi*), as he lies on his deathbed (*maraṇamañce nipannassa*), the place where his immoral actions have taken place comes to mind (*dussīlakamme samādāya pavattitaṭṭhānaṃ āpāthamāgacchati*). He opens his eyes (*so ummīletvā*) and sees this world (*idhalokaṃ passati*), [then] closes them (*nimīletvā*) and sees the next world (*paralokaṃ passati*), and the four woeful states (*cattāro apāyā*) stand before him (*upaṭṭhahanti*), as if he is being struck on the head (*sattisatena sīse pahariyamāno viya hoti*) with hundreds of spears (*sattisatena*).

He dies (*so marati*) crying out (*viravanto*)—"Stop it! Stop it!" (*‘‘vāretha, vārethā’’ti*).

Therefore it was said (*tena vuttaṃ*)—"Confused, he makes time" (*‘‘sammūḷho kālaṃ karotī’’ti*).

The fifth *pada* is clear.
150
<p n="150" rend="bodytext"><hi rend="paranum">150</hi><hi rend="dot">.</hi> ‘‘Pañcime <pb ed="T" n="2.0102"/><pb ed="P" n="2.0086"/>, gahapatayo, ānisaṃsā sīlavato sīlasampadāya. Katame pañca? Idha, gahapatayo, sīlavā sīlasampanno appamādādhikaraṇaṃ mahantaṃ bhogakkhandhaṃ adhigacchati. Ayaṃ paṭhamo ānisaṃso sīlavato sīlasampadāya.</p> <p rend="bodytext">‘‘Puna <pb ed="V" n="2.0068"/> caparaṃ, gahapatayo, sīlavato sīlasampannassa kalyāṇo kittisaddo abbhuggacchati. Ayaṃ dutiyo ānisaṃso sīlavato sīlasampadāya.</p> <pb ed="V" n="2.0068"/> <p rend="bodytext">‘‘Puna caparaṃ, gahapatayo, sīlavā sīlasampanno yaññadeva parisaṃ upasaṅkamati – yadi khattiyaparisaṃ yadi brāhmaṇaparisaṃ yadi gahapatiparisaṃ yadi samaṇaparisaṃ visārado upasaṅkamati amaṅkubhūto. Ayaṃ tatiyo ānisaṃso sīlavato sīlasampadāya.</p> <p rend="bodytext">‘‘Puna caparaṃ, gahapatayo, sīlavā sīlasampanno asammūḷho kālaṅkaroti. Ayaṃ catuttho ānisaṃso sīlavato sīlasampadāya.</p> <p rend="bodytext">‘‘Puna caparaṃ, gahapatayo, sīlavā sīlasampanno kāyassa bhedā paraṃ maraṇā sugatiṃ saggaṃ lokaṃ upapajjati. Ayaṃ pañcamo ānisaṃso sīlavato sīlasampadāya. Ime kho, gahapatayo, pañca ānisaṃsā sīlavato sīlasampadāyā’’ti.</p>
150. “Householders, there are these five advantages for one who is virtuous, for one accomplished in virtue. Which five? Here, householders, a virtuous person, consummate in virtue, by reason of heedfulness acquires a great mass of wealth (mahantaṃ bhogakkhandhaṃ adhigacchati). This is the first advantage for one who is virtuous, for one accomplished in virtue.

“And further, householders, the fine reputation (kalyāṇo kittisaddo abbhuggacchati) of the virtuous person, consummate in virtue, gets spread about. This is the second advantage for one who is virtuous, for one accomplished in virtue.

“And further, householders, whatever assembly (yaññadeva parisaṃ upasaṅkamati) the virtuous person, consummate in virtue, approaches—whether an assembly of noble warriors (khattiyaparisaṃ), of brahmans (brāhmaṇaparisaṃ), of householders (gahapatiparisaṃ), or of contemplatives (samaṇaparisaṃ)—he/she does so with confidence & unabashed (visārado upasaṅkamati amaṅkubhūto). This is the third advantage for one who is virtuous, for one accomplished in virtue.

“And further, householders, the virtuous person, consummate in virtue, dies unconfused (asammūḷho kālaṅkaroti). This is the fourth advantage for one who is virtuous, for one accomplished in virtue.

“And further, householders, the virtuous person, consummate in virtue—on the break-up of the body (kāyassa bhedā), after death (paraṃ maraṇā)—reappears in a good destination, a heavenly world (sugatiṃ saggaṃ lokaṃ upapajjati). This is the fifth advantage for one who is virtuous, for one accomplished in virtue. These, householders, are the five advantages for one who is virtuous, for one accomplished in virtue.”
<p n="150" rend="bodytext"><hi rend="paranum">150</hi><hi rend="dot">.</hi><hi rend="bold">Ānisaṃsakathā</hi> vuttavipariyāyena veditabbā.</p>
The *ānisaṃsakathā* should be understood through the opposite of what has been stated.
151
<p n="151" rend="bodytext"><hi rend="paranum">151</hi><hi rend="dot">.</hi> Atha kho bhagavā pāṭaligāmike upāsake bahudeva rattiṃ dhammiyā kathāya sandassetvā samādapetvā samuttejetvā sampahaṃsetvā uyyojesi – ‘‘abhikkantā kho, gahapatayo, ratti, yassadāni tumhe kālaṃ maññathā’’ti. ‘‘Evaṃ, bhante’’ti kho pāṭaligāmikā upāsakā bhagavato paṭissutvā uṭṭhāyāsanā bhagavantaṃ abhivādetvā padakkhiṇaṃ katvā pakkamiṃsu. Atha kho bhagavā acirapakkantesu pāṭaligāmikesu upāsakesu <pb ed="T" n="2.0103"/> suññāgāraṃ pāvisi.</p> <p rend="subhead">Pāṭaliputtanagaramāpanaṃ</p>
Then, the Blessed One, having for much of the night instructed, aroused, inspired, and delighted the lay followers of Pāṭaligāma with a discourse on the Dhamma, dismissed them, saying: “The night is far advanced, householders. Now do what you think fit.”

“Even so, Lord (evaṃ, bhante),” replied the lay followers of Pāṭaligāma. Rising from their seats, they bowed down to the Blessed One, circumambulated him, and departed.

Then, not long after the lay followers of Pāṭaligāma had left, the Blessed One entered an empty dwelling (suññāgāraṃ pāvisi).

Reaching the city of Pāṭaliputra (pāṭaliputtanagaramāpanaṃ).
<p n="151" rend="bodytext"><hi rend="paranum">151</hi><hi rend="dot">.</hi><hi rend="bold">Bahudeva rattiṃ dhammiyā kathāyā</hi>ti aññāya pāḷimuttakāya dhammikathāya ceva āvasathānumodanāya ca ākāsagaṅgaṃ otārento viya yojanappamāṇaṃ mahāmadhuṃ pīḷetvā madhupānaṃ pāyento viya bahudeva rattiṃ sandassetvā sampahaṃsetvā uyyojesi. <hi rend="bold">Abhikkantā</hi>ti atikkantā khīṇā khayavayaṃ upetā. <hi rend="bold">Suññāgāra</hi>nti pāṭiyekkaṃ suññāgāraṃ nāma natthi, tattheva pana ekapasse sāṇipākārena parikkhipitvā – ‘‘idha satthā vissamissatī’’ti mañcakaṃ paññapesuṃ. Bhagavā – ‘‘catūhipi iriyāpathehi paribhuttaṃ etesaṃ mahapphalaṃ bhavissatī’’ti tattha sīhaseyyaṃ <pb ed="P" n="2.0540"/> kappesi. Taṃ sandhāya vuttaṃ – ‘‘suññāgāraṃ pāvisī’’ti.</p> <p rend="subhead">Pāṭaliputtanagaramāpanavaṇṇanā</p>
151. *bahudeva rattiṃ dhammiyā kathāyā* means, after showing, delighting, and sending [them] away for much of the night with a Dhamma talk different from that in the Pali [canon], with a Dhamma talk and with rejoicing in the lodging, as if bringing down the sky-Ganges, as if squeezing a great honey the measure of a *yojana* and giving a honey drink.

*abhikkantā* means passed, diminished, approached destruction and decay.

*suññāgāra* means there is no *suññāgāra* by way of distinction, but right there, having fenced off one side with a screen of cloth, they prepared a couch, [saying,] "Here the Teacher will rest."

The Blessed One, [thinking,] "The great fruit of these will come about because it has been made use of with all four postures," assumed the lion's posture there.

With reference to that, it was said, "He entered the empty house."

Description of the Arrival at the City of Pāṭaliputra.
152
<p n="152" rend="bodytext"><hi rend="paranum">152</hi><hi rend="dot">.</hi> Tena <pb ed="M" n="2.0074"/> kho pana samayena sunidhavassakārā <note>sunīdhavassakārā (syā. ka.)</note> magadhamahāmattā pāṭaligāme nagaraṃ māpenti vajjīnaṃ paṭibāhāya. Tena samayena sambahulā devatāyo <pb ed="P" n="2.0087"/> sahasseva <note>sahassasseva (sī. pī. ka.), sahassaseva (ṭīkāyaṃ pāṭhantaraṃ), sahassasahasseva (udānaṭṭhakathā)</note> pāṭaligāme vatthūni pariggaṇhanti. Yasmiṃ padese mahesakkhā devatā vatthūni pariggaṇhanti, mahesakkhānaṃ tattha raññaṃ rājamahāmattānaṃ cittāni namanti nivesanāni māpetuṃ. Yasmiṃ padese majjhimā devatā vatthūni pariggaṇhanti, majjhimānaṃ tattha raññaṃ rājamahāmattānaṃ cittāni namanti nivesanāni māpetuṃ. Yasmiṃ padese nīcā devatā vatthūni pariggaṇhanti, nīcānaṃ tattha raññaṃ rājamahāmattānaṃ cittāni namanti nivesanāni māpetuṃ. Addasā kho bhagavā dibbena cakkhunā visuddhena atikkantamānusakena tā devatāyo sahasseva pāṭaligāme vatthūni pariggaṇhantiyo. Atha kho bhagavā <pb ed="V" n="2.0069"/> rattiyā paccūsasamayaṃ paccuṭṭhāya āyasmantaṃ ānandaṃ āmantesi – ‘‘ke nu kho <note>ko nu kho (sī. syā. pī. ka.)</note>, ānanda, pāṭaligāme nagaraṃ māpentī’’ti <note>māpetīti (sī. syā. pī. ka.)</note>? ‘‘Sunidhavassakārā, bhante, magadhamahāmattā pāṭaligāme nagaraṃ māpenti vajjīnaṃ paṭibāhāyā’’ti. ‘‘Seyyathāpi, ānanda, devehi tāvatiṃsehi saddhiṃ mantetvā, evameva kho, ānanda, sunidhavassakārā magadhamahāmattā pāṭaligāme nagaraṃ māpenti vajjīnaṃ paṭibāhāya. Idhāhaṃ, ānanda, addasaṃ dibbena cakkhunā visuddhena atikkantamānusakena sambahulā devatāyo sahasseva pāṭaligāme vatthūni pariggaṇhantiyo. Yasmiṃ <pb ed="T" n="2.0104"/>, ānanda, padese mahesakkhā devatā vatthūni pariggaṇhanti, mahesakkhānaṃ tattha raññaṃ rājamahāmattānaṃ cittāni namanti nivesanāni māpetuṃ. Yasmiṃ padese majjhimā devatā vatthūni pariggaṇhanti, majjhimānaṃ tattha raññaṃ rājamahāmattānaṃ cittāni namanti nivesanāni māpetuṃ. Yasmiṃ padese nīcā devatā vatthūni pariggaṇhanti, nīcānaṃ tattha raññaṃ rājamahāmattānaṃ cittāni namanti nivesanāni māpetuṃ. Yāvatā, ānanda, ariyaṃ āyatanaṃ yāvatā vaṇippatho idaṃ agganagaraṃ bhavissati pāṭaliputtaṃ puṭabhedanaṃ <pb ed="P" n="2.0088"/>. Pāṭaliputtassa kho, ānanda, tayo antarāyā bhavissanti – aggito vā udakato vā mithubhedā vā’’ti.</p>
152.

At that time (tena samayena), Sunidha and Vassakāra, the ministers of Magadha, were building a city at Pāṭaligāma to ward off the Vajjis. At that time, many deities (devatāyo) were taking possession of sites in Pāṭaligāma, thousands of them. In the area where powerful deities (mahesakkhā devatā) were taking possession of sites, there the minds of the kings and royal ministers were inclined to build dwellings. In the area where deities of middling power (majjhimā devatā) were taking possession of sites, there the minds of the kings and royal ministers were inclined to build dwellings. In the area where lower deities (nīcā devatā) were taking possession of sites, there the minds of the kings and royal ministers were inclined to build dwellings.

Then the Blessed One (bhagavā), with his divine eye (dibbena cakkhunā), purified and surpassing the human, saw those deities (devatāyo) taking possession of sites in Pāṭaligāma, thousands of them.

Then the Blessed One (bhagavā), arising in the last watch of the night, addressed the venerable Ānanda: "Who, Ānanda, is building a city (nagaram) at Pāṭaligāma?"

"Sunidha and Vassakāra, venerable sir (bhante), the ministers of Magadha, are building a city (nagaram) at Pāṭaligāma to ward off the Vajjis."

"Just as if, Ānanda, they had consulted with the gods (devehi) of the Thirty-three, even so, Ānanda, Sunidha and Vassakāra, the ministers of Magadha, are building a city (nagaram) at Pāṭaligāma to ward off the Vajjis. Here, Ānanda, I saw, with the divine eye (dibbena cakkhunā), purified and surpassing the human, many deities (devatāyo) taking possession of sites in Pāṭaligāma, thousands of them.

Wherever, Ānanda, powerful deities (mahesakkhā devatā) take possession of sites, there the minds of the kings and royal ministers are inclined to build dwellings. In whatever area middling deities (majjhimā devatā) take possession of sites, there the minds of the kings and royal ministers are inclined to build dwellings. In whatever area lower deities (nīcā devatā) take possession of sites, there the minds of the kings and royal ministers are inclined to build dwellings.

As far, Ānanda, as the Aryan sphere extends, as far as trade routes extend, this Pāṭaliputta will be the foremost city (agganagaraṃ), a trade center (puṭabhedanaṃ).

There will be three dangers for Pāṭaliputta: from fire (aggito), from water (udakato), or from internal division (mithubhedā)."
<p n="152" rend="bodytext"><hi rend="paranum">152</hi><hi rend="dot">.</hi><hi rend="bold">Sunidhavassakārā</hi>ti <pb ed="M" n="2.0130"/> sunidho ca vassakāro ca dve brāhmaṇā. <hi rend="bold">Magadhamahāmattā</hi>ti magadharañño mahāmattā mahāamaccā, magadharaṭṭhe vā mahāmattā mahatiyā issariyamattāya samannāgatāti <hi rend="bold">magadhamahāmattā. Pāṭaligāme nagara</hi>nti pāṭaligāmaṃ nagaraṃ katvā māpenti. <hi rend="bold">Vajjīnaṃ paṭibāhāyā</hi>ti vajjirājakulānaṃ āyamukhapacchindanatthaṃ. <hi rend="bold">Sahassevā</hi>ti ekekavaggavasena sahassaṃ sahassaṃ hutvā. <hi rend="bold">Vatthūnī</hi>ti gharavatthūni. <hi rend="bold">Cittāni namanti nivesanāni māpetu</hi>nti raññañca rājamahāmattānañca nivesanāni māpetuṃ vatthuvijjāpāṭhakānaṃ cittāni namanti. Te kira attano sippānubhāvena heṭṭhā pathaviyaṃ tiṃsahatthamatte ṭhāne – ‘‘idha nāgaggāho, idha yakkhaggāho, idha bhūtaggāho, pāsāṇo vā khāṇuko vā atthī’’ti passanti. Te tadā sippaṃ jappitvā devatāhi saddhiṃ mantayamānā viya māpenti. Athavā nesaṃ sarīre devatā adhimuccitvā tattha tattha nivesanāni māpetuṃ cittaṃ nāmenti. Tā catūsu koṇesu khāṇuke koṭṭetvā vatthumhi gahitamatte paṭivigacchanti. Saddhānaṃ kulānaṃ saddhā devatā tathā karonti, assaddhānaṃ kulānaṃ assaddhā devatāva. Kiṃ kāraṇā? Saddhānañhi evaṃ hoti – ‘‘idha manussā nivesanaṃ māpetvā paṭhamaṃ bhikkhusaṅghaṃ nisīdāpetvā maṅgalaṃ vaḍḍhāpessanti. Atha mayaṃ sīlavantānaṃ dassanaṃ, dhammakathaṃ, pañhāvissajjanaṃ <pb ed="V" n="2.0117"/>, anumodanañca sotuṃ labhissāma, manussā dānaṃ datvā amhākaṃ pattiṃ dassantī’’ti.</p> <p rend="bodytext"><hi rend="bold">Tāvatiṃsehī</hi>ti yathā hi ekasmiṃ kule ekaṃ paṇḍitamanussaṃ, ekasmiṃ vā vihāre ekaṃ bahussutabhikkhuṃ upādāya – ‘‘asukakule manussā paṇḍitā, asukavihāre bhikkhū bahussutā’’ti saddo abbhuggacchati, evameva sakkaṃ devarājānaṃ vissakammañca devaputtaṃ upādāya – ‘‘tāvatiṃsā paṇḍitā’’ti saddo abbhuggato. Tenāha – ‘‘tāvatiṃsehī’’ti. Tāvatiṃsehi saddhiṃ mantetvāpi viya māpentīti attho.</p> <hi rend="bold">Tāvatiṃsehī</hi> <p rend="bodytext"><hi rend="bold">Yāvatā ariyaṃ āyatana</hi>nti yattakaṃ ariyakamanussānaṃ osaraṇaṭṭhānaṃ <pb ed="P" n="2.0541"/> nāma atthi. <hi rend="bold">Yāvatā vaṇippatho</hi>ti yattakaṃ vāṇijānaṃ ābhatabhaṇḍassa <pb ed="M" n="2.0131"/> rāsivaseneva kayavikkayaṭṭhānaṃ nāma, vāṇijānaṃ vasanaṭṭhānaṃ vā atthi. <hi rend="bold">Idaṃ agganagara</hi>nti tesaṃ ariyāyatanavaṇippathānaṃ idaṃ agganagaraṃ jeṭṭhakaṃ pāmokkhaṃ bhavissatīti. <hi rend="bold">Puṭabhedana</hi>nti bhaṇḍapuṭabhedanaṭṭhānaṃ, bhaṇḍabhaṇḍikānaṃ mocanaṭṭhānanti vuttaṃ hoti. Sakalajambudīpe aladdhabhaṇḍampi hi idheva labhissanti, aññattha vikkayena agacchantampi ca idheva gamissati. Tasmā idheva puṭaṃ bhindissantīti attho. Catūsu hi dvāresu cattāri sabhāyaṃ ekanti evaṃ divase divase pañcasatasahassāni uṭṭhahissantīti dasseti.</p> <hi rend="bold">Yāvatā ariyaṃ āyatana</hi> <pb ed="P" n="2.0541"/> <hi rend="bold">Yāvatā vaṇippatho</hi> <pb ed="M" n="2.0131"/> <hi rend="bold">Idaṃ agganagara</hi> <hi rend="bold">Puṭabhedana</hi> <p rend="bodytext"><hi rend="bold">Aggito vā</hi>tiādīsu cakārattho vā-saddo. Agginā ca udakena ca mithubhedena ca nassissatīti attho. Ekakoṭṭhāso agginā nassissati, nibbāpetuṃ na sakkhissanti. Ekaṃ gaṅgā gahetvā gamissati. Eko – ‘‘iminā akathitaṃ amussa, amunā akathitaṃ imassā’’ti vadantānaṃ pisuṇavācānaṃ vasena bhinnānaṃ manussānaṃ aññamaññabhedeneva nassissatīti attho. Iti vatvā bhagavā paccūsakāle gaṅgāya tīraṃ gantvā katamukhadhovano bhikkhācāravelaṃ āgamayamāno nisīdi.</p> <hi rend="bold">Aggito vā</hi>
152. “*Sunidhavassakārā*” means Sunidha and Vassakāra were two *brāhmaṇas* (brāhmaṇo brahmacārī).
"*Magadhamahāmattā*" means the *mahāmattas* (high officials) of the Magadha king, the great ministers (*mahāamaccā*), or the *mahāmattas* in the Magadha country were endowed with great power (mahatiyā issariyamattāya samannāgatāti).
"*Pāṭaligāme nagara*" means they were causing a city to be made, having made a city in Pāṭaligāma (Pāṭaliputra).
"*Vajjīnaṃ paṭibāhāyā*" means for the purpose of preventing the source of income of the Vajjī kings.
"*Sahassevā*" means having become a thousand and a thousand, by way of each group.
"*Vatthūnī*" means house-sites.
"*Cittāni namanti nivesanāni māpetu*" means the minds of the architects of house-sites are inclined to build dwellings for the king and also for the royal *mahāmattas*.
They, by the power of their craft, in a place thirty *hatthas* (cubits) down into the earth (pathaviyaṃ), see, “Here is a seizing by *nāgas*, here is a seizing by *yakṣas*, here is a seizing by *bhūtas*, here is a stone or a stake.”
They then, having chanted the craft, build as if consulting with the gods (*devatās*).
Or else, *devatās*, having entered into their bodies, incline their minds to build dwellings in that place.
They, having struck stakes in the four corners, turn back at the very moment that the ground (*vastu*) is taken.
The *devatās* (gods) act in that way toward believing families (*kulānas*), [and] unbelieving *devatās* toward unbelieving families.
What is the reason? For believers, it happens thus: “Here, humans, having caused a dwelling to be built, will first seat the *bhikkhusaṅgha* (community of monks), and will increase auspiciousness (*maṅgalaṃ*).
Then we will obtain seeing the virtuous (*sīlavantānaṃ*), a talk on the Dharma (dharmakathāṃ), answering questions (*pañhāvissajjanaṃ*), and rejoicing in approval, [and] humans, having given alms (*dānaṃ*), will give the merit (*pattiṃ*) to us.”

“*Tāvatiṃsehī*” means just as, indeed, in one family, having taken one learned person (*paṇḍitamanussaṃ*), or in one monastery, having taken one learned monk (*bahussutabhikkhuṃ*)—the sound goes forth, “The people in such-and-such a family are learned, the monks in such-and-such a monastery are very learned (*bahussutā*)”—just so, having taken Sakka, the king of the gods (devarājānaṃ), and Viśvakarman, the god's son, the sound went forth, “The *tāvatiṃsas* are learned.”
Therefore, it is said, "*tāvatiṃsehī*."
The meaning is that they build as if consulting with the *tāvatiṃsas*.

“*Tāvatiṃsehī*", "*yāvatā ariyaṃ āyatana*" means as far as there is a place of resort for noble humans (*ariyakamanussānaṃ*).
"*Yāvatā vaṇippatho*" means as far as there is a place of trade and commerce (*kayavikkayaṭṭhānaṃ*) for the merchandise brought by merchants, like a heap, or there is a dwelling place for merchants.
"*Idaṃ agganagara*" means this chief city will be the best and foremost of those places of resort and trade of the noble ones.
"*Puṭabhedana*" means a place for breaking open bundles of merchandise, it means a place for releasing goods and wares.
Even goods not obtained in all of *Jambudvīpa*, they will obtain right here, and even those not going elsewhere for sale will go right here.
Therefore, they will break open the bundles right here, is the meaning.
Indeed, four at the four gates, one in the assembly hall—thus, he indicates that five hundred thousand will arise day by day.

"*Yāvatā ariyaṃ āyatana*", "*yāvatā vaṇippatho*", "*idaṃ agganagara*", "*puṭabhedana*", in "*aggito vā*" etc., the word *vā* has the meaning of “and”.
The meaning is that it will be destroyed by fire, by water, and by disunion.
One part will be destroyed by fire; they will not be able to extinguish it.
The Ganges (*gaṅgā*) will take and go with one [part].
One—through the influence of the backbiting words of humans who are divided by saying, “This was not said to that one; that was not said to this one,” it will be destroyed by mutual dissension itself.
Having said this, the Blessed One, at the time of dawn, having gone to the shore of the Ganges, having done washing of his face, waiting for the time of the alms round, sat down.

"*Aggito vā*".
153
<p n="153" rend="bodytext"><hi rend="paranum">153</hi><hi rend="dot">.</hi> Atha <pb ed="M" n="2.0075"/> kho sunidhavassakārā magadhamahāmattā yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkamiṃsu; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavatā saddhiṃ sammodiṃsu, sammodanīyaṃ kathaṃ sāraṇīyaṃ vītisāretvā ekamantaṃ aṭṭhaṃsu, ekamantaṃ ṭhitā kho sunidhavassakārā magadhamahāmattā bhagavantaṃ etadavocuṃ – ‘‘adhivāsetu no bhavaṃ gotamo ajjatanāya bhattaṃ saddhiṃ bhikkhusaṅghenā’’ti. Adhivāsesi bhagavā tuṇhībhāvena. Atha kho sunidhavassakārā magadhamahāmattā bhagavato adhivāsanaṃ viditvā yena sako āvasatho tenupasaṅkamiṃsu; upasaṅkamitvā sake āvasathe paṇītaṃ khādanīyaṃ bhojanīyaṃ paṭiyādāpetvā bhagavato kālaṃ ārocāpesuṃ – ‘‘kālo, bho gotama, niṭṭhitaṃ bhatta’’nti.</p> <p rend="bodytext">Atha kho bhagavā pubbaṇhasamayaṃ nivāsetvā pattacīvaramādāya saddhiṃ bhikkhusaṅghena yena sunidhavassakārānaṃ magadhamahāmattānaṃ <pb ed="T" n="2.0105"/> āvasatho tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā paññatte āsane nisīdi. Atha kho sunidhavassakārā magadhamahāmattā buddhappamukhaṃ bhikkhusaṅghaṃ paṇītena khādanīyena bhojanīyena sahatthā santappesuṃ sampavāresuṃ. Atha kho sunidhavassakārā magadhamahāmattā bhagavantaṃ bhuttāviṃ onītapattapāṇiṃ aññataraṃ nīcaṃ āsanaṃ gahetvā ekamantaṃ nisīdiṃsu. Ekamantaṃ nisinne kho sunidhavassakāre magadhamahāmatte bhagavā imāhi gāthāhi anumodi –</p> <pb ed="T" n="2.0105"/> <p rend="gatha1">‘‘Yasmiṃ <pb ed="V" n="2.0070"/> padese kappeti, vāsaṃ paṇḍitajātiyo;</p> <pb ed="V" n="2.0070"/> <p rend="gathalast">Sīlavantettha bhojetvā, saññate brahmacārayo <note>brahmacārino (syā.)</note>.</p> <note>brahmacārino (syā.)</note> <p rend="gatha1">‘‘Yā tattha devatā āsuṃ, tāsaṃ dakkhiṇamādise;</p> <p rend="gathalast">Tā pūjitā pūjayanti <note>pūjitā pūjayanti naṃ (ka.)</note>, mānitā mānayanti naṃ.</p> <note>pūjitā pūjayanti naṃ (ka.)</note> <p rend="gatha1">‘‘Tato <pb ed="P" n="2.0089"/> naṃ anukampanti, mātā puttaṃva orasaṃ;</p> <pb ed="P" n="2.0089"/> <p rend="gathalast">Devatānukampito poso, sadā bhadrāni passatī’’ti.</p> <p rend="bodytext">Atha kho bhagavā sunidhavassakāre magadhamahāmatte imāhi gāthāhi anumoditvā uṭṭhāyāsanā pakkāmi.</p>
Then Sunidha and Vassakāra, the chief ministers of Magadha, went to the Blessed One; having gone, they exchanged courteous greetings with the Blessed One, and after exchanging friendly greetings and courtesies, they stood to one side. Standing to one side, Sunidha and Vassakāra, the chief ministers of Magadha, said this to the Blessed One: “May Master Gotama consent to our meal today, together with the Saṅgha of monks.”

The Blessed One consented by maintaining silence ( *tuṇhībhāvena* ).

Then Sunidha and Vassakāra, the chief ministers of Magadha, understanding the Blessed One’s acquiescence, went to their own dwelling. Having gone, they had exquisite staple and non-staple food prepared in their own dwelling, and announced the time to the Blessed One: “It’s time, Master Gotama; the meal is ready.”

Then, in the forenoon, the Blessed One, having dressed and taken his bowl and robes, together with the Saṃgha of monks, went to the dwelling of Sunidha and Vassakāra, the chief ministers of Magadha; having gone, he sat down on the prepared seat.

Then Sunidha and Vassakāra, the chief ministers of Magadha, with their own hands served and satisfied the Saṃgha of monks, with the Buddha at its head, with exquisite staple and non-staple food.

Then Sunidha and Vassakāra, the chief ministers of Magadha, when the Blessed One had finished his meal and withdrawn his hand from the bowl, took a low seat and sat to one side.

While Sunidha and Vassakāra, the chief ministers of Magadha, were sitting to one side, the Blessed One rejoiced them with these verses:

“In whatever place the wise person makes a dwelling,

having fed the virtuous, the restrained, the ব্রহ্মচারীs (brahmacārī):

Whatever deities are there, to them one should dedicate the offering;

being honored, they honor [him], being revered, they revere [him].

Then they will feel sympathy for him, like a mother for her own child;

a person with whom the deities sympathize always sees auspicious things.”

Then the Blessed One, having rejoiced Sunidha and Vassakāra, the chief ministers of Magadha, with these verses, got up from his seat and departed.
<p n="153" rend="bodytext"><hi rend="paranum">153</hi><hi rend="dot">.</hi> Sunidhavassakārāpi – ‘‘amhākaṃ rājā samaṇassa gotamassa upaṭṭhāko, so amhe pucchissati, ‘satthā kira pāṭaligāmaṃ agamāsi, tassa santikaṃ upasaṅkamittha, na upasaṅkamitthā’ti. Upasaṅkamimhāti ca vutte – ‘nimantayittha, na nimantayitthā’ti ca pucchissati. Na nimantayimhāti ca vutte amhākaṃ dosaṃ āropetvā niggaṇhissati. Idaṃ cāpi mayaṃ āgataṭṭhāne nagaraṃ māpema, samaṇassa kho pana gotamassa gatagataṭṭhāne kāḷakaṇṇisattā <pb ed="V" n="2.0118"/> paṭikkamanti, taṃ mayaṃ nagaramaṅgalaṃ vadāpessāmā’’ti cintetvā satthāraṃ upasaṅkamitvā nimantayiṃsu. Tasmā – ‘‘atha kho sunidhavassakārā’’tiādi vuttaṃ.</p> <p rend="bodytext"><hi rend="bold">Pubbaṇhasamaya</hi>nti pubbaṇhakāle. <hi rend="bold">Nivāsetvā</hi>ti gāmappavesananīhārena nivāsanaṃ nivāsetvā kāyabandhanaṃ <pb ed="P" n="2.0542"/> bandhitvā. <hi rend="bold">Pattacīvaramādāyā</hi>ti pattañca cīvarañca ādiyitvā kāyappaṭibaddhaṃ katvā.</p> <hi rend="bold">Pubbaṇhasamaya</hi> <hi rend="bold">Nivāsetvā</hi> <pb ed="P" n="2.0542"/> <hi rend="bold">Pattacīvaramādāyā</hi> <p rend="bodytext"><hi rend="bold">Sīlavantetthā</hi>ti sīlavante ettha. <hi rend="bold">Saññate</hi>ti kāyavācāmanehi saññate.</p> <hi rend="bold">Sīlavantetthā</hi> <hi rend="bold">Saññate</hi> <p rend="bodytext"><hi rend="bold">Tāsaṃ</hi><pb ed="M" n="2.0132"/><hi rend="bold">dakkhiṇamādiye</hi>ti saṅghassa dinne cattāro paccaye tāsaṃ gharadevatānaṃ ādiseyya, pattiṃ dadeyya. <hi rend="bold">Pūjitā pūjayantī</hi>ti – ‘‘ime manussā amhākaṃ ñātakāpi na honti, evampi no pattiṃ dentī’’ti ārakkhaṃ susaṃvihitaṃ karothāti suṭṭhu ārakkhaṃ karonti. <hi rend="bold">Mānitā mānayantī</hi>ti kālānukālaṃ balikammakaraṇena mānitā ‘‘ete manussā amhākaṃ ñātakāpi na honti, catumāsachamāsantare no balikammaṃ karontī’’ti mānenti, mānentiyo uppannaṃ parissayaṃ haranti.</p> <hi rend="bold">Tāsaṃ</hi> <pb ed="M" n="2.0132"/> <hi rend="bold">dakkhiṇamādiye</hi> <hi rend="bold">Pūjitā pūjayantī</hi> <hi rend="bold">Mānitā mānayantī</hi> <p rend="bodytext"><hi rend="bold">Tato na</hi>nti tato naṃ paṇḍitajātikaṃ manussaṃ. <hi rend="bold">Orasa</hi>nti ure ṭhapetvā saṃvaḍḍhitaṃ, yathā mātā orasaṃ puttaṃ anukampati, uppannaparissayaharaṇatthameva tassa vāyamati, evaṃ anukampantīti attho. <hi rend="bold">Bhadrāni passatī</hi>ti sundarāni passati.</p> <hi rend="bold">Tato na</hi> <hi rend="bold">Orasa</hi> <hi rend="bold">Bhadrāni passatī</hi>
Here is the translation of the provided text into English:

153. Sunidha and Vassakāra [said further]: "Our king is a supporter of the *śramaṇa* Gautama. He will ask us, 'Did the teacher go to Pāṭaligāma? Did you approach him, or did you not approach him?'"

If we say that we approached him, he will ask, "Did you invite him, or did you not invite him?"

If we say that we did not invite him, he will find fault with us and punish us.

Moreover, we are building a city at this arrival place. Black-eared spirits depart from the places the *śramaṇa* Gautama frequents. Therefore, we will have him consecrate the city," thinking this, they approached the teacher and invited him.

Therefore, it was said, "Then Sunidha and Vassakāra..." and so forth.

*pubbaṇhasamaya* means in the morning.

*nivāsetvā* means having dressed, with the intention of entering the village, having put on the body-binding [garment],

having bound [it].

*pattacīvaramādāyā* means having taken the bowl (*patra*) and robe (*cīvara*), having fastened it to the body.

*pubbaṇhasamaya nivāsetvā pattacīvaramādāyā*

*śīlavantetthā* means the virtuous ones here.

*saññate* means restrained in body, speech, and mind.

*śīlavantetthā saññate*

*tāsaṃ dakkhiṇamādiye* means to instruct those household deities to assign the four requisites given to the *saṃgha*, and to give them a share.

*pūjitā pūjayantī* means - "These people are not even our relatives, yet they give us a share," thinking this, they provide well-arranged protection; they provide excellent protection.

*mānitā mānayantī* means honored by making offerings (*balikamma*) at the appropriate time. "These people are not even our relatives, [yet] every four or six months they make offerings to us," thinking this, they honor them; the honoring ones remove any arisen danger.

*tāsaṃ dakkhiṇamādiye pūjitā pūjayantī mānitā mānayantī*

*tato na* means then a man of wise birth.

*orasa* means having placed on the breast and raised, just as a mother has compassion on her own son, she strives only for the sake of removing arisen danger; thus, the meaning is having compassion.

*bhadrāni passatī* means sees beautiful things (*sundarāṇi*).

*tato na orasa bhadrāni passatī*
154
<p n="154" rend="bodytext"><hi rend="paranum">154</hi><hi rend="dot">.</hi> Tena <pb ed="M" n="2.0076"/> kho pana samayena sunidhavassakārā magadhamahāmattā bhagavantaṃ piṭṭhito piṭṭhito anubandhā honti – ‘‘yenajja samaṇo gotamo dvārena nikkhamissati, taṃ gotamadvāraṃ nāma bhavissati. Yena titthena gaṅgaṃ nadiṃ tarissati, taṃ gotamatitthaṃ nāma bhavissatī’’ti. Atha kho bhagavā yena dvārena nikkhami <pb ed="T" n="2.0106"/>, taṃ gotamadvāraṃ nāma ahosi. Atha kho bhagavā yena gaṅgā nadī tenupasaṅkami. Tena kho pana samayena gaṅgā nadī pūrā hoti samatittikā kākapeyyā. Appekacce manussā nāvaṃ pariyesanti, appekacce uḷumpaṃ pariyesanti, appekacce kullaṃ bandhanti apārā <note>pārā (sī. syā. ka.), orā (vi. mahāvagga)</note>, pāraṃ gantukāmā. Atha kho bhagavā – seyyathāpi nāma balavā puriso samiñjitaṃ vā bāhaṃ pasāreyya, pasāritaṃ vā bāhaṃ samiñjeyya, evameva – gaṅgāya nadiyā orimatīre antarahito pārimatīre paccuṭṭhāsi saddhiṃ bhikkhusaṅghena. Addasā kho bhagavā te manusse appekacce nāvaṃ pariyesante appekacce uḷumpaṃ pariyesante appekacce kullaṃ bandhante apārā pāraṃ gantukāme. Atha kho bhagavā etamatthaṃ viditvā tāyaṃ velāyaṃ imaṃ udānaṃ udānesi –</p> <p rend="gatha1">‘‘Ye taranti aṇṇavaṃ saraṃ, setuṃ katvāna visajja pallalāni;</p> <p rend="gathalast">Kullañhi jano bandhati <note>kullaṃ jano ca bandhati (syā.), kullaṃ hi jano pabandhati (sī. pī. ka.)</note>, tiṇṇā <note>nitiṇṇā, na tiṇṇā (ka.)</note> medhāvino janā’’ti.</p> <note>kullaṃ jano ca bandhati (syā.), kullaṃ hi jano pabandhati (sī. pī. ka.)</note> <note>nitiṇṇā, na tiṇṇā (ka.)</note> <p rend="centre">Paṭhamabhāṇavāro.</p> <p rend="subhead">Ariyasaccakathā</p>
Then, at that time, Sunidha and Vassakāra, the chief ministers of Magadha, were following behind the Blessed One, step by step, saying: “Whatever gate the ascetic Gotama will depart through today, that will be called the Gotama Gate. And whatever ford he crosses the river Ganges by, that will be called the Gotama Ford.”

Then the Blessed One departed through a certain gate, and that gate was called the Gotama Gate.

Then the Blessed One approached the river Ganges. At that time, the river Ganges was full to the brim, so that a crow could drink from it. Some people were searching for boats, some were searching for rafts, and some were binding together rafts, wanting to go from this shore to the other shore.

Then the Blessed One—just as a strong man might extend his flexed arm or flex his extended arm—vanished from the near bank of the Ganges River and reappeared on the far bank together with the *bhikkhu-saṅgha*, the community of monks.

The Blessed One saw those people—some searching for boats, some searching for rafts, and some binding rafts—wanting to go from this shore to the other shore.

Then, having understood this matter, the Blessed One at that time uttered this inspired utterance:

"Those who cross the ocean, the stream, having made a bridge, abandon the pools;

For people still bind together a raft, while the wise have already crossed over."

The first recitation section.

The Discourse on the Noble Truths.
<p n="154" rend="bodytext"><hi rend="paranum">154</hi><hi rend="dot">.</hi><hi rend="bold">Uḷumpa</hi>nti pāragamanatthāya āṇiyo koṭṭetvā kataṃ. <hi rend="bold">Kulla</hi>nti valliādīhi bandhitvā kataṃ.</p> <p rend="bodytext">‘‘Ye taranti aṇṇava’’nti gāthāya <hi rend="bold">aṇṇava</hi>nti sabbantimena paricchedena yojanamattaṃ gambhīrassa ca puthulassa ca udakaṭṭhānassetaṃ adhivacanaṃ. <hi rend="bold">Sara</hi>nti idha nadī adhippetā. Idaṃ vuttaṃ hoti, ye gambhīravitthataṃ taṇhāsaraṃ taranti, te ariyamaggasaṅkhātaṃ setuṃ katvāna. <hi rend="bold">Visajja pallalāni</hi> anāmasitvā udakabharitāni ninnaṭṭhānāni. Ayaṃ pana idaṃ appamattakaṃ taritukāmopi kullañhi jano pabandhati. Buddhā ca buddhasāvakā ca vināyeva kullena tiṇṇā medhāvino janāti.</p> <hi rend="bold">aṇṇava</hi> <hi rend="bold">Sara</hi> <hi rend="bold">Visajja pallalāni</hi> <p rend="centre">Paṭhamabhāṇavāravaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.</p> <p rend="subhead">Ariyasaccakathāvaṇṇanā</p>
154. *Uḷumpa* means made by hammering pegs (*āṇi*) for the sake of crossing over (*pāragamanatthāya*).
*Kulla* means made by binding with creepers (*valli*) and the like.

"Those who cross the ocean (*aṇṇava*)" – in this verse, *aṇṇava* is a designation (*adhivacanaṃ*) for a body of water (*udakaṭṭhānassa*) that is approximately a league (*yojanamattaṃ*) deep (*gambhīrassa*) and wide (*puthulassa*) in its final extent (*sabbantimena paricchedena*).
*Sara* here implies a river (*nadī adhippetā*).
This means, those who cross the deep and vast pool of craving (*taṇhāsaraṃ*), having made a bridge (*setuṃ katvāna*) known as the Noble Path (*ariyamaggasaṅkhātaṃ*).
*Visajja pallalāni* [means] low-lying places (*ninnaṭṭhānāni*) filled with water (*udakabharitāni*), without being touched (*anāmasitvā*).
However, even someone who wants to cross a small amount (*appamattakaṃ taritukāmopi*) binds a raft (*kullañhi jano pabandhati*).
The Buddhas and the disciples of the Buddha, wise ones (*medhāvino*), cross over (*tiṇṇā*) by means of a raft (*kullena*).

*Aṇṇava, Sara, Visajja pallalāni.* The explanation of the first section is complete.

Explanation of the Discourse on the Noble Truths (*ariyasaccakathāvaṇṇanā*).
155
<p n="155" rend="bodytext"><hi rend="paranum">155</hi><hi rend="dot">.</hi> Atha <pb ed="V" n="2.0071"/><pb ed="P" n="2.0090"/> kho bhagavā āyasmantaṃ ānandaṃ āmantesi – ‘‘āyāmānanda, yena koṭigāmo tenupasaṅkamissāmā’’ti. ‘‘Evaṃ, bhante’’ti kho āyasmā ānando bhagavato paccassosi. Atha kho bhagavā mahatā bhikkhusaṅghena saddhiṃ yena koṭigāmo tadavasari. Tatra sudaṃ <pb ed="T" n="2.0107"/> bhagavā koṭigāme viharati. Tatra kho bhagavā bhikkhū āmantesi –</p> <p rend="bodytext">‘‘Catunnaṃ <pb ed="M" n="2.0077"/>, bhikkhave, ariyasaccānaṃ ananubodhā appaṭivedhā evamidaṃ dīghamaddhānaṃ sandhāvitaṃ saṃsaritaṃ mamañceva tumhākañca. Katamesaṃ catunnaṃ? Dukkhassa, bhikkhave, ariyasaccassa ananubodhā appaṭivedhā evamidaṃ dīghamaddhānaṃ sandhāvitaṃ saṃsaritaṃ mamañceva tumhākañca. Dukkhasamudayassa, bhikkhave, ariyasaccassa ananubodhā appaṭivedhā evamidaṃ dīghamaddhānaṃ sandhāvitaṃ saṃsaritaṃ mamañceva tumhākañca. Dukkhanirodhassa, bhikkhave, ariyasaccassa ananubodhā appaṭivedhā evamidaṃ dīghamaddhānaṃ sandhāvitaṃ saṃsaritaṃ mamañceva tumhākañca. Dukkhanirodhagāminiyā paṭipadāya, bhikkhave, ariyasaccassa ananubodhā appaṭivedhā evamidaṃ dīghamaddhānaṃ sandhāvitaṃ saṃsaritaṃ mamañceva tumhākañca. Tayidaṃ, bhikkhave, dukkhaṃ ariyasaccaṃ anubuddhaṃ paṭividdhaṃ, dukkhasamudayaṃ <note>dukkhasamudayo (syā.)</note> ariyasaccaṃ anubuddhaṃ paṭividdhaṃ, dukkhanirodhaṃ <note>dukkhanirodho (syā.)</note> ariyasaccaṃ anubuddhaṃ paṭividdhaṃ, dukkhanirodhagāminī paṭipadā ariyasaccaṃ anubuddhaṃ paṭividdhaṃ, ucchinnā bhavataṇhā, khīṇā bhavanetti, natthidāni punabbhavo’’ti. Idamavoca bhagavā. Idaṃ vatvāna sugato athāparaṃ etadavoca satthā –</p> <pb ed="M" n="2.0077"/> <note>dukkhasamudayo (syā.)</note> <note>dukkhanirodho (syā.)</note> <p rend="gatha1">‘‘Catunnaṃ <pb ed="P" n="2.0091"/> ariyasaccānaṃ, yathābhūtaṃ adassanā;</p> <pb ed="P" n="2.0091"/> <p rend="gathalast">Saṃsitaṃ dīghamaddhānaṃ, tāsu tāsveva jātisu.</p> <p rend="gatha1">Tāni etāni diṭṭhāni, bhavanetti samūhatā;</p> <p rend="gathalast">Ucchinnaṃ mūlaṃ dukkhassa, natthi dāni punabbhavo’’ti.</p> <p rend="bodytext">Tatrapi <pb ed="T" n="2.0108"/> sudaṃ bhagavā koṭigāme viharanto etadeva bahulaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ dhammiṃ kathaṃ karoti – ‘‘iti sīlaṃ, iti samādhi, iti paññā. Sīlaparibhāvito samādhi mahapphalo hoti mahānisaṃso. Samādhiparibhāvitā paññā mahapphalā hoti mahānisaṃsā. Paññāparibhāvitaṃ cittaṃ sammadeva āsavehi vimuccati, seyyathidaṃ – kāmāsavā, bhavāsavā, avijjāsavā’’ti.</p> <pb ed="T" n="2.0108"/> <p rend="subhead">Anāvattidhammasambodhiparāyaṇā</p>
155. Then the Blessed One spoke to the Venerable Ānanda, saying: “Come, Ānanda, we will go to Koṭigāma.”

“So be it, O Lord,” replied the Venerable Ānanda to the Blessed One.

Then the Blessed One, together with a large Saṅgha of monks, went to Koṭigāma.

There the Blessed One stayed near Koṭigāma.

There the Blessed One addressed the monks, saying:

“It is through not understanding, not penetrating the Four Noble Truths (*catunnaṃ ariyasaccānaṃ*), monks, that this long course of existence has been wandered through by me as well as by you.

Which four? It is through not understanding the noble truth of suffering (*dukkhaṃ ariyasaccaṃ*), monks, that this long course of existence has been wandered through by me as well as by you.

It is through not understanding the noble truth of the origin of suffering (*dukkhasamudayaṃ ariyasaccaṃ*), monks, that this long course of existence has been wandered through by me as well as by you.

It is through not understanding the noble truth of the cessation of suffering (*dukkhanirodhaṃ ariyasaccaṃ*), monks, that this long course of existence has been wandered through by me as well as by you.

It is through not understanding the noble truth of the path leading to the cessation of suffering (*dukkhanirodhagāminiyā paṭipadāya ariyasaccassa*), monks, that this long course of existence has been wandered through by me as well as by you.

But now, monks, that the noble truth of suffering has been understood and penetrated, the noble truth of the origin of suffering has been understood and penetrated, the noble truth of the cessation of suffering has been understood and penetrated, and the noble truth of the path leading to the cessation of suffering has been understood and penetrated, craving for becoming has been cut off, the conduit to existence has been destroyed, now there is no further existence.”

This is what the Blessed One said.

Having said this, the Well-Gone, the Teacher, said further:

“Through not seeing the Four Noble Truths (*catunnaṃ ariyasaccānaṃ*), in accordance with reality,

we have wandered through a long course of existence, in those very births.

These have been seen, the guide to existence is eradicated;

the root of suffering is cut off, now there is no further existence.”

And also at Koṭigāma the Blessed One often gave this Dhamma talk to the bhikkhus: “Such and such is virtue (*sīlaṃ*); such and such is concentration (*samādhi*); and such and such is wisdom (*paññā*).

Great becomes the fruit, great is the gain of concentration when it is fully developed by virtuous conduct;

great becomes the fruit, great is the gain of wisdom when it is fully developed by concentration;

utterly freed from the taints is the mind that is fully developed in wisdom, that is, from the taint of sensual desire, the taint of becoming, and the taint of ignorance.”

Leading to the ultimate wisdom and awakening from which there is no return.
<p n="155" rend="bodytext"><hi rend="paranum">155</hi><hi rend="dot">.</hi><hi rend="bold">Koṭigāmo</hi>ti <pb ed="V" n="2.0119"/> mahāpanādassa pāsādakoṭiyaṃ katagāmo. <hi rend="bold">Ariyasaccāna</hi>nti ariyabhāvakarānaṃ saccānaṃ. <hi rend="bold">Ananubodhā</hi>ti abujjhanena ajānanena. <hi rend="bold">Appaṭivedhā</hi>ti appaṭivijjhanena. <hi rend="bold">Sandhāvita</hi>nti bhavato bhavaṃ gamanavasena <pb ed="P" n="2.0543"/> sandhāvitaṃ. <hi rend="bold">Saṃsarita</hi>nti punappunaṃ gamanāgamanavasena saṃsaritaṃ. <hi rend="bold">Mamañceva</hi><pb ed="M" n="2.0133"/><hi rend="bold">tumhākañcā</hi>ti mayā ca tumhehi ca. Atha vā <hi rend="bold">sandhāvitaṃ saṃsarita</hi>nti sandhāvanaṃ saṃsaraṇaṃ mamañceva tumhākañca ahosīti emamettha attho veditabbo. <hi rend="bold">Bhavanetti samūhatā</hi>ti bhavato bhavaṃ nayanasamatthā taṇhārajju suṭṭhu hatā chinnā appavattikatā.</p> <p rend="subhead">Anāvattidhammasambodhiparāyaṇavaṇṇanā</p>
155. *Koṭigāmo* means a village made in the *pāsāda-koṭi* (mansion-summit) of Mahāpanāda.

*Ariyasaccāna* means of the truths that produce noble states (*ariyabhāva*).

*Ananubodhā* means by non-awakening, by non-knowing.

*Appaṭivedhā* means by non-penetration.

*Sandhāvita* means according to the manner of going from existence to existence (*bhavato bhavaṃ gamanavasena*) sandhāvitaṃ.

*Saṃsarita* means *saṃsaritaṃ* according to the manner of repeated going and coming (*punappunaṃ gamanāgamanavasena*).

*Mamañceva tumhākañcā* means by me and by you.

Or else, *sandhāvitaṃ saṃsarita* means the *sandhāvanaṃ* and *saṃsaraṇaṃ* were mine and yours; this is the meaning to be understood here.

*Bhavanetti samūhatā* means the aggregate of the craving-rope (*taṇhārajju*) that is capable of leading from existence to existence (*bhavato bhavaṃ nayanasamatthā*), is well struck, cut off, and without possibility of recurrence (*appavattikatā*).

Explanation of non-returning, *dharma*, complete awakening (*sambodhi*), final refuge (*parāyaṇa*).
156
<p n="156" rend="bodytext"><hi rend="paranum">156</hi><hi rend="dot">.</hi> Atha <pb ed="V" n="2.0072"/> kho bhagavā koṭigāme yathābhirantaṃ viharitvā āyasmantaṃ ānandaṃ āmantesi – ‘‘āyāmānanda, yena nātikā <note>nādikā (syā. pī.)</note> tenupaṅkamissāmā’’ti. ‘‘Evaṃ, bhante’’ti kho āyasmā ānando bhagavato <pb ed="M" n="2.0078"/> paccassosi. Atha kho bhagavā mahatā bhikkhusaṅghena saddhiṃ yena nātikā tadavasari. Tatrapi sudaṃ bhagavā nātike viharati giñjakāvasathe. Atha kho āyasmā ānando yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṃ abhivādetvā ekamantaṃ nisīdi. Ekamantaṃ nisinno kho āyasmā ānando bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – ‘‘sāḷho nāma, bhante, bhikkhu nātike kālaṅkato, tassa kā gati, ko abhisamparāyo? Nandā nāma, bhante, bhikkhunī nātike kālaṅkatā, tassā kā gati, ko abhisamparāyo? Sudatto <pb ed="P" n="2.0092"/> nāma, bhante, upāsako nātike kālaṅkato, tassa kā gati, ko abhisamparāyo? Sujātā nāma, bhante, upāsikā nātike kālaṅkatā, tassā kā gati <pb ed="T" n="2.0109"/>, ko abhisamparāyo? Kukkuṭo <note>kakudho (syā.)</note> nāma, bhante, upāsako nātike kālaṅkato, tassa kā gati, ko abhisamparāyo? Kāḷimbo <note>kāliṅgo (pī.), kāraḷimbo (syā.)</note> nāma, bhante, upāsako…pe… nikaṭo nāma, bhante, upāsako… kaṭissaho <note>kaṭissabho (sī. pī.)</note> nāma, bhante, upāsako… tuṭṭho nāma, bhante, upāsako… santuṭṭho nāma, bhante, upāsako… bhaddo <note>bhaṭo (syā.)</note> nāma, bhante, upāsako… subhaddo <note>subhaṭo (syā.)</note> nāma, bhante, upāsako nātike kālaṅkato, tassa kā gati, ko abhisamparāyo’’ti?</p>
156.

Then the Blessed One, having stayed near Koṭigāma as long as he pleased, said to Venerable Ānanda, “Come, Ānanda, we will head for Nādikā.”

“Yes, venerable sir,” Ānanda replied to the Blessed One.

Then the Blessed One, together with a large *bhikkhu-saṃgha* (community of monks), went to Nādikā.

There he stayed near Nādikā at the Giñjakāvasatha (Brick Hall).

Then Venerable Ānanda approached the Blessed One, and after paying homage to him, sat down at one side.

As he was sitting there, Venerable Ānanda said to the Blessed One, “Sāḷha, venerable sir, a *bhikkhu* (monk) has passed away in Nādikā. What is his *gati* (destination), what his *abhisamparāya* (future state)? Nandā, venerable sir, a *bhikkhunī* (nun) has passed away in Nādikā. What is her destination, what her future state? Sudatta, venerable sir, a male lay follower (*upāsaka*) has passed away in Nādikā. What is his destination, what his future state? Sujātā, venerable sir, a female lay follower (*upāsikā*) has passed away in Nādikā. What is her destination, what her future state? Kukkuṭa, venerable sir, a male lay follower has passed away in Nādikā. What is his destination, what his future state? Kāḷimba, venerable sir, a male lay follower… Nikaṭa, venerable sir, a male lay follower… Kaṭissaha, venerable sir, a male lay follower… Tuṭṭha, venerable sir, a male lay follower… Santuṭṭha, venerable sir, a male lay follower… Bhadda, venerable sir, a male lay follower… Subhadda, venerable sir, a male lay follower has passed away in Nādikā. What is his destination, what his future state?”
<p n="156" rend="bodytext"><hi rend="paranum">156</hi><hi rend="dot">.</hi><hi rend="bold">Nātikā</hi>ti ekaṃ taḷākaṃ nissāya dvinnaṃ cūḷapitumahāpituputtānaṃ dve gāmā. <hi rend="bold">Nātike</hi>ti ekasmiṃ ñātigāmake. <hi rend="bold">Giñjakāvasathe</hi>ti iṭṭhakāmaye āvasathe.</p>
nātikā: two villages of two sons of nephews, relying on one pond.
nātike: in one village of relatives.
giñjakāvasathe: in a brick-made dwelling.
157
<p n="157" rend="bodytext"><hi rend="paranum">157</hi><hi rend="dot">.</hi> ‘‘Sāḷho, ānanda, bhikkhu āsavānaṃ khayā anāsavaṃ cetovimuttiṃ paññāvimuttiṃ diṭṭheva dhamme sayaṃ abhiññā sacchikatvā upasampajja vihāsi. Nandā, ānanda, bhikkhunī pañcannaṃ orambhāgiyānaṃ saṃyojanānaṃ parikkhayā opapātikā tattha parinibbāyinī anāvattidhammā tasmā lokā. Sudatto, ānanda, upāsako tiṇṇaṃ saṃyojanānaṃ parikkhayā rāgadosamohānaṃ tanuttā sakadāgāmī sakideva imaṃ lokaṃ āgantvā dukkhassantaṃ karissati. Sujātā, ānanda, upāsikā tiṇṇaṃ saṃyojanānaṃ parikkhayā sotāpannā avinipātadhammā niyatā sambodhiparāyaṇā <note>parāyanā (sī. syā. pī. ka.)</note>. Kukkuṭo, ānanda, upāsako pañcannaṃ orambhāgiyānaṃ saṃyojanānaṃ parikkhayā opapātiko tattha parinibbāyī anāvattidhammo tasmā lokā. Kāḷimbo, ānanda, upāsako…pe… nikaṭo, ānanda, upāsako… kaṭissaho <pb ed="M" n="2.0079"/>, ānanda, upāsako… tuṭṭho, ānanda, upāsako <pb ed="T" n="2.0110"/> … santuṭṭho, ānanda, upāsako… bhaddo, ānanda, upāsako… subhaddo, ānanda, upāsako pañcannaṃ orambhāgiyānaṃ saṃyojanānaṃ parikkhayā opapātiko tattha parinibbāyī anāvattidhammo tasmā lokā <pb ed="P" n="2.0093"/>. Paropaññāsaṃ, ānanda, nātike upāsakā <pb ed="V" n="2.0073"/> kālaṅkatā, pañcannaṃ orambhāgiyānaṃ saṃyojanānaṃ parikkhayā opapātikā tattha parinibbāyino anāvattidhammā tasmā lokā. Sādhikā navuti <note>chādhikā navuti (syā.)</note>, ānanda, nātike upāsakā kālaṅkatā tiṇṇaṃ saṃyojanānaṃ parikkhayā rāgadosamohānaṃ tanuttā sakadāgāmino sakideva imaṃ lokaṃ āgantvā dukkhassantaṃ karissanti. Sātirekāni <note>dasātirekāni (syā.)</note>, ānanda, pañcasatāni nātike upāsakā kālaṅkatā, tiṇṇaṃ saṃyojanānaṃ parikkhayā sotāpannā avinipātadhammā niyatā sambodhiparāyaṇā.</p> <p rend="subhead">Dhammādāsadhammapariyāyā</p>
157. Sāḷha, Ānanda, the monk, through the destruction of the āsavas, has dwelt having attained in this very life, through his own super-knowledge (abhiññā), the undefiled liberation of mind (cetovimutti), the liberation by wisdom (paññāvimutti).

Nandā, Ānanda, the nun, through the destruction of the five lower fetters (pañcannaṃ orambhāgiyānaṃ saṃyojanānaṃ parikkhayā), has arisen spontaneously (opapātikā) and will attain complete liberation (parinibbāyinī) in that very place, not subject to return (anāvattidhammā) from that world (tasmā lokā).

Sudatta, Ānanda, the lay follower (upāsaka), through the destruction of the three fetters (tiṇṇaṃ saṃyojanānaṃ parikkhayā), and with the lessening of greed (rāga), hatred (dosa), and delusion (moha), is a once-returner (sakadāgāmī), who, returning only once more to this world (sakideva imaṃ lokaṃ āgantvā), will make an end of suffering (dukkhassantaṃ karissati).

Sujātā, Ānanda, the female lay follower (upāsikā), through the destruction of the three fetters (tiṇṇaṃ saṃyojanānaṃ parikkhayā), is a stream-enterer (sotāpannā), not subject to falling (avinipātadhammā), certain (niyatā), destined for enlightenment (sambodhiparāyaṇā).

Kukkuṭa, Ānanda, the lay follower (upāsako), through the destruction of the five lower fetters (pañcannaṃ orambhāgiyānaṃ saṃyojanānaṃ parikkhayā), has arisen spontaneously (opapātiko) and will attain complete liberation (parinibbāyī) in that very place, not subject to return (anāvattidhammo) from that world (tasmā lokā).

Kāḷimba, Ānanda, the lay follower (upāsako)... Nikaṭa, Ānanda, the lay follower (upāsako)... Kaṭissaha, Ānanda, the lay follower (upāsako)... Tuṭṭha, Ānanda, the lay follower (upāsako)... Santuṭṭha, Ānanda, the lay follower (upāsako)... Bhadda, Ānanda, the lay follower (upāsako)... Subhadda, Ānanda, the lay follower (upāsako), through the destruction of the five lower fetters (pañcannaṃ orambhāgiyānaṃ saṃyojanānaṃ parikkhayā), has arisen spontaneously (opapātiko) and will attain complete liberation (parinibbāyī) in that very place, not subject to return (anāvattidhammo) from that world (tasmā lokā).

More than fifty, Ānanda, lay followers (upāsakā) in Nātika who have died (kālaṅkatā), through the destruction of the five lower fetters (pañcannaṃ orambhāgiyānaṃ saṃyojanānaṃ parikkhayā), have arisen spontaneously (opapātikā) and will attain complete liberation (parinibbāyino) in that very place, not subject to return (anāvattidhammā) from that world (tasmā lokā).

More than ninety, Ānanda, lay followers (upāsakā) in Nātika who have died (kālaṅkatā), through the destruction of the three fetters (tiṇṇaṃ saṃyojanānaṃ parikkhayā), and with the lessening of greed (rāga), hatred (dosa), and delusion (moha), are once-returners (sakadāgāmino), who, returning only once more to this world (sakideva imaṃ lokaṃ āgantvā), will make an end of suffering (dukkhassantaṃ karissanti).

More than five hundred, Ānanda, lay followers (upāsakā) in Nātika who have died (kālaṅkatā), through the destruction of the three fetters (tiṇṇaṃ saṃyojanānaṃ parikkhayā), are stream-enterers (sotāpannā), not subject to falling (avinipātadhammā), certain (niyatā), destined for enlightenment (sambodhiparāyaṇā).

The Mirror of the Dhamma Discourse (dhammādāsadhammapariyāyā).
<p n="157" rend="bodytext"><hi rend="paranum">157</hi><hi rend="dot">.</hi><hi rend="bold">Orambhāgiyāna</hi>nti heṭṭhābhāgiyānaṃ, kāmabhaveyeva paṭisandhiggāhāpakānanti attho. Oranti laddhanāmehi vā tīhi maggehi pahātabbānītipi <hi rend="bold">orambhāgiyāni.</hi> Tattha kāmacchando, byāpādoti imāni dve samāpattiyā vā avikkhambhitāni, maggena vā asamucchinnāni nibbattavasena uddhaṃ bhāgaṃ rūpabhavañca arūpabhavañca gantuṃ na denti. Sakkāyadiṭṭhiādīni tīṇi tattha nibbattampi ānetvā puna idheva nibbattāpentīti sabbānipi orambhāgiyāneva. <hi rend="bold">Anāvattidhammā</hi>ti paṭisandhivasena anāgamanasabhāvā.</p> <p rend="bodytext"><hi rend="bold">Rāgadosamohānaṃ tanuttā</hi>ti ettha kadāci karahaci uppattiyā ca, pariyuṭṭhānamandatāya cāti dvedhāpi tanubhāvo veditabbo. Sakadāgāmissa hi puthujjanānaṃ viya abhiṇhaṃ rāgādayo nuppajjanti, kadāci karahaci uppajjanti. Uppajjamānā ca puthujjanānaṃ viya bahalabahalā nuppajjanti, makkhikāpattaṃ viya tanukatanukā uppajjanti. Dīghabhāṇakatipiṭakamahāsīvatthero panāha – ‘‘yasmā sakadāgāmissa puttadhītaro honti, orodhā ca honti, tasmā bahalā kilesā. Idaṃ pana bhavatanukavasena kathita’’nti. Taṃ aṭṭhakathāyaṃ – ‘‘sotāpannassa sattabhave ṭhapetvā aṭṭhame bhave bhavatanukaṃ natthi. Sakadāgāmissa dve bhave ṭhapetvā pañcasu bhavesu bhavatanukaṃ natthi. Anāgāmissa rūpārūpabhave ṭhapetvā kāmabhave bhavatanukaṃ natthi. Khīṇāsavassa kismiñci bhave bhavatanukaṃ natthī’’ti vuttattā paṭikkhittaṃ hoti.</p> <hi rend="bold">Rāgadosamohānaṃ tanuttā</hi> <p rend="bodytext"><hi rend="bold">Imaṃ</hi><pb ed="V" n="2.0120"/><hi rend="bold">loka</hi>nti imaṃ kāmāvacaralokaṃ sandhāya vuttaṃ. Ayañcettha <pb ed="P" n="2.0544"/> adhippāyo, sace hi manussesu sakadāgāmiphalaṃ patto devesu nibbattitvā <pb ed="M" n="2.0134"/> arahattaṃ sacchikaroti, iccetaṃ kusalaṃ. Asakkonto pana avassaṃ manussalokaṃ āgantvā sacchikaroti. Devesu sakadāgāmiphalaṃ pattopi sace manussesu nibbattitvā arahattaṃ sacchikaroti, iccetaṃ kusalaṃ. Asakkonto pana avassaṃ devalokaṃ gantvā sacchikarotīti.</p> <hi rend="bold">Imaṃ</hi> <pb ed="V" n="2.0120"/> <hi rend="bold">loka</hi> <pb ed="P" n="2.0544"/> <pb ed="M" n="2.0134"/> <p rend="bodytext"><hi rend="bold">Avinipātadhammo</hi>ti ettha vinipatanaṃ vinipāto, nāssa vinipāto dhammoti avinipātadhammo. Catūsu apāyesu avinipātadhammo catūsu apāyesu avinipātasabhāvoti attho. <hi rend="bold">Niyato</hi>ti dhammaniyāmena niyato. <hi rend="bold">Sambodhiparāyaṇo</hi>ti uparimaggattayasaṅkhātā sambodhi paraṃ ayanaṃ assa gati paṭisaraṇaṃ avassaṃ pattabbāti sambodhiparāyaṇo.</p> <hi rend="bold">Avinipātadhammo</hi> <hi rend="bold">Niyato</hi> <hi rend="bold">Sambodhiparāyaṇo</hi> <p rend="subhead">Dhammādāsadhammapariyāyavaṇṇanā</p>
<p n="157" rend="bodytext"><hi rend="paranum">157</hi><hi rend="dot">.
</hi><hi rend="bold">Orambhāgiyāna</hi>nti: "belonging to the lower division [of existence]"; *heṭṭhābhāgiyānaṃ*, [means] those who grasp rebirth in the realm of desire (kāmadhātu); this is the meaning.
*Oranti laddhanāmehi vā tīhi maggehi pahātabbānītipi* <hi rend="bold">orambhāgiyāni.</hi>
There, desire for sensual pleasures (*kāmacchando*) and ill-will (*byāpāda*): these two are either not suppressed by meditative attainment (samāpatti), or, if not entirely eradicated by the path (magga), they do not allow one to go upwards to the realm of form (rūpabhava) and the formless realm (*arūpabhava*) by way of renewed existence.
Self-view (*sakkāyadiṭṭhi*) and the like, these three, even having brought about rebirth there, again cause rebirth here; therefore, all of these are indeed the lower fetters (*orambhāgiyāneva*).
<hi rend="bold">Anāvattidhammā</hi>ti: the characteristic of not returning, by way of rebirth (*paṭisandhivasena anāgamanasabhāvā*).
</p> <p rend="bodytext"><hi rend="bold">Rāgadosamohānaṃ tanuttā</hi>ti: Because of the attenuation of attachment (rāga), aversion (dosa), and delusion (moha). Here, the attenuated state *tanubhāvo* should be understood in two ways: either by a rare, occasional arising (*kadāci karahaci uppattiyā ca*), or because the arising of defilements is weak (*pariyuṭṭhānamandatāya cāti dvedhāpi tanubhāvo veditabbo*).
For the once-returner (*sakadāgāmissa*), unlike ordinary people (*puthujjanānaṃ viya*), attachment (*rāga*) and the like do not frequently arise (*abhiṇhaṃ rāgādayo nuppajjanti*); they arise only occasionally (*kadāci karahaci uppajjanti*).
And when they arise, they do not arise thickly and densely like those of ordinary people (*uppajjamānā ca puthujjanānaṃ viya bahalabahalā nuppajjanti*); they arise thinly, like a fly's wing (*makkhikāpattaṃ viya tanukatanukā uppajjanti*).
The Venerable Dīghabhāṇakatipiṭakamahāsīvatthera said: “Because the once-returner (*sakadāgāmissa*) has sons and daughters (*puttadhītaro honti*), and also has a harem (*orodhā ca honti*), therefore the defilements (*kilesā*) are thick (*bahalā*).
However, this is spoken of in terms of attenuation of existence (*idaṃ pana bhavatanukavasena kathita’’nti*)."
In the commentary (*aṭṭhakathāyaṃ*) on this it says: "Having placed the stream-enterer (*sotāpannassa*) in seven existences, there is no attenuation of existence in the eighth existence (*sattabhave ṭhapetvā aṭṭhame bhave bhavatanukaṃ natthi*).
Having placed the once-returner (*sakadāgāmissa*) in two existences, there is no attenuation of existence in the five existences (*dve bhave ṭhapetvā pañcasu bhavesu bhavatanukaṃ natthi*).
Having placed the non-returner (*anāgāmissa*) in the realms of form and formlessness (*rūpārūpabhave ṭhapetvā*), there is no attenuation of existence in the realm of desire (*kāmabhave bhavatanukaṃ natthi*).
Because it has been said that for the *arhat* there is no attenuation of existence in any existence whatsoever (*khīṇāsavassa kismiñci bhave bhavatanukaṃ natthī’’ti vuttattā*), it is rejected (*paṭikkhittaṃ hoti*)."
</p> <hi rend="bold">Rāgadosamohānaṃ tanuttā</hi> <p rend="bodytext"><hi rend="bold">Imaṃ</hi><pb ed="v" n="2.
0120"/><hi rend="bold">loka</hi>nti: "*loka*", [means] this (*imaṃ*) world of the realm of desire (kāmāvacaralokaṃ); referring to this, it was said (*sandhāya vuttaṃ*).
And here (*ayañcettha*) the intention (*adhippāyo*) is: if, having attained the fruit of once-returning (*sakadāgāmiphalaṃ patto*) among humans (*manussesu*), one is reborn (*nibbattitvā*) among the gods (*devesu*) and <pb ed="m" n="2.
0134"/> realizes *arhatship* (*arahattaṃ sacchikaroti*), this is skillful (*iccetaṃ kusalaṃ*).
But if one is unable (*asakkonto pana*), one will necessarily (*avassaṃ*) come to the human world (*manussalokaṃ āgantvā*) and realize it (*sacchikaroti*).
Even having attained the fruit of once-returning (*sakadāgāmiphalaṃ pattopi*) among the gods (*devesu*), if one is reborn among humans (*manussesu nibbattitvā*) and realizes *arhatship* (*arahattaṃ sacchikaroti*), this is skillful (*iccetaṃ kusalaṃ*).
But if one is unable (*asakkonto pana*), one will necessarily (*avassaṃ*) go to the world of the gods (*devalokaṃ gantvā*) and realize it (*sacchikarotīti*).
</p> <hi rend="bold">Imaṃ</hi> <pb ed="v" n="2.
0120"/> <hi rend="bold">Loka</hi> <pb ed="p" n="2.
0544"/> <pb ed="m" n="2.
0134"/> <p rend="bodytext"><hi rend="bold">Avinipātadhammo</hi>ti: "*avinipātadhammo*", here, *vinipatanaṃ* [means] ruin (*vinipāto*); *nāssa vinipāto dhammoti avinipātadhammo*: the characteristic of not having ruin.
*Catūsu apāyesu avinipātadhammo*: the quality of not falling into the four woeful states; *catūsu apāyesu avinipātasabhāvoti attho*: this is the meaning.
<hi rend="bold">Niyato</hi>ti: certain; *dhammaniyāmena niyato*: certain by the fixed nature of phenomena.
