She, having said, "Father, for the sake of seeing you," asked, "Father, who came first?"

"The four Great Kings, laywoman."
"Father, are you greater than the four Great Kings?" "These laywomen are like gardeners; since the Teacher's conception, they have been protecting [him] with swords in their hands."

"Father, at the end of their journey, who came?" "Śakra, the lord of the gods."

"Father, are you greater than the king of the gods?" "This laywoman is like a novice who collects goods; at the time of the Teacher's descent from the Tāvatiṃsa heaven, she descended carrying the bowl and robe."

"Father, at the end of his journey, who came shining?" "Laywoman, this is your Blessed One, Teacher, and the Great Brahmā."

"Father, are you greater than my Blessed One, the Great Brahmā?" "Yes, laywoman, on the day of our Teacher's birth, four Great Brahmās received the great man with a golden net."

Then the Brāhmaṇī, thinking, "Such is the power of my son; what will be the power of my son, the Blessed One, the Teacher?" suddenly joy of five colors arose and pervaded her whole body.

The Elder, thinking, "Joy and happiness have arisen in my mother's mind; now is the time for teaching the Dharma," said, "What are you thinking, great laywoman?"

She said, "Father, such is the quality of my son; what will be the quality of the Teacher? This is what I am thinking."

"Great laywoman, at the moment of my Teacher's birth, at the Great Renunciation, at Enlightenment, and at the turning of the Wheel of the Dharma, the ten thousand world-systems trembled. There is no one equal to him in morality, concentration, wisdom, liberation, and the vision of knowledge and liberation." Thus, having expanded, he told a Dharma teaching connected with the Buddha's qualities.

At the end of the Dharma teaching of the Brāhmaṇī's beloved son, having been established in the fruit of stream-entry, she said to her son, "Father, Upatissa, why did you do this? You did not give me such nectar for so long!"

The Elder, thinking, "Now the root of support has been given to my mother, the beautiful Brāhmaṇī; it will suffice with this," having sent away the Brāhmaṇī, he said, "Cunda, what time is it?"

"It is the strong dawn, venerable sir."

"Then assemble the Saṅgha of monks."

"The Saṅgha is assembled, venerable sir."

"Lift me up and seat me, Cunda." Having lifted him up, he seated him.

The Elder addressed the monks: "Friends, for forty-four years that I have been wandering with you, if anything of my bodily or verbal [action] has displeased you, forgive me that, friends."

"Venerable sir, there is nothing unpleasant from you for us who have been wandering without abandoning you like a shadow. But you, forgive us."

Then the Elder, as the tip of the dawn was becoming visible, shaking the great earth, passed into complete nirvāṇa in the element of nirvāṇa without remainder.

Many gods and humans honored the Elder's passing into nirvāṇa.

The venerable Cunda, having taken the bowl and robe and water strainer of the Elder, went to Jetavana, and having taken the venerable Ānanda, approached the Blessed One.

The Blessed One, having taken the water strainer, having spoken of the Elder's virtues in five hundred verses, having had a shrine built for the relics, gave the venerable Ānanda a sign for the purpose of going to Rājagṛha.

The Elder announced to the monks.

The Blessed One, surrounded by a great Saṅgha of monks, went to Rājagṛha.

While there, the venerable Mahāmaudgalyāyana passed into nirvāṇa.

The Blessed One, having taken his relics, having had a shrine built, having departed from Rājagṛha, gradually going towards the Ganges, went to Ukkacela.

There, on the bank of the Ganges, having sat down surrounded by the Saṅgha of monks, having taught a sutra connected with the passing into nirvāṇa of Śāriputra and Maudgalyāyana, having departed from Ukkacela, he went to Vaiśālī.

Thus having gone, then the Blessed One, in the morning time, having dressed, taking his bowl and robe, entered Vaiśālī for alms. This is the sequential story here.

*Nisīdana* here means a piece of skin.
*Udenacetiya* means the *vihāra* (monastery) built at the place of the shrine of Udena Yakṣa is called.

*Gotamakādīsupi*, this same method [applies].

*Bhāvitā* means cultivated.

*Bahulīkatā* means done again and again.

*Yānīkatā* means made like a yoked vehicle.

*Vatthukatā* means made like a thing (vatthu) by way of being a foundation (patiṭṭhāna).

*Anuṭṭhitā* means established (adhiṭṭhitā).

*Paricitā* means accumulated all around, well developed (suvaḍḍhitā).

*Susamāraddhā* means very well begun (suṭṭhu samāraddhā).

Having spoken thus without restriction and then showing [it] with restriction again, [the text] says, “*Tathāgatassa kho*” etc.

Here, *kappa* means life-span (āyukappaṃ).

At that particular time, one should remain completing the life-span of human beings as it is.

*Kappāvasesaṃ vā* means – “Whether little or much” (Dī.
Ni.
2.
7; A.
Ni.
6.
74) or exceeding the stated hundred years.

The elder Mahāsīva, however, said, “There is no such thing as thunder in the wrong place for Buddhas.”

Just as, indeed, in the village of Veḷuva, [he] suppresses the deadly feeling that has arisen for ten months, so too, by repeatedly entering into that attainment for ten months each, one might remain for this fortunate eon (bhadrakappa) itself. Why, then, did [he] not remain? The body that is taken up (upādinnakasarīraṃ), indeed, is overcome by decay etc., and the Buddhas, without attaining the state of non-decay etc., pass into complete nirvāṇa (parinibbāyanti) at the fifth division of life, just at the time when [they] are pleasing and agreeable to many people.

When Buddhas who have attained enlightenment and great disciples have passed into complete nirvāṇa, [the preceptor] ought to remain like a single stump, or surrounded by young novices.

Then – [one] might incur the state of being scorned, [thinking] ‘Alas, the assembly of Buddhas!’

Therefore, [he] did not remain.”

Even when [it is] said thus, it is not pleasing. “Life-span (āyukappaṃ)” is just what is defined in the commentary.
167
<p n="167" rend="bodytext"><hi rend="paranum">167</hi><hi rend="dot">.</hi> Ekamantaṃ nisinnaṃ kho āyasmantaṃ ānandaṃ bhagavā etadavoca – ‘‘ramaṇīyā, ānanda, vesālī, ramaṇīyaṃ udenaṃ cetiyaṃ, ramaṇīyaṃ gotamakaṃ cetiyaṃ, ramaṇīyaṃ sattambaṃ <note>sattambakaṃ (pī.)</note> cetiyaṃ, ramaṇīyaṃ bahuputtaṃ cetiyaṃ, ramaṇīyaṃ sārandadaṃ cetiyaṃ, ramaṇīyaṃ cāpālaṃ cetiyaṃ. Yassa <pb ed="P" n="2.0103"/> kassaci, ānanda, cattāro iddhipādā bhāvitā bahulīkatā yānīkatā vatthukatā anuṭṭhitā paricitā susamāraddhā, so ākaṅkhamāno kappaṃ vā tiṭṭheyya kappāvasesaṃ vā. Tathāgatassa kho, ānanda, cattāro iddhipādā bhāvitā bahulīkatā yānīkatā vatthukatā anuṭṭhitā paricitā susamāraddhā, so ākaṅkhamāno <note>ākaṅkhamāno (?)</note>, ānanda, tathāgato kappaṃ vā tiṭṭheyya kappāvasesaṃ vā’’ti. Evampi kho āyasmā ānando bhagavatā oḷārike nimitte kayiramāne oḷārike obhāse kayiramāne nāsakkhi paṭivijjhituṃ; na bhagavantaṃ yāci – ‘‘tiṭṭhatu, bhante, bhagavā kappaṃ, tiṭṭhatu sugato kappaṃ bahujanahitāya bahujanasukhāya lokānukampāya atthāya hitāya sukhāya devamanussāna’’nti, yathā taṃ mārena pariyuṭṭhitacitto. Dutiyampi <pb ed="M" n="2.0087"/> kho bhagavā…pe… tatiyampi kho bhagavā āyasmantaṃ ānandaṃ āmantesi – ‘‘ramaṇīyā, ānanda, vesālī, ramaṇīyaṃ udenaṃ cetiyaṃ, ramaṇīyaṃ gotamakaṃ cetiyaṃ, ramaṇīyaṃ sattambaṃ cetiyaṃ, ramaṇīyaṃ bahuputtaṃ <pb ed="T" n="2.0121"/> cetiyaṃ, ramaṇīyaṃ sārandadaṃ cetiyaṃ, ramaṇīyaṃ cāpālaṃ cetiyaṃ. Yassa kassaci, ānanda, cattāro iddhipādā bhāvitā bahulīkatā yānīkatā vatthukatā anuṭṭhitā paricitā susamāraddhā, so ākaṅkhamāno kappaṃ vā tiṭṭheyya kappāvasesaṃ vā. Tathāgatassa kho, ānanda, cattāro iddhipādā bhāvitā bahulīkatā yānīkatā vatthukatā anuṭṭhitā paricitā susamāraddhā, so ākaṅkhamāno, ānanda, tathāgato kappaṃ vā tiṭṭheyya kappāvasesaṃ vā’’ti. Evampi kho āyasmā ānando bhagavatā oḷārike nimitte kayiramāne oḷārike obhāse kayiramāne nāsakkhi paṭivijjhituṃ <pb ed="P" n="2.0104"/>; na bhagavantaṃ yāci – ‘‘tiṭṭhatu <pb ed="V" n="2.0080"/>, bhante, bhagavā kappaṃ, tiṭṭhatu sugato kappaṃ bahujanahitāya bahujanasukhāya lokānukampāya atthāya hitāya sukhāya devamanussāna’’nti, yathā taṃ mārena pariyuṭṭhitacitto. Atha kho bhagavā āyasmantaṃ ānandaṃ āmantesi – ‘‘gaccha tvaṃ, ānanda, yassadāni kālaṃ maññasī’’ti. ‘‘Evaṃ, bhante’’ti kho āyasmā ānando bhagavato paṭissutvā uṭṭhāyāsanā bhagavantaṃ abhivādetvā padakkhiṇaṃ katvā avidūre aññatarasmiṃ rukkhamūle nisīdi.</p> <p rend="subhead">Mārayācanakathā</p>
167. Seated to one side, the Blessed One said to venerable Ānanda: "Delightful, Ānanda, is Vesālī; delightful is the Udena Shrine; delightful is the Gotamaka Shrine; delightful is the Sattamba Shrine (or Sattambaka); delightful is the Many Sons' Shrine; delightful is the Sārandada Shrine; delightful is the Cāpāla Shrine.

Whosoever, Ānanda, has developed the four bases of power (*cattāro iddhipādā*), cultivated them, made them his vehicle, made them his foundation, established them, become familiar with them, and properly undertaken them, could, if he wished, remain for an eon (*kappaṃ*) or the remainder of an eon.

The Tathāgata, Ānanda, has developed the four bases of power (*cattāro iddhipādā*), cultivated them, made them his vehicle, made them his foundation, established them, become familiar with them, and properly undertaken them; therefore, the Tathāgata, Ānanda, could, if he wished, remain for an eon (*kappaṃ*) or the remainder of an eon."

Even so, venerable Ānanda, when the Blessed One gave such a blatant sign, such a clear indication, was unable to grasp his meaning; he did not beseech the Blessed One: "May the Blessed One remain, O Lord! May the Well-Gone One remain, O Lord, throughout the world-period, for the welfare and happiness of the multitude, out of compassion for the world, for the benefit, well-being, and happiness of gods and humans!", so much was his mind possessed by Māra.

A second time… A third time, the Blessed One addressed venerable Ānanda: "Delightful, Ānanda, is Vesālī; delightful is the Udena Shrine; delightful is the Gotamaka Shrine; delightful is the Sattamba Shrine; delightful is the Many Sons' Shrine; delightful is the Sārandada Shrine; delightful is the Cāpāla Shrine.

Whosoever, Ānanda, has developed the four bases of power (*cattāro iddhipādā*), cultivated them, made them his vehicle, made them his foundation, established them, become familiar with them, and properly undertaken them, could, if he wished, remain for an eon (*kappaṃ*) or the remainder of an eon.

The Tathāgata, Ānanda, has developed the four bases of power (*cattāro iddhipādā*), cultivated them, made them his vehicle, made them his foundation, established them, become familiar with them, and properly undertaken them; therefore, the Tathāgata, Ānanda, could, if he wished, remain for an eon (*kappaṃ*) or the remainder of an eon."

Even so, venerable Ānanda, when the Blessed One gave such a blatant sign, such a clear indication, was unable to grasp his meaning; he did not beseech the Blessed One: "May the Blessed One remain, O Lord! May the Well-Gone One remain, O Lord, throughout the world-period, for the welfare and happiness of the multitude, out of compassion for the world, for the benefit, well-being, and happiness of gods and humans!", so much was his mind possessed by Māra.

Then the Blessed One addressed venerable Ānanda: "Go now, Ānanda, and do what seems fitting to you."

"Even so, O Lord," said venerable Ānanda in response to the Blessed One. Rising from his seat, he respectfully saluted the Blessed One, circumambulated him, and sat down under a tree not far away.

The Account of Māra's Request
<p n="167" rend="bodytext"><hi rend="paranum">167</hi><hi rend="dot">.</hi><hi rend="bold">Yathā taṃ mārena pariyuṭṭhitacitto</hi>ti ettha tanti nipātamattaṃ. Yathā mārena pariyuṭṭhitacitto ajjhotthaṭacitto aññopi koci puthujjano paṭivijjhituṃ na sakkuṇeyya, evameva nāsakkhi paṭivijjhitunti attho. Kiṃ kāraṇā? Māro hi yassa sabbena sabbaṃ dvādasa vipallāsā appahīnā, tassa cittaṃ pariyuṭṭhāti. Therassa cattāro vipallāsā appahīnā, tenassa māro cittaṃ pariyuṭṭhāti. So pana cittapariyuṭṭhānaṃ karonto kiṃ karotīti? Bheravaṃ rūpārammaṇaṃ vā dasseti, saddārammaṇaṃ vā sāveti, tato sattā taṃ disvā vā sutvā vā satiṃ vissajjetvā vivaṭamukhā honti. Tesaṃ mukhena hatthaṃ pavesetvā hadayaṃ maddati. Tato visaññāva hutvā tiṭṭhanti. Therassa panesa mukhena hatthaṃ pavesetuṃ kiṃ sakkhissati <pb ed="V" n="2.0130"/>? Bheravārammaṇaṃ pana dasseti. Taṃ disvā thero nimittobhāsaṃ na paṭivijjhi. Bhagavā jānantoyeva – ‘‘kimatthaṃ yāvatatiyaṃ āmantesī’’ti? Parato ‘‘tiṭṭhatu, bhante, bhagavā’’ti yācite ‘‘tuyhevetaṃ dukkaṭaṃ, tuyhevetaṃ aparaddha’’nti dosāropanena sokatanukaraṇatthaṃ.</p> <p rend="subhead">Mārayācanakathāvaṇṇanā</p>
167. "Like one whose mind was possessed by Māra (yathā taṃ māreṇa pariyuṭṭhitacitto)"—here, *taṃ* is merely a particle.

Just as another ordinary person whose mind is possessed by Māra, whose mind is overwhelmed, might not be able to penetrate [the truth], even so, he was not able to penetrate it—this is the meaning.

What is the reason? Māra possesses the mind of one for whom the twelve distortions (*dvādasa vipallāsā*) have not been completely abandoned.

Māra possesses the mind of an elder (*therassa*) for whom the four distortions (*cattāro vipallāsā*) have not been completely abandoned.

So, what does he do while causing this possession of the mind (cittapariyuṭṭhānaṃ karonto)? He displays a terrifying visible object (*bheravaṃ rūpārammaṇaṃ vā dasseti*) or causes a terrifying sound to be heard (*saddārammaṇaṃ vā sāveti*). Then, those beings, having abandoned mindfulness (*satiṃ vissajjetvā*) upon seeing or hearing that, become open-mouthed.

Having inserted his hand into their mouths, he crushes their hearts (*hadayaṃ maddati*).

Then, having become unconscious (*visaññāva hutvā*), they remain standing (*tiṭṭhanti*).

Will he be able to insert his hand into the elder's (*therassa*) mouth? Rather, he displays a terrifying object (*bheravārammaṇaṃ pana dasseti*).

Having seen that, the elder (*thero*) did not penetrate the reflected image of the sign (*nimittobhāsaṃ na paṭivijjhi*).

The Blessed One, knowing this, [asked,] "Why did you address [him] up to the third time (kimatthaṃ yāvatatiyaṃ āmantesī)?" Later, when [Māra] was entreated, "Stop, venerable sir, Blessed One (tiṭṭhatu, bhante, bhagavā)," [the Buddha said,] "This evil is yours, this transgression is yours (tuyhevetaṃ dukkaṭaṃ, tuyhevetaṃ aparaddha)," thus, by imputing blame, [he taught] for the purpose of alleviating sorrow (dosāropanena sokatanukaraṇatthaṃ).

The Story of Māra's Entreaty (mārayācanakathāvaṇṇanā)
168
<p n="168" rend="bodytext"><hi rend="paranum">168</hi><hi rend="dot">.</hi> Atha kho māro pāpimā acirapakkante āyasmante ānande yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā ekamantaṃ aṭṭhāsi. Ekamantaṃ ṭhito kho māro pāpimā bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – ‘‘parinibbātudāni, bhante, bhagavā, parinibbātu sugato, parinibbānakālo <pb ed="T" n="2.0122"/> dāni, bhante, bhagavato. Bhāsitā kho panesā, bhante, bhagavatā vācā – ‘na tāvāhaṃ, pāpima, parinibbāyissāmi, yāva me bhikkhū na sāvakā bhavissanti viyattā vinītā visāradā bahussutā dhammadharā dhammānudhammappaṭipannā sāmīcippaṭipannā anudhammacārino, sakaṃ ācariyakaṃ uggahetvā ācikkhissanti desessanti paññapessanti paṭṭhapessanti vivarissanti vibhajissanti uttānī <note>uttāniṃ (ka.), uttāni (sī. pī.)</note> karissanti, uppannaṃ parappavādaṃ sahadhammena suniggahitaṃ niggahetvā sappāṭihāriyaṃ dhammaṃ desessantī’ti <pb ed="M" n="2.0088"/>. Etarahi kho pana, bhante, bhikkhū bhagavato sāvakā viyattā vinītā visāradā bahussutā dhammadharā dhammānudhammappaṭipannā <pb ed="P" n="2.0105"/> sāmīcippaṭipannā anudhammacārino, sakaṃ ācariyakaṃ uggahetvā ācikkhanti desenti paññapenti paṭṭhapenti vivaranti vibhajanti uttānīkaronti, uppannaṃ parappavādaṃ sahadhammena suniggahitaṃ niggahetvā sappāṭihāriyaṃ dhammaṃ desenti. Parinibbātudāni, bhante, bhagavā, parinibbātu sugato, parinibbānakālodāni, bhante, bhagavato.</p> <p rend="bodytext">‘‘Bhāsitā kho panesā, bhante, bhagavatā vācā – ‘na tāvāhaṃ, pāpima, parinibbāyissāmi, yāva me bhikkhuniyo na sāvikā bhavissanti viyattā vinītā visāradā bahussutā dhammadharā dhammānudhammappaṭipannā sāmīcippaṭipannā anudhammacāriniyo, sakaṃ ācariyakaṃ uggahetvā ācikkhissanti desessanti paññapessanti paṭṭhapessanti vivarissanti vibhajissanti uttānīkarissanti, uppannaṃ parappavādaṃ sahadhammena suniggahitaṃ niggahetvā sappāṭihāriyaṃ dhammaṃ desessantī’ti <pb ed="T" n="2.0123"/>. Etarahi kho pana, bhante, bhikkhuniyo bhagavato sāvikā viyattā vinītā visāradā bahussutā dhammadharā dhammānudhammappaṭipannā sāmīcippaṭipannā anudhammacāriniyo <pb ed="V" n="2.0081"/>, sakaṃ ācariyakaṃ uggahetvā ācikkhanti desenti paññapenti paṭṭhapenti vivaranti vibhajanti uttānīkaronti, uppannaṃ parappavādaṃ sahadhammena suniggahitaṃ niggahetvā sappāṭihāriyaṃ dhammaṃ desenti. Parinibbātudāni, bhante, bhagavā, parinibbātu sugato, parinibbānakālodāni, bhante, bhagavato.</p> <pb ed="T" n="2.0123"/> <pb ed="V" n="2.0081"/> <p rend="bodytext">‘‘Bhāsitā kho panesā, bhante, bhagavatā vācā – ‘na tāvāhaṃ, pāpima, parinibbāyissāmi, yāva me upāsakā na sāvakā bhavissanti viyattā vinītā visāradā bahussutā dhammadharā dhammānudhammappaṭipannā sāmīcippaṭipannā anudhammacārino, sakaṃ ācariyakaṃ uggahetvā ācikkhissanti desessanti paññapessanti paṭṭhapessanti vivarissanti vibhajissanti uttānīkarissanti, uppannaṃ parappavādaṃ sahadhammena suniggahitaṃ niggahetvā sappāṭihāriyaṃ dhammaṃ desessantī’ti. Etarahi kho pana, bhante, upāsakā bhagavato sāvakā viyattā vinītā visāradā bahussutā dhammadharā dhammānudhammappaṭipannā sāmīcippaṭipannā anudhammacārino, sakaṃ ācariyakaṃ uggahetvā ācikkhanti desenti paññapenti paṭṭhapenti vivaranti vibhajanti uttānīkaronti, uppannaṃ parappavādaṃ sahadhammena suniggahitaṃ niggahetvā sappāṭihāriyaṃ dhammaṃ desenti. Parinibbātudāni <pb ed="M" n="2.0089"/>, bhante, bhagavā, parinibbātu sugato, parinibbānakālodāni <pb ed="T" n="2.0124"/>, bhante, bhagavato.</p> <pb ed="M" n="2.0089"/> <pb ed="T" n="2.0124"/> <p rend="bodytext">‘‘Bhāsitā kho panesā, bhante, bhagavatā vācā – ‘na tāvāhaṃ, pāpima parinibbāyissāmi, yāva me upāsikā na sāvikā bhavissanti viyattā vinītā visāradā bahussutā dhammadharā dhammānudhammappaṭipannā sāmīcippaṭipannā anudhammacāriniyo, sakaṃ ācariyakaṃ uggahetvā ācikkhissanti desessanti paññapessanti paṭṭhapessanti vivarissanti vibhajissanti uttānīkarissanti, uppannaṃ parappavādaṃ sahadhammena suniggahitaṃ niggahetvā sappāṭihāriyaṃ dhammaṃ desessantī’ti. Etarahi kho pana, bhante, upāsikā bhagavato sāvikā viyattā vinītā visāradā bahussutā dhammadharā dhammānudhammappaṭipannā sāmīcippaṭipannā anudhammacāriniyo, sakaṃ ācariyakaṃ <pb ed="P" n="2.0106"/> uggahetvā ācikkhanti desenti paññapenti paṭṭhapenti vivaranti vibhajanti uttānīkaronti, uppannaṃ parappavādaṃ sahadhammena suniggahitaṃ niggahetvā sappāṭihāriyaṃ dhammaṃ desenti. Parinibbātudāni, bhante, bhagavā, parinibbātu sugato, parinibbānakālodāni, bhante, bhagavato.</p> <pb ed="P" n="2.0106"/> <p rend="bodytext">‘‘Bhāsitā kho panesā, bhante, bhagavatā vācā – ‘na tāvāhaṃ, pāpima, parinibbāyissāmi <pb ed="V" n="2.0082"/>, yāva me idaṃ brahmacariyaṃ na iddhaṃ ceva bhavissati phītañca vitthārikaṃ bāhujaññaṃ puthubhūtaṃ yāva devamanussehi suppakāsita’nti. Etarahi kho pana, bhante, bhagavato brahmacariyaṃ iddhaṃ ceva phītañca vitthārikaṃ bāhujaññaṃ puthubhūtaṃ, yāva devamanussehi suppakāsitaṃ. Parinibbātudāni, bhante, bhagavā, parinibbātu sugato, parinibbānakālodāni, bhante, bhagavato’’ti <pb ed="T" n="2.0125"/>.</p> <pb ed="V" n="2.0082"/> <pb ed="T" n="2.0125"/> <p rend="bodytext">Evaṃ vutte bhagavā māraṃ pāpimantaṃ etadavoca – ‘‘appossukko tvaṃ, pāpima, hohi, na ciraṃ tathāgatassa parinibbānaṃ bhavissati. Ito tiṇṇaṃ māsānaṃ accayena tathāgato parinibbāyissatī’’ti.</p> <p rend="subhead">Āyusaṅkhāraossajjanaṃ</p>
§168. Then, not long after the Venerable Ānanda had departed, Māra the Evil One approached the Blessed One. Having approached, he stood to one side.

Standing to one side, Māra the Evil One said this to the Blessed One: “Now, Blessed One, may the Blessed One attain complete **nirvāṇa** (*parinirvāṇa*); may the Well-Gone One attain complete **nirvāṇa**; now, Blessed One, is the time for the Blessed One’s complete **nirvāṇa**.”

“But, Blessed One, this was spoken by the Blessed One: ‘I will not attain complete **nirvāṇa**, Evil One, until my monks become disciples, wise, disciplined, confident, learned, upholders of the *dharma*, practicing the *dharma* in accordance with the *dharma*, practicing correctly, living in accordance with the *dharma*, having learned their teacher’s teaching, they proclaim it, teach it, make it known, establish it, reveal it, explain it, and make it clear; refuting with good arguments any arisen false doctrines, they teach the *dharma* with its wondrous qualities.’

But now, Blessed One, the monks are disciples of the Blessed One, wise, disciplined, confident, learned, upholders of the *dharma*, practicing the *dharma* in accordance with the *dharma*, practicing correctly, living in accordance with the *dharma*, having learned their teacher’s teaching, they proclaim it, teach it, make it known, establish it, reveal it, explain it, and make it clear; refuting with good arguments any arisen false doctrines, they teach the *dharma* with its wondrous qualities. Now, Blessed One, may the Blessed One attain complete **nirvāṇa**; may the Well-Gone One attain complete **nirvāṇa**; now, Blessed One, is the time for the Blessed One’s complete **nirvāṇa**.”

“But, Blessed One, this was spoken by the Blessed One: ‘I will not attain complete **nirvāṇa**, Evil One, until my nuns become disciples, wise, disciplined, confident, learned, upholders of the *dharma*, practicing the *dharma* in accordance with the *dharma*, practicing correctly, living in accordance with the *dharma*, having learned their teacher’s teaching, they proclaim it, teach it, make it known, establish it, reveal it, explain it, and make it clear; refuting with good arguments any arisen false doctrines, they teach the *dharma* with its wondrous qualities.’

But now, Blessed One, the nuns are disciples of the Blessed One, wise, disciplined, confident, learned, upholders of the *dharma*, practicing the *dharma* in accordance with the *dharma*, practicing correctly, living in accordance with the *dharma*, having learned their teacher’s teaching, they proclaim it, teach it, make it known, establish it, reveal it, explain it, and make it clear; refuting with good arguments any arisen false doctrines, they teach the *dharma* with its wondrous qualities. Now, Blessed One, may the Blessed One attain complete **nirvāṇa**; may the Well-Gone One attain complete **nirvāṇa**; now, Blessed One, is the time for the Blessed One’s complete **nirvāṇa**.”

“But, Blessed One, this was spoken by the Blessed One: ‘I will not attain complete **nirvāṇa**, Evil One, until my laymen become disciples, wise, disciplined, confident, learned, upholders of the *dharma*, practicing the *dharma* in accordance with the *dharma*, practicing correctly, living in accordance with the *dharma*, having learned their teacher’s teaching, they proclaim it, teach it, make it known, establish it, reveal it, explain it, and make it clear; refuting with good arguments any arisen false doctrines, they teach the *dharma* with its wondrous qualities.’

But now, Blessed One, the laymen are disciples of the Blessed One, wise, disciplined, confident, learned, upholders of the *dharma*, practicing the *dharma* in accordance with the *dharma*, practicing correctly, living in accordance with the *dharma*, having learned their teacher’s teaching, they proclaim it, teach it, make it known, establish it, reveal it, explain it, and make it clear; refuting with good arguments any arisen false doctrines, they teach the *dharma* with its wondrous qualities. Now, Blessed One, may the Blessed One attain complete **nirvāṇa**; may the Well-Gone One attain complete **nirvāṇa**; now, Blessed One, is the time for the Blessed One’s complete **nirvāṇa**.”

“But, Blessed One, this was spoken by the Blessed One: ‘I will not attain complete **nirvāṇa**, Evil One, until my laywomen become disciples, wise, disciplined, confident, learned, upholders of the *dharma*, practicing the *dharma* in accordance with the *dharma*, practicing correctly, living in accordance with the *dharma*, having learned their teacher’s teaching, they proclaim it, teach it, make it known, establish it, reveal it, explain it, and make it clear; refuting with good arguments any arisen false doctrines, they teach the *dharma* with its wondrous qualities.’

But now, Blessed One, the laywomen are disciples of the Blessed One, wise, disciplined, confident, learned, upholders of the *dharma*, practicing the *dharma* in accordance with the *dharma*, practicing correctly, living in accordance with the *dharma*, having learned their teacher’s teaching, they proclaim it, teach it, make it known, establish it, reveal it, explain it, and make it clear; refuting with good arguments any arisen false doctrines, they teach the *dharma* with its wondrous qualities. Now, Blessed One, may the Blessed One attain complete **nirvāṇa**; may the Well-Gone One attain complete **nirvāṇa**; now, Blessed One, is the time for the Blessed One’s complete **nirvāṇa**.”

“But, Blessed One, this was spoken by the Blessed One: ‘I will not attain complete **nirvāṇa**, Evil One, until this **brahmacarya** (holy life) of mine is successful, prosperous, widespread, well-known, and well-proclaimed among gods and humans.’

But now, Blessed One, this holy life of the Blessed One is successful, prosperous, widespread, well-known, and well-proclaimed among gods and humans. Now, Blessed One, may the Blessed One attain complete **nirvāṇa**; may the Well-Gone One attain complete **nirvāṇa**; now, Blessed One, is the time for the Blessed One’s complete **nirvāṇa**.”

When this was said, the Blessed One said this to Māra the Evil One: “Be without worry, Evil One, before long the complete **nirvāṇa** of the **Tathāgata** will come about. In three months from now, the **Tathāgata** will attain complete **nirvāṇa**."
Relinquishing the life-force (*āyusaṅkhāraossajjanaṃ*)
<p n="168" rend="bodytext"><hi rend="paranum">168</hi><hi rend="dot">.</hi><hi rend="bold">Māro pāpimā</hi>ti ettha <hi rend="bold">māro</hi>ti satte anatthe niyojento māretīti <hi rend="bold">māro. Pāpimā</hi>ti tasseva vevacanaṃ. So hi pāpadhammasamannāgatattā ‘‘pāpimā’’ti vuccati. Kaṇho, antako, namuci, pamattabandhūtipi tasseva nāmāni. <hi rend="bold">Bhāsitā kho panesā</hi>ti ayañhi bhagavato sambodhipattiyā aṭṭhame sattāhe bodhimaṇḍeyeva āgantvā – ‘‘bhagavā yadatthaṃ tumhehi pāramiyo pūritā, so vo attho anuppatto, paṭividdhaṃ sabbaññutaññāṇaṃ, kiṃ te lokavicāraṇenā’’ti vatvā, yathā ajja <pb ed="P" n="2.0556"/>, evameva ‘‘parinibbātu dāni, bhante, bhagavā’’ti yāci. Bhagavā cassa – ‘‘na <pb ed="M" n="2.0146"/> tāvāha’’ntiādīni vatvā paṭikkhipi. Taṃ sandhāya ‘‘bhāsitā kho panesā bhante’’tiādimāha.</p> <p rend="bodytext">Tattha <hi rend="bold">viyattā</hi>ti maggavasena viyattā. Tatheva vinītā tathā visāradā. <hi rend="bold">Bahussutā</hi>ti tepiṭakavasena bahu sutametesanti <hi rend="bold">bahussutā.</hi> Tameva dhammaṃ dhārentīti <hi rend="bold">dhammadharā.</hi> Athavā pariyattibahussutā ceva paṭivedhabahussutā ca. Pariyattipaṭivedhadhammānaṃyeva dhāraṇato dhammadharāti evamettha attho daṭṭhabbo. <hi rend="bold">Dhammānudhammapaṭipannā</hi>ti ariyadhammassa anudhammabhūtaṃ vipassanādhammaṃ paṭipannā. <hi rend="bold">Sāmīcippaṭipannā</hi>ti anucchavikapaṭipadaṃ paṭipannā. <hi rend="bold">Anudhammacārino</hi>ti anudhammacaraṇasīlā. <hi rend="bold">Sakaṃ ācariyaka</hi>nti attano ācariyavādaṃ. <hi rend="bold">Ācikkhissantī</hi>tiādīni sabbāni aññamaññassa vevacanāni. <hi rend="bold">Sahadhammenā</hi>ti sahetukena sakāraṇena vacanena. <hi rend="bold">Sappāṭihāriya</hi>nti yāva na niyyānikaṃ katvā dhammaṃ desessanti.</p> <hi rend="bold">viyattā</hi> <hi rend="bold">Bahussutā</hi> <hi rend="bold">bahussutā.</hi> <hi rend="bold">dhammadharā.</hi> <hi rend="bold">Dhammānudhammapaṭipannā</hi> <hi rend="bold">Sāmīcippaṭipannā</hi> <hi rend="bold">Anudhammacārino</hi> <hi rend="bold">Sakaṃ ācariyaka</hi> <hi rend="bold">Ācikkhissantī</hi> <hi rend="bold">Sahadhammenā</hi> <hi rend="bold">Sappāṭihāriya</hi> <p rend="bodytext"><hi rend="bold">Brahmacariya</hi>nti sikkhattayasaṅgahitaṃ sakalaṃ sāsanabrahmacariyaṃ. <hi rend="bold">Iddha</hi>nti samiddhaṃ jhānassādavasena. <hi rend="bold">Phīta</hi>nti vuddhippattaṃ sabbaphāliphullaṃ viya abhiññāya sampattivasena. <hi rend="bold">Vitthārika</hi>nti vitthataṃ tasmiṃ tasmiṃ disābhāge patiṭṭhitavasena. <hi rend="bold">Bāhujañña</hi>nti bahujanehi ñātaṃ paṭividdhaṃ mahājanābhisamayavasena. <hi rend="bold">Puthubhūta</hi>nti sabbākāravasena puthulabhāvappattaṃ. Kathaṃ? <hi rend="bold">Yāva devamanussehi</hi><pb ed="V" n="2.0131"/><hi rend="bold">suppakāsita</hi>nti yattakā viññujātikā devā ceva manussā ca atthi sabbehi suṭṭhu pakāsitanti attho.</p> <hi rend="bold">Brahmacariya</hi> <hi rend="bold">Iddha</hi> <hi rend="bold">Phīta</hi> <hi rend="bold">Vitthārika</hi> <hi rend="bold">Bāhujañña</hi> <hi rend="bold">Puthubhūta</hi> <hi rend="bold">Yāva devamanussehi</hi> <pb ed="V" n="2.0131"/> <hi rend="bold">suppakāsita</hi> <p rend="bodytext"><hi rend="bold">Appossukko</hi>ti nirālayo. Tvañhi pāpima, aṭṭhamasattāhato paṭṭhāya – ‘‘parinibbātu dāni, bhante, bhagavā parinibbātu, sugato’’ti viravanto āhiṇḍittha. Ajja dāni paṭṭhāya vigatussāho hohi; mā mayhaṃ parinibbānatthaṃ vāyāmaṃ karohīti vadati.</p> <hi rend="bold">Appossukko</hi> <p rend="subhead">Āyusaṅkhāraossajjanavaṇṇanā</p>
168. " *Māro pāpimā* ": Here, *māro* means that which leads beings (*satte*) to misfortune (*anatthe*), therefore it is called *māro*. *Pāpimā* is a synonym for that. Because he is endowed with evil qualities (*pāpadhammasamannāgatattā*), he is called "*pāpimā*." *Kaṇho*, *antako*, *namuci*, *pamattabandhū* are also names for him. " *Bhāsitā kho panesā* ": For, in the eighth week after the Blessed One's attainment of perfect awakening (*sambodhipattiyā*), having come to the *bodhimaṇḍa*, he said, "Blessed One, the purpose for which you have fulfilled the perfections (*pāramiyo*) has been attained; that purpose has been reached; the knowledge of omniscience (*sabbaññutaññāṇaṃ*) has been realized, what is the use of considering the world (*lokavicāraṇena*)?" Just as today, in the same way, he requested, "May the Blessed One attain *parinirvāṇa* now, venerable sir." The Blessed One refused him, saying, "Not yet," and so on. Referring to that, he said, " *Bhāsitā kho panesā bhante*."

There, *viyattā* means skilled due to the path (*maggavasena*). Likewise, *vinītā* and *visāradā*. *Bahussutā* means that much has been heard by them due to the three baskets (*tepiṭakavasena*), therefore they are *bahussutā*. *Dhammadharā* means those who bear that same Dharma (*dhammaṃ dhārentīti*). Or, both learned in theory (*pariyattibahussutā*) and learned in realization (*paṭivedhabahussutā*). *Dhammadharā* means those who hold to both the Dharma of theory and the Dharma of realization (*pariyattipaṭivedhadhammānaṃyeva dhāraṇato dhammadharāti*). Thus, the meaning here should be understood. *Dhammānudhammapaṭipannā* means those who practice the *vipassanādhamma*, which is in accordance with the Dharma (*ariyadhammassa anudhammabhūtaṃ*). *Sāmīcippaṭipannā* means those who practice the appropriate practice (*anucchavikapaṭipadaṃ*). *Anudhammacārino* means those whose habit is to act in accordance with the Dharma (*anudhammacaraṇasīlā*). *Sakaṃ ācariyaka* means one's own teacher's doctrine (*attano ācariyavādaṃ*). *Ācikkhissantī* and so on, all these are synonyms for each other (*aññamaññassa vevacanāni*). *Sahadhammenā* means with reasoned, causal speech (*sahetukena sakāraṇena vacanena*). *Sappāṭihāriya* means until they teach the Dharma after making it lead to liberation (*niyyānikaṃ katvā dhammaṃ desessanti*).

*Viyattā*, *bahussutā*, *bahussutā*, *dhammadharā*, *dhammānudhammapaṭipannā*, *sāmīcippaṭipannā*, *anudhammacārino*, *sakaṃ ācariyaka*, *ācikkhissantī*, *sahadhammenā*, *sappāṭihāriya*. *Brahmacariya* means the entire holy life (*sāsanabrahmacariyaṃ*) included in the three trainings (*sikkhattayasaṅgahitaṃ*). *Iddha* means successful (*samiddhaṃ*) due to the taste of *jhāna* (*jhānassādavasena*). *Phīta* means having attained growth (*vuddhippattaṃ*), like being full of all fruits and flowers (*sabbaphāliphullaṃ viya*), due to the attainment of higher knowledge (*abhiññāya sampattivasena*). *Vitthārika* means expanded (*vitthataṃ*) due to being established in each and every direction (*tasmiṃ tasmiṃ disābhāge patiṭṭhitavasena*). *Bāhujañña* means known and penetrated by many people (*bahujanehi ñātaṃ paṭividdhaṃ*) due to the agreement of the great multitude (*mahājanābhisamayavasena*). *Puthubhūta* means having attained abundant existence (*puthulabhāvappattaṃ*) due to all aspects (*sabbākāravasena*).

How? *Yāva devamanussehi suppakāsita* means the meaning is that it is well proclaimed by all the *devas* and humans (*devā ceva manussā ca*) who are intelligent (*viññujātikā*) to whatever extent they exist (*yattakā atthi*).

*Brahmacariya*, *iddha*, *phīta*, *vitthārika*, *bāhujañña*, *puthubhūta*, *yāva devamanussehi suppakāsita*. *Appossukko* means without longing (*nirālayo*).

Because you, evil one (*pāpima*), from the eighth week onwards, were wandering about, crying out, "May the Blessed One attain *parinirvāṇa* now, venerable sir; may the Blessed One attain *parinirvāṇa*, Sugata." Now, from today onwards, be without enthusiasm (*vigatussāho hohi*); do not make an effort for my *parinirvāṇa* (*mā mayhaṃ parinibbānatthaṃ vāyāmaṃ karohi*)," he says.

*Appossukko*. Description of the abandonment of the life-principle (*āyusaṅkhāraossajjanavaṇṇanā*).
169
<p n="169" rend="bodytext"><hi rend="paranum">169</hi><hi rend="dot">.</hi> Atha kho bhagavā cāpāle cetiye sato sampajāno āyusaṅkhāraṃ ossaji. Ossaṭṭhe ca bhagavatā āyusaṅkhāre mahābhūmicālo ahosi bhiṃsanako salomahaṃso <note>lomahaṃso (syā.)</note>, devadundubhiyo <note>devadudrabhiyo (ka.)</note> ca phaliṃsu <pb ed="M" n="2.0090"/>. Atha kho bhagavā <pb ed="P" n="2.0107"/> etamatthaṃ viditvā tāyaṃ velāyaṃ imaṃ udānaṃ udānesi –</p> <p rend="gatha1">‘‘Tulamatulañca sambhavaṃ, bhavasaṅkhāramavassaji muni;</p> <p rend="gathalast">Ajjhattarato samāhito, abhindi kavacamivattasambhava’’nti.</p> <p rend="subhead">Mahābhūmicālahetu</p>
Then, the Blessed One, at the Cāpāla shrine ( *cāpāle cetiye*), mindfully and clearly comprehending, relinquished the life-principle ( *āyusaṅkhāraṃ ossaji*).

And as the Blessed One relinquished the life-principle ( *āyusaṅkhāre*), there was a great earthquake ( *mahābhūmicālo ahosi*), frightening and hair-raising ( *bhiṃsanako salomahaṃso*), and heavenly drums ( *devadundubhiyo*) cracked.

Then the Blessed One, having understood this matter, at that time, uttered this solemn utterance ( *udānaṃ udānesi*):

"The balanced and the unbalanced coming into existence, the sage has relinquished the becoming-principle.

Delighting in the internal, composed, he burst the armor of becoming's origin."

The cause of the great earthquake.
<p n="169" rend="bodytext"><hi rend="paranum">169</hi><hi rend="dot">.</hi><hi rend="bold">Sato sampajāno āyusaṅkhāraṃ ossajī</hi>ti satiṃ sūpaṭṭhitaṃ katvā ñāṇena paricchinditvā āyusaṅkhāraṃ vissajji, pajahi. Tattha na bhagavā hatthena leḍḍuṃ viya āyusaṅkhāraṃ ossaji, temāsamattameva pana samāpattiṃ <pb ed="M" n="2.0147"/> samāpajjitvā tato paraṃ na samāpajjissāmīti cittaṃ uppādesi. Taṃ sandhāya vuttaṃ – ‘‘ossajī’’ti. ‘‘Ussajjī’’ti pi pāṭho. <hi rend="bold">Mahābhūmicālo</hi>ti <pb ed="P" n="2.0557"/> mahanto pathavīkampo. Tadā kira dasasahassī lokadhātu kampittha. <hi rend="bold">Bhiṃsanako</hi>ti bhayajanako. <hi rend="bold">Devadundubhiyo ca phaliṃsū</hi>ti devabheriyo phaliṃsu, devo sukkhagajjitaṃ gajji, akālavijjulatā nicchariṃsu, khaṇikavassaṃ vassīti vuttaṃ hoti.</p> <p rend="bodytext"><hi rend="bold">Udānaṃ udānesī</hi>ti kasmā udānesi? Koci nāma vadeyya – ‘‘bhagavā pacchato pacchato anubandhitvā – ‘parinibbāyatha, bhante, parinibbāyatha, bhante’ti upadduto bhayena āyusaṅkhāraṃ vissajjesī’’ti. ‘‘Tassokāso mā hotu, bhītassa udānaṃ nāma natthī’’ti etassa dīpanatthaṃ pītivegavissaṭṭhaṃ udānaṃ udānesi.</p> <hi rend="bold">Udānaṃ udānesī</hi> <p rend="bodytext">Tattha sabbesaṃ soṇasiṅgālādīnampi paccakkhabhāvato tulitaṃ paricchinnanti tulaṃ. Kiṃ taṃ? Kāmāvacarakammaṃ. Na tulaṃ, na vā tulaṃ sadisamassa aññaṃ lokiyaṃ kammaṃ atthīti <hi rend="bold">atulaṃ.</hi> Kiṃ taṃ? Mahaggatakammaṃ. Athavā kāmāvacararūpāvacaraṃ tulaṃ, arūpāvacaraṃ atulaṃ. Appavipākaṃ vā tulaṃ, bahuvipākaṃ atulaṃ. <hi rend="bold">Sambhava</hi>nti sambhavassa hetubhūtaṃ, piṇḍakārakaṃ rāsikārakanti attho. <hi rend="bold">Bhavasaṅkhāra</hi>nti punabbhavasaṅkhāraṇakaṃ. <hi rend="bold">Avassajī</hi>ti vissajjesi. <hi rend="bold">Munī</hi>ti buddhamuni. <hi rend="bold">Ajjhattarato</hi>ti niyakajjhattarato. <hi rend="bold">Samāhito</hi>ti upacārappanāsamādhivasena samāhito. <hi rend="bold">Abhindi kavacamivā</hi>ti kavacaṃ viya abhindi. <hi rend="bold">Attasambhava</hi>nti attani sañjātaṃ kilesaṃ. Idaṃ vuttaṃ hoti – ‘‘savipākaṭṭhena sambhavaṃ, bhavābhisaṅkhāraṇaṭṭhena bhavasaṅkhāranti ca laddhanāmaṃ tulātulasaṅkhātaṃ <pb ed="V" n="2.0132"/> lokiyakammañca ossaji. Saṅgāmasīse mahāyodho kavacaṃ viya attasambhavaṃ kilesañca ajjhattarato samāhito hutvā abhindī’’ti.</p> <hi rend="bold">atulaṃ.</hi> <hi rend="bold">Sambhava</hi> <hi rend="bold">Bhavasaṅkhāra</hi> <hi rend="bold">Avassajī</hi> <hi rend="bold">Munī</hi> <hi rend="bold">Ajjhattarato</hi> <hi rend="bold">Samāhito</hi> <hi rend="bold">Abhindi kavacamivā</hi> <hi rend="bold">Attasambhava</hi> <pb ed="V" n="2.0132"/> <p rend="bodytext">Atha vā <hi rend="bold">tula</hi>nti tulento tīrento. <hi rend="bold">Atulañca sambhava</hi>nti nibbānañceva sambhavañca. <hi rend="bold">Bhavasaṅkhāra</hi>nti bhavagāmikammaṃ. <hi rend="bold">Avassaji munī</hi>ti ‘‘pañcakkhandhā aniccā, pañcannaṃ khandhānaṃ nirodho nibbānaṃ nicca’’ntiādinā (paṭi. ma. 3.38) nayena tulayanto buddhamuni bhave ādīnavaṃ, nibbāne ca ānisaṃsaṃ disvā taṃ khandhānaṃ mūlabhūtaṃ bhavasaṅkhārakammaṃ – ‘‘kammakkhayāya saṃvattatī’’ti (ma. ni. 2.81) evaṃ vuttena kammakkhayakarena ariyamaggena <pb ed="P" n="2.0558"/> avassaji. Kathaṃ? Ajjhattarato samāhito abhindi kavacamiva attani <pb ed="M" n="2.0148"/> sambhavaṃ. So hi vipassanāvasena ajjhattarato samathavasena samāhitoti evaṃ pubbabhāgato paṭṭhāya samathavipassanābalena kavacamiva attabhāvaṃ pariyonandhitvā ṭhitaṃ, attani sambhavattā ‘‘attasambhava’’nti laddhanāmaṃ sabbakilesajālaṃ abhindi. Kilesābhāvena ca katakammaṃ appaṭisandhikattā avassaṭṭhaṃ nāma hotīti evaṃ kilesappahānena kammaṃ pajahi, pahīnakilesassa ca bhayaṃ nāma natthi, tasmā abhītova āyusaṅkhāraṃ ossaji, abhītabhāvañāpanatthañca udānaṃ udānesīti veditabbo.</p> <hi rend="bold">tula</hi> <hi rend="bold">Atulañca sambhava</hi> <hi rend="bold">Bhavasaṅkhāra</hi> <hi rend="bold">Avassaji munī</hi> <pb ed="P" n="2.0558"/> <pb ed="M" n="2.0148"/> <p rend="subhead">Mahābhūmicālavaṇṇanā</p>
169. "Mindful, fully aware, he relinquished the life-force (*āyusaṅkhāra*)" means, having made mindfulness well-established, having discriminated with knowledge, he abandoned and relinquished the life-force.

There, the Blessed One did not relinquish the life-force as if [throwing] a clod of dirt with his hand. But only, having attained meditative absorption (*samāpatti*) for the duration of three months, he produced the thought, "From now on, I will not attain meditative absorption,"

Referring to that, it was said, "He relinquished."

"He let go" is also a reading.

"A great earthquake (*mahābhūmicālo*)" means a great earth tremor (*pathavīkampo*).

Then, it is said, the ten-thousand world-system trembled.

"Frightful (*bhiṃsanako*)" means causing fear (*bhayajanako*).

"And the drums of the gods sounded (*devadundubhiyo ca phaliṃsū*)" means the drums of the gods sounded, the god thundered with dry thunder, untimely lightning flashes shot forth, and a momentary rain fell.

"He uttered an exclamation of joy (*udānaṃ udānesī*)" Why did he utter an exclamation of joy? Someone might say, "The Blessed One, following behind, harassed [him] saying, 'Attain complete liberation, *bhante*, attain complete liberation, *bhante*,' out of fear, he relinquished the life-force."

"Lest an opportunity occur for him; for a frightened person, there is no exclamation of joy" for the purpose of illuminating this, he uttered an exclamation of joy permeated with the rush of joy.

"He uttered an exclamation of joy (*udānaṃ udānesī*)" There, because the state of being perceived by all, including jackals and foxes etc., is weighed and delimited, [it is] weighed (*tulaṃ*).

What is that? Action belonging to the desire realm (*kāmāvacarakammaṃ*).

Because there is no other worldly action (*lokiyaṃ kammaṃ*) similar or equal to it, [it is] unequalled (*atulaṃ*).

What is that? Action connected with greatness (*mahaggatakammaṃ*).

Or, action belonging to the desire and form realms (*kāmāvacararūpāvacaraṃ*) [is] weighed (*tulaṃ*), action belonging to the formless realm (*arūpāvacaraṃ*) [is] unequalled (*atulaṃ*).

Or, action with little result (*appavipākaṃ*) [is] weighed (*tulaṃ*), action with great result (*bahuvipākaṃ*) [is] unequalled (*atulaṃ*).

"Becoming (*sambhava*)" means having as its cause the arising of becoming, meaning the maker of a lump, the maker of a heap.

"The formation of becoming (*bhavasaṅkhāra*)" means the fashioning of renewed existence (*punabbhavasaṅkhāraṇakaṃ*).

"He relinquished (*avassajī*)" means he released (*vissajjesi*).

"A sage (*munī*)" means a Buddha-sage (*buddhamuni*).

"From inner delight (*ajjhattarato*)" means delighting in one's own inner [being] (*niyakajjhattarato*).

"Concentrated (*samāhito*)" means concentrated through the power of approach-attainment-concentration (*upacārappanāsamādhivasena*).

"He broke through as if [breaking] armor (*abhindi kavacamivā*)" means he broke through as if [breaking] armor (*kavacaṃ viya abhindi*).

"Self-originated (*attasambhava*)" means defilement (*kilesaṃ*) born of self (*attani sañjātaṃ*).

This was said: "Because of having the characteristic of result, [it is] becoming (*sambhavaṃ*), and because of having the characteristic of fashioning existence, [it is called] the formation of becoming (*bhavasaṅkhāranti*), these two designations are obtained. Having weighed the well-known weighed and unweighed [actions], he relinquished worldly action (*lokiyakammañca ossaji*).

In the forefront of battle, the great warrior, like [breaking] armor, having become concentrated from inner delight, broke through defilement (*kilesañca*) born of self (*attasambhavaṃ*)."

Unequalled (*atulaṃ*).

Becoming (*sambhava*)

The formation of becoming (*bhavasaṅkhāra*)

He relinquished (*avassajī*)

A sage (*munī*)

From inner delight (*ajjhattarato*)

Concentrated (*samāhito*)

He broke through as if [breaking] armor (*abhindi kavacamivā*)

Self-originated (*attasambhava*)

Or, "Weighed (*tula*)" means weighing, crossing over.

"Unequalled and becoming (*atulañca sambhava*)" means *nirvāṇa* and also becoming.

"The formation of becoming (*bhavasaṅkhāra*)" means action leading to becoming (*bhavagāmikammaṃ*).

"The sage relinquished (*avassaji munī*)" means, by the method of "The five aggregates are impermanent (*pañcakkhandhā aniccā*), the cessation of the five aggregates is permanent *nirvāṇa* (*pañcannaṃ khandhānaṃ nirodho nibbānaṃ nicca*)," etc. (Paṭisambhidāmagga.

Majjhima Nikāya.
3.
38), the Buddha-sage (*buddhamuni*), weighing the danger in existence and having seen the benefit in *nirvāṇa*, that formation of becoming which is the root of the aggregates—"it leads to the destruction of action" (Majjhima Nikāya.
2.
81) Thus, with the noble path, spoken of as the cause of the destruction of karma, he released (his life-force).

How? Being inwardly delighted, being concentrated, he broke the armor, as it were, of self-existence in himself.

Because he was inwardly delighted through insight (vipassanā), being concentrated through tranquility (samatha), thus, starting from the preliminary stage, by the power of tranquility and insight, having tied his own existence with strength like an armor, he broke all the nets of defilements, which had the name "self-caused" ( *attasambhava* ) because they arose in himself.

And because of the absence of defilements, and because the karma done (by him) no longer led to rebirth, it was released. Thus, through the abandonment of defilements, he abandoned karma, and for one who has abandoned defilements, there is no fear. Therefore, being without fear, he released the life-sustaining force ( *āyusaṅkhāra* ), and this should be understood as having uttered a solemn utterance for the purpose of making known his state of fearlessness.

Measure, immeasurable, and existence, the formations of becoming, released by the sage.

Description of the Great Earthquake.
170
<p n="170" rend="bodytext"><hi rend="paranum">170</hi><hi rend="dot">.</hi> Atha kho āyasmato ānandassa etadahosi – ‘‘acchariyaṃ vata bho, abbhutaṃ vata bho, mahā vatāyaṃ bhūmicālo; sumahā vatāyaṃ bhūmicālo bhiṃsanako salomahaṃso; devadundubhiyo ca phaliṃsu. Ko nu kho hetu ko paccayo mahato bhūmicālassa pātubhāvāyā’’ti?</p> <p rend="bodytext">Atha kho āyasmā ānando yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami, upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṃ abhivādetvā ekamantaṃ nisīdi, ekamantaṃ nisinno kho āyasmā ānando bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – ‘‘acchariyaṃ, bhante, abbhutaṃ, bhante, mahā vatāyaṃ, bhante, bhūmicālo; sumahā vatāyaṃ <pb ed="V" n="2.0083"/>, bhante, bhūmicālo bhiṃsanako salomahaṃso; devadundubhiyo ca phaliṃsu. Ko nu kho, bhante <pb ed="T" n="2.0126"/>, hetu ko paccayo mahato bhūmicālassa pātubhāvāyā’’ti?</p> <pb ed="V" n="2.0083"/> <pb ed="T" n="2.0126"/>
Then, the Venerable Ānanda considered thus: "How amazing! How wondrous! This earthquake is truly great! This earthquake is exceedingly great, frightening, and hair-raising! And the drums of the gods resounded! What could be the cause (hetu) and what the condition (pratyaya) for such a great earthquake (mahāto bhūmicālassa pātubhāvāya)?"

Then, the Venerable Ānanda approached the Blessed One, and after approaching, paying homage to the Blessed One, sat down to one side. Having sat down to one side, the Venerable Ānanda said to the Blessed One: "Amazing, O Blessed One! Wondrous, O Blessed One! Truly great, O Blessed One, is this earthquake! Exceedingly great, O Blessed One, is this earthquake, frightening, and hair-raising! And the drums of the gods resounded! What, O Blessed One, could be the cause (hetu) and what the condition (pratyaya) for such a great earthquake (mahāto bhūmicālassa pātubhāvāya)?"
171
<p n="171" rend="bodytext"><hi rend="paranum">171</hi><hi rend="dot">.</hi> ‘‘Aṭṭha kho ime, ānanda, hetū, aṭṭha paccayā mahato bhūmicālassa pātubhāvāya. Katame aṭṭha? Ayaṃ, ānanda, mahāpathavī udake patiṭṭhitā, udakaṃ vāte patiṭṭhitaṃ, vāto ākāsaṭṭho. Hoti kho so, ānanda, samayo, yaṃ mahāvātā vāyanti. Mahāvātā vāyantā udakaṃ kampenti. Udakaṃ kampitaṃ pathaviṃ kampeti. Ayaṃ paṭhamo <pb ed="P" n="2.0108"/> hetu paṭhamo paccayo mahato bhūmicālassa pātubhāvāya.</p> <p rend="bodytext">‘‘Puna caparaṃ, ānanda, samaṇo vā hoti brāhmaṇo vā iddhimā cetovasippatto, devo vā mahiddhiko mahānubhāvo, tassa parittā pathavīsaññā bhāvitā hoti, appamāṇā āposaññā. So imaṃ pathaviṃ kampeti saṅkampeti sampakampeti sampavedheti. Ayaṃ dutiyo hetu dutiyo paccayo mahato bhūmicālassa pātubhāvāya.</p> <p rend="bodytext">‘‘Puna <pb ed="M" n="2.0091"/> caparaṃ, ānanda, yadā bodhisatto tusitakāyā cavitvā sato sampajāno mātukucchiṃ okkamati, tadāyaṃ pathavī kampati saṅkampati sampakampati sampavedhati. Ayaṃ tatiyo hetu tatiyo paccayo mahato bhūmicālassa pātubhāvāya.</p> <pb ed="M" n="2.0091"/> <p rend="bodytext">‘‘Puna caparaṃ, ānanda, yadā bodhisatto sato sampajāno mātukucchismā nikkhamati, tadāyaṃ pathavī kampati saṅkampati sampakampati sampavedhati. Ayaṃ catuttho hetu catuttho paccayo mahato bhūmicālassa pātubhāvāya.</p> <p rend="bodytext">‘‘Puna caparaṃ, ānanda, yadā <pb ed="T" n="2.0127"/> tathāgato anuttaraṃ sammāsambodhiṃ abhisambujjhati, tadāyaṃ pathavī kampati saṅkampati sampakampati sampavedhati. Ayaṃ pañcamo hetu pañcamo paccayo mahato bhūmicālassa pātubhāvāya.</p> <pb ed="T" n="2.0127"/> <p rend="bodytext">‘‘Puna caparaṃ, ānanda, yadā tathāgato anuttaraṃ dhammacakkaṃ pavatteti, tadāyaṃ pathavī kampati saṅkampati sampakampati sampavedhati. Ayaṃ chaṭṭho hetu chaṭṭho paccayo mahato bhūmicālassa pātubhāvāya.</p> <p rend="bodytext">‘‘Puna <pb ed="V" n="2.0084"/> caparaṃ, ānanda, yadā tathāgato sato sampajāno āyusaṅkhāraṃ ossajjati, tadāyaṃ pathavī kampati saṅkampati sampakampati sampavedhati. Ayaṃ sattamo hetu sattamo paccayo mahato bhūmicālassa pātubhāvāya.</p> <pb ed="V" n="2.0084"/> <p rend="bodytext">‘‘Puna caparaṃ, ānanda, yadā tathāgato anupādisesāya <pb ed="P" n="2.0109"/> nibbānadhātuyā parinibbāyati, tadāyaṃ pathavī kampati saṅkampati sampakampati sampavedhati. Ayaṃ aṭṭhamo hetu aṭṭhamo paccayo mahato bhūmicālassa pātubhāvāya. Ime kho, ānanda, aṭṭha hetū, aṭṭha paccayā mahato bhūmicālassa pātubhāvāyā’’ti.</p> <pb ed="P" n="2.0109"/> <p rend="subhead">Aṭṭha parisā</p>
171. “Ānanda, there are these eight reasons, eight causes, for the appearance of a great earthquake.

Which are the eight? This great earth, Ānanda, is established on water, the water is established on wind, and the wind is standing on space.

There comes a time, Ānanda, when great winds blow.

The great winds blowing shake the water.

The water, shaken, shakes the earth.

This is the first reason, the first cause for the occurrence of a great earthquake.

“Again, Ānanda, when an ascetic or a Brahmin who has psychic powers and has mastered his mind, or a powerful and mighty deva, develops a limited earth-perception and an immeasurable water-perception,

he makes this earth tremble, quiver, shake, and quake.

This is the second reason, the second cause for the arising of mighty earthquakes.

“Again, Ānanda, when a Bodhisattva departs from the Tusita heaven, mindfully and clearly aware, and descends into his mother’s womb, then the earth shudders, shakes, and violently quakes.

This is the third reason, the third cause for the occurrence of a great earthquake.

“Again, Ānanda, when the Bodhisattva, mindful and clearly aware, emerges from his mother’s womb, then the earth shudders, shakes, and violently quakes.

This is the fourth reason, the fourth cause for the occurrence of a great earthquake.

“Again, Ānanda, when the Tathāgata awakens to unsurpassed perfect enlightenment (anuttaraṃ sammāsambodhiṃ abhisambujjhati), then the earth shudders, shakes, and violently quakes.

This is the fifth reason, the fifth cause for the occurrence of a great earthquake.

“Again, Ānanda, when the Tathāgata sets in motion the unsurpassed Wheel of the Dharma (anuttaraṃ dhammacakkaṃ pavatteti), then the earth shudders, shakes, and violently quakes.

This is the sixth reason, the sixth cause for the occurrence of a great earthquake.

“Again, Ānanda, when the Tathāgata, mindful and clearly aware, relinquishes the life-principle (āyusaṅkhāraṃ ossajjati), then the earth shudders, shakes, and violently quakes.

This is the seventh reason, the seventh cause for the occurrence of a great earthquake.

“Again, Ānanda, when the Tathāgata attains complete extinction in the *Nirvana*-element without remainder (anupādisesāya nibbānadhātuyā parinibbāyati), then the earth shudders, shakes, and violently quakes.

This is the eighth reason, the eighth cause for the occurrence of a great earthquake.

These, Ānanda, are the eight reasons, the eight causes for the occurrence of a great earthquake.”

Eight Assemblies
<p n="171" rend="bodytext"><hi rend="paranum">171</hi><hi rend="dot">.</hi><hi rend="bold">Yaṃ mahāvātā</hi>ti yena samayena yasmiṃ vā samaye mahāvātā vāyanti, mahāvātā vāyantāpi ukkhepakavātā nāma uṭṭhahanti, te vāyantā saṭṭhisahassādhikanavayojanasatasahassabahalaṃ udakasandhārakaṃ vātaṃ upacchindanti, tato ākāse udakaṃ bhassati, tasmiṃ bhassante pathavī bhassati. Puna vāto attano balena antodhamakaraṇe viya udakaṃ ābandhitvā gaṇhāti, tato udakaṃ uggacchati, tasmiṃ uggacchante pathavī uggacchati. Evaṃ udakaṃ kampitaṃ pathaviṃ kampeti. Etañca kampanaṃ yāva ajjakālāpi hotiyeva, bahalabhāvena pana na ogacchanuggacchanaṃ paññāyati.</p> <p rend="bodytext"><hi rend="bold">Mahiddhiko mahānubhāvo</hi>ti ijjhanassa mahantatāya mahiddhiko, anubhavitabbassa mahantatāya mahānubhāvo. <hi rend="bold">Parittā</hi>ti dubbalā. <hi rend="bold">Appamāṇā</hi>ti balavā. <hi rend="bold">So imaṃ pathaviṃ kampetī</hi>ti so iddhiṃ nibbattetvā saṃvejento mahāmoggallāno viya, vīmaṃsanto vā mahānāgattherassa bhāgineyyo saṅgharakkhitasāmaṇero viya pathaviṃ kampeti. So kirāyasmā khuraggeyeva arahattaṃ patvā cintesi <pb ed="V" n="2.0133"/> – ‘‘atthi nu kho koci bhikkhu, yena pabbajitadivaseyeva arahattaṃ patvā vejayanto pāsādo kampitapubbo’’ti? Tato – ‘‘natthi kocī’’ti ñatvā – ‘‘ahaṃ kampessāmī’’ti abhiññābalena vejayantamatthake ṭhatvā pādena paharitvā kampetuṃ nāsakkhi. Atha naṃ sakkassa nāṭakitthiyo āhaṃsu – ‘‘putta saṅgharakkhita, tvaṃ pūtigandheneva sīsena vejayantaṃ kampetuṃ icchasi, suppatiṭṭhito tāta pāsādo, kathaṃ kampetuṃ <pb ed="P" n="2.0559"/> sakkhissasī’’ti?</p> <hi rend="bold">Mahiddhiko mahānubhāvo</hi> <hi rend="bold">Parittā</hi> <hi rend="bold">Appamāṇā</hi> <hi rend="bold">So imaṃ pathaviṃ kampetī</hi> <pb ed="V" n="2.0133"/> <pb ed="P" n="2.0559"/> <p rend="bodytext">Sāmaṇero <pb ed="M" n="2.0149"/> – ‘‘imā devatā mayā saddhiṃ keḷiṃ karonti, ahaṃ kho pana ācariyaṃ nālatthaṃ, kahaṃ nu kho me ācariyo sāmuddikamahānāgatthero’’ti āvajjento mahāsamudde udakaleṇaṃ māpetvā divāvihāraṃ nisinnoti ñatvā tattha gantvā theraṃ vanditvā aṭṭhāsi. Tato naṃ thero – ‘‘kiṃ, tāta saṅgharakkhita, asikkhitvāva yuddhaṃ paviṭṭhosī’’ti vatvā ‘‘nāsakkhi, tāta, vejayantaṃ kampetu’’nti pucchi. Ācariyaṃ, bhante, nālatthanti. Atha naṃ thero – ‘‘tāta tumhādise akampente ko añño kampessati. Diṭṭhapubbaṃ te, tāta, udakapiṭṭhe gomayakhaṇḍaṃ pilavantaṃ, tāta, kapallakapūvaṃ pacantā antantena paricchindanti, iminā opammena jānāhī’’ti āha. So – ‘‘vaṭṭissati, bhante, ettakenā’’ti vatvā pāsādena patiṭṭhitokāsaṃ udakaṃ hotūti adhiṭṭhāya vejayantābhimukho agamāsi.</p> <pb ed="M" n="2.0149"/> <p rend="bodytext">Devadhītaro taṃ disvā – ‘‘ekavāraṃ lajjitvā gato, punapi sāmaṇero eti, punapi etī’’ti vadiṃsu. Sakko devarājā – ‘‘mā mayhaṃ puttena saddhiṃ kathayittha, idāni tena ācariyo laddho, khaṇena pāsādaṃ kampessatī’’ti āha. Sāmaṇeropi pādaṅguṭṭhena pāsādathūpikaṃ pahari. Pāsādo catūhi disāhi oṇamati. Devatā – ‘‘patiṭṭhātuṃ dehi, tāta, pāsādassa patiṭṭhātuṃ dehi, tāta, pāsādassā’’ti viraviṃsu. Sāmaṇero pāsādaṃ yathāṭhāne ṭhapetvā pāsādamatthake ṭhatvā udānaṃ udānesi –</p> <p rend="gatha1">‘‘Ajjevāhaṃ pabbajito, ajja pattāsavakkhayaṃ;</p> <p rend="gathalast">Ajja kampemi pāsādaṃ, aho buddhassuḷāratā.</p> <p rend="gatha1">Ajjevāhaṃ pabbajito…pe… aho dhammassuḷāratā.</p> <p rend="gatha1">Ajjevāhaṃ pabbajito…pe… aho saṅghassuḷāratāti.</p> <p rend="bodytext">Ito <pb ed="V" n="2.0134"/> paresu chasu pathavīkampesu yaṃ vattabbaṃ, taṃ mahāpadāne vuttameva.</p> <pb ed="V" n="2.0134"/> <p rend="bodytext">Iti imesu aṭṭhasu pathavīkampesu paṭhamo dhātukopena, dutiyo iddhānubhāvena, tatiyacatutthā puññatejena, pañcamo ñāṇatejena, chaṭṭho sādhukāradānavasena, sattamo kāruññabhāvena, aṭṭhamo ārodanena. Mātukucchiṃ okkamante ca tato nikkhamante ca mahāsatte tassa puññatejena pathavī akampittha. Abhisambodhiyaṃ ñāṇatejena abhihatā <pb ed="M" n="2.0150"/> hutvā akampittha. Dhammacakkappavattane <pb ed="P" n="2.0560"/> sādhukārabhāvasaṇṭhitā sādhukāraṃ dadamānā akampittha. Āyusaṅkhārossajjane kāruññasabhāvasaṇṭhitā cittasaṅkhobhaṃ asahamānā akampittha. Parinibbāne ārodanavegatunnā hutvā akampittha. Ayaṃ panattho pathavīdevatāya vasena veditabbo, mahābhūtapathaviyā panetaṃ natthi acetanattāti.</p> <pb ed="M" n="2.0150"/> <pb ed="P" n="2.0560"/> <p rend="bodytext"><hi rend="bold">Ime kho, ānanda, aṭṭha hetū</hi>ti ettha <hi rend="bold">ime</hi>ti niddiṭṭhanidassanaṃ. Ettāvatā ca panāyasmā ānando – ‘‘addhā ajja bhagavatā āyusaṅkhāro ossaṭṭho’’ti sallakkhesi. Bhagavā pana sallakkhitabhāvaṃ jānantopi okāsaṃ adatvāva aññānipi aṭṭhakāni sampiṇḍento – ‘‘aṭṭha kho imā’’tiādimāha.</p> <hi rend="bold">Ime kho, ānanda, aṭṭha hetū</hi> <hi rend="bold">ime</hi> <p rend="subhead">Aṭṭhaparisavaṇṇanā</p>
171. **yaṃ mahāvātā**ti: At whatever time, or at which time, great winds blow, and when those great winds are blowing, winds called "lifting winds" arise, these blowing winds cut through the wind that holds the water, which is sixty-nine million yojanas thick. Then, water pours down in the sky, and as it pours down, the earth pours down.

Furthermore, the wind, by its own power, like in the case of inward blowing, binds the water and takes it. Then, the water rises up, and as that water rises up, the earth rises up.

Thus, the water, shaken, shakes the earth. (udakaṃ kampitaṃ pathaviṃ kampeti.)

And this shaking continues even until today. However, due to its thickness, the sinking and rising are not apparent.

**mahiddhiko mahānubhāvo**ti: *Mahiddhiko* because of the greatness of his power, *mahānubhāvo* because of the greatness of what is to be experienced.

**parittā**ti: [They are] weak.

**appamāṇā**ti: [They are] powerful.

**so imaṃ pathaviṃ kampetī**ti: He, having created power and causing agitation, like the great Maudgalyāyana, or investigating, like Saṅgharakkhitasāmaṇera, the nephew of Mahānāgatthera, shakes the earth.

It is said that venerable Khuragga, having attained arhatship right on the edge of a razor, thought: "Is there any monk by whom, on the very day of his ordination, having attained arhatship, the Vejayanta palace has been shaken before?" Then, knowing that there was none, and thinking, "I will shake it," he stood at the top of the Vejayanta [palace] with the power of his higher knowledge, and struck it with his foot, but was not able to shake it.

Then, the celestial courtesans of Śakra said to him: "O son Saṅgharakkhita, you wish to shake the Vejayanta [palace] with a head like a foul smell? The palace is well-established, dear one. How will you be able to shake it?"

**mahiddhiko mahānubhāvo parittā appamāṇā so imaṃ pathaviṃ kampetī**

The novice: "These deities are playing with me. But I have not found a teacher. Where might my teacher, Sāmuddikamahānāgatthera, be?" Reflecting, he realized that [his teacher] had fashioned a water cave in the great ocean and was dwelling there during the day. Knowing this, he went there, paid homage to the elder, and stood [before him].

Then, the elder [said] to him: "Why, dear Saṅgharakkhita, have you entered the battle without training?" And he asked, "Were you able to shake the Vejayanta [palace], dear one?"

"Venerable sir, I have not found a teacher."

Then, the elder [said] to him: "Dear one, who else will shake [it] if those like you do not shake it? Have you ever seen, dear one, a piece of cow dung floating on the surface of the water, or those who are cooking cakes covering [the water] all around? Understand with this simile."

He said: "It will suffice, venerable sir, with this much." Having said this, he resolved, "Let there be water in the place where the palace is established!" and went towards the Vejayanta [palace].

The daughters of the gods, seeing him, said: "Having been ashamed once, he has gone, and again the novice comes, again he comes!"

Śakra, the lord of gods, [thought]: "Do not speak with my son! Now, he has found a teacher, and in a moment he will shake the palace!"

The novice then struck the pinnacle of the palace with his big toe.

The palace bends in the four directions.

The deities cried out: "Give a foundation, dear one, to the palace! Give a foundation, dear one, to the palace!"

The novice, having placed the palace in its proper place, standing on the top of the palace, uttered a solemn utterance:

"Today itself I was ordained; today I attained the destruction of the influxes;

Today I shake the palace; Hail to the magnificence of the Buddha!"

"Today itself I was ordained…pe… Hail to the magnificence of the Dharma!"

"Today itself I was ordained…pe… Hail to the magnificence of the Saṅgha!"

Henceforth, what is to be said about the remaining six earth-shakings has already been said in the *Mahāpadāna*.

Thus, in these eight earth-shakings, the first is due to disturbance of the elements (dhātukopena), the second due to the power of psychic abilities (iddhānubhāvena), the third and fourth due to the power of merit (puññatejena), the fifth due to the power of knowledge (ñāṇatejena), the sixth due to the giving of approval and offerings (sādhukāradānavasena), the seventh due to compassion (kāruññabhāvena), [and] the eighth due to lamentation (ārodanena).

When the great being entered the mother's womb, and when he came out from there, due to the power of his merit, the earth shook.

Having been struck by the power of knowledge at complete awakening, it shook.

At the turning of the wheel of Dharma, established in the state of giving approval, giving approval, it shook.

At the abandoning of the life force, established in a state of compassion, not enduring mental agitation, it shook.
Having become agitated and spurred on by the force of lamentation at the *parinirvāṇa*, he did not tremble.

However, this meaning should be understood in terms of the *pathavīdevatā* (earth deity), because this does not exist in the great elemental earth, due to its being inanimate.

</p> <pb ed="m" n="2.
0150"/> <pb ed="p" n="2.
0560"/> <p rend="bodytext">"These, Ānanda, are the eight causes," here, "these" indicates a specification and example.

Furthermore, the venerable Ānanda considered, "Indeed, today the Blessed One has relinquished the life-principle."

Although the Blessed One knew the state of having been considered thus, without giving an opportunity, while combining other *aṭṭhakas* (groups of eight), he spoke, beginning with, "These are the eight."

</p> <hi rend="bold">These, Ānanda, are the eight causes.</hi> <hi rend="bold">These</hi> <p rend="subhead">Explanation of the Eight Assemblies</p>
172
<p n="172" rend="bodytext"><hi rend="paranum">172</hi><hi rend="dot">.</hi> ‘‘Aṭṭha kho imā, ānanda, parisā. Katamā aṭṭha? Khattiyaparisā, brāhmaṇaparisā, gahapatiparisā, samaṇaparisā, cātumahārājikaparisā <note>cātummahārājikaparisā (sī. syā. kaṃ. pī.)</note>, tāvatiṃsaparisā, māraparisā, brahmaparisā. Abhijānāmi kho panāhaṃ, ānanda <pb ed="M" n="2.0092"/>, anekasataṃ khattiyaparisaṃ upasaṅkamitā. Tatrapi mayā sannisinnapubbaṃ ceva sallapitapubbañca sākacchā ca samāpajjitapubbā <pb ed="T" n="2.0128"/>. Tattha yādisako tesaṃ vaṇṇo hoti, tādisako mayhaṃ vaṇṇo hoti. Yādisako tesaṃ saro hoti, tādisako mayhaṃ saro hoti. Dhammiyā kathāya sandassemi samādapemi samuttejemi sampahaṃsemi. Bhāsamānañca maṃ na jānanti – ‘ko nu kho ayaṃ bhāsati devo vā manusso vā’ti? Dhammiyā kathāya sandassetvā samādapetvā samuttejetvā sampahaṃsetvā antaradhāyāmi. Antarahitañca maṃ na jānanti – ‘ko nu kho ayaṃ antarahito devo vā manusso vā’ti? Abhijānāmi kho panāhaṃ, ānanda, anekasataṃ brāhmaṇaparisaṃ…pe… gahapatiparisaṃ… samaṇaparisaṃ… cātumahārājikaparisaṃ… tāvatiṃsaparisaṃ… māraparisaṃ… brahmaparisaṃ upasaṅkamitā. Tatrapi mayā sannisinnapubbaṃ ceva sallapitapubbañca sākacchā ca samāpajjitapubbā. Tattha yādisako tesaṃ vaṇṇo hoti, tādisako mayhaṃ vaṇṇo hoti. Yādisako tesaṃ saro hoti, tādisako mayhaṃ saro hoti. Dhammiyā kathāya sandassemi samādapemi samuttejemi sampahaṃsemi. Bhāsamānañca maṃ na jānanti – ‘ko nu kho ayaṃ bhāsati devo vā manusso vā’ti? Dhammiyā <pb ed="P" n="2.0110"/> kathāya sandassetvā samādapetvā samuttejetvā sampahaṃsetvā antaradhāyāmi. Antarahitañca maṃ na jānanti – ‘ko nu kho ayaṃ antarahito devo vā manusso vā’ti? Imā kho, ānanda, aṭṭha parisā.</p> <p rend="subhead">Aṭṭha abhibhāyatanāni</p>
172. “Ānanda, there are these eight assemblies. What are the eight? They are the assembly of nobles ( *khattiyaparisā*), the assembly of Brahmins (*brāhmaṇaparisā*), the assembly of householders (*gahapatiparisā*), the assembly of ascetics (*samaṇaparisā*), the assembly of the Four Great Kings (*cātumahārājikaparisā*), the assembly of the Thirty-Three Gods (*tāvatiṃsaparisā*), the assembly of Māras (*māraparisā*), and the assembly of Brahmās (*brahmaparisā*).

I remember well, Ānanda, many hundreds of assemblies of nobles that I have approached. There, before seating myself, before talking, before engaging in conversation, whatever their appearance (*vaṇṇa*) was, my appearance would become. Whatever their voice (*sara*) was, my voice would become. I instructed, urged, roused, & encouraged them with Dhamma talk.

While I was speaking, they didn’t know me: ‘Who is this who speaks—a *deva* or a *manussa*?’ Having instructed, urged, roused, & encouraged them with *Dhamma* talk, I disappeared. And still they did not know: “He who has just disappeared — was he a *deva* or a *manussa*?”

I remember well, Ānanda, many hundreds of assemblies of Brahmins… of householders… of ascetics… of the Four Great Kings… of the Thirty-three Gods… of *Māras*… of *Brahmās* that I have approached. There, before seating myself, before talking, before engaging in conversation, whatever their appearance (*vaṇṇa*) was, my appearance would become. Whatever their voice (*sara*) was, my voice would become. I instructed, urged, roused, & encouraged them with *Dhamma* talk.

While I was speaking, they didn’t know me: ‘Who is this who speaks—a *deva* or a *manussa*?’ Having instructed, urged, roused, & encouraged them with Dhamma talk, I disappeared. And still they did not know: “He who has just disappeared — was he a *deva* or a *manussa*?” These, Ānanda, are the eight assemblies.

The eight sources of superiority (*aṭṭha abhibhāyatanāni*).
<p n="172" rend="bodytext"><hi rend="paranum">172</hi><hi rend="dot">.</hi> Tattha <hi rend="bold">anekasataṃ khattiyaparisa</hi>nti bimbisārasamāgamañātisamāgalicchavīsamāgamādisadisaṃ, sā pana aññesu cakkavāḷesupi labbhateyeva. <hi rend="bold">Sallapitapubba</hi>nti ālāpasallāpo katapubbo. <hi rend="bold">Sākacchā</hi>ti dhammasākacchāpi samāpajjitapubbā. <hi rend="bold">Yādisako tesaṃ vaṇṇo</hi>ti te odātāpi honti kāḷāpi maṅguracchavīpi, satthā suvaṇṇavaṇṇova. Idaṃ pana saṇṭhānaṃ paṭicca kathitaṃ. Saṇṭhānampi ca kevalaṃ tesaṃ paññāyatiyeva, na pana bhagavā milakkhusadiso hoti, nāpi āmuttamaṇikuṇḍalo, buddhaveseneva nisīdati. Te pana attano samānasaṇṭhānameva passanti. <hi rend="bold">Yādisako tesaṃ saro</hi>ti te chinnassarāpi honti gaggarassarāpi kākassarāpi, satthā brahmassarova. Idaṃ pana bhāsantaraṃ sandhāya kathitaṃ. Sacepi hi satthā rājāsane nisinno katheti, ‘‘ajja rājā madhurena sarena kathetī’’ti tesaṃ hoti. Kathetvā pakkante pana bhagavati puna rājānaṃ āgataṃ disvā – ‘‘ko nu kho aya’’nti vīmaṃsā uppajjati. Tattha <hi rend="bold">ko nu kho aya</hi>nti imasmiṃ ṭhāne idāneva māgadhabhāsāya sīhaḷabhāsāya madhurenākārena kathento ko nu kho ayaṃ antarahito, kiṃ devo, udāhu manussoti evaṃ vīmaṃsantāpi <pb ed="V" n="2.0135"/> na jānantīti attho. Kimatthaṃ panevaṃ ajānantānaṃ dhammaṃ desetīti? Vāsanatthāya <pb ed="M" n="2.0151"/>. Evaṃ sutopi hi dhammo anāgate paccayo hoti yevāti anāgataṃ paṭicca deseti. <hi rend="bold">Anekasataṃ brāhmaṇaparisa</hi>ntiādīnampi soṇadaṇḍakūṭadaṇḍasamāgamādivasena <pb ed="P" n="2.0561"/> ceva aññacakkavāḷavasena ca sambhavo veditabbo.</p> <p rend="bodytext">Imā pana aṭṭha parisā bhagavā kimatthaṃ āhari? Abhītabhāvadassanatthameva. Imā kira āharitvā evamāha – ‘‘ānanda, imāpi aṭṭha parisā upasaṅkamitvā dhammaṃ desentassa tathāgatassa bhayaṃ vā sārajjaṃ vā natthi, māraṃ pana ekakaṃ disvā tathāgato bhāyeyyāti ko evaṃ saññaṃ uppādetumarahati. Abhīto, ānanda, tathāgato acchambhī, sato sampajāno āyusaṅkhāraṃ ossajī’’ti.</p> <p rend="subhead">Aṭṭhaabhibhāyatanavaṇṇanā</p>
172. There, namely, "[There was] a gathering of many hundreds of *kṣatriyas*," like the gathering of Bimbisāra, a gathering of relatives, a gathering of Licchavis, and so on. But that is obtained in other world systems as well.

"[They] have spoken before" means speech, conversation, has been done before.

"*Sākacchā*" means there have been previous discussions about the *dharma*.

"*Yādisako tesaṃ vaṇṇo*," as to what was their complexion: they can be white, black, or the color of *maṅgura*, but the Teacher's color is like gold.

This was said with reference to the body.

And indeed, it is only their body that is apparent; the Blessed One is not like a barbarian, nor does he sit wearing jeweled earrings; he sits only in the manner of a Buddha.

But they see only their own similar form.

"*Yādisako tesaṃ saro*," as to what was their voice: they can have broken voices, hoarse voices, or crow-like voices, but the Teacher's voice is like Brahma's.

This was said with reference to a different language.

Even if the Teacher, seated on the royal seat, should speak, they think, "Today the king speaks with a sweet voice."

Having spoken, when the Blessed One had departed, seeing the king come again, the thought arises, "Who now, pray, is this?"

There, "*ko nu kho aya*," in this place, just now, speaking in the Magadhi language, in the Sinhala language, with a sweet manner, who now, pray, is this who has disappeared? Is it a god, or a human?—even while pondering thus, they do not know the meaning.

Why then does he teach the Dharma to those who do not know? For the sake of habituation.

Even the Dharma that has been heard in this way becomes a condition in the future. He teaches having regard to the future.

"*Anekasataṃ brāhmaṇaparisa*," [there was] a gathering of many hundreds of *brāhmaṇas*, and so on, and also the arising based on the assembly of Soṇadaṇḍa, Kūṭadaṇḍa, and so on, and also based on another world system, should be understood.

Why did the Blessed One bring forward these eight assemblies? Just for the sake of showing the state of being fearless.

It is said that having brought these forward, he spoke thus: "Ānanda, even these eight assemblies, having approached and listened to the Tathāgata teaching the Dharma, there is no fear or hesitation for the Tathāgata. Who is capable of producing the thought that the Tathāgata would be afraid at seeing Māra alone?

Fearless, Ānanda, is the Tathāgata, without trembling, mindful, fully aware, he relinquished the life force."

Explanation of the eight abhibhāyatana.
173
<p n="173" rend="bodytext"><hi rend="paranum">173</hi><hi rend="dot">.</hi> ‘‘Aṭṭha <pb ed="V" n="2.0085"/> kho imāni, ānanda, abhibhāyatanāni. Katamāni aṭṭha <pb ed="T" n="2.0129"/>? Ajjhattaṃ rūpasaññī eko bahiddhā rūpāni passati parittāni suvaṇṇadubbaṇṇāni. ‘Tāni abhibhuyya jānāmi passāmī’ti evaṃsaññī hoti. Idaṃ paṭhamaṃ abhibhāyatanaṃ.</p> <p rend="bodytext">‘‘Ajjhattaṃ rūpasaññī eko bahiddhā rūpāni passati appamāṇāni suvaṇṇadubbaṇṇāni. ‘Tāni abhibhuyya jānāmi passāmī’ti evaṃsaññī hoti. Idaṃ dutiyaṃ abhibhāyatanaṃ.</p> <p rend="bodytext">‘‘Ajjhattaṃ arūpasaññī eko bahiddhā rūpāni passati parittāni suvaṇṇadubbaṇṇāni. ‘Tāni abhibhuyya jānāmi passāmī’ti evaṃsaññī hoti. Idaṃ tatiyaṃ abhibhāyatanaṃ.</p> <p rend="bodytext">‘‘Ajjhattaṃ <pb ed="M" n="2.0093"/> arūpasaññī eko bahiddhā rūpāni passati appamāṇāni suvaṇṇadubbaṇṇāni. ‘Tāni abhibhuyya jānāmi passāmī’ti evaṃsaññī hoti. Idaṃ catutthaṃ abhibhāyatanaṃ.</p> <pb ed="M" n="2.0093"/> <p rend="bodytext">‘‘Ajjhattaṃ arūpasaññī eko bahiddhā rūpāni passati nīlāni nīlavaṇṇāni nīlanidassanāni nīlanibhāsāni. Seyyathāpi nāma umāpupphaṃ nīlaṃ nīlavaṇṇaṃ nīlanidassanaṃ nīlanibhāsaṃ. Seyyathā vā pana taṃ vatthaṃ bārāṇaseyyakaṃ ubhatobhāgavimaṭṭhaṃ nīlaṃ nīlavaṇṇaṃ nīlanidassanaṃ nīlanibhāsaṃ. Evameva ajjhattaṃ arūpasaññī eko bahiddhā rūpāni passati nīlāni nīlavaṇṇāni nīlanidassanāni nīlanibhāsāni. ‘Tāni abhibhuyya jānāmi passāmī’ti evaṃsaññī hoti. Idaṃ pañcamaṃ abhibhāyatanaṃ.</p> <p rend="bodytext">‘‘Ajjhattaṃ <pb ed="P" n="2.0111"/> arūpasaññī eko bahiddhā rūpāni passati pītāni pītavaṇṇāni pītanidassanāni pītanibhāsāni. Seyyathāpi nāma kaṇikārapupphaṃ pītaṃ pītavaṇṇaṃ pītanidassanaṃ pītanibhāsaṃ. Seyyathā <pb ed="T" n="2.0130"/> vā pana taṃ vatthaṃ bārāṇaseyyakaṃ ubhatobhāgavimaṭṭhaṃ pītaṃ pītavaṇṇaṃ pītanidassanaṃ pītanibhāsaṃ. Evameva ajjhattaṃ arūpasaññī eko bahiddhā rūpāni passati pītāni pītavaṇṇāni pītanidassanāni pītanibhāsāni. ‘Tāni abhibhuyya jānāmi passāmī’ti evaṃsaññī hoti. Idaṃ chaṭṭhaṃ abhibhāyatanaṃ.</p> <pb ed="P" n="2.0111"/> <pb ed="T" n="2.0130"/> <p rend="bodytext">‘‘Ajjhattaṃ <pb ed="V" n="2.0086"/> arūpasaññī eko bahiddhā rūpāni passati lohitakāni lohitakavaṇṇāni lohitakanidassanāni lohitakanibhāsāni. Seyyathāpi nāma bandhujīvakapupphaṃ lohitakaṃ lohitakavaṇṇaṃ lohitakanidassanaṃ lohitakanibhāsaṃ. Seyyathā vā pana taṃ vatthaṃ bārāṇaseyyakaṃ ubhatobhāgavimaṭṭhaṃ lohitakaṃ lohitakavaṇṇaṃ lohitakanidassanaṃ lohitakanibhāsaṃ. Evameva ajjhattaṃ arūpasaññī eko bahiddhā rūpāni passati lohitakāni lohitakavaṇṇāni lohitakanidassanāni lohitakanibhāsāni. ‘Tāni abhibhuyya jānāmi passāmī’ti evaṃsaññī hoti. Idaṃ sattamaṃ abhibhāyatanaṃ.</p> <pb ed="V" n="2.0086"/> <p rend="bodytext">‘‘Ajjhattaṃ arūpasaññī eko bahiddhā rūpāni passati odātāni odātavaṇṇāni odātanidassanāni odātanibhāsāni. Seyyathāpi nāma osadhitārakā <pb ed="M" n="2.0094"/> odātā odātavaṇṇā odātanidassanā odātanibhāsā. Seyyathā vā pana taṃ vatthaṃ bārāṇaseyyakaṃ ubhatobhāgavimaṭṭhaṃ odātaṃ odātavaṇṇaṃ odātanidassanaṃ odātanibhāsaṃ. Evameva ajjhattaṃ arūpasaññī eko bahiddhā rūpāni passati odātāni odātavaṇṇāni odātanidassanāni odātanibhāsāni. ‘Tāni abhibhuyya jānāmi passāmī’ti evaṃsaññī hoti. Idaṃ aṭṭhamaṃ abhibhāyatanaṃ <pb ed="T" n="2.0131"/>. Imāni kho, ānanda, aṭṭha abhibhāyatanāni.</p> <pb ed="M" n="2.0094"/> <pb ed="T" n="2.0131"/> <p rend="subhead">Aṭṭha vimokkhā</p>
173. These, Ānanda, are the eight dimensions of mastery. What are the eight?

Perceiving forms internally, one sees external forms that are limited, beautiful & ugly. Mastering them, one has the perception, ‘I know; I see.’ This is the first dimension of mastery.

Perceiving forms internally, one sees external forms that are immeasurable, beautiful & ugly. Mastering them, one has the perception, ‘I know; I see.’ This is the second dimension of mastery.

Not perceiving form internally, one sees external forms that are limited, beautiful & ugly. Mastering them, one has the perception, ‘I know; I see.’ This is the third dimension of mastery.

Not perceiving form internally, one sees external forms that are immeasurable, beautiful & ugly. Mastering them, one has the perception, ‘I know; I see.’ This is the fourth dimension of mastery.

Not perceiving form internally, one sees external forms that are blue, of blue colour, of blue lustre. Just as a flax-flower is blue, blue in its color, blue in its features, blue in its glow, or just as Vārāṇasī muslin, smooth on both sides, is blue, blue in its color, blue in its features, blue in its glow, in the same way, not perceiving form internally, one sees external forms that are blue, of blue colour, of blue lustre. Mastering them, one has the perception, ‘I know; I see.’ This is the fifth dimension of mastery.

Not perceiving form internally, one sees external forms that are yellow, of yellow colour, of yellow lustre. Just as a *kaṇikāra*-flower is yellow, yellow in its color, yellow in its features, yellow in its glow, or just as Vārāṇasī muslin, smooth on both sides, is yellow, yellow in its color, yellow in its features, yellow in its glow, in the same way, not perceiving form internally, one sees external forms that are yellow, of yellow colour, of yellow lustre. Mastering them, one has the perception, ‘I know; I see.’ This is the sixth dimension of mastery.

Not perceiving form internally, one sees external forms that are red, of red colour, of red lustre. Just as a *bandhujīvaka*-flower is red, red in its color, red in its features, red in its glow, or just as Vārāṇasī muslin, smooth on both sides, is red, red in its color, red in its features, red in its glow, in the same way, not perceiving form internally, one sees external forms that are red, of red colour, of red lustre. Mastering them, one has the perception, ‘I know; I see.’
This is the seventh means of mastery.

“Not perceiving forms internally, one sees external forms that are white, of white colour, of white lustre, white in radiance.

Just as the morning star is white, of white colour, white in appearance, with white luminosity, or like fine Benares muslin which, burnished on both sides, is white, white in color, of a white luster.

So not perceiving forms internally, one sees external forms that are white, of white colour, of white lustre, white in radiance, and mastering these, one is aware that one knows and sees them.

This is the eighth means of mastery.

These, Ānanda, are the eight means of mastery.

Eight liberations.
<p n="173" rend="bodytext"><hi rend="paranum">173</hi><hi rend="dot">.</hi><hi rend="bold">Abhibhāyatanānī</hi>ti abhibhavanakāraṇāni. Kiṃ abhibhavanti? Paccanīkadhammepi ārammaṇānipi. Tāni hi paṭipakkhabhāvena paccanīkadhamme abhibhavanti, puggalassa ñāṇuttariyatāya ārammaṇāni.</p> <p rend="bodytext"><hi rend="bold">Ajjhattaṃ rūpasaññī</hi>tiādīsu pana ajjhattarūpe parikammavasena ajjhattaṃ rūpasaññī nāma hoti. Ajjhattañhi nīlaparikammaṃ karonto kese vā pitte vā akkhitārakāya vā karoti. Pītaparikammaṃ karonto mede vā chaviyā vā hatthapādapiṭṭhesu vā akkhīnaṃ pītakaṭṭhāne vā karoti. Lohitaparikammaṃ karonto maṃse vā lohite vā jivhāya vā akkhīnaṃ rattaṭṭhāne vā karoti. Odātaparikammaṃ karonto aṭṭhimhi vā dante vā nakhe vā akkhīnaṃ setaṭṭhāne vā karoti. Taṃ pana sunīlaṃ supītaṃ sulohitakaṃ suodātakaṃ na hoti, avisuddhameva hoti.</p> <hi rend="bold">Ajjhattaṃ rūpasaññī</hi> <p rend="bodytext"><hi rend="bold">Eko bahiddhā rūpāni passatī</hi>ti yassevaṃ parikammaṃ ajjhattaṃ uppannaṃ hoti, nimittaṃ pana bahiddhā, so evaṃ ajjhattaṃ parikammassa bahiddhā ca appanāya vasena – ‘‘ajjhattaṃ rūpasaññī eko bahiddhā rūpāni passatī’’ti vuccati. <hi rend="bold">Parittānī</hi>ti avaḍḍhitāni. <hi rend="bold">Suvaṇṇadubbaṇṇānī</hi>ti suvaṇṇāni vā honti, dubbaṇṇāni vā. Parittavaseneva idaṃ abhibhāyatanaṃ vuttanti veditabbaṃ. <hi rend="bold">Tāni abhibhuyyā</hi>ti yathā nāma sampannagahaṇiko kaṭacchumattaṃ bhattaṃ labhitvā – ‘‘kiṃ <pb ed="M" n="2.0152"/> ettha bhuñjitabbaṃ atthī’’ti saṅkaḍḍhitvā ekakabaḷameva karoti, evameva ñāṇuttariko puggalo visadañāṇo <pb ed="V" n="2.0136"/> – ‘‘kiṃ ettha parittake ārammaṇe samāpajjitabbaṃ atthi, nāyaṃ mama bhāro’’ti tāni rūpāni abhibhavitvā samāpajjati, saha nimittuppādenevettha appanaṃ pāpetīti attho. <hi rend="bold">Jānāmi</hi><pb ed="P" n="2.0562"/><hi rend="bold">passāmī</hi>ti iminā panassa ābhogo kathito. So ca kho samāpattito vuṭṭhitassa, na antosamāpattiyaṃ. <hi rend="bold">Evaṃsaññī hotī</hi>ti ābhogasaññāyapi jhānasaññāyapi evaṃsaññī hoti.
