Abhibhavanasaññā hissa antosamāpattiyampi atthi, ābhogasaññā pana samāpattito vuṭṭhitasseva.</p> <hi rend="bold">Eko bahiddhā rūpāni passatī</hi> <hi rend="bold">Parittānī</hi> <hi rend="bold">Suvaṇṇadubbaṇṇānī</hi> <hi rend="bold">Tāni abhibhuyyā</hi> <pb ed="M" n="2.0152"/> <pb ed="V" n="2.0136"/> <hi rend="bold">Jānāmi</hi> <pb ed="P" n="2.0562"/> <hi rend="bold">passāmī</hi> <hi rend="bold">Evaṃsaññī hotī</hi> <p rend="bodytext"><hi rend="bold">Appamāṇānī</hi>ti vaḍḍhitappamāṇāni, mahantānīti attho. <hi rend="bold">Abhibhuyyā</hi>ti ettha pana yathā mahagghaso puriso ekaṃ bhattavaḍḍhitakaṃ labhitvā – ‘‘aññampi hotu, kiṃ etaṃ mayhaṃ karissatī’’ti taṃ na mahantato passati, evameva ñāṇuttaro puggalo visadañāṇo ‘‘kiṃ ettha samāpajjitabbaṃ, nayidaṃ appamāṇaṃ, na mayhaṃ cittekaggatākaraṇe bhāro atthī’’ti tāni abhibhavitvā samāpajjati, saha nimittuppādenevettha appanaṃ pāpetīti attho.</p> <hi rend="bold">Appamāṇānī</hi> <hi rend="bold">Abhibhuyyā</hi> <p rend="bodytext"><hi rend="bold">Ajjhattaṃ arūpasaññī</hi>ti alābhitāya vā anatthikatāya vā ajjhattarūpe parikammasaññāvirahito.</p> <hi rend="bold">Ajjhattaṃ arūpasaññī</hi> <p rend="bodytext"><hi rend="bold">Eko bahiddhā rūpāni passatī</hi>ti yassa parikammampi nimittampi bahiddhāva uppannaṃ, so evaṃ bahiddhā parikammassa ceva appanāya ca vasena – ‘‘ajjhattaṃ arūpasaññī eko bahiddhā rūpāni passatī’’ti vuccati. Sesamettha catutthābhibhāyatane vuttanayameva. Imesu pana catūsu parittaṃ vitakkacaritavasena āgataṃ, appamāṇaṃ mohacaritavasena, suvaṇṇaṃ dosacaritavasena, dubbaṇṇaṃ rāgacaritavasena. Etesañhi etāni sappāyāni. Sā ca nesaṃ sappāyatā vitthārato visuddhimagge caritaniddese vuttā.</p> <hi rend="bold">Eko bahiddhā rūpāni passatī</hi> <p rend="bodytext">Pañcamaabhibhāyatanādīsu <hi rend="bold">nīlānī</hi>ti sabbasaṅgāhakavasena vuttaṃ. <hi rend="bold">Nīlavaṇṇānī</hi>ti vaṇṇavasena. <hi rend="bold">Nīlanidassanānī</hi>ti nidassanavasena, apaññāya mānavivarāni asambhinnavaṇṇāni ekanīlāneva hutvā dissantīti vuttaṃ hoti. <hi rend="bold">Nīlanibhāsānī</hi>ti idaṃ pana obhāsavasena vuttaṃ, nīlobhāsāni nīlappabhāyuttānīti attho. Etena nesaṃ visuddhataṃ dasseti. Visuddhavaṇṇavaseneva <pb ed="M" n="2.0153"/> hi imāni cattāri abhibhāyatanāni vuttāni. <hi rend="bold">Umāpuppha</hi>nti etañhi pupphaṃ siniddhaṃ mudu, dissamānampi nīlameva hoti. Girikaṇṇikapupphādīni pana dissamānāni setadhātukāneva honti. Tasmā idameva gahitaṃ, na <pb ed="P" n="2.0563"/> tāni. <hi rend="bold">Bārāṇaseyyaka</hi>nti bārāṇasisambhavaṃ. Tattha kira kappāsopi <pb ed="V" n="2.0137"/> mudu, suttakantikāyopi tantavāyāpi chekā, udakampi suci siniddhaṃ. Tasmā taṃ vatthaṃ ubhatobhāgavimaṭṭhaṃ hoti; dvīsupi passesu maṭṭhaṃ mudu siniddhaṃ khāyati.</p> <hi rend="bold">nīlānī</hi> <hi rend="bold">Nīlavaṇṇānī</hi> <hi rend="bold">Nīlanidassanānī</hi> <hi rend="bold">Nīlanibhāsānī</hi> <pb ed="M" n="2.0153"/> <hi rend="bold">Umāpuppha</hi> <pb ed="P" n="2.0563"/> <hi rend="bold">Bārāṇaseyyaka</hi> <pb ed="V" n="2.0137"/> <p rend="bodytext"><hi rend="bold">Pītānī</hi>tiādīsupi imināva nayena attho veditabbo. ‘‘Nīlakasiṇaṃ uggaṇhanto nīlasmiṃ nimittaṃ gaṇhāti pupphasmiṃ vā vatthasmiṃ vā vaṇṇadhātuyā vā’’tiādikaṃ panettha kasiṇakaraṇañca parikammañca appanāvidhānañca sabbaṃ visuddhimagge vitthārato vuttameva. Imānipi aṭṭha abhibhāyatanāni abhītabhāvadassanatthameva ānītāni. Imāni kira vatvā evamāha – ‘‘ānanda, evarūpāpi samāpattiyo samāpajjantassa ca vuṭṭhahantassa ca tathāgatassa bhayaṃ vā sārajjaṃ vā natthi, māraṃ pana ekakaṃ disvā tathāgato bhāyeyyāti ko evaṃ saññaṃ uppādetumarahati. Abhīto, ānanda, tathāgato acchambhī, sato sampajāno āyusaṅkhāraṃ ossajī’’ti.</p> <hi rend="bold">Pītānī</hi> <p rend="subhead">Aṭṭhavimokkhavaṇṇanā</p>
173. *Abhibhāyatanānī* means the causes of overcoming.

What do they overcome? They overcome opposing qualities and objects.

They overcome opposing qualities by means of being on the opposing side, [and they overcome] objects by means of the excellence of a person's knowledge.

*Ajjhattaṃ rūpasaññī* etc., [means:] Moreover, *ajjhattaṃ rūpasaññī* is what someone is called when internal form is the means of preliminary work.

When doing preliminary work on internal [form], he makes [it] hair, bile, or the pupil of the eye.

When doing preliminary work on yellow [form], he makes [it] fat, skin, the soles of the hands and feet, or the yellow place of the eyes.

When doing preliminary work on red [form], he makes [it] flesh, blood, the tongue, or the red place of the eyes.

When doing preliminary work on white [form], he makes [it] bones, teeth, nails, or the white place of the eyes.

But that is not very blue, very yellow, very red, [or] very white; it is just impure.

*Ajjhattaṃ rūpasaññī eko bahiddhā rūpāni passatī* means, for whomever the preliminary work has arisen internally and the sign is external, in that way, because of the preliminary work being internal and the application being external, it is said, "ajjhattaṃ rūpasaññī eko bahiddhā rūpāni passatī."

*Parittānī* means undeveloped.

*Suvaṇṇadubbaṇṇānī* means they are either beautiful or ugly.

This *abhibhāyatana* is to be understood as having been spoken of only by way of being limited.

*Tāni abhibhuyyā* means, just as a rich householder, having obtained a ladleful of food, thinks, "What is there to eat here?" and gathers [it] up and makes [it] just one mouthful; even so, a person of superior knowledge, with clear knowledge . . . , thinks, "What is there to attain here in [this] limited object? This is not my burden." Overcoming those forms, he attains [absorption]. The meaning is that he brings the application about together with the arising of the sign.

*Jānāmi passāmī* means that with this, its expanse is spoken of.

And that is for one who has arisen from attainment, not during the attainment.

*Evaṃsaññī hotī* means he is evaṃsaññī even with regard to the perception of expanse and with regard to the perception of *jhāna*.

The perception of overcoming exists for him even during the attainment, but the perception of expanse exists only for one who has arisen from the attainment.

*Eko bahiddhā rūpāni passatī parittānī suvaṇṇadubbaṇṇānī tāni abhibhuyyā*

*Jānāmi passāmī evaṃsaññī hotī*

*Appamāṇānī* means of increased measure; the meaning is, they are great.

*Abhibhuyyā* means, here, just as a very hungry person, having obtained one portion of food, does not see that it is very large, [thinking,] "Let there be something else; what will this do for me?" Even so, a person of superior knowledge, with clear knowledge, [thinking,] "What is there to attain here? This is not unlimited. There is no burden for me in making concentration of mind," overcoming those, he attains [absorption]. The meaning is that he brings the application about together with the arising of the sign.

*Appamāṇānī abhibhuyyā*

*Ajjhattaṃ arūpasaññī* means he is without the perception of preliminary work on internal form because of not obtaining or because of uselessness.

*Ajjhattaṃ arūpasaññī eko bahiddhā rūpāni passatī* means, for whomever the preliminary work and the sign have arisen externally, in that way, because of the preliminary work and the application being external, it is said, "ajjhattaṃ arūpasaññī eko bahiddhā rūpāni passatī."

The remainder here is just in the manner stated in the fourth *abhibhāyatana*.

Moreover, in these four, the limited comes by way of the disposition of one given to discursive thinking, the unlimited by way of the disposition of one given to delusion, the beautiful by way of the disposition of one given to aversion, [and] the ugly by way of the disposition of one given to passion.

For these, these are suitable.

And their suitability is stated in detail in the chapter on the conduct in the *Visuddhimagga*.

*Eko bahiddhā rūpāni passatī*

In the fifth *abhibhāyatana* etc., *nīlānī* is stated by way of including everything.

*Nīlavaṇṇānī* is by way of color.

*Nīlanidassanānī* is by way of appearance; it is said that the holes in the māna, without wisdom, with unmixed colors, appear as just one blue.

*Nīlanibhāsānī* means that this is stated by way of light; the meaning is, they are blue lights, connected with blue radiance.

By this, he shows their purity.

Indeed, these four *abhibhāyatanas* are stated only by way of pure color.
*umāpuppha* means that this flower is smooth and soft; even when seen, it is only blue.

Girikaṇṇika flowers, etc., however, when seen, are only white in substance.

Therefore, only this is taken, not those.

*bārāṇaseyyaka* means originating in Vārāṇasī.

There, it is said that even the cotton is soft, and the spinners and weavers are skilled, and the water is pure and smooth.

Therefore, that cloth is polished on both sides; on both sides it appears polished, soft, and smooth.

*nīlānī*, *nīlavaṇṇānī*, *nīlanidassanānī*, *nīlanibhāsānī* *umāpuppha* *bārāṇaseyyaka*

*pītānī*, etc., in these also, the meaning should be understood in this way.

"When acquiring the blue *kasiṇa*, he takes the mark in the blue, whether in a flower or in a cloth or in the element of color," etc., here, the making of the *kasiṇa*, the preliminary work, the establishment of the *appanā*, and everything is already extensively stated in the *Visuddhimagga*.

These eight sources of superiority (*abhibhāyatana*) have also been brought only for the purpose of showing the state of fearlessness (*abhītabhāva*).

Having said these things, he said thus: "Ānanda, even for the Tathāgata who enters into such attainments (*samāpatti*) and emerges from them, there is no fear or hesitation. Who would think of producing such a notion that the Tathāgata would be afraid upon seeing Māra alone?

Fearless, Ānanda, is the Tathāgata, without trembling, mindful, fully aware, he relinquished the life force (*āyusaṅkhāra*)."

*pītānī* Explanation of the Eight Deliverances (*aṭṭhavimokkha*)
174
<p n="174" rend="bodytext"><hi rend="paranum">174</hi><hi rend="dot">.</hi> ‘‘Aṭṭha kho ime, ānanda, vimokkhā. Katame aṭṭha? Rūpī rūpāni passati, ayaṃ paṭhamo vimokkho. Ajjhattaṃ <pb ed="P" n="2.0112"/> arūpasaññī bahiddhā rūpāni passati, ayaṃ dutiyo vimokkho. Subhanteva adhimutto hoti, ayaṃ tatiyo vimokkho. Sabbaso rūpasaññānaṃ samatikkamā paṭighasaññānaṃ atthaṅgamā nānattasaññānaṃ amanasikārā ‘ananto ākāso’ti ākāsānañcāyatanaṃ upasampajja viharati, ayaṃ catuttho vimokkho. Sabbaso ākāsānañcāyatanaṃ samatikkamma ‘anantaṃ viññāṇa’nti viññāṇañcāyatanaṃ upasampajja viharati, ayaṃ pañcamo vimokkho. Sabbaso viññāṇañcāyatanaṃ samatikkamma ‘natthi kiñcī’ti ākiñcaññāyatanaṃ upasampajja viharati, ayaṃ chaṭṭho vimokkho. Sabbaso ākiñcaññāyatanaṃ samatikkamma nevasaññānāsaññāyatanaṃ upasampajja viharati. Ayaṃ sattamo vimokkho. Sabbaso nevasaññānāsaññāyatanaṃ samatikkamma saññāvedayitanirodhaṃ upasampajja viharati, ayaṃ aṭṭhamo vimokkho. Ime kho, ānanda, aṭṭha vimokkhā.</p>
“Now there are eight liberations, Ānanda.

What are the eight? Possessing form, one sees forms. That is the first liberation (*prathamo vimokkho*).

Not percipient of form internally, one sees forms externally. This is the second liberation (*dutiyo vimokkho*).

Experiencing loveliness, one is intent upon it; this is the third liberation (*tatiyo vimokkho*).

Through the complete surmounting of perceptions of material form, the passing away of perceptions of impingement, and non-attention to perceptions of diversity, ‘Space is infinite,’ one enters and dwells in the base of the infinity of space. This is the fourth liberation (*catuttho vimokkho*).

By transcending the Sphere of Infinite Space, thinking: “Consciousness is infinite”, one enters and abides in the Sphere of Infinite Consciousness. That is the fifth liberation (*pañcamo vimokkho*).

By transcending the Sphere of Infinite Consciousness, thinking: “There is no thing”, one enters and abides in the Sphere of NoThingness. That is the sixth liberation (*chaṭṭho vimokkho*).

By transcending the Sphere of No-Thing- ness, one reaches and abides in the Sphere of Neither-Percep- tion-Nor-Non-Perception. That is the seventh liberation (*sattamo vimokkho*).

By transcending the Sphere of Neither-Perception-Nor-Non-Perception, one enters and abides in the Cessation of Perception and Feeling. That is the eighth liberation (*aṭṭhamo vimokkho*).

These, Ānanda, are the eight liberations (*aṭṭha vimokkhā*).
<p n="174" rend="bodytext"><hi rend="paranum">174</hi><hi rend="dot">.</hi> Vimokkhakathā uttānatthāyeva. Imepi aṭṭha vimokkhā abhītabhāvadassanatthameva ānītā. Imepi kira vatvā evamāha – ‘‘ānanda, etāpi samāpattiyo samāpajjantassa ca vuṭṭhahantassa ca tathāgatassa bhayaṃ vā sārajjaṃ vā natthi…pe… ossajī’’ti.</p>
174. The discourse on liberation is clear in meaning.

These eight liberations are also brought forth to show the state of fearlessness.

Having said this, he said thus: "Ānanda, for the Tathāgata, even when entering into and emerging from these attainments ( *samāpatti*), there is no fear or timidity... pe... I relinquish."
175
<p n="175" rend="bodytext"><hi rend="paranum">175</hi><hi rend="dot">.</hi> ‘‘Ekamidāhaṃ <pb ed="V" n="2.0087"/>, ānanda, samayaṃ uruvelāyaṃ viharāmi najjā nerañjarāya tīre ajapālanigrodhe paṭhamābhisambuddho. Atha kho, ānanda, māro pāpimā yenāhaṃ tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā ekamantaṃ aṭṭhāsi. Ekamantaṃ ṭhito kho, ānanda, māro pāpimā maṃ <pb ed="T" n="2.0132"/> etadavoca – ‘parinibbātudāni, bhante, bhagavā; parinibbātu sugato, parinibbānakālodāni, bhante, bhagavato’ti. Evaṃ vutte ahaṃ, ānanda, māraṃ pāpimantaṃ etadavocaṃ –</p> <p rend="bodytext">‘‘‘Na tāvāhaṃ, pāpima, parinibbāyissāmi, yāva me bhikkhū na sāvakā bhavissanti viyattā vinītā visāradā bahussutā dhammadharā dhammānudhammappaṭipannā <pb ed="M" n="2.0095"/> sāmīcippaṭipannā anudhammacārino, sakaṃ ācariyakaṃ uggahetvā ācikkhissanti desessanti paññapessanti paṭṭhapessanti <pb ed="P" n="2.0113"/> vivarissanti vibhajissanti uttānīkarissanti, uppannaṃ parappavādaṃ sahadhammena suniggahitaṃ niggahetvā sappāṭihāriyaṃ dhammaṃ desessanti.</p> <pb ed="M" n="2.0095"/> <pb ed="P" n="2.0113"/> <p rend="bodytext">‘‘‘Na tāvāhaṃ, pāpima, parinibbāyissāmi, yāva me bhikkhuniyo na sāvikā bhavissanti viyattā vinītā visāradā bahussutā dhammadharā dhammānudhammappaṭipannā sāmīcippaṭipannā anudhammacāriniyo, sakaṃ ācariyakaṃ uggahetvā ācikkhissanti desessanti paññapessanti paṭṭhapessanti vivarissanti vibhajissanti uttānīkarissanti, uppannaṃ parappavādaṃ sahadhammena <pb ed="T" n="2.0133"/> suniggahitaṃ niggahetvā sappāṭihāriyaṃ dhammaṃ desessanti.</p> <pb ed="T" n="2.0133"/> <p rend="bodytext">‘‘‘Na tāvāhaṃ, pāpima, parinibbāyissāmi, yāva me upāsakā na sāvakā bhavissanti viyattā vinītā visāradā bahussutā dhammadharā dhammānudhammappaṭipannā sāmīcippaṭipannā anudhammacārino, sakaṃ ācariyakaṃ uggahetvā ācikkhissanti desessanti paññapessanti paṭṭhapessanti vivarissanti vibhajissanti uttānīkarissanti, uppannaṃ parappavādaṃ sahadhammena suniggahitaṃ niggahetvā sappāṭihāriyaṃ dhammaṃ desessanti.</p> <p rend="bodytext">‘‘‘Na tāvāhaṃ, pāpima, parinibbāyissāmi, yāva me upāsikā na sāvikā bhavissanti viyattā vinītā visāradā bahussutā dhammadharā dhammānudhammappaṭipannā sāmīcippaṭipannā anudhammacāriniyo, sakaṃ ācariyakaṃ uggahetvā ācikkhissanti desessanti paññapessanti paṭṭhapessanti vivarissanti vibhajissanti uttānīkarissanti, uppannaṃ parappavādaṃ sahadhammena suniggahitaṃ niggahetvā sappāṭihāriyaṃ dhammaṃ desessanti.</p> <p rend="bodytext">‘‘‘Na <pb ed="V" n="2.0088"/> tāvāhaṃ, pāpima, parinibbāyissāmi, yāva me idaṃ brahmacariyaṃ na iddhañceva bhavissati phītañca vitthārikaṃ bāhujaññaṃ puthubhūtaṃ yāva devamanussehi suppakāsita’nti.</p> <pb ed="V" n="2.0088"/>
175. “One time, Ānanda, I was staying at Uruvelā on the bank of the Nerañjarā River at the Goat-herd Banyan, newly awakened. Then Māra, the Evil One, approached me and, on arrival, stood to one side. Standing to one side, Māra the Evil One, said this to me: ‘Now is the time for the Blessed Lord’s final Nirvāṇa, O venerable one; may the Well-Gone One be completely liberated! Now is the time for the Blessed Lord’s Parinirvāṇa, O venerable one!’

“When this was said, I, Ānanda, said this to Māra the Evil One: ‘I will not attain *parinirvāṇa*, Evil One, until my monks become disciples—accomplished, trained, skilled, learned, upholders of the *dharma*, living according to the *dharma*, practicing masterfully, living in accordance with the *dharma*; having learned from their own teachers, they will declare it, teach it, describe it, set it forth, reveal it, explain it in detail, and make it clear; when opposing teachings arise, they will refute them thoroughly in accordance with the *dharma*, and they will teach the *dharma* with wondrous effect.

“‘I will not attain *parinirvāṇa*, Evil One, until my nuns become disciples—accomplished, trained, skilled, learned, upholders of the *dharma*, living according to the *dharma*, practicing masterfully, living in accordance with the *dharma*; having learned from their own teachers, they will declare it, teach it, describe it, set it forth, reveal it, explain it in detail, and make it clear; when opposing teachings arise, they will refute them thoroughly in accordance with the *dharma*, and they will teach the *dharma* with wondrous effect.

“‘I will not attain *parinirvāṇa*, Evil One, until my male lay followers become disciples—accomplished, trained, skilled, learned, upholders of the *dharma*, living according to the *dharma*, practicing masterfully, living in accordance with the *dharma*; having learned from their own teachers, they will declare it, teach it, describe it, set it forth, reveal it, explain it in detail, and make it clear; when opposing teachings arise, they will refute them thoroughly in accordance with the *dharma*, and they will teach the *dharma* with wondrous effect.’

“‘I will not attain *parinirvāṇa*, Evil One, until my female lay followers become disciples—accomplished, trained, skilled, learned, upholders of the *dharma*, living according to the *dharma*, practicing masterfully, living in accordance with the *dharma*; having learned from their own teachers, they will declare it, teach it, describe it, set it forth, reveal it, explain it in detail, and make it clear; when opposing teachings arise, they will refute them thoroughly in accordance with the *dharma*, and they will teach the *dharma* with wondrous effect.’

“‘Evil One, I will not attain *parinirvāṇa* until this holy life of mine is powerful, prosperous, widely spread, disseminated among many people, and well-expounded as far as there are gods and humans.’”
<p n="175" rend="bodytext"><hi rend="paranum">175</hi><hi rend="dot">.</hi> Idānipi bhagavā ānandassa okāsaṃ adatvāva <hi rend="bold">ekamidāha</hi>ntiādinā nayena aparampi desanaṃ ārabhi. Tattha <hi rend="bold">paṭhamābhisambuddho</hi>ti abhisambuddho hutvā paṭhamameva aṭṭhame sattāhe.</p>
Now, without giving Ānanda an opportunity, the Blessed One began another teaching in the manner of "He spoke one thing" (ekamidāha).

There, *first fully awakened* (paṭhamābhisambuddho) means having become fully awakened, in the first week, in the eighth week.
176
<p n="176" rend="bodytext"><hi rend="paranum">176</hi><hi rend="dot">.</hi> ‘‘Idāneva kho, ānanda, ajja cāpāle cetiye māro pāpimā yenāhaṃ tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā ekamantaṃ aṭṭhāsi. Ekamantaṃ ṭhito kho, ānanda, māro pāpimā maṃ etadavoca – ‘parinibbātudāni, bhante, bhagavā, parinibbātu sugato, parinibbānakālodāni, bhante, bhagavato. Bhāsitā kho panesā, bhante, bhagavatā vācā – ‘‘na tāvāhaṃ, pāpima <pb ed="M" n="2.0096"/>, parinibbāyissāmi <pb ed="P" n="2.0114"/>, yāva me bhikkhū na sāvakā bhavissanti…pe… yāva me bhikkhuniyo na sāvikā bhavissanti…pe… yāva me upāsakā na sāvakā bhavissanti…pe… yāva me upāsikā na sāvikā bhavissanti…pe… yāva me idaṃ brahmacariyaṃ na iddhañceva bhavissati phītañca vitthārikaṃ bāhujaññaṃ puthubhūtaṃ, yāva devamanussehi suppakāsita’’nti. Etarahi kho pana, bhante, bhagavato brahmacariyaṃ <pb ed="T" n="2.0134"/> iddhañceva phītañca vitthārikaṃ bāhujaññaṃ puthubhūtaṃ, yāva devamanussehi suppakāsitaṃ. Parinibbātudāni, bhante, bhagavā, parinibbātu sugato, parinibbānakālodāni, bhante, bhagavato’ti.</p>
176. Just now, Ānanda, today at the Cāpāla Shrine, Māra the Evil One approached me, and having approached, stood to one side.

Standing to one side, Ānanda, Māra the Evil One said this to me: ‘Now, venerable sir, let the Blessed One attain final **Nirvāṇa** (parinibbāna); let the Well-Gone One attain final **Nirvāṇa**; now is the time for the Blessed One's final **Nirvāṇa**.’

But these words were spoken by the Blessed One: ‘Evil One, I will not attain final **Nirvāṇa** (parinibbāyissāmi) until my monks are not yet disciples …pe… until my nuns are not yet disciples …pe… until my male lay followers are not yet disciples …pe… until my female lay followers are not yet disciples …pe… until this holy life (**brahmacariya**) is not powerful, prosperous, widespread, well-known, and well proclaimed among gods and humans.’

But now, venerable sir, the Blessed One's holy life (**brahmacariyaṃ**) is powerful, prosperous, widespread, well-known, and well proclaimed among gods and humans.

Now, venerable sir, let the Blessed One attain final **Nirvāṇa** (parinibbāna); let the Well-Gone One attain final **Nirvāṇa**; now is the time for the Blessed One's final **Nirvāṇa**.’
177
<p n="177" rend="bodytext"><hi rend="paranum">177</hi><hi rend="dot">.</hi> ‘‘Evaṃ vutte, ahaṃ, ānanda, māraṃ pāpimantaṃ etadavocaṃ – ‘appossukko tvaṃ, pāpima, hohi, naciraṃ tathāgatassa parinibbānaṃ bhavissati. Ito tiṇṇaṃ māsānaṃ accayena tathāgato parinibbāyissatī’ti. Idāneva kho, ānanda, ajja cāpāle cetiye tathāgatena satena sampajānena āyusaṅkhāro ossaṭṭho’’ti.</p> <p rend="subhead">Ānandayācanakathā</p>
“When this was said, I, Ānanda, spoke thus to Māra, the Evil One: ‘Be without worry, Evil One. Before long, the final passing away (parinirvāṇa) of the Tathāgata will occur. In three months from now, the Tathāgata will attain parinirvāṇa.’ And just now, Ānanda, here at the Cāpāla shrine, the Tathāgata, mindful and fully aware, has relinquished the life principle (āyusaṅkhāra).”

The Account of Ānanda's Entreaty
<p n="177" rend="bodytext"><hi rend="paranum">177</hi><hi rend="dot">.</hi><hi rend="bold">Ossaṭṭho</hi>ti vissajjito paricchinno, evaṃ kira vatvā – ‘‘tenāyaṃ dasasahassī lokadhātu kampitthā’’ti āha.</p> <p rend="subhead">Ānandayācanakathā</p>
177. *Ossaṭṭho* means released, distinguished. Thus, it is said, “Then this ten-thousandfold world system trembled.”

The Story of Ānanda's Request
178
<p n="178" rend="bodytext"><hi rend="paranum">178</hi><hi rend="dot">.</hi> Evaṃ <pb ed="P" n="2.0115"/> vutte āyasmā ānando bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – ‘‘tiṭṭhatu, bhante, bhagavā kappaṃ, tiṭṭhatu sugato kappaṃ bahujanahitāya bahujanasukhāya lokānukampāya atthāya hitāya sukhāya devamanussāna’’nti.</p> <p rend="bodytext">‘‘Alaṃdāni, ānanda. Mā tathāgataṃ yāci, akālodāni, ānanda, tathāgataṃ yācanāyā’’ti. Dutiyampi kho āyasmā ānando…pe… tatiyampi kho āyasmā ānando bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – ‘‘tiṭṭhatu, bhante, bhagavā kappaṃ, tiṭṭhatu sugato kappaṃ bahujanahitāya bahujanasukhāya lokānukampāya atthāya hitāya sukhāya devamanussāna’’nti.</p> <p rend="bodytext">‘‘Saddahasi <pb ed="V" n="2.0089"/> tvaṃ, ānanda, tathāgatassa bodhi’’nti? ‘‘Evaṃ, bhante’’. ‘‘Atha kiñcarahi tvaṃ, ānanda, tathāgataṃ yāvatatiyakaṃ abhinippīḷesī’’ti? ‘‘Sammukhā metaṃ, bhante, bhagavato sutaṃ sammukhā paṭiggahitaṃ – ‘yassa kassaci, ānanda, cattāro iddhipādā bhāvitā bahulīkatā yānīkatā vatthukatā anuṭṭhitā paricitā susamāraddhā, so ākaṅkhamāno <pb ed="T" n="2.0135"/> kappaṃ vā tiṭṭheyya kappāvasesaṃ vā. Tathāgatassa kho, ānanda, cattāro iddhipādā bhāvitā bahulīkatā yānīkatā vatthukatā anuṭṭhitā paricitā susamāraddhā. So <pb ed="M" n="2.0097"/> ākaṅkhamāno, ānanda, tathāgato kappaṃ vā tiṭṭheyya kappāvasesaṃ vā’’’ti. ‘‘Saddahasi tvaṃ, ānandā’’ti? ‘‘Evaṃ, bhante’’. ‘‘Tasmātihānanda, tuyhevetaṃ dukkaṭaṃ, tuyhevetaṃ aparaddhaṃ, yaṃ tvaṃ tathāgatena evaṃ oḷārike nimitte kayiramāne oḷārike obhāse kayiramāne nāsakkhi paṭivijjhituṃ, na tathāgataṃ yāci – ‘tiṭṭhatu, bhante, bhagavā kappaṃ, tiṭṭhatu sugato kappaṃ bahujanahitāya bahujanasukhāya lokānukampāya atthāya hitāya sukhāya devamanussāna’’nti. Sace tvaṃ, ānanda, tathāgataṃ yāceyyāsi, dveva te vācā tathāgato paṭikkhipeyya, atha tatiyakaṃ adhivāseyya. Tasmātihānanda, tuyhevetaṃ dukkaṭaṃ, tuyhevetaṃ aparaddhaṃ.</p> <pb ed="V" n="2.0089"/> <pb ed="T" n="2.0135"/> <pb ed="M" n="2.0097"/>
178. Thus, when this was said, Venerable Ānanda said this to the Blessed One: “May the Blessed One remain for an eon ( *kappa*), O venerable one! May the Well-Gone (*sugata*) remain for an eon, for the benefit of many, for the happiness of many, out of compassion for the world, for the good, benefit, and happiness of gods (*deva*) and humans!”

“Enough, Ānanda. Do not beg the *Tathāgata*. It is not the right time, Ānanda, for begging the *Tathāgata*.”

A second time... A third time, Venerable Ānanda said this to the Blessed One: “May the Blessed One remain for an eon, O venerable one! May the Well-Gone (*sugata*) remain for an eon, for the benefit of many, for the happiness of many, out of compassion for the world, for the good, benefit, and happiness of gods (*deva*) and humans!”

“Ānanda, do you have faith in the *Tathāgata*'s enlightenment (*bodhi*)?” “Yes, venerable one.”

“Then why, Ānanda, did you press the *Tathāgata* so much, even up to the third time?” “Venerable sir, I have heard and learned directly from the Blessed One: ‘Anyone, Ānanda, in whom the four bases of power (*iddhipāda*) are developed, pursued, given a means of transport, given a grounding, steadied, consolidated, and well-undertaken, could—if he wanted—remain for an eon or the remainder of an eon.’

The *Tathāgata*, Ānanda, has done so. He could—if he wanted—remain for an eon or the remainder of an eon.”

“Do you have faith, Ānanda?” “Yes, venerable one.”

“Therefore, Ānanda, the fault is yours; herein have you failed, inasmuch as you were unable to grasp the plain suggestion, the significant prompting given by the *Tathāgata*, and you did not then entreat the *Tathāgata* to remain: ‘May the Blessed One remain for an eon, O venerable one! May the Well-Gone (*sugata*) remain for an eon, for the benefit of many, for the happiness of many, out of compassion for the world, for the good, benefit, and happiness of gods (*deva*) and humans!’”

“If, Ānanda, you had begged him, the *Tathāgata* would twice have refused you, but the third time he would have consented.

Therefore, Ānanda, yours is the fault, yours is the failure.
<p n="178" rend="bodytext"><hi rend="paranum">178</hi><hi rend="dot">.</hi><hi rend="bold">Ala</hi>nti paṭikkhepavacanametaṃ. <hi rend="bold">Bodhi</hi>nti catumaggañāṇapaṭiveghaṃ. <hi rend="bold">Saddahasi tva</hi>nti evaṃ vuttabhāvaṃ tathāgatassa saddahasīti vadati. <hi rend="bold">Tasmātihānandā</hi>ti <pb ed="M" n="2.0154"/> yasmā idaṃ vacanaṃ saddahasi, tasmā tuyhevetaṃ dukkaṭanti dasseti.</p>
"Ala" means this is a word of refusal.

"Bodhi" means the penetration of the knowledge of the four paths (catumārga-jñāna-prativedha).

"Do you believe?" means he says, "Do you believe the state of the Tathāgata's statement thus?"

"Therefore, Ānanda..." Since you believe this statement, therefore, he shows that this is a *dukkata* offense for you.
179
<p n="179" rend="bodytext"><hi rend="paranum">179</hi><hi rend="dot">.</hi> ‘‘Ekamidāhaṃ, ānanda, samayaṃ rājagahe viharāmi gijjhakūṭe pabbate. Tatrāpi kho tāhaṃ, ānanda, āmantesiṃ <pb ed="P" n="2.0116"/> – ‘ramaṇīyaṃ, ānanda, rājagahaṃ, ramaṇīyo, ānanda, gijjhakūṭo pabbato. Yassa kassaci, ānanda, cattāro iddhipādā bhāvitā bahulīkatā yānīkatā vatthukatā anuṭṭhitā paricitā susamāraddhā, so ākaṅkhamāno kappaṃ vā tiṭṭheyya kappāvasesaṃ vā. Tathāgatassa kho, ānanda, cattāro iddhipādā bhāvitā bahulīkatā yānīkatā vatthukatā anuṭṭhitā paricitā susamāraddhā, so ākaṅkhamāno, ānanda, tathāgato kappaṃ vā tiṭṭheyya <pb ed="T" n="2.0136"/> kappāvasesaṃ vā’ti. Evampi kho tvaṃ, ānanda, tathāgatena oḷārike nimitte kayiramāne oḷārike obhāse kayiramāne nāsakkhi paṭivijjhituṃ, na tathāgataṃ yāci – ‘tiṭṭhatu, bhante, bhagavā kappaṃ, tiṭṭhatu sugato kappaṃ bahujanahitāya bahujanasukhāya lokānukampāya atthāya hitāya sukhāya devamanussāna’nti. Sace tvaṃ, ānanda, tathāgataṃ yāceyyāsi, dve te vācā tathāgato paṭikkhipeyya, atha tatiyakaṃ adhivāseyya. Tasmātihānanda, tuyhevetaṃ dukkaṭaṃ, tuyhevetaṃ aparaddhaṃ.</p>
179. “On one occasion, Ānanda, I was staying near Rājagaha, on Vulture Peak Mountain.

And there, Ānanda, I addressed you: ‘Delightful, Ānanda, is Rājagaha; delightful is the Vulture's Peak Mountain.

Anyone, Ānanda, in whom the four bases of spiritual power (*ṛddhipāda*) are developed, practiced frequently, made his vehicle, made his basis, established, become familiar with them, and properly undertaken, could—if he wanted—remain for an eon (*kalpa*) or the remainder of an eon.

The *Tathāgata*, Ānanda, has developed the four bases of spiritual power, practiced frequently, made his vehicle, made his basis, established, become familiar with them, and properly undertaken. The *Tathāgata*, Ānanda, could—if he wanted—remain for an eon or the remainder of an eon.”

But you, Ānanda—even when the *Tathāgata* had given such a plain sign, such a clear hint—weren't able to understand. You did not entreat the *Tathāgata*: ‘Lord (*bhante*), may the Blessed One (*bhagavā*) remain for an eon (*kalpa*). May the Well-Gone (*sugata*) remain for an eon—for the benefit of the many, for the happiness of the many, out of compassion for the world, for the welfare, benefit, and happiness of gods (*deva*) and humans (*manuṣyā*)’.

If you, Ānanda, had entreated the *Tathāgata*, the *Tathāgata* would have rejected your speech twice, but the third time he would have consented.

Therefore, Ānanda, the wrong-doing (*duṣkṛta*) is yours; yours is the fault (*aparāddha*).
<p n="179" rend="bodytext"><hi rend="paranum">179</hi><hi rend="dot">.</hi><hi rend="bold">Ekamidāha</hi>nti <pb ed="V" n="2.0138"/> idaṃ bhagavā – ‘‘na kevalaṃ ahaṃ idheva taṃ āmantesiṃ, aññadāpi āmantetvā oḷārikaṃ nimittaṃ akāsiṃ, tampi <pb ed="P" n="2.0564"/> tayā na paṭividdhaṃ, tavevāyaṃ aparādho’’ti evaṃ sokavinodanatthāya nānappakārato therasseva dosāropanatthaṃ ārabhi.</p>
<p n="179" rend="bodytext"><hi rend="paranum">179</hi><hi rend="dot">.
</hi><hi rend="bold">ekamidāha</hi>nti <pb ed="v" n="2.
0138"/> Here, the Blessed One [said]: "Not only here I addressed him, but at another time, having addressed him, I made a gross sign, but even that <pb ed="p" n="2.
0564"/> was not understood by her. This is your fault." Thus, for the sake of dispelling sorrow, in various ways, he began to impute fault to the elder himself.
</p>
180
<p n="180" rend="bodytext"><hi rend="paranum">180</hi><hi rend="dot">.</hi> ‘‘Ekamidāhaṃ, ānanda, samayaṃ tattheva rājagahe viharāmi gotamanigrodhe…pe… tattheva rājagahe viharāmi corapapāte… tattheva rājagahe viharāmi vebhārapasse sattapaṇṇiguhāyaṃ… tattheva rājagahe viharāmi isigilipasse kāḷasilāyaṃ… tattheva rājagahe viharāmi <pb ed="V" n="2.0090"/> sītavane sappasoṇḍikapabbhāre… tattheva rājagahe viharāmi tapodārāme… tattheva rājagahe viharāmi veḷuvane kalandakanivāpe… tattheva rājagahe viharāmi jīvakambavane… tattheva rājagahe viharāmi maddakucchismiṃ migadāye <pb ed="M" n="2.0098"/> tatrāpi kho tāhaṃ, ānanda, āmantesiṃ – ‘ramaṇīyaṃ, ānanda, rājagahaṃ, ramaṇīyo gijjhakūṭo pabbato, ramaṇīyo gotamanigrodho, ramaṇīyo corapapāto, ramaṇīyā vebhārapasse sattapaṇṇiguhā, ramaṇīyā isigilipasse kāḷasilā, ramaṇīyo sītavane sappasoṇḍikapabbhāro <pb ed="P" n="2.0117"/>, ramaṇīyo tapodārāmo, ramaṇīyo veḷuvane <pb ed="T" n="2.0137"/> kalandakanivāpo, ramaṇīyaṃ jīvakambavanaṃ, ramaṇīyo maddakucchismiṃ migadāyo. Yassa kassaci, ānanda, cattāro iddhipādā bhāvitā bahulīkatā yānīkatā vatthukatā anuṭṭhitā paricitā susamāraddhā…pe… ākaṅkhamāno, ānanda, tathāgato kappaṃ vā tiṭṭheyya kappāvasesaṃ vā’ti. Evampi kho tvaṃ, ānanda, tathāgatena oḷārike nimitte kayiramāne oḷārike obhāse kayiramāne nāsakkhi paṭivijjhituṃ, na tathāgataṃ yāci – ‘tiṭṭhatu, bhante, bhagavā kappaṃ, tiṭṭhatu sugato kappaṃ bahujanahitāya bahujanasukhāya lokānukampāya atthāya hitāya sukhāya devamanussāna’nti. Sace tvaṃ, ānanda, tathāgataṃ yāceyyāsi, dveva te vācā tathāgato paṭikkhipeyya, atha tatiyakaṃ adhivāseyya. Tasmātihānanda, tuyhevetaṃ dukkaṭaṃ, tuyhevetaṃ aparaddhaṃ.</p>
“180. Once, Ānanda, I was staying right there near Rājagaha (Rājagṛha) at the Gotama Banyan tree… right there near Rājagaha at Robbers Cliff… right there near Rājagaha in Sattapaṇṇa Cave on the side of Mount Vebhāra… right there near Rājagaha at the Black Rock on Isigili Mountain… right there near Rājagaha in the Cool Forest at the Slope by the Snakes’ Pool… right there near Rājagaha at Tapodārāma (Tapodārāma) Park… right there near Rājagaha at the Bamboo Forest, the Squirrels’ Feeding Ground, Venuvana (Veḷuvana)… right there near Rājagaha at Jīvakambavana (Jīvakambavana)… right there near Rājagaha in the Maddakucchi Deer Park.

There also, Ānanda, I addressed you: ‘Delightful, Ānanda, is Rājagaha; delightful is Gijjhakūṭa (Gṛdhrakūṭa) Mountain; delightful is Gotamanigrodha (Gotamanigrodha); delightful is Corapapāta (Corapapāta); delightful is Sattapaṇṇiguhā (Sattapaṇṇiguhā) on the side of Mount Vebhāra; delightful is the Black Rock on the side of Mount Isigili; delightful is Sappasoṇḍikapabbhāra (Sappasoṇḍikapabbhāra) in the Cool Forest; delightful is Tapodārāma (Tapodārāma) Park; delightful is Kalandakanivāpa (Kalandakanivāpa) in Veḷuvana (Veḷuvana); delightful is Jīvakambavana (Jīvakambavana); delightful is the Maddakucchi Deer Park.

Whosoever, Ānanda, has developed, practiced frequently, made their vehicle, made their base, established, become familiar with, and properly undertaken the four roads to power (catvāro ṛddhipādāḥ)… could undoubtedly live for a kalpa or the remainder of one.

But you, Ānanda, even when the Tathāgata gave such a blatant sign, such a blatant hint, weren’t able to understand his meaning. You did not beg the Tathāgata: ‘Lord (bhante), may the Blessed One (bhagavā) remain for a kalpa; may the Well-Gone (sugato) remain for a kalpa, for the benefit of the many, for the happiness of the many, out of sympathy for the world, for the welfare, benefit, & happiness of human beings & devas.’

If you, Ānanda, had begged the Tathāgata, the Tathāgata would have twice refused you, but after the third time he would have acquiesced.

Therefore, Ānanda, yours is the wrongdoing; yours is the fault."
181
<p n="181" rend="bodytext"><hi rend="paranum">181</hi><hi rend="dot">.</hi> ‘‘Ekamidāhaṃ, ānanda, samayaṃ idheva vesāliyaṃ viharāmi udene cetiye. Tatrāpi kho tāhaṃ, ānanda, āmantesiṃ – ‘ramaṇīyā, ānanda, vesālī, ramaṇīyaṃ udenaṃ cetiyaṃ. Yassa kassaci, ānanda, cattāro iddhipādā bhāvitā bahulīkatā yānīkatā vatthukatā anuṭṭhitā paricitā susamāraddhā, so ākaṅkhamāno kappaṃ vā tiṭṭheyya kappāvasesaṃ vā. Tathāgatassa kho, ānanda, cattāro iddhipādā bhāvitā <pb ed="T" n="2.0138"/> bahulīkatā yānīkatā vatthukatā anuṭṭhitā paricitā susamāraddhā, so ākaṅkhamāno, ānanda, tathāgato kappaṃ vā tiṭṭheyya kappāvasesaṃ vā’ti. Evampi kho tvaṃ, ānanda, tathāgatena oḷārike nimitte kayiramāne oḷārike obhāse kayiramāne nāsakkhi paṭivijjhituṃ, na tathāgataṃ yāci – ‘tiṭṭhatu, bhante, bhagavā kappaṃ, tiṭṭhatu sugato kappaṃ bahujanahitāya bahujanasukhāya lokānukampāya atthāya hitāya sukhāya devamanussāna’nti. Sace tvaṃ, ānanda, tathāgataṃ yāceyyāsi, dveva te vācā tathāgato paṭikkhipeyya, atha tatiyakaṃ adhivāseyya, tasmātihānanda, tuyhevetaṃ dukkaṭaṃ, tuyhevetaṃ aparaddhaṃ.</p>
“181.”Once, Ānanda, I was staying right here in Vesālī at the Udena shrine.

So also there, Ānanda, I addressed you, saying: ‘Vesālī is delightful, Ānanda; delightful is the Udena shrine.

Anyone, Ānanda, in whom the four bases of power (catāro iddhipādā) are developed, pursued, given a means of transport, given a grounding, steadied, consolidated, and well-undertaken, could—if he wanted—remain for an eon (kappaṃ) or the remainder of an eon (kappāvasesaṃ).

In the Tathāgata, Ānanda, the four bases of power (catāro iddhipādā) are developed, pursued, given a means of transport, given a grounding, steadied, consolidated, and well-undertaken. He could—if he wanted—remain for an eon (kappaṃ) or the remainder of an eon (kappāvasesaṃ).’

But you, Ānanda—even when the Tathāgata had given such a blatant sign, such a blatant hint—weren’t able to understand his meaning. You didn’t beg of the Tathāgata, ‘Lord (bhante), may the Blessed One (bhagavā) remain for an eon (kappaṃ). May the One Well-Gone (sugato) remain for an eon (kappaṃ)—for the benefit of the many, for the happiness of the many, out of sympathy for the world, for the welfare, benefit, & happiness of human beings & devas.’

For if you had done so, Ananda, twice the Tathāgata might have declined, but the third time he would have consented. Therefore, Ānanda, this is your fault, this is your offense.
182
<p n="182" rend="bodytext"><hi rend="paranum">182</hi><hi rend="dot">.</hi> ‘‘Ekamidāhaṃ <pb ed="M" n="2.0099"/><pb ed="P" n="2.0118"/>, ānanda, samayaṃ idheva vesāliyaṃ viharāmi gotamake cetiye <pb ed="V" n="2.0091"/> …pe… idheva vesāliyaṃ viharāmi sattambe cetiye… idheva vesāliyaṃ viharāmi bahuputte cetiye… idheva vesāliyaṃ viharāmi sārandade cetiye… idāneva kho tāhaṃ, ānanda, ajja cāpāle cetiye āmantesiṃ – ‘ramaṇīyā, ānanda, vesālī, ramaṇīyaṃ udenaṃ cetiyaṃ, ramaṇīyaṃ gotamakaṃ cetiyaṃ, ramaṇīyaṃ sattambaṃ cetiyaṃ, ramaṇīyaṃ bahuputtaṃ cetiyaṃ, ramaṇīyaṃ sārandadaṃ cetiyaṃ, ramaṇīyaṃ cāpālaṃ cetiyaṃ. Yassa kassaci, ānanda, cattāro iddhipādā bhāvitā bahulīkatā yānīkatā vatthukatā <pb ed="T" n="2.0139"/> anuṭṭhitā paricitā susamāraddhā, so ākaṅkhamāno kappaṃ vā tiṭṭheyya kappāvasesaṃ vā. Tathāgatassa kho, ānanda, cattāro iddhipādā bhāvitā bahulīkatā yānīkatā vatthukatā anuṭṭhitā paricitā susamāraddhā, so ākaṅkhamāno, ānanda, tathāgato kappaṃ vā tiṭṭheyya kappāvasesaṃ vā’ti. Evampi kho tvaṃ, ānanda, tathāgatena oḷārike nimitte kayiramāne oḷārike obhāse kayiramāne nāsakkhi paṭivijjhituṃ, na tathāgataṃ yāci – ‘tiṭṭhatu bhagavā kappaṃ, tiṭṭhatu sugato kappaṃ bahujanahitāya bahujanasukhāya lokānukampāya atthāya hitāya sukhāya devamanussāna’nti. Sace tvaṃ, ānanda, tathāgataṃ yāceyyāsi, dveva te vācā tathāgato paṭikkhipeyya, atha tatiyakaṃ adhivāseyya. Tasmātihānanda, tuyhevetaṃ dukkaṭaṃ, tuyhevetaṃ aparaddhaṃ.</p>
182.
"Once, Ānanda, I was staying at Vesālī at the Gotamaka shrine... at the Sattamba shrine… at the ManySon shrine… at the Sārandada shrine… And just now, Ānanda, today at the Capāla Shrine, I addressed you: ‘Vesālī is refreshing, Ānanda. Refreshing, too, are the Udena shrine, the Gotamaka shrine, the Sattamba shrine, the ManySon shrine, the Sārandada shrine, the Capāla shrine.’

Ānanda, anyone who has developed, cultivated, practiced, and grounded the four bases of power (*catvāro ṛddhipādā bhāvitā bahulīkatā yānīkatā vatthukatā*), and properly undertaken them, could remain for an eon (kappaṃ) or until the end of an eon.

The Tathāgata, Ānanda, has developed, cultivated, practiced, and grounded the four bases of power (*catvāro ṛddhipādā bhāvitā bahulīkatā yānīkatā vatthukatā*), and properly undertaken them. The Tathāgata could remain for an eon (kappaṃ) or until the end of an eon.”

“But you, Ānanda, even when the Tathāgata had given such a blatant sign, such a blatant hint, weren’t able to understand his meaning. You didn’t beg of the Tathāgata, ‘Lord, may the Blessed One (bhagavā) remain for an eon (kappaṃ). May the Well-Gone One (sugata) remain for an eon (kappaṃ)—for the benefit of the many, for the happiness of the many, out of sympathy for the world, for the welfare, benefit, & happiness of human beings & devas.’

If you had begged the Tathāgata, Ānanda, the Tathāgata would twice have refused you, but the third time he would have consented.

Therefore, Ānanda, yours is the fault, yours is the failure.
183
<p n="183" rend="bodytext"><hi rend="paranum">183</hi><hi rend="dot">.</hi> ‘‘Nanu etaṃ <note>evaṃ (syā. pī.)</note>, ānanda, mayā paṭikacceva <note>paṭigacceva (sī. pī.)</note> akkhātaṃ – ‘sabbeheva piyehi manāpehi nānābhāvo vinābhāvo aññathābhāvo. Taṃ kutettha, ānanda, labbhā, yaṃ taṃ jātaṃ bhūtaṃ saṅkhataṃ palokadhammaṃ, taṃ vata mā palujjīti netaṃ ṭhānaṃ vijjati’. Yaṃ kho panetaṃ, ānanda, tathāgatena cattaṃ vantaṃ muttaṃ pahīnaṃ paṭinissaṭṭhaṃ ossaṭṭho āyusaṅkhāro, ekaṃsena vācā bhāsitā – ‘na ciraṃ tathāgatassa parinibbānaṃ <pb ed="P" n="2.0119"/> bhavissati. Ito tiṇṇaṃ māsānaṃ accayena tathāgato parinibbāyissatī’ti. Tañca <note>taṃ vacanaṃ (sī.)</note> tathāgato jīvitahetu puna paccāvamissatīti <note>paccāgamissatīti (syā. ka.)</note> netaṃ ṭhānaṃ vijjati. Āyāmānanda, yena mahāvanaṃ kūṭāgārasālā tenupasaṅkamissāmā’’ti. ‘‘Evaṃ, bhante’’ti kho <pb ed="M" n="2.0100"/> āyasmā ānando bhagavato paccassosi.</p> <p rend="bodytext">Atha kho bhagavā <pb ed="T" n="2.0140"/> āyasmatā ānandena saddhiṃ yena mahāvanaṃ kūṭāgārasālā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā āyasmantaṃ ānandaṃ āmantesi – ‘‘gaccha tvaṃ, ānanda, yāvatikā bhikkhū vesāliṃ upanissāya viharanti, te sabbe upaṭṭhānasālāyaṃ sannipātehī’’ti. ‘‘Evaṃ, bhante’’ti kho āyasmā ānando bhagavato paṭissutvā yāvatikā bhikkhū vesāliṃ upanissāya viharanti, te sabbe upaṭṭhānasālāyaṃ sannipātetvā yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṃ abhivādetvā ekamantaṃ aṭṭhāsi. Ekamantaṃ ṭhito kho āyasmā ānando bhagavantaṃ etadavoca <pb ed="V" n="2.0092"/> – ‘‘sannipatito, bhante, bhikkhusaṅgho, yassadāni, bhante, bhagavā kālaṃ maññatī’’ti.</p> <pb ed="T" n="2.0140"/> <pb ed="V" n="2.0092"/>
183. “Ānanda, have I not explained this before, that of all things that are dear and beloved there is change, separation, and becoming otherwise? Ānanda, how could this be possible? Whatever is born, become, compounded, is liable to decay—that it should not decay is impossible. And that, Ānanda, which the *Tathāgata* has relinquished, given up, abandoned, and rejected—the life-principle—the *Tathāgata* has spoken with certainty: ‘The *parinirvāṇa* of the *Tathāgata* will not be long delayed. In three months' time the *Tathāgata* will attain *parinirvāṇa*.’ That the *Tathāgata* would turn back on that statement for the sake of continuing to live is impossible. Come, Ānanda, let us go to the Gabled Hall in the Great Forest.” “So be it, Lord,” the Venerable Ānanda replied to the Blessed One.

Then the Blessed One, together with the Venerable Ānanda, went to the Gabled Hall in the Great Forest. Having gone there, he addressed the Venerable Ānanda: “Go, Ānanda, gather in the hall of audience all the monks who dwell in dependence on Vaiśālī.” “So be it, Lord,” the Venerable Ānanda replied to the Blessed One. Having gathered all the monks who dwelt in dependence on Vaiśālī in the hall of audience, he went to the Blessed One, respectfully greeted him, and stood to one side. Standing to one side, the Venerable Ānanda said to the Blessed One, “The *bhikkhu-saṃgha* is assembled, Lord. May the Blessed One do what he thinks it is now time to do.”
<p n="183" rend="bodytext"><hi rend="paranum">183</hi><hi rend="dot">.</hi><hi rend="bold">Piyehi manāpehī</hi>ti mātāpitābhātābhaginiādikehi jātiyā <hi rend="bold">nānābhāvo,</hi> maraṇena <hi rend="bold">vinābhāvo,</hi> bhavena <hi rend="bold">aññathābhāvo. Taṃ kutettha labbhā</hi>ti <hi rend="bold">ta</hi>nti tasmā, yasmā sabbeheva piyehi manāpehi nānābhāvo, tasmā dasa pāramiyo pūretvāpi, sambodhiṃ patvāpi, dhammacakkaṃ pavattetvāpi, yamakapāṭihāriyaṃ dassetvāpi, devorohaṇaṃ katvāpi, yaṃ taṃ jātaṃ bhūtaṃ saṅkhataṃ palokadhammaṃ, taṃ vata tathāgatassāpi sarīraṃ mā palujjīti netaṃ ṭhānaṃ vijjati, rodantenāpi kandantenāpi na sakkā taṃ kāraṇaṃ laddhunti. <hi rend="bold">Puna paccāvamissatī</hi>ti yaṃ cattaṃ vantaṃ, taṃ vata puna paṭikhādissatīti attho.</p>
"piyehi manāpehī" means "variousness" due to kinship with mother, father, brother, sister, and so on, "separation" due to death, "otherness" due to existence.

"taṃ kutettha labbhā" means "ta"nti tasmā, yasmā sabbeheva piyehi manāpehi nānābhāvo, tasmā dasa pāramiyo pūretvāpi, sambodhiṃ patvāpi, dhammacakkaṃ pavattetvāpi, yamakapāṭihāriyaṃ dassetvāpi, devorohaṇaṃ katvāpi, yaṃ taṃ jātaṃ bhūtaṃ saṅkhataṃ palokadhammaṃ, taṃ vata tathāgatassāpi sarīraṃ mā palujjīti netaṃ ṭhānaṃ vijjati, rodantenāpi kandantenāpi na sakkā taṃ kāraṇaṃ laddhunti.

"puna paccāvamissatī" means the meaning is that which is given up and vomited, it will be eaten again.
184
<p n="184" rend="bodytext"><hi rend="paranum">184</hi><hi rend="dot">.</hi> Atha kho bhagavā yenupaṭṭhānasālā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā paññatte āsane nisīdi. Nisajja kho bhagavā bhikkhū āmantesi – ‘‘tasmātiha, bhikkhave, ye te mayā dhammā abhiññā desitā, te vo sādhukaṃ uggahetvā āsevitabbā bhāvetabbā bahulīkātabbā, yathayidaṃ brahmacariyaṃ addhaniyaṃ assa ciraṭṭhitikaṃ, tadassa bahujanahitāya bahujanasukhāya lokānukampāya atthāya hitāya sukhāya devamanussānaṃ. Katame ca te, bhikkhave, dhammā mayā abhiññā desitā, ye vo sādhukaṃ uggahetvā āsevitabbā bhāvetabbā bahulīkātabbā, yathayidaṃ brahmacariyaṃ <pb ed="P" n="2.0120"/> addhaniyaṃ assa ciraṭṭhitikaṃ, tadassa bahujanahitāya bahujanasukhāya lokānukampāya atthāya hitāya sukhāya <pb ed="T" n="2.0141"/> devamanussānaṃ. Seyyathidaṃ – cattāro satipaṭṭhānā cattāro sammappadhānā cattāro iddhipādā pañcindriyāni pañca balāni satta bojjhaṅgā ariyo aṭṭhaṅgiko maggo. Ime kho te, bhikkhave, dhammā mayā abhiññā desitā, ye vo sādhukaṃ uggahetvā āsevitabbā bhāvetabbā bahulīkātabbā, yathayidaṃ brahmacariyaṃ addhaniyaṃ assa ciraṭṭhitikaṃ, tadassa bahujanahitāya bahujanasukhāya lokānukampāya atthāya hitāya sukhāya devamanussāna’’nti.</p>
184. Then the Blessed One went to the assembly hall, and upon arriving, sat down on the prepared seat.

Having sat down, the Blessed One addressed the monks: “Therefore, monks, those things ( *dhammā*) that I have taught, having directly known (*abhiññā*), you should thoroughly learn, cultivate, develop, and frequently practice, so that this holy life (*brahmacariyaṃ*) may long endure and remain steadfast for the benefit (*atthāya*), welfare (*hitāya*), and happiness (*sukhāya*) of the multitude, out of compassion (*lokānukampāya*) for the world, for the benefit, welfare, and happiness of gods and men (*devamanussānaṃ*).

“And what, monks, are those things (*dhammā*) that I have taught, having directly known (*abhiññā*) , that you should thoroughly learn, cultivate, develop, and frequently practice, so that this holy life (*brahmacariyaṃ*) may long endure and remain steadfast for the benefit, welfare, and happiness of the multitude, out of compassion for the world, for the benefit, welfare, and happiness of gods and men (*devamanussānaṃ*)?

They are: the four foundations of mindfulness (*cattāro satipaṭṭhānā*), the four right efforts (*cattāro sammappadhānā*), the four bases of power (*cattāro iddhipādā*), the five faculties (*pañcindriyāni*), the five strengths (*pañca balāni*), the seven factors of awakening (*satta bojjhaṅgā*), the noble eightfold path (*ariyo aṭṭhaṅgiko maggo*).

“These, monks, are the things (*dhammā*) that I have taught, having directly known (*abhiññā*), that you should thoroughly learn, cultivate, develop, and frequently practice, so that this holy life (*brahmacariyaṃ*) may long endure and remain steadfast for the benefit, welfare, and happiness of the multitude, out of compassion for the world, for the benefit, welfare, and happiness of gods and men (*devamanussānaṃ*.”
<p n="184" rend="bodytext"><hi rend="paranum">184</hi><hi rend="dot">.</hi><hi rend="bold">Yathayidaṃ brahmacariya</hi>nti yathā idaṃ sikkhāttayasaṅgahaṃ sāsanabrahmacariyaṃ. <hi rend="bold">Addhaniya</hi>nti addhānakkhamaṃ. <hi rend="bold">Ciraṭṭhitika</hi>nti cirappavattivasena ciraṭṭhitikaṃ. <hi rend="bold">Cattāro satipaṭṭhānā</hi>tiādi sabbaṃ lokiyalokuttaravaseneva kathitaṃ. Etesaṃ pana bodhipakkhiyānaṃ dhammānaṃ vinicchayo sabbākārena visuddhimagge paṭipadāñāṇadassanavisuddhiniddese vutto. Sesamettha uttānamevāti.</p> <p rend="centre">Tatiyabhāṇavāravaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.</p> <p rend="subhead">Nāgāpalokitavaṇṇanā</p>
[API Error: 502]
185
<p n="185" rend="bodytext"><hi rend="paranum">185</hi><hi rend="dot">.</hi> Atha kho bhagavā bhikkhū āmantesi – ‘‘handadāni, bhikkhave, āmantayāmi vo, vayadhammā saṅkhārā, appamādena sampādetha. Naciraṃ tathāgatassa <pb ed="M" n="2.0101"/> parinibbānaṃ bhavissati. Ito tiṇṇaṃ māsānaṃ accayena tathāgato parinibbāyissatī’’ti. Idamavoca bhagavā, idaṃ vatvāna sugato athāparaṃ etadavoca satthā <note>ito paraṃ syāmapotthake evaṃpi pāṭho dissati –§daharāpi ca ye vuddhā, ye bālā ye ca paṇḍitā.§aḍḍhāceva daliddā ca, sabbe maccuparāyanā.§yathāpi kumbhakārassa, kataṃ mattikabhājanaṃ.§khuddakañca mahantañca, yañca pakkaṃ yañca āmakaṃ.§sabbaṃ bhedapariyantaṃ, evaṃ maccāna jīvitaṃ.§athāparaṃ etadavoca satthā</note>. –</p> <p rend="gatha1">‘‘Paripakko <pb ed="T" n="2.0142"/> vayo mayhaṃ, parittaṃ mama jīvitaṃ;</p> <pb ed="T" n="2.0142"/> <p rend="gathalast">Pahāya vo gamissāmi, kataṃ me saraṇamattano.</p> <p rend="gatha1">‘‘Appamattā satīmanto, susīlā hotha bhikkhavo;</p> <p rend="gathalast">Susamāhitasaṅkappā, sacittamanurakkhatha.</p> <p rend="gatha1">‘‘Yo <pb ed="V" n="2.0093"/><pb ed="P" n="2.0121"/> imasmiṃ dhammavinaye, appamatto vihassati;</p> <pb ed="V" n="2.0093"/> <pb ed="P" n="2.0121"/> <p rend="gathalast">Pahāya jātisaṃsāraṃ, dukkhassantaṃ karissatī’’ti <note>viharissati (syā.), vihessati (sī.)</note>.</p> <note>viharissati (syā.), vihessati (sī.)</note> <p rend="centre">Tatiyo bhāṇavāro.</p> <p rend="subhead">Nāgāpalokitaṃ</p>
185. Then the Blessed One addressed the monks: "Now, then, monks, I exhort you: All conditioned things are subject to decay. Strive with earnestness.

It will not be long until the Tathāgata’s *parinirvāṇa*.

In three months' time from now, the Tathāgata will attain *parinirvāṇa*."

The Blessed One said this. Having said this, the Well-Gone One, the Teacher, further said this:

[Note: "Even the young and the old, the foolish and the wise. Rich and poor alike, all are subject to death. Just as a potter makes earthen vessels, whether small or large, baked or unbaked, all are subject to breakage. Further, the Teacher said this:"]

My years are now ripe; little of my life remains.

I will leave you, having made myself my refuge.

Monks, be diligent, mindful, and virtuous.

Be of concentrated resolve, protect your own minds.

Whoever in this *dharma-vinaya* lives diligently,

having abandoned the cycle of birth, will make an end of suffering."

Third recitation section.

Nāgāpalokitaṃ.
186
<p n="186" rend="bodytext"><hi rend="paranum">186</hi><hi rend="dot">.</hi> Atha <pb ed="P" n="2.0122"/> kho bhagavā pubbaṇhasamayaṃ nivāsetvā pattacīvaramādāya vesāliṃ piṇḍāya pāvisi. Vesāliyaṃ piṇḍāya caritvā pacchābhattaṃ piṇḍapātappaṭikkanto nāgāpalokitaṃ vesāliṃ apaloketvā āyasmantaṃ ānandaṃ āmantesi – ‘‘idaṃ pacchimakaṃ, ānanda, tathāgatassa vesāliyā dassanaṃ bhavissati. Āyāmānanda, yena bhaṇḍagāmo <note>bhaṇḍugāmo (ka.)</note> tenupasaṅkamissāmā’’ti. ‘‘Evaṃ, bhante’’ti kho āyasmā ānando bhagavato paccassosi.</p> <p rend="bodytext">Atha <pb ed="M" n="2.0102"/> kho bhagavā mahatā bhikkhusaṅghena saddhiṃ yena bhaṇḍagāmo tadavasari. Tatra sudaṃ bhagavā bhaṇḍagāme viharati. Tatra kho bhagavā bhikkhū āmantesi – ‘‘catunnaṃ, bhikkhave, dhammānaṃ ananubodhā appaṭivedhā evamidaṃ dīghamaddhānaṃ sandhāvitaṃ saṃsaritaṃ mamañceva tumhākañca. Katamesaṃ catunnaṃ? Ariyassa, bhikkhave, sīlassa ananubodhā appaṭivedhā evamidaṃ dīghamaddhānaṃ sandhāvitaṃ saṃsaritaṃ mamaṃ ceva tumhākañca. Ariyassa, bhikkhave, samādhissa ananubodhā appaṭivedhā evamidaṃ dīghamaddhānaṃ sandhāvitaṃ saṃsaritaṃ <pb ed="T" n="2.0143"/> mamaṃ ceva tumhākañca. Ariyāya, bhikkhave, paññāya ananubodhā appaṭivedhā evamidaṃ dīghamaddhānaṃ sandhāvitaṃ saṃsaritaṃ mamaṃ ceva tumhākañca. Ariyāya, bhikkhave, vimuttiyā ananubodhā appaṭivedhā evamidaṃ dīghamaddhānaṃ sandhāvitaṃ saṃsaritaṃ mamaṃ ceva tumhākañca. Tayidaṃ, bhikkhave, ariyaṃ sīlaṃ anubuddhaṃ <pb ed="P" n="2.0123"/> paṭividdhaṃ, ariyo samādhi anubuddho paṭividdho, ariyā paññā anubuddhā paṭividdhā, ariyā vimutti anubuddhā paṭividdhā, ucchinnā bhavataṇhā, khīṇā bhavanetti, natthi dāni punabbhavo’’ti. Idamavoca bhagavā, idaṃ vatvāna sugato athāparaṃ etadavoca satthā –</p> <pb ed="M" n="2.0102"/> <pb ed="T" n="2.0143"/> <pb ed="P" n="2.0123"/> <p rend="gatha1">‘‘Sīlaṃ samādhi paññā ca, vimutti ca anuttarā;</p> <p rend="gathalast">Anubuddhā ime dhammā, gotamena yasassinā.</p> <p rend="gatha1">‘‘Iti <pb ed="V" n="2.0094"/> buddho abhiññāya, dhammamakkhāsi bhikkhunaṃ;</p> <pb ed="V" n="2.0094"/> <p rend="gathalast">Dukkhassantakaro satthā, cakkhumā parinibbuto’’ti.</p> <p rend="bodytext">Tatrāpi sudaṃ bhagavā bhaṇḍagāme viharanto etadeva bahulaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ dhammiṃ kathaṃ karoti – ‘‘iti sīlaṃ, iti samādhi, iti paññā. Sīlaparibhāvito samādhi mahapphalo hoti mahānisaṃso. Samādhiparibhāvitā paññā mahapphalā hoti mahānisaṃsā. Paññāparibhāvitaṃ cittaṃ sammadeva āsavehi vimuccati, seyyathidaṃ – kāmāsavā, bhavāsavā, avijjāsavā’’ti.</p> <p rend="subhead">Catumahāpadesakathā</p>
186. Then, the Blessed One, early in the morning, having dressed, taking his bowl and outer robe, went into Vesālī for alms.

Having gone for alms in Vesālī, after the meal, returning from his alms round, gazing on Vesālī with an elephant’s look, he addressed Ven. Ānanda: “Ānanda, this is the Tathāgata’s last look at Vesālī.

Come, Ānanda, let us go to Bhaṇḍagāma.”

“So be it, O Lord,” the Venerable Ānanda replied to the Blessed One.

Then the Blessed One, together with a large *Saṅgha* of monks, went to Bhaṇḍagāma.

There the Blessed One stayed near Bhaṇḍagāma.

There the Blessed One addressed the monks, saying: “Monks, it is through not realizing, through not penetrating four principles that this long course of birth and death has been passed through and undergone by me as well as by you.

Which four? It is through not realizing, through not penetrating the noble virtue (*ariya sīla*), monks… that this long course of birth and death has been passed through and undergone by me as well as by you.

It is through not realizing, through not penetrating the noble concentration (*ariya samādhi*), monks… that this long course of birth and death has been passed through and undergone by me as well as by you.

It is through not realizing, through not penetrating the noble wisdom (*ariya paññā*), monks… that this long course of birth and death has been passed through and undergone by me as well as by you.

It is through not realizing, through not penetrating the noble emancipation (*ariya vimutti*), monks… that this long course of birth and death has been passed through and undergone by me as well as by you.

But now, monks, the noble virtue has been awakened to and penetrated, the noble concentration has been awakened to and penetrated, the noble wisdom has been awakened to and penetrated, the noble emancipation has been awakened to and penetrated; craving for becoming has been cut off, the guide to becoming is exhausted, and there will be no more rebirth.”

Thus spoke the Blessed One. Having spoken thus, the Fortunate One, the Teacher, then said further:

“Virtue (*sīla*), concentration (*samādhi*), wisdom (*paññā*), and unsurpassed emancipation (*vimutti*);

these *dharmas* have been awakened to by Gotama, the glorious one.”

“Thus the Buddha, having directly known, explained the Dharma to the monks;

the Teacher puts an end to suffering, he who has vision, has attained *parinirvāṇa*.”

There also, the Blessed One, while living in Bhaṇḍagāma, often gave this *Dhamma* talk to the monks: “Such is virtue (*sīla*), such is concentration (*samādhi*), such is wisdom (*paññā*).

Concentration (*samādhi*) nurtured with virtue (*sīla*) is of great fruit, great reward.

Discernment (*paññā*) nurtured with concentration (*samādhi*) is of great fruit, great reward.

The mind nurtured with discernment (*paññā*) is rightly released from the effluents, i. e. , the effluent of sensuality (*kāmāsava*), the effluent of becoming (*bhavāsava*), the effluent of ignorance (*avijjāsava*).”

Discourse on the Four Great Authorities
<p n="186" rend="bodytext"><hi rend="paranum">186</hi><hi rend="dot">.</hi><hi rend="bold">Nāgāpalokita</hi>nti yathā hi mahājanassa aṭṭhīni koṭiyā koṭiṃ āhacca ṭhitāni paccekabuddhānaṃ, aṅkusakalaggāni viya, na evaṃ buddhānaṃ. Buddhānaṃ <pb ed="M" n="2.0155"/> pana saṅkhalikāni viya ekābaddhāni hutvā ṭhitāni, tasmā pacchato apalokanakāle na sakkā hoti gīvaṃ parivattetuṃ. Yathā pana hatthināgo pacchābhāgaṃ apaloketukāmo sakalasarīreneva parivattati, evaṃ parivattitabbaṃ hoti. Bhagavato pana nagaradvāre ṭhatvā – ‘‘vesāliṃ apalokessāmī’’ti citte uppannamatte – ‘‘bhagavā anekāni kappakoṭisahassāni pāramiyo pūrentehi tumhehi na gīvaṃ parivattetvā <pb ed="V" n="2.0139"/> apalokanakammaṃ kata’’nti ayaṃ pathavī kulālacakkaṃ viya parivattetvā bhagavantaṃ <pb ed="P" n="2.0565"/> vesālinagarābhimukhaṃ akāsi. Taṃ sandhāyetaṃ vuttaṃ.</p> <p rend="bodytext">Nanu ca na kevalaṃ vesāliyāva, sāvatthirājagahanāḷandapāṭaligāmakoṭigāmanātikagāmakesupi tato tato nikkhantakāle taṃ taṃ sabbaṃ pacchimadassanameva, tattha tattha kasmā nāgāpalokitaṃ nāpalokesīti? Anacchariyattā. Tattha tattha hi nivattetvā apalokentassetaṃ na acchariyaṃ hoti, tasmā nāpalokesi. Api ca vesālirājāno āsannavināsā, tiṇṇaṃ vassānaṃ upari vinassissanti. Te taṃ nagaradvāre <hi rend="bold">nāgāpalokitaṃ</hi> nāma cetiyaṃ katvā gandhamālādīhi pūjessanti, taṃ nesaṃ dīgharattaṃ hitāya sukhāya bhavissatīti tesaṃ anukampāya apalokesi.</p> <hi rend="bold">nāgāpalokitaṃ</hi> <p rend="bodytext"><hi rend="bold">Dukkhassantakaro</hi>ti vaṭṭadukkhassa antakaro. <hi rend="bold">Cakkhumā</hi>ti pañcahi cakkhūhi cakkhumā. <hi rend="bold">Parinibbuto</hi>ti kilesaparinibbānena parinibbuto.</p> <hi rend="bold">Dukkhassantakaro</hi> <hi rend="bold">Cakkhumā</hi> <hi rend="bold">Parinibbuto</hi> <p rend="subhead">Catumahāpadesavaṇṇanā</p>
<p n="186" rend="bodytext"><hi rend="paranum">186</hi><hi rend="dot">.
</hi><hi rend="bold">Nāgāpalokita</hi>nti: Just as the bones of the great mass of people are positioned having struck against a billion *koṭis* in the case of the solitary buddhas, like the point of a hook, not so in the case of the Buddhas.

But for the Buddhas <pb ed="m" n="2.
0155"/> they are positioned having become joined together like chains. Therefore, at the time of looking back, it is not possible to turn the neck.

Just as, however, an elephant, wishing to look back at the rear part, turns around with its entire body, so it should be turned around.

However, to the Blessed One, standing at the city gate – the thought having arisen in his mind, “I will look at Vaiśālī" – "O Blessed One, by you, who for countless *kappa-koṭi-sahasras* were fulfilling the perfections (*pāramī*) it was not proper to turn the neck before <pb ed="v" n="2.
0139"/> the act of looking back (*apalokanakamma*) was done,” this earth, having turned around the Blessed One like a potter's wheel <pb ed="p" n="2.
0565"/> turned (him) towards Vaiśālī city.

This was said with reference to this.

</p> <p rend="bodytext">But indeed, not only to Vaiśālī, but also in Sāvatthi, Rājagaha, Nāḷanda, Pāṭaligāma, Koṭigāma, and Nātikagāmaka, at the time of departing from here and there, all that was only a rear view. Why did he not look back, with the *nāgāpalokita*, there and there? Because it was not wondrous.

Indeed, there and there, having turned back and looking, that was not wondrous; therefore, he did not look back.

Moreover, the kings of Vaiśālī are near destruction; after three years they will perish.

Having made that caitya named <hi rend="bold">nāgāpalokita</hi> at that city gate, they will honor (it) with perfumes, garlands, and so on. That will be for their long-lasting benefit and happiness. Out of compassion for them, he looked back.
</p> <hi rend="bold">Nāgāpalokitaṃ</hi> <p rend="bodytext"><hi rend="bold">Dukkhassantakaro</hi>ti: (It is) the end-maker of the round of suffering (*vaṭṭadukkha*).

<hi rend="bold">Cakkhumā</hi>ti: (He) has eyes (*cakkhumā*) with the five eyes (*pañcahi cakkhūhi*).

<hi rend="bold">Parinibbuto</hi>ti: (He) is fully extinguished (*parinibbuto*) by the extinction of defilements (*kilesaparinibbāna*).
</p> <hi rend="bold">Dukkhassantakaro</hi> <hi rend="bold">Cakkhumā</hi> <hi rend="bold">Parinibbuto</hi> <p rend="subhead">Explanation of the Four Great Authorities (*catumahāpadesavaṇṇanā*)</p>
187
<p n="187" rend="bodytext"><hi rend="paranum">187</hi><hi rend="dot">.</hi> Atha <pb ed="T" n="2.0144"/> kho bhagavā bhaṇḍagāme yathābhirantaṃ viharitvā āyasmantaṃ ānandaṃ āmantesi – ‘‘āyāmānanda, yena hatthigāmo, yena ambagāmo, yena jambugāmo, yena bhoganagaraṃ tenupasaṅkamissāmā’’ti. ‘‘Evaṃ, bhante’’ti kho āyasmā ānando bhagavato paccassosi. Atha kho <pb ed="M" n="2.0103"/> bhagavā mahatā bhikkhusaṅghena saddhiṃ yena bhoganagaraṃ tadavasari. Tatra sudaṃ bhagavā bhoganagare viharati ānande <note>sānandare (ka.)</note> cetiye. Tatra kho bhagavā bhikkhū āmantesi – ‘‘cattārome, bhikkhave, mahāpadese desessāmi, taṃ suṇātha, sādhukaṃ manasikarotha, bhāsissāmī’’ti. ‘‘Evaṃ <pb ed="P" n="2.0124"/>, bhante’’ti kho te bhikkhū bhagavato paccassosuṃ. Bhagavā etadavoca –</p>
187. Then, the Blessed One, having stayed near Bhaṇḍagāma as long as he pleased, addressed the venerable Ānanda, saying: “Come, Ānanda, let us go to Hatthigāma, to Ambagāma, to Jambugāma, to Bhoganagara.”

“So be it, venerable sir,” the venerable Ānanda replied to the Blessed One.

Then, the Blessed One, together with a large *bhikkhu-saṅgha*, went to Bhoganagara.

There the Blessed One stayed near Bhoganagara at the Ānanda shrine.

There the Blessed One addressed the *bhikkhus*, saying: “O *bhikkhus*, I will teach you the four great standards (*mahāpadesa*). Listen, pay close attention, and I will speak.”

“So be it, venerable sir,” those *bhikkhus* replied to the Blessed One.

The Blessed One said this:
<p n="187" rend="bodytext"><hi rend="paranum">187</hi><hi rend="dot">.</hi><hi rend="bold">Mahāpadese</hi>ti mahāokāse, mahāapadese vā, buddhādayo mahante mahante apadisitvā vuttāni mahākāraṇānīti attho.</p>
"mahāpadese": "mahāokāse", or "mahāapadese"; *buddha*, and so forth, having pointed out the great, great, causes, are declared to be great reasons (mahākāraṇāni), this is the meaning (artha).
188
<p n="188" rend="bodytext"><hi rend="paranum">188</hi><hi rend="dot">.</hi> ‘‘Idha, bhikkhave, bhikkhu evaṃ vadeyya – ‘sammukhā metaṃ, āvuso, bhagavato sutaṃ sammukhā paṭiggahitaṃ, ayaṃ dhammo ayaṃ vinayo idaṃ satthusāsana’nti. Tassa, bhikkhave, bhikkhuno bhāsitaṃ neva abhinanditabbaṃ nappaṭikkositabbaṃ. Anabhinanditvā appaṭikkositvā tāni padabyañjanāni sādhukaṃ uggahetvā sutte osāretabbāni <note>otāretabbāni</note>, vinaye sandassetabbāni. Tāni ce sutte osāriyamānāni <note>otāriyamānāni</note> vinaye sandassiyamānāni na ceva sutte osaranti <note>otaranti (sī. pī. a. ni. 4.180</note>, na ca vinaye sandissanti, niṭṭhamettha gantabbaṃ – ‘addhā, idaṃ na ceva tassa bhagavato vacanaṃ; imassa ca bhikkhuno duggahita’nti. Itihetaṃ, bhikkhave, chaḍḍeyyātha. Tāni ce sutte osāriyamānāni vinaye sandassiyamānāni sutte ceva <pb ed="T" n="2.0145"/> osaranti, vinaye ca sandissanti, niṭṭhamettha gantabbaṃ – ‘addhā, idaṃ tassa bhagavato vacanaṃ; imassa ca bhikkhuno suggahita’nti. Idaṃ, bhikkhave, paṭhamaṃ mahāpadesaṃ dhāreyyātha.</p> <p rend="bodytext">‘‘Idha <pb ed="V" n="2.0095"/> pana, bhikkhave, bhikkhu evaṃ vadeyya – ‘amukasmiṃ nāma āvāse saṅgho viharati sathero sapāmokkho. Tassa me saṅghassa sammukhā sutaṃ sammukhā <pb ed="T" n="2.0146"/> paṭiggahitaṃ, ayaṃ dhammo ayaṃ vinayo idaṃ satthusāsana’nti. Tassa, bhikkhave, bhikkhuno bhāsitaṃ neva abhinanditabbaṃ nappaṭikkositabbaṃ. Anabhinanditvā appaṭikkositvā tāni padabyañjanāni sādhukaṃ uggahetvā sutte osāretabbāni, vinaye sandassetabbāni. Tāni ce sutte osāriyamānāni vinaye sandassiyamānāni na ceva sutte osaranti, na ca vinaye sandissanti, niṭṭhamettha gantabbaṃ – ‘addhā, idaṃ na ceva tassa bhagavato vacanaṃ; tassa ca saṅghassa duggahita’nti. Itihetaṃ, bhikkhave, chaḍḍeyyātha. Tāni ce sutte osāriyamānāni vinaye sandassiyamānāni sutte ceva <pb ed="M" n="2.0104"/> osaranti vinaye ca sandissanti, niṭṭhamettha gantabbaṃ – ‘addhā <pb ed="P" n="2.0125"/>, idaṃ tassa bhagavato vacanaṃ; tassa ca saṅghassa suggahita’nti. Idaṃ, bhikkhave, dutiyaṃ mahāpadesaṃ dhāreyyātha.</p> <pb ed="V" n="2.0095"/> <pb ed="T" n="2.0146"/> <pb ed="M" n="2.0104"/> <pb ed="P" n="2.0125"/> <p rend="bodytext">‘‘Idha pana, bhikkhave, bhikkhu evaṃ vadeyya – ‘amukasmiṃ nāma āvāse sambahulā therā bhikkhū viharanti bahussutā āgatāgamā dhammadharā vinayadharā mātikādharā. Tesaṃ me therānaṃ sammukhā sutaṃ sammukhā paṭiggahitaṃ – ayaṃ dhammo ayaṃ vinayo idaṃ satthusāsana’nti. Tassa, bhikkhave, bhikkhuno bhāsitaṃ neva abhinanditabbaṃ…pe… na ca vinaye sandissanti, niṭṭhamettha gantabbaṃ – ‘addhā, idaṃ na ceva tassa bhagavato vacanaṃ; tesañca therānaṃ duggahita’nti. Itihetaṃ, bhikkhave, chaḍḍeyyātha. Tāni ce sutte osāriyamānāni…pe… vinaye ca sandissanti, niṭṭhamettha gantabbaṃ – ‘addhā, idaṃ tassa bhagavato vacanaṃ; tesañca therānaṃ suggahita’nti. Idaṃ, bhikkhave, tatiyaṃ mahāpadesaṃ dhāreyyātha.</p> <p rend="bodytext">‘‘Idha pana, bhikkhave, bhikkhu evaṃ vadeyya – ‘amukasmiṃ nāma āvāse eko thero bhikkhu viharati bahussuto āgatāgamo dhammadharo vinayadharo mātikādharo. Tassa me therassa sammukhā sutaṃ sammukhā paṭiggahitaṃ – ayaṃ dhammo ayaṃ vinayo idaṃ satthusāsana’nti. Tassa, bhikkhave, bhikkhuno bhāsitaṃ neva abhinanditabbaṃ nappaṭikkositabbaṃ. Anabhinanditvā appaṭikkositvā tāni padabyañjanāni sādhukaṃ uggahetvā sutte osāritabbāni, vinaye sandassetabbāni. Tāni ce sutte osāriyamānāni vinaye sandassiyamānāni na ceva sutte osaranti, na ca vinaye sandissanti, niṭṭhamettha gantabbaṃ – ‘addhā, idaṃ na ceva tassa bhagavato vacanaṃ; tassa ca therassa duggahita’nti. Itihetaṃ, bhikkhave, chaḍḍeyyātha. Tāni ca sutte osāriyamānāni vinaye sandassiyamānāni sutte ceva osaranti, vinaye ca sandissanti <pb ed="V" n="2.0096"/>, niṭṭhamettha gantabbaṃ – ‘addhā <pb ed="P" n="2.0126"/>, idaṃ tassa bhagavato vacanaṃ; tassa ca therassa suggahita’nti. Idaṃ, bhikkhave, catutthaṃ mahāpadesaṃ dhāreyyātha. Ime kho, bhikkhave, cattāro mahāpadese dhāreyyāthā’’ti.</p> <pb ed="V" n="2.0096"/> <pb ed="P" n="2.0126"/> <p rend="bodytext">Tatrapi sudaṃ bhagavā bhoganagare viharanto <pb ed="T" n="2.0147"/> ānande cetiye etadeva bahulaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ dhammiṃ kathaṃ karoti – ‘‘iti sīlaṃ, iti samādhi, iti paññā. Sīlaparibhāvito samādhi mahapphalo hoti mahānisaṃso <pb ed="M" n="2.0105"/>. Samādhiparibhāvitā paññā mahapphalā hoti mahānisaṃsā. Paññāparibhāvitaṃ cittaṃ sammadeva āsavehi vimuccati, seyyathidaṃ – kāmāsavā, bhavāsavā, avijjāsavā’’ti.</p> <pb ed="T" n="2.0147"/> <pb ed="M" n="2.0105"/> <p rend="subhead">Kammāraputtacundavatthu</p>
188. Monks, a monk might say thus: ‘Face to face with the Blessed One, friend, I have heard and learned thus: This is the *Dhamma* (law, teaching), this is the *Vinaya* (the monastic discipline), this is the Teacher’s instruction.’

Monks, that monk’s speech should neither be approved nor disapproved.

Without approval or disapproval, carefully studying those words and expressions, one should compare them with the *Sūtras* (discourses) and examine them against the *Vinaya*.

If, upon being compared with the *Sūtras* and examined against the *Vinaya*, they do not conform to the *Sūtras* (see Sī.
Pī.
A.
Ni.
4.
180), and do not accord with the *Vinaya*, then you should conclude: ‘Indeed, this is not the word of the Blessed One; this monk has misunderstood it.’

Monks, you should reject it in this way.

But if, upon being compared with the *Sūtras* and examined against the *Vinaya*, they conform to the *Sūtras*, and accord with the *Vinaya*, then you should conclude: ‘Indeed, this is the word of the Blessed One; this monk has understood it rightly.’

This, monks, is the first Great Reference you should bear in mind.

Furthermore, monks, a monk might say thus: ‘In an abode of such and such a name lives a *Saṅgha* (community) with elders and a chief.

Face to face with that *Saṅgha* (community), I have heard and learned thus: This is the *Dhamma*, this is the *Vinaya*, this is the Teacher’s instruction.’

Monks, that monk’s speech should neither be approved nor disapproved.

Without approval or disapproval, carefully studying those words and expressions, one should compare them with the *Sūtras* and examine them against the *Vinaya*.

If, upon being compared with the *Sūtras* and examined against the *Vinaya*, they do not conform to the *Sūtras*, and do not accord with the *Vinaya*, then you should conclude: ‘Indeed, this is not the word of the Blessed One; that *Saṅgha* (community) has misunderstood it.’

Monks, you should reject it in this way.

But if, upon being compared with the *Sūtras* and examined against the *Vinaya*, they conform to the *Sūtras*, and accord with the *Vinaya*, then you should conclude: ‘Indeed, this is the word of the Blessed One; that *Saṅgha* (community) has understood it rightly.’

This, monks, is the second Great Reference you should bear in mind.

Furthermore, monks, a monk might say thus: ‘In an abode of such and such a name live many elder monks who are learned, who have mastered the traditions, who are upholders of the *Dhamma*, upholders of the *Vinaya*, upholders of the *Mātikā* (the outlines of the *Dhamma*) .

Face to face with those elders, I have heard and learned thus: This is the *Dhamma*, this is the *Vinaya*, this is the Teacher’s instruction.’

Monks, that monk’s speech should neither be approved nor disapproved… and do not accord with the *Vinaya*, then you should conclude: ‘Indeed, this is not the word of the Blessed One; those elders have misunderstood it.’

Monks, you should reject it in this way.

But if, upon being compared with the *Sūtras*…and accord with the *Vinaya*, then you should conclude: ‘Indeed, this is the word of the Blessed One; those elders have understood it rightly.’

This, monks, is the third Great Reference you should bear in mind.

Furthermore, monks, a monk might say thus: ‘In an abode of such and such a name lives a single elder monk who is learned, who has mastered the traditions, who is an upholder of the *Dhamma*, an upholder of the *Vinaya*, an upholder of the *Mātikā*.

Face to face with that elder, I have heard and learned thus: This is the *Dhamma*, this is the *Vinaya*, this is the Teacher’s instruction.’

Monks, that monk’s speech should neither be approved nor disapproved.

Without approval or disapproval, carefully studying those words and expressions, one should compare them with the *Sūtras* and examine them against the *Vinaya*.
If, when these are compared to the *suttas* (discourses) and verified by the *vinaya* (the monastic discipline), they do not align with the *suttas*, nor are they in accordance with the *vinaya*, then one should conclude: 'Indeed, this is not the word of the Blessed One (tassa bhagavato vacanaṃ); this *thera* (elder monk) has misunderstood it.'
In that way, *bhikkhus* (monks), you should reject it.
But if, when these are compared to the *suttas* and verified by the *vinaya*, they do align with the *suttas* and are in accordance with the *vinaya*, then one should conclude: 'Indeed, this is the word of the Blessed One; this *thera* has understood it rightly.'
This, *bhikkhus*, is the fourth great reference (mahāpadesaṃ) you should bear in mind.
"These, *bhikkhus*, are the four great references you should bear in mind."
There also the Blessed One, while dwelling near Bhoganagara at the Ānanda Shrine, frequently gave this Dhamma talk to the monks: "Such is virtue (*sīlaṃ*), such is concentration (*samādhi*), such is wisdom (*paññā*)."
Concentration (*samādhi*) developed with virtue (*sīla-paribhāvito*) is of great fruit (mahapphalo) and great benefit (mahānisaṃso).
Wisdom (*paññā*) developed with concentration (*samādhi-paribhāvitā*) is of great fruit and great benefit.
The mind (cittaṃ) developed with wisdom is utterly freed from the *āsavas* (influxes or taints), that is, the *kāmāsava* (influx of sensuality), the *bhavāsava* (influx of becoming), and the *avijjāsava* (influx of ignorance)."

The story of Cunda, the son of the smith.
<p n="188" rend="bodytext"><hi rend="paranum">188</hi><hi rend="dot">.</hi><hi rend="bold">Neva abhinanditabba</hi>nti haṭṭhatuṭṭhehi sādhukāraṃ datvā pubbeva na sotabbaṃ, evaṃ kate hi pacchā ‘‘idaṃ na sametī’’ti vuccamāno – ‘‘kiṃ pubbeva ayaṃ dhammo, idāni na dhammo’’ti vatvā laddhiṃ na vissajjeti. <hi rend="bold">Nappaṭikkositabba</hi>nti – ‘‘kiṃ esa bālo vadatī’’ti evaṃ pubbeva na vattabbaṃ, evaṃ vutte hi vattuṃ yuttampi na vakkhati. Tenāha – ‘‘anabhinanditvā appaṭikkositvā’’ti. <hi rend="bold">Padabyañjanānī</hi>ti padasaṅkhātāni byañjanāni. <hi rend="bold">Sādhukaṃ uggahetvā</hi>ti imasmiṃ <pb ed="M" n="2.0156"/> ṭhāne pāḷi vuttā, imasmiṃ ṭhāne attho vutto, imasmiṃ ṭhāne anusandhi kathito, imasmiṃ ṭhāne pubbāparaṃ kathitanti suṭṭhu gahetvā. <hi rend="bold">Sutte osāretabbānī</hi>ti sutte otāretabbāni. <hi rend="bold">Vinaye sandassetabbānī</hi>ti vinaye saṃsandetabbāni.</p> <p rend="bodytext">Ettha ca <hi rend="bold">sutta</hi>nti vinayo. Yathāha – ‘‘kattha paṭikkhittaṃ? Sāvatthiyaṃ suttavibhaṅge’’ti (cuḷava. 457). <hi rend="bold">Vinayo</hi>ti khandhako. Yathāha – ‘‘vinayātisāre’’ti. Evaṃ vinayapiṭakampi na <pb ed="V" n="2.0140"/> pariyādiyati. Ubhatovibhaṅgā pana suttaṃ, khandhakaparivārā vinayoti evaṃ vinayapiṭakaṃ pariyādiyati. Athavā suttantapiṭakaṃ suttaṃ, vinayapiṭakaṃ vinayoti evaṃ dveyeva piṭakāni pariyādiyanti. Suttantābhidhammapiṭakāni <pb ed="P" n="2.0566"/> vā suttaṃ, vinayapiṭakaṃ vinayoti evampi tīṇi piṭakāni na tāva pariyādiyanti. Asuttanāmakañhi buddhavacanaṃ nāma atthi. Seyyathidaṃ – jātakaṃ, paṭisambhidā, niddeso, suttanipāto, dhammapadaṃ, udānaṃ, itivuttakaṃ, vimānavatthu, petavatthu, theragāthā, therīgāthā, apadānanti.</p> <hi rend="bold">sutta</hi> <hi rend="bold">Vinayo</hi> <pb ed="V" n="2.0140"/> <pb ed="P" n="2.0566"/> <p rend="bodytext">Sudinnatthero pana – ‘‘asuttanāmakaṃ buddhavacanaṃ na atthī’’ti taṃ sabbaṃ paṭipakkhipitvā – ‘‘tīṇi piṭakāni suttaṃ, vinayo pana kāraṇa’’nti āha. Tato taṃ kāraṇaṃ dassento idaṃ suttamāhari –</p> <p rend="indent">‘‘Ye kho tvaṃ, gotami, dhamme jāneyyāsi, ime dhammā sarāgāya saṃvattanti no virāgāya, saññogāya saṃvattanti no visaññogāya, ācayāya saṃvattanti no apacayāya, mahicchatāya saṃvattanti no appicchatāya, asantuṭṭhiyā saṃvattanti no santuṭṭhiyā, saṅgaṇikāya saṃvattanti no pavivekāya, kosajjāya saṃvattanti no vīriyārambhāya, dubbharatāya saṃvattanti no subharatāya. Ekaṃsena, gotami, dhāreyyāsi – ‘neso dhammo, neso vinayo, netaṃ satthusāsana’nti. Ye ca kho tvaṃ, gotami, dhamme jāneyyāsi, ime dhammā virāgāya saṃvattanti no sarāgāya, visaññogāya saṃvattanti no saññogāya, apacayāya saṃvattanti no ācayāya, appicchatāya saṃvattanti no mahicchatāya, santuṭṭhiyā saṃvattanti no asantuṭṭhiyā, pavivekāya saṃvattanti no saṅgaṇikāya <pb ed="M" n="2.0157"/>, vīriyārambhāya saṃvattanti no kosajjāya, subharatāya saṃvattanti no dubbharatāya. Ekaṃsena, gotami, dhāreyyāsi – ‘eso dhammo, eso vinayo, etaṃ satthusāsana’nti’’ (a. ni. 8.53).</p> <pb ed="M" n="2.0157"/> <p rend="bodytext">Tasmā <hi rend="bold">sutte</hi>ti tepiṭake buddhavacane otāretabbāni. <hi rend="bold">Vinaye</hi>ti etasmiṃ rāgādivinayakāraṇe saṃsandetabbānīti ayamettha attho. <hi rend="bold">Na ceva sutte osarantī</hi>ti suttapaṭipāṭiyā katthaci anāgantvā challiṃ uṭṭhapetvā guḷhavessantara-guḷhaummagga-guḷhavinaya-vedallapiṭakānaṃ aññatarato āgatāni paññāyantīti attho. Evaṃ āgatāni hi rāgādivinaye ca na paññāyamānāni chaḍḍetabbāni honti. Tena vuttaṃ – ‘‘iti hetaṃ, bhikkhave, chaḍḍeyyāthā’’ti. Etenupāyena sabbattha attho veditabbo.</p> <hi rend="bold">sutte</hi> <hi rend="bold">Vinaye</hi> <hi rend="bold">Na ceva sutte osarantī</hi> <p rend="bodytext"><hi rend="bold">Idaṃ</hi><pb ed="V" n="2.0141"/>, <hi rend="bold">bhikkhave, catutthaṃ mahāpadesaṃ dhāreyyāthā</hi>ti idaṃ <pb ed="P" n="2.0567"/> catutthaṃ dhammassa patiṭṭhānokāsaṃ dhāreyyātha.</p> <hi rend="bold">Idaṃ</hi> <pb ed="V" n="2.0141"/> <hi rend="bold">bhikkhave, catutthaṃ mahāpadesaṃ dhāreyyāthā</hi> <pb ed="P" n="2.0567"/> <p rend="bodytext">Imasmiṃ pana ṭhāne imaṃ pakiṇṇakaṃ veditabbaṃ. Sutte cattāro mahāpadesā, khandhake cattāro mahāpadesā, cattāri pañhabyākaraṇāni, suttaṃ, suttānulomaṃ, ācariyavādo, attanomati, tisso saṅgītiyoti.</p> <p rend="bodytext">Tattha – ‘‘ayaṃ dhammo, ayaṃ vinayo’’ti dhammavinicchaye patte ime cattāro mahāpadesā pamāṇaṃ. Yaṃ ettha sameti tadeva gahetabbaṃ, itaraṃ viravantassapi na gahetabbaṃ.</p> <p rend="bodytext">‘‘Idaṃ kappati, idaṃ na kappatī’’ti kappiyākappiyavinicchaye patte – ‘‘yaṃ, bhikkhave, mayā idaṃ na kappatīti appaṭikkhittaṃ, taṃ ce akappiyaṃ anulometi, kappiyaṃ paṭibāhati, taṃ vo na kappatī’’tiādinā (mahāva. 305) nayena khandhake vuttā cattāro mahāpadesā pamāṇaṃ. Tesaṃ vinicchayakathā <hi rend="bold">samantapāsādikāyaṃ</hi> vuttā. Tattha vuttanayena yaṃ kappiyaṃ anulometi, tadeva kappiyaṃ, itaraṃ akappiyanti evaṃ sanniṭṭhānaṃ kātabbaṃ.</p> <hi rend="bold">samantapāsādikāyaṃ</hi> <p rend="bodytext">Ekaṃsabyākaraṇīyo pañho, vibhajjabyākaraṇīyo pañho, paṭipucchābyākaraṇīyo pañho, ṭhapanīyo pañhoti imāni <hi rend="bold">cattāri pañhabyākaraṇāni</hi> nāma. Tattha ‘‘cakkhuṃ anicca’’nti puṭṭhena – ‘‘āma anicca’’nti ekaṃseneva byākātabbaṃ <pb ed="M" n="2.0158"/>. Esa nayo sotādīsu. Ayaṃ <hi rend="bold">ekaṃsabyākaraṇīyo</hi> pañho. ‘‘Aniccaṃ nāma cakkhu’’nti puṭṭhena – ‘‘na cakkhumeva, sotampi aniccaṃ ghānampi anicca’’nti evaṃ vibhajitvā byākātabbaṃ. Ayaṃ <hi rend="bold">vibhajjabyākaraṇīyo</hi> pañho. ‘‘Yathā cakkhu tathā sotaṃ, yathā sotaṃ tathā cakkhu’’nti puṭṭhena ‘‘kenaṭṭhena pucchasī’’ti paṭipucchitvā ‘‘dassanaṭṭhena pucchāmī’’ti vutte ‘‘na hī’’ti byākātabbaṃ, ‘‘aniccaṭṭhena pucchāmī’’ti vutte āmāti byākātabbaṃ. Ayaṃ <hi rend="bold">paṭipucchābyākaraṇīyo</hi> pañho. ‘‘Taṃ jīvaṃ taṃ sarīra’’ntiādīni puṭṭhena pana ‘‘abyākatametaṃ bhagavatā’’ti ṭhapetabbo, esa pañho na byākātabbo. Ayaṃ <hi rend="bold">ṭhapanīyo</hi> pañho. Iti tenākārena pañhe sampatte imāni cattāri pañhabyākaraṇāni pamāṇaṃ. Imesaṃ vasena so pañho byākātabbo.</p> <hi rend="bold">cattāri pañhabyākaraṇāni</hi> <pb ed="M" n="2.0158"/> <hi rend="bold">ekaṃsabyākaraṇīyo</hi> <hi rend="bold">vibhajjabyākaraṇīyo</hi> <hi rend="bold">paṭipucchābyākaraṇīyo</hi> <hi rend="bold">ṭhapanīyo</hi> <p rend="bodytext">Suttādīsu pana <hi rend="bold">suttaṃ</hi> nāma tisso saṅgītiyo ārūḷhāni tīṇi piṭakāni. <hi rend="bold">Suttānulomaṃ</hi> nāma anulomakappiyaṃ. <hi rend="bold">Ācariyavādo</hi> nāma aṭṭhakathā. <hi rend="bold">Attanomati</hi> nāma nayaggāhena <pb ed="V" n="2.0142"/> anubuddhiyā attano paṭibhānaṃ. Tattha suttaṃ appaṭibāhiyaṃ, taṃ paṭibāhantena buddhova paṭibāhito hoti. Anulomakappiyaṃ <pb ed="P" n="2.0568"/> pana suttena samentameva gahetabbaṃ, na itaraṃ. Ācariyavādopi suttena samentoyeva gahetabbo, na itaro. Attanomati pana sabbadubbalā, sāpi suttena samentāyeva gahetabbā, na itarā. Pañcasatikā, sattasatikā, sahassikāti imā pana <hi rend="bold">tisso saṅgītiyo.</hi> Suttampi tāsu āgatameva pamāṇaṃ, itaraṃ gārayhasuttaṃ na gahetabbaṃ. Tattha otarantānipi hi padabyañjanāni na ceva sutte otaranti, na ca vinaye sandissantīti veditabbāni.</p> <hi rend="bold">suttaṃ</hi> <hi rend="bold">Suttānulomaṃ</hi> <hi rend="bold">Ācariyavādo</hi> <hi rend="bold">Attanomati</hi> <pb ed="V" n="2.0142"/> <pb ed="P" n="2.0568"/> <hi rend="bold">tisso saṅgītiyo.</hi> <p rend="subhead">Kammāraputtacundavatthuvaṇṇanā</p>
188.
"'Should not be welcomed' means: One should not give applause with joyful and delighted [hearts], giving approval beforehand, saying, 'Excellent!' For if one does so, and later one is told, 'This does not fit,' if he says, 'Why, was this the Dharma before, and is it not the Dharma now?', he will not give up his view.
