"'Should not be rejected' means: One should not say beforehand, 'What is this fool saying?' For if one speaks thus, he will not speak even if it is fitting to speak.

Therefore, it was said: "'Without welcoming, without rejecting.'"

"'Words and consonants' means: the consonants which are reckoned as words.

"'Having thoroughly grasped' means: Having thoroughly grasped, 'In this place the *pāḷi* is spoken, in this place the meaning is spoken, in this place the connection is spoken, in this place what comes before and what comes after is spoken.'

"'Should be tested against the Sūtras' means: They should be tested [by comparing them] with the Sūtras.

"'Should be compared with the Vinaya' means: They should be collated with the Vinaya.

Herein, *sutta* is the Vinaya. As it is said: “Where has it been rejected? In Sāvatthī, in the Sutta-vibhaṅga” (Cuḷava. 457).

*Vinaya* is the Khandhaka. As it is said: “In transgression of the Vinaya.”

Thus, the Vinaya-piṭaka is not completely mastered.

However, the Ubhatovibhaṅga is the Sūtra, the Khandhaka-parivāra is the Vinaya. Thus, the Vinaya-piṭaka is completely mastered.

Alternatively, the Suttanta-piṭaka is the Sūtra, the Vinaya-piṭaka is the Vinaya. Thus, these two Piṭakas are completely mastered.

Or else, the Suttanta-abhidhamma-piṭakas are the Sūtra, the Vinaya-piṭaka is the Vinaya. Even so, the three Piṭakas are not entirely mastered.

For there is no word of the Buddha called "not-Sūtra."

That is to say: the Jātaka, the Paṭisambhidā, the Niddesa, the Sutta-nipāta, the Dhammapada, the Udāna, the Itivuttaka, the Vimānavatthu, the Petavatthu, the Theragāthā, the Therīgāthā, and the Apadāna.

Sūtra and Vinaya

Sudinnatthero, however, having rejected all of that, saying, “There is no word of the Buddha called 'not-Sūtra,'” said: “The three Piṭakas are the Sūtra, but the Vinaya is the cause."

Then, showing that reason, he recited this Sūtra:

“Whatever states you, Gotamī, may know: 'These states lead to passion, not to dispassion; to bondage, not to freedom from bondage; to increase, not to decrease; to great desires, not to fewness of wishes; to discontent, not to contentment; to sociability, not to solitude; to laziness, not to putting forth energy; to difficulty in being supported, not to ease in being supported.'

You should definitely know, Gotamī: 'This is not the Dharma, this is not the Vinaya, this is not the Teacher’s instruction.'

And whatever states you, Gotamī, may know: 'These states lead to dispassion, not to passion; to freedom from bondage, not to bondage; to decrease, not to increase; to fewness of wishes, not to great desires; to contentment, not to discontent; to solitude, not to sociability, to putting forth energy, not to laziness; to ease in being supported, not to difficulty in being supported.'

You should definitely know, Gotamī: 'This is the Dharma, this is the Vinaya, this is the Teacher’s instruction'” (A. Ni. 8.53).

Therefore, "'Should be tested against the Sūtras' means: They should be tested against the Buddha-word in those three Piṭakas.

"'Vinaya' means: They should be collated with this cause of Vinaya, [which is] aversion to passion, etc." This is the meaning here.

"'And should not be practiced in the Sūtras' means: Without appearing anywhere in the order of the Sūtras, having raised a bark [of doctrine], they appear as having come from one of the Guḷhavessantara, Guḷhaummagga, Guḷhavinaya, or Vedallapiṭaka.

For what has come thus, if it is not apparent in the Vinaya concerning aversion to passion, etc., should be discarded.

Therefore, it was said: “Thus, O *bhikkhus*, you should discard it.”

By this means, the meaning should be understood everywhere.
They do not occur in the sūtras or the Vinaya; indeed, they do not appear in the sūtras.

This, monks, is the fourth Great Referral you should bear in mind: this fourth you should bear in mind as the basis and opportunity for the Dhamma.

This, monks, is the fourth Great Referral you should bear in mind.

But in this case, this miscellaneous matter should be understood. In the sūtras, there are four Great Referrals; in the Khandhaka, four Great Referrals; four ways of answering questions; the sūtra, what accords with the sūtra, the teacher's doctrine, one's own opinion, and the three recitations.

Therein, when a decision about the Dhamma is reached—"This is the Dhamma, this is the Vinaya"—these four Great Referrals are the standard. Whatever agrees here should be accepted; the other, even if clamoring, should not be accepted.

When a decision about what is allowable and what is not is reached—"This is allowable, this is not allowable"—the four Great Referrals stated in the Khandhaka according to the method beginning with "Whatever, monks, has not been rejected by me, saying, 'This is not allowable,' if it conforms with what is not allowable, if it goes against what is allowable, that is not allowable for you" are the standard.

The discussion of their decision is stated in the *Samantapāsādikā*. According to the method stated there, whatever conforms with what is allowable is allowable, and the other is not allowable; thus, a conclusion should be made.

In the *Samantapāsādikā*:

A question that should be answered directly, a question that should be answered with a distinction, a question that should be answered with a counter-question, a question that should be set aside: these are called the four ways of answering questions (*cattāri pañhabyākaraṇāni*).

Therein, when asked, "Is the eye impermanent?", it should be answered directly with "Yes, it is impermanent." This method [applies] to the ear, etc. This is a question that should be answered directly (*ekaṃsabyākaraṇīyo pañho*).

When asked, "Is the eye impermanent?", it should be answered by distinguishing, "Not only the eye, but the ear is impermanent, the nose is impermanent." This is a question that should be answered with a distinction (*vibhajjabyākaraṇīyo pañho*).

When asked, "As is the eye, so is the ear; as is the ear, so is the eye," having counter-questioned, "In what sense do you ask?", when [the other] says, "I ask in the sense of seeing," it should be answered, "No." When [the other] says, "I ask in the sense of impermanence," it should be answered, "Yes." This is a question that should be answered with a counter-question (*paṭipucchābyākaraṇīyo pañho*).

But when asked about "Is the life-principle the same as the body?", etc., it should be set aside [saying], "This has not been explained by the Blessed One"; this question should not be answered. This is a question that should be set aside (*ṭhapanīyo pañho*).

Thus, when a question arises in that way, these four ways of answering questions are the standard. According to these, that question should be answered.

In the sūtras, etc., the *sūtra* (*suttaṃ*) is the three collections (*piṭaka*) that have ascended to the three recitations (*tisso saṅgītiyo*). *What accords with the sūtra* (*suttānulomaṃ*) is what suitably accords. *The teacher's doctrine* (*ācariyavādo*) is the commentary (*aṭṭhakathā*). *One's own opinion* (*attanomati*) is one's own insight through grasping the method by way of subsequent understanding.

Therein, the sūtra is irrefutable; by refuting that, the Buddha himself is refuted. But what suitably accords should be accepted only if it agrees with the sūtra, not the other. The teacher's doctrine, too, should be accepted only if it agrees with the sūtra, not the other. But one's own opinion is the weakest of all; that, too, should be accepted only if it agrees with the sūtra, not the other.

The five-hundred [recitation], the seven-hundred [recitation], the thousand [recitation]: these are the three recitations (*tisso saṅgītiyo*). Even the sūtra that has come down in those [recitations] is the standard; the other, the censured sūtra, should not be accepted.

Therein, even the words and expressions that occur should be understood as not occurring in the sūtra, and not appearing in the Vinaya.
Sūtra, in accordance with the sūtras, the teacher's doctrine, one's own opinion, the three recitations.

Explanation of the story of the metalworker Cunda.
189
<p n="189" rend="bodytext"><hi rend="paranum">189</hi><hi rend="dot">.</hi> Atha kho bhagavā bhoganagare yathābhirantaṃ viharitvā āyasmantaṃ ānandaṃ āmantesi – ‘‘āyāmānanda, yena pāvā tenupasaṅkamissāmā’’ti. ‘‘Evaṃ, bhante’’ti kho āyasmā ānando bhagavato paccassosi. Atha kho bhagavā mahatā bhikkhusaṅghena saddhiṃ yena pāvā tadavasari. Tatra sudaṃ bhagavā pāvāyaṃ viharati cundassa kammāraputtassa ambavane. Assosi kho cundo kammāraputto – ‘‘bhagavā kira pāvaṃ anuppatto, pāvāyaṃ viharati mayhaṃ ambavane’’ti. Atha kho cundo kammāraputto yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṃ abhivādetvā ekamantaṃ nisīdi. Ekamantaṃ nisinnaṃ kho cundaṃ kammāraputtaṃ bhagavā dhammiyā kathāya sandassesi samādapesi samuttejesi sampahaṃsesi. Atha kho cundo kammāraputto bhagavatā dhammiyā kathāya sandassito samādapito samuttejito sampahaṃsito bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – ‘‘adhivāsetu me, bhante, bhagavā svātanāya bhattaṃ saddhiṃ bhikkhusaṅghenā’’ti. Adhivāsesi bhagavā tuṇhībhāvena. Atha kho cundo kammāraputto bhagavato adhivāsanaṃ <pb ed="P" n="2.0127"/> viditvā uṭṭhāyāsanā <pb ed="T" n="2.0148"/> bhagavantaṃ abhivādetvā padakkhiṇaṃ katvā pakkāmi.</p> <p rend="bodytext">Atha kho cundo kammāraputto tassā rattiyā accayena sake nivesane paṇītaṃ khādanīyaṃ bhojanīyaṃ paṭiyādāpetvā pahūtañca sūkaramaddavaṃ bhagavato kālaṃ ārocāpesi – ‘‘kālo, bhante, niṭṭhitaṃ bhatta’’nti. Atha kho bhagavā pubbaṇhasamayaṃ nivāsetvā pattacīvaramādāya saddhiṃ bhikkhusaṅghena yena cundassa kammāraputtassa nivesanaṃ tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā paññatte āsane nisīdi. Nisajja kho bhagavā cundaṃ kammāraputtaṃ āmantesi – ‘‘yaṃ te, cunda, sūkaramaddavaṃ paṭiyattaṃ, tena maṃ parivisa. Yaṃ panaññaṃ khādanīyaṃ bhojanīyaṃ paṭiyattaṃ, tena bhikkhusaṅghaṃ <pb ed="V" n="2.0097"/> parivisā’’ti. ‘‘Evaṃ, bhante’’ti kho cundo kammāraputto bhagavato paṭissutvā yaṃ ahosi sūkaramaddavaṃ paṭiyattaṃ, tena bhagavantaṃ parivisi. Yaṃ panaññaṃ khādanīyaṃ bhojanīyaṃ paṭiyattaṃ <pb ed="M" n="2.0106"/>, tena bhikkhusaṅghaṃ parivisi. Atha kho bhagavā cundaṃ kammāraputtaṃ āmantesi – ‘‘yaṃ te, cunda, sūkaramaddavaṃ avasiṭṭhaṃ, taṃ sobbhe nikhaṇāhi. Nāhaṃ taṃ, cunda, passāmi sadevake loke samārake sabrahmake sassamaṇabrāhmaṇiyā pajāya sadevamanussāya, yassa taṃ paribhuttaṃ sammā pariṇāmaṃ gaccheyya aññatra tathāgatassā’’ti. ‘‘Evaṃ, bhante’’ti kho cundo kammāraputto bhagavato paṭissutvā yaṃ ahosi sūkaramaddavaṃ avasiṭṭhaṃ, taṃ sobbhe nikhaṇitvā yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṃ abhivādetvā ekamantaṃ nisīdi. Ekamantaṃ nisinnaṃ <pb ed="T" n="2.0149"/> kho cundaṃ kammāraputtaṃ bhagavā dhammiyā kathāya sandassetvā samādapetvā samuttejetvā sampahaṃsetvā uṭṭhāyāsanā pakkāmi.</p> <pb ed="V" n="2.0097"/> <pb ed="M" n="2.0106"/> <pb ed="T" n="2.0149"/>
189. Then the Blessed One, having stayed near Bhoganagara as long as he pleased, said to the Venerable Ānanda, “Come, Ānanda, we will head for Pāvā.”

“Yes, venerable sir,” the venerable Ānanda replied to the Fortunate One.

Then the Blessed One, together with a large *saṅgha* of monks, went to Pāvā.

There the Fortunate One lived near Pāvā in Cunda the Smith’s mango grove.

Cunda the silversmith heard, “The Blessed One, they say, on reaching Pāvā, is staying near Pāvā in my mango grove. ”

And he went to the Blessed One, and having respectfully greeted him, sat down at one side.

and the Lord instructed, inspired, fired and delighted him with a talk on *dhamma*.

Then Cunda said: ‘May the Lord accept a meal from me tomorrow with his order of monks!’

The Lord signified his acceptance by silence.

Then Cunda the silversmith, realizing that the Blessed One had accepted, after rising from his seat, worshipping and circumambulating the Fortunate One, went away.

Then, at the end of the night, after having exquisite staple & non-staple food—including a large amount of *sūkaramaddava*—prepared in his own home, he announced the time to the Blessed One: “It’s time, lord. The meal is ready. ”

Thereupon the Blessed One, in the forenoon, having got ready, took bowl and robe and went with the community of *bhikkhus* to the house of Cunda, and there sat down on the seat prepared for him.

and said: ‘Serve the “pig’s delight” that has been prepared to me,

but serve the Community of monks with the other foodstuffs which had been prepared.

‘Very good, Lord’, said Cunda, and did so.

‘Very good, Lord’, said Cunda and, having buried the remains of the ‘pig’s delight’ in a pit, he came to the Lord, saluted him and sat down to one side.

Thereafter the Blessed One spoke to Cunda, saying: “Whatever, Cunda, is left over of the *sūkaramaddava*, bury that in a pit.

For I do not see in all this world, with its gods, *Māras*, and *Brahmās*, among the host of ascetics and brahmans, gods and men, anyone who could eat it and entirely digest it except the *Tathāgata* alone.”

‘Very good, Lord’, said Cunda and, having buried the remains of the ‘pig’s delight’ in a pit, he came to the Lord, saluted him and sat down to one side.

Then the Lord, having instructed, inspired, fired and delighted him with a talk on *dhamma*, rose from his seat and departed.
<p n="189" rend="bodytext"><hi rend="paranum">189</hi><hi rend="dot">.</hi><hi rend="bold">Kammāraputtassā</hi>ti suvaṇṇakāraputtassa. So kira aḍḍho mahākuṭumbiko bhagavato paṭhamadassaneneva sotāpanno hutvā attano ambavane vihāraṃ kārāpetvā niyyātesi. Taṃ sandhāya vuttaṃ – ‘‘ambavane’’ti.</p> <p rend="bodytext"><hi rend="bold">Sūkaramaddava</hi>nti nātitaruṇassa nātijiṇṇassa ekajeṭṭhakasūkarassa pavattamaṃsaṃ. Taṃ kira mudu ceva siniddhañca hoti, taṃ paṭiyādāpetvā sādhukaṃ pacāpetvāti <pb ed="M" n="2.0159"/> attho. Eke bhaṇanti – <hi rend="bold">‘‘sūkaramaddava</hi>nti pana muduodanassa pañcagorasayūsapācanavidhānassa nāmetaṃ, yathā gavapānaṃ nāma pākanāma’’nti. Keci bhaṇanti – <hi rend="bold">‘‘sūkaramaddavaṃ</hi> nāma rasāyanavidhi, taṃ pana rasāyanasatthe āgacchati, taṃ cundena – ‘bhagavato parinibbānaṃ na bhaveyyā’ti rasāyanaṃ paṭiyatta’’nti. Tattha pana dvisahassadīpaparivāresu catūsu mahādīpesu devatā ojaṃ pakkhipiṃsu.</p> <hi rend="bold">Sūkaramaddava</hi> <pb ed="M" n="2.0159"/> <hi rend="bold">‘‘sūkaramaddava</hi> <hi rend="bold">‘‘sūkaramaddavaṃ</hi> <p rend="bodytext"><hi rend="bold">Nāhaṃ ta</hi>nti imaṃ sīhanādaṃ kimatthaṃ nadati? Parūpavādamocanatthaṃ. Attanā paribhuttāvasesaṃ neva bhikkhūnaṃ, na manussānaṃ dātuṃ adāsi, āvāṭe nikhaṇāpetvā vināsesīti hi vattukāmānaṃ idaṃ sutvā vacanokāso na bhavissatīti paresaṃ upavādamocanatthaṃ sīhanādaṃ nadatīti.</p> <hi rend="bold">Nāhaṃ ta</hi>
189. *Kammāraputtassā* means *suvaṇṇakāraputtassa*, the son of a goldsmith.

He was a wealthy head of household who, upon his first sight of the Blessed One, became a *sotāpanna* (stream-enterer). He then had a monastery built in his mango grove and offered it.

Referring to that, it was said, "In the mango grove."

*Sūkaramaddava* means the flesh of a single, mature pig that is neither too young nor too old.

It is said that it was tender and succulent. Having prepared it and having it well cooked, that is the meaning.

Some say, "*Sūkaramaddava* is not the name of a method for preparing soft rice with five products of the cow and broth. It is like *gavapāna*, which is a cooking term."

Some say, "*Sūkaramaddavaṃ* is the name of a recipe for an elixir. That comes in the treatise on elixirs. Cunda prepared that elixir, thinking, 'May the Blessed One's *parinirvāṇa* not happen.'"

There, deities infused sustenance into the four great continents and their surrounding two thousand isles.

*Sūkaramaddava*

*Sūkaramaddava* *Sūkaramaddavaṃ*

"*Nāhaṃ ta* (I did not eat that)," why does he utter this lion's roar? For the sake of release from others' accusations.

"He did not give the remainder that he had consumed to monks or to humans, but had it buried in a pit and destroyed it." Because the opportunity to speak these words will not be for those who desire to say this, he utters the lion's roar for the sake of release from others' accusations.

*Nāhaṃ ta*
190
<p n="190" rend="bodytext"><hi rend="paranum">190</hi><hi rend="dot">.</hi> Atha kho bhagavato cundassa kammāraputtassa bhattaṃ bhuttāvissa kharo ābādho uppajji, lohitapakkhandikā pabāḷhā vedanā vattanti māraṇantikā. Tā sudaṃ <pb ed="P" n="2.0128"/> bhagavā sato sampajāno adhivāsesi avihaññamāno. Atha kho bhagavā āyasmantaṃ ānandaṃ āmantesi – ‘‘āyāmānanda, yena kusinārā tenupasaṅkamissāmā’’ti. ‘‘Evaṃ, bhante’’ti kho āyasmā ānando bhagavato paccassosi.</p> <p rend="gatha1">Cundassa bhattaṃ bhuñjitvā, kammārassāti me sutaṃ;</p> <p rend="gathalast">Ābādhaṃ samphusī dhīro, pabāḷhaṃ māraṇantikaṃ.</p> <p rend="gatha1">Bhuttassa ca sūkaramaddavena,</p> <p rend="gatha2">Byādhippabāḷho udapādi satthuno;</p> <p rend="gatha3">Virecamāno <note>viriccamāno (sī. syā. ka.), viriñcamāno (?)</note> bhagavā avoca,</p> <note>viriccamāno (sī. syā. ka.), viriñcamāno (?)</note> <p rend="gathalast">Gacchāmahaṃ kusināraṃ nagaranti.</p> <p rend="subhead">Pānīyāharaṇaṃ</p>
190. Then, after the Blessed One had eaten the meal provided by Cunda the metalworker’s son, a severe sickness arose, with bloody diarrhea, intense pains, and near death.

But the Blessed One endured it mindfully, with full awareness, and without being troubled.

Then the Blessed One addressed the Venerable Ānanda, saying, “Come, Ānanda, let us go to Kuśinārā.”

“So be it, Lord,” the Venerable Ānanda replied to the Blessed One.

Having eaten Cunda's meal, so I have heard, the metalworker's,

the wise man was assailed by dire sickness, intense and deadly.

And after eating tender pork,

a severe illness arose in the Teacher.

As the Blessed One was purging—the Blessed One said,

"Let us go to the city of Kuśinārā."

Acquisition of drinking water.
<p n="190" rend="bodytext"><hi rend="paranum">190</hi><hi rend="dot">.</hi><hi rend="bold">Bhuttassa ca sūkaramaddavenā</hi>ti bhuttassa udapādi, na pana bhuttapaccayā. Yadi hi abhuttassa uppajjissatha, atikharo bhavissati. Siniddhabhojanaṃ bhuttattā panassa tanuvedanā ahosi. Teneva padasā gantuṃ asakkhi. <hi rend="bold">Virecamāno</hi>ti abhiṇhaṃ pavattalohitavirecanova samāno <pb ed="V" n="2.0143"/>. <hi rend="bold">Avocā</hi>ti attanā patthitaṭṭhāne parinibbānatthāya evamāha. Imā pana dhammasaṅgāhakattherehi ṭhapitagāthāyoti veditabbā.</p> <p rend="subhead">Pānīyāharaṇavaṇṇanā</p>
190. "bhuttassa ca sūkaramaddavenā" means it arose from what was eaten, not just because of what was eaten.

If it were to arise from what was not eaten, it would be too harsh.

Because he had eaten rich food, he experienced mild pain.

He was barely able to walk.

"virecamāno" means being similar to someone with frequent bloody diarrhea.

"avocā" means he spoke thus for the sake of attaining complete nirvāṇa in a place desired by himself.

These verses, however, should be understood as having been established by the compilers of the Dharma.

Description of fetching water.
191
<p n="191" rend="bodytext"><hi rend="paranum">191</hi><hi rend="dot">.</hi> Atha kho bhagavā maggā okkamma yena aññataraṃ rukkhamūlaṃ tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā āyasmantaṃ ānandaṃ āmantesi – ‘‘iṅgha me tvaṃ, ānanda, catugguṇaṃ saṅghāṭiṃ paññapehi, kilantosmi, ānanda, nisīdissāmī’’ti. ‘‘Evaṃ, bhante’’ti kho āyasmā ānando <pb ed="V" n="2.0098"/> bhagavato paṭissutvā catugguṇaṃ saṅghāṭiṃ paññapesi. Nisīdi bhagavā paññatte āsane. Nisajja kho bhagavā āyasmantaṃ <pb ed="T" n="2.0150"/><pb ed="M" n="2.0107"/> ānandaṃ āmantesi – ‘‘iṅgha me tvaṃ, ānanda, pānīyaṃ āhara, pipāsitosmi, ānanda, pivissāmī’’ti. Evaṃ vutte āyasmā ānando bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – ‘‘idāni, bhante, pañcamattāni sakaṭasatāni atikkantāni, taṃ cakkacchinnaṃ udakaṃ parittaṃ luḷitaṃ āvilaṃ sandati. Ayaṃ, bhante, kakudhā <note>kakuthā (sī. pī.)</note> nadī avidūre acchodakā sātodakā <pb ed="P" n="2.0129"/> sītodakā setodakā <note>setakā (sī.)</note> suppatitthā ramaṇīyā. Ettha bhagavā pānīyañca pivissati, gattāni ca sītī <note>sītaṃ (sī. pī. ka.)</note> karissatī’’ti.</p> <p rend="bodytext">Dutiyampi kho bhagavā āyasmantaṃ ānandaṃ āmantesi – ‘‘iṅgha me tvaṃ, ānanda, pānīyaṃ āhara, pipāsitosmi, ānanda, pivissāmī’’ti. Dutiyampi kho āyasmā ānando bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – ‘‘idāni, bhante, pañcamattāni sakaṭasatāni atikkantāni, taṃ cakkacchinnaṃ udakaṃ parittaṃ luḷitaṃ āvilaṃ sandati. Ayaṃ, bhante, kakudhā nadī avidūre acchodakā sātodakā sītodakā setodakā suppatitthā ramaṇīyā. Ettha bhagavā pānīyañca pivissati, gattāni ca sītīkarissatī’’ti.</p> <p rend="bodytext">Tatiyampi kho bhagavā āyasmantaṃ ānandaṃ āmantesi – ‘‘iṅgha me tvaṃ, ānanda, pānīyaṃ āhara, pipāsitosmi, ānanda, pivissāmī’’ti. ‘‘Evaṃ, bhante’’ti kho āyasmā ānando bhagavato paṭissutvā <pb ed="T" n="2.0151"/> pattaṃ gahetvā yena sā nadikā tenupasaṅkami. Atha kho sā nadikā cakkacchinnā parittā luḷitā āvilā sandamānā, āyasmante ānande upasaṅkamante acchā vippasannā anāvilā sandittha <note>sandati (syā.)</note>. Atha kho āyasmato ānandassa etadahosi – ‘‘acchariyaṃ vata, bho, abbhutaṃ vata, bho, tathāgatassa mahiddhikatā mahānubhāvatā. Ayañhi sā nadikā cakkacchinnā parittā luḷitā āvilā sandamānā mayi upasaṅkamante acchā vippasannā anāvilā sandatī’’ti. Pattena pānīyaṃ ādāya yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – ‘‘acchariyaṃ, bhante, abbhutaṃ, bhante, tathāgatassa mahiddhikatā mahānubhāvatā. Idāni sā bhante nadikā cakkacchinnā parittā luḷitā āvilā sandamānā mayi upasaṅkamante acchā vippasannā anāvilā sandittha. Pivatu bhagavā pānīyaṃ pivatu sugato pānīya’’nti. Atha kho bhagavā pānīyaṃ apāyi.</p> <pb ed="T" n="2.0151"/> <note>sandati (syā.)</note> <p rend="subhead">Pukkusamallaputtavatthu</p>
191. Then the Blessed One, stepping aside from the road, approached a certain tree and, having arrived, addressed the Venerable Ānanda, "Come, Ānanda, fold my outer robe in four and lay it down; I am tired, Ānanda, I will sit down."

"So be it, Lord," the Venerable Ānanda replied to the Blessed One, and folded the outer robe in four and laid it down.

The Blessed One sat down on the prepared seat.

Seated, the Blessed One addressed the Venerable Ānanda, "Come, Ānanda, fetch me some water; I am thirsty, Ānanda, I will drink."

When this was said, the Venerable Ānanda said to the Blessed One, "Just now, Lord, five hundred carts have passed by, and the water, cut by the wheels, is meager, stirred up, and flows turbid.

But, Lord, the Kakudhā River is not far away, with clear water, pleasant water, cool water, translucent water, with easily accessible banks, delightful. There the Blessed One can drink water, and cool his limbs."

A second time, the Blessed One addressed the Venerable Ānanda, "Come, Ānanda, fetch me some water; I am thirsty, Ānanda, I will drink."

A second time, the Venerable Ānanda said to the Blessed One, "Just now, Lord, five hundred carts have passed by, and the water, cut by the wheels, is meager, stirred up, and flows turbid.

But, Lord, the Kakudhā River is not far away, with clear water, pleasant water, cool water, translucent water, with easily accessible banks, delightful. There the Blessed One can drink water, and cool his limbs."

A third time, the Blessed One addressed the Venerable Ānanda, "Come, Ānanda, fetch me some water; I am thirsty, Ānanda, I will drink."

"So be it, Lord," the Venerable Ānanda replied to the Blessed One, and taking the bowl, he approached that river.

Then that river, cut by the wheels, meager, stirred up, flowing turbid, as the Venerable Ānanda approached, flowed clear, serene, and undisturbed.

Then the Venerable Ānanda thought, "Amazing, indeed, wonderful, indeed, is the great power and might of the *Tathāgata*!

Indeed, this river, cut by the wheels, meager, stirred up, flowing turbid, as I approached, flows clear, serene, and undisturbed!"

Taking water in the bowl, he approached the Blessed One; having approached, he said to the Blessed One, "Amazing, Lord, wonderful, Lord, is the great power and might of the *Tathāgata*.

Now that river, Lord, cut by the wheels, meager, stirred up, flowing turbid, as I approached, flows clear, serene, and undisturbed.

May the Blessed One drink the water, may the *Sugata* drink the water!"

Then the Blessed One drank the water.

Pukkusamallaputtavatthu
<p n="191" rend="bodytext"><hi rend="paranum">191</hi><hi rend="dot">.</hi><hi rend="bold">Iṅghā</hi>ti codanatthe nipāto. <hi rend="bold">Acchodakā</hi>ti <pb ed="P" n="2.0569"/> pasannodakā. <hi rend="bold">Sātodakā</hi>ti madhurodakā. <hi rend="bold">Sītodakā</hi>ti tanusītalasalilā. <hi rend="bold">Setakā</hi>ti nikkaddamā. <hi rend="bold">Suppatitthā</hi>ti sundaratitthā.</p> <p rend="subhead">Pukkusamallaputtavatthuvaṇṇanā</p>
191.
*iṅghā* is a particle in the sense of impelling.
*acchodakā* means having clear water (*prasannodakā*).
*sātodakā* means having sweet water (*madhurodakā*).
*sītodakā* means having thin, cool water (*tanusītalasalilā*).
*setakā* means free from mud (*nikkaddamā*).
*suppatitthā* means having a beautiful bathing place (*sundaratitthā*).

Commentary on the story of Pukkusa Mallaputta.
192
<p n="192" rend="bodytext"><hi rend="paranum">192</hi><hi rend="dot">.</hi> Tena <pb ed="M" n="2.0108"/><pb ed="V" n="2.0099"/><pb ed="P" n="2.0130"/> rokho pana samayena pukkuso mallaputto āḷārassa kālāmassa sāvako kusinārāya pāvaṃ addhānamaggappaṭippanno hoti. Addasā kho pukkuso mallaputto bhagavantaṃ aññatarasmiṃ rukkhamūle nisinnaṃ. Disvā yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṃ abhivādetvā ekamantaṃ nisīdi. Ekamantaṃ nisinno kho pukkuso mallaputto bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – ‘‘acchariyaṃ, bhante, abbhutaṃ, bhante, santena vata, bhante, pabbajitā vihārena viharanti. Bhūtapubbaṃ, bhante <pb ed="T" n="2.0152"/>, āḷāro kālāmo addhānamaggappaṭippanno maggā okkamma avidūre aññatarasmiṃ rukkhamūle divāvihāraṃ nisīdi. Atha kho, bhante, pañcamattāni sakaṭasatāni āḷāraṃ kālāmaṃ nissāya nissāya atikkamiṃsu. Atha kho, bhante, aññataro puriso tassa sakaṭasatthassa <note>sakaṭasatassa (ka.)</note> piṭṭhito piṭṭhito āgacchanto yena āḷāro kālāmo tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā āḷāraṃ kālāmaṃ etadavoca – ‘api, bhante, pañcamattāni sakaṭasatāni atikkantāni addasā’ti? ‘Na kho ahaṃ, āvuso, addasa’nti. ‘Kiṃ pana, bhante, saddaṃ assosī’ti? ‘Na kho ahaṃ, āvuso, saddaṃ assosi’nti. ‘Kiṃ pana, bhante, sutto ahosī’ti? ‘Na kho ahaṃ, āvuso, sutto ahosi’nti. ‘Kiṃ pana, bhante, saññī ahosī’ti? ‘Evamāvuso’ti. ‘So tvaṃ, bhante, saññī samāno jāgaro pañcamattāni sakaṭasatāni nissāya nissāya atikkantāni neva addasa, na pana saddaṃ assosi; apisu <note>api hi (sī. syā. pī.)</note> te, bhante, saṅghāṭi rajena okiṇṇā’ti? ‘Evamāvuso’ti. Atha kho, bhante, tassa purisassa etadahosi – ‘acchariyaṃ vata bho, abbhutaṃ vata bho, santena vata bho pabbajitā vihārena viharanti. Yatra hi nāma saññī samāno <pb ed="P" n="2.0131"/> jāgaro pañcamattāni sakaṭasatāni nissāya nissāya atikkantāni neva dakkhati, na pana saddaṃ sossatī’ti! Āḷāre kālāme uḷāraṃ pasādaṃ pavedetvā pakkāmī’’ti.</p>
Now, at that time, Pukkusa Mallaputta, a disciple of Āḷāra Kālāma, was traveling on the road from Kusinārā to Pāvā.

Pukkusa Mallaputta saw the Blessed One (Bhagavān) sitting at the root of a certain tree.

Having seen him, he approached the Blessed One; having approached, he respectfully greeted the Blessed One and sat down to one side.

Sitting to one side, Pukkusa Mallaputta said this to the Blessed One: “Amazing, venerable sir (bhante)! Astounding, venerable sir (bhante)! Indeed, those who have gone forth abide in a peaceful abiding, venerable sir (bhante)!”

“Once, venerable sir (bhante), Āḷāra Kālāma, while traveling on the road, went aside from the road and sat down not far away at the root of a tree for the day’s abiding.

Then, venerable sir (bhante), five hundred carts passed by Āḷāra Kālāma, right near him.

Then, venerable sir (bhante), a certain man, coming along right behind that caravan of carts, approached Āḷāra Kālāma and said to him, ‘Venerable sir (bhante), did you see five hundred carts that have passed by?’ ‘No, friend (āvuso), I did not see.’

‘Then, venerable sir (bhante), did you hear a sound?’ ‘No, friend (āvuso), I did not hear a sound.’

‘Then, venerable sir (bhante), were you asleep?’ ‘No, friend (āvuso), I was not asleep.’

‘Then, venerable sir (bhante), were you conscious (saññī)?’ ‘Yes, friend (āvuso).’

‘So you, venerable sir (bhante), being conscious (saññī), awake, did not see five hundred carts passing by, one by one, nor did you hear a sound; and yet, venerable sir (bhante), your outer robe is covered with dust?’ ‘So it is, friend (āvuso).’

Then, venerable sir (bhante), this occurred to that man: ‘Amazing indeed, sir (bho)! Astounding indeed, sir (bho)! Those who have gone forth abide in a peaceful abiding, sir (bho)!

Where, indeed, being conscious (saññī) and awake, he will not see five hundred carts passing by, one by one, nor will he hear a sound!’ Having expressed great faith in Āḷāra Kālāma, he departed."
<p n="192" rend="bodytext"><hi rend="paranum">192</hi><hi rend="dot">.</hi><hi rend="bold">Pukkuso</hi>ti tassa nāmaṃ. <hi rend="bold">Mallaputto</hi>ti mallarājaputto. Mallā kira vārena rajjaṃ kārenti. Yāva nesaṃ vāro na pāpuṇāti, tāva vaṇijjaṃ karonti. Ayampi vaṇijjameva karonto pañca sakaṭasatāni yojāpetvā dhuravāte vāyante purato gacchati, pacchā vāte vāyante satthavāhaṃ purato pesetvā sayaṃ pacchā gacchati. Tadā pana pacchā vāto vāyi, tasmā esa purato satthavāhaṃ pesetvā sabbaratanayāne <pb ed="M" n="2.0160"/> nisīditvā kusinārato nikkhamitvā ‘‘pāvaṃ gamissāmī’’ti maggaṃ paṭipajji. Tena vuttaṃ – ‘‘kusinārāya pāvaṃ addhānamaggappaṭipanno hotī’’ti.</p> <p rend="bodytext"><hi rend="bold">Āḷāro</hi>ti tassa nāmaṃ. Dīghapiṅgalo kireso, tenassa āḷāroti nāmaṃ ahosi. <hi rend="bold">Kālāmo</hi>ti gottaṃ. <hi rend="bold">Yatra hi nāmā</hi>ti yo nāma. <hi rend="bold">Neva dakkhatī</hi>ti na addasa. Yatrasaddayuttattā panetaṃ anāgatavasena vuttaṃ. Evarūpañhi īdisesu ṭhānesu saddalakkhaṇaṃ.</p> <hi rend="bold">Āḷāro</hi> <hi rend="bold">Kālāmo</hi> <hi rend="bold">Yatra hi nāmā</hi> <hi rend="bold">Neva dakkhatī</hi>
192. His name was Pukkusa.

He was the son of a Malla king, (mallaputto ti mallarājaputto).

The Mallas manage the kingdom in turns.

Until their turn arrives, they engage in trade.

This one, also engaged in trade, having arranged five hundred carts, was going ahead while the favorable winds blew. When the winds blew from behind, he sent the caravan ahead and he himself went behind.

Then, the wind blew from behind. Therefore, having sent the caravan ahead, he sat in the all-jeweled carriage, departed from Kusinārā, and set out on the road, thinking, "I will go to Pāvā".

It was said by him: "He is on the road to Pāvā from Kusinārā," (kusinārāya pāvaṃ addhānamaggappaṭipanno hotīti).

His name was Āḷāra.

He was tall and yellowish-brown, therefore his name became Āḷāra.

His clan was Kālāma.

"Where indeed is the name," (yatra hi nāmā) that is the name.

"He does not see," (neva dakkhatī) he did not see.

Because of the association with truth, this was said in terms of the future.

Such is the characteristic of truth in such places.

Āḷāra, Kālāma, where indeed is the name, he does not see.
193
<p n="193" rend="bodytext"><hi rend="paranum">193</hi><hi rend="dot">.</hi> ‘‘Taṃ kiṃ maññasi, pukkusa, katamaṃ nu kho dukkarataraṃ vā durabhisambhavataraṃ vā – yo vā saññī samāno jāgaro pañcamattāni <pb ed="T" n="2.0153"/> sakaṭasatāni nissāya nissāya atikkantāni neva passeyya, na pana saddaṃ <pb ed="M" n="2.0109"/> suṇeyya; yo vā saññī samāno jāgaro deve vassante deve gaḷagaḷāyante vijjullatāsu <note>vijjutāsu (sī. syā. pī.)</note> niccharantīsu asaniyā phalantiyā neva passeyya, na pana saddaṃ suṇeyyā’’ti? ‘‘Kiñhi, bhante, karissanti pañca vā sakaṭasatāni cha vā sakaṭasatāni satta vā sakaṭasatāni aṭṭha vā sakaṭasatāni nava vā sakaṭasatāni <note>nava vā sakaṭasatāni dasa vā sakaṭasatāni (sī.)</note>, sakaṭasahassaṃ vā sakaṭasatasahassaṃ vā. Atha kho etadeva dukkarataraṃ ceva durabhisambhavatarañca yo <pb ed="V" n="2.0100"/> saññī samāno jāgaro deve vassante deve gaḷagaḷāyante vijjullatāsu niccharantīsu asaniyā phalantiyā neva passeyya, na pana saddaṃ suṇeyyā’’ti.</p> <p rend="bodytext">‘‘Ekamidāhaṃ, pukkusa, samayaṃ ātumāyaṃ viharāmi bhusāgāre. Tena kho pana samayena deve vassante deve gaḷagaḷāyante vijjullatāsu niccharantīsu asaniyā phalantiyā avidūre bhusāgārassa dve kassakā bhātaro hatā cattāro ca balibaddā <note>balibaddā (sī. pī.)</note>. Atha kho, pukkusa, ātumāya mahājanakāyo nikkhamitvā yena te dve kassakā bhātaro hatā cattāro ca balibaddā tenupasaṅkami. Tena kho panāhaṃ, pukkusa, samayena bhusāgārā nikkhamitvā bhusāgāradvāre abbhokāse caṅkamāmi. Atha kho, pukkusa, aññataro puriso tamhā mahājanakāyā yenāhaṃ tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā maṃ abhivādetvā ekamantaṃ aṭṭhāsi. Ekamantaṃ <pb ed="T" n="2.0154"/> ṭhitaṃ kho ahaṃ, pukkusa, taṃ purisaṃ etadavocaṃ – ‘kiṃ nu kho eso, āvuso, mahājanakāyo sannipatito’ti? ‘Idāni <pb ed="P" n="2.0132"/>, bhante, deve vassante deve gaḷagaḷāyante vijjullatāsu niccharantīsu asaniyā phalantiyā dve kassakā bhātaro hatā cattāro ca balibaddā. Ettheso mahājanakāyo sannipatito. Tvaṃ pana, bhante, kva ahosī’ti? ‘Idheva kho ahaṃ, āvuso, ahosi’nti. ‘Kiṃ pana, bhante, addasā’ti? ‘Na kho ahaṃ, āvuso, addasa’nti. ‘Kiṃ pana, bhante, saddaṃ assosī’ti? ‘Na kho ahaṃ, āvuso, saddaṃ assosi’nti. ‘Kiṃ pana, bhante, sutto ahosī’ti? ‘Na kho ahaṃ, āvuso, sutto ahosi’nti. ‘Kiṃ pana, bhante, saññī ahosī’ti? ‘Evamāvuso’ti. ‘So tvaṃ, bhante, saññī samāno jāgaro deve vassante deve gaḷagaḷāyante <pb ed="M" n="2.0110"/> vijjullatāsu niccharantīsu asaniyā phalantiyā neva addasa, na pana saddaṃ assosī’ti? ‘‘Evamāvuso’’ti?</p> <note>balibaddā (sī. pī.)</note> <pb ed="T" n="2.0154"/> <pb ed="P" n="2.0132"/> <pb ed="M" n="2.0110"/> <p rend="bodytext">‘‘Atha kho, pukkusa, purisassa etadahosi – ‘acchariyaṃ vata bho, abbhutaṃ vata bho, santena vata bho pabbajitā vihārena viharanti. Yatra hi nāma saññī samāno jāgaro deve vassante deve gaḷagaḷāyante vijjullatāsu niccharantīsu asaniyā phalantiyā neva dakkhati, na pana saddaṃ sossatī’ti <note>suṇissati (syā.)</note>. Mayi uḷāraṃ pasādaṃ pavedetvā maṃ abhivādetvā padakkhiṇaṃ katvā pakkāmī’’ti.</p> <note>suṇissati (syā.)</note> <p rend="bodytext">Evaṃ vutte pukkuso mallaputto bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – ‘‘esāhaṃ, bhante, yo me āḷāre kālāme pasādo taṃ mahāvāte vā ophuṇāmi sīghasotāya <pb ed="T" n="2.0155"/><note>siṅghasotāya (ka.)</note> vā nadiyā pavāhemi. Abhikkantaṃ, bhante, abhikkantaṃ, bhante! Seyyathāpi, bhante, nikkujjitaṃ vā ukkujjeyya, paṭicchannaṃ <pb ed="V" n="2.0101"/> vā vivareyya, mūḷhassa vā maggaṃ ācikkheyya, andhakāre vā telapajjotaṃ dhāreyya ‘cakkhumanto rūpāni dakkhantī’ti; evamevaṃ bhagavatā anekapariyāyena dhammo pakāsito. Esāhaṃ, bhante, bhagavantaṃ saraṇaṃ gacchāmi dhammañca <pb ed="P" n="2.0133"/> bhikkhusaṅghañca. Upāsakaṃ maṃ bhagavā dhāretu ajjatagge pāṇupetaṃ saraṇaṃ gata’’nti.</p> <pb ed="T" n="2.0155"/> <note>siṅghasotāya (ka.)</note> <pb ed="V" n="2.0101"/> <pb ed="P" n="2.0133"/>
“What do you think, Pukkusa? Which is more difficult to do, more difficult to master: one who, being conscious and awake when 500 carts passed by right near, would neither see them nor hear a sound; or one who, being conscious and awake when the rain-deva was raining, the rain-deva was pouring, lightning-streaks were shooting out, and a thunderbolt splits , would neither see them nor hear a sound? ” “Lord, what would 500 carts amount to—or 600 carts, or 700 carts, or 800 carts, or 900 carts, or 1,000 carts… or 100,000 carts? To see or hear nothing when such a storm rages is more difficult…’

“One time, Pukkusa, I was staying near Ātumā in a threshing-barn. And at that time there was a heavy rain, with thunder rolling, lightning flashing, and thunderbolts crashing. And two farmers who were brothers were killed close to the barn, together with four oxen,. Then a lot of people went out of Atuma to where the two brothers and the four oxen were killed. And, Pukkusa, I had at that time gone out of the door of the threshing-floor and was walking up and down outside. And a man from the crowd came to me, saluted me and stood to one side. Standing to one side, Pukkusa, I said to the man, ‘Why has this great crowd gathered?’ ‘Lord, there has been a great storm and two farmers, brothers, and four oxen have been killed. That is why this great crowd has gathered.’ ‘And where were you, Lord?’ ‘I was right here, friend.’ ‘Then, Lord, did you see anything?’ ‘No, friend, I didn’t see anything.’ ‘Then, Lord, did you hear any sound?’ ‘No, friend, I didn’t hear any sound.’ ‘Then, Lord, were you asleep?’ ‘No, friend, I wasn’t asleep.’ ‘Then, Lord, were you consciousr’ ‘Yes, friend.’ ‘Then, Lord, being conscious & awake when the rain-deva was raining, the rain-deva was pouring, lightning-streaks were shooting out, and a thunderbolt split , you neither saw anything nor heard a sound. ’ ‘‘Yes, friend.’’

“And, Pukkusa, that man thought: “It is wonderful, it is marvellous! These wanderers are so calm that they neither see nor hear when the rain-god streams and splashes, lightning flashes and thunder crashes!” Proclaiming my lofty powers, he saluted me, passed by to the right and departed.’

When this was said, Pukkusa Mallaputta said to the Blessed One, “The conviction I had in Āḷāra Kālāma I winnow before a high wind or wash away in the swift current of a river.
Excellent, Lord, excellent! Just as, Lord, one might set upright what is overturned (**nikkujjitaṃ vā ukkujjeyya**), or reveal what is hidden (**paṭicchannaṃ vā vivareyya**), or show the way to one who is lost (**mūḷhassa vā maggaṃ ācikkheyya**), or hold up an oil lamp in the darkness so that those with eyes might see forms (**andhakāre vā telapajjotaṃ dhāreyya ‘cakkhumanto rūpāni dakkhantī’ti**); in the very same way, the Dhamma has been made clear in many ways by the Blessed One (**evamevaṃ bhagavatā anekapariyāyena dhammo pakāsito**).

I go to the Blessed One for refuge, Lord (**esāhaṃ, bhante, bhagavantaṃ saraṇaṃ gacchāmi**), to the Dhamma (**dhammañca**), and to the Order of Monks (**bhikkhusaṅghañca**).

May the Blessed One accept me as a lay follower (**upāsakaṃ maṃ bhagavā dhāretu**) who has gone for refuge, from this day forward, for life (**ajjatagge pāṇupetaṃ saraṇaṃ gata’’nti**).

[Note:] For Siṅghasota.
<p n="193" rend="bodytext"><hi rend="paranum">193</hi><hi rend="dot">.</hi><hi rend="bold">Niccharantīsū</hi>ti vicarantīsu. <hi rend="bold">Asaniyā phalantiyā</hi>ti navavidhāya asaniyā bhijjamānāya viya mahāravaṃ ravantiyā. Navavidhā hi asaniyo – asaññā, vicakkā, saterā, gaggarā, kapisīsā, macchavilolikā, kukkuṭakā, daṇḍamaṇikā, sukkhāsanīti. Tattha asaññā asaññaṃ karoti. Vicakkā ekaṃ cakkaṃ karoti. Saterā saterasadisā hutvā patati. Gaggarā gaggarāyamānā patati. Kapisīsā bhamukaṃ ukkhipento makkaṭo viya hoti. Macchavilolikā vilolitamaccho viya hoti. Kukkuṭakā kukkuṭasadisā hutvā patati. Daṇḍamaṇikā naṅgalasadisā hutvā patati. Sukkhāsanī patitaṭṭhānaṃ samugghāṭeti.</p> <p rend="bodytext"><hi rend="bold">Deve</hi><pb ed="V" n="2.0144"/><hi rend="bold">vassante</hi>ti sukkhagajjitaṃ gajjitvā antarantarā vassante. <hi rend="bold">Ātumāya</hi>nti ātumaṃ nissāya viharāmi. <hi rend="bold">Bhusāgāre</hi>ti khalasālāyaṃ. <hi rend="bold">Ettheso</hi>ti etasmiṃ kāraṇe eso mahājanakāyo sannipatito. <hi rend="bold">Kva ahosī</hi>ti kuhiṃ ahosi. <hi rend="bold">So taṃ bhante</hi>ti so tvaṃ bhante.</p> <hi rend="bold">Deve</hi> <pb ed="V" n="2.0144"/> <hi rend="bold">vassante</hi> <hi rend="bold">Ātumāya</hi> <hi rend="bold">Bhusāgāre</hi> <hi rend="bold">Ettheso</hi> <hi rend="bold">Kva ahosī</hi> <hi rend="bold">So taṃ bhante</hi>
193. *Niccharantīsū* means among those wandering.

*Asaniyā phalantiyā* means like a great roar sounding as a ninefold thunderbolt is splitting.

For there are nine kinds of thunderbolts: *asaññā*, *vicakkā*, *saterā*, *gaggarā*, *kapisīsā*, *macchavilolikā*, *kukkuṭakā*, *daṇḍamaṇikā*, *sukkhāsanī*.

There, *asaññā* renders one senseless ( *asaññāṃ karoti*).

*Vicakkā* makes a single wheel (*ekaṃ cakkaṃ karoti*).

*Saterā* falls having become similar to a shower of hail (*saterasadisā hutvā patati*).

*Gaggarā* falls rumbling (*gaggarāyamānā patati*).

*Kapisīsā* is like a monkey raising its brow (*bhamukaṃ ukkhipento makkaṭo viya hoti*).

*Macchavilolikā* is like a disturbed fish (*vilolitamaccho viya hoti*).

*Kukkuṭakā* falls having become similar to a cock (*kukkuṭasadisā hutvā patati*).

*Daṇḍamaṇikā* falls having become similar to a plough (*naṅgalasadisā hutvā patati*).

*Sukkhāsanī* digs up the place where it falls (*patitaṭṭhānaṃ samugghāṭeti*).

*Deve vassante* means while the god rains, raining intermittently having thundered a dry thunder.

*Ātumāya* means I live relying on myself (*ātumaṃ nissāya viharāmi*).

*Bhusāgāre* means in the barn (*khalasālāyaṃ*).

*Ettheso* means this great crowd has gathered for this reason (*etasmiṃ kāraṇe eso mahājanakāyo sannipatito*).

*Kva ahosī* means where were you? (*kuhiṃ ahosi*).

*So taṃ bhante* means you, venerable sir (*so tvaṃ bhante*).

*Deve vassante ātumāya bhusāgāre ettheso kva ahosī so taṃ bhante*
194
<p n="194" rend="bodytext"><hi rend="paranum">194</hi><hi rend="dot">.</hi> Atha kho pukkuso mallaputto aññataraṃ purisaṃ āmantesi – ‘‘iṅgha me tvaṃ, bhaṇe, siṅgīvaṇṇaṃ yugamaṭṭhaṃ dhāraṇīyaṃ āharā’’ti. ‘‘Evaṃ, bhante’’ti kho so puriso pukkusassa mallaputtassa paṭissutvā taṃ siṅgīvaṇṇaṃ yugamaṭṭhaṃ dhāraṇīyaṃ āhari <note>āharasi (ka.)</note>. Atha kho pukkuso mallaputto taṃ siṅgīvaṇṇaṃ yugamaṭṭhaṃ dhāraṇīyaṃ bhagavato upanāmesi – ‘‘idaṃ, bhante, siṅgīvaṇṇaṃ yugamaṭṭhaṃ dhāraṇīyaṃ, taṃ me bhagavā paṭiggaṇhātu anukampaṃ upādāyā’’ti. ‘‘Tena hi, pukkusa, ekena maṃ acchādehi, ekena ānanda’’nti. ‘‘Evaṃ, bhante’’ti kho pukkuso mallaputto bhagavato paṭissutvā ekena bhagavantaṃ acchādeti, ekena āyasmantaṃ ānandaṃ. Atha kho bhagavā pukkusaṃ mallaputtaṃ dhammiyā kathāya sandassesi samādapesi samuttejesi sampahaṃsesi. Atha kho pukkuso mallaputto bhagavatā dhammiyā kathāya sandassito samādapito samuttejito sampahaṃsito uṭṭhāyāsanā bhagavantaṃ abhivādetvā padakkhiṇaṃ katvā pakkāmi.</p>
Then Pukkusa Mallaputta addressed a certain man: "Come now, I say. Fetch me a pair of gold-colored robes, ready to wear."

"So be it, lord," the man replied to Pukkusa Mallaputta, and fetched the pair of gold-colored robes, ready to wear.

Then Pukkusa Mallaputta presented the pair of gold-colored robes, ready to wear, to the Blessed One, saying, "May the Blessed One accept this pair of gold-colored robes, ready to wear, out of kindness."

"Then, Pukkusa, clothe me with one, and Ānanda with the other."

Responding, "As you say, lord," to the Blessed One, Pukkusa Mallaputta clothed the Blessed One with one, and Venerable Ānanda with the other.

Then the Blessed One instructed, urged, roused, and encouraged Pukkusa Mallaputta with a *dharma* talk.

Then Pukkusa Mallaputta—instructed, urged, roused, and encouraged with the Blessed One’s *dharma* talk—got up from his seat and, bowing down to the Blessed One and circumambulating him (*pradakṣiṇa*), left.
<p n="194" rend="bodytext"><hi rend="paranum">194</hi><hi rend="dot">.</hi><hi rend="bold">Siṅgīvaṇṇa</hi>nti siṅgīsuvaṇṇavaṇṇaṃ. <hi rend="bold">Yugamaṭṭha</hi>nti <pb ed="P" n="2.0570"/> maṭṭhayugaṃ, saṇhasāṭakayugaḷanti attho. <hi rend="bold">Dhāraṇīya</hi>nti antarantarā mayā dhāretabbaṃ, paridahitabbanti attho. Taṃ kira so tathārūpe chaṇadivaseyeva dhāretvā sesakāle nikkhipati. Evaṃ uttamaṃ maṅgalavatthayugaṃ sandhāyāha. <hi rend="bold">Anukampaṃ upādāyā</hi>ti mayi anukampaṃ paṭicca. <hi rend="bold">Acchādehī</hi>ti upacāravacanametaṃ – ekaṃ mayhaṃ dehi, ekaṃ ānandassāti attho. Kiṃ pana thero taṃ gaṇhīti? Āma gaṇhi. Kasmā? Matthakappattakiccattā. Kiñcāpi hesa evarūpaṃ lābhaṃ paṭikkhipitvā upaṭṭhākaṭṭhānaṃ paṭipanno. Taṃ panassa upaṭṭhākakiccaṃ matthakaṃ pattaṃ. Tasmā aggahesi. Ye cāpi evaṃ vadeyyuṃ – ‘‘anārādhako maññe ānando <pb ed="M" n="2.0161"/> pañcavīsati vassāni upaṭṭhahantena na kiñci bhagavato santikā tena laddhapubba’’nti. Tesaṃ vacanokāsacchedanatthampi aggahesi. Api ca jānāti bhagavā – ‘‘ānando gahetvāpi attanā na dhāressati, mayhaṃyeva pūjaṃ karissati. Mallaputtena pana ānandaṃ pūjentena saṅghopi pūjito bhavissati, evamassa mahāpuññarāsi bhavissatī’’ti therassa ekaṃ dāpesi. Theropi teneva kāraṇena aggahesīti. <hi rend="bold">Dhammiyā kathāyā</hi>ti vatthānumodanakathāya.</p>
194. *Siṅgīvaṇṇa* means *siṅgīsuvaṇṇavaṇṇaṃ* (the color of gold).

*Yugamaṭṭha* means *maṭṭhayugaṃ*, which means a pair of smooth cloths.

*Dhāraṇīya* means something that I should wear from time to time, something to be put on. It seems that he would wear it on such festive days and then put it away at other times. He said this with reference to an excellent pair of auspicious cloths.

*Anukampaṃ upādāya* means out of compassion for me.

*Acchādehī* is a term of respect – it means, "Give one to me, and one to Ānanda."

Did the elder accept it? Yes, he did. Why? Because the service he provided had reached its peak. Although he was one who would refuse such gains and attend to his duties as an attendant, his duty as an attendant had reached its peak. Therefore, he accepted it.

And also, he accepted it in order to cut off the opportunity for those who might say, "I think Ānanda is displeasing, having attended the Blessed One for twenty-five years, nothing has ever been obtained by him from the Blessed One."

Moreover, the Blessed One knows, "Even having taken it, Ānanda will not wear it himself, but will only make an offering to me. And by Mallaputta honoring Ānanda, the Saṅgha will also be honored, thus there will be a great heap of merit for him," so he gave one to the elder. The elder also accepted it for the same reason.

*Dhammiyā kathāya* means with a talk of appreciation for the cloth.
195
<p n="195" rend="bodytext"><hi rend="paranum">195</hi><hi rend="dot">.</hi> Atha <pb ed="T" n="2.0156"/><pb ed="M" n="2.0111"/> kho āyasmā ānando acirapakkante pukkuse mallaputte taṃ siṅgīvaṇṇaṃ yugamaṭṭhaṃ dhāraṇīyaṃ bhagavato kāyaṃ upanāmesi. Taṃ bhagavato kāyaṃ upanāmitaṃ hataccikaṃ viya <note>vītaccikaṃviya (sī. pī.)</note> khāyati. Atha kho āyasmā ānando bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – ‘‘acchariyaṃ, bhante, abbhutaṃ, bhante, yāva parisuddho, bhante, tathāgatassa chavivaṇṇo pariyodāto. Idaṃ, bhante, siṅgīvaṇṇaṃ yugamaṭṭhaṃ dhāraṇīyaṃ bhagavato <pb ed="P" n="2.0134"/> kāyaṃ upanāmitaṃ hataccikaṃ viya khāyatī’’ti. ‘‘Evametaṃ, ānanda, evametaṃ, ānanda dvīsu kālesu ativiya tathāgatassa kāyo parisuddho hoti chavivaṇṇo pariyodāto. Katamesu dvīsu? Yañca, ānanda, rattiṃ tathāgato anuttaraṃ sammāsambodhiṃ abhisambujjhati, yañca rattiṃ anupādisesāya nibbānadhātuyā parinibbāyati. Imesu kho, ānanda, dvīsu kālesu ativiya tathāgatassa kāyo parisuddho hoti chavivaṇṇo pariyodāto. ‘‘Ajja kho, panānanda, rattiyā pacchime yāme kusinārāyaṃ upavattane mallānaṃ sālavane antarena <note>antare (syā.)</note> yamakasālānaṃ tathāgatassa parinibbānaṃ bhavissati <note>bhavissatīti (ka.)</note>. Āyāmānanda, yena kakudhā nadī tenupasaṅkamissāmā’’ti. ‘‘Evaṃ, bhante’’ti kho āyasmā ānando bhagavato paccassosi.</p> <p rend="gatha1">Siṅgīvaṇṇaṃ <pb ed="V" n="2.0102"/> yugamaṭṭhaṃ, pukkuso abhihārayi;</p> <pb ed="V" n="2.0102"/> <p rend="gathalast">Tena acchādito satthā, hemavaṇṇo asobhathāti.</p>
195. Then, soon after Pukkusa of the Malla clan had departed, the Venerable Ānanda arranged the set of golden-hued robes, burnished and ready for wear, about the body of the Blessed One. But when the set of robes was arranged upon the body of the Blessed One, it became as though faded, and its splendor dimmed. And the Venerable Ananda said to the Blessed One: “Marvellous it is, O Lord, most wonderful indeed it is, how clear and radiant the skin of the *Tathāgata* appears! This set of golden-hued robes, burnished and ready for wear, Lord, now that it is arranged upon the body of the Blessed One seems to have become faded, its splendor dimmed.”

“It is so, Ānanda. There are two times when the color of the *Tathāgata’s* skin is especially clear & bright. What are these two times? The night on which the *Tathāgata* awakens to the unsurpassed perfect self-awakening (*anuttaraṃ sammāsambodhiṃ abhisambujjhati*), and the night on which the *Tathāgata* attains final passing away into the state of *Nibbāna* in which no element of clinging remains (*anupādisesāya nibbānadhātuyā parinibbāyati*). On these two occasions the *Tathāgata’s* skin appears especially clear and bright.

"And now today, Ānanda, in the last watch of this very night, in the Mallas’ *Sāla* Grove, in the vicinity of Kusinara, between two *sala* trees, the *Tathāgata* will come to his *Parinibbāna*."

“Come, Ānanda, we will head for Kakudha River.”

“So be it, O Lord.” the Venerable Ānanda replied to the Blessed One.

The golden-hued, burnished set of robes, Pukkusa offered.

Covered by that, the Teacher, golden-colored, shone forth.
<p n="195" rend="bodytext"><hi rend="paranum">195</hi><hi rend="dot">.</hi><hi rend="bold">Bhagavato kāyaṃ upanāmita</hi>nti nivāsanapārupanavasena allīyāpitaṃ. Bhagavāpi tato ekaṃ nivāsesi, ekaṃ pārupi. <hi rend="bold">Hataccikaṃ viyā</hi>ti yathā hatacciko aṅgāro antanteneva jotati, bahi panassa pabhā natthi, evaṃ bahi paṭicchannappabhaṃ hutvā khāyatīti attho.</p> <p rend="bodytext"><hi rend="bold">Imesu kho, ānanda, dvīsupi kālesū</hi>ti kasmā imesu dvīsu kālesu evaṃ hoti? Āhāravisesena ceva balavasomanassena ca. Etesu hi dvīsu kālesu sakalacakkavāḷe devatā āhāre ojaṃ pakkhipanti, taṃ paṇītabhojanaṃ kucchiṃ pavisitvā pasannarūpaṃ samuṭṭhāpeti. Āhārasamuṭṭhānarūpassa pasannattā manacchaṭṭhāni indriyāni ativiya virocanti. Sambodhidivase cassa – ‘‘anekakappakoṭisatasahassasañcito vata me kilesarāsi ajja pahīno’’ti āvajjantassa balavasomanassaṃ uppajjati, cittaṃ pasīdati, citte pasanne lohitaṃ pasīdati, lohite pasanne manacchaṭṭhāni indriyāni ativiya virocanti. Parinibbānadivasepi – ‘‘ajja, dānāhaṃ, anekehi <pb ed="P" n="2.0571"/> buddhasatasahassehi paviṭṭhaṃ <hi rend="bold">amatamahānibbānaṃ</hi> nāma nagaraṃ pavisissāmī’’ti āvajjantassa <pb ed="V" n="2.0145"/> balavasomanassaṃ uppajjati, cittaṃ pasīdati, citte pasanne lohitaṃ pasīdati, lohite pasanne manacchaṭṭhāni indriyāni ativiya virocanti. Iti āhāravisesena ceva balavasomanassena ca imesu dvīsu kālesu evaṃ hotīti veditabbaṃ. <hi rend="bold">Upavattane</hi>ti pācīnato nivattanasālavane. <hi rend="bold">Antarena yamakasālāna</hi>nti yamakasālarukkhānaṃ majjhe.</p> <hi rend="bold">Imesu kho, ānanda, dvīsupi kālesū</hi> <pb ed="P" n="2.0571"/> <hi rend="bold">amatamahānibbānaṃ</hi> <pb ed="V" n="2.0145"/> <hi rend="bold">Upavattane</hi> <hi rend="bold">Antarena yamakasālāna</hi> <p rend="bodytext"><hi rend="bold">Siṅgīvaṇṇa</hi>nti gāthā saṅgītikāle ṭhapitā.</p> <hi rend="bold">Siṅgīvaṇṇa</hi>
195. *bhagavato kāyaṃ upanāmita* means closely adhered to, like clothing or covering.

The Blessed One also put on one (robe) and wore one.

*hataccikaṃ viyā* means just as a charcoal ember glows only inside, but its light is not visible outside, so it appears with its outer light covered. This is the meaning.

O Ānanda, *imesu kho, ānanda, dvīsupi kālesū*? Why is it like this at these two times? Because of the special food and the strong joy.

Indeed, at these two times, the deities in the entire world-system infuse energy into the food, and that excellent food, entering the stomach, produces a clear form.

Because of the clarity of the form produced by the food, the mind-based six senses shine exceedingly.

And on the day of enlightenment, thinking, "Today, my heap of defilements, accumulated over hundreds of thousands of millions of eons, has been eliminated," joy arises, the mind is clear, when the mind is clear, the blood is clear, when the blood is clear, the mind-based six senses shine exceedingly.

And even on the day of final emancipation, thinking, "Today, I, as a gift, will enter the city called *amatamahānibbāna*, which has been entered by hundreds of thousands of Buddhas," joy arises, the mind is clear, when the mind is clear, the blood is clear, when the blood is clear, the mind-based six senses shine exceedingly.

Thus, it should be understood that it is like this at these two times because of the special food and the strong joy.

*upavattane* means in the eastern Sāla forest of retreat.

*antarena yamakasālāna* means in the middle of the twin Sāla trees.

*imesu kho, ānanda, dvīsupi kālesū*
*amatamahānibbānaṃ*
*upavattane* *antarena yamakasālāna*
*siṅgīvaṇṇa* means the verse was established at the time of the Sangiti (council).

*siṅgīvaṇṇa*
196
<p n="196" rend="bodytext"><hi rend="paranum">196</hi><hi rend="dot">.</hi> Atha kho bhagavā mahatā bhikkhusaṅghena saddhiṃ yena kakudhā nadī tenupasaṅkami <pb ed="T" n="2.0157"/>; upasaṅkamitvā kakudhaṃ nadiṃ ajjhogāhetvā nhatvā ca pivitvā ca paccuttaritvā yena ambavanaṃ tenupasaṅkami. Upasaṅkamitvā āyasmantaṃ cundakaṃ āmantesi – ‘‘iṅgha me tvaṃ, cundaka, catugguṇaṃ saṅghāṭiṃ paññapehi, kilantosmi, cundaka, nipajjissāmī’’ti.</p> <p rend="bodytext">‘‘Evaṃ, bhante’’ti kho āyasmā cundako bhagavato paṭissutvā catugguṇaṃ saṅghāṭiṃ paññapesi. Atha kho bhagavā dakkhiṇena passena sīhaseyyaṃ kappesi pāde pādaṃ accādhāya sato sampajāno uṭṭhānasaññaṃ <pb ed="P" n="2.0135"/> manasikaritvā. Āyasmā pana cundako tattheva bhagavato purato nisīdi.</p> <pb ed="P" n="2.0135"/> <p rend="gatha1">Gantvāna <pb ed="M" n="2.0112"/> buddho nadikaṃ kakudhaṃ,</p> <pb ed="M" n="2.0112"/> <p rend="gatha2">Acchodakaṃ sātudakaṃ vippasannaṃ;</p> <p rend="gatha3">Ogāhi satthā akilantarūpo <note>sukilantarūpo (sī. pī.)</note>,</p> <note>sukilantarūpo (sī. pī.)</note> <p rend="gathalast">Tathāgato appaṭimo ca <note>appaṭimodha (pī.)</note> loke.</p> <note>appaṭimodha (pī.)</note> <p rend="gatha1">Nhatvā ca pivitvā cudatāri satthā <note>pivitvā cundakena, pivitvā ca uttari (ka.)</note>,</p> <note>pivitvā cundakena, pivitvā ca uttari (ka.)</note> <p rend="gatha2">Purakkhato bhikkhugaṇassa majjhe;</p> <p rend="gatha3">Vattā <note>satthā (sī. syā. pī.)</note> pavattā bhagavā idha dhamme,</p> <note>satthā (sī. syā. pī.)</note> <p rend="gathalast">Upāgami ambavanaṃ mahesi.</p> <p rend="gatha1">Āmantayi cundakaṃ nāma bhikkhuṃ,</p> <p rend="gatha2">Catugguṇaṃ <pb ed="T" n="2.0158"/> santhara me nipajjaṃ;</p> <pb ed="T" n="2.0158"/> <p rend="gatha3">So codito bhāvitattena cundo,</p> <p rend="gathalast">Catugguṇaṃ santhari khippameva.</p> <p rend="gatha1">Nipajji satthā akilantarūpo,</p> <p rend="gathalast">Cundopi tattha pamukhe <note>samukhe (ka.)</note> nisīdīti.</p> <note>samukhe (ka.)</note>
Then the Blessed One, together with a large community of monks, went to the Kakudha River; having arrived at the Kakudha River, he went down into the river, bathed, drank, and came back out, and then went to a mango grove. Having arrived there, he said to Venerable Cundaka, "Come, Cundaka, please arrange my outer robe folded in four, I am tired, Cundaka, I will lie down."

"As you say, Lord," Venerable Cundaka replied to the Blessed One, and arranged the outer robe folded in four.

Then the Blessed One lay down on his right side in the lion's posture, placing one foot on top of the other, mindful and fully aware, keeping in mind the thought of rising.

And Venerable Cundaka sat down right there in front of the Blessed One.

Having gone to the Kakudha River,
With its clear and pleasant water,
The teacher, tireless in form, entered it,
The Tathāgata, unparalleled in the world.

Having bathed and drunk, the teacher came out,
Surrounded by the community of monks;
The Blessed One, the speaker and initiator of the Dharma here,
Approached the mango grove, the great sage.

He addressed the monk named Cundaka,
"Fold a robe in four for me to lie down on";
Urged on by the well-developed one, Cunda,
Quickly spread out the four-folded robe.

The teacher, tireless in form, lay down,
And Cunda sat there in front of him.
<p n="196" rend="bodytext"><hi rend="paranum">196</hi><hi rend="dot">.</hi><hi rend="bold">Nhatvā</hi><pb ed="M" n="2.0162"/><hi rend="bold">ca pivitvā cā</hi>ti ettha tadā kira bhagavati nahāyante antonadiyaṃ macchakacchapā ca ubhatotīresu vanasaṇḍo ca sabbaṃ suvaṇṇavaṇṇameva hoti. <hi rend="bold">Ambavana</hi>nti tassāyeva nadiyā tīre ambavanaṃ. <hi rend="bold">Āyasmantaṃ cundaka</hi>nti tasmiṃ kira khaṇe ānandatthero udakasāṭakaṃ pīḷento ohīyi, cundatthero samīpe ahosi. Taṃ bhagavā āmantesi.</p> <p rend="bodytext"><hi rend="bold">Gantvāna buddho nadikaṃ kakudha</hi>nti imāpi gāthā saṅgītikāleyeva ṭhapitā. Tattha <hi rend="bold">pavattā bhagavā idha dhamme</hi>ti bhagavā idha sāsane dhamme pavattā, caturāsīti dhammakkhandhasahassāni pavattānīti attho. <hi rend="bold">Pamukhe nisīdī</hi>ti satthu puratova nisīdi. Ettāvatā ca thero anuppatto. Evaṃ anuppattaṃ atha kho bhagavā āyasmantaṃ ānandaṃ āmantesi.</p> <hi rend="bold">Gantvāna buddho nadikaṃ kakudha</hi> <hi rend="bold">pavattā bhagavā idha dhamme</hi> <hi rend="bold">Pamukhe nisīdī</hi>
196.
Having slain, and having drunk, it was like this: At that time, when the Fortunate One was bathing in the inner river, the fish and turtles, and the forest clumps on both banks, all became of golden color.

"Mango grove": On the bank of that very river was a mango grove.

"Venerable Cundaka": At that moment, Venerable Ānanda, squeezing his water garment, stepped aside, and Venerable Cunda was near.

The Fortunate One addressed him.

Having gone, the Buddha [to] the river Kakudha, these verses were established at the time of the Saṅgīti.

There, "The Fortunate One promulgates the Dharma here": The Fortunate One promulgates the Dharma here in the dispensation. The meaning is that eighty-four thousand aggregates of the Dharma were promulgated.

"He sat in front": He sat right in front of the Teacher.

By this much, the Elder had arrived.

Having thus arrived, then the Fortunate One addressed Venerable Ānanda.

Having gone, the Buddha [to] the river Kakudha, the Fortunate One promulgates the Dharma here, he sat in front.
197
<p n="197" rend="bodytext"><hi rend="paranum">197</hi><hi rend="dot">.</hi> Atha kho bhagavā āyasmantaṃ ānandaṃ āmantesi – ‘‘siyā kho <note>yo kho (ka.)</note>, panānanda, cundassa <pb ed="V" n="2.0103"/> kammāraputtassa koci vippaṭisāraṃ uppādeyya – ‘tassa te, āvuso cunda, alābhā tassa te dulladdhaṃ, yassa te tathāgato pacchimaṃ piṇḍapātaṃ paribhuñjitvā parinibbuto’ti. Cundassa, ānanda, kammāraputtassa evaṃ vippaṭisāro paṭivinetabbo – ‘tassa te, āvuso cunda, lābhā tassa te suladdhaṃ, yassa te tathāgato pacchimaṃ piṇḍapātaṃ paribhuñjitvā parinibbuto. Sammukhā metaṃ, āvuso cunda, bhagavato sutaṃ sammukhā paṭiggahitaṃ – dve me piṇḍapātā samasamaphalā <pb ed="P" n="2.0136"/><note>samā samaphalā (ka.)</note> samavipākā <note>samasamavipākā (sī. syā. pī.)</note>, ativiya aññehi piṇḍapātehi mahapphalatarā ca mahānisaṃsatarā ca. Katame dve? Yañca piṇḍapātaṃ paribhuñjitvā tathāgato anuttaraṃ sammāsambodhiṃ abhisambujjhati, yañca piṇḍapātaṃ paribhuñjitvā tathāgato anupādisesāya nibbānadhātuyā parinibbāyati. Ime dve piṇḍapātā samasamaphalā samavipākā <pb ed="M" n="2.0113"/>, ativiya aññehi piṇḍapātehi mahapphalatarā ca mahānisaṃsatarā ca. Āyusaṃvattanikaṃ āyasmatā cundena kammāraputtena kammaṃ upacitaṃ, vaṇṇasaṃvattanikaṃ āyasmatā cundena kammāraputtena kammaṃ upacitaṃ, sukhasaṃvattanikaṃ āyasmatā cundena kammāraputtena kammaṃ upacitaṃ, yasasaṃvattanikaṃ āyasmatā cundena kammāraputtena kammaṃ upacitaṃ, saggasaṃvattanikaṃ <pb ed="T" n="2.0159"/> āyasmatā cundena kammāraputtena kammaṃ upacitaṃ, ādhipateyyasaṃvattanikaṃ āyasmatā cundena kammāraputtena kammaṃ upacita’nti. Cundassa, ānanda, kammāraputtassa evaṃ vippaṭisāro paṭivinetabbo’’ti. Atha kho bhagavā etamatthaṃ viditvā tāyaṃ velāyaṃ imaṃ udānaṃ udānesi –</p> <p rend="gatha1">‘‘Dadato puññaṃ pavaḍḍhati,</p> <p rend="gatha2">Saṃyamato veraṃ na cīyati;</p> <p rend="gatha3">Kusalo ca jahāti pāpakaṃ,</p> <p rend="gathalast">Rāgadosamohakkhayā sanibbuto’’ti.</p> <p rend="centre">Catuttho bhāṇavāro.</p> <p rend="subhead">Yamakasālā</p>
197. Then the Blessed One addressed the Venerable Ānanda, saying: "It may come to pass, Ānanda, that someone will cause remorse to Cunda the metalworker, saying: ‘It is no gain to you, friend Cunda, but a loss, that it was from you the *Tathāgata* took his last alms meal, and then came to his end.’

"In this way, Ānanda, the remorse of Cunda the metalworker should be dispelled: ‘It is a gain to you, friend Cunda, a blessing that the *Tathāgata* took his last alms meal from you, and then came to his end.

"For, friend Cunda, I have heard and understood from the Lord’s own lips that these two alms-givings are of very great fruit, of very great result, more fruitful and advantageous than any other.

"Which two? There is that alms offering which when a *Tathāgata* has eaten he attains unsurpassed, supreme Enlightenment (*sammāsambodhi*), and that which when he has eaten he attains final *Nibbāna* in the *Nibbāna*-element (*nibbānadhātu*) that has no substrate remaining for further existence.

"These two alms-givings are more fruitful and profitable than all others.

"By his deed the worthy Cunda has accumulated *karma* (*kamma*) which makes for long life, beauty, well being, glory, heavenly rebirth, and sovereignty.”

"In this way, Ānanda, Cunda the metalworker’s remorse should be allayed.”

Then, the Blessed One, having understood the matter, on that occasion, uttered this inspired utterance (*udāna*):

“Generosity increases merit (*puñña*);
Restraint does not generate enmity (*vera*);
The skillful abandon evil;
With the destruction of *rāga*, *dosa*, and *moha*, one is at peace (*sanibbuto*).”

The fourth chapter on recitation.

The Twin Sala Trees.
<p n="197" rend="bodytext"><hi rend="paranum">197</hi><hi rend="dot">.</hi><hi rend="bold">Alābhā</hi>ti ye aññesaṃ dānānisaṃsasaṅkhātā lābhā honti, te alābhā. <hi rend="bold">Dulladdha</hi>nti puññavisesena laddhampi manussattaṃ dulladdhaṃ. <hi rend="bold">Yassa te</hi>ti yassa tava. Uttaṇḍulaṃ vā atikilinnaṃ vā ko jānāti, kīdisampi pacchimaṃ piṇḍapātaṃ paribhuñjitvā tathāgato parinibbuto, addhā te yaṃ vā taṃ vā dinnaṃ bhavissatīti. <hi rend="bold">Lābhā</hi>ti diṭṭhadhammikasamparāyikadānānisaṃsasaṅkhātā lābhā. <hi rend="bold">Suladdha</hi>nti tuyhaṃ manussattaṃ suladdhaṃ. <hi rend="bold">Samasamaphalā</hi>ti sabbākārena samānaphalā.</p> <p rend="bodytext">Nanu ca yaṃ sujātāya dinnaṃ piṇḍapātaṃ bhuñjitvā tathāgato abhisambuddho, so sarāgasadosasamohakāle paribhutto, ayaṃ pana cundena dinno vītarāgavītadosavītamohakāle paribhutto, kasmā ete samaphalāti? Parinibbānasamatāya ca samāpattisamatāya ca anussaraṇasamatāya ca. Bhagavā <pb ed="P" n="2.0572"/> hi sujātāya dinnaṃ piṇḍapātaṃ paribhuñjitvā saupādisesāya nibbānadhātuyā parinibbuto, cundena dinnaṃ paribhuñjitvā anupādisesāya nibbānadhātuyā parinibbutoti evaṃ <hi rend="bold">parinibbānasamatāya</hi>pi samaphalā. Abhisambujjhanadivase ca catuvīsatikoṭisatasahassasaṅkhyā <pb ed="V" n="2.0146"/> samāpattiyo samāpajji, parinibbānadivasepi sabbā tā samāpajjīti evaṃ <hi rend="bold">samāpattisamatāyapi</hi> samaphalā. Sujātā ca aparabhāge assosi – ‘‘na kiresā rukkhadevatā, bodhisatto kiresa, taṃ kira piṇḍapātaṃ paribhuñjitvā anuttaraṃ sammāsambodhiṃ abhisambuddho <pb ed="M" n="2.0163"/>, sattasattāhaṃ kirassa tena yāpanaṃ ahosī’’ti. Tassā idaṃ sutvā – ‘‘lābhā vata me’’ti anussarantiyā balavapītisomanassaṃ udapādi. Cundassāpi aparabhāge – ‘‘avasānapiṇḍapāto kira mayā dinno, dhammasīsaṃ kira me gahitaṃ, mayhaṃ kira piṇḍapātaṃ paribhuñjitvā satthā anupādisesāya nibbānadhātuyā parinibbuto’’ti sutvā ‘‘lābhā vata me’’ti anussarato balavasomanassaṃ udapādīti evaṃ <hi rend="bold">anussaraṇasamatāya</hi>pi samaphalāti veditabbā.</p> <pb ed="P" n="2.0572"/> <hi rend="bold">parinibbānasamatāya</hi> <pb ed="V" n="2.0146"/> <hi rend="bold">samāpattisamatāyapi</hi> <pb ed="M" n="2.0163"/> <hi rend="bold">anussaraṇasamatāya</hi> <p rend="bodytext"><hi rend="bold">Yasasaṃvattanika</hi>nti parivārasaṃvattanikaṃ. <hi rend="bold">Ādhipateyyasaṃvattanika</hi>nti jeṭṭhakabhāvasaṃvattanikaṃ.</p> <hi rend="bold">Yasasaṃvattanika</hi> <hi rend="bold">Ādhipateyyasaṃvattanika</hi> <p rend="bodytext"><hi rend="bold">Saṃyamato</hi>ti sīlasaṃyamena saṃyamantassa, saṃvare ṭhitassāti attho. <hi rend="bold">Veraṃ na cīyatī</hi>ti pañcavidhaṃ veraṃ na vaḍḍhati. <hi rend="bold">Kusalo ca jahāti pāpaka</hi>nti kusalo pana ñāṇasampanno ariyamaggena anavasesaṃ pāpakaṃ lāmakaṃ akusalaṃ jahāti. <hi rend="bold">Rāgadosamohakkhayā sa nibbuto</hi>ti so imaṃ pāpakaṃ jahitvā rāgādīnaṃ khayā kilesanibbānena nibbutoti. Iti cundassa ca dakkhiṇaṃ, attano ca dakkhiṇeyyasampattiṃ sampassamāno udānaṃ udānesīti.</p> <hi rend="bold">Saṃyamato</hi> <hi rend="bold">Veraṃ na cīyatī</hi> <hi rend="bold">Kusalo ca jahāti pāpaka</hi> <hi rend="bold">Rāgadosamohakkhayā sa nibbuto</hi> <p rend="centre">Catutthabhāṇavāravaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.</p> <p rend="subhead">Yamakasālāvaṇṇanā</p>
197. *Alābhā*: "non-gains," meaning those gains that are accounted as benefits of giving (dāna) to others are, in fact, non-gains.
*Dulladdha*: "ill-obtained," meaning that even a human existence obtained through the power of merit (*puṇya*) is ill-obtained.
*Yassa te*: "whose is yours," meaning "whose is thine."
Who knows whether it was hulled or over-soaked, the last alms-food (*piṇḍapāta*) that the *Tathāgata* ate before attaining complete extinction (*parinibbāna*)? Assuredly, whatever was given to you will come to pass.
*Lābhā*: "gains," meaning those gains that are accounted as the benefits of giving ( *dāna*) in this life and the next.
*Suladdha*: "well-obtained," meaning this human existence of yours is well-obtained.
*Samasamaphalā*: "equally equal result," meaning results equal in every way.

Now, the alms-food (*piṇḍapāta*) that was given to Sujātā, which the *Tathāgata* ate and attained complete enlightenment (*abhisambuddho*), was enjoyed during a time of passion (*sarāga*), hatred (*dosa*), and delusion (*moha*). But this alms-food that was given by Cunda was enjoyed during a time devoid of passion (*vītarāga*), devoid of hatred (*vītadosa*), and devoid of delusion (*vītamoha*). Why are these results equal? [They are equal] because of the equality of final extinction (*parinibbānasamatā*), the equality of attainments (*samāpattisamatā*), and the equality of remembrance (*anussaraṇasamatā*).

The Blessed One (*bhagavā*), having eaten the alms-food (*piṇḍapāta*) given by Sujātā and attained complete extinction (*parinibbuto*) with a remainder of the substrata (*saupādisesāya nibbānadhātuyā*), and having eaten the alms-food given by Cunda and attained complete extinction (*parinibbuto*) without a remainder of the substrata (*anupādisesāya nibbānadhātuyā*), thus, the equality of final extinction (*parinibbānasamatā*) is also an equal result.
On the day of complete enlightenment (*abhisambujjhanadivase*) and having attained countless (*catuvīsatikoṭisatasahassasaṅkhyā*) meditative attainments (*samāpatti*), on the day of final extinction (*parinibbānadivase*) also, all those [attainments] were attained. Thus, the equality of attainments (*samāpattisamatā*) is also an equal result.
Sujātā, at another time, heard – "This is not a tree deity (*rukkhadevatā*); this is a *bodhisattva*. Having eaten this alms-food (*piṇḍapāta*), he has attained unsurpassed complete perfect enlightenment (*anuttaraṃ sammāsambodhiṃ*), and for seven weeks he lived on that."
Having heard this, she remembered – "Gains to me indeed!", and a strong joy and gladness (*balavapītisomanassaṃ*) arose.
To Cunda also, at another time – "The final alms-food (*piṇḍapāta*) was given by me; the head of the *Dharma* was taken by me; having eaten the alms-food from me, the Teacher (*satthā*) attained complete extinction (*parinibbuto*) without a remainder of the substrata (*anupādisesāya nibbānadhātuyā*)," having heard this, he remembered – "Gains to me indeed!", and a strong gladness (*balavasomanassaṃ*) arose. Thus, it should be understood that the equality of remembrance (*anussaraṇasamatā*) is also an equal result.

*Parinibbānasamatāya*. *Samāpattisamatāyapi*. *Anussaraṇasamatāya*.
*Yasasaṃvattanika* means conducive to retinue (*parivārasaṃvattanikaṃ*).
*ādhipateyyasaṃvattanika* means conducive to chieftainship (*jeṭṭhakabhāvasaṃvattanikaṃ*).

*Yasasaṃvattanika*. *ādhipateyyasaṃvattanika*.
*Saṃyamato* means for one who is restrained by the restraint of morality (*sīlasaṃyamena saṃyamantassa*), for one established in restraint (*saṃvare ṭhitassāti attho*).
*Veraṃ na cīyatī* means five kinds of enmity (*pañcavidhaṃ veraṃ*) do not increase (*na vaḍḍhati*).
*Kusalo ca jahāti pāpaka* means the skillful one (*kusalo*), the one endowed with wisdom (*ñāṇasampanno*), by means of the noble path (*ariyamaggena*), abandons completely (*anavasesaṃ*) evil (*pāpakaṃ*), base (*lāmakaṃ*), unskillful (*akusalaṃ*).
*Rāgadosamohakkhayā sa nibbuto* means he, having abandoned this evil (*pāpakaṃ jahitvā*) by means of the destruction of passion (*rāga*), etc., is extinguished (*nibbuto*) by the extinction of defilements (*kilesanibbānena*).

Thus, Cunda's giving (*dakkhiṇaṃ*), and he himself, seeing the accomplishment of worthy recipients (*dakkhiṇeyyasampattiṃ sampassamāno*), uttered an exclamation of joy (*udānaṃ udānesīti*).

*Saṃyamato*. *Veraṃ na cīyatī*. *Kusalo ca jahāti pāpaka*. *Rāgadosamohakkhayā sa nibbuto*.
The commentary on the fourth division for recitation is finished.

Explanation of the Yamaka Sala.
198
<p n="198" rend="bodytext"><hi rend="paranum">198</hi><hi rend="dot">.</hi> Atha <pb ed="P" n="2.0137"/> kho bhagavā āyasmantaṃ ānandaṃ āmantesi – ‘‘āyāmānanda, yena hiraññavatiyā nadiyā pārimaṃ tīraṃ, yena kusinārā upavattanaṃ mallānaṃ sālavanaṃ tenupasaṅkamissāmā’’ti <pb ed="V" n="2.0104"/>. ‘‘Evaṃ, bhante’’ti kho āyasmā ānando bhagavato paccassosi. Atha kho bhagavā mahatā bhikkhusaṅghena saddhiṃ yena hiraññavatiyā nadiyā pārimaṃ tīraṃ, yena kusinārā upavattanaṃ mallānaṃ sālavanaṃ tenupasaṅkami. Upasaṅkamitvā āyasmantaṃ ānandaṃ āmantesi – ‘‘iṅgha me tvaṃ, ānanda, antarena yamakasālānaṃ uttarasīsakaṃ mañcakaṃ paññapehi, kilantosmi, ānanda, nipajjissāmī’’ti. ‘‘Evaṃ, bhante’’ti kho āyasmā ānando bhagavato paṭissutvā antarena yamakasālānaṃ uttarasīsakaṃ mañcakaṃ paññapesi. Atha kho bhagavā dakkhiṇena passena sīhaseyyaṃ kappesi pāde <pb ed="T" n="2.0160"/> pādaṃ accādhāya sato sampajāno.</p> <p rend="bodytext">Tena <pb ed="M" n="2.0114"/> kho pana samayena yamakasālā sabbaphāliphullā honti akālapupphehi. Te tathāgatassa sarīraṃ okiranti ajjhokiranti abhippakiranti tathāgatassa pūjāya. Dibbānipi mandāravapupphāni antalikkhā papatanti, tāni tathāgatassa sarīraṃ okiranti ajjhokiranti abhippakiranti tathāgatassa pūjāya. Dibbānipi candanacuṇṇāni antalikkhā papatanti, tāni tathāgatassa sarīraṃ okiranti <pb ed="P" n="2.0138"/> ajjhokiranti abhippakiranti tathāgatassa pūjāya. Dibbānipi tūriyāni antalikkhe vajjanti tathāgatassa pūjāya. Dibbānipi saṅgītāni antalikkhe vattanti tathāgatassa pūjāya.</p> <pb ed="M" n="2.0114"/> <pb ed="P" n="2.0138"/>
198. Then the Blessed One addressed the Venerable Ānanda, saying: “Come, Ānanda, let us cross to the farther bank of the Hiraññavatī River, and go to the Mallas’ Sāla Grove, in the vicinity of Kusinārā.”

“So be it, Lord.” And the Venerable Ānanda answered the Blessed One.

Then the Blessed One with a large *Saṅgha* of monks went to the far shore of the Hiraññavatī River, to Upavattana, the Mallans’ Sal Forest near Kusinārā.

On arrival, he said to Ven. Ānanda, “Please, Ānanda, prepare for me a couch between the twin *yamaka-sāla* trees, with the head to the north. I am weary, Ānanda, and want to lie down.”

“So be it, Lord.” And the Venerable Ānanda, having promised the Blessed One, prepared a bed between the twin *yamaka-sāla* trees, with its head to the north.

Then the Fortunate One lay down on his right side in the lion’s posture, after placing one foot on the top of the other, mindfully, with full awareness.

Now at that time the Twin Sal Trees were full of flowering blossoms, outside of flowering time.

They shower, strew, & sprinkle on the *Tathāgata’s* body in homage to him.

Heavenly coral-tree blossoms fell from the sky, showering, strewing, & sprinkling the *Tathāgata’s* body in homage to him.

divine sandal-wood powder fell from the sky, sprinkling and covering the *Tathāgata’s* body in homage.

Heavenly music was playing in the sky, in homage to the *Tathāgata*.

Heavenly songs were sung in the sky, in homage to the *Tathāgata*.
<p n="198" rend="bodytext"><hi rend="paranum">198</hi><hi rend="dot">.</hi><hi rend="bold">Mahatā bhikkhusaṅghena saddhi</hi>nti idha bhikkhūnaṃ gaṇanaparicchedo natthi. Veḷuvagāme vedanāvikkhambhanato paṭṭhāya hi – ‘‘na cirena bhagavā parinibbāyissatī’’ti sutvā tato tato āgatesu bhikkhūsu ekabhikkhupi pakkanto nāma natthi. Tasmā gaṇanavītivatto saṅgho ahosi. <hi rend="bold">Upavattanaṃ mallānaṃ sālavana</hi>nti yatheva hi kalambanadītīrato rājamātuvihāradvārena thūpārāmaṃ gantabbaṃ <pb ed="P" n="2.0573"/> hoti, evaṃ hiraññavatiyā pārimatīrato sālavanuyyānaṃ, yathā anurādhapurassa thūpārāmo, evaṃ taṃ kusinārāyaṃ hoti. Yathā thūpārāmato dakkhiṇadvārena nagaraṃ pavisanamaggo pācīnamukho <pb ed="V" n="2.0147"/> gantvā uttarena nivatto, evaṃ uyyānato sālavanaṃ pācīnamukhaṃ gantvā uttarena nivattaṃ. Tasmā taṃ – ‘‘upavattana’’nti vuccati. <hi rend="bold">Antarena yamakasālānaṃ</hi><pb ed="M" n="2.0164"/><hi rend="bold">uttarasīsaka</hi>nti tassa kira mañcakassa ekā sālapanti sīsabhāge hoti, ekā pādabhāge. Tatrāpi eko taruṇasālo sīsabhāgassa āsanno hoti, eko pādabhāgassa. Api ca <hi rend="bold">yamakasālā</hi> nāma mūlakhandhaviṭapapattehi aññamaññaṃ saṃsibbitvā ṭhitasālāti vuttaṃ. <hi rend="bold">Mañcakaṃ paññapehī</hi>ti tasmiṃ kira uyyāne rājakulassa sayanamañco atthi, taṃ sandhāya paññapehīti āha. Theropi taṃyeva paññapetvā adāsi.</p> <p rend="bodytext"><hi rend="bold">Kilantosmi, ānanda, nipajjissāmī</hi>ti tathāgatassa hi –</p> <hi rend="bold">Kilantosmi, ānanda, nipajjissāmī</hi> <p rend="gatha1">‘‘Gocari kaḷāpo gaṅgeyyo, piṅgalo pabbateyyako;</p> <p rend="gatha2">Hemavato ca tambo ca, mandākini uposatho;</p> <p rend="gathalast">Chaddantoyeva dasamo, ete nāgānamuttamā’’ti. –</p> <p rend="bodytext">Ettha yaṃ dasannaṃ gocarisaṅkhātānaṃ pakatihatthīnaṃ balaṃ, taṃ ekassa kaḷāpassāti. Evaṃ dasaguṇavaḍḍhitāya gaṇanāya pakatihatthīnaṃ koṭisahassabalappamāṇaṃ balaṃ, taṃ sabbampi cundassa piṇḍapātaṃ paribhuttakālato paṭṭhāya caṅgavāre pakkhittaudakaṃ viya parikkhayaṃ gataṃ. Pāvānagarato tīṇi gāvutāni kusinārānagaraṃ, etasmiṃ antare pañcavīsatiyā ṭhānesu nisīditvā mahatā ussāhena āgacchantopi sūriyassa atthaṅgamitavelāyaṃ sañjhāsamaye bhagavā sālavanaṃ paviṭṭho. Evaṃ rogo sabbaṃ ārogyaṃ maddanto āgacchati. Etamatthaṃ dassento viya sabbalokassa saṃvegakaraṃ vācaṃ bhāsanto – ‘‘kilantosmi, ānanda, nipajjissāmī’’ti āha.</p> <p rend="bodytext">Kasmā pana bhagavā evaṃ mahantena ussāhena idhāgato, kiṃ aññattha na sakkā parinibbāyitunti? Parinibbāyituṃ nāma na katthaci na sakkā, tīhi pana kāraṇehi idhāgato, idañhi bhagavā evaṃ passati – ‘‘mayi aññattha parinibbāyante mahāsudassanasuttassa atthuppatti na bhavissati, kusinārāyaṃ <pb ed="P" n="2.0574"/> pana parinibbāyante yamahaṃ devaloke anubhavitabbaṃ sampattiṃ manussalokeyeva anubhaviṃ, taṃ dvīhi bhāṇavārehi maṇḍetvā desessāmi, taṃ me sutvā bahū janā kusalaṃ kātabbaṃ maññissantī’’ti.</p> <pb ed="P" n="2.0574"/> <p rend="bodytext">Aparampi <pb ed="M" n="2.0165"/> passati – ‘‘maṃ aññattha parinibbāyantaṃ subhaddo na passissati, so ca buddhaveneyyo <pb ed="V" n="2.0148"/>, na sāvakaveneyyo; na taṃ sāvakā vinetuṃ sakkonti. Kusinārāyaṃ parinibbāyantaṃ pana maṃ so upasaṅkamitvā pañhaṃ pucchissati, pañhāvissajjanapariyosāne ca saraṇesu patiṭṭhāya mama santike pabbajjañca upasampadañca labhitvā kammaṭṭhānaṃ gahetvā mayi dharamāneyeva arahattaṃ patvā pacchimasāvako bhavissatī’’ti.</p> <pb ed="M" n="2.0165"/> <pb ed="V" n="2.0148"/> <p rend="bodytext">Aparampi passati – ‘‘mayi aññattha parinibbāyante dhātubhājanīye mahākalaho bhavissati, lohitaṃ nadī viya sandissati. Kusinārāyaṃ parinibbute doṇabrāhmaṇo taṃ vivādaṃ vūpasametvā dhātuyo vibhajissatī’’ti. Imehi tīhi kāraṇehi bhagavā evaṃ mahantena ussāhena idhāgatoti veditabbo.</p> <p rend="bodytext"><hi rend="bold">Sīhaseyya</hi>nti ettha kāmabhogīseyyā, petaseyyā, sīhaseyyā, tathāgataseyyāti catasso seyyā.</p> <hi rend="bold">Sīhaseyya</hi> <p rend="bodytext">Tattha – ‘‘yebhuyyena, bhikkhave, kāmabhogī sattā vāmena passena sentī’’ti ayaṃ <hi rend="bold">kāmabhogīseyyā.</hi> Tesu hi yebhuyyena dakkhiṇena passena sayantā nāma natthi.</p> <hi rend="bold">kāmabhogīseyyā.</hi> <p rend="bodytext">‘‘Yebhuyyena, bhikkhave, petā uttānā sentī’’ti ayaṃ <hi rend="bold">petaseyyā.</hi> Appamaṃsalohitattā hi petā aṭṭhisaṅghāṭajaṭitā ekena passena sayituṃ na sakkonti, uttānāva senti.</p> <hi rend="bold">petaseyyā.</hi> <p rend="bodytext">‘‘Sīho, bhikkhave, migarājā dakkhiṇena passena seyyaṃ kappeti…pe… attamano hotī’’ti (a. ni. 4.246) ayaṃ <hi rend="bold">sīhaseyyā.</hi> Tejussadattā hi sīho migarājā dve purimapāde ekasmiṃ ṭhāne, pacchimapāde ekasmiṃ ṭhāne ṭhapetvā naṅguṭṭhaṃ antarasatthimhi pakkhipitvā purimapādapacchimapādanaṅguṭṭhānaṃ ṭhitokāsaṃ sallakkhetvā dvinnaṃ purimapādānaṃ matthake sīsaṃ ṭhapetvā sayati. Divasaṃ sayitvāpi pabujjhamāno na utrasanto pabujjhati, sīsaṃ pana ukkhipitvā purimapādādīnaṃ ṭhitokāsaṃ sallakkheti. Sace kiñci ṭhānaṃ vijahitvā ṭhitaṃ hoti – ‘‘na yidaṃ tuyhaṃ jātiyā sūrabhāvassa ca anurūpa’’nti anattamano hutvā tattheva sayati, na gocarāya pakkamati. Avijahitvā ṭhite pana <pb ed="P" n="2.0575"/> – ‘‘tuyhaṃ jātiyā ca sūrabhāvassa ca anurūpamida’’nti haṭṭhatuṭṭho uṭṭhāya sīhavijambhitaṃ <pb ed="M" n="2.0166"/> vijambhitvā kesarabhāraṃ vidhunitvā tikkhattuṃ sīhanādaṃ naditvā gocarāya pakkamati.</p> <hi rend="bold">sīhaseyyā.</hi> <pb ed="P" n="2.0575"/> <pb ed="M" n="2.0166"/> <p rend="bodytext">‘‘Catutthajjhānaseyyā <pb ed="V" n="2.0149"/> pana <hi rend="bold">tathāgatassa seyyā</hi>ti vuccati’’ (a. ni. 4.246). Tāsu idha sīhaseyyā āgatā. Ayañhi tejussadairiyāpathattā uttamaseyyā nāma.</p> <pb ed="V" n="2.0149"/> <hi rend="bold">tathāgatassa seyyā</hi> <p rend="bodytext"><hi rend="bold">Pāde pāda</hi>nti dakkhiṇapāde vāmapādaṃ. <hi rend="bold">Accādhāyā</hi>ti atiādhāya, īsakaṃ atikkamma ṭhapetvā. Gopphakena hi gopphake, jāṇunā vā jāṇumhi saṅghaṭṭiyamāne abhiṇhaṃ vedanā uppajjati, cittaṃ ekaggaṃ na hoti, seyyā aphāsukā hoti. Yathā pana na saṅghaṭṭeti, evaṃ atikkamma ṭhapite vedanā nuppajjati, cittaṃ ekaggaṃ hoti, seyyā phāsu hoti. Tasmā evaṃ nipajji. Anuṭṭhānaseyyaṃ upagatattā panettha – ‘‘uṭṭhānasaññaṃ manasi karitvā’’ti na vuttaṃ. Kāyavasena cettha anuṭṭhānaṃ veditabbaṃ, niddāvasena pana taṃ rattiṃ bhagavato bhavaṅgassa okāsoyeva nāhosi. Paṭhamayāmasmiñhi mallānaṃ dhammadesanā ahosi, majjhimayāme subhaddassa pacchimayāme bhikkhusaṅghaṃ ovadi, balavapaccūse parinibbāyi.</p> <hi rend="bold">Pāde pāda</hi> <hi rend="bold">Accādhāyā</hi> <p rend="bodytext"><hi rend="bold">Sabbaphāliphullā</hi>ti sabbe samantato pupphitā mūlato paṭṭhāya yāva aggā ekacchannā ahesuṃ, na kevalañca yamakasālāyeva, sabbepi rukkhā sabbapāliphullāva ahesuṃ. Na kevalañhi tasmiṃyeva uyyāne, sakalañhipi dasasahassacakkavāḷe pupphūpagā pupphaṃ gaṇhiṃsu, phalūpagā phalaṃ gaṇhiṃsu, sabbarukkhānaṃ khandhesu khandhapadumāni, sākhāsu sākhāpadumāni, vallīsu vallipadumāni, ākāsesu ākāsapadumāni pathavītalaṃ bhinditvā daṇḍapadumāni pupphiṃsu. Sabbo mahāsamuddo pañcavaṇṇapadumasañchanno ahosi.
