Tiyojanasahassavitthato himavā ghanabaddhamorapiñchakalāpo viya, nirantaraṃ mālādāmagavacchiko viya, suṭṭhu pīḷetvā ābaddhapupphavaṭaṃsako viya, supūritaṃ pupphacaṅkoṭakaṃ viya ca atiramaṇīyo ahosi.</p> <hi rend="bold">Sabbaphāliphullā</hi> <p rend="bodytext"><hi rend="bold">Te tathāgatassa sarīraṃ okirantī</hi>ti te yamakasālā bhummadevatāhi sañcalitakhandhasākhaviṭapā tathāgatassa sarīraṃ avakiranti, sarīrassa upari pupphāni vikirantīti attho. <hi rend="bold">Ajjhokirantī</hi>ti ajjhottharantā viya kiranti. <hi rend="bold">Abhippakirantī</hi>ti abhiṇhaṃ punappunaṃ pakirantiyeva. <hi rend="bold">Dibbānī</hi>ti <pb ed="M" n="2.0167"/> devaloke nandapokkharaṇīsambhavāni, tāni honti <pb ed="P" n="2.0576"/> suvaṇṇavaṇṇāni paṇṇacchattappamāṇapattāni, mahātumbamattaṃ reṇuṃ gaṇhanti. Na kevalañca mandāravapupphāneva, aññānipi pana dibbāni pāricchattakakoviḷārapupphādīni suvaṇṇacaṅkoṭakāni pūretvā cakkavāḷamukhavaṭṭiyampi tidasapurepi brahmalokepi ṭhitāhi devatāhi paviṭṭhāni, antalikkhā patanti. <hi rend="bold">Tathāgatassa sarīra</hi>nti antarā avikiṇṇāneva āgantvā pattakiñjakkhareṇucuṇṇehi tathāgatassa sarīrameva okiranti.</p> <hi rend="bold">Te tathāgatassa sarīraṃ okirantī</hi> <hi rend="bold">Ajjhokirantī</hi> <hi rend="bold">Abhippakirantī</hi> <hi rend="bold">Dibbānī</hi> <pb ed="M" n="2.0167"/> <pb ed="P" n="2.0576"/> <hi rend="bold">Tathāgatassa sarīra</hi> <p rend="bodytext"><hi rend="bold">Dibbānipi</hi><pb ed="V" n="2.0150"/><hi rend="bold">candanacuṇṇānī</hi>ti devatānaṃ upakappanacandanacuṇṇāni. Na kevalañca devatānaṃyeva, nāgasupaṇṇamanussānampi upakappanacandanacuṇṇāni. Na kevalañca candanacuṇṇāneva, kāḷānusārikalohitacandanādisabbadibbagandhajālacuṇṇāni, haritālaañjanasuvaṇṇarajatacuṇṇāni sabbadibbagandhavāsavikatiyo suvaṇṇarajatādisamugge pūretvā cakkavāḷamukhavaṭṭiādīsu ṭhitāhi devatāhi paviṭṭhāni antarā avippakiritvā tathāgatasseva sarīraṃ okiranti.</p> <hi rend="bold">Dibbānipi</hi> <pb ed="V" n="2.0150"/> <hi rend="bold">candanacuṇṇānī</hi> <p rend="bodytext"><hi rend="bold">Dibbānipi tūriyānī</hi>ti devatānaṃ upakappanatūriyāni. Na kevalañca tāniyeva, sabbānipi tantibaddhacammapariyonaddhaghanasusirabhedāni dasasahassacakkavāḷesu devanāgasupaṇṇamanussānaṃ tūriyāni ekacakkavāḷe sannipatitvā antalikkhe vajjantīti veditabbāni.</p> <hi rend="bold">Dibbānipi tūriyānī</hi> <p rend="bodytext"><hi rend="bold">Dibbānipi saṅgītānī</hi>ti varuṇavāraṇadevatā kira nāmetā dīghāyukā devatā – ‘‘mahāpuriso manussapathe nibbattitvā buddho bhavissatī’’ti sutvā ‘‘paṭisandhiggahaṇadivase naṃ gahetvā gamissāmā’’ti mālaṃ ganthetumārabhiṃsu. Tā ganthamānāva – ‘‘mahāpuriso mātukucchiyaṃ nibbatto’’ti sutvā ‘‘tumhe kassa ganthathā’’ti vuttā ‘‘na tāva niṭṭhāti, kucchito nikkhamanadivase gaṇhitvā gamissāmā’’ti āhaṃsu. Punapi ‘‘nikkhanto’’ti sutvā ‘‘mahābhinikkhamanadivase gamissāmā’’ti. Ekūnatiṃsavassāni ghare vasitvā ‘‘ajja mahābhinikkhamanaṃ nikkhanto’’tipi sutvā ‘‘abhisambodhidivase gamissāmā’’ti. Chabbassāni padhānaṃ katvā ‘‘ajja abhisambuddho’’tipi sutvā ‘‘dhammacakkappavattanadivase gamissāmā’’ti. ‘‘Sattasattāhāni bodhimaṇḍe vītināmetvā <pb ed="P" n="2.0577"/> isipatanaṃ gantvā dhammacakkaṃ pavattita’’ntipi sutvā ‘‘yamakapāṭihāriyadivase gamissāmā’’ti. ‘‘Ajja yamakapāṭihāriyaṃ karī’’tipi <pb ed="M" n="2.0168"/> sutvā ‘‘devorohaṇadivase gamissāmā’’ti. ‘‘Ajja devorohaṇaṃ karī’’tipi sutvā ‘‘āyusaṅkhārossajjane gamissāmā’’ti. ‘‘Ajja āyusaṅkhāraṃ ossajī’’tipi sutvā ‘‘na tāva niṭṭhāti, parinibbānadivase gamissāmā’’ti. ‘‘Ajja bhagavā yamakasālānamantare dakkhiṇena passena sato sampajāno sīhaseyyaṃ upagato balavapaccūsasamaye parinibbāyissati. Tumhe kassa ganthathā’’ti sutvā pana – ‘‘kinnāmetaṃ, ‘ajjeva mātukucchiyaṃ paṭisandhiṃ gaṇhi, ajjeva mātukucchito nikkhami, ajjeva mahābhinikkhamanaṃ nikkhami, ajjeva buddho ahosi, ajjeva dhammacakkaṃ pavattayi, ajjeva yamakapāṭihāriyaṃ akāsi, ajjeva devalokā otiṇṇo, ajjeva āyusaṅkhāraṃ ossaji, ajjeva kira parinibbāyissatī’ti. Nanu nāma dutiyadivase yāgupānakālamattampi ṭhātabbaṃ assa. Dasa pāramiyo pūretvā buddhattaṃ pattassa nāma ananucchavikameta’’nti apariniṭṭhitāva mālāyo gahetvā āgamma anto cakkavāḷe <pb ed="V" n="2.0151"/> okāsaṃ alabhamānā cakkavāḷamukhavaṭṭiyaṃ lambitvā cakkavāḷamukhavaṭṭiyāva ādhāvantiyo hatthena hatthaṃ gīvāya gīvaṃ gahetvā tīṇi ratanāni ārabbha dvattiṃsa mahāpurisalakkhaṇāni chabbaṇṇarasmiyo dasa pāramiyo aḍḍhachaṭṭhāni jātakasatāni cuddasa buddhañāṇāni ārabbha gāyitvā tassa tassa avasāne ‘‘mahāyaso, mahāyaso’’ti vadanti. Idametaṃ paṭicca vuttaṃ – ‘‘dibbānipi saṅgītāni antalikkhe vattanti tathāgatassa pūjāyā’’ti.</p> <hi rend="bold">Dibbānipi saṅgītānī</hi> <pb ed="P" n="2.0577"/> <pb ed="M" n="2.0168"/> <pb ed="V" n="2.0151"/>
198. "With a great *bhikkhu-saṃgha*": Here, there is no calculation or limitation of the *bhikkhu*s.

From the time of the suppression of the feeling in the *veḷuvagāma*, indeed, having heard that "The Blessed One will not attain *parinirvāṇa* soon," among the *bhikkhu*s who came from here and there, there was not even one *bhikkhu* who departed.

Therefore, the *saṃgha* was beyond calculation.

"*Upavattanaṃ mallānaṃ sālavanaṃ*": Just as, indeed, from the bank of the *kalamba* river, by the gate of the *rājamātuvihāra*, the *thūpārāma* is to be reached, it is, and so it is with Kusinārā.

Just as from the *thūpārāma* by the southern gate, the road for entering the city faces east, having gone to the north, it turns back, so from the garden, the *sālavana* faces east, having gone to the north, it turns back.

Therefore, it is called "*upavattana*."

"*Antarena yamakasālānaṃ*, *uttarasīsaka*": Of that couch, it seems, one row of *sāla* trees is at the head end, one at the foot end.

Even there, one young *sāla* tree is near the head end, one at the foot end.

Moreover, "*yamakasālā*" means *sāla* trees standing intertwined with each other by roots, trunks, branches, and leaves.

"*Mañcakaṃ paññapehī*": In that garden, it seems, there is a royal couch. With reference to that, he said, "Prepare [it]."

The Elder, having prepared that very thing, gave it.

"I am weary, Ānanda, I will lie down": Indeed, of the *tathāgata*:

"I am weary, Ānanda, I will lie down."

"Gocari Kaḷāpo Gaṅgeyyo, Piṅgalo Pabbateyyako;

Hemavato ca Tambo ca, Mandākinī Uposatho;

Chaddantoyeva Dasamo, Ete Nāgānamuttamā."

Here, the strength of ten ordinary elephants, reckoned as *gocarisaṅkhātānaṃ*, is that of one *kaḷāpa*.

Thus, by calculation increased tenfold, the strength of the ordinary elephants, a mass of strength of a hundred thousand *koṭi*, all of that, from the time of consuming Cunda's alms-food, was exhausted like water thrown into a cesspool.

From Pāvā-nagara three *gāvuta*s to Kusinārā-nagara, in this interval, having sat down in twenty-five places, though coming with great effort, at the time when the sun had set, at the time of twilight, the Blessed One entered the *sālavana*.

Thus, disease comes crushing all health.

As if showing this meaning, speaking a speech that causes agitation to the whole world – "I am weary, Ānanda, I will lie down," he said.

Why, indeed, did the Blessed One come here with such great effort? Is it not possible to attain *parinirvāṇa* elsewhere? To attain *parinirvāṇa* is not impossible anywhere, but he came here for three reasons. For the Blessed One sees thus: "If I attain *parinirvāṇa* elsewhere, the arising of the meaning of the *mahāsudassanasutta* will not occur.

But if I attain *parinirvāṇa* in Kusinārā, I will beautify with two recitations, and teach, that accomplishment that I experienced in the *devaloka* right here in the world of humans. Having heard that from me, many people will think that good should be done."

Moreover, he sees: "If I attain *parinirvāṇa* elsewhere, Subhadda will not see me, and he is to be trained by the Buddha, not to be trained by a disciple; the disciples cannot train him.

But if I attain *parinirvāṇa* in Kusinārā, having approached me, he will ask a question, and at the end of the answer to the question, having been established in the refuges, and having received the going forth and the full ordination in my presence, having taken up a meditation subject, while I am still existing, having attained *arahatta*, he will become the last disciple."

Moreover, he sees: "If I attain *parinirvāṇa* elsewhere, there will be a great quarrel in the sharing of the relics. Blood will appear like a river.

Having attained *parinirvāṇa* in Kusinārā, the *doṇabrāhmaṇa* will calm that dispute, and will divide the relics."

By these three reasons, it should be understood that the Blessed One came here with such great effort.

"*Sīhaseyya*": Here, *kāmabhogīseyyā*, *petaseyyā*, *sīhaseyyā*, *tathāgataseyyā*—these are the four ways of lying down.

"*Sīhaseyya*": There – "For the most part, *bhikkhu*s, beings who enjoy sensual pleasures lie down on their left side"—this is the *kāmabhogīseyyā*.

Among those, indeed, there is no one who lies down on their right side for the most part.

"*Kāmabhogīseyyā*."

"For the most part, *bhikkhu*s, ghosts lie down supine"—this is the *petaseyyā*.

Because of having little flesh and blood, indeed, ghosts, tangled with a skeleton, are not able to lie down on one side, they lie down only supine.

"*Petaseyyā*."
"The lion, monks, the king of beasts, arranges his lying down on his right side... content in mind" (A.N. 4.246): this is the lion's posture (*sīhaseyyā*).

For the lion, the king of beasts, has vigor and strength; he places his two forepaws in one place, his hind paws in another place, tucks his tail between his thighs, observes the space where the forepaws, hind paws, and tail are situated, and lies down placing his head on top of the two forepaws.

Even after sleeping during the day, he awakens without trembling; but raising his head, he observes the place where the forepaws, etc., are situated. If any place has been abandoned, having moved from its position, he becomes discontent, thinking, "This is not befitting your birth and bravery," and he lies down right there, not setting out for pasture. But if they remain without having moved from their position, delighted and pleased, he gets up, stretches in the lion's stretch (*sīhavijambhitaṃ vijambhitvā*), shakes out his mane (*kesarabhāraṃ vidhunitvā*), roars the lion's roar (*sīhanādaṃ naditvā*) three times, and sets out for pasture.

lion's posture (*sīhaseyyā*)

"The fourth jhāna posture (*catutthajjhānaseyyā*), however, is called the *Tathāgata's posture* (*tathāgatassa seyyā*)" (A.N. 4.246). Among those, the lion's posture (*sīhaseyyā*) is mentioned here. For this, due to the vigor and strength of its deportment, is called the supreme posture (*uttamaseyyā*).

*Tathāgata's posture* (*tathāgatassa seyyā*)

"*Foot on foot* (*pāde pāda*)": the left foot on the right foot. "*Having over-placed* (*accādhāyā*)": having placed it slightly crossing over. For if ankle is pressed against ankle, or knee against knee, pain frequently arises, the mind is not one-pointed, and the lying down is uncomfortable. However, when it is placed crossing over in such a way that they do not press against each other, pain does not arise, the mind is one-pointed, and the lying down is comfortable. Therefore, he lies down thus.

Since he has approached the posture of non-rising (*anuṭṭhānaseyyaṃ*), therefore it is not said here, "Having made the perception of rising in his mind." Here, non-rising should be understood in terms of the body; but in terms of sleep, there was no opportunity at all for the Blessed One's life-continuum (*bhavaṅgassa*) during that night. For in the first watch, there was a teaching of the Dhamma to the Mallas; in the middle watch, to Subhadda; in the last watch, he exhorted the community of monks; and in the strong dawn, he attained final nirvāṇa (*parinibbāyi*).

*Foot on foot* (*pāde pāda*) *Having over-placed* (*accādhāyā*)

"*All in full bloom* (*sabbaphāliphullā*)": all were in bloom on all sides, from the root up to the tip, uniformly covered. And not only the twin *sāla* trees, but all the trees were all in full bloom.

For not only in that park alone, but also in the entire ten-thousand world-system (*dasasahassacakkavāḷe*), those fit for flowers took flowers, those fit for fruit took fruit; on the trunks of all the trees were trunk-lotuses, on the branches were branch-lotuses, on the vines were vine-lotuses, in the skies were sky-lotuses, and breaking through the surface of the earth were stalk-lotuses. The entire great ocean was covered with five-colored lotuses. The Himalayas, three thousand yojanas in extent, was like a densely bound peacock's tail feather, like an uninterrupted garland creeper, like a well-pressed, tied flower diadem, and like a fully filled flower basket (*pupphacaṅkoṭakaṃ*), and was exceedingly lovely.

*All in full bloom* (*sabbaphāliphullā*)

"*They were strewing the body of the Tathāgata* (*te tathāgatassa sarīraṃ okirantī*)": those twin *sāla* trees, with their trunks, branches, and boughs moved by the earth-bound deities, were scattering flowers on the body of the Tathāgata, meaning they were strewing flowers on top of the body. "*Scattering over* (*ajjhokirantī*)": they scatter as if spreading over. "*Strewn upon* (*abhippakirantī*)": scattering again and again, repeatedly. "*Divine* (*dibbānī*)": born in the Nanda lotus pond in the world of the gods; those are golden in color, with petals the size of a sunshade, holding pollen the size of a large gourd. And not only *mandārava* flowers alone, but also other divine *pāricchattaka*, *kovidāra*, and other flowers, having filled golden baskets (*suvaṇṇacaṅkoṭakāni*), were thrown by the deities standing at the edge of the world-wheel, in the Tāvatiṃsa heaven, and even in the Brahmā world, falling from the sky.
The body of the *tathāgata*, without being scattered in between, having come, with powders of lotus filaments, they sprinkled the body of the *tathāgata*.

Those, sprinkling, scattering, and thoroughly scattering the body of the *tathāgata*, [with] divine...

The body of the *tathāgata*. Divine *candanacuṇṇāni*, divine sandalwood powder prepared for the gods.

Not only for the gods, but also for the *nāgas*, *supaṇṇas*, and humans, [there were] prepared sandalwood powders.

Not only sandalwood powder, but also *kāḷānusārika*, *lohitacandana*, and all sorts of divine fragrant *jāla* powders, *haritāla*, *añjana*, gold, silver powders, all sorts of divine fragrant substances, filling the gold, silver, and other containers, those gods situated in the *cakkavāḷamukhavaṭṭi* and others, having entered, without scattering in between, sprinkled the body of the *tathāgata*.

Divine...

Divine *candanacuṇṇāni*, divine musical instruments, musical instruments prepared for the gods.

Not only those, but all sorts of stringed, leather-bound, fully covered, hollow instruments, the musical instruments of gods, *nāgas*, *supaṇṇas*, and humans in ten thousand world systems, having assembled in one world system, are known to play in the sky.

Divine musical instruments, divine songs—the deities *varuṇa* and *vāraṇa*, it is said, these long-lived deities, having heard that “A great man, having been born in the human path, will become a Buddha,” began to string garlands, [thinking,] “On the day of conception, we will take him and go.”

Those stringing garlands, having heard that “A great man has been born in his mother’s womb,” when asked, “For whom are you stringing these?”, said, “It is not yet finished; on the day of his departure from the womb, we will take him and go.”

Again, having heard that “He has departed,” [they said,] “On the day of the Great Departure, we will go.”

Having lived in the house for twenty-nine years, having heard that “Today, he has gone forth on the Great Departure,” [they said,] “On the day of enlightenment, we will go.”

Having practiced asceticism for six years, having heard that “Today, he has become enlightened,” [they said,] “On the day of the turning of the wheel of Dharma, we will go.”

“Having spent seven weeks at the *bodhimaṇḍa*, having gone to *isipatana*, the wheel of Dharma was turned,” having heard this too, [they said,] “On the day of the Twin Miracle, we will go.”

“Today, he performed the Twin Miracle,” having heard this, [they said,] “On the day of the descent from the heavens, we will go.”

“Today, there is the descent from the heavens,” having heard this, [they said,] “At the abandonment of the life force, we will go.”

“Today, he has abandoned the life force,” having heard this, [they said,] “It is not yet finished; on the day of *parinirvāṇa*, we will go.”

“Today, the Blessed One, between the twin *sāla* trees, lying down on his right side, mindful and fully aware, having attained the lion’s posture, at the strong dawn, will pass into *parinirvāṇa*.”

Having heard this, [they asked,] “For whom are you stringing these garlands?” They responded, “What is this? ‘Today itself, he took rebirth in his mother’s womb, today itself he departed from his mother’s womb, today itself he went forth on the Great Departure, today itself he became a Buddha, today itself he turned the wheel of Dharma, today itself he performed the Twin Miracle, today itself he descended from the heavens, today itself he abandoned the life force, today itself he will pass into *parinirvāṇa*.’

Indeed, by the second day, he should remain only for the time of drinking gruel. It is not fitting for one who has fulfilled the ten perfections and attained Buddhahood.” Having not yet finished [stringing] the garlands, taking the garlands, having come inside the universe, not finding an opportunity, hanging down on the rim of the universe, running towards the rim of the universe, with hand in hand, neck to neck, having taken hold, and beginning with the three jewels, the thirty-two marks of a great man, the six-colored rays, the ten perfections, two and a half *jātaka* hundreds, fourteen Buddha knowledges, singing, at the end of each, they say, “Great fame, great fame.”

Having relied on this, it was said: “Divine songs proceed in the sky in worship of the *tathāgata*.”

Divine songs...
199
<p n="199" rend="bodytext"><hi rend="paranum">199</hi><hi rend="dot">.</hi> Atha kho bhagavā āyasmantaṃ ānandaṃ āmantesi – ‘‘sabbaphāliphullā kho, ānanda, yamakasālā akālapupphehi. Te tathāgatassa sarīraṃ okiranti ajjhokiranti abhippakiranti tathāgatassa pūjāya. Dibbānipi mandāravapupphāni antalikkhā papatanti, tāni tathāgatassa sarīraṃ okiranti ajjhokiranti abhippakiranti tathāgatassa pūjāya. Dibbānipi candanacuṇṇāni antalikkhā papatanti, tāni tathāgatassa sarīraṃ okiranti ajjhokiranti abhippakiranti tathāgatassa pūjāya. Dibbānipi tūriyāni antalikkhe vajjanti tathāgatassa pūjāya. Dibbānipi saṅgītāni antalikkhe vattanti tathāgatassa pūjāya. Na kho, ānanda, ettāvatā tathāgato sakkato vā hoti garukato vā mānito vā pūjito vā apacito vā. Yo kho, ānanda, bhikkhu <pb ed="T" n="2.0161"/> vā bhikkhunī vā upāsako vā upāsikā vā dhammānudhammappaṭipanno viharati sāmīcippaṭipanno anudhammacārī, so tathāgataṃ sakkaroti garuṃ karoti māneti pūjeti apaciyati <note>idaṃ padaṃ sīsyāipotthakesu na dissati</note>, paramāya pūjāya. Tasmātihānanda, dhammānudhammappaṭipannā viharissāma sāmīcippaṭipannā anudhammacārinoti. Evañhi vo, ānanda, sikkhitabba’’nti.</p> <p rend="subhead">Upavāṇatthero</p>
Then the Blessed One addressed the venerable Ānanda: "Ānanda, the twin *sāla* trees are in full bloom with untimely blossoms.

They shower, utterly shower, and thoroughly shower the body of the *Tathāgata* in homage.

Divine *mandārava* flowers fall from the sky; they shower, utterly shower, and thoroughly shower the body of the *Tathāgata* in homage.

Divine sandalwood powder falls from the sky; they shower, utterly shower, and thoroughly shower the body of the *Tathāgata* in homage.

Divine musical instruments play in the sky in homage to the *Tathāgata*.

Divine songs resound in the sky in homage to the *Tathāgata*.

But it is not in this way, Ānanda, that the *Tathāgata* is honored, respected, esteemed, worshipped, or venerated.

Rather, Ānanda, whichever *bhikṣu* or *bhikṣuṇī*, *upāsaka* or *upāsikā* lives practicing the Dhamma in accordance with the Dhamma (*dhammānudhammappaṭipanno*), lives practicing properly (*sāmīcippaṭipanno*), and behaves in accordance with the Dhamma (*anudhammacārī*), that person honors, respects, esteems, worships, and venerates the *Tathāgata* with the highest worship (*paramāya pūjāya*).

Therefore, Ānanda, you should train yourselves thus: ‘We will live practicing the Dhamma in accordance with the Dhamma (*dhammānudhammappaṭipannā*), live practicing properly (*sāmīcippaṭipannā*), and behave in accordance with the Dhamma (*anudhammacārino*)’.

Thus, Ānanda, should you train yourselves."

Upavāṇa the Elder
<p n="199" rend="bodytext"><hi rend="paranum">199</hi><hi rend="dot">.</hi> Bhagavā pana yamakasālānaṃ antarā dakkhiṇena passena nipannoyeva pathavītalato yāva cakkavāḷamukhavaṭṭiyā, cakkavāḷamukhavaṭṭito ca yāva brahmalokā sannipatitāya parisāya mahantaṃ ussāhaṃ disvā āyasmato ānandassa ārocesi. Tena vuttaṃ – ‘‘atha kho bhagavā āyasmantaṃ ānandaṃ…pe… tathāgatassa pūjāyā’’ti. Evaṃ mahāsakkāraṃ dassetvā tenāpi attano asakkatabhāvameva dassanto <hi rend="bold">na kho, ānanda, ettāvatā</hi>tiādimāha.</p> <p rend="bodytext">Idaṃ vuttaṃ hoti – ‘‘ānanda, mayā dīpaṅkarapādamūle nipannena aṭṭha dhamme samodhānetvā abhinīhāraṃ karontena <pb ed="P" n="2.0578"/> na mālāgandhatūriyasaṅgītānaṃ atthāya abhinīhāro kato, na etadatthāya pāramiyo pūritā. Tasmā na kho ahaṃ etāya pūjāya pūjito nāma homī’’ti.</p> <pb ed="P" n="2.0578"/> <p rend="bodytext">Kasmā <pb ed="M" n="2.0169"/> pana bhagavā aññattha ekaṃ umāpupphamattampi gahetvā buddhaguṇe āvajjetvā katāya pūjāya buddhañāṇenāpi aparicchinnaṃ vipākaṃ vaṇṇetvā idha evaṃ mahantaṃ pūjaṃ paṭikkhipatīti? Parisānuggahena ceva sāsanassa ca ciraṭṭhitikāmatāya. Sace hi bhagavā evaṃ na paṭikkhipeyya, anāgate sīlassa āgataṭṭhāne sīlaṃ na paripūressanti, samādhissa āgataṭṭhāne samādhiṃ na paripūressanti, vipassanāya āgataṭṭhāne vipassanāgabbhaṃ na gāhāpessanti. Upaṭṭhāke samādapetvā pūjaṃyeva kārentā viharissanti. Āmisapūjā ca nāmesā sāsanaṃ ekadivasampi ekayāgupānakālamattampi sandhāretuṃ na sakkoti. Mahāvihārasadisañhi vihārasahassaṃ mahācetiyasadisañca cetiyasahassampi sāsanaṃ dhāretuṃ na sakkonti. Yena kammaṃ kataṃ, tasseva hoti. Sammāpaṭipatti pana tathāgatassa anucchavikā pūjā. Sā hi tena patthitā ceva, sakkoti sāsanañca sandhāretuṃ, tasmā taṃ dassento <hi rend="bold">yo kho ānandā</hi>tiādimāha.</p> <pb ed="M" n="2.0169"/> <hi rend="bold">yo kho ānandā</hi> <p rend="bodytext">Tattha <hi rend="bold">dhammānudhammappaṭipanno</hi>ti navavidhassa lokuttaradhammassa anudhammaṃ pubbabhāgapaṭipadaṃ paṭipanno <pb ed="V" n="2.0152"/>. Sāyeva pana paṭipadā anucchavikattā ‘‘sāmīcī’’ti vuccati. Taṃ sāmīciṃ paṭipannoti <hi rend="bold">sāmīcippaṭipanno.</hi> Tameva pubbabhāgapaṭipadāsaṅkhātaṃ anudhammaṃ carati pūretīti <hi rend="bold">anudhammacārī.</hi></p> <hi rend="bold">dhammānudhammappaṭipanno</hi> <pb ed="V" n="2.0152"/> <hi rend="bold">sāmīcippaṭipanno.</hi> <hi rend="bold">anudhammacārī.</hi> <p rend="bodytext"><hi rend="bold">Pubbabhāgapaṭipadā</hi>ti ca sīlaṃ ācārapaññatti dhutaṅgasamādānaṃ yāva gotrabhuto sammāpaṭipadā veditabbā. Tasmā yo bhikkhu chasu agāravesu patiṭṭhāya paññattiṃ atikkamati, anesanāya jīvikaṃ kappeti, ayaṃ na dhammānudhammappaṭipanno. Yo pana sabbaṃ attano paññattaṃ sikkhāpadaṃ jinavelaṃ jinamariyādaṃ jinakāḷasuttaṃ aṇumattampi na vītikkamati, ayaṃ dhammānudhammappaṭipanno nāma. Bhikkhuniyāpi eseva nayo. Yo upāsako pañca verāni dasa akusalakammapathe samādāya vattati appeti, ayaṃ na dhammānudhammappaṭipanno. Yo pana tīsu saraṇesu, pañcasupi sīlesu, dasasu sīlesu paripūrakārī hoti, māsassa aṭṭha uposathe karoti, dānaṃ deti, gandhapūjaṃ mālāpūjaṃ karoti, mātaraṃ pitaraṃ <pb ed="P" n="2.0579"/> upaṭṭhāti, dhammike samaṇabrāhmaṇe upaṭṭhāti, ayaṃ dhammānudhammappaṭipanno nāma. Upāsikāyapi eseva nayo.</p> <hi rend="bold">Pubbabhāgapaṭipadā</hi> <pb ed="P" n="2.0579"/> <p rend="bodytext"><hi rend="bold">Paramāya</hi><pb ed="M" n="2.0170"/><hi rend="bold">pūjāyā</hi>ti uttamāya pūjāya. Ayañhi nirāmisapūjā nāma sakkoti mama sāsanaṃ sandhāretuṃ. Yāva hi imā catasso parisā maṃ imāya pūjessanti, tāva mama sāsanaṃ majjhe nabhassa puṇṇacando viya virocissatīti dasseti.</p> <hi rend="bold">Paramāya</hi> <pb ed="M" n="2.0170"/> <hi rend="bold">pūjāyā</hi> <p rend="subhead">Upavāṇattheravaṇṇanā</p>
199. Furthermore, the Blessed One, having lain down between the twin *sāla* trees with his right side, from the surface of the earth up to the circular mouth of the *cakkavāḷa*, and from the circular mouth of the *cakkavāḷa* up to the great effort of the assembly gathered in the Brahmā realm, announced to venerable Ānanda, having seen [it].

That was said by him: "Then, the Blessed One [said] to venerable Ānanda...pe... for the worship of the Tathāgata."

Having shown such great honor, and even showing the state of being incapable of honoring himself by that, he said, beginning with, "No, Ānanda, not with this."

This was said: "Ānanda, by me, having lain down at the base of Dīpaṃkara’s feet, by [me] making an aspiration, having harmonized the eight qualities, [page 2.0578] the aspiration was not made for the sake of garlands, scents, musical instruments, and singing; the perfections were not fulfilled for this purpose. Therefore, I am not called worshiped by this worship."

[Page 2.0578] Why then [page 2.0169] does the Blessed One, having taken even one *umā* flower elsewhere, and having reflected on the qualities of the Buddha, having described the unlimited result even by the knowledge of the Buddha, reject such a great worship here? Due to the favor of the assembly and due to the desire for the long standing of the Dispensation.

If, indeed, the Blessed One would not reject thus, in the future, they will not completely fulfill morality in the place where morality has come; they will not completely fulfill *samādhi* in the place where *samādhi* has come; they will not cause the essence of insight (*vipassanā*) to be grasped in the place where *vipassanā* has come. Having pleased the attendants, they will live only causing worship. And this material worship is not able to maintain the Dispensation even for a single day, even for the time of a single rice-gruel drink. Indeed, thousands of monasteries similar to the Great Monastery and thousands of *cetiya*s similar to the Great *cetiya* are not able to maintain the Dispensation. The *karma* that is done belongs to him alone. Furthermore, right practice is worship befitting the Tathāgata. Indeed, that is desired by him, and it is able to maintain the Dispensation; therefore, showing that, he said, beginning with, "The one, Ānanda."

[Page 2.0169] "The one, Ānanda" [page 2.0152] "Dhammānudhammappaṭipanno": practicing the *anudhamma*, the preliminary practice, of the ninefold supramundane *dharma*,

That practice itself, due to being befitting, is called "proper (*sāmīcī*)". Because he has undertaken that proper [practice], [he is called] "practicing properly (*sāmīcippaṭipanno*)". Because he lives fulfilling that *anudhamma* known as the preliminary practice, [he is called] "living according to the *dharma* (*anudhammacārī*)".

Dhammānudhammappaṭipanno, [page 2.0152] Sāmīcippaṭipanno, Anudhammacārī.

"Preliminary practice (*pubbabhāgapaṭipadā*)" and also morality, rules of conduct, undertaking the *dhuta* practices, up to the mundane right practice, should be understood.

Therefore, that *bhikkhu* who, having stood in the six kinds of disrespect, transgresses the precepts, makes a living by improper means, this one is not practicing according to the *dharma* (*dhammānudhammappaṭipanno*). But that one who does not transgress even a little all the precepts that he himself has laid down, the proper time of the Jinas, the limit of the Jinas, the black thread of the Jinas, this one is called practicing according to the *dharma* (*dhammānudhammappaṭipanno*). This is the same method for a *bhikkhunī*.

That lay follower who, having undertaken the five abstinences, [and] the ten unwholesome paths of action, behaves improperly, this one is not practicing according to the *dharma* (*dhammānudhammappaṭipanno*).

But that one who is a complete doer in the three refuges, even in the five moralities, [and] in the ten moralities, makes eight *uposatha*s in a month, gives alms, does scent worship, does flower worship, attends to [his] mother [and] father, [page 2.0579] attends to righteous *samaṇa*s and *brāhmaṇa*s, this one is called practicing according to the *dharma* (*dhammānudhammappaṭipanno*). This is the same method for a lay woman.

Preliminary practice (*pubbabhāgapaṭipadā*), [page 2.0579] "for the supreme [page 2.0170] worship (*pūjā*)": for the highest worship. Indeed, this unmaterial worship is able to maintain my Dispensation. Indeed, as long as these four assemblies will worship me with this, so long will my Dispensation shine in the midst of the sky like the full moon, he shows.

For the supreme [page 2.
Of the *pūjā*. Explanation of Upavāṇa Thera

<p n="200" rend="bodytext"><hi rend="paranum">200</hi><hi rend="dot">.</hi> Tena <pb ed="V" n="2.0105"/> kho pana samayena āyasmā upavāṇo bhagavato purato ṭhito hoti bhagavantaṃ bījayamāno. Atha kho bhagavā āyasmantaṃ upavāṇaṃ apasāresi – ‘‘apehi, bhikkhu, mā me purato aṭṭhāsī’’ti. Atha kho āyasmato ānandassa etadahosi – ‘‘ayaṃ kho <pb ed="M" n="2.0115"/> āyasmā <pb ed="P" n="2.0139"/> upavāṇo dīgharattaṃ bhagavato upaṭṭhāko santikāvacaro samīpacārī. Atha ca pana bhagavā pacchime kāle āyasmantaṃ upavāṇaṃ apasāreti – ‘apehi bhikkhu, mā me purato aṭṭhāsī’ti. Ko nu kho hetu, ko paccayo, yaṃ bhagavā āyasmantaṃ upavāṇaṃ apasāreti – ‘apehi, bhikkhu, mā me purato aṭṭhāsī’ti? Atha kho āyasmā ānando bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – ‘ayaṃ, bhante, āyasmā upavāṇo dīgharattaṃ bhagavato upaṭṭhāko santikāvacaro samīpacārī. Atha ca pana bhagavā pacchime kāle āyasmantaṃ upavāṇaṃ apasāreti – ‘‘apehi, bhikkhu, mā me purato aṭṭhāsī’’ti. Ko nu kho, bhante, hetu, ko paccayo, yaṃ bhagavā āyasmantaṃ upavāṇaṃ apasāreti – ‘‘apehi, bhikkhu, mā me purato aṭṭhāsī’’ti? ‘‘Yebhuyyena, ānanda, dasasu lokadhātūsu devatā sannipatitā <pb ed="T" n="2.0162"/> tathāgataṃ dassanāya. Yāvatā, ānanda, kusinārā upavattanaṃ mallānaṃ sālavanaṃ samantato dvādasa yojanāni, natthi so padeso vālaggakoṭinitudanamattopi mahesakkhāhi devatāhi apphuṭo. Devatā, ānanda, ujjhāyanti – ‘dūrā ca vatamha āgatā tathāgataṃ dassanāya. Kadāci karahaci tathāgatā loke uppajjanti arahanto sammāsambuddhā. Ajjeva rattiyā pacchime yāme tathāgatassa parinibbānaṃ bhavissati. Ayañca mahesakkho bhikkhu bhagavato purato ṭhito ovārento, na mayaṃ labhāma pacchime kāle tathāgataṃ dassanāyā’’’ti.</p>
200. Now at that time venerable Upavāṇa was standing in front of the Fortunate One, fanning the Fortunate One.

Then the Fortunate One dismissed venerable Upavāṇa, saying, "Go away, *bhikṣu*, do not stand in front of me."

Then the venerable Ānanda thought: “This venerable Upavāṇa has for long been the Fortunate One’s attendant, keeping close at hand, at his beck and call.

And now in his final hour the Fortunate One tells him to stand aside and not stand in front of him."

What could be the cause, what the reason, that the Fortunate One dismisses venerable Upavāṇa, saying, 'Go away, *bhikṣu*, do not stand in front of me?'" Then the venerable Ānanda said this to the Fortunate One: "This, venerable sir, venerable Upavāṇa has for long been the Fortunate One’s attendant, keeping close at hand, at his beck and call.

And now in his final hour the Fortunate One tells him to stand aside and not stand in front of him."

"What now, venerable sir, is the cause, what is the reason, that the Fortunate One dismisses venerable Upavāṇa, saying, 'Go away, *bhikṣu*, do not stand in front of me?'" "Ānanda, for the most part, deities have gathered in the ten world-realms to see the *Tathāgata*.

For a distance of twelve *yojanas* around Kusinārā, the Upavattana, the *sāla* grove of the Mallas, there is not a spot that could be pricked with the tip of a hair that is not filled with powerful deities.

The deities, Ānanda, are complaining, ‘From afar have we come to see the *Tathāgata*.

Only occasionally, infrequently, do *Tathāgatas*, worthy ones, perfectly awakened ones arise in the world.

And this day, in the last watch of the night, the *Tathāgata*'s *parinirvāṇa* will come about.

And this eminent *bhikṣu* is standing in front of the Fortunate One, blocking the way. We aren’t getting to see the *Tathāgata* in his final hour.’”
<p n="200" rend="bodytext"><hi rend="paranum">200</hi><hi rend="dot">.</hi><hi rend="bold">Apasāresī</hi>ti apanesi. <hi rend="bold">Apehī</hi>ti apagaccha. Thero ekavacaneneva tālavaṇṭaṃ nikkhipitvā ekamantaṃ aṭṭhāsi. <hi rend="bold">Upaṭṭhāko</hi>tiādi paṭhamabodhiyaṃ anibaddhupaṭṭhākabhāvaṃ sandhāyāha. <hi rend="bold">Ayaṃ, bhante, āyasmā upavāṇo</hi>ti evaṃ therena vutte ānando upavāṇassa sadosabhāvaṃ sallakkheti, ‘handassa niddosabhāvaṃ kathessāmī’ti bhagavā <hi rend="bold">yebhuyyena ānandā</hi>tiādimāha. Tattha <hi rend="bold">yebhuyyenā</hi>ti idaṃ asaññasattānañceva arūpadevatānañca ohīnabhāvaṃ sandhāya vuttaṃ. <hi rend="bold">Apphuṭo</hi>ti asamphuṭṭho abharito vā. Bhagavato kira āsannapadese vālaggamatte okāse sukhumattabhāvaṃ māpetvā dasa dasa mahesakkhā devatā aṭṭhaṃsu. Tāsaṃ parato vīsati vīsati. Tāsaṃ parato tiṃsati tiṃsati. Tāsaṃ parato cattālīsaṃ cattālīsaṃ. Tāsaṃ parato paññāsaṃ paññāsaṃ. Tāsaṃ parato saṭṭhi saṭṭhi devatā aṭṭhaṃsu. Tā aññamaññaṃ hatthena vā pādena vā vatthena vā na byābādhenti. ‘‘Apehi maṃ, mā ghaṭṭehī’’ti vattabbākāraṃ nāma natthi. ‘‘Tā <pb ed="V" n="2.0153"/> kho pana devatāyo dasapi hutvā vīsatipi hutvā tiṃsampi hutvā cattālīsampi hutvā paññāsampi hutvā āraggakoṭinitudanamattepi tiṭṭhanti, na ca aññamaññaṃ byābādhentī’’ti (a. ni. 1.37) vuttasadisāva ahesuṃ. <hi rend="bold">Ovārento</hi>ti āvārento. Thero kira pakatiyāpi mahāsarīro hatthipotakasadiso. So paṃsukūlacīvaraṃ pārupitvā atimahā viya ahosi.</p> <p rend="bodytext"><hi rend="bold">Tathāgataṃ dassanāyā</hi>ti bhagavato mukhaṃ daṭṭhuṃ alabhamānā evaṃ ujjhāyiṃsu. Kiṃ pana tā theraṃ vinivijjha passituṃ na sakkontīti? Āma, na sakkonti. Devatā hi puthujjane vinivijjha passituṃ sakkonti, na khīṇāsave. Therassa ca mahesakkhatāya <pb ed="P" n="2.0580"/> tejussadatāya upagantumpi na sakkonti. Kasmā <pb ed="M" n="2.0171"/> pana therova tejussado, na aññe arahantoti? Yasmā kassapabuddhassa cetiye ārakkhadevatā ahosi.</p> <hi rend="bold">Tathāgataṃ dassanāyā</hi> <pb ed="P" n="2.0580"/> <pb ed="M" n="2.0171"/> <p rend="bodytext">Vipassimhi kira sammāsambuddhe parinibbute ekagghanasuvaṇṇakkhandhasadisassa dhātusarīrassa ekameva cetiyaṃ akaṃsu, dīghāyukabuddhānañhi ekameva cetiyaṃ hoti. Taṃ manussā ratanāyāmāhi vidatthivitthatāhi dvaṅgulabahalāhi suvaṇṇiṭṭhakāhi haritālena ca manosilāya ca mattikākiccaṃ tilateleneva udakakiccaṃ sādhetvā yojanappamāṇaṃ uṭṭhapesuṃ. Tato bhummā devatā yojanappamāṇaṃ, tato ākāsaṭṭhakadevatā, tato uṇhavalāhakadevatā, tato abbhavalāhakadevatā, tato cātumahārājikā devatā, tato tāvatiṃsā devatā yojanappamāṇaṃ uṭṭhapesunti evaṃ sattayojanikaṃ cetiyaṃ ahosi. Manussesu mālāgandhavatthādīni gahetvā āgatesu ārakkhadevatā gahetvā tesaṃ passantānaṃyeva cetiyaṃ pūjesi.</p> <p rend="bodytext">Tadā ayaṃ thero brāhmaṇamahāsālo hutvā ekaṃ pītakaṃ vatthaṃ ādāya gato. Devatā tassa hatthato vatthaṃ gahetvā cetiyaṃ pūjesi. Brāhmaṇo taṃ disvā pasannacitto ‘‘ahampi anāgate evarūpassa buddhassa cetiye ārakkhadevatā homī’’ti patthanaṃ katvā tato cuto devaloke nibbatti. Tassa devaloke ca manussaloke ca saṃsarantasseva kassapo bhagavā loke uppajjitvā parinibbāyi. Tassāpi ekameva dhātusarīraṃ ahosi. Taṃ gahetvā yojanikaṃ cetiyaṃ kāresuṃ. So tattha ārakkhadevatā hutvā sāsane antarahite sagge nibbattitvā amhākaṃ bhagavato kāle tato cuto mahākule paṭisandhiṃ gahetvā nikkhamma pabbajitvā arahattaṃ patto. Iti cetiye ārakkhadevatā hutvā āgatattā thero tejussadoti veditabbo.</p> <p rend="bodytext"><hi rend="bold">Devatā</hi><pb ed="V" n="2.0154"/>, <hi rend="bold">ānanda, ujjhāyantī</hi>ti iti ānanda, devatā ujjhāyanti, na mayhaṃ puttassa añño koci doso atthīti dasseti.</p> <hi rend="bold">Devatā</hi> <pb ed="V" n="2.0154"/> <hi rend="bold">ānanda, ujjhāyantī</hi>
200. “*Apasāresī*” means *apanesi*.
“*Apehī*” means *apagaccha*.
The elder, with just a single word, having put down the fan, stood to one side.
"*Upaṭṭhāko* tiādi" he said, referring to the state of not being bound to a regular attendant during his initial awakening.
"*Ayaṃ, bhante, āyasmā Upavāṇo*" Thus, when the elder had spoken, Ānanda considered Upavāṇa's state of being faulty, and the Blessed One said, "*Yebhuyyena ānandā*," and so forth, to explain that he was actually faultless.
There, "*yebhuyyenā*" this was said referring to the diminished state of both the non-percipient beings (*asaññasatta*) and the formless deities (*arūpadevatā*).
"*Apphuṭo*" means *asamphuṭṭho* or *abharito*.
It is said that near the Blessed One, in a space the size of a hair tip, having fashioned a subtle form, ten powerful deities (*mahesakkhā devatā*) stood.
Beyond them were twenty [deities], twenty [deities].
Beyond them were thirty [deities], thirty [deities].
Beyond them were forty [deities], forty [deities].
Beyond them were fifty [deities], fifty [deities].
Beyond them were sixty [deities], sixty [deities].
Those deities did not bother each other with their hands, feet, or clothing.
There was no talk such as, "Go away from me, do not touch me."
"Those deities, even having been ten, or having been twenty, or having been thirty, or having been forty, or having been fifty, stand even in a space the size of the tip of a needle, and they do not bother each other," they were just like what was said in A.
ni.
1.
37.
"*Ovārento*" means *āvārento*.
It is said that the elder was, by nature, a very large man, like a young elephant.
Having put on a robe made of rags from a dust heap (*paṃsukūlacīvara*), he was very large.

"*Tathāgataṃ dassanāyā*" means that, not obtaining the chance to see the face of the Blessed One, they murmured thus.
"Why are those deities not able to see through the elder?" Yes, they are not able.
Deities are indeed able to see through ordinary people (*puthujjane*), but not those who have destroyed the āsavas.
And because of the elder's great power (*mahesakkhatāya*) and radiance (*tejussadatāya*), they were not able to approach him.
Why is it that the elder alone is radiant (*tejussado*), and not other *arhats*? Because he was the guardian deity (*ārakkhadevatā*) of the *cetiya* of the Buddha Kassapa.

"*Tathāgataṃ dassanāyā*" In the time of the Buddha Vipassī, when the perfectly awakened one (*sammāsambuddha*) had attained final *nirvāṇa* (*parinibbute*), they made a single *cetiya* for the relics of his body (*dhātusarīra*), which was like a single mass of solid gold. For long-lived Buddhas, there is indeed only one *cetiya*.
Men raised it, using gold bricks (*suvaṇṇiṭṭhakāhi*) inlaid with jewels (*ratanāyāmāhi*) that were a span wide (*vidatthivitthatāhi*) and two finger-breadths thick (*dvaṅgulabahalāhi*), and having accomplished the mud work with *haritāla* and *manosilā*, and the water work with sesame oil (*tilateleneva*), to the measure of a *yojana*.
Then the earth deities [*bhummā devatā*] [raised it] to the measure of a *yojana*, then the sky-dwelling deities [*ākāsaṭṭhakadevatā*], then the hot-cloud deities [*uṇhavalāhakadevatā*], then the rain-cloud deities [*abbhavalāhakadevatā*], then the deities of the Four Great Kings [*cātumahārājikā devatā*], then the deities of the *Tāvatiṃsa* heaven raised it to the measure of a *yojana*. Thus, that *cetiya* was seven *yojanas* high.
When men came, having taken flowers, scents, cloths, and so forth, the guardian deity (*ārakkhadevatā*), having taken [those items], worshiped the *cetiya* right in front of those onlookers.

Then this elder, having been a wealthy *brāhmin* [*brāhmaṇamahāsāla*], having taken a single yellow cloth, went [there].
The deity, having taken the cloth from his hand, worshiped the *cetiya*.
The *brāhmin*, having seen that, with a pleased mind, made the aspiration, "May I also, in the future, be a guardian deity (*ārakkhadevatā*) of a *cetiya* of a Buddha such as this!" Having made that aspiration, he passed away from there and was reborn in the world of the gods (*devaloke*).
While he was wandering in the world of gods (*devaloka*) and the world of humans (*manussaloka*), Kassapa, the Blessed One, arose in the world and attained complete extinction (*parinibbāyi*). Even he had only one relics-body (*dhātusarīra*). Taking that, they had a league-wide shrine (*yojanikaṃ cetiyaṃ*) built. He, having become a guardian deity (*ārakkhadevatā*) there, after the Dispensation had disappeared, was reborn in heaven (*sagge nibbattitvā*), and in the time of our Blessed One, having fallen from there, taking rebirth in a great family (*mahākule paṭisandhiṃ gahetvā*), having gone forth and renounced, attained Arhatship. Thus, because the Elder came having been a guardian deity (*ārakkhadevatā*) at the shrine (*cetiye*), he should be known as Tejussada.

"The deities (*devatā*) are murmuring, Ānanda," thus, Ānanda, the deities (*devatā*) are murmuring, showing that there is no other fault in my son.

The deities (*devatā*) are murmuring, Ānanda.
201
<p n="201" rend="bodytext"><hi rend="paranum">201</hi><hi rend="dot">.</hi> ‘‘Kathaṃbhūtā pana, bhante, bhagavā devatā manasikarotī’’ti <note>manasi karontīti (syā. ka.)</note>? ‘‘Santānanda, devatā ākāse pathavīsaññiniyo kese pakiriya kandanti, bāhā paggayha kandanti, chinnapātaṃ papatanti <note>chinnaṃpādaṃviya papatanti (syā.)</note>, āvaṭṭanti, vivaṭṭanti – ‘atikhippaṃ bhagavā parinibbāyissati, atikhippaṃ sugato parinibbāyissati, atikhippaṃ cakkhuṃ <note>cakkhumā (syā. ka.)</note> loke antaradhaṃāyissatī’ti.</p> <p rend="bodytext">‘‘Santānanda, devatā pathaviyaṃ pathavīsaññiniyo kese pakiriya kandanti, bāhā paggayha kandanti, chinnapātaṃ <pb ed="P" n="2.0140"/> papatanti, āvaṭṭanti, vivaṭṭanti – ‘atikhippaṃ bhagavā parinibbāyissati, atikhippaṃ sugato parinibbāyissati, atikhippaṃ cakkhuṃ loke antaradhāyissatī’’’ti.</p> <pb ed="P" n="2.0140"/> <p rend="bodytext">‘‘Yā <pb ed="M" n="2.0116"/><pb ed="V" n="2.0106"/> pana tā devatā vītarāgā, tā satā sampajānā adhivāsenti – ‘aniccā saṅkhārā, taṃ kutettha labbhā’ti.</p> <pb ed="M" n="2.0116"/> <pb ed="V" n="2.0106"/> <p rend="subhead">Catusaṃvejanīyaṭṭhānāni</p>
“But, lord, what is the state of the *devatās* the Blessed One is paying attention to?”

“Ānanda, there are *devatās* in space who perceive earth to be earth. Tearing at their hair, they are weeping. Uplifting their arms, they are weeping. As if their feet were cut out from under them, they fall down and roll back & forth, crying, ‘All too soon, the Blessed One will attain *parinirvāṇa*! All too soon, the Well-Gone One will attain *parinirvāṇa*! All too soon, the Eye will disappear from the world!’

“Ānanda, there are *devatās* on earth who perceive earth to be earth. Tearing at their hair, they are weeping. Uplifting their arms, they are weeping. As if their feet were cut out from under them, they fall down and roll back & forth, crying, ‘All too soon, the Blessed One will attain *parinirvāṇa*! All too soon, the Well-Gone One will attain *parinirvāṇa*! All too soon, the Eye will disappear from the world!’

“But those *devatās* who are free from craving acquiesce, mindful and clearly comprehending: ‘Impermanent are conditioned things (*saṃskāras*). What else is there to expect?’”

The Four Places That Cause Emotion
<p n="201" rend="bodytext"><hi rend="paranum">201</hi><hi rend="dot">.</hi><hi rend="bold">Kathaṃbhūtā pana, bhante</hi>ti kasmā āha? Bhagavā tumhe – ‘‘devatā ujjhāyantī’’ti vadatha, kathaṃ bhūtā pana tā tumhe manasi karotha <pb ed="M" n="2.0172"/>, kiṃ tumhākaṃ parinibbānaṃ adhivāsentīti pucchati. Atha bhagavā – ‘‘nāhaṃ adhivāsanakāraṇaṃ vadāmī’’ti tāsaṃ anadhivāsanabhāvaṃ dassento <hi rend="bold">santānandā</hi>tiādimāha.</p> <p rend="bodytext">Tattha <pb ed="P" n="2.0581"/><hi rend="bold">ākāse pathavīsaññiniyo</hi>ti ākāse pathaviṃ māpetvā tattha pathavīsaññiniyo. <hi rend="bold">Kandantī</hi>ti rodanti. <hi rend="bold">Chinnapātaṃ papatantī</hi>ti majjhe chinnā viya hutvā yato vā tato vā papatanti. <hi rend="bold">Āvaṭṭantī</hi>ti āvaṭṭantiyo patitaṭṭhānameva āgacchanti. <hi rend="bold">Vivaṭṭantī</hi>ti patitaṭṭhānato parabhāgaṃ vaṭṭamānā gacchanti. Apica dve pāde pasāretvā sakiṃ purato sakiṃ pacchato sakiṃ vāmato sakiṃ dakkhiṇato saṃparivattamānāpi – ‘‘āvaṭṭanti vivaṭṭantī’’ti vuccanti. <hi rend="bold">Santānanda, devatā pathaviyaṃ pathavīsaññiniyo</hi>ti pakatipathavī kira devatā dhāretuṃ na sakkoti. Tattha hatthako brahmā viya devatā osīdanti. Tenāha bhagavā – ‘‘oḷārikaṃ hatthaka, attabhāvaṃ abhinimmināhī’’ti (a. ni. 3.128). Tasmā yā devatā pathaviyaṃ pathaviṃ māpesuṃ, tā sandhāyetaṃ vuttaṃ – ‘‘pathaviyaṃ pathavīsaññiniyo’’ti.</p> <pb ed="P" n="2.0581"/> <hi rend="bold">ākāse pathavīsaññiniyo</hi> <hi rend="bold">Kandantī</hi> <hi rend="bold">Chinnapātaṃ papatantī</hi> <hi rend="bold">Āvaṭṭantī</hi> <hi rend="bold">Vivaṭṭantī</hi> <hi rend="bold">Santānanda, devatā pathaviyaṃ pathavīsaññiniyo</hi> <p rend="bodytext"><hi rend="bold">Vītarāgā</hi>ti pahīnadomanassā silāthambhasadisā anāgāmikhīṇāsavadevatā.</p> <hi rend="bold">Vītarāgā</hi> <p rend="subhead">Catusaṃvejanīyaṭhānavaṇṇanā</p>
<p n="201" rend="bodytext"><hi rend="paranum">201</hi><hi rend="dot">.
</hi><hi rend="bold">“What kind [of gods] are they, venerable sir?”</hi> Why does he say this? The Blessed One said to you, “You say ‘the gods are murmuring.’" But what kind of gods do you keep in mind?" <pb ed="m" n="2.
0172"/> He asks, "Are you dwelling in nirvāṇa (parinibbāna)?".
Then the Blessed One, showing that they do not tolerate, said, "I am not speaking about the cause of tolerating (adhivāsanakāraṇaṃ)," and he began with <hi rend="bold">Santānanda</hi>.
</p> <p rend="bodytext">There, <pb ed="p" n="2.
0581"/><hi rend="bold">"those who perceive earth in the sky" (ākāse pathavīsaññiniyo)</hi> means those who, having fashioned earth in the sky (ākāse pathaviṃ māpetvā), perceive earth (pathavīsaññiniyo) there.
<hi rend="bold">"Weeping (kandantī)"</hi> means they are crying (rodanti).
<hi rend="bold">"Falling with severed limbs (chinnapātaṃ papatantī)"</hi> means having been as if severed in the middle (majjhe chinnā viya hutvā), they fall from here or there (yato vā tato vā papatanti).
<hi rend="bold">"Revolving (āvaṭṭantī)"</hi> means the revolving ones (āvaṭṭantiyo) come to the very place where they fell (patitaṭṭhānameva āgacchanti).
<hi rend="bold">"Spinning around (vivaṭṭantī)"</hi> means moving around (vaṭṭamānā gacchanti) to a different place (parabhāgaṃ) from the place where they fell (patitaṭṭhānato).
Moreover, even while stretching out two feet, one to the front (purato), one to the back (pacchato), one to the left (vāmatas), one to the right (dakkhiṇato), and revolving (saṃparivattamānāpi), they are called "revolving (āvaṭṭanti) and spinning around (vivaṭṭantī)."
<hi rend="bold">"Santānanda, devatā pathaviyaṃ pathavīsaññiniyo"</hi> means the natural earth is not able to hold the gods (devatā dhāretuṃ na sakkoti).
There, the gods sink down like Hatthaka Brahmā.
Therefore, the Blessed One said (bhagavā) – “Hatthaka, create a gross (oḷārikaṃ) self-image (attabhāvaṃ abhinimmināhī)” (a.
ni.
3.
128).
Therefore, the statement (vuttaṃ) – "those who perceive earth in the earth (pathaviyaṃ pathavīsaññiniyo)" – refers to those gods (devatā) who fashioned earth in the earth (pathaviyaṃ pathaviṃ māpesuṃ).
</p> <pb ed="p" n="2.
0581"/> <hi rend="bold">those who perceive earth in the sky (ākāse pathavīsaññiniyo)</hi> <hi rend="bold">weeping (kandantī)</hi> <hi rend="bold">falling with severed limbs (chinnapātaṃ papatantī)</hi> <hi rend="bold">revolving (āvaṭṭantī)</hi> <hi rend="bold">spinning around (vivaṭṭantī)</hi> <hi rend="bold">Santānanda, devatā pathaviyaṃ pathavīsaññiniyo</hi> <p rend="bodytext"><hi rend="bold">"Free from desire (vītarāgā)"</hi> means the anāgāmins (anāgāmi), āsravas-exhausted gods (khīṇāsavadevatā), who have abandoned sadness (pahīnadomanassā), are like stone pillars (silāthambhasadisā).
</p> <hi rend="bold">Free from desire (vītarāgā)</hi> <p rend="subhead">Description of the four inspiring places (catusaṃvejanīyaṭhānavaṇṇanā)</p>
202
<p n="202" rend="bodytext"><hi rend="paranum">202</hi><hi rend="dot">.</hi> ‘‘Pubbe <pb ed="T" n="2.0163"/>, bhante, disāsu vassaṃ vuṭṭhā <note>vassaṃvutthā (sī. syā. kaṃ. pī.)</note> bhikkhū āgacchanti tathāgataṃ dassanāya. Te mayaṃ labhāma manobhāvanīye bhikkhū dassanāya, labhāma payirupāsanāya. Bhagavato pana mayaṃ, bhante, accayena na labhissāma manobhāvanīye bhikkhū dassanāya, na labhissāma payirupāsanāyā’’ti.</p> <p rend="bodytext">‘‘Cattārimāni, ānanda, saddhassa kulaputtassa dassanīyāni saṃvejanīyāni ṭhānāni. Katamāni cattāri? ‘Idha tathāgato jāto’ti, ānanda, saddhassa kulaputtassa dassanīyaṃ saṃvejanīyaṃ ṭhānaṃ. ‘Idha tathāgato anuttaraṃ sammāsambodhiṃ abhisambuddho’ti, ānanda, saddhassa kulaputtassa dassanīyaṃ saṃvejanīyaṃ ṭhānaṃ. ‘Idha tathāgatena anuttaraṃ dhammacakkaṃ pavattita’nti, ānanda, saddhassa kulaputtassa dassanīyaṃ saṃvejanīyaṃ ṭhānaṃ. ‘Idha tathāgato anupādisesāya nibbānadhātuyā parinibbuto’ti, ānanda, saddhassa kulaputtassa dassanīyaṃ saṃvejanīyaṃ ṭhānaṃ. Imāni kho <pb ed="P" n="2.0141"/>, ānanda, cattāri saddhassa kulaputtassa dassanīyāni saṃvejanīyāni ṭhānāni.</p> <pb ed="P" n="2.0141"/> <p rend="bodytext">‘‘Āgamissanti kho, ānanda, saddhā bhikkhū bhikkhuniyo upāsakā upāsikāyo – ‘idha tathāgato jāto’tipi, ‘idha tathāgato anuttaraṃ sammāsambodhiṃ abhisambuddho’tipi, ‘idha tathāgatena anuttaraṃ dhammacakkaṃ pavattita’ntipi, ‘idha tathāgato anupādisesāya nibbānadhātuyā parinibbuto’tipi. Ye hi keci, ānanda, cetiyacārikaṃ āhiṇḍantā pasannacittā kālaṅkarissanti, sabbe te kāyassa bhedā paraṃ maraṇā sugatiṃ saggaṃ lokaṃ upapajjissantī’’ti.</p> <p rend="subhead">Ānandapucchākathā</p>
202. “Formerly, lord, monks who had spent the Rains in various places used to come to see the Tathāgata. And we used to welcome them so that such inspiring monks might see you and pay their respects. But now, after the Blessed One is gone, we won’t get to see or attend to the monks who inspire the heart.”

“There are four places, Ānanda, that a pious person should visit and look upon with feelings of reverence. Which four? ‘Here the *Tathāgata* was born!’ This, Ānanda, is a place that a pious person should visit and look upon with feelings of reverence. ‘Here the *Tathāgata* became fully enlightened in unsurpassed, supreme Enlightenment!’ This, Ānanda, is a place that a pious person should visit and look upon with feelings of reverence. ‘Here the *Tathāgata* set rolling the unexcelled Wheel of the *Dharma*!’ This, Ānanda, is a place that a pious person should visit and look upon with feelings of reverence. ‘Here the *Tathāgata* passed away into the state of *Nirvāṇa* in which no element of clinging remains!’ This, Ānanda, are the four places that a pious person should visit and look upon with feelings of reverence."

“And truly there will come to these places, Ānanda, pious monks and nuns, laymen and laywomen, reflecting: ‘Here the *Tathāgata* was born! Here the *Tathāgata* became fully enlightened in unsurpassed, supreme Enlightenment! Here the *Tathāgata* set rolling the unexcelled Wheel of the *Dharma*! Here the *Tathāgata* passed away into the state of *Nirvāṇa* in which no element of clinging remains!’ And any who die while making the pilgrimage to these shrines with a devout heart will, at the breaking-up of the body after death, be reborn in a heavenly world.”

The Story of Ānanda's Questions
<p n="202" rend="bodytext"><hi rend="paranum">202</hi><hi rend="dot">.</hi><hi rend="bold">Vassaṃvuṭṭhā</hi>ti buddhakāle kira dvīsu kālesu bhikkhū sannipatanti upakaṭṭhāya vassūpanāyikāya kammaṭṭhānaggahaṇatthaṃ, vuṭṭhavassā ca gahitakammaṭṭhānānuyogena nibbattitavisesārocanatthaṃ. Yathā ca buddhakāle, evaṃ tambapaṇṇidīpepi apāragaṅgāya bhikkhū lohapāsāde sannipatiṃsu, pāragaṅgāya bhikkhū tissamahāvihāre. Tesu apāragaṅgāya bhikkhū saṅkārachaḍḍakasammajjaniyo gahetvā āgantvā mahāvihāre sannipatitvā cetiye sudhākammaṃ katvā – ‘‘vuṭṭhavassā āgantvā lohapāsāde sannipatathā’’ti vattaṃ katvā phāsukaṭṭhānesu vasitvā vuṭṭhavassā āgantvā lohapāsāde pañcanikāyamaṇḍale, yesaṃ pāḷi paguṇā, te pāḷiṃ sajjhāyanti. Yesaṃ aṭṭhakathā paguṇā, te aṭṭhakathaṃ sajjhāyanti. <pb ed="M" n="2.0173"/> Yo pāḷiṃ vā aṭṭhakathaṃ vā virādheti <pb ed="V" n="2.0155"/>, taṃ – ‘‘kassa santike tayā gahita’’nti vicāretvā ujuṃ katvā gāhāpenti. Pāragaṅgāvāsinopi tissamahāvihāre evameva karonti. Evaṃ dvīsu kālesu sannipatitesu bhikkhūsu ye pure vassūpanāyikāya kammaṭṭhānaṃ gahetvā gatā visesārocanatthaṃ āgacchanti, evarūpe sandhāya ‘‘pubbe bhante vassaṃvuṭṭhā’’tiādimāha.</p> <p rend="bodytext"><hi rend="bold">Manobhāvanīye</hi>ti manasā bhāvite sambhāvite. Ye vā mano manaṃ bhāventi vaḍḍhenti rāgarajādīni pavāhenti, evarūpeti attho. Thero <pb ed="P" n="2.0582"/> kira vattasampanno mahallakaṃ bhikkhuṃ disvā thaddho hutvā na nisīdati, paccuggamanaṃ katvā hatthato chattañca pattacīvarañca gahetvā pīṭhaṃ papphoṭetvā deti, tattha nisinnassa vattaṃ katvā senāsanaṃ paṭijaggitvā deti. Navakaṃ bhikkhuṃ disvā tuṇhībhūto na nisīdati, samīpe ṭhatvā vattaṃ karoti. So tāya vattapaṭipattiyā aparihāniṃ patthayamāno evamāha.</p> <hi rend="bold">Manobhāvanīye</hi> <pb ed="P" n="2.0582"/> <p rend="bodytext">Atha bhagavā – ‘‘ānando manobhāvanīyānaṃ dassanaṃ na labhissāmī’’ti cinteti, handassa, manobhāvanīyānaṃ dassanaṭṭhānaṃ ācikkhissāmi, yattha vasanto ito cito ca anāhiṇḍitvāva lacchati manobhāvanīye bhikkhū dassanāyāti cintetvā <hi rend="bold">cattārimānī</hi>tiādimāha.</p> <hi rend="bold">cattārimānī</hi> <p rend="bodytext">Tattha <hi rend="bold">saddhassā</hi>ti buddhādīsu pasannacittassa vattasampannassa, yassa pāto paṭṭhāya cetiyaṅgaṇavattādīni sabbavattāni katāneva paññāyanti. <hi rend="bold">Dassanīyānī</hi>ti dassanārahāni dassanatthāya gantabbāni. <hi rend="bold">Saṃvejanīyānī</hi>ti saṃvegajanakāni. <hi rend="bold">Ṭhānānī</hi>ti kāraṇāni, padesaṭhānāneva vā.</p> <hi rend="bold">saddhassā</hi> <hi rend="bold">Dassanīyānī</hi> <hi rend="bold">Saṃvejanīyānī</hi> <hi rend="bold">Ṭhānānī</hi> <p rend="bodytext"><hi rend="bold">Ye hi kecī</hi>ti idaṃ cetiyacārikāya satthakabhāvadassanatthaṃ vuttaṃ. Tattha <hi rend="bold">cetiyacārikaṃ āhiṇḍantā</hi>ti ye ca tāva tattha tattha cetiyaṅgaṇaṃ sammajjantā, āsanāni dhovantā bodhimhi udakaṃ siñcantā āhiṇḍanti, tesu vattabbameva natthi asukavihāre ‘‘cetiyaṃ vandissāmā’’ti nikkhamitvā pasannacittā antarā kālaṅkarontāpi anantarāyena sagge patiṭṭhahissanti yevāti dasseti.</p> <hi rend="bold">Ye hi kecī</hi> <hi rend="bold">cetiyacārikaṃ āhiṇḍantā</hi> <p rend="subhead">Ānandapucchākathāvaṇṇanā</p>
202. *Vassaṃvuṭṭhā* means that at the time of the Buddha, monks would assemble at two times: near the approach of the rainy season retreat (*vassūpanāyikā*) to receive meditation instruction (*kammaṭṭhāna*), and after the rainy season retreat to announce the attainment of special qualities through the practice of the meditation instruction they had received.

Just as in the time of the Buddha, so too on Tambapaṇṇidīpa (Sri Lanka), monks from Aparagaṅga assembled at the Lohapāsāda (Brazen Palace), and monks from Pāragaṅga assembled at the Tissamahāvihāra.

Of those, the monks from Aparagaṅga, having taken brooms for sweeping away debris and having come to the Mahāvihāra, having assembled and performed the lime-plastering of the *cetiya*, having made the rule, "Having completed the rainy season retreat, come and assemble at the Lohapāsāda," having lived in comfortable places, having completed the rainy season retreat, having come to the Lohapāsāda in the Pañcanikāyamaṇḍala (the area of the five fraternities), those for whom the Pali was well-versed recited the Pali.

Those for whom the commentary (*aṭṭhakathā*) was well-versed recited the commentary.

If someone violates the Pali or the commentary, having investigated, "From whom did you receive [this teaching]?" they set it right and cause [him] to take it up [correctly].

The residents of Pāragaṅga also do just this at the Tissamahāvihāra.

Thus, in the case of monks assembled at these two times, those who had previously gone to receive *kammaṭṭhāna* for the *vassūpanāyikā* come to announce their special attainments. Referring to those of such a nature, [the text] begins by saying, "Previously, venerable sirs, *vassaṃvuṭṭhā.*"

*Manobhāvanīye* means cultivated and esteemed in the mind.

Or, those who cultivate and increase in the mind sensual desire (*rāga*), passion (*raja*), etc., and who send [them] forth, this is the meaning.

The elder, endowed with good conduct (*vattasampanno*), having seen an elder monk, being respectful, does not sit down, having gone to meet [him], having taken the umbrella and bowl and robe from his hand, having tapped the seat, he gives [it to him], having performed the duties for the one sitting there, having prepared the lodging, he gives [it to him].

Having seen a novice monk, being silent, he does not sit down, having stood nearby, he performs the duties.

He, desiring non-decline in that practice of duties, spoke thus.

*Manobhāvanīye*

Then, the Blessed One thought, "Ānanda will not obtain the sight of those who are delightful to the mind." Then, because of that, [the Buddha thought]: "I will point out the place of seeing those who are delightful to the mind, where, dwelling there, without wandering here and there, he will easily obtain monks who are delightful to the mind for the purpose of seeing." Having thought this, he began by saying "*cattārimānī*."

*Cattārimānī*: There, *saddhassā* means one whose mind is serene towards the Buddha and so forth, one endowed with good conduct, for whom all the duties, beginning with the duties of the *cetiya*-courtyard, appear to be done from the very start of the day.

*Dassanīyānī* means worthy of being seen, to be gone to for the purpose of seeing.

*Saṃvejanīyānī* means causing agitation.

*Ṭhānānī* means causes, or simply places.

*Saddhassā dassanīyānī saṃvejanīyānī ṭhānānī*: *Ye hi kecī* This was said for the purpose of showing the profitable nature of wandering to a *cetiya*.

There, *cetiyacārikaṃ āhiṇḍantā* means those who, in various places, sweep the *cetiya* courtyard, wash the seats, sprinkle water on the *bodhi* tree, and wander about. Of those, there is nothing more to be said. [Even] those of serene mind who, having set out thinking, "We will worship the *cetiya*" in a certain monastery, die in between, even they will be established in heaven without obstruction. This he shows.

*Ye hi kecī cetiyacārikaṃ āhiṇḍantā*: Explanation of Ānanda's question.
203
<p n="203" rend="bodytext"><hi rend="paranum">203</hi><hi rend="dot">.</hi> ‘‘Kathaṃ <pb ed="T" n="2.0164"/> mayaṃ, bhante, mātugāme paṭipajjāmā’’ti? ‘‘Adassanaṃ, ānandā’’ti. ‘‘Dassane, bhagavā, sati kathaṃ paṭipajjitabba’’nti? ‘‘Anālāpo, ānandā’’ti <pb ed="M" n="2.0117"/>. ‘‘Ālapantena pana, bhante, kathaṃ paṭipajjitabba’’nti? ‘‘Sati, ānanda, upaṭṭhāpetabbā’’ti.</p>
[API Error: 502]
<p n="203" rend="bodytext"><hi rend="paranum">203</hi><hi rend="dot">.</hi><hi rend="bold">Adassanaṃ</hi><pb ed="V" n="2.0156"/><pb ed="M" n="2.0174"/>, <hi rend="bold">ānandā</hi>ti yadetaṃ mātugāmassa adassanaṃ, ayamettha uttamā paṭipattīti dasseti. Dvāraṃ pidahitvā senāsane nisinno hi bhikkhu āgantvā dvāre ṭhitampi mātugāmaṃ yāva na passati, tāvassa ekaṃseneva na lobho uppajjati, na cittaṃ calati. Dassane pana satiyeva tadubhayampi assa. Tenāha – ‘‘adassanaṃ ānandā’’ti. <hi rend="bold">Dassane bhagavā sati katha</hi>nti bhikkhaṃ gahetvā upagataṭṭhānādīsu dassane sati kathaṃ paṭipajjitabbanti pucchati. Atha bhagavā yasmā khaggaṃ gahetvā – ‘‘sace mayā saddhiṃ ālapasi, ettheva te sīsaṃ pātessāmī’’ti ṭhitapurisena vā, ‘‘sace mayā saddhiṃ ālapasi, ettheva te maṃsaṃ murumurāpetvā khādissāmī’’ti <pb ed="P" n="2.0583"/> ṭhitayakkhiniyā vā ālapituṃ varaṃ. Ekasseva hi attabhāvassa tappaccayā vināso hoti, na apāyesu aparicchinnadukkhānubhavanaṃ. Mātugāmena pana ālāpasallāpe sati vissāso hoti, vissāse sati otāro hoti, otiṇṇacitto sīlabyasanaṃ patvā apāyapūrako hoti; tasmā <hi rend="bold">anālāpo</hi>ti āha. Vuttampi cetaṃ –</p> <p rend="gatha1">‘‘Sallape asihatthena, pisācenāpi sallape;</p> <p rend="gatha2">Āsīvisampi āsīde, yena daṭṭho na jīvati;</p> <p rend="gathalast">Na tveva eko ekāya, mātugāmena sallape’’ti. (a. ni. 5.55);</p> <p rend="bodytext"><hi rend="bold">Ālapantena panā</hi>ti sace mātugāmo divasaṃ vā pucchati, sīlaṃ vā yācati, dhammaṃ vā sotukāmo hoti, pañhaṃ vā pucchati, tathārūpaṃ vā panassa pabbajitehi kattabbakammaṃ hoti, evarūpe kāle anālapantaṃ ‘‘mūgo ayaṃ, badhiro ayaṃ, bhutvāva baddhamukho nisīdatī’’ti vadati, tasmā avassaṃ ālapitabbaṃ hoti. Evaṃ ālapantena pana kathaṃ paṭipajjitabbanti pucchati. Atha bhagavā – ‘‘etha tumhe, bhikkhave, mātumattīsu mātucittaṃ upaṭṭhapetha, bhaginimattīsu bhaginicittaṃ upaṭṭhapetha, dhītumattīsu dhītucittaṃ upaṭṭhapethā’’ti (saṃ. ni. 4.127) imaṃ ovādaṃ sandhāya <hi rend="bold">sati, ānanda, upaṭṭhapetabbā</hi>ti āha.</p> <hi rend="bold">Ālapantena panā</hi> <hi rend="bold">sati, ānanda, upaṭṭhapetabbā</hi>
[API Error: 502]
204
<p n="204" rend="bodytext"><hi rend="paranum">204</hi><hi rend="dot">.</hi> ‘‘Kathaṃ <pb ed="V" n="2.0107"/> mayaṃ, bhante, tathāgatassa sarīre paṭipajjāmā’’ti? ‘‘Abyāvaṭā tumhe, ānanda, hotha tathāgatassa sarīrapūjāya. Iṅgha tumhe, ānanda, sāratthe ghaṭatha anuyuñjatha <note>sadatthe anuyuñjatha (sī. syā.), sadatthaṃ anuyuñjatha (pī.), sāratthe anuyuñjatha (ka.)</note>, sāratthe appamattā ātāpino pahitattā viharatha. Santānanda, khattiyapaṇḍitāpi brāhmaṇapaṇḍitāpi gahapatipaṇḍitāpi tathāgate abhippasannā, te tathāgatassa sarīrapūjaṃ karissantī’’ti.</p>
<p n="204" rend="bodytext"><hi rend="paranum">204</hi><hi rend="dot">.
</hi> "How, venerable sir (bhante), should we treat the body (śarīra) of the *tathāgata*?" "Ānanda, you should not be occupied with the worship (pūjā) of the body (śarīra) of the *tathāgata*.

Rather, Ānanda, strive (ghaṭatha) and be zealous (anuyuñjatha) on your own behalf, for your own good (sāratthe).
being heedful (appamattā), ardent (*ātāpino*), & resolute (*pahitattā*) you should apply yourselves to your own good (sāratthe).
Ānanda, wise nobles (*khattiyapaṇḍitā*), wise brahmans (*brāhmaṇapaṇḍitā*), & wise householders (*gahapatipaṇḍitā*) are highly confident (*abhippasannā*) in the *tathāgata*. They will conduct the *tathāgata*'s funeral (śarīrapūjaṃ karissantī)."
</p>
<p n="204" rend="bodytext"><hi rend="paranum">204</hi><hi rend="dot">.</hi><hi rend="bold">Abyāvaṭā</hi>ti atantibaddhā nirussukkā hotha. <hi rend="bold">Sāratthe ghaṭathā</hi>ti uttamatthe arahatte ghaṭetha. <hi rend="bold">Anuyuñjathā</hi>ti tadadhigamāya anuyogaṃ <pb ed="M" n="2.0175"/> karotha. <hi rend="bold">Appamattā</hi>ti tattha avippamuṭṭhasatī. Vīriyātāpayogena <hi rend="bold">ātāpino.</hi> Kāye ca jīvite ca nirapekkhatāya <hi rend="bold">pahitattā</hi> pesitacittā viharatha.</p>
204. *Abyāvaṭā* means not bound by craving, without attachment.
*Sāratthe ghaṭathā* means strive for the highest purpose, strive for arhathood.
*Anuyuñjathā* means engage in repeated practice for the attainment of that.
*Appamattā* means with unforgotten mindfulness there.
Through the application of energetic heat, *ātāpino*.
In body and in life, being resolutely *pahitattā* through detachment, abide with directed minds.
205
<p n="205" rend="bodytext"><hi rend="paranum">205</hi><hi rend="dot">.</hi> ‘‘Kathaṃ pana, bhante, tathāgatassa sarīre paṭipajjitabba’’nti? ‘‘Yathā kho, ānanda, rañño cakkavattissa sarīre paṭipajjanti, evaṃ tathāgatassa sarīre paṭipajjitabba’’nti. ‘‘Kathaṃ pana, bhante, rañño cakkavattissa sarīre paṭipajjantī’’ti? ‘‘Rañño, ānanda, cakkavattissa sarīraṃ ahatena vatthena veṭhenti, ahatena vatthena veṭhetvā vihatena kappāsena veṭhenti, vihatena kappāsena veṭhetvā ahatena vatthena <pb ed="P" n="2.0142"/> veṭhenti. Etenupāyena pañcahi yugasatehi rañño cakkavattissa sarīraṃ <note>sarīre (syā. ka.)</note> veṭhetvā āyasāya teladoṇiyā pakkhipitvā aññissā āyasāya doṇiyā paṭikujjitvā sabbagandhānaṃ citakaṃ karitvā rañño cakkavattissa sarīraṃ jhāpenti. Cātumahāpathe <note>cātummahāpathe (sī. syā. kaṃ. pī.)</note> rañño cakkavattissa thūpaṃ karonti <pb ed="T" n="2.0165"/>. Evaṃ kho, ānanda, rañño cakkavattissa sarīre paṭipajjanti. Yathā kho, ānanda, rañño cakkavattissa sarīre paṭipajjanti, evaṃ tathāgatassa sarīre paṭipajjitabbaṃ. Cātumahāpathe tathāgatassa thūpo kātabbo. Tattha ye mālaṃ vā gandhaṃ vā cuṇṇakaṃ <note>vaṇṇakaṃ (sī. pī.)</note> vā āropessanti vā abhivādessanti vā cittaṃ vā pasādessanti tesaṃ taṃ bhavissati dīgharattaṃ hitāya sukhāya.</p> <p rend="subhead">Thūpārahapuggalo</p>
205. "But how, venerable sir, should they proceed with the body of the *Tathāgata*?"

"Just as they proceed, Ānanda, with the body of a wheel-turning monarch (*rajño cakkavattissa sarīre patipajjanti*), so should they proceed with the body of the *Tathāgata*."

"But how, venerable sir, do they proceed with the body of a wheel-turning monarch?"

"Ānanda, they wrap the body of a wheel-turning monarch in new linen (*ahatena vatthena veṭhenti*). Having wrapped it in new linen, they wrap it in teased cotton. Having wrapped it in teased cotton, they wrap it again in new linen.

In this way, having wrapped the body of the wheel-turning monarch in five hundred layers of linen and cotton, they place it in an iron oil-vat (*āyasāya teladoṇiyā pakkhipitvā*) and cover it with another iron vat. Then, having made a pyre of all kinds of perfumes (*sabbagandhānaṃ citakaṃ karitvā*), they cremate the body of the wheel-turning monarch. At a crossroads (*cātumahāpathe*) they build a *stūpa* for the wheel-turning monarch.

That is how, Ānanda, they proceed with the body of a wheel-turning monarch. Just as they proceed with the body of a wheel-turning monarch, so should they proceed with the body of the *Tathāgata*. At a crossroads (*cātumahāpathe*) a *stūpa* should be built for the *Tathāgata*. Whoever offers garlands (*mālaṃ vā*), incense (*gandhaṃ vā*), or perfume powder (*cuṇṇakaṃ vā*) there, or reveres, or gladdens their minds, that will be for their long-term benefit and happiness.

A person worthy of a *stūpa*.
<p n="205" rend="bodytext"><hi rend="paranum">205</hi><hi rend="dot">.</hi><hi rend="bold">Kathaṃ</hi><pb ed="V" n="2.0157"/><hi rend="bold">pana, bhante</hi>ti tehi khattiyapaṇḍitādīhi kathaṃ paṭipajjitabbaṃ. Addhā maṃ te paṭipucchissanti – ‘‘kathaṃ, bhante, ānanda tathāgatassa sarīre paṭipajjitabba’’nti; ‘‘tesāhaṃ kathaṃ paṭivacanaṃ demī’’ti pucchati. <hi rend="bold">Ahatena vatthenā</hi>ti navena kāsikavatthena. <hi rend="bold">Vihatena kappāsenā</hi>ti supothitena kappāsena. Kāsikavatthañhi sukhumattā telaṃ na gaṇhāti, kappāso pana gaṇhāti. Tasmā ‘‘vihatena kappāsenā’’ti āha. <hi rend="bold">Āyasāyā</hi>ti sovaṇṇāya. Sovaṇṇañhi idha ‘‘ayasa’’nti adhippetaṃ.</p> <p rend="subhead">Thūpārahapuggalavaṇṇanā</p>
205. "How so? *bhante*?" How should those *kṣatriya* scholars and others act?

Indeed, they will ask me: "How, *bhante*, should the body of the *Tathāgata* be treated?" "How should I give them an answer?" he asks.

"*Ahatena vatthena*" means with new Kāśika cloth.

"*Vihatena kappāsena*" means with well-beaten cotton.

Because Kāśika cloth, due to its fineness, does not absorb oil, but cotton does absorb it.

Therefore, he said, "with well-beaten cotton."

"*Āyasāyā*" means with gold.

Indeed, here, gold is what is meant by "*ayasa*."

Description of the person worthy of a *stūpa*.
206
<p n="206" rend="bodytext"><hi rend="paranum">206</hi><hi rend="dot">.</hi> ‘‘Cattārome, ānanda, thūpārahā. Katame cattāro? Tathāgato arahaṃ sammāsambuddho thūpāraho, paccekasambuddho thūpāraho, tathāgatassa sāvako thūpāraho, rājā cakkavattī <note>cakkavatti (syā. ka.)</note> thūpārahoti.</p> <p rend="bodytext">‘‘Kiñcānanda <pb ed="M" n="2.0118"/>, atthavasaṃ paṭicca tathāgato arahaṃ sammāsambuddho thūpāraho? ‘Ayaṃ tassa bhagavato arahato sammāsambuddhassa thūpo’ti, ānanda, bahujanā cittaṃ pasādenti. Te tattha cittaṃ pasādetvā kāyassa bhedā paraṃ maraṇā sugatiṃ saggaṃ lokaṃ upapajjanti. Idaṃ kho, ānanda, atthavasaṃ paṭicca tathāgato arahaṃ sammāsambuddho thūpāraho.</p> <pb ed="M" n="2.0118"/> <p rend="bodytext">‘‘Kiñcānanda, atthavasaṃ paṭicca paccekasambuddho thūpāraho? ‘Ayaṃ tassa bhagavato paccekasambuddhassa <pb ed="V" n="2.0108"/><pb ed="P" n="2.0143"/> thūpo’ti, ānanda, bahujanā cittaṃ pasādenti. Te tattha cittaṃ pasādetvā kāyassa bhedā paraṃ maraṇā sugatiṃ saggaṃ lokaṃ upapajjanti. Idaṃ kho, ānanda, atthavasaṃ paṭicca paccekasambuddho thūpāraho.</p> <pb ed="V" n="2.0108"/> <pb ed="P" n="2.0143"/> <p rend="bodytext">‘‘Kiñcānanda, atthavasaṃ paṭicca tathāgatassa sāvako <pb ed="T" n="2.0166"/> thūpāraho? ‘Ayaṃ tassa bhagavato arahato sammāsambuddhassa sāvakassa thūpo’ti ānanda, bahujanā cittaṃ pasādenti. Te tattha cittaṃ pasādetvā kāyassa bhedā paraṃ maraṇā sugatiṃ saggaṃ lokaṃ upapajjanti. Idaṃ kho, ānanda, atthavasaṃ paṭicca tathāgatassa sāvako thūpāraho.</p> <pb ed="T" n="2.0166"/> <p rend="bodytext">‘‘Kiñcānanda, atthavasaṃ paṭicca rājā cakkavattī thūpāraho? ‘Ayaṃ tassa dhammikassa dhammarañño thūpo’ti, ānanda, bahujanā cittaṃ pasādenti. Te tattha cittaṃ pasādetvā kāyassa bhedā paraṃ maraṇā sugatiṃ saggaṃ lokaṃ upapajjanti. Idaṃ kho, ānanda, atthavasaṃ paṭicca rājā cakkavattī thūpāraho. Ime kho, ānanda cattāro thūpārahā’’ti.</p> <p rend="subhead">Ānandaacchariyadhammo</p>
“These four, Ānanda, are worthy of a stupa (thūpāraha).

Which four? A *Tathāgata*, a worthy one, a completely awakened Buddha (sammāsambuddho), is worthy of a stupa; an individual Buddha (paccekasambuddho) is worthy of a stupa; a disciple (*śrāvaka*) of a *Tathāgata* is worthy of a stupa; a wheel-turning monarch (*cakravartin*) is worthy of a stupa.

And for what reason, Ānanda, is a *Tathāgata*, a worthy one, a completely awakened Buddha worthy of a stupa? Because, Ānanda, many people are calmed and made happy at the thought: ‘This is the stupa of that Blessed One, worthy and completely awakened Buddha.’ Having calmed their minds there, then—on the break-up of the body, after death—they will reappear in a good destination, a heavenly world (sugatiṃ saggaṃ lokaṃ upapajjanti). It is for this reason, Ānanda, that a *Tathāgata*, a worthy one, a completely awakened Buddha is worthy of a stupa.

And for what reason, Ānanda, is an individual Buddha worthy of a stupa? Because, Ānanda, many people are calmed and made happy at the thought: ‘This is the stupa of that Blessed One, an individual Buddha’. Having calmed their minds there, then—on the break-up of the body, after death—they will reappear in a good destination, a heavenly world. It is for this reason, Ānanda, that an individual Buddha is worthy of a stupa.

And for what reason, Ānanda, is a disciple of a *Tathāgata* worthy of a stupa? Because, Ānanda, many people are calmed and made happy at the thought: ‘This is the stupa of a disciple of that Blessed One, worthy and completely awakened Buddha.’ Having calmed their minds there, then—on the break-up of the body, after death—they will reappear in a good destination, a heavenly world. It is for this reason, Ānanda, that a disciple of a *Tathāgata* is worthy of a stupa.

And for what reason, Ānanda, is a wheel-turning monarch worthy of a stupa? Because, Ānanda, many people are calmed and made happy at the thought: ‘This is the stupa of that righteous monarch, a king of dharma (dhammarañño).’ Having calmed their minds there, then—on the break-up of the body, after death—they will reappear in a good destination, a heavenly world. It is for this reason, Ānanda, that a wheel-turning monarch is worthy of a stupa. These, Ānanda, are the four who are worthy of a stupa.”
<p n="206" rend="bodytext"><hi rend="paranum">206</hi><hi rend="dot">.</hi><hi rend="bold">Rājā cakkavattī</hi>ti ettha kasmā bhagavā agāramajjhe vasitvā kālaṅkatassa rañño thūpārahataṃ anujānāti, na sīlavato puthujjanassa bhikkhussāti? Anacchariyattā. Puthujjanabhikkhūnañhi <pb ed="P" n="2.0584"/> thūpe anuññāyamāne tambapaṇṇidīpe tāva thūpānaṃ okāso na bhaveyya, tathā aññesu ṭhānesu. Tasmā ‘‘anacchariyā te bhavissantī’’ti nānujānāti. Rājā cakkavattī ekova nibbattati, tenassa thūpo acchariyo hoti. Puthujjanasīlavato pana parinibbutabhikkhuno viya mahantampi sakkāraṃ kātuṃ vaṭṭatiyeva.</p> <p rend="subhead">Ānandaacchariyadhammavaṇṇanā</p>
<p n="206" rend="bodytext"><hi rend="paranum">206</hi><hi rend="dot">.
</hi><hi rend="bold">rājā cakkavattī</hi>: Here, why does the Blessed One, having lived in the midst of houses, approve of a *stūpa* being worthy of a deceased king, but not of a virtuous ordinary *bhikkhu*? Because it is not extraordinary. For if *stūpas* were to be approved for ordinary *bhikkhus*, then even on the island of Tambapaṇṇi there would be no space for *stūpas*, and likewise in other places. Therefore, he does not approve, [saying,] "They will not be extraordinary." A *rājā cakkavattī* arises alone; therefore, his *stūpa* is extraordinary. However, it is indeed fitting to perform even a great honor for an ordinary, virtuous *parinibbuta-bhikkhu*, like one who has attained *parinibbāna*.
</p> <p rend="subhead">Description of Ānanda's Extraordinary Qualities</p>
207
<p n="207" rend="bodytext"><hi rend="paranum">207</hi><hi rend="dot">.</hi> Atha kho āyasmā ānando vihāraṃ pavisitvā kapisīsaṃ ālambitvā rodamāno aṭṭhāsi – ‘‘ahañca vatamhi sekho sakaraṇīyo, satthu ca me parinibbānaṃ bhavissati, yo mama anukampako’’ti. Atha kho bhagavā bhikkhū āmantesi – ‘‘kahaṃ nu kho, bhikkhave, ānando’’ti? ‘‘Eso, bhante, āyasmā ānando vihāraṃ pavisitvā kapisīsaṃ ālambitvā rodamāno ṭhito – ‘ahañca vatamhi sekho sakaraṇīyo, satthu ca me parinibbānaṃ bhavissati, yo mama anukampako’’’ti. Atha kho bhagavā aññataraṃ bhikkhuṃ āmantesi – ‘‘ehi tvaṃ, bhikkhu, mama vacanena ānandaṃ āmantehi <pb ed="M" n="2.0119"/> – ‘satthā taṃ, āvuso ānanda, āmantetī’’’ti. ‘‘Evaṃ <pb ed="P" n="2.0144"/>, bhante’’ti kho so bhikkhu bhagavato paṭissutvā yenāyasmā ānando tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā āyasmantaṃ ānandaṃ etadavoca <pb ed="T" n="2.0167"/> – ‘‘satthā taṃ, āvuso ānanda, āmantetī’’ti. ‘‘Evamāvuso’’ti kho āyasmā ānando tassa bhikkhuno paṭissutvā yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṃ abhivādetvā ekamantaṃ nisīdi. Ekamantaṃ nisinnaṃ kho āyasmantaṃ ānandaṃ bhagavā etadavoca – ‘‘alaṃ, ānanda, mā soci mā paridevi, nanu etaṃ, ānanda, mayā paṭikacceva akkhātaṃ – ‘sabbeheva piyehi manāpehi nānābhāvo vinābhāvo aññathābhāvo’; taṃ kutettha, ānanda, labbhā. Yaṃ taṃ jātaṃ bhūtaṃ saṅkhataṃ <pb ed="V" n="2.0109"/> palokadhammaṃ, taṃ vata tathāgatassāpi sarīraṃ mā palujjī’ti netaṃ ṭhānaṃ vijjati. Dīgharattaṃ kho te, ānanda, tathāgato paccupaṭṭhito mettena kāyakammena hitena sukhena advayena appamāṇena, mettena vacīkammena hitena sukhena advayena appamāṇena, mettena manokammena hitena sukhena advayena appamāṇena. Katapuññosi tvaṃ, ānanda, padhānamanuyuñja, khippaṃ hohisi anāsavo’’ti.</p>
207. Then the Venerable Ānanda went into the monastery, leaned against the doorpost, and stood weeping: “Alas, I am still a learner, with much to do! And the Teacher is about to attain parinirvāṇa, he who was so compassionate to me!”

Then the Blessed One addressed the monks: “Where is Ānanda?”

“Venerable Sir, the Venerable Ānanda has gone into the monastery, leaned against the doorpost, and is standing there weeping, saying: ‘Alas, I am still a learner, with much to do! And the Teacher is about to attain *parinirvāṇa*, he who was so compassionate to me!’”

Then the Blessed One addressed a certain monk: “Go, monk, and summon Ānanda in my name, saying, ‘The Teacher calls you, friend Ānanda.’”

“Yes, Venerable Sir,” said that monk in response to the Blessed One. He went to the Venerable Ānanda, and on arrival, he said to the Venerable Ānanda: “The Teacher calls you, friend Ānanda.”

“Very well, friend,” replied the Venerable Ānanda to that monk. Then he went to the Blessed One, and after bowing down to him, sat down to one side.

As the Venerable Ānanda was sitting to one side, the Blessed One said to him: “Enough, Ānanda! Do not grieve, do not lament! Have I not already declared that separation, division, and otherness are inevitable with all things that are dear and beloved? Where, Ānanda, could this *not* be found?

That which is born, come into being, compounded, is subject to decay; it is impossible that the body even of the *Tathāgata* should *not* decay.

For a long time, Ānanda, the *Tathāgata* has been attended upon by you with loving-kindness in thought, word, and deed, helpfully, happily, wholeheartedly, and without measure.

You have performed meritorious deeds, Ānanda. Strive on, and you will quickly be free from defilements.” ( *katapuññosi tvaṃ, Ānanda, padhānamanuyuñja, khippaṃ hohisi anāsavo’ti.*)
<p n="207" rend="bodytext"><hi rend="paranum">207</hi><hi rend="dot">.</hi><hi rend="bold">Vihāra</hi>nti idha maṇḍalamālo vihāroti adhippeto, taṃ pavisitvā. <hi rend="bold">Kapisīsa</hi>nti dvārabāhakoṭiyaṃ ṭhitaṃ aggaḷarukkhaṃ. <hi rend="bold">Rodamāno aṭṭhāsī</hi>ti so kirāyasmā cintesi – ‘‘satthārā mama saṃvegajanakaṃ vasanaṭṭhānaṃ kathitaṃ, cetiyacārikāya sātthakabhāvo kathito, mātugāme paṭipajjitabbapañho vissajjito, attano sarīre paṭipatti akkhātā, cattāro thūpārahā kathitā, dhuvaṃ ajja bhagavā parinibbāyissatī’’ti, tassevaṃ cintayato balavadomanassaṃ uppajji. Athassa etadahosi – ‘‘bhagavato santike rodanaṃ nāma aphāsukaṃ, ekamantaṃ gantvā <pb ed="M" n="2.0176"/> sokaṃ tanukaṃ karissāmī’’ti, so tathā akāsi. Tena vuttaṃ – ‘‘rodamāno aṭṭhāsī’’ti.</p> <p rend="bodytext"><hi rend="bold">Ahañca vatamhī</hi>ti ahañca vata amhi, ahaṃ vatamhītipi pāṭho. <hi rend="bold">Yo mama anukampako</hi>ti yo maṃ anukampati anusāsati, sve dāni paṭṭhāya kassa mukhadhovanaṃ dassāmi, kassa pāde dhovissāmi, kassa senāsanaṃ paṭijaggissāmi, kassa pattacīvaraṃ gahetvā vicarissāmīti bahuṃ vilapi. <hi rend="bold">Āmantesī</hi>ti bhikkhusaṅghassa antare theraṃ adisvā āmantesi.</p> <hi rend="bold">Ahañca vatamhī</hi> <hi rend="bold">Yo mama anukampako</hi> <hi rend="bold">Āmantesī</hi> <p rend="bodytext"><hi rend="bold">Mettena</hi><pb ed="V" n="2.0158"/><hi rend="bold">kāyakammenā</hi>ti mettacittavasena pavattitena mukhadhovanadānādikāyakammena. <hi rend="bold">Hitenā</hi>ti hitavuddhiyā katena. <hi rend="bold">Sukhenā</hi>ti sukhasomanasseneva katena, na dukkhinā dummanena hutvāti attho. <hi rend="bold">Advayenā</hi>ti dve koṭṭhāse katvā akatena. Yathā hi eko sammukhāva karoti na parammukhā, eko parammukhāva karoti na sammukhā evaṃ vibhāgaṃ akatvā katenāti vuttaṃ hoti. <hi rend="bold">Appamāṇenā</hi>ti pamāṇavirahitena. Cakkavāḷampi hi atisambādhaṃ, bhavaggampi atinīcaṃ, tayā kataṃ kāyakammameva <pb ed="P" n="2.0585"/> bahunti dasseti.</p> <hi rend="bold">Mettena</hi> <pb ed="V" n="2.0158"/> <hi rend="bold">kāyakammenā</hi> <hi rend="bold">Hitenā</hi> <hi rend="bold">Sukhenā</hi> <hi rend="bold">Advayenā</hi> <hi rend="bold">Appamāṇenā</hi> <pb ed="P" n="2.0585"/> <p rend="bodytext"><hi rend="bold">Mettena vacīkammenā</hi>ti mettacittavasena pavattitena mukhadhovanakālārocanādinā vacīkammena. Api ca ovādaṃ sutvā – ‘‘sādhu, bhante’’ti vacanampi mettaṃ vacīkammameva. <hi rend="bold">Mettena manokammenā</hi>ti kālasseva sarīrapaṭijagganaṃ katvā vivittāsane nisīditvā – ‘‘satthā arogo hotu, abyāpajjo sukhī’’ti evaṃ pavattitena manokammena. <hi rend="bold">Katapuññosī</hi>ti kappasatasahassaṃ abhinīhārasampannosīti dasseti. Katapuññosīti ca ettāvatā vissattho mā pamādamāpajji, atha kho padhānamanuyuñja. Evañhi anuyutto khippaṃ hohisi anāsavo, dhammasaṅgītikāle arahattaṃ pāpuṇissasi.
