Na hi mādisassa katapāricariyā nipphalā nāma hotīti dasseti.</p> <hi rend="bold">Mettena vacīkammenā</hi> <hi rend="bold">Mettena manokammenā</hi> <hi rend="bold">Katapuññosī</hi>
207. *Vihāra* means here a *vihāra* with a circular arrangement of garlands. Having entered into that.

*Kapisīsa* means the cross-bar (*aggaḷarukkhaṃ*) fixed at the door pillar corner (*dvārabāhakoṭiyaṃ ṭhitaṃ*).

*Rodamāno aṭṭhāsī* means that venerable one thought, “The Teacher has spoken of a dwelling place productive of religious emotion (*saṃvegajanakaṃ vasanaṭṭhānaṃ*), the advantage of pilgrimage to a shrine (*cetiyacārikāya sātthakabhāvo*) has been spoken of, the question to be practiced regarding a woman (*mātugāme paṭipajjitabbapañho*) has been explained, practice regarding one's own body (*attano śarīre paṭipatti*) has been declared, four worthy of a stupa (*cattāro thūpārahā*) have been spoken of, surely today the Blessed One will attain *parinirvāṇa*," thinking thus, a strong grief (*balavadomanassaṃ*) arose.

Then this occurred to him: "Weeping (*rodanaṃ*) in the presence of the Blessed One is unseemly (*aphāsukaṃ*), having gone to a secluded place, I will lessen (*tanukaṃ karissāmī’ti*) [my] sorrow (*śokaṃ*)," thus he did.

Therefore it was said – “He stood weeping (*rodamāno aṭṭhāsī*)."

*Ahañca vatamhī* means *ahañca vata amhi*, there is also the reading *ahaṃ vatamhītipi*.

*Yo mama anukampako* means he who has compassion on me (*yo maṃ anukampati*) and instructs me (*anusāsati*), from tomorrow onwards to whom will I give face-washing water (*mukhadhovanaṃ dassāmi*)? Whose feet will I wash (*pāde dhovissāmi*)? Whose lodging will I prepare (*senāsanaṃ paṭijaggissāmi*)? Whose bowl and robe (*pattacīvaraṃ*) having taken, will I wander about (*vicarissāmīti*)? He lamented much (*bahuṃ vilapi*).

*Āmantesī* means having not seen the elder (*theraṃ adisvā*) in the midst of the *bhikkhusaṅgha*, he addressed him (*āmantesi*).

*Ahañca vatamhī yo mama anukampako āmantesī mettena kāyakammenā* means with loving-kindness by way of bodily action (*mettacittavasena pavattitena mukhadhovanadānādikāyakammena*).

*Hitenā* means done with the increase of benefit (*hitavuddhiyā katena*).

*Sukhena* means done with pleasure and joy (*sukhasomanasseneva katena*), not having become sorrowful and sad (*na dukkhinā dummanena hutvāti*), is the meaning (*attho*).

*Advayenā* means having made two portions (*dve koṭṭhāse katvā*) by the non-dual (*akatena*).

Just as one makes directly (*sammukhāva karoti*) and not behind the back (*na parammukhā*), one makes behind the back (*parammukhāva karoti*) and not directly (*na sammukhā*), thus without making a division, it is said to be done by the non-dual (*evaṃ vibhāgaṃ akatvā katenāti vuttaṃ hoti*).

*Appamāṇenā* means without measure (*pamāṇavirahitena*).

For even the *cakkavāḷa* is very crowded (*atisambādhaṃ*), even the peak of existence (*bhavaggaṃ*) is very low (*atinīcaṃ*), the bodily action (*kāyakammameva*) done by you (*tayā kataṃ*) shows much (*bahunti dasseti*).

*Mettena kāyakammenā hitenā sukhena advayenā appamāṇenā mettena vacīkammenā* means with loving-kindness by way of verbal action (*mettacittavasena pavattitena mukhadhovanakālārocanādinā vacīkammena*).

Moreover, having heard the advice (*ovādaṃ sutvā*) – “Good, venerable sir (*sādhu, bhante*)” – even that word (*vacanampi*) is loving-kindness by way of verbal action (*mettaṃ vacīkammameva*).

*Mettena manokammenā* means having prepared the body (*śarīrapaṭijagganaṃ katvā*) at the right time itself, having sat down on a secluded seat (*vivittāsane nisīditvā*) – “May the Teacher be without disease (*arogo hotu*), without oppression (*abyāpajjo*), happy (*sukhī*)” – thus with loving-kindness by way of mental action (*evaṃ pavattitena manokammena*).

*Katapuññosī* means it shows that you are accomplished in aspiration for a hundred thousand aeons (*kappasatasahassaṃ abhinīhārasampannosīti dasseti*).

*Katapuññosīti ca ettāvatā vissattho mā pamādamāpajji*, and because you are meritorious in this way, do not become complacent (*vissattho mā pamādamāpajji*), but apply yourself to exertion (*atha kho padhānamanuyuñja*).

For thus applying yourself (*evañhi anuyutto*) you will quickly be without *āsavas* (*khippaṃ hohisi anāsavo*), at the time of the *dharmasaṅgīti* you will attain *arhattva* (*dhammasaṅgītikāle arahattaṃ pāpuṇissasi*).

For it shows that the service done by one like me is not fruitless (*na hi mādisassa katapāricariyā nipphalā nāma hotīti dasseti*).

*Mettena vacīkammenā mettena manokammenā katapuññosī*
208
<p n="208" rend="bodytext"><hi rend="paranum">208</hi><hi rend="dot">.</hi> Atha kho bhagavā bhikkhū āmantesi – ‘‘yepi te, bhikkhave, ahesuṃ atītamaddhānaṃ arahanto sammāsambuddhā, tesampi bhagavantānaṃ etapparamāyeva upaṭṭhākā ahesuṃ, seyyathāpi mayhaṃ ānando. Yepi te, bhikkhave, bhavissanti anāgatamaddhānaṃ arahanto sammāsambuddhā, tesampi bhagavantānaṃ etapparamāyeva upaṭṭhākā bhavissanti, seyyathāpi mayhaṃ ānando. Paṇḍito, bhikkhave, ānando; medhāvī, bhikkhave, ānando. Jānāti ‘ayaṃ kālo tathāgataṃ dassanāya upasaṅkamituṃ bhikkhūnaṃ, ayaṃ kālo bhikkhunīnaṃ, ayaṃ kālo upāsakānaṃ <pb ed="T" n="2.0168"/>, ayaṃ <pb ed="P" n="2.0145"/> kālo upāsikānaṃ, ayaṃ kālo rañño rājamahāmattānaṃ titthiyānaṃ titthiyasāvakāna’nti.</p>
Then the Blessed One addressed the monks: ‘Monks, all those who were *arhats*, perfectly awakened Buddhas in the past had just such a chief attendant as Ānanda.

And so too, monks, will those Blessed Lords who come in the future.

Ānanda is wise, monks; Ānanda is intelligent, monks.

He knows, 'This is the right time for monks to come to see the *Tathāgata*, this is the right time for nuns, this is the right time for male lay-followers, this is the right time for female lay-followers, this is the right time for kings, for royal ministers, for leaders of other schools, and for their pupils.'
<p n="208" rend="bodytext"><hi rend="paranum">208</hi><hi rend="dot">.</hi> Evañca pana vatvā mahāpathaviṃ pattharanto viya ākāsaṃ vitthārento viya cakkavāḷagiriṃ osārento viya sineruṃ ukkhipento viya mahājambuṃ khandhe gahetvā cālento viya āyasmato ānandassa guṇakathaṃ ārabhanto atha kho bhagavā bhikkhū āmantesi. Tattha ‘‘yepi <pb ed="M" n="2.0177"/> te, bhikkhave, etarahī’’ti kasmā na vuttaṃ? Aññassa buddhassa natthitāya. Eteneva cetaṃ veditabbaṃ – ‘‘yathā cakkavāḷantarepi añño buddho natthī’’ti. <hi rend="bold">Paṇḍito</hi>ti byatto. <hi rend="bold">Medhāvī</hi>ti khandhadhātuāyatanādīsu kusalo.</p>
208. And then, after saying this, as if spreading out the great earth, as if expanding the sky, as if lowering the *cakravāḷa* mountain, as if lifting up Mount Meru, as if taking the great *jambu* tree by its trunk and shaking it, beginning a talk about the good qualities of the venerable Ānanda, then the Blessed One addressed the *bhikkhus*.

There, why was it not said, "Those who are here now, *bhikkhus*?" Because there is no other Buddha.

By this very [reason] it should be understood: "Just as there is no other Buddha even within the *cakravāḷa*."

*Paṇḍito* means articulate.

*Medhāvī* means skilled in the aggregates (*skandha*), elements (*dhātu*), sense-fields (*āyatana*) and so on.
209
<p n="209" rend="bodytext"><hi rend="paranum">209</hi><hi rend="dot">.</hi> ‘‘Cattārome, bhikkhave, acchariyā abbhutā dhammā <note>abbhutadhammā (syā. ka.)</note> ānande. Katame cattāro? Sace, bhikkhave, bhikkhuparisā ānandaṃ dassanāya upasaṅkamati, dassanena sā attamanā hoti. Tatra ce ānando dhammaṃ <pb ed="M" n="2.0120"/> bhāsati, bhāsitenapi sā attamanā hoti. Atittāva, bhikkhave, bhikkhuparisā hoti, atha kho ānando tuṇhī hoti. Sace, bhikkhave, bhikkhunīparisā ānandaṃ dassanāya upasaṅkamati, dassanena sā attamanā hoti. Tatra ce ānando dhammaṃ bhāsati, bhāsitenapi sā attamanā hoti. Atittāva, bhikkhave, bhikkhunīparisā hoti, atha kho ānando tuṇhī hoti. Sace, bhikkhave, upāsakaparisā ānandaṃ dassanāya upasaṅkamati, dassanena sā attamanā hoti. Tatra ce ānando dhammaṃ bhāsati, bhāsitenapi sā attamanā hoti. Atittāva, bhikkhave, upāsakaparisā hoti, atha kho ānando tuṇhī hoti. Sace, bhikkhave, upāsikāparisā ānandaṃ dassanāya upasaṅkamati, dassanena sā attamanā hoti. Tatra ce, ānando, dhammaṃ bhāsati, bhāsitenapi sā attamanā hoti. Atittāva, bhikkhave, upāsikāparisā hoti, atha kho ānando tuṇhī hoti. Ime kho, bhikkhave, cattāro acchariyā abbhutā dhammā ānande.</p> <p rend="bodytext">‘‘Cattārome, bhikkhave, acchariyā abbhutā dhammā raññe cakkavattimhi. Katame cattāro <pb ed="V" n="2.0110"/>? Sace, bhikkhave, khattiyaparisā rājānaṃ cakkavattiṃ dassanāya <pb ed="T" n="2.0169"/> upasaṅkamati, dassanena sā attamanā hoti. Tatra ce rājā cakkavattī bhāsati, bhāsitenapi sā attamanā hoti. Atittāva, bhikkhave, khattiyaparisā hoti. Atha kho rājā cakkavattī tuṇhī hoti. Sace bhikkhave, brāhmaṇaparisā…pe… gahapatiparisā…pe… samaṇaparisā rājānaṃ cakkavattiṃ dassanāya upasaṅkamati, dassanena sā attamanā hoti. Tatra ce rājā cakkavattī bhāsati, bhāsitenapi sā attamanā hoti. Atittāva, bhikkhave, samaṇaparisā hoti, atha kho rājā cakkavattī tuṇhī hoti. Evameva <pb ed="P" n="2.0146"/> kho, bhikkhave, cattārome acchariyā abbhutā dhammā ānande. Sace, bhikkhave, bhikkhuparisā ānandaṃ dassanāya upasaṅkamati, dassanena sā attamanā hoti. Tatra ce ānando dhammaṃ bhāsati, bhāsitenapi sā attamanā hoti. Atittāva, bhikkhave, bhikkhuparisā hoti. Atha kho ānando tuṇhī hoti. Sace, bhikkhave bhikkhunīparisā…pe… upāsakaparisā…pe… upāsikāparisā ānandaṃ dassanāya upasaṅkamati, dassanena sā attamanā <pb ed="M" n="2.0121"/> hoti. Tatra ce ānando dhammaṃ bhāsati, bhāsitenapi sā attamanā hoti. Atittāva, bhikkhave, upāsikāparisā hoti. Atha kho ānando tuṇhī hoti. Ime kho, bhikkhave, cattāro acchariyā abbhutā dhammā ānande’’ti.</p> <pb ed="V" n="2.0110"/> <pb ed="T" n="2.0169"/> <pb ed="P" n="2.0146"/> <pb ed="M" n="2.0121"/> <p rend="subhead">Mahāsudassanasuttadesanā</p>
"Monks, Ānanda has these four amazing and astounding qualities. What are the four? If, monks, a company of monks approaches Ānanda to see him, they become joyful on seeing him; and if he then speaks to them of the Dharma, they are made joyful by his discourse; before they are sated, monks, the company of monks is, and then Ānanda is silent. If, monks, a company of nuns approaches Ānanda to see him, they are gratified at the sight of him. And if he speaks Dhamma to them, they are gratified with what he says. Before they are sated, monks, the company of nuns is, and then Ānanda is silent. If, monks, a group of male lay followers approaches to see Ānanda, they are gratified at the sight of him. And if he speaks Dhamma to them, they are gratified with what he says. Before they are sated, monks, the company of male lay followers is, and then Ānanda is silent. If, monks, a group of female lay followers approaches to see Ānanda, they are gratified at the sight of him. And if Ānanda speaks words of welcome, their minds are uplifted with the speech. Before they are sated, monks, the company of female lay followers is, and then Ānanda is silent. These are the four amazing & astounding qualities in Ānanda.

"Monks, a Universal Monarch has these four amazing and astounding qualities. What are the four? If, monks, a group of nobles approaches a Universal Monarch to see him, they are gratified at the sight of him. And if he then speaks, they are made joyful by his talk; Before they are sated, monks, the company of nobles is. And then the Universal Monarch remains silent. If a group of Brahmins… of householders… of ascetics approaches a Universal Monarch to see him, they are gratified at the sight of him. And if he speaks to them, they are gratified with what he says. Before they are sated, monks, the company of ascetics is, and then the Universal Monarch remains silent. In the same way, monks, there are these four amazing & astounding qualities in Ānanda. If, monks, a company of monks approaches Ānanda to see him, they become joyful on seeing him; and if he then speaks to them of the Dharma, they are made joyful by his discourse; Before they are sated, monks, the company of monks is. And then Ānanda is silent. If, monks, a group of nuns… a group of male lay followers… a group of female lay followers approaches to see Ānanda, they are gratified at the sight of him. And if he speaks Dhamma to them, they are gratified with what he says. Before they are sated, monks, the company of female lay followers is. And then Ānanda is silent. There are the four wonderful and marvellous things, monks, about Ānanda."
Mahāsudassana Sutta discourse
<p n="209" rend="bodytext"><hi rend="paranum">209</hi><hi rend="dot">.</hi><hi rend="bold">Bhikkhuparisā ānandaṃ dassanāyā</hi>ti ye bhagavantaṃ passitukāmā theraṃ upasaṅkamanti, ye ca ‘‘āyasmā kirānando samantapāsādiko abhirūpo dassanīyo bahussuto saṅghasobhano’’ti therassa guṇe sutvā āgacchanti, te sandhāya ‘‘bhikkhuparisā ānandaṃ dassanāya upasaṅkamantī’’ti vuttaṃ. Esa nayo sabbattha. <hi rend="bold">Attamanā</hi>ti savanena no dassanaṃ sametīti sakamanā tuṭṭhacittā. <hi rend="bold">Dhamma</hi>nti ‘‘kacci, āvuso, khamanīyaṃ, kacci yāpanīyaṃ, kacci yoniso manasikārena kammaṃ karotha, ācariyupajjhāye vattaṃ pūrethā’’ti evarūpaṃ paṭisanthāradhammaṃ. Tattha bhikkhunīsu – ‘‘kacci, bhaginiyo, aṭṭha garudhamme samādāya vattathā’’ti idampi nānākaraṇaṃ hoti. Upāsakesu āgatesu ‘‘upāsaka, na te kacci sīsaṃ vā aṅgaṃ vā <pb ed="V" n="2.0159"/> rujjati, arogā te puttabhātaro’’ti na evaṃ paṭisanthāraṃ karoti. Evaṃ pana karoti – ‘‘kathaṃ upāsakā tīṇi saraṇāni pañca sīlāni rakkhatha, māsassa aṭṭha <pb ed="P" n="2.0586"/> uposathe karotha, mātāpitūnaṃ upaṭṭhānavattaṃ pūretha, dhammikasamaṇabrāhmaṇe paṭijaggathā’’ti. Upāsikāsupi eseva nayo.</p> <p rend="bodytext">Idāni ānandattherassa cakkavattinā saddhiṃ upamaṃ karonto <hi rend="bold">cattārome bhikkhave</hi>tiādimāha. Tattha <hi rend="bold">khattiyā</hi>ti abhisittā ca anabhisittā ca khattiyajātikā. Te kira – ‘‘rājā cakkavattī nāma abhirūpo dassanīyo pāsādiko ākāsena vicaranto rajjaṃ anusāsati dhammiko dhammarājā’’ti tassa guṇakathaṃ sutvā ‘‘savanena dassanampi sama’’nti attamanā honti. <hi rend="bold">Bhāsatī</hi>ti kathento – ‘‘kathaṃ, tātā, rājadhammaṃ pūretha, paveṇiṃ rakkhathā’’ti paṭisanthāraṃ karoti. Brāhmaṇesu pana – ‘‘kathaṃ ācariyā mante vācetha, kathaṃ antevāsikā mante gaṇhanti, dakkhiṇaṃ vā vatthāni vā kapilaṃ vā alatthā’’ti paṭisanthāraṃ karoti. Gahapatīsu – ‘‘kathaṃ tātā, na vo rājakulato daṇḍena vā balinā vā pīḷā atthi, sammā <pb ed="M" n="2.0178"/> devo dhāraṃ anupavecchati, sassāni sampajjantī’’ti evaṃ paṭisanthāraṃ karoti. Samaṇesu – ‘‘kathaṃ, bhante, pabbajitaparikkhārā sulabhā, samaṇadhamme na pamajjathā’’ti evaṃ paṭisanthāraṃ karoti.</p> <hi rend="bold">cattārome bhikkhave</hi> <hi rend="bold">khattiyā</hi> <hi rend="bold">Bhāsatī</hi> <pb ed="M" n="2.0178"/> <p rend="subhead">Mahāsudassanasuttadesanāvaṇṇanā</p>
209. "The assembly of monks approached Ānanda for a viewing" means those who desired to see the Blessed One approached the elder; and those who, having heard the elder's qualities, that venerable Ānanda was universally pleasing, handsome, delightful, very learned, an ornament to the Saṅgha, came thinking, "Hearing is the same as seeing." That is what is meant by, "The assembly of monks approached Ānanda for a viewing."

This method applies everywhere.

*Attamanā* means with joyful minds, their minds were delighted because the sound came but the sight did not come.

*Dhamma* means the conversational Dhamma, "Are you well, friend? Are you able to live? Do you act with careful consideration? Do you fulfill your duties to your teachers and preceptors?" Such is the nature of conversational Dhamma.

There, with the nuns: "Are you maintaining the eight weighty rules?" This too is a variation.

When lay followers have arrived: "Lay follower, is your head or limb injured? Are your children and siblings free from disease?" One does not engage in such conversation.

But rather, one does this: "How do you lay followers keep the three refuges and five precepts? Do you observe the eight *uposatha* days of the month? Do you fulfill your duties to your mother and father? Do you honor righteous *śramaṇas* and *brāhmaṇas*?"

The same method applies to lay women as well.

Now, making a comparison of the venerable Ānanda with a wheel-turning monarch, he says, "These four monks," and so forth.

There, *khattiyā* means those of the *kṣatriya* class, both consecrated and unconsecrated.

It is said that they, having heard the praise of him, "The king, a wheel-turning monarch, is handsome, delightful, pleasing, travels through the sky, governs the kingdom, is righteous, a king of Dharma," are joyful, thinking, "Hearing is the same as seeing."

*Bhāsatī* means while speaking, he engages in conversational exchange: "How, fathers, do you fulfill the royal Dharma? Do you protect the tradition?"

But with *brāhmaṇas*: "How, teachers, do you recite the *mantras*? How do the novices learn the *mantras*? Have you obtained a donation, clothing, or a cow?" He engages in such conversation.

With householders: "How, fathers, is there no oppression from the royal family through punishment or force? Does the *deva* properly provide rain? Do the crops thrive?" He engages in such conversation.

With *śramaṇas*: "How, venerable sirs, are the requisites for renunciants easily obtained? Do you not neglect the Dharma of a *śramaṇa*?" He engages in such conversation.

These four monks, *kṣatriyas*, *bhāsatī*.

Explanation of the teaching of the Mahāsudassana Sūtra.
210
<p n="210" rend="bodytext"><hi rend="paranum">210</hi><hi rend="dot">.</hi> Evaṃ vutte āyasmā ānando bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – ‘‘mā, bhante, bhagavā imasmiṃ khuddakanagarake ujjaṅgalanagarake sākhānagarake parinibbāyi. Santi, bhante, aññāni mahānagarāni, seyyathidaṃ – campā <pb ed="T" n="2.0170"/> rājagahaṃ sāvatthī sāketaṃ kosambī bārāṇasī; ettha bhagavā parinibbāyatu. Ettha bahū khattiyamahāsālā, brāhmaṇamahāsālā gahapatimahāsālā tathāgate abhippasannā. Te tathāgatassa sarīrapūjaṃ karissantī’’ti ‘‘māhevaṃ, ānanda, avaca; māhevaṃ, ānanda, avaca – ‘khuddakanagarakaṃ ujjaṅgalanagarakaṃ sākhānagaraka’nti.</p> <p rend="bodytext">‘‘Bhūtapubbaṃ, ānanda, rājā mahāsudassano nāma ahosi cakkavattī dhammiko dhammarājā cāturanto vijitāvī janappadatthāvariyappatto sattaratanasamannāgato. Rañño, ānanda, mahāsudassanassa ayaṃ kusinārā kusāvatī nāma rājadhānī ahosi, puratthimena ca pacchimena ca dvādasayojanāni āyāmena; uttarena ca dakkhiṇena ca sattayojanāni vitthārena. Kusāvatī, ānanda, rājadhānī iddhā ceva ahosi phītā ca <pb ed="P" n="2.0147"/> bahujanā ca ākiṇṇamanussā ca subhikkhā ca. Seyyathāpi, ānanda, devānaṃ āḷakamandā nāma rājadhānī iddhā ceva hoti phītā <pb ed="V" n="2.0111"/> ca bahujanā ca ākiṇṇayakkhā ca subhikkhā ca; evameva kho, ānanda, kusāvatī rājadhānī iddhā ceva ahosi phītā ca bahujanā ca ākiṇṇamanussā ca subhikkhā ca. Kusāvatī, ānanda, rājadhānī dasahi saddehi avivittā ahosi divā ceva rattiñca, seyyathidaṃ – hatthisaddena assasaddena rathasaddena bherisaddena mudiṅgasaddena vīṇāsaddena gītasaddena saṅkhasaddena sammasaddena pāṇitāḷasaddena ‘asnātha pivatha khādathā’ti dasamena saddena.</p> <pb ed="P" n="2.0147"/> <pb ed="V" n="2.0111"/> <p rend="bodytext">‘‘Gaccha tvaṃ, ānanda, kusināraṃ pavisitvā kosinārakānaṃ mallānaṃ <pb ed="T" n="2.0171"/> ārocehi – ‘ajja kho, vāseṭṭhā, rattiyā pacchime yāme tathāgatassa parinibbānaṃ <pb ed="M" n="2.0122"/> bhavissati. Abhikkamatha vāseṭṭhā, abhikkamatha vāseṭṭhā. Mā pacchā vippaṭisārino ahuvattha – amhākañca no gāmakkhette tathāgatassa parinibbānaṃ ahosi, na mayaṃ labhimhā pacchime kāle tathāgataṃ dassanāyā’’’ti. ‘‘Evaṃ, bhante’’ti kho āyasmā ānando bhagavato paṭissutvā nivāsetvā pattacīvaramādāya attadutiyo kusināraṃ pāvisi.</p> <pb ed="T" n="2.0171"/> <pb ed="M" n="2.0122"/> <p rend="subhead">Mallānaṃ vandanā</p>
210. When this had been said, the Venerable Ānanda spoke to the Blessed One, saying: “Let not the Blessed One pass away in this insignificant little town, this uncivilized township, this branch township.

There are other great cities, lord, such as Campā, Rājagaha, Sāvatthī, Sāketa, Kosambī, or Bārāṇasī; let the Blessed One attain final nirvāṇa there. In those places there are wealthy nobles, wealthy Brahmins, and wealthy householders who are devoted to the *Tathāgata*. They will provide for the *Tathāgata*'s bodily ( *śarīra*) offering ( *pūjā*)."

“Do not say that, Ānanda! Do not say, ‘This insignificant little town, this uncivilized township, this branch township.’"

“In the past, Ānanda, there was a king named Mahāsudassana, a wheel-turning monarch, a righteous king, a king of righteousness, a conqueror of the four quarters, a stabilizer of his country, endowed with the seven treasures.

This Kusinārā, Ānanda, was the royal capital of King Mahāsudassana, named Kusāvatī. It was twelve *yojanas* long from east to west, and seven *yojanas* wide from north to south.

Kusāvatī, Ānanda, the capital, was powerful and prosperous, full of people, crowded with humans, and well-supplied with food.

Just as the deva-city of Āḷakamandā is powerful and prosperous, full of people, crowded with *yakṣas*, and well-supplied with food, so too was Kusāvatī, Ānanda, the capital, powerful and prosperous, full of people, crowded with humans, and well-supplied with food.

Kusāvatī, Ānanda, the capital, was never without ten sounds, day or night, namely the sound of elephants, the sound of horses, the sound of chariots, the sound of kettle drums, the sound of side drums, the sound of lutes, the sound of singing, the sound of cymbals, the sound of gongs, and as the tenth sound, the sound of clapping and cries of "Eat, drink, and be merry!"

“Go, Ānanda, enter Kusinārā and announce to the Mallas of Kusinārā: ‘Today, Vāseṭṭhas, in the last watch of the night, the final *nirvāṇa* of the *Tathāgata* will occur. Approach him, Vāseṭṭhas, approach him. Do not be remorseful later, thinking, “In our own village area the *Tathāgata*’s final *nirvāṇa* took place, but we did not get to see the *Tathāgata* for the last time.”’”

“So be it, lord,” said the Venerable Ānanda, and after agreeing with the Blessed One, he dressed, took his bowl and robe, and went with a companion into Kusinārā.

Veneration of the Mallas
<p n="210" rend="bodytext"><hi rend="paranum">210</hi><hi rend="dot">.</hi><hi rend="bold">Khuddakanagarake</hi>ti nagarapatirūpake sambādhe khuddakanagarake. <hi rend="bold">Ujjaṅgalanagarake</hi>ti visamanagarake. <hi rend="bold">Sākhānagarake</hi>ti yathā rukkhānaṃ sākhā nāma khuddakā honti, evameva aññesaṃ mahānagarānaṃ sākhāsadise khuddakanagarake. <hi rend="bold">Khattiyamahāsālā</hi>ti khattiyamahāsārappattā mahākhattiyā. Esa nayo sabbattha.</p> <p rend="bodytext">Tesu <hi rend="bold">khattiyamahāsālā</hi> nāma yesaṃ koṭisatampi koṭisahassampi dhanaṃ nikhaṇitvā ṭhapitaṃ, divasaparibbayo ekaṃ kahāpaṇasakaṭaṃ nigacchati, sāyaṃ dve pavisanti. <hi rend="bold">Brāhmaṇamahāsālā</hi> nāma yesaṃ asītikoṭidhanaṃ nihitaṃ hoti, divasaparibbayo eko kahāpaṇakumbho nigacchati, sāyaṃ ekasakaṭaṃ pavisati. <hi rend="bold">Gahapatimahāsālā</hi> nāma yesaṃ cattālīsakoṭidhanaṃ nihitaṃ hoti, divasaparibbayo pañca kahāpaṇambaṇāni nigacchanti, sāyaṃ kumbho pavisati.</p> <hi rend="bold">khattiyamahāsālā</hi> <hi rend="bold">Brāhmaṇamahāsālā</hi> <hi rend="bold">Gahapatimahāsālā</hi> <p rend="bodytext"><hi rend="bold">Mā</hi><pb ed="V" n="2.0160"/><hi rend="bold">hevaṃ, ānanda, avacā</hi>ti ānanda, mā evaṃ avaca, na imaṃ ‘‘khuddakanagara’’nti <pb ed="P" n="2.0587"/> vattabbaṃ. Ahañhi imasseva nagarassa sampattiṃ kathetuṃ – ‘‘anekavāraṃ tiṭṭhaṃ nisīdaṃ mahantena ussāhena, mahantena parakkamena idhāgato’’ti vatvā <hi rend="bold">bhūtapubba</hi>ntiādimāha. <hi rend="bold">Subhikkhā</hi>ti khajjabhojjasampannā. <hi rend="bold">Hatthisaddenā</hi>ti ekasmiṃ hatthimhi saddaṃ karonte caturāsītihatthisahassāni saddaṃ karonti, iti hatthisaddena avivittā, hoti, tathā assasaddena. Puññavanto panettha sattā catusindhavayuttehi rathehi aññamaññaṃ anubandhamānā antaravīthīsu vicaranti, iti rathasaddena avivittā hoti. Niccaṃ payojitāneva panettha bheriādīni tūriyāni, iti bherisaddādīhipi avivittā hoti. Tattha <hi rend="bold">sammasaddo</hi>ti kaṃsatāḷasaddo. <hi rend="bold">Pāṇitāḷasaddo</hi>ti pāṇinā caturassaambaṇatāḷasaddo. Kuṭabherisaddotipi vadanti.</p> <hi rend="bold">Mā</hi> <pb ed="V" n="2.0160"/> <hi rend="bold">hevaṃ, ānanda, avacā</hi> <pb ed="P" n="2.0587"/> <hi rend="bold">bhūtapubba</hi> <hi rend="bold">Subhikkhā</hi> <hi rend="bold">Hatthisaddenā</hi> <hi rend="bold">sammasaddo</hi> <hi rend="bold">Pāṇitāḷasaddo</hi> <p rend="bodytext"><hi rend="bold">Asnātha</hi><pb ed="M" n="2.0179"/><hi rend="bold">pivatha khādathā</hi>ti asnātha pivatha khādatha. Ayaṃ panettha saṅkhepo, bhuñjatha bhoti iminā dasamena saddena avivittā hoti anupacchinnasaddā. Yathā pana aññesu nagaresu ‘‘kacavaraṃ chaḍḍetha, kudālaṃ gaṇhatha, pacchiṃ gaṇhatha, pavāsaṃ gamissāma, taṇḍulapuṭaṃ gaṇhatha, bhattapuṭaṃ gaṇhatha, phalakāvudhādīni sajjāni karothā’’ti evarūpā saddā honti, na yidha evaṃ ahosīti dasseti.</p> <hi rend="bold">Asnātha</hi> <pb ed="M" n="2.0179"/> <hi rend="bold">pivatha khādathā</hi> <p rend="bodytext">‘‘Dasamena saddenā’’ti ca vatvā ‘‘kusāvatī, ānanda, rājadhānī sattahi pākārehi parikkhittā ahosī’’ti sabbaṃ <hi rend="bold">mahāsudassanasuttaṃ</hi> niṭṭhāpetvā <hi rend="bold">gaccha tvaṃ ānandā</hi>tiādimāha. Tattha <hi rend="bold">abhikkamathā</hi>ti abhimukhā kamatha, āgacchathāti attho. Kiṃ pana te bhagavato āgatabhāvaṃ na jānantīti? Jānanti. Buddhānaṃ gatagataṭṭhānaṃ nāma mahantaṃ kolāhalaṃ hoti, kenacideva karaṇīyena nisinnattā na āgatā. ‘‘Te āgantvā bhikkhusaṅghassa ṭhānanisajjokāsaṃ saṃvidahitvā dassantī’’ti tesaṃ santike avelāyampi bhagavā pesesi.</p> <hi rend="bold">mahāsudassanasuttaṃ</hi> <hi rend="bold">gaccha tvaṃ ānandā</hi> <hi rend="bold">abhikkamathā</hi> <p rend="subhead">Mallānaṃ vandanāvaṇṇanā</p>
210. *Khuddakanagarake* means a small town (*nagarapatirūpake sambādhe khuddakanagarake*).

*Ujjaṅgalanagarake* means an uneven town (*visamanagarake*).

*Sākhānagarake* means just as the branches of trees are small, likewise, a small town similar to the branch of a large town (*yathā rukkhānaṃ sākhā nāma khuddakā honti, evameva aññesaṃ mahānagarānaṃ sākhāsadise khuddakanagarake*).

*Khattiyamahāsālā* means great nobles who have attained to the essence of warriors (*khattiyamahāsārappattā mahākhattiyā*).

This method [of explanation] applies to all cases (*esa nayo sabbattha*).

Amongst them, *khattiyamahāsālā* are those who have a hundred *koṭis*, or a thousand *koṭis*, of wealth buried; their daily expenditure amounts to a cartload of *kahāpaṇas*, and two [cartloads] enter in the evening.

*Brāhmaṇamahāsālā* are those who have eighty *koṭis* of wealth deposited; their daily expenditure amounts to a pot of *kahāpaṇas*, and one cart enters in the evening.

*Gahapatimahāsālā* are those who have forty *koṭis* of wealth deposited; their daily expenditure amounts to five *kahāpaṇambaṇas*, and a pot enters in the evening.

*Khattiyamahāsālā*, *brāhmaṇamahāsālā*, *gahapatimahāsālā*:

"Do not speak thus, Ānanda (*mā hevaṃ, ānanda, avacā*)!

It should not be said, "This is a small town" (*na imaṃ khuddakanagara'nti vattabbaṃ*).

For I, to describe the prosperity of this very town, said, "Standing up and sitting down many times, with great effort and great exertion, I came here (*anekavāraṃ tiṭṭhaṃ nisīdaṃ mahantena ussāhena, mahantena parakkamena idhāgato*)", and so on, speaking of former times (*bhūtapubba*).

*Subhikkhā* means abundant with food and drink (*khajjabhojjasampannā*).

*Hatthisaddena* means when one elephant makes a sound, eighty-four thousand elephants make a sound; thus it is not free from the sound of elephants (*iti hatthisaddena avivittā, hoti, tathā assasaddena*), and likewise with the sound of horses.

Here, virtuous beings, yoked to four Sindhava horses, chasing each other, wander in the inner streets; thus it is not free from the sound of chariots (*iti rathasaddena avivittā hoti*).

Here, drums and other musical instruments are always played; thus it is not free from the sound of drums and other things (*iti bherisaddādīhipi avivittā hoti*).

There, *sammasaddo* means the sound of brass cymbals (*kaṃsatāḷasaddo*).

*Pāṇitāḷasaddo* means the sound of clapping with the hands, the sound of four-sided drums (*pāṇinā caturassaambaṇatāḷasaddo*).

Some also say [it is] the sound of kettle drums (*kuṭabherisaddotipi vadanti*).

Do not [speak thus]!

"Do not speak thus, Ānanda (*hevaṃ, ānanda, avacā*)!"

Former times (*bhūtapubba*)

Abundant with food (*subhikkhā*)

With the sound of elephants (*hatthisaddena*)

Sound of cymbals (*sammasaddo*)

Sound of clapping (*pāṇitāḷasaddo*)

Bathed (*asnātha*)

Drink and eat (*pivatha khādathā*) means bathed, drink and eat (*asnātha pivatha khādatha*).

Here is a summary; you are fed, it is not free from this tenth sound (*iminā dasamena saddena avivittā hoti*) and has continuous sound (*anupacchinnasaddā*).

Just as in other towns there are sounds, "Throw away the rubbish, take the hoe, take the basket, we will go to exile, take the rice bag, take the food bag, make the weapons ready (*yathā pana aññesu nagaresu kacavaraṃ chaḍḍetha, kudālaṃ gaṇhatha, pacchiṃ gaṇhatha, pavāsaṃ gamissāma, taṇḍulapuṭaṃ gaṇhatha, bhattapuṭaṃ gaṇhatha, phalakāvudhādīni sajjāni karothā*)," such sounds there are, but not here, he shows (*na yidha evaṃ ahosīti dasseti*).

Bathed (*asnātha*)

Drink and eat (*pivatha khādathā*)

And having said, "with the tenth sound," and "Kusāvatī, Ānanda, was a capital surrounded by seven walls (*kusāvatī, ānanda, rājadhānī sattahi pākārehi parikkhittā ahosī*)," having finished the entire Great Vision Sūtra (*sabbaṃ mahāsudassanasuttaṃ niṭṭhāpetvā*), he said, "Go you, Ānanda (*gaccha tvaṃ ānandā*)," and so on.

There, *abhikkamathā* means face [it], go forward; the meaning is come (*abhimukhā kamatha, āgacchathāti attho*).

What, do they not know the Blessed One has come (*kiṃ pana te bhagavato āgatabhāvaṃ na jānantīti*)? They know (*jānanti*).

The Buddhas going and standing has a great commotion, because of some duty they did not come due to being seated (*buddhānaṃ gatagataṭṭhānaṃ nāma mahantaṃ kolāhalaṃ hoti, kenacideva karaṇīyena nisinnattā na āgatā*).

"Having come, they will arrange a place for the *bhikkhu* assembly to sit down and will show [it] (*te āgantvā bhikkhusaṅghassa ṭhānanisajjokāsaṃ saṃvidahitvā dassantī*)," even at the wrong time, the Blessed One sent to them (*tesaṃ santike avelāyampi bhagavā pesesi*).

Great Vision Sūtra (*mahāsudassanasuttaṃ*)

Go you, Ānanda (*gaccha tvaṃ ānandā*)

Go forward (*abhikkamathā*)

Explanation of the Mallas' veneration (*mallānaṃ vandanāvaṇṇanā*)
211
<p n="211" rend="bodytext"><hi rend="paranum">211</hi><hi rend="dot">.</hi> Tena kho pana samayena kosinārakā mallā sandhāgāre <note>santhāgāre (sī. syā. pī.)</note> sannipatitā honti kenacideva karaṇīyena. Atha kho āyasmā ānando yena kosinārakānaṃ mallānaṃ sandhāgāraṃ tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā kosinārakānaṃ mallānaṃ ārocesi – ‘‘ajja kho, vāseṭṭhā, rattiyā pacchime yāme tathāgatassa parinibbānaṃ bhavissati. Abhikkamatha vāseṭṭhā abhikkamatha vāseṭṭhā. Mā pacchā vippaṭisārino ahuvattha – ‘amhākañca no gāmakkhette tathāgatassa parinibbānaṃ <pb ed="P" n="2.0148"/> ahosi, na mayaṃ labhimhā pacchime kāle tathāgataṃ dassanāyā’’’ti. Idamāyasmato ānandassa vacanaṃ sutvā mallā ca mallaputtā ca mallasuṇisā ca mallapajāpatiyo ca aghāvino dummanā cetodukkhasamappitā appekacce kese pakiriya kandanti, bāhā paggayha kandanti, chinnapātaṃ papatanti, āvaṭṭanti vivaṭṭanti – ‘atikhippaṃ bhagavā parinibbāyissati, atikhippaṃ sugato parinibbāyissati, atikhippaṃ cakkhuṃ <pb ed="T" n="2.0172"/> loke antaradhāyissatī’ti. Atha kho mallā ca mallaputtā ca mallasuṇisā ca mallapajāpatiyo ca aghāvino dummanā cetodukkhasamappitā yena upavattanaṃ mallānaṃ sālavanaṃ yenāyasmā ānando tenupasaṅkamiṃsu. Atha kho āyasmato ānandassa etadahosi – ‘‘sace kho ahaṃ kosinārake malle ekamekaṃ bhagavantaṃ vandāpessāmi, avandito bhagavā kosinārakehi mallehi bhavissati, athāyaṃ ratti vibhāyissati. Yaṃnūnāhaṃ kosinārake malle kulaparivattaso kulaparivattaso <pb ed="V" n="2.0112"/> ṭhapetvā bhagavantaṃ vandāpeyyaṃ – ‘itthannāmo, bhante, mallo saputto sabhariyo sapariso sāmacco bhagavato pāde <pb ed="M" n="2.0123"/> sirasā vandatī’ti. Atha kho āyasmā ānando kosinārake malle kulaparivattaso kulaparivattaso ṭhapetvā bhagavantaṃ vandāpesi – ‘itthannāmo, bhante, mallo saputto sabhariyo sapariso sāmacco bhagavato pāde sirasā vandatī’’’ti. Atha kho āyasmā ānando etena upāyena paṭhameneva yāmena kosinārake malle bhagavantaṃ vandāpesi.</p> <p rend="subhead">Subhaddaparibbājakavatthu</p>
211. At that time, the Mallas of Kuśinagara were assembled in their assembly hall ( *saṃdhāgāra*) for some business.

Then the venerable Ānanda approached the assembly hall (*saṃdhāgāra*) of the Mallas of Kuśinagara; having approached, he announced to the Mallas of Kuśinagara: "Today, O Vāseṭṭhas, in the last watch of the night, the *parinirvāṇa* of the *Tathāgata* will take place.

Approach, O Vāseṭṭhas, approach!

Lest you later regret, saying, 'The *parinirvāṇa* of the *Tathāgata* took place in our own township, and we did not get to see him at the end!'"

Having heard the words of the venerable Ānanda, the Mallas, together with their sons, daughters-in-law, and wives, were afflicted, saddened, their minds overwhelmed with sorrow. Some wept, tearing their hair; they wept, raising their arms; they fell to the ground as if their feet were cut off, rolled back and forth, crying, "All too soon the Blessed One (*bhagavā*) will attain *parinirvāṇa*! All too soon the Well-Gone One (*sugato*) will attain *parinirvāṇa*! All too soon the Eye will disappear from the world!"

Then the Mallas, together with their sons, daughters-in-law, and wives, afflicted and saddened, their minds overwhelmed with sorrow, went to Upavattana, the Sāla Grove of the Mallas, to where the venerable Ānanda was.

Then the venerable Ānanda thought: "If I were to have each of the Mallas of Kuśinagara venerate the Blessed One (*bhagavantam*) individually, the night would dawn before they all had the chance.

What if I were to have the Mallas of Kuśinagara, arranged by families and clans, venerate the Blessed One (*bhagavantam*) , saying, 'Venerable Sir (*bhante*), the Malla named so-and-so, with his sons, wife, retinue, and ministers, venerates the feet of the Blessed One (*bhagavato pāde*) with his head'?"

Then the venerable Ānanda, having arranged the Mallas of Kuśinagara by families and clans, had them venerate the Blessed One (*bhagavantam*), saying: "Venerable Sir (*bhante*), the Malla named so-and-so, with his sons, wife, retinue, and ministers, venerates the feet of the Blessed One (*bhagavato pāde*) with his head."

Then the venerable Ānanda, by this method, had the Mallas of Kuśinagara venerate the Blessed One (*bhagavantam*) in the first watch of the night.

The Story of Subhadda the Wanderer
<p n="211" rend="bodytext"><hi rend="paranum">211</hi><hi rend="dot">.</hi><hi rend="bold">Amhākañca no</hi>ti ettha <hi rend="bold">no</hi> kāro nipātamattaṃ. <hi rend="bold">Aghāvino</hi>ti uppannadukkhā. <hi rend="bold">Dummanā</hi>ti anattamanā. <hi rend="bold">Cetodukkhasamappitā</hi>ti domanassasamappitā. <hi rend="bold">Kulaparivattaso kulaparivattaso ṭhapetvā</hi>ti ekekaṃ <pb ed="P" n="2.0588"/> kulaparivattaṃ kulasaṅkhepaṃ vīthisabhāgena ceva racchāsabhāgena ca visuṃ visuṃ ṭhapetvā.</p> <p rend="subhead">Subhaddaparibbājakavatthuvaṇṇanā</p>
[API Error: 502]
212
<p n="212" rend="bodytext"><hi rend="paranum">212</hi><hi rend="dot">.</hi> Tena kho pana samayena subhaddo nāma paribbājako kusinārāyaṃ paṭivasati. Assosi kho subhaddo paribbājako – ‘‘ajja kira rattiyā pacchime yāme samaṇassa gotamassa parinibbānaṃ bhavissatī’’ti. Atha <pb ed="P" n="2.0149"/> kho subhaddassa paribbājakassa etadahosi – ‘‘sutaṃ kho pana metaṃ paribbājakānaṃ vuḍḍhānaṃ mahallakānaṃ ācariyapācariyānaṃ bhāsamānānaṃ – ‘kadāci karahaci tathāgatā loke uppajjanti arahanto sammāsambuddhā’ti. Ajjeva <pb ed="T" n="2.0173"/> rattiyā pacchime yāme samaṇassa gotamassa parinibbānaṃ bhavissati. Atthi ca me ayaṃ kaṅkhādhammo uppanno, evaṃ pasanno ahaṃ samaṇe gotame, ‘pahoti me samaṇo gotamo tathā dhammaṃ desetuṃ, yathāhaṃ imaṃ kaṅkhādhammaṃ pajaheyya’’’nti. Atha kho subhaddo paribbājako yena upavattanaṃ mallānaṃ sālavanaṃ, yenāyasmā ānando tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā āyasmantaṃ ānandaṃ etadavoca – ‘‘sutaṃ metaṃ, bho ānanda, paribbājakānaṃ vuḍḍhānaṃ mahallakānaṃ ācariyapācariyānaṃ bhāsamānānaṃ – ‘kadāci karahaci tathāgatā loke uppajjanti arahanto <pb ed="T" n="2.0174"/> sammāsambuddhā’ti. Ajjeva rattiyā pacchime yāme samaṇassa gotamassa parinibbānaṃ bhavissati. Atthi ca me ayaṃ kaṅkhādhammo uppanno – evaṃ pasanno ahaṃ samaṇe gotame ‘pahoti me samaṇo gotamo tathā dhammaṃ desetuṃ, yathāhaṃ imaṃ kaṅkhādhammaṃ pajaheyya’nti. Sādhāhaṃ, bho ānanda, labheyyaṃ samaṇaṃ gotamaṃ dassanāyā’’ti. Evaṃ vutte āyasmā ānando subhaddaṃ paribbājakaṃ etadavoca – ‘‘alaṃ, āvuso subhadda, mā tathāgataṃ viheṭhesi, kilanto bhagavā’’ti. Dutiyampi kho subhaddo paribbājako…pe… tatiyampi kho subhaddo paribbājako āyasmantaṃ ānandaṃ etadavoca – ‘‘sutaṃ metaṃ, bho ānanda, paribbājakānaṃ vuḍḍhānaṃ mahallakānaṃ ācariyapācariyānaṃ bhāsamānānaṃ – ‘kadāci karahaci tathāgatā <pb ed="M" n="2.0124"/> loke uppajjanti arahanto sammāsambuddhā’ti. Ajjeva rattiyā pacchime yāme samaṇassa <pb ed="P" n="2.0150"/> gotamassa parinibbānaṃ bhavissati. Atthi ca me ayaṃ kaṅkhādhammo uppanno – evaṃ pasanno ahaṃ samaṇe gotame, ‘pahoti me samaṇo gotamo tathā <pb ed="V" n="2.0113"/> dhammaṃ desetuṃ, yathāhaṃ imaṃ kaṅkhādhammaṃ pajaheyya’nti. Sādhāhaṃ, bho ānanda, labheyyaṃ samaṇaṃ gotamaṃ dassanāyā’’ti. Tatiyampi kho āyasmā ānando subhaddaṃ paribbājakaṃ etadavoca – ‘‘alaṃ, āvuso subhadda, mā tathāgataṃ viheṭhesi, kilanto bhagavā’’ti.</p>
212. Now at that time, a wandering ascetic named Subhadda was staying near Kusinārā.

Subhadda the wandering ascetic heard it said, "Tonight, in the last watch of the night, the *parinirvāṇa* of the *śramaṇa* Gotama will take place."

Then the thought occurred to Subhadda the wandering ascetic: "I have heard it said by old and venerable wandering ascetics, teachers of teachers, that only rarely do Tathāgatas, *arhats*, perfectly awakened ones, arise in the world."

Tonight, in the last watch of the night, the *śramaṇa* Gotama will attain *parinirvāṇa*.

Now, a doubt has arisen in me, and I am confident that the *śramaṇa* Gotama can teach me the *dharma* in such a way that I might dispel this doubt."

Then Subhadda the wandering ascetic went to the Upavattana, the *sāla* grove of the Mallas, and approached the venerable Ānanda. Having approached, he said to the venerable Ānanda: "I have heard it said, venerable Ānanda, by old and venerable wandering ascetics, teachers of teachers, that only rarely do Tathāgatas, *arhats*, perfectly awakened ones, arise in the world.

Tonight, in the last watch of the night, the *śramaṇa* Gotama will attain *parinirvāṇa*.

Now a doubt has arisen in me—and I am confident that the *śramaṇa* Gotama can teach me the *dharma* in such a way that I might dispel this doubt."

"It would be good, venerable Ānanda, if I could be allowed to see the *śramaṇa* Gotama."

When this was said, the venerable Ānanda said to Subhadda the wandering ascetic, "Enough, friend Subhadda! Do not disturb the *Tathāgata*. The Blessed One (*bhagavān*) is weary."

A second time... and a third time, Subhadda the wandering ascetic said to the venerable Ānanda, "I have heard it said, venerable Ānanda, by old and venerable wandering ascetics, teachers of teachers, that only rarely do Tathāgatas arise in the world, *arhats*, perfectly awakened ones.

Tonight, in the last watch of the night, the *śramaṇa* Gotama will attain *parinirvāṇa*.

Now a doubt has arisen in me—and I am confident that the *śramaṇa* Gotama can teach me the *dharma* in such a way that I might dispel this doubt."

"It would be good, venerable Ānanda, if I could be allowed to see the *śramaṇa* Gotama."

For a third time, the venerable Ānanda said to Subhadda the wandering ascetic, "Enough, friend Subhadda! Do not disturb the *Tathāgata*. The Blessed One (*bhagavān*) is weary."
<p n="212" rend="bodytext"><hi rend="paranum">212</hi><hi rend="dot">.</hi><hi rend="bold">Subhaddo</hi><pb ed="V" n="2.0161"/><hi rend="bold">nāma paribbājako</hi>ti udiccabrāhmaṇamahāsālakulā pabbajito channaparibbājako. <hi rend="bold">Kaṅkhādhammo</hi>ti vimatidhammo. Kasmā panassa ajja evaṃ ahosīti? Tathāvidhaupanissayattā. Pubbe kira puññakaraṇakāle dve bhātaro ahesuṃ. Te ekatova sassaṃ akaṃsu. Tattha jeṭṭhakassa – ‘‘ekasmiṃ sasse navavāre aggasassadānaṃ mayā dātabba’’nti ahosi. So vappakāle bījaggaṃ nāma datvā gabbhakāle kaniṭṭhena saddhiṃ <pb ed="M" n="2.0180"/> mantesi – ‘‘gabbhakāle gabbhaṃ phāletvā dassāmā’’ti kaniṭṭho – ‘‘taruṇasassaṃ nāsetukāmosī’’ti āha. Jeṭṭho kaniṭṭhassa ananuvattanabhāvaṃ ñatvā khettaṃ vibhajitvā attano koṭṭhāsato gabbhaṃ phāletvā khīraṃ nīharitvā sappinavanītena saṃyojetvā adāsi, puthukakāle puthukaṃ kāretvā adāsi, lāyanakāle lāyanaggaṃ, veṇikaraṇe veṇaggaṃ, kalāpādīsu kalāpaggaṃ, khalaggaṃ, khalabhaṇḍaggaṃ, koṭṭhagganti evaṃ ekasasse navavāre aggadānaṃ adāsi. Kaniṭṭho pana uddharitvā adāsi.</p> <p rend="bodytext">Tesu jeṭṭhako <hi rend="bold">aññāsikoṇḍaññatthero</hi> jāto. Bhagavā – ‘‘kassa nu kho ahaṃ paṭhamaṃ dhammaṃ deseyya’’nti olokento ‘‘aññāsikoṇḍañño ekasmiṃ sasse nava aggadānāni adāsi, imaṃ aggadhammaṃ tassa desessāmī’’ti sabbapaṭhamaṃ dhammaṃ desesi. So aṭṭhārasahi brahmakoṭīhi saddhiṃ sotāpattiphale patiṭṭhāsi. Kaniṭṭho pana ohīyitvā pacchā dānassa dinnattā satthu parinibbānakāle evaṃ cintetvā satthāraṃ daṭṭhukāmo ahosi.</p> <hi rend="bold">aññāsikoṇḍaññatthero</hi> <p rend="bodytext"><hi rend="bold">Mā tathāgataṃ viheṭhesī</hi>ti thero kira – ‘‘ete aññatitthiyā nāma attano gahaṇameva gaṇhanti, tassa vissajjāpanatthāya bhagavato bahuṃ bhāsamānassa kāyavācāvihesā bhavissati, pakatiyāpi ca kilantoyeva bhagavā’’ti maññamāno evamāha. Paribbājako – ‘‘na me ayaṃ bhikkhu okāsaṃ karoti, atthikena pana anuvattitvā kāretabbo’’ti theraṃ anuvattanto dutiyampi tatiyampi āha.</p> <hi rend="bold">Mā tathāgataṃ viheṭhesī</hi>
212. *Subhaddo nāma paribbājako* means the wanderer Subhadda, who renounced the world from a wealthy, Brahmin family in Northern India and was surrounded by sixty wanderers.

*Kaṅkhādhammo* means the doctrine of doubt, or the doctrine of uncertainty.

Why did that occur for him today? Because of a specific underlying condition.

It is said that in the past, while performing a meritorious act, there were two brothers. They farmed a field together. For the elder brother, there was [this thought]: "In one harvest, I must give the best grain offering nine times."

So, at the time of sowing, he gave the best seed. During the embryonic stage [of the crop], he consulted with his younger brother, "During the embryonic stage, we will split the embryo and give [it as an offering]." The younger brother said, "You wish to destroy the young crop!"

The elder brother, knowing that his younger brother did not agree, divided the field. From his portion, he split the embryo, extracted the milky sap, combined it with ghee and fresh butter, and gave it as an offering. At the time of *puthuka* (a type of grain), he had *puthuka* prepared and gave it as an offering. At the time of reaping, the best of the harvest, at the time of winnowing, the best of the winnowed grain, from bundles, the best bundle, the best of the threshing floor, the best of the threshing-floor produce, the best of the granary—in this way, in one harvest, he gave the best offering nine times.

The younger brother, however, harvested and gave [his offering].

Among them, the elder brother was born as the Venerable Aññāsikoṇḍañña. The Blessed One, looking around, [thought]: "To whom shall I first teach the Dhamma?" [He saw]: "Aññāsikoṇḍañña gave nine best offerings in one harvest. I will teach him this supreme Dhamma." So, he taught the Dhamma first of all. He was established in the fruit of stream-entry together with eighteen *brahma* crores.

The younger brother, however, having been inferior, because he gave the offering later, thinking thus at the time of the Teacher's *parinibbāna*, he wished to see the Teacher.

*Aññāsikoṇḍaññatthero*

*Mā tathāgataṃ viheṭhesī*: It is said that the Elder [Aññāsikoṇḍañña], thinking, "These other sectarians take only their own views. For the Blessed One, speaking much to dismiss them, there will be physical and verbal weariness, and naturally the Blessed One is already tired," spoke thus.

The wanderer [Subhadda]: "This monk does not give me an opportunity. But having persisted with my request I must make him do it." Following the Elder, he spoke a second and third time.

*Mā tathāgataṃ viheṭhesī*
213
<p n="213" rend="bodytext"><hi rend="paranum">213</hi><hi rend="dot">.</hi> Assosi kho bhagavā āyasmato ānandassa subhaddena paribbājakena saddhiṃ imaṃ kathāsallāpaṃ. Atha kho bhagavā āyasmantaṃ ānandaṃ āmantesi – ‘‘alaṃ, ānanda, mā subhaddaṃ vāresi, labhataṃ, ānanda, subhaddo tathāgataṃ dassanāya. Yaṃ kiñci maṃ subhaddo pucchissati, sabbaṃ taṃ aññāpekkhova pucchissati, no vihesāpekkho. Yaṃ cassāhaṃ puṭṭho byākarissāmi, taṃ khippameva ājānissatī’’ti. Atha kho āyasmā ānando subhaddaṃ paribbājakaṃ etadavoca – ‘‘gacchāvuso subhadda, karoti te bhagavā okāsa’’nti. Atha kho subhaddo paribbājako yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavatā saddhiṃ sammodi, sammodanīyaṃ kathaṃ sāraṇīyaṃ vītisāretvā ekamantaṃ nisīdi. Ekamantaṃ nisinno kho subhaddo paribbājako bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – ‘‘yeme, bho gotama, samaṇabrāhmaṇā saṅghino gaṇino gaṇācariyā ñātā yasassino titthakarā sādhusammatā bahujanassa, seyyathidaṃ <pb ed="T" n="2.0175"/> – pūraṇo kassapo, makkhali gosālo, ajito kesakambalo, pakudho kaccāyano, sañcayo belaṭṭhaputto, nigaṇṭho nāṭaputto, sabbete sakāya paṭiññāya abbhaññiṃsu, sabbeva na abbhaññiṃsu <pb ed="P" n="2.0151"/>, udāhu ekacce abbhaññiṃsu, ekacce na abbhaññiṃsū’’ti? ‘‘Alaṃ, subhadda, tiṭṭhatetaṃ – ‘sabbete sakāya paṭiññāya abbhaññiṃsu, sabbeva na abbhaññiṃsu, udāhu ekacce abbhaññiṃsu, ekacce na abbhaññiṃsū’ti. Dhammaṃ te, subhadda, desessāmi; taṃ suṇāhi sādhukaṃ manasikarohi, bhāsissāmī’’ti. ‘‘Evaṃ, bhante’’ti kho subhaddo paribbājako bhagavato paccassosi. Bhagavā etadavoca –</p>
213. Now, the Blessed One heard this conversation between the Venerable Ānanda and Subhadda the wanderer.

Then the Blessed One addressed the Venerable Ānanda, saying: “Enough, Ānanda, do not hinder Subhadda. Let Subhadda see the *Tathāgata*.

Whatever Subhadda asks me, he will ask for the sake of knowledge, not to be bothersome.

And whatever I answer when asked, he will quickly understand.”

Then the Venerable Ānanda said to Subhadda the wanderer: “Go ahead, friend Subhadda, the Blessed One gives you leave.”

Then Subhadda the wanderer approached the Blessed One; having approached, he exchanged greetings with the Blessed One, and after an exchange of friendly greetings and courtesies, he sat down to one side.

Seated to one side, Subhadda the wanderer said to the Blessed One: “Venerable Gotama, these *śramaṇas* and *brāhmaṇas* who are leaders of groups, heads of communities, teachers of groups, well-known, famous, founders of sects, and highly regarded by many people, such as Pūraṇa Kassapa, Makkhali Gosāla, Ajita Kesakambala, Pakudha Kaccāyana, Sañjaya Belaṭṭhaputta, and Nigaṇṭha Nāṭaputta—have they all realized the truth according to their own claims, or have none of them realized it, or have some realized it and some not?”

“Enough, Subhadda! Let it be as it may, whether all of them have attained realization, as each of them would have it believed, or whether none of them has, or whether some have attained realization and others not.

I will teach you the *Dharma*, Subhadda; listen and heed it well, and I will speak.”

“As you say, lord,” Subhadda the wanderer responded to the Blessed One.

The Blessed One said:
<p n="213" rend="bodytext"><hi rend="paranum">213</hi><hi rend="dot">.</hi><hi rend="bold">Assosi</hi><pb ed="P" n="2.0589"/><hi rend="bold">kho</hi>ti sāṇidvāre ṭhitassa bhāsato pakatisoteneva assosi, sutvā ca pana subhaddasseva atthāya mahatā ussāhena āgatattā <hi rend="bold">alaṃ ānandā</hi>tiādimāha. Tattha <hi rend="bold">ala</hi>nti paṭikkhepatthe nipāto. <hi rend="bold">Aññāpekkhovā</hi>ti aññātukāmova hutvā. <hi rend="bold">Abbhaññiṃsū</hi>ti yathā tesaṃ paṭiññā, tatheva jāniṃsu. Idaṃ vuttaṃ hoti – sace nesaṃ sā paṭiññā niyyānikā, sabbe abbhaññaṃsu, no ce, na abbhaññaṃsu. Tasmā kiṃ tesaṃ paṭiññā niyyānikā, aniyyānikāti <pb ed="V" n="2.0162"/> ayameva <pb ed="M" n="2.0181"/> tassa pañhassa attho. Atha bhagavā tesaṃ aniyyānikabhāvakathanena atthābhāvato ceva okāsābhāvato ca ‘‘ala’’nti paṭikkhipitvā dhammameva desesi. Paṭhamayāmasmiñhi mallānaṃ dhammaṃ desetvā majjhimayāme subhaddassa, pacchimayāme bhikkhusaṅghaṃ ovaditvā balavapaccūsasamaye parinibbāyissāmicceva bhagavā āgato.</p>

214
<p n="214" rend="bodytext"><hi rend="paranum">214</hi><hi rend="dot">.</hi> ‘‘Yasmiṃ kho, subhadda, dhammavinaye ariyo aṭṭhaṅgiko maggo na upalabbhati, samaṇopi tattha na upalabbhati. Dutiyopi tattha samaṇo <pb ed="M" n="2.0125"/> na upalabbhati. Tatiyopi tattha samaṇo na upalabbhati. Catutthopi tattha samaṇo na upalabbhati. Yasmiñca kho, subhadda, dhammavinaye ariyo aṭṭhaṅgiko maggo upalabbhati, samaṇopi tattha upalabbhati, dutiyopi tattha samaṇo upalabbhati, tatiyopi tattha samaṇo upalabbhati, catutthopi tattha samaṇo upalabbhati. Imasmiṃ kho, subhadda, dhammavinaye ariyo aṭṭhaṅgiko maggo upalabbhati, idheva, subhadda, samaṇo, idha dutiyo samaṇo, idha tatiyo samaṇo, idha catuttho samaṇo, suññā parappavādā samaṇebhi <pb ed="V" n="2.0114"/> aññehi <note>aññe (pī.)</note>. Ime <pb ed="T" n="2.0176"/> ca <note>idheva (ka.)</note>, subhadda, bhikkhū sammā vihareyyuṃ, asuñño loko arahantehi assāti.</p> <p rend="gatha1">‘‘Ekūnatiṃso vayasā subhadda,</p> <p rend="gatha2">Yaṃ pabbajiṃ kiṃkusalānuesī;</p> <p rend="gatha3">Vassāni paññāsa samādhikāni,</p> <p rend="gathalast">Yato ahaṃ pabbajito subhadda.</p> <p rend="gatha1">Ñāyassa dhammassa padesavattī,</p> <p rend="gathalast">Ito bahiddhā samaṇopi natthi.</p> <p rend="bodytext">‘‘Dutiyopi <pb ed="P" n="2.0152"/> samaṇo natthi. Tatiyopi samaṇo natthi. Catutthopi samaṇo natthi. Suññā parappavādā samaṇebhi aññehi. Ime ca, subhadda, bhikkhū sammā vihareyyuṃ, asuñño loko arahantehi assā’’ti.</p> <pb ed="P" n="2.0152"/>
[API Error: 502]
<p n="214" rend="bodytext"><hi rend="paranum">214</hi><hi rend="dot">.</hi><hi rend="bold">Samaṇopi tattha na upalabbhatī</hi>ti paṭhamo sotāpannasamaṇopi tattha natthi, dutiyo sakadāgāmisamaṇopi, tatiyo anāgāmisamaṇopi, catuttho arahattasamaṇopi tattha natthīti attho. ‘‘Imasmiṃ kho’’ti purimadesanāya aniyamato vatvā idāni attano sāsanaṃ niyamento āha. <hi rend="bold">Suññā parappavādā samaṇebhī</hi>ti catunnaṃ maggānaṃ atthāya āraddhavipassakehi catūhi, maggaṭṭhehi catūhi, phalaṭṭhehi catūhīti dvādasahi samaṇehi suññā parappavādā tucchā rittakā. <hi rend="bold">Ime ca subhaddā</hi>ti ime dvādasa bhikkhū. <hi rend="bold">Sammā vihareyyu</hi>nti ettha sotāpanno attano adhigataṭṭhānaṃ aññassa kathetvā taṃ sotāpannaṃ karonto sammā viharati nāma. Esa nayo sakadāgāmiādīsu. Sotāpattimaggaṭṭho aññampi sotāpattimaggaṭṭhaṃ karonto sammā viharati nāma. Esa nayo sesamaggaṭṭhesu. Sotāpattimaggatthāya āraddhavipassako attano paguṇaṃ kammaṭṭhānaṃ kathetvā aññampi sotāpattimaggatthāya āraddhavipassakaṃ karonto sammā viharati nāma. Esa nayo sesamaggatthāya āraddhavipassakesu. Idaṃ sandhāyāha – ‘‘sammā vihareyyu’’nti. <hi rend="bold">Asuñño loko arahantehi assā</hi>ti naḷavanaṃ saravanaṃ viya nirantaro <pb ed="P" n="2.0590"/> assa.</p> <p rend="bodytext"><hi rend="bold">Ekūnatiṃso vayasā</hi>ti vayena ekūnatiṃsavasso hutvā. <hi rend="bold">Yaṃ pabbaji</hi>nti ettha <hi rend="bold">ya</hi>nti nipātamattaṃ. <hi rend="bold">Kiṃ kusalānuesī</hi>ti ‘‘kiṃ kusala’’nti anuesanto pariyesanto. Tattha – ‘‘kiṃ kusala’’nti sabbaññutaññāṇaṃ adhippetaṃ, taṃ gavesantoti attho. <hi rend="bold">Yato aha</hi>nti yato paṭṭhāya ahaṃ pabbajito, etthantare samadhikāni paññāsa vassāni hontīti dasseti. <hi rend="bold">Ñāyassa dhammassā</hi>ti ariyamaggadhammassa. <hi rend="bold">Padesavattī</hi>ti padese vipassanāmagge pavattanto. <hi rend="bold">Ito bahiddhā</hi>ti mama sāsanato bahiddhā. <hi rend="bold">Samaṇopi</hi><pb ed="M" n="2.0182"/><hi rend="bold">natthī</hi>ti padesavattivipassakopi natthi, paṭhamasamaṇo sotāpannopi natthīti vuttaṃ hoti.</p> <hi rend="bold">Ekūnatiṃso vayasā</hi> <hi rend="bold">Yaṃ pabbaji</hi> <hi rend="bold">ya</hi> <hi rend="bold">Kiṃ kusalānuesī</hi> <hi rend="bold">Yato aha</hi> <hi rend="bold">Ñāyassa dhammassā</hi> <hi rend="bold">Padesavattī</hi> <hi rend="bold">Ito bahiddhā</hi> <hi rend="bold">Samaṇopi</hi> <pb ed="M" n="2.0182"/> <hi rend="bold">natthī</hi> <p rend="bodytext"><hi rend="bold">Ye etthā</hi>ti ye tumhe ettha sāsane satthārā sammukhā antevāsikābhisekena abhisittā, tesaṃ vo lābhā tesaṃ vo suladdhanti. Bāhirasamaye kira yaṃ antevāsikaṃ ācariyo – ‘‘imaṃ pabbājehi <pb ed="V" n="2.0163"/>, imaṃ ovada, imaṃ anusāsā’’ti vadati, so tena attano ṭhāne ṭhapito hoti, tasmā tassa – ‘‘imaṃ pabbajehi, imaṃ ovada, imaṃ anusāsā’’ti ime lābhā honti. Therampi subhaddo tameva bāhirasamayaṃ gahetvā evamāha.</p> <hi rend="bold">Ye etthā</hi> <pb ed="V" n="2.0163"/> <p rend="bodytext"><hi rend="bold">Alattha kho</hi>ti kathaṃ alattha? Thero kira naṃ ekamantaṃ netvā udakatumbato pānīyena sīsaṃ temetvā tacapañcakakammaṭṭhānaṃ kathetvā kesamassuṃ ohāretvā kāsāyāni vatthāni acchādāpetvā saraṇāni datvā bhagavato santikaṃ ānesi. Bhagavā upasampādetvā kammaṭṭhānaṃ ācikkhi. So taṃ gahetvā uyyānassa ekamante caṅkamaṃ adhiṭṭhāya ghaṭento vāyamanto vipassanaṃ vaḍḍhento saha paṭisambhidāhi arahattaṃ patvā āgamma bhagavantaṃ vanditvā nisīdi. Taṃ sandhāya – ‘‘acirūpasampanno kho panā’’tiādi vuttaṃ.</p> <hi rend="bold">Alattha kho</hi> <p rend="bodytext"><hi rend="bold">So ca bhagavato pacchimo sakkhisāvako ahosī</hi>ti saṅgītikārakānaṃ vacanaṃ. Tattha yo bhagavati dharamāne pabbajitvā aparabhāge upasampadaṃ labhitvā kammaṭṭhānaṃ gahetvā arahattaṃ pāpuṇāti, upasampadampi vā dharamāneyeva labhitvā aparabhāge kammaṭṭhānaṃ gahetvā arahattaṃ pāpuṇāti, kammaṭṭhānampi vā dharamāneyeva gahetvā aparabhāge arahattameva pāpuṇāti, sabbopi so pacchimo sakkhisāvako. Ayaṃ pana dharamāneyeva bhagavati <pb ed="P" n="2.0591"/> pabbajito ca upasampanno ca kammaṭṭhānañca gahetvā arahattaṃ pattoti.</p> <hi rend="bold">So ca bhagavato pacchimo sakkhisāvako ahosī</hi> <pb ed="P" n="2.0591"/> <p rend="centre">Pañcamabhāṇavāravaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.</p> <p rend="subhead">Tathāgatapacchimavācāvaṇṇanā</p>
214. " *Samaṇopi tattha na upalabbhatī* " means there is not even the first *sotāpanna-samaṇa* there, nor the second *sakadāgāmi-samaṇa*, nor the third *anāgāmi-samaṇa*, nor the fourth *arahatta-samaṇa*.

" *Imasmiṃ kho* " – having spoken generally in the previous teaching, he now speaks, defining his own dispensation.

" *Suññā parappavādā samaṇebhī* " – the *parappavādā* (other doctrines) are empty, hollow, and devoid [of truth] because of the twelve *samaṇa*s: the four who have undertaken insight for the sake of the four paths, the four who are established in the paths, and the four who are established in the fruits.

" *Ime ca subhaddā* " – these twelve monks.

" *Sammā vihareyyu* " – here, the *sotāpanna* lives rightly by telling another about the state he has attained, thus making that person a *sotāpanna*.

This is the way with the *sakadāgāmi*s and so on.

The one established in the *sotāpatti* path lives rightly by making another also established in the *sotāpatti* path.

This is the way with the remaining path-followers.

The one who has undertaken insight for the sake of the *sotāpatti* path lives rightly by telling another about his own skillful meditation subject, thus making that other person also one who has undertaken insight for the sake of the *sotāpatti* path.

This is the way with the remaining insight-practitioners who have undertaken [practice] for the sake of the path.

With this in mind, he said, " *sammā vihareyyu* ."

" *Asuñño loko arahantehi assā* " – it would be uninterrupted, like a grove of reeds or a grove of rushes.

Being twenty-nine years old – having been twenty-nine years of age.

" *Yaṃ pabbaji* " – here, *yaṃ* is merely a particle.

" *Kiṃ kusalānuesī* " – seeking and searching, inquiring "What is wholesome?"

There, "What is wholesome?" refers to the knowledge of omniscience; he was searching for that, is the meaning.

" *Yato ahaṃ* " – he shows that from when he went forth, in this interval, there are more than fifty years.

" *Ñāyassa dhammassā* " – of the Dhamma of the Noble Path (*āryamārga-dharma*).

" *Padesavattī* " – continuing in a region, in the path of insight (*vipaśyanā-mārga*).

" *Ito bahiddhā* " – outside my dispensation (*śāsana*).

" *Samaṇopi natthī* " – there is no regional insight-practitioner (*padesavattī-vipaśyaka*), it is said that there is no first *samaṇa*, the *sotāpanna*.

Being twenty-nine years old, when he went forth, what is the wholesome he was seeking? From when I, of the Law, of the Dhamma, continuing in a region, outside of this, a *śramaṇa*.

" *Ye etthā* " – you who here in the *śāsana* have been consecrated by the Teacher (*śāstṛ*) face to face with the consecration of disciples – for them, what gain; for them, what good fortune!

It is said that in other schools, when a teacher says to a pupil, "Ordain this one, advise this one, instruct this one," that pupil is established by him in his own place; therefore, for him, "Ordain this one, advise this one, instruct this one" – these are gains.

The Elder Subhadda, too, taking up that very other school, spoke thus.

" *Alattha kho* " – how did he obtain [arahantship]? It seems the Elder, taking him aside, wetting his head with water from a water pot, speaking about the meditation subject of the five aspects of the body, shaving off his hair and beard, having him put on ochre robes, giving him the refuges, brought him to the Blessed One.

The Blessed One ordained him and taught him a meditation subject.

Taking that, in a secluded part of the park, taking his stand on the walking course, striving and exerting himself, developing insight, attaining arahantship together with the discriminations, he came and, having paid homage to the Blessed One, sat down.

Referring to that, "Though newly ordained..." etc., was said.

" *So ca bhagavato pacchimo sakkhisāvako ahosī* " – this is the saying of the compilers [of the canon].

There, whoever, while the Blessed One was living, went forth, and in the subsequent part obtained ordination, took a meditation subject, and attained arahantship; or even having obtained ordination while he was still living, in the subsequent part took a meditation subject and attained arahantship; or even having taken a meditation subject while he was still living, in the subsequent part attained arahantship alone – all of them are the last disciples by direct experience (*sākṣi-śrāvaka*).

But this one, while the Blessed One was still living, both went forth, was ordained, and took a meditation subject, and attained arahantship.

The fifth section for recitation is finished.
Explanation of the last words of the Tathāgata.
215
<p n="215" rend="bodytext"><hi rend="paranum">215</hi><hi rend="dot">.</hi> Evaṃ vutte subhaddo paribbājako bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – ‘‘abhikkantaṃ, bhante, abhikkantaṃ, bhante. Seyyathāpi, bhante, nikkujjitaṃ vā ukkujjeyya, paṭicchannaṃ vā vivareyya, mūḷhassa vā maggaṃ ācikkheyya, andhakāre vā telapajjotaṃ dhāreyya, ‘cakkhumanto rūpāni dakkhantī’ti, evamevaṃ bhagavatā anekapariyāyena dhammo pakāsito. Esāhaṃ, bhante, bhagavantaṃ saraṇaṃ gacchāmi dhammañca bhikkhusaṅghañca. Labheyyāhaṃ, bhante, bhagavato santike pabbajjaṃ, labheyyaṃ upasampada’’nti. ‘‘Yo kho, subhadda, aññatitthiyapubbo imasmiṃ dhammavinaye <pb ed="T" n="2.0177"/> ākaṅkhati pabbajjaṃ, ākaṅkhati upasampadaṃ, so cattāro <pb ed="M" n="2.0126"/> māse parivasati. Catunnaṃ māsānaṃ accayena āraddhacittā bhikkhū pabbājenti upasampādenti bhikkhubhāvāya. Api ca mettha puggalavemattatā viditā’’ti. ‘‘Sace, bhante, aññatitthiyapubbā imasmiṃ dhammavinaye ākaṅkhantā pabbajjaṃ ākaṅkhantā upasampadaṃ cattāro māse parivasanti, catunnaṃ māsānaṃ accayena āraddhacittā bhikkhū pabbājenti upasampādenti bhikkhubhāvāya. Ahaṃ cattāri vassāni parivasissāmi, catunnaṃ vassānaṃ accayena āraddhacittā bhikkhū pabbājentu upasampādentu bhikkhubhāvāyā’’ti.</p> <p rend="bodytext">Atha kho bhagavā āyasmantaṃ ānandaṃ āmantesi – ‘‘tenahānanda, subhaddaṃ pabbājehī’’ti. ‘‘Evaṃ, bhante’’ti kho āyasmā ānando bhagavato paccassosi. Atha kho subhaddo <pb ed="V" n="2.0115"/> paribbājako āyasmantaṃ ānandaṃ etadavoca – ‘‘lābhā vo, āvuso ānanda; suladdhaṃ vo, āvuso ānanda, ye ettha satthu <note>satthārā (syā.)</note> sammukhā antevāsikābhisekena abhisittā’’ti. Alattha <pb ed="P" n="2.0153"/> kho subhaddo paribbājako bhagavato santike pabbajjaṃ, alattha upasampadaṃ. Acirūpasampanno kho panāyasmā subhaddo eko vūpakaṭṭho appamatto ātāpī pahitatto viharanto nacirasseva – ‘yassatthāya kulaputtā sammadeva agārasmā anagāriyaṃ pabbajanti’ tadanuttaraṃ brahmacariyapariyosānaṃ diṭṭheva dhamme sayaṃ abhiññā sacchikatvā upasampajja vihāsi. ‘Khīṇā jāti, vusitaṃ brahmacariyaṃ, kataṃ karaṇīyaṃ, nāparaṃ itthattāyā’ti <pb ed="T" n="2.0178"/> abbhaññāsi. Aññataro kho panāyasmā subhaddo arahataṃ ahosi. So bhagavato pacchimo sakkhisāvako ahosīti.</p> <pb ed="V" n="2.0115"/> <note>satthārā (syā.)</note> <pb ed="P" n="2.0153"/> <pb ed="T" n="2.0178"/> <p rend="centre">Pañcamo bhāṇavāro.</p> <p rend="subhead">Tathāgatapacchimavācā</p>
215. Then Subhadda the wanderer said to the Blessed One: “Magnificent, lord! Magnificent!
Just as, venerable sir, one might set upright what has been overturned, or reveal what is hidden, or point out the path to one who is lost, or hold up a lamp in the darkness so that those with eyes might see forms, even so has the Dhamma been made clear in many ways by the Blessed One.
I go to the Blessed One for refuge, and to the Dhamma, and to the Saṅgha of monks.
May I receive the going forth in the Blessed One’s presence? May I receive the full admission?”

“Subhadda, whoever, having formerly belonged to another sect, wishes to receive the going forth in this Dhamma and Discipline, wishes to receive the full admission, remains on probation for a period of four months. After four months, if the monks are satisfied with him, they give him the going forth and the full admission to the state of a *bhikkhu*.
However, there can be a distinction of persons in this.”

“Venerable sir, if those who formerly belonged to another sect and desire the going forth and the full admission in this Dhamma and Discipline live on probation for four months, and if at the end of the four months the *bhikkhus* being satisfied with them give them the going forth and the full admission to the *bhikkhus*' state, then I will live on probation for four years. At the end of the four years if the *bhikkhus* are satisfied with me, let them give me the going forth and the full admission to the *bhikkhus*' state."

Then the Blessed One said to the venerable Ānanda: “Then, Ānanda, let Subhadda receive the going forth.”
“So be it, venerable sir,” the venerable Ānanda replied to the Blessed One.
Then Subhadda the wanderer said to the venerable Ānanda: “It is a gain for you, friend Ānanda; a blessing for you, friend Ānanda, that in the presence of the Teacher himself you have received the sprinkling of ordination as a disciple.”

Then Subhadda the wanderer received the going forth in the Blessed One’s presence, he received the full admission.
And soon, not long after his full admission, dwelling alone, withdrawn, diligent, ardent, and resolute, the venerable Subhadda, by realizing for himself with direct knowledge, here and now entered upon and abided in that supreme goal of the holy life (*brahmacariyapariyosāna*) for the sake of which clansmen rightly go forth from the home life into homelessness.
He understood: ‘Destroyed is birth; the holy life has been lived; what had to be done has been done; there is nothing further here.’
And the venerable Subhadda became another one of the *arhats*.
He was the last personal disciple of the Blessed One.

The fifth section for recitation.
The Last Words of the *Tathāgata*.
216
<p n="216" rend="bodytext"><hi rend="paranum">216</hi><hi rend="dot">.</hi> Atha <pb ed="P" n="2.0154"/> kho bhagavā āyasmantaṃ ānandaṃ āmantesi – ‘‘siyā kho panānanda, tumhākaṃ evamassa – ‘atītasatthukaṃ pāvacanaṃ, natthi no satthā’ti. Na kho panetaṃ, ānanda, evaṃ daṭṭhabbaṃ. Yo vo, ānanda, mayā dhammo ca vinayo <pb ed="M" n="2.0127"/> ca desito paññatto, so vo mamaccayena satthā. Yathā kho panānanda, etarahi bhikkhū aññamaññaṃ āvusovādena samudācaranti, na kho mamaccayena evaṃ samudācaritabbaṃ. Theratarena, ānanda, bhikkhunā navakataro bhikkhu nāmena vā gottena vā āvusovādena vā samudācaritabbo. Navakatarena bhikkhunā therataro bhikkhu ‘bhante’ti vā ‘āyasmā’ti vā samudācaritabbo. Ākaṅkhamāno, ānanda, saṅgho mamaccayena khuddānukhuddakāni sikkhāpadāni samūhanatu. Channassa, ānanda, bhikkhuno mamaccayena brahmadaṇḍo dātabbo’’ti. ‘‘Katamo pana, bhante, brahmadaṇḍo’’ti? ‘‘Channo, ānanda, bhikkhu yaṃ iccheyya, taṃ vadeyya. So bhikkhūhi neva vattabbo, na ovaditabbo, na anusāsitabbo’’ti.</p>
216. Then the Blessed One addressed the Venerable Ānanda, saying: “It may be, Ānanda, that this thought will occur to you: ‘The teaching has lost its arbitrator; we are without a Teacher.’

But it should not be seen like that, Ānanda.

Ānanda, whatever Dharma (dhammo) and Discipline (vinayo) I have taught and established, that will be your Teacher after my passing (mamaccayena satthā).

Just as now, Ānanda, the monks address one another as ‘friend’ (āvusovādena), it should not be done so after my passing.

The senior monk (theratarena bhikkhunā), Ānanda, may address the newer monk (navakataro bhikkhu) by name (nāmena), clan (gottena), or as ‘friend’ (āvusovādena).

The newer monk (navakatarena bhikkhunā) should address the senior monk (therataro bhikkhu) as ‘venerable sir’ (bhante’ti) or ‘venerable’ (āyasmā’ti).

If the Saṅgha wishes, Ānanda, after my passing, it may abolish the lesser and minor precepts (khuddānukhuddakāni sikkhāpadāni samūhanatu).

After my passing, Ānanda, the monk Channa should be given the Brahma-penalty (brahmadaṇḍo dātabbo).’

‘‘But venerable sir (bhante), what is the Brahma-penalty (brahmadaṇḍo)?’’ ‘‘Channa, Ānanda, may say whatever the monk wishes.

He should not be spoken to, admonished, or instructed by the monks (bhikkhūhi neva vattabbo, na ovaditabbo, na anusāsitabbo).’’
<p n="216" rend="bodytext"><hi rend="paranum">216</hi><hi rend="dot">.</hi> Idāni bhikkhusaṅghassa ovādaṃ ārabhi, taṃ dassetuṃ <hi rend="bold">atha kho bhagavā</hi>tiādi vuttaṃ. Tattha <hi rend="bold">desito paññatto</hi>ti dhammopi desito ceva <pb ed="M" n="2.0183"/> paññatto ca, vinayopi desito ceva paññatto ca. <hi rend="bold">Paññatto</hi> ca nāma ṭhapito paṭṭhapitoti attho. <hi rend="bold">So vo mamaccayenā</hi>ti so dhammavinayo tumhākaṃ mamaccayena satthā. Mayā hi vo ṭhiteneva – ‘‘idaṃ lahukaṃ, idaṃ garukaṃ, idaṃ satekicchaṃ, idaṃ atekicchaṃ, idaṃ lokavajjaṃ, idaṃ paṇṇattivajjaṃ, ayaṃ āpatti puggalassa santike vuṭṭhāti, ayaṃ āpatti gaṇassa santike vuṭṭhāti, ayaṃ saṅghassa santike vuṭṭhātī’’ti <pb ed="V" n="2.0164"/> sattāpattikkhandhavasena otiṇṇe vatthusmiṃ sakhandhakaparivāro ubhatovibhaṅgo <hi rend="bold">vinayo</hi> nāma desito, taṃ sakalampi vinayapiṭakaṃ mayi parinibbute tumhākaṃ satthukiccaṃ sādhessati.</p> <p rend="bodytext">Ṭhiteneva ca mayā – ‘‘ime cattāro satipaṭṭhānā, cattāro sammappadhānā, cattāro iddhipādā, pañca indriyāni, pañca balāni, satta bojjhaṅgā, ariyo aṭṭhaṅgiko maggo’’ti tena tenākārena ime dhamme vibhajitvā vibhajitvā suttantapiṭakaṃ desitaṃ, taṃ sakalampi suttantapiṭakaṃ mayi parinibbute tumhākaṃ satthukiccaṃ sādhessati. Ṭhiteneva ca mayā – ‘‘ime pañcakkhandhā, dvādasāyatanāni, aṭṭhārasa dhātuyo, cattāri saccāni, bāvīsatindriyāni, nava hetū, cattāro āhārā, satta phassā, satta vedanā, satta saññā, satta sañcetanā, satta cittāni. Tatrāpi ‘ettakā dhammā kāmāvacarā, ettakā rūpāvacarā, ettakā arūpāvacarā, ettakā pariyāpannā, ettakā apariyāpannā, ettakā lokiyā, ettakā lokuttarā’ti’’ ime dhamme vibhajitvā vibhajitvā catuvīsatisamantapaṭṭhānaanantanayamahāpaṭṭhānapaṭimaṇḍitaṃ abhidhammapiṭakaṃ desitaṃ, taṃ sakalampi abhidhammapiṭakaṃ mayi parinibbute tumhākaṃ satthukiccaṃ sādhessati.</p> <p rend="bodytext">Iti sabbampetaṃ abhisambodhito yāva parinibbānā pañcacattālīsavassāni bhāsitaṃ lapitaṃ – ‘‘tīṇi piṭakāni, pañca nikāyā, navaṅgāni, caturāsīti dhammakkhandhasahassānī’’ti evaṃ mahāpabhedaṃ hoti. Iti <pb ed="P" n="2.0592"/> imāni caturāsīti dhammakkhandhasahassāni tiṭṭhanti, ahaṃ ekova parinibbāyāmi. Ahañca kho pana dāni ekakova ovadāmi anusāsāmi, mayi parinibbute imāni caturāsīti dhammakkhandhasahassāni tumhe ovadissanti anusāsissantīti evaṃ bhagavā bahūni kāraṇāni dassento – ‘‘so vo mamaccayena satthā’’ti ovaditvā puna anāgate cārittaṃ dassento <hi rend="bold">yathā kho panā</hi>tiādimāha.</p> <pb ed="P" n="2.0592"/> <hi rend="bold">yathā kho panā</hi> <p rend="bodytext">Tattha <pb ed="M" n="2.0184"/><hi rend="bold">samudācarantī</hi>ti kathenti voharanti. <hi rend="bold">Nāmena vā gottena vā</hi>ti navakāti avatvā ‘‘tissa, nāgā’’ti evaṃ nāmena vā, ‘‘kassapa, gotamā’’ti evaṃ gottena vā, ‘‘āvuso tissa, āvuso kassapā’’ti evaṃ āvusovādena vā samudācaritabbo. <hi rend="bold">Bhanteti vā āyasmāti vā</hi>ti bhante tissa, āyasmā tissāti evaṃ samudācaritabbo. <hi rend="bold">Samūhanatū</hi>ti ākaṅkhamāno samūhanatu, yadi icchati samūhaneyyāti attho. Kasmā pana samūhanathāti ekaṃseneva avatvā vikappavacaneneva ṭhapesīti? Mahākassapassa balaṃ diṭṭhattā. Passati hi bhagavā <pb ed="V" n="2.0165"/> – ‘‘samūhanathāti vuttepi saṅgītikāle kassapo na samūhanissatī’’ti. Tasmā vikappeneva ṭhapesi.</p> <pb ed="M" n="2.0184"/> <hi rend="bold">samudācarantī</hi> <hi rend="bold">Nāmena vā gottena vā</hi> <hi rend="bold">Bhanteti vā āyasmāti vā</hi> <hi rend="bold">Samūhanatū</hi> <pb ed="V" n="2.0165"/> <p rend="bodytext">Tattha – ‘‘ekacce therā evamāhaṃsu – cattāri pārājikāni ṭhapetvā avasesāni khuddānukhuddakānī’’tiādinā nayena pañcasatikasaṅgītiyaṃ <hi rend="bold">khuddānukhuddakakathā</hi> āgatāva vinicchayo pettha <hi rend="bold">samantapāsādikāyaṃ</hi> vutto. Keci panāhu – ‘‘bhante, nāgasena, katamaṃ khuddakaṃ, katamaṃ anukhuddaka’’nti milindena raññā pucchito. ‘‘Dukkaṭaṃ, mahārāja, khuddakaṃ, dubbhāsitaṃ anukhuddaka’’nti vuttattā nāgasenatthero khuddānukhuddakaṃ jānāti. Mahākassapo pana taṃ ajānanto –</p> <hi rend="bold">khuddānukhuddakakathā</hi> <hi rend="bold">samantapāsādikāyaṃ</hi> <p rend="indent">‘‘Suṇātu me, āvuso, saṅgho santamhākaṃ sikkhāpadāni gihigatāni, gihinopi jānanti – ‘‘idaṃ vo samaṇānaṃ sakyaputtiyānaṃ kappati, idaṃ vo na kappatī’’ti. Sace mayaṃ khuddānukhuddakāni sikkhāpadāni samūhanissāma, bhavissanti vattāro – ‘‘dhūmakālikaṃ samaṇena gotamena sāvakānaṃ sikkhāpadaṃ paññattaṃ, yāva nesaṃ satthā aṭṭhāsi, tāvime sikkhāpadesu sikkhiṃsu, yato imesaṃ satthā parinibbuto, na dānime sikkhāpadesu sikkhantī’’ti. Yadi saṅghassa <pb ed="P" n="2.0593"/> pattakallaṃ, saṅgho apaññattaṃ na paññapeyya, paññattaṃ na samucchindeyya, yathāpaññattesu sikkhāpadesu samādāya vatteyya. Esā ñattīti –</p> <pb ed="P" n="2.0593"/> <p rend="bodytext">Kammavācaṃ sāvesīti. Na taṃ evaṃ gahetabbaṃ. Nāgasenatthero hi – ‘‘paravādino okāso mā ahosī’’ti evamāha. Mahākassapatthero ‘‘khuddānukhuddakāpattiṃ na samūhanissāmī’’ti kammavācaṃ sāvesi.</p> <p rend="bodytext"><hi rend="bold">Brahmadaṇḍakathāpi</hi><pb ed="M" n="2.0185"/> saṅgītiyaṃ āgatattāsamantapāsādikāyaṃ vinicchitā.</p> <hi rend="bold">Brahmadaṇḍakathāpi</hi> <pb ed="M" n="2.0185"/> <p rend="bodytext"><hi rend="bold">Kaṅkhā</hi>ti dveḷhakaṃ. <hi rend="bold">Vimatī</hi>ti vinicchituṃ asamatthatā, buddho nu kho, na buddho nu kho, dhammo nu kho, na dhammo nu kho, saṅgho nu kho, na saṅgho nu kho, maggo nu kho, na maggo nu kho, paṭipadā nu kho, na paṭipadā nu khoti yassa saṃsayo uppajjeyya, taṃ vo vadāmi ‘‘pucchatha bhikkhave’’ti ayamettha saṅkhepattho. <hi rend="bold">Satthugāravenāpi na puccheyyāthā</hi>ti mayaṃ satthusantike pabbajimha, cattāro paccayāpi no satthu santakāva, te mayaṃ ettakaṃ kālaṃ kaṅkhaṃ akatvā <pb ed="V" n="2.0166"/> na arahāma ajja pacchimakāle kaṅkhaṃ kātunti sace evaṃ satthari gāravena na pucchatha. <hi rend="bold">Sahāyakopi bhikkhave sahāyakassa ārocetū</hi>ti tumhākaṃ yo yassa bhikkhuno sandiṭṭho sambhatto, so tassa ārocetu, ahaṃ etassa bhikkhussa kathessāmi, tassa kathaṃ sutvā sabbe nikkaṅkhā bhavissathāti dasseti.</p> <hi rend="bold">Kaṅkhā</hi> <hi rend="bold">Vimatī</hi> <hi rend="bold">Satthugāravenāpi na puccheyyāthā</hi> <pb ed="V" n="2.0166"/> <hi rend="bold">Sahāyakopi bhikkhave sahāyakassa ārocetū</hi> <p rend="bodytext"><hi rend="bold">Evaṃ pasanno</hi>ti evaṃ saddahāmi ahanti attho. <hi rend="bold">Ñāṇamevā</hi>ti nikkaṅkhabhāvapaccakkhakaraṇañāṇaṃyeva, ettha tathāgatassa na saddhāmattanti attho. <hi rend="bold">Imesañhi, ānandā</hi>ti imesaṃ antosāṇiyaṃ nisinnānaṃ pañcannaṃ bhikkhusatānaṃ. <hi rend="bold">Yo pacchimako</hi>ti yo guṇavasena pacchimako. Ānandattheraṃyeva sandhāyāha.</p> <hi rend="bold">Evaṃ pasanno</hi> <hi rend="bold">Ñāṇamevā</hi> <hi rend="bold">Imesañhi, ānandā</hi> <hi rend="bold">Yo pacchimako</hi>
216. Now, he begins the instruction to the monastic community, and to show that, it is said, "Then, indeed, the Blessed One," etc.

There, "taught and designated" means the Dharma is both taught and designated, and the Vinaya is both taught and designated.

"Designated" means named, established, and set forth; this is the meaning.

"So vo mamaccayenā" means that the Dharma and Vinaya will be your teacher after my passing.

Indeed, by me standing firm – "This is light, this is heavy, this requires treatment, this does not require treatment, this is objectionable to the world, this is objectionable by designation, this offense is resolved in the presence of an individual, this offense is resolved in the presence of a group, this offense is resolved in the presence of the Sangha" – thus, due to the force of the aggregates of offenses, in a matter that has been decided, with its related aggregates, the Ubhatovibhaṅga called the "Vinaya" was taught; all of that Vinaya Piṭaka, when I have passed into *nirvāṇa*, will accomplish the task of your teacher.

And, by me standing firm – "These are the four foundations of mindfulness (catvāri smṛtyupasthānāni), the four right exertions (catvāri samyakprahāṇāni), the four bases of spiritual power (catvāri ṛddhipādāḥ), the five faculties (pañca indriyāṇi), the five powers (pañca balāni), the seven factors of awakening (sapta bojjhaṅgāḥ), the noble eightfold path (āryāṣṭāṅgiko mārgaḥ)" – in that way, dividing and distinguishing these dharmas, the Sūtra Piṭaka was taught; all of that Sūtra Piṭaka, when I have passed into *nirvāṇa*, will accomplish the task of your teacher.

And, by me standing firm – "These are the five aggregates (pañcakkhandhā), the twelve sense bases (dvādasāyatanāni), the eighteen elements (aṣṭārasa dhātuyo), the four truths (cattāri satyāni), the twenty-two faculties (bāvīsatindriyāni), the nine causes (nava hetū), the four kinds of nutriment (cattāro āhārā), the seven contacts (sapta phassā), the seven feelings (sapta vedanā), the seven perceptions (sapta saññā), the seven volitions (sapta sañcetanā), the seven consciousnesses (sapta cittāni)."

There also, 'So many *dharmas* belong to the realm of desire (*kāmāvacarā*), so many belong to the realm of form (*rūpāvacarā*), so many belong to the formless realm (*arūpāvacarā*), so many are included (*pariyāpannā*), so many are not included (*apariyāpannā*), so many are mundane (*lokiyā*), so many are supramundane (*lokuttarā*)' – dividing and distinguishing these *dharmas*, the Abhidhamma Piṭaka, adorned with the twenty-four conditions of the Samantapaṭṭhāna and the Anantanayamahāpaṭṭhāna, was taught; all of that Abhidhamma Piṭaka, when I have passed into *nirvāṇa*, will accomplish the task of your teacher.

Thus, all of this, from complete enlightenment until passing into *nirvāṇa*, for forty-five years, was spoken and uttered – "The three Piṭakas, the five Nikāyas, the nine divisions, the eighty-four thousand aggregates of Dharma (dhammakkhandhasahassānī)" – thus, there is a great distinction.

Thus, these eighty-four thousand aggregates of Dharma remain, but I alone will pass into *nirvāṇa*.

And now, indeed, I alone instruct and admonish, but when I have passed into *nirvāṇa*, these eighty-four thousand aggregates of Dharma will instruct and admonish you; thus, the Blessed One, showing many reasons – "The Dharma is your teacher after my passing" – having instructed thus, and again showing the conduct in the future, said "Just as, indeed," etc.

Just as, indeed, there, "<hi rend="bold">samudācarantī</hi>" means they speak and refer to.

"<hi rend="bold">nāmena vā gottena vā</hi>" means, not saying "novice," but "Tissa, Nāga," thus by name, or "Kassapa, Gotama," thus by lineage, or "Āvuso Tissa, Āvuso Kassapa," thus with the greeting "Āvuso," one should address him.

"<hi rend="bold">bhanteti vā āyasmāti vā</hi>" means, "Bhante Tissa, Āyasmā Tissa," thus one should address him.

"<hi rend="bold">samūhanatū</hi>" means, if he desires, let him remove it; the meaning is, if he wishes, he should remove it.

Why, indeed, did he establish it with a differentiating statement instead of saying it with a one-sided statement? Because he saw the strength of Mahākassapa.

For the Blessed One sees – "Even if I say, 'Let him remove it,' Kassapa will not remove it at the Saṅgīti time."

Therefore, he established it with a differentiating statement.

There – "Some elders said thus – having set aside the four pārājikas, the remaining lesser and minor [rules]," – in this way, in the Pañcasatikasaṅgīti, the topic of the lesser and minor [rules] came up, and the decision is said to be in the Samantapāsādikā.

Some, however, said – "Bhante Nāgasena, which is lesser, which is minor?" – thus Milinda the king was asked.

"Dukkaṭaṃ, Mahārāja, is lesser, dubbhāsitaṃ is minor," because it was said, Nāgasena Thera knows the lesser and minor.

But Mahākassapa, not knowing that –

"<hi rend="bold">khuddānukhuddakakathā</hi> <hi rend="bold">samantapāsādikāyaṃ</hi>" "Let the Sangha listen to me, friends, our training rules have gone to the householders, even the householders know – 'This is suitable for you ascetics, sons of the Sakyas, this is not suitable for you.'"

If we were to remove the lesser and minor training rules, there would be speakers – "The training rule was designated for those with smoky minds by the ascetic Gotama for the disciples; as long as their teacher remained, so long did these train in the training rules; since their teacher has passed away, now these do not train in the training rules."

If it seems appropriate to the Sangha, the Sangha should not lay down what has not been laid down, nor should it abolish what has been laid down. It should proceed in conformity with and according to the training rules that have been laid down.

This is the declaration –

He recited the Kammavāca.

That should not be taken thus.

Nāgasena Thera, indeed, said thus – "Lest the opponents have an opportunity."

Mahākassapa Thera recited the Kammavāca, "I will not remove the offense regarding the lesser and minor."

Brahmadaṇḍakathāpi
0185"/> *saṅgītiyaṃ āgatattāsamantapāsādikāyaṃ vinicchitā*.
</p> <hi rend="bold">brahmadaṇḍakathāpi</hi> <pb ed="m" n="2.
