0166"/> na *arahāma ajja pacchimakāle kaṅkhaṃ kātunti sace evaṃ satthari gāravena na *pucchatha*.
<hi rend="bold">sahāyakopi bhikkhave sahāyakassa ārocetū</hi>ti tumhākaṃ yo yassa *bhikkhuno sandiṭṭho sambhatto*, so tassa *ārocetu*, ahaṃ etassa *bhikkhussa kathessāmi*, tassa *kathaṃ sutvā sabbe nikkaṅkhā bhavissathāti dasseti*.
</p> <hi rend="bold">kaṅkhā</hi> <hi rend="bold">vimatī</hi> <hi rend="bold">satthugāravenāpi na puccheyyāthā</hi> <pb ed="v" n="2.

<hi rend="bold">ñāṇamevā</hi>ti *nikkaṅkhabhāvapaccakkhakaraṇañāṇaṃyeva*, ettha *tathāgatassa na saddhāmattanti attho*.

217
<p n="217" rend="bodytext"><hi rend="paranum">217</hi><hi rend="dot">.</hi> Atha kho bhagavā bhikkhū āmantesi – ‘‘siyā kho pana, bhikkhave, ekabhikkhussāpi kaṅkhā vā vimati vā buddhe vā dhamme vā saṅghe vā magge vā paṭipadāya vā, pucchatha, bhikkhave, mā pacchā vippaṭisārino <pb ed="P" n="2.0155"/> ahuvattha – ‘sammukhībhūto no satthā ahosi <pb ed="V" n="2.0116"/>, na mayaṃ sakkhimhā bhagavantaṃ sammukhā paṭipucchitu’’’ nti. Evaṃ vutte te bhikkhū tuṇhī ahesuṃ. Dutiyampi kho bhagavā…pe… tatiyampi kho bhagavā bhikkhū āmantesi – ‘‘siyā kho pana, bhikkhave, ekabhikkhussāpi kaṅkhā vā vimati vā buddhe vā dhamme vā saṅghe vā magge vā paṭipadāya vā, pucchatha, bhikkhave, mā pacchā vippaṭisārino ahuvattha – ‘sammukhībhūto no satthā ahosi <pb ed="T" n="2.0179"/>, na mayaṃ sakkhimhā bhagavantaṃ sammukhā paṭipucchitu’’’ nti. Tatiyampi kho te bhikkhū tuṇhī ahesuṃ. Atha kho bhagavā bhikkhū āmantesi – ‘‘siyā kho pana, bhikkhave, satthugāravenapi na puccheyyātha. Sahāyakopi, bhikkhave, sahāyakassa ārocetū’’ti. Evaṃ vutte te bhikkhū tuṇhī ahesuṃ. Atha kho āyasmā ānando bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – ‘‘acchariyaṃ, bhante, abbhutaṃ, bhante, evaṃ pasanno ahaṃ, bhante, imasmiṃ bhikkhusaṅghe, ‘natthi ekabhikkhussāpi kaṅkhā vā vimati vā buddhe vā dhamme vā saṅghe vā magge vā paṭipadāya vā’’’ti. ‘‘Pasādā kho tvaṃ, ānanda, vadesi, ñāṇameva hettha, ānanda, tathāgatassa. Natthi imasmiṃ bhikkhusaṅghe ekabhikkhussāpi kaṅkhā vā vimati vā buddhe vā dhamme vā saṅghe vā magge vā paṭipadāya vā. Imesañhi, ānanda, pañcannaṃ bhikkhusatānaṃ yo pacchimako bhikkhu, so sotāpanno avinipātadhammo niyato sambodhiparāyaṇo’’ti.</p>
217. Then the Blessed One addressed the monks, saying: “It may be, monks, that even one monk has doubt or perplexity about the Buddha, the *Dharma* (dhamma), or the *Sangha* (saṅgha), the path (*mārga*, magge) or the practice (*pratipadā*, paṭipadāya), ask! Do not afterwards feel remorse, thinking: ‘The Teacher (*śāstṛ*, satthā) was there before us, and we failed to ask the Lord face to face!’”

When this was said, the monks were silent.

A second time, … A third time, the Blessed One addressed the monks, saying: “It may be, monks, that even one monk has doubt or perplexity about the Buddha, the Dharma, or the Sangha, the path or the practice, ask! Do not afterwards feel remorse, thinking: ‘The Teacher was there before us, and we failed to ask the Lord face to face!’”

A third time, the monks were silent.

Then the Blessed One addressed the monks, saying: “It may be, monks, out of respect for the Teacher (śāstṛ-gāraveṇa) that you do not ask.

Then, monks, let one friend tell it to another.”

When this was said, the monks were silent.

Then the Venerable Ānanda said to the Blessed One: “It is wonderful, Lord (*bhante*), it is marvellous! I clearly perceive that in this *bhikṣu-saṃgha* (bhikkhusaṅghe) there is not one monk who has doubts or uncertainty about the Buddha, the Dharma, or the Sangha, or about the path or the practice.”

“Out of confidence, Ānanda, you speak thus. But here, Ānanda, the *Tathāgata* (tathāgatassa) knows for certain that in this *bhikṣu-saṃgha* there is not one monk who has doubts or uncertainty about the Buddha, the Dharma, or the Sangha, or about the path or the practice.

For, Ānanda, among these five hundred monks even the lowest is a *stream-enterer* (sotāpanna), secure from downfall, assured, and bound for enlightenment (*sambodhi-parāyaṇa*).”
218
<p n="218" rend="bodytext"><hi rend="paranum">218</hi><hi rend="dot">.</hi> Atha <pb ed="T" n="2.0180"/><pb ed="M" n="2.0128"/> kho bhagavā bhikkhū āmantesi – ‘‘handa <pb ed="P" n="2.0156"/> dāni, bhikkhave, āmantayāmi vo, vayadhammā saṅkhārā appamādena sampādethā’’ti. Ayaṃ tathāgatassa pacchimā vācā.</p> <p rend="subhead">Parinibbutakathā</p>
Then the Blessed One addressed the monks, "Come now, monks, I exhort you: All conditioned things are subject to decay. Strive with earnestness!" This was the last word of the *Tathāgata*.
<p n="218" rend="bodytext"><hi rend="paranum">218</hi><hi rend="dot">.</hi><hi rend="bold">Appamādena sampādethā</hi>ti satiavippavāsena sabbakiccāni sampādeyyātha. Iti bhagavā parinibbānamañce nipanno pañcacattālīsa vassāni dinnaṃ ovādaṃ sabbaṃ ekasmiṃ appamādapadeyeva pakkhipitvā adāsi. <hi rend="bold">Ayaṃ tathāgatassa pacchimā vācā</hi>ti idaṃ pana saṅgītikārakānaṃ <pb ed="P" n="2.0594"/> vacanaṃ.</p> <p rend="subhead">Parinibbutakathāvaṇṇanā</p>
"Accomplish [your goals] with diligence (appamādena sampādethā)," meaning you should accomplish all your tasks with mindfulness (satiavippavāsena).

Thus, the Blessed One, lying on the deathbed (parinibbānamañce), having given advice for forty-five years, placed it all into a single word: diligence (appamāda).

"This is the last teaching of the Tathāgata (ayaṃ tathāgatassa pacchimā vācā)," this statement, however, is the word of the compilers (saṅgītikārakānaṃ vacanaṃ).

Explanation of the Discourse on the Final Passing (parinibbutakathāvaṇṇanā).
219
<p n="219" rend="bodytext"><hi rend="paranum">219</hi><hi rend="dot">.</hi> Atha kho bhagavā paṭhamaṃ jhānaṃ samāpajji, paṭhamajjhānā vuṭṭhahitvā dutiyaṃ jhānaṃ samāpajji, dutiyajjhānā vuṭṭhahitvā tatiyaṃ jhānaṃ samāpajji, tatiyajjhānā vuṭṭhahitvā catutthaṃ jhānaṃ samāpajji. Catutthajjhānā vuṭṭhahitvā ākāsānañcāyatanaṃ samāpajji, ākāsānañcāyatanasamāpattiyā vuṭṭhahitvā viññāṇañcāyatanaṃ samāpajji, viññāṇañcāyatanasamāpattiyā vuṭṭhahitvā ākiñcaññāyatanaṃ samāpajji, ākiñcaññāyatanasamāpattiyā vuṭṭhahitvā nevasaññānāsaññāyatanaṃ samāpajji, nevasaññānāsaññāyatanasamāpattiyā vuṭṭhahitvā saññāvedayitanirodhaṃ samāpajji.</p> <p rend="bodytext">Atha kho āyasmā ānando āyasmantaṃ anuruddhaṃ etadavoca – ‘‘parinibbuto, bhante anuruddha <pb ed="V" n="2.0117"/>, bhagavā’’ti. ‘‘Nāvuso ānanda, bhagavā parinibbuto, saññāvedayitanirodhaṃ samāpanno’’ti.</p> <pb ed="V" n="2.0117"/> <p rend="bodytext">Atha kho bhagavā saññāvedayitanirodhasamāpattiyā vuṭṭhahitvā nevasaññānāsaññāyatanaṃ samāpajji, nevasaññānāsaññāyatanasamāpattiyā vuṭṭhahitvā ākiñcaññāyatanaṃ samāpajji, ākiñcaññāyatanasamāpattiyā vuṭṭhahitvā viññāṇañcāyatanaṃ samāpajji, viññāṇañcāyatanasamāpattiyā vuṭṭhahitvā ākāsānañcāyatanaṃ samāpajji, ākāsānañcāyatanasamāpattiyā vuṭṭhahitvā catutthaṃ jhānaṃ <pb ed="T" n="2.0181"/> samāpajji, catutthajjhānā vuṭṭhahitvā tatiyaṃ jhānaṃ samāpajji, tatiyajjhānā vuṭṭhahitvā dutiyaṃ jhānaṃ samāpajji, dutiyajjhānā vuṭṭhahitvā paṭhamaṃ jhānaṃ samāpajji, paṭhamajjhānā vuṭṭhahitvā dutiyaṃ jhānaṃ samāpajji, dutiyajjhānā vuṭṭhahitvā tatiyaṃ jhānaṃ samāpajji, tatiyajjhānā vuṭṭhahitvā catutthaṃ jhānaṃ samāpajji, catutthajjhānā vuṭṭhahitvā samanantarā bhagavā parinibbāyi.</p> <pb ed="T" n="2.0181"/>
219. Then the Blessed One entered the first *jhāna*. Rising from the first *jhāna*, he entered the second *jhāna*. Rising from the second *jhāna*, he entered the third *jhāna*. Rising from the third *jhāna*, he entered the fourth *jhāna*.

Rising from the fourth *jhāna*, he entered the dimension of the infinitude of space (*ākāsānañcāyatana*). Rising from the attainment of the dimension of the infinitude of space, he entered the dimension of the infinitude of consciousness (*viññāṇañcāyatana*). Rising from the attainment of the dimension of the infinitude of consciousness, he entered the dimension of nothingness (*ākiñcaññāyatana*). Rising from the attainment of the dimension of nothingness, he entered the dimension of neither-perception-nor-non-perception (*nevasaññānāsaññāyatana*). Rising from the attainment of the dimension of neither-perception-nor-non-perception, he entered the cessation of perception and feeling (*saññāvedayitanirodha*).

Then venerable Ānanda said this to venerable Anuruddha: "The Blessed One has attained final *nirvana*, venerable Anuruddha."

"No, friend Ānanda, the Blessed One has not attained final *nirvana*. He has entered the cessation of perception and feeling (*saññāvedayitanirodhaṃ samāpanno*)."

Then the Blessed One, rising from the attainment of the cessation of perception and feeling (*saññāvedayitanirodhasamāpattiyā vuṭṭhahitvā*), entered the dimension of neither-perception-nor-non-perception (*nevasaññānāsaññāyatanaṃ samāpajji*). Rising from the attainment of the dimension of neither-perception-nor-non-perception, he entered the dimension of nothingness. Rising from the attainment of the dimension of nothingness, he entered the dimension of the infinitude of consciousness. Rising from the attainment of the dimension of the infinitude of space, he entered the fourth *jhāna*. Rising from the fourth *jhāna*, he entered the third *jhāna*. Rising from the third *jhāna*, he entered the second *jhāna*. Rising from the second *jhāna*, he entered the first *jhāna*. Rising from the first *jhāna*, he entered the second *jhāna*. Rising from the second *jhāna*, he entered the third *jhāna*. Rising from the third *jhāna*, he entered the fourth *jhāna*. Rising from the fourth *jhāna*, immediately thereafter, the Blessed One attained final *nirvana* (*parinibbāyi*).
<p n="219" rend="bodytext"><hi rend="paranum">219</hi><hi rend="dot">.</hi> Ito paraṃ yaṃ parinibbānaparikammaṃ katvā bhagavā parinibbuto, taṃ dassetuṃ <hi rend="bold">atha kho bhagavā paṭhamaṃ jhāna</hi>ntiādi vuttaṃ. Tattha <hi rend="bold">parinibbuto bhante</hi>ti nirodhaṃ samāpannassa bhagavato assāsapassāsānaṃ abhāvaṃ disvā pucchati. <hi rend="bold">Na āvuso</hi>ti thero kathaṃ jānāti? Thero kira satthārā saddhiṃyeva taṃ taṃ samāpattiṃ samāpajjanto yāva nevasaññānāsaññāyatanā vuṭṭhānaṃ, tāva gantvā idāni bhagavā <pb ed="M" n="2.0186"/> nirodhaṃ samāpanno, antonirodhe ca kālaṅkiriyā nāma natthīti jānāti.</p> <p rend="bodytext"><hi rend="bold">Atha kho bhagavā saññāvedayitanirodhasamāpattiyā vuṭṭhahitvā nevasaññānāsaññāyatanaṃ samāpajji…pe… tatiyajjhānā vuṭṭhahitvā catutthajjhānaṃ samāpajjī</hi>ti ettha bhagavā catuvīsatiyā ṭhānesu paṭhamajjhānaṃ samāpajji, terasasu ṭhānesu dutiyajjhānaṃ, tathā tatiyajjhānaṃ, pannarasasu ṭhānesu catutthajjhānaṃ samāpajji. Kathaṃ? Dasasu asubhesu, dvattiṃsākāre aṭṭhasu kasiṇesu, mettākaruṇāmuditāsu, ānāpāne, paricchedākāseti imesu tāva catuvīsatiyā ṭhānesu paṭhamajjhānaṃ samāpajji. Ṭhapetvā pana dvattiṃsākārañca dasa asubhāni ca sesesu terasasu dutiyajjhānaṃ <pb ed="V" n="2.0167"/>, tesuyeva ca tatiyajjhānaṃ samāpajji. Aṭṭhasu pana kasiṇesu, upekkhābrahmavihāre, ānāpāne, paricchedākāse, catūsu arūpesūti imesu pannarasasu ṭhānesu catutthajjhānaṃ samāpajji. Ayampi ca saṅkhepakathāva. Nibbānapuraṃ pavisanto pana bhagavā dhammassāmī sabbāpi catuvīsatikoṭisatasahassasaṅkhyā samāpattiyo pavisitvā videsaṃ gacchanto ñātijanaṃ āliṅgetvā viya sabbasamāpattisukhaṃ anubhavitvā paviṭṭho.</p> <hi rend="bold">Atha kho bhagavā saññāvedayitanirodhasamāpattiyā vuṭṭhahitvā nevasaññānāsaññāyatanaṃ samāpajji…pe… tatiyajjhānā vuṭṭhahitvā catutthajjhānaṃ samāpajjī</hi> <pb ed="V" n="2.0167"/> <p rend="bodytext"><hi rend="bold">Catutthajjhānā vuṭṭhahitvā samanantarā bhagavā parinibbāyī</hi>ti ettha jhānasamanantaraṃ, paccavekkhaṇāsamanantaranti dve samanantarāni. Tattha jhānā vuṭṭhāya bhavaṅgaṃ otiṇṇassa tattheva parinibbānaṃ <hi rend="bold">jhānasamanantaraṃ</hi> nāma. Jhānā vuṭṭhahitvā puna jhānaṅgāni paccavekkhitvā bhavaṅgaṃ otiṇṇassa tattheva parinibbānaṃ <hi rend="bold">paccavekkhaṇāsamanantaraṃ</hi> nāma. Imānipi dve samanantarāneva. Bhagavā pana jhānaṃ samāpajjitvā jhānā vuṭṭhāya jhānaṅgāni paccavekkhitvā bhavaṅgacittena abyākatena dukkhasaccena parinibbāyi. Ye <pb ed="P" n="2.0595"/> hi keci buddhā vā paccekabuddhā vā ariyasāvakā vā antamaso kunthakipillikaṃ upādāya sabbe bhavaṅgacitteneva abyākatena dukkhasaccena kālaṅkarontīti. <hi rend="bold">Mahābhūmicālādīni</hi> vuttanayānevāti.</p> <hi rend="bold">Catutthajjhānā vuṭṭhahitvā samanantarā bhagavā parinibbāyī</hi> <hi rend="bold">jhānasamanantaraṃ</hi> <hi rend="bold">paccavekkhaṇāsamanantaraṃ</hi> <pb ed="P" n="2.0595"/> <hi rend="bold">Mahābhūmicālādīni</hi>
219. Next, in order to show how the Bhagavān, having performed the preliminary act of *parinirvāṇa*, attained *parinirvāṇa*, it is said, "Then, indeed, the Bhagavān [entered] the first *jhāna*, etc."

There, [the words] "*parinibbuto bhante* [has attained *parinirvāṇa*, venerable sir]" is a question asked after seeing the cessation of inhalation and exhalation of the Bhagavān who has entered cessation (*nirodhaṃ samāpannassa*).

"No, friend" — how does the elder know? The elder, it is said, went along with the Teacher, entering into that and that meditative absorption (*samāpatti*) up to arising from the sphere of neither perception nor non-perception (*nevasaññānāsaññāyatana*), and now the Bhagavān has entered cessation (*nirodhaṃ samāpanno*), and knows that there is no death in cessation.

Then, indeed, the Bhagavān, arising from the meditative attainment of the cessation of perception and feeling (*saññāvedayitanirodhasamāpattiyā vuṭṭhahitvā*) entered the sphere of neither perception nor non-perception (*nevasaññānāsaññāyatanaṃ samāpajji*)…pe… arising from the third *jhāna*, entered the fourth *jhāna*—here, the Bhagavān entered the first *jhāna* in twenty-four places, the second *jhāna* in thirteen places, likewise the third *jhāna*, and the fourth *jhāna* in fifteen places.

How? In the ten impurities (*asubhesu*), in the thirty-two aspects (*dvattiṃsākāre*), in the eight *kasiṇas*, in loving-kindness (*mettā*), compassion (*karuṇā*), joy (*muditā*), in mindfulness of breathing (*ānāpāne*), in the delimited space (*paricchedākāseti*)—in these twenty-four places, the first *jhāna* was entered.

However, setting aside the thirty-two aspects (*dvattiṃsākārañca*) and the ten impurities (*dasa asubhāni ca*), in the remaining thirteen, the second *jhāna*,… in those same, the third *jhāna* was entered.

However, in the eight *kasiṇas*, equanimity (*upekkhā*), the divine abidings (*brahmavihāre*), mindfulness of breathing (*ānāpāne*), delimited space (*paricchedākāse*), in the four formless realms (*arūpesūti*)—in these fifteen places, the fourth *jhāna* was entered.

This is just a summary talk.

However, the Bhagavān, the lord of the Dharma, entering the city of nirvāṇa (*nibbānapuraṃ pavisanto*), having entered into all the meditative attainments (*samāpatti*) numbering twenty-four *koṭis*, hundreds of thousands, and going to a foreign land, like embracing relatives, having experienced all the bliss of meditative attainment (*sabbasamāpatti-sukhaṃ*), entered.

Then, indeed, the Bhagavān, arising from the meditative attainment of the cessation of perception and feeling (*saññāvedayitanirodhasamāpattiyā vuṭṭhahitvā*) entered the sphere of neither perception nor non-perception (*nevasaññānāsaññāyatanaṃ samāpajji*)…pe… arising from the third *jhāna*, entered the fourth *jhāna*.

Having arisen from the fourth *jhāna*, immediately, the Bhagavān attained *parinirvāṇa*—here, immediately after the *jhāna*, immediately after reviewing—these are the two immediate successions.

There, having arisen from *jhāna*, for one who has fallen into the life-continuum (*bhavaṅgaṃ otiṇṇassa*), *parinirvāṇa* in that very place is called immediately after *jhāna* (*jhānasamanantaraṃ*).

Having arisen from *jhāna*, again, having reviewed the factors of *jhāna* (*jhānaṅgāni paccavekkhitvā*), for one who has fallen into the life-continuum (*bhavaṅgaṃ otiṇṇassa*), *parinirvāṇa* in that very place is called immediately after reviewing (*paccavekkhaṇāsamanantaraṃ*).

These two are just immediate successions.

However, the Bhagavān, having entered *jhāna* (*jhānaṃ samāpajjitvā*), having arisen from *jhāna*, having reviewed the factors of *jhāna* (*jhānaṅgāni paccavekkhitvā*), attained *parinirvāṇa* with the life-continuum mind (*bhavaṅgacittena*), unpronounced, with the truth of suffering (*dukkhasaccena*).

Indeed, any Buddhas, solitary Buddhas, or noble disciples, even taking a small ant as the limit, all die with the life-continuum mind (*bhavaṅgacitteneva*), unpronounced, with the truth of suffering (*dukkhasaccena*).

Great earthquakes, etc., are just in accordance with what has been said.

Having arisen from the fourth *jhāna*, immediately, the Bhagavān attained *parinirvāṇa*. Immediately after *jhāna*. Immediately after reviewing. Great earthquakes, etc.
220
<p n="220" rend="bodytext"><hi rend="paranum">220</hi><hi rend="dot">.</hi> Parinibbute bhagavati saha parinibbānā mahābhūmicālo ahosi bhiṃsanako salomahaṃso. Devadundubhiyo ca phaliṃsu. Parinibbute <pb ed="P" n="2.0157"/> bhagavati saha parinibbānā brahmāsahampati imaṃ gāthaṃ abhāsi –</p> <p rend="gatha1">‘‘Sabbeva <pb ed="M" n="2.0129"/> nikkhipissanti, bhūtā loke samussayaṃ;</p> <pb ed="M" n="2.0129"/> <p rend="gatha2">Yattha etādiso satthā, loke appaṭipuggalo;</p> <p rend="gathalast">Tathāgato balappatto, sambuddho parinibbuto’’ti.</p>
And when the Blessed One attained final emancipation (*parinibbāna*), simultaneously with the *parinibbāna*, there was a great earthquake (*mahābhūmicālo*), terrible (*bhiṃsanako*) and hair-raising (*salomahaṃso*).

And the divine drums (*devadundubhiyo*) resounded.

When the Blessed One attained final emancipation (*parinibbāna*), simultaneously with the *parinibbāna*, Brahmā Sahampati uttered this verse:

"All beings will lay down their aggregate in the world;

Where the teacher is such, an unparalleled individual in the world;

The *Tathāgata* who has attained strength, the fully awakened one (*sambuddha*), has attained final emancipation (*parinibbuto*)."
<p n="220" rend="bodytext"><hi rend="paranum">220</hi><hi rend="dot">.</hi><hi rend="bold">Bhūtā</hi>ti sattā. <hi rend="bold">Appaṭipuggalo</hi>ti paṭibhāgapuggalavirahito. <hi rend="bold">Balappatto</hi>ti dasavidhañāṇabalaṃ patto.</p>
[p. 220]
*bhūtā*ti sattā: *Bhuta* means beings (*sattvāḥ*).
*appaṭipuggalo*ti paṭibhāgapuggalavirahito: *Appaṭipuggalo* means one who is without a counterpart (*paṭibhāga-puggala-virahitaḥ*).
*balappatto*ti dasavidhañāṇabalaṃ patto: *Balappatto* means one who has attained the power of ten kinds of knowledge (*daśavidha-jñāna-balam* *prāptaḥ*).
221
<p n="221" rend="bodytext"><hi rend="paranum">221</hi><hi rend="dot">.</hi> Parinibbute bhagavati saha parinibbānā sakko devānamindo imaṃ gāthaṃ abhāsi –</p> <p rend="gatha1">‘‘Aniccā vata saṅkhārā, uppādavayadhammino;</p> <p rend="gathalast">Uppajjitvā nirujjhanti, tesaṃ vūpasamo sukho’’ti.</p>
[API Error: 502]
<p n="221" rend="bodytext"><hi rend="paranum">221</hi><hi rend="dot">.</hi><hi rend="bold">Uppādavayadhammino</hi>ti <pb ed="M" n="2.0187"/> uppādavayasabhāvā. <hi rend="bold">Tesaṃ vūpasamo</hi>ti tesaṃ saṅkhārānaṃ vūpasamo, asaṅkhataṃ nibbānameva sukhanti attho.</p>
"uppādavayadhammino" means those things that have the nature of arising and decaying (utpāda-vyaya-svabhāvā).

"tesaṃ vūpasamo" means the subsiding of those conditioned phenomena (saṃskārāṇām), unconditioned nirvāṇa (asaṃkhataṃ nirvāṇam) itself is happiness, is the meaning (artha).
222
<p n="222" rend="bodytext"><hi rend="paranum">222</hi><hi rend="dot">.</hi> Parinibbute bhagavati saha parinibbānā āyasmā anuruddho imā gāthāyo abhāsi –</p> <p rend="gatha1">‘‘Nāhu <pb ed="T" n="2.0182"/><pb ed="V" n="2.0118"/> assāsapassāso, ṭhitacittassa tādino;</p> <pb ed="T" n="2.0182"/> <pb ed="V" n="2.0118"/> <p rend="gathalast">Anejo santimārabbha, yaṃ kālamakarī muni.</p> <p rend="gatha1">‘‘Asallīnena cittena, vedanaṃ ajjhavāsayi;</p> <p rend="gathalast">Pajjotasseva nibbānaṃ, vimokkho cetaso ahū’’ti.</p>
222. Immediately after the Blessed One (bhagavati) had attained complete extinction (parinibbute), the Venerable Āniruddha (āyasmā anuruddho) uttered these verses (imā gāthāyo abhāsi):

"There was no in-and-out breathing for him, the steadfast one, whose heart was firm (ṭhitacittassa tādino);

The sage (muni), free from craving (anejo), has passed away to peace (santimārabbha), he who made an end of time (yam kālamakarī).

With an unattached (asallīnena) mind, he endured feeling (vedanaṃ ajjhavāsayi);

Like the extinguishing of a lamp (pajjotasseva nibbānaṃ), was the liberation (vimokkho) of his mind (cetaso ahū’ti)."
<p n="222" rend="bodytext"><hi rend="paranum">222</hi><hi rend="dot">.</hi><hi rend="bold">Nāhu assāsapassāso</hi>ti na jāto assāsapassāso. <hi rend="bold">Anejo</hi>ti taṇhāsaṅkhātāya ejāya abhāvena anejo. <hi rend="bold">Santimārabbhā</hi>ti anupādisesaṃ nibbānaṃ ārabbha paṭicca sandhāya. <hi rend="bold">Yaṃ kālamakarī</hi>ti yo kālaṃ akari. Idaṃ vuttaṃ hoti – ‘‘āvuso, yo mama satthā buddhamuni santiṃ gamissāmīti, santiṃ ārabbha kālamakari, tassa ṭhitacittassa tādino idāni assāsapassāso na jāto, natthi, nappavattatī’’ti.</p> <p rend="bodytext"><hi rend="bold">Asallīnenā</hi>ti alīnena asaṅkuṭitena suvikasiteneva cittena. <hi rend="bold">Vedanaṃ ajjhavāsayī</hi>ti vedanaṃ adhivāsesi, na vedanānuvattī hutvā ito cito ca samparivatti. <hi rend="bold">Vimokkho</hi>ti kenaci dhammena anāvaraṇavimokkho sabbaso apaññattibhāvūpagamo pajjotanibbānasadiso jāto.</p> <hi rend="bold">Asallīnenā</hi> <hi rend="bold">Vedanaṃ ajjhavāsayī</hi> <hi rend="bold">Vimokkho</hi>
222.
"There was no in-breath and out-breath" means there was no arising of in-breath and out-breath.
"Without craving" means without craving, due to the absence of craving as a designation of craving.
"Relying on peace" means relying on peace, having approached extinction, conditioned and connected.
"When he made time" means when he did time.
This was said: "Friend, my teacher, the Buddha, the sage, thinking 'I will go to peace,' relying on peace, made time; for him, whose mind was steadfast, of such a nature, now there is no arising of in-breath and out-breath, it is not, it does not occur."

"Without clinging" means with a mind that is unattached, uncontracted, very fully developed.
"He dwelt in feeling" means he endured feeling; not becoming one who follows feeling, going here and there.
"Release" means by some *dharma*, release without obstruction, the attainment of a state of complete non-conceptualization, is like the extinction of a lamp.

Without clinging, he dwelt in feeling, release.
223
<p n="223" rend="bodytext"><hi rend="paranum">223</hi><hi rend="dot">.</hi> Parinibbute bhagavati saha parinibbānā āyasmā ānando imaṃ gāthaṃ abhāsi –</p> <p rend="gatha1">‘‘Tadāsi yaṃ bhiṃsanakaṃ, tadāsi lomahaṃsanaṃ;</p> <p rend="gathalast">Sabbākāravarūpete, sambuddhe parinibbute’’ti.</p>
When the Blessed One (bhagavati) had attained complete extinction (parinibbute), at the complete extinction (parinibbānā), venerable (āyasmā) Ānanda (ānando) uttered this verse (imaṃ gāthaṃ abhāsi):

"Then (tadā) it was frightening (yaṃ bhiṃsanakaṃ), then (tadā) it was hair-raising (lomahaṃsanaṃ);
With all the best qualities, at the extinction (parinibbute) of the Fully Awakened One (sambuddhe)," thus (iti).
<p n="223" rend="bodytext"><hi rend="paranum">223</hi><hi rend="dot">.</hi><hi rend="bold">Tadāsī</hi>ti <pb ed="V" n="2.0168"/> ‘‘saha parinibbānā mahābhūmicālo’’ti evaṃ heṭṭhā vuttaṃ bhūmicālameva sandhāyāha. Tañhi lomahaṃsanañca bhiṃsanakañca āsi. <hi rend="bold">Sabbākāravarūpete</hi>ti sabbavarakāraṇūpete.</p>
223. "tadāsī" [iti] (thus).
‘‘saha parinibbānā mahābhūmicālo’’ti: "Together with complete extinction, a great earthquake," thus, concerning the earthquake mentioned below, [it] is said.
tañhi lomahaṃsanañca bhiṃsanakañca āsi: That was hair-raising and terrifying.
"sabbākāravarūpete" [iti] (thus) sabbavarakāraṇūpete: Endowed with all excellent forms, endowed with all excellent causes.
224
<p n="224" rend="bodytext"><hi rend="paranum">224</hi><hi rend="dot">.</hi> Parinibbute bhagavati ye te tattha bhikkhū avītarāgā appekacce bāhā paggayha kandanti, chinnapātaṃ papatanti, āvaṭṭanti vivaṭṭanti, ‘‘atikhippaṃ bhagavā parinibbuto <pb ed="P" n="2.0158"/>, atikhippaṃ sugato parinibbuto, atikhippaṃ cakkhuṃ loke antarahito’’ti. Ye pana te bhikkhū vītarāgā, te satā sampajānā adhivāsenti – ‘‘aniccā saṅkhārā, taṃ kutettha labbhā’’ti.</p>
When the Blessed One had attained *parinirvāṇa*, some monks there who were not yet free from passion wept, raising their arms. Some flung themselves down as if their feet were cut off, rolling back and forth, crying, "All too soon has the Blessed One attained *parinirvāṇa*! All too soon has the Well-Gone One attained *parinirvāṇa*! All too soon has the Eye disappeared from the world!"

But those monks who were free from passion endured, mindful and fully aware, reflecting, "Impermanent are compounded things (*saṅkhārā*); what else is to be expected?"
<p n="224" rend="bodytext"><hi rend="paranum">224</hi><hi rend="dot">.</hi><hi rend="bold">Avītarāgā</hi>ti puthujjanā ceva sotāpannasakadāgāmino ca. Tesañhi domanassaṃ appahīnaṃ. Tasmā tepi bāhā paggayha kandanti. Ubhopi hatthe sīse ṭhapetvā rodantīti sabbaṃ purimanayeneva veditabbaṃ.</p>
<p n="224" rend="bodytext"><hi rend="paranum">224</hi><hi rend="dot">.
</hi><hi rend="bold">avītarāgā</hi>ti, ordinary people, stream-enterers (sotāpanna), and once-returners (sakadāgāmino) as well.
For their sorrow (domanassaṃ) is not abandoned (appahīnaṃ).
Therefore (tasmā), they too (tepi), raising their arms (bāhā paggayha), weep (kandanti).
Both (ubhopi), placing their hands (hatthe) on their heads (sīse ṭhapetvā), weep (rodantīti). All (sabbaṃ) this is to be understood (veditabbaṃ) in the same way as before (purimanayeneva).
</p>
225
<p n="225" rend="bodytext"><hi rend="paranum">225</hi><hi rend="dot">.</hi> Atha kho āyasmā anuruddho bhikkhū āmantesi – ‘‘alaṃ, āvuso, mā socittha mā paridevittha. Nanu etaṃ, āvuso, bhagavatā paṭikacceva akkhātaṃ – ‘sabbeheva piyehi manāpehi nānābhāvo vinābhāvo aññathābhāvo’. Taṃ kutettha, āvuso, labbhā. ‘Yaṃ taṃ jātaṃ bhūtaṃ saṅkhataṃ palokadhammaṃ, taṃ vata mā palujjī’ti, netaṃ ṭhānaṃ <pb ed="T" n="2.0183"/> vijjati <pb ed="M" n="2.0130"/>. Devatā, āvuso, ujjhāyantī’’ti. ‘‘Kathaṃbhūtā pana, bhante, āyasmā anuruddho devatā manasi karotī’’ti <note>bhante anuruddha devatā manasi karontīti (syā. ka.)</note>?</p> <p rend="bodytext">‘‘Santāvuso ānanda, devatā ākāse pathavīsaññiniyo kese pakiriya kandanti, bāhā paggayha kandanti, chinnapātaṃ papatanti, āvaṭṭanti, vivaṭṭanti – ‘atikhippaṃ bhagavā parinibbuto, atikhippaṃ sugato parinibbuto, atikhippaṃ cakkhuṃ loke antarahito’ti. Santāvuso ānanda, devatā pathaviyā pathavīsaññiniyo kese pakiriya kandanti, bāhā paggayha kandanti, chinnapātaṃ papatanti, āvaṭṭanti, vivaṭṭanti – ‘atikhippaṃ bhagavā parinibbuto <pb ed="V" n="2.0119"/>, atikhippaṃ sugato parinibbuto, atikhippaṃ cakkhuṃ loke antarahito’ti. Yā pana tā devatā vītarāgā, tā satā sampajānā adhivāsenti – ‘aniccā saṅkhārā, taṃ kutettha labbhā’ti. Atha kho āyasmā ca anuruddho āyasmā ca ānando taṃ rattāvasesaṃ dhammiyā kathāya vītināmesuṃ.</p> <pb ed="V" n="2.0119"/>
225. Then the Venerable Anuruddha addressed the monks, saying: “Enough, friends! Do not grieve, do not lament!

Has not the Blessed One already declared that with all that is dear and beloved there must be change, separation, and severance? (sabbeheva piyehi manāpehi nānābhāvo vinābhāvo aññathābhāvo).
What else is there to expect, friends?

Of that which is born, come into being, compounded and subject to decay, how can one say: ‘May it not come to dissolution!’? There can be no such state of things.

The deities, friends, are complaining."

“But, venerable sir, of what kind are the deities of whom the Venerable Anuruddha is mindful?”

"Friend Ānanda, there are devatās who perceive space to be earth. Tearing at their hair, they are weeping. Uplifting their arms, they are weeping. As if their feet were cut out from under them, they fall down and roll back & forth, crying, ‘All too soon has the Blessed One totally unbound! All too soon has the One Well-Gone totally unbound! All too soon, has the One with Eyes disappeared from the world!’

Friend Ānanda, there are devatās who perceive earth to be earth. Tearing at their hair, they are weeping. Uplifting their arms, they are weeping. As if their feet were cut out from under them, they fall down and roll back & forth, crying, ‘All too soon has the Blessed One totally unbound! All too soon has the One Well-Gone totally unbound! All too soon, has the One with Eyes disappeared from the world!’

But those devatās who are free from passion acquiesce, mindful & alert: ‘Inconstant are compounded things. What else is there to expect?’” (aniccā saṅkhārā).

Then Ven. Anuruddha & Ven. Ānanda spent the remainder of the night in Dhamma talk.
<p n="225" rend="bodytext"><hi rend="paranum">225</hi><hi rend="dot">.</hi><hi rend="bold">Ujjhāyantī</hi>ti ‘‘ayyā attanāpi adhivāsetuṃ na sakkonti, sesajanaṃ kathaṃ samassāsessantī’’ti vadantiyo ujjhāyanti. <hi rend="bold">Kathaṃbhūtā pana bhante āyasmā anuruddho devatā manasikarotī</hi>ti devatā, bhante, kathaṃbhūtā āyasmā anuruddho sallakkheti, kiṃ tā satthu parinibbānaṃ adhivāsentīti?</p> <p rend="bodytext">Atha tāsaṃ pavattidassanatthaṃ thero <hi rend="bold">santāvuso</hi>tiādimāha. Taṃ vuttatthameva. <hi rend="bold">Rattāvasesa</hi>nti <pb ed="P" n="2.0596"/> balavapaccūse parinibbutattā rattiyā avasesaṃ <pb ed="M" n="2.0188"/> cullakaddhānaṃ. <hi rend="bold">Dhammiyā kathāyā</hi>ti aññā pāṭiyekkā dhammakathā nāma natthi, ‘‘āvuso sadevake nāma loke appaṭipuggalassa satthuno ayaṃ maccurājā na lajjati, kimaṅgaṃ pana lokiyamahājanassa lajjissatī’’ti evarūpāya pana maraṇapaṭisaṃyuttāya kathāya vītināmesuṃ. Tesañhi taṃ kathaṃ kathentānaṃ muhutteneva aruṇaṃ uggacchi.</p> <hi rend="bold">santāvuso</hi> <hi rend="bold">Rattāvasesa</hi> <pb ed="P" n="2.0596"/> <pb ed="M" n="2.0188"/> <hi rend="bold">Dhammiyā kathāyā</hi>
[API Error: 502]
226
<p n="226" rend="bodytext"><hi rend="paranum">226</hi><hi rend="dot">.</hi> Atha kho āyasmā anuruddho āyasmantaṃ ānandaṃ āmantesi – ‘‘gacchāvuso ānanda, kusināraṃ pavisitvā kosinārakānaṃ mallānaṃ ārocehi – ‘parinibbuto, vāseṭṭhā, bhagavā, yassadāni kālaṃ maññathā’’’ti. ‘‘Evaṃ, bhante’’ti kho āyasmā ānando āyasmato anuruddhassa paṭissutvā pubbaṇhasamayaṃ nivāsetvā pattacīvaramādāya attadutiyo kusināraṃ pāvisi. Tena <pb ed="P" n="2.0159"/> kho pana samayena kosinārakā mallā sandhāgāre sannipatitā honti teneva karaṇīyena. Atha kho āyasmā ānando yena kosinārakānaṃ mallānaṃ sandhāgāraṃ tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā <pb ed="T" n="2.0184"/> kosinārakānaṃ mallānaṃ ārocesi – ‘parinibbuto, vāseṭṭhā, bhagavā, yassadāni kālaṃ maññathā’ti. Idamāyasmato ānandassa vacanaṃ sutvā mallā ca mallaputtā ca mallasuṇisā ca mallapajāpatiyo ca aghāvino dummanā cetodukkhasamappitā appekacce kese pakiriya kandanti, bāhā paggayha kandanti, chinnapātaṃ papatanti, āvaṭṭanti, vivaṭṭanti – ‘‘atikhippaṃ bhagavā parinibbuto, atikhippaṃ sugato parinibbuto, atikhippaṃ cakkhuṃ loke antarahito’’ti.</p> <p rend="subhead">Buddhasarīrapūjā</p>
Then the Venerable Anuruddha spoke to the Venerable Ānanda, saying: “Go now, friend Ānanda, to Kusinārā, and announce to the Mallas of Kusinārā: ‘The Blessed One, Vāsiṣṭhas, has attained *parinirvāṇa*. Now is the time for you to do as you think fit.’”

“So be it, venerable sir.” And the Venerable Ānanda, having assented to the Venerable Anuruddha, prepared himself in the forenoon, and taking bowl and robe, went with a companion into Kusinārā.

Now at that time the Mallas of Kusinārā had gathered in the council hall for some public business.

Then the Venerable Ānanda went to the council hall of the Mallas of Kusinārā; on arrival he announced to the Mallas of Kusinārā: “The Blessed One, Vāsiṣṭhas, has attained *parinirvāṇa*. Now is the time for you to do as you think fit.”

And when they heard the Venerable Ānanda’s words, the Mallas, their sons, their daughters-in-law and their wives were struck with anguish and sorrow, their minds were overcome with grief so that some were tearing their hair and weeping, some were raising their arms and weeping, some were falling to the ground as if cut off at the feet, and rolling around, crying, "All too soon has the Blessed One attained *parinirvāṇa*! All too soon has the Well-Gone One attained *parinirvāṇa*! All too soon has the Eye disappeared from the world!"

The Buddha's bodily veneration.
<p n="226" rend="bodytext"><hi rend="paranum">226</hi><hi rend="dot">.</hi><hi rend="bold">Atha kho</hi>ti aruṇuggaṃ disvāva thero theraṃ etadavoca. <hi rend="bold">Teneva karaṇīyenā</hi>ti kīdisena nu kho parinibbānaṭṭhāne mālāgandhādisakkārena bhavitabbaṃ, kīdisena bhikkhusaṅghassa nisajjaṭṭhānena bhavitabbaṃ, kīdisena khādanīyabhojanīyena bhavitabbanti, evaṃ yaṃ bhagavato parinibbutabhāvaṃ sutvā kattabbaṃ teneva karaṇīyena.</p> <p rend="subhead">Buddhasarīrapūjāvaṇṇanā</p>
226. Then, having seen the sunrise, the elder spoke thus to the elder.

"In that very way, what kind of offering of garlands, scents, and so forth should be made at the place of complete nirvāṇa? What kind of seating arrangement should be made for the community of monks? What kind of food and edibles should be offered?" Thus, whatever should be done upon hearing of the Blessed One's having attained complete nirvāṇa, should be done in that very way.

Buddha's body-worship description.
227
<p n="227" rend="bodytext"><hi rend="paranum">227</hi><hi rend="dot">.</hi> Atha <pb ed="M" n="2.0131"/> kho kosinārakā mallā purise āṇāpesuṃ – ‘‘tena hi, bhaṇe, kusinārāyaṃ gandhamālañca sabbañca tāḷāvacaraṃ sannipātethā’’ti. Atha kho kosinārakā mallā gandhamālañca sabbañca tāḷāvacaraṃ pañca ca dussayugasatāni ādāya yena upavattanaṃ mallānaṃ sālavanaṃ, yena bhagavato sarīraṃ tenupasaṅkamiṃsu; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavato sarīraṃ naccehi gītehi vāditehi mālehi gandhehi sakkarontā garuṃ karontā mānentā pūjentā celavitānāni karontā maṇḍalamāḷe paṭiyādentā ekadivasaṃ vītināmesuṃ.</p> <p rend="bodytext">Atha kho kosinārakānaṃ mallānaṃ etadahosi – ‘‘ativikālo kho ajja bhagavato sarīraṃ jhāpetuṃ, sve dāni mayaṃ bhagavato sarīraṃ jhāpessāmā’’ti. Atha kho kosinārakā mallā bhagavato sarīraṃ naccehi gītehi vāditehi mālehi gandhehi sakkarontā garuṃ karontā mānentā <pb ed="V" n="2.0120"/> pūjentā celavitānāni karontā maṇḍalamāḷe paṭiyādentā dutiyampi divasaṃ vītināmesuṃ, tatiyampi <pb ed="T" n="2.0185"/> divasaṃ vītināmesuṃ, catutthampi divasaṃ vītināmesuṃ, pañcamampi divasaṃ vītināmesuṃ, chaṭṭhampi divasaṃ vītināmesuṃ.</p> <pb ed="V" n="2.0120"/> <pb ed="T" n="2.0185"/> <p rend="bodytext">Atha kho sattamaṃ divasaṃ kosinārakānaṃ mallānaṃ <pb ed="P" n="2.0160"/> etadahosi – ‘‘mayaṃ bhagavato sarīraṃ naccehi gītehi vāditehi mālehi gandhehi sakkarontā garuṃ karontā mānentā pūjentā dakkhiṇena dakkhiṇaṃ nagarassa haritvā bāhirena bāhiraṃ dakkhiṇato nagarassa bhagavato sarīraṃ jhāpessāmā’’ti.</p> <pb ed="P" n="2.0160"/>
227. Then the Mallas of Kuśinagara ordered their men: “Go now, gather perfumes (gandha), garlands (mālā), and all musical instruments (tāḷāvacara) in Kuśinagara!”

Then the Mallas of Kuśinagara, taking perfumes, garlands, all musical instruments, and five hundred pairs of cloths, went to Upavattana, the Sala Grove of the Mallas, where the Blessed One's body was. Approaching the Blessed One’s body, they honored, respected, esteemed, and venerated it with dances (nacca), songs (gīta), instrumental music (vādita), garlands (mālā), and perfumes (gandha), setting up cloth canopies (celavitāna) and arranging circular wreaths (maṇḍalamāḷa), and spent the day.

Then the Mallas of Kuśinagara had this thought: “It is too late today to cremate the Blessed One’s body; we will cremate the Blessed One’s body tomorrow.”

Then the Mallas of Kuśinagara, honoring, respecting, and venerating the Blessed One's body with dances, songs, instrumental music, garlands, and perfumes, setting up cloth canopies and arranging circular wreaths, spent the second day, the third day, the fourth day, the fifth day, and the sixth day.

Then, on the seventh day, the Mallas of Kuśinagara had this thought: "We will carry the Blessed One's body with dances, songs, instrumental music, garlands, and perfumes, honoring, respecting, esteeming, and venerating it, to the south, around the outside of the city (nagara), and cremate the Blessed One's body south of the city."
<p n="227" rend="bodytext"><hi rend="paranum">227</hi><hi rend="dot">.</hi><hi rend="bold">Sabbañca tāḷāvacara</hi>nti sabbaṃ tūriyabhaṇḍaṃ. <hi rend="bold">Sannipātethā</hi>ti bheriṃ carāpetvā samāharatha. Te tatheva akaṃsu. <hi rend="bold">Maṇḍalamāḷe</hi>ti dussamaṇḍalamāḷe. <hi rend="bold">Paṭiyādentā</hi>ti sajjentā.</p> <p rend="bodytext"><hi rend="bold">Dakkhiṇena dakkhiṇa</hi>nti nagarassa dakkhiṇadisābhāgeneva dakkhiṇadisābhāgaṃ. <hi rend="bold">Bāhirena bāhira</hi>nti <pb ed="V" n="2.0169"/> antonagaraṃ appavesetvā bāhireneva nagarassa bāhirapassaṃ haritvā. <hi rend="bold">Dakkhiṇato nagarassā</hi>ti anurādhapurassa dakkhiṇadvārasadise ṭhāne ṭhapetvā sakkārasammānaṃ katvā jetavanasadise ṭhāne jhāpessāmāti attho.</p> <hi rend="bold">Dakkhiṇena dakkhiṇa</hi> <hi rend="bold">Bāhirena bāhira</hi> <pb ed="V" n="2.0169"/> <hi rend="bold">Dakkhiṇato nagarassā</hi>
227.
" *Sabbañca tāḷāvacara* " means all musical instruments.
" *Sannipātethā* " means having caused a drum to be paraded, gather together.
They did just that.
" *Maṇḍalamāḷe* " means cloth maṇḍala-s.
" *Paṭiyādentā* " means equipping.

" *Dakkhiṇena dakkhiṇa* " means the southern part of the city just like the southern direction part.
" *Bāhirena bāhira* " not leading into the inner city, but having removed the outer part outside the city.
" *Dakkhiṇato nagarassā* " means having placed [it] in a place similar to the southern gate of Anurādhapura, and having performed honor and respect, [we] will cremate [him] in a place similar to Jetavana, is the meaning.

*Dakkhiṇena dakkhiṇa bāhirena bāhira dakkhiṇato nagarassā*
228
<p n="228" rend="bodytext"><hi rend="paranum">228</hi><hi rend="dot">.</hi> Tena kho pana samayena aṭṭha mallapāmokkhā sīsaṃnhātā ahatāni vatthāni nivatthā ‘‘mayaṃ bhagavato sarīraṃ uccāressāmā’’ti na sakkonti uccāretuṃ. Atha kho kosinārakā mallā āyasmantaṃ anuruddhaṃ etadavocuṃ – ‘‘ko nu kho, bhante anuruddha, hetu ko paccayo, yenime aṭṭha mallapāmokkhā sīsaṃnhātā ahatāni vatthāni nivatthā ‘mayaṃ bhagavato sarīraṃ uccāressāmā’ti na sakkonti uccāretu’’nti? ‘‘Aññathā kho, vāseṭṭhā, tumhākaṃ adhippāyo, aññathā devatānaṃ adhippāyo’’ti. ‘‘Kathaṃ pana, bhante, devatānaṃ adhippāyo’’ti? ‘‘Tumhākaṃ kho, vāseṭṭhā, adhippāyo – ‘mayaṃ bhagavato sarīraṃ naccehi gītehi vāditehi mālehi gandhehi <pb ed="M" n="2.0132"/> sakkarontā garuṃ karontā mānentā pūjentā dakkhiṇena dakkhiṇaṃ nagarassa haritvā bāhirena bāhiraṃ dakkhiṇato nagarassa bhagavato sarīraṃ jhāpessāmā’ti; devatānaṃ kho, vāseṭṭhā, adhippāyo – ‘mayaṃ bhagavato sarīraṃ dibbehi naccehi <pb ed="T" n="2.0186"/> gītehi vāditehi gandhehi sakkarontā garuṃ karontā mānentā pūjentā uttarena uttaraṃ nagarassa haritvā uttarena dvārena nagaraṃ pavesetvā majjhena majjhaṃ nagarassa haritvā puratthimena dvārena nikkhamitvā puratthimato nagarassa makuṭabandhanaṃ nāma mallānaṃ cetiyaṃ ettha bhagavato sarīraṃ jhāpessāmā’ti. ‘‘Yathā, bhante, devatānaṃ adhippāyo, tathā hotū’’ti.</p>
Then, at that time, eight Malla chiefs, having bathed their heads and wearing new clothes, tried to lift up the Blessed One's body, thinking, "We will lift up the Blessed One’s body," but they were not able to lift it.

Then the Mallas of Kusinārā said this to the venerable Anuruddha: “What is the reason, venerable Anuruddha, what is the cause, why these eight leading Mallas, having bathed their heads and wearing new clothes, thinking, ‘We will lift up the Blessed One’s body,’ are unable to lift it?” “Vāseṭṭhas, your intention is one thing, and the deities’ intention is another.”

“Then what, venerable sir, is the deities’ intention?” “Vāseṭṭhas, your intention is: ‘We will honor, respect, esteem, and venerate the Blessed One’s body with dance, song, music, garlands, and scents, carry it southward to the southern part of the city, outside the city to the south, and cremate the Blessed One’s body there.’ But the deities’ intention, Vāseṭṭhas, is: ‘We will honor, respect, esteem, and venerate the Blessed One’s body with heavenly dance, song, music, and scents, carry it northward to the northern part of the city, bring it into the city through the northern gate, carry it through the middle of the city, exit through the eastern gate, and cremate the Blessed One’s body at the Mallas’ shrine called Makuṭabandhana to the east of the city.’”

“As the deities wish, venerable sir, so let it be.”
<p n="228" rend="bodytext"><hi rend="paranum">228</hi><hi rend="dot">.</hi><hi rend="bold">Aṭṭha mallapāmokkhā</hi>ti majjhimavayā thāmasampannā aṭṭhamallarājāno. <hi rend="bold">Sīsaṃ nhātā</hi>ti sīsaṃ dhovitvā nahātā. <hi rend="bold">Āyasmantaṃ anuruddha</hi>nti therova dibbacakkhukoti pākaṭo, tasmā te santesupi aññesu mahātheresu – ‘‘ayaṃ no pākaṭaṃ katvā kathessatī’’ti theraṃ pucchiṃsu. <hi rend="bold">Kathaṃ pana, bhante, devatānaṃ adhippāyo</hi>ti bhante, amhākaṃ tāva adhippāyaṃ jānāma. Devatānaṃ kathaṃ adhippāyoti pucchanti. Thero paṭhamaṃ tesaṃ adhippāyaṃ dassento <hi rend="bold">tumhākaṃ kho</hi>tiādimāha. <hi rend="bold">Makuṭabandhanaṃ nāma mallānaṃ cetiya</hi>nti mallarājūnaṃ pasādhanamaṅgalasālāya etaṃ nāmaṃ. Cittīkataṭṭhena panesā ‘‘cetiya’’nti vuccati.</p>
228.
"aṭṭha mallapāmokkhā" means eight wrestling champions, [who were] of middle age, endowed with strength, [and were] eight malla kings.
"sīsaṃ nhātā" means having washed the head, [and] having bathed.
"āyasmantaṃ anuruddha" means the venerable Anuruddha, who was known as a *thera* with divine eyes, therefore, even with other great *theras* present, they asked the *thera*, "This one will make it known to us and will speak."
"kathaṃ pana, bhante, devatānaṃ adhippāyo" means "But how, venerable sir, [is] the intention of the gods?" The monks said, "Venerable sir, we know our own intention."
They ask, "How is the intention of the gods?"
The *thera*, first showing their intention, said, "Your..." and so on.
"makuṭabandhanaṃ nāma mallānaṃ cetiyaṃ" means this name [is] the auspicious hall for the adornment of the malla kings' *cetiya*.
Because of the constructed meaning, it is called "cetiya".
229
<p n="229" rend="bodytext"><hi rend="paranum">229</hi><hi rend="dot">.</hi> Tena kho pana samayena kusinārā yāva sandhisamalasaṃkaṭīrā jaṇṇumattena odhinā mandāravapupphehi santhatā <note>saṇṭhitā (syā.)</note> hoti. Atha kho devatā ca kosinārakā ca mallā bhagavato sarīraṃ dibbehi ca mānusakehi ca naccehi <pb ed="P" n="2.0161"/> gītehi vāditehi mālehi gandhehi sakkarontā garuṃ karontā mānentā pūjentā uttarena uttaraṃ nagarassa haritvā uttarena dvārena nagaraṃ pavesetvā majjhena majjhaṃ nagarassa haritvā puratthimena dvārena nikkhamitvā puratthimato nagarassa makuṭabandhanaṃ nāma mallānaṃ cetiyaṃ ettha ca bhagavato sarīraṃ nikkhipiṃsu.</p>
229. At that time, Kusinārā, even to its rubbish heaps and cesspools ( *sandhisamalasaṃkaṭīrā* ), was covered knee-deep in coral-tree flowers ( *mandāravapupphehi santhatā* ).

Then, the deities ( *devatā* ) and the Mallas of Kusinārā, honoring, respecting, and venerating the Blessed One's ( *bhagavato* ) body ( *sarīraṃ* ) with divine and human dances ( *naccehi* ), songs ( *gītehi* ), music ( *vāditehi* ), garlands ( *mālehi* ), and scents ( *gandhehi* ), carried it to the north of the town ( *uttarena uttaraṃ nagarassa haritvā* ), entered the town through the north gate ( *uttarena dvārena nagaraṃ pavesetvā* ), carried it through the middle of the town ( *majjhena majjhaṃ nagarassa haritvā* ), and exited through the east gate ( *puratthimena dvārena nikkhamitvā* ) to the Mallas’ shrine called Makuṭabandhana to the east of the town ( *puratthimato nagarassa makuṭabandhanaṃ nāma mallānaṃ cetiyaṃ* ), and there they laid down the Blessed One's body ( *ettha ca bhagavato sarīraṃ nikkhipiṃsu* ).
<p n="229" rend="bodytext"><hi rend="paranum">229</hi><hi rend="dot">.</hi><hi rend="bold">Yāva</hi><pb ed="P" n="2.0597"/><pb ed="M" n="2.0189"/><hi rend="bold">sandhisamalasaṅkaṭīrā</hi>ti ettha <hi rend="bold">sandhi</hi> nāma gharasandhi. <hi rend="bold">Samalaṃ</hi> nāma gūtharāsiniddhamanapanāḷi. <hi rend="bold">Saṅkaṭīraṃ</hi> nāma saṅkāraṭṭhānaṃ. <hi rend="bold">Dibbehi ca mānusakehi ca naccehī</hi>ti upari devatānaṃ naccāni honti, heṭṭhā manussānaṃ. Esa nayo gītādīsu. Apica devatānaṃ antare manussā, manussānaṃ antare devatāti evampi sakkarontā pūjentā agamaṃsu. <hi rend="bold">Majjhena majjhaṃ nagarassa haritvā</hi>ti evaṃ hariyamāne bhagavato sarīre bandhulamallasenāpatibhariyā <hi rend="bold">mallikā</hi> nāma – ‘‘bhagavato sarīraṃ āharantī’’ti sutvā attano sāmikassa kālaṃ kiriyato paṭṭhāya aparibhuñjitvā ṭhapitaṃ visākhāya pasādhanasadisaṃ <hi rend="bold">mahālatāpasādhanaṃ</hi> nīharāpetvā – ‘‘iminā satthāraṃ pūjessāmī’’ti taṃ majjāpetvā gandhodakena dhovitvā dvāre ṭhitā.</p> <p rend="bodytext">Taṃ kira pasādhanaṃ tāsañca dvinnaṃ itthīnaṃ, devadāniyacorassa geheti tīsuyeva ṭhānesu ahosi. Sā ca satthu sarīre dvāraṃ sampatte – ‘‘otāretha, tātā, satthusarīra’’nti vatvā taṃ pasādhanaṃ satthusarīre paṭimuñci. Taṃ sīsato paṭṭhāya paṭimukkaṃ yāvapādatalāgataṃ. Suvaṇṇavaṇṇaṃ bhagavato sarīraṃ sattaratanamayena mahāpasādhanena pasādhitaṃ ativiya virocittha. Taṃ sā disvā pasannacittā patthanaṃ akāsi – ‘‘bhagavā yāva vaṭṭe saṃsarissāmi, tāva me pāṭiyekkaṃ pasādhanakiccaṃ mā hotu, niccaṃ paṭimukkapasādhanasadisameva sarīraṃ hotū’’ti.</p> <p rend="bodytext">Atha bhagavantaṃ sattaratanamayena mahāpasādhanena ukkhipitvā puratthimena dvārena nīharitvā puratthimena nagarassa makuṭabandhanaṃ mallānaṃ cetiyaṃ, ettha bhagavato sarīraṃ nikkhipiṃsu.</p> <p rend="subhead">Mahākassapattheravatthuvaṇṇanā</p>
229.
Yāva…
Sandhisamalasaṅkaṭīrā: Here, *sandhi* means house-sandhi.
*Samalaṃ* means gūtharāsiniddhamanapanāḷi.
*Saṅkaṭīraṃ* means saṅkāraṭṭhānaṃ.
*Dibbehi ca mānusakehi ca naccehī*: Above, the dances of the gods occur; below, those of humans.
This is the method in songs, and so forth (gītādīsu).
Moreover, among the gods are humans; among humans are gods; thus they honored and venerated and went.
*Majjhena majjhaṃ nagarassa haritvā*: Thus, as the Blessed One's body was being carried, Bandhulamallasenāpatibhariyā, named Mallikā, having heard, "They are bringing the Blessed One's body," from the time of her husband’s death, having not enjoyed it, having had the great *latāpasādhana*, similar to Visakha’s finery, which had been kept, brought out—"With this I will honor the Teacher"—having sprinkled it, having washed it with scented water, she stood at the door.

That finery, it is said, was in three places only: in the houses of those two women and the devadāniya thief.
And when she arrived at the door of the Teacher’s body, saying, "Lower it, fathers, the Teacher’s body," she fastened that finery on the Teacher’s body.
That, from the head onward, was covered, extending to the soles of the feet.
The golden-colored body of the Blessed One, adorned with the great finery made of seven jewels, shone exceedingly.
Having seen that, with a pleased mind, she made a request: "As long as I wander in the round (vaṭṭe saṃsarissāmi), may there not be occasional finery-work for me; may my body always be just like covered-with-finery finery."

Then, having lifted up the Blessed One with the great finery made of seven jewels, having carried him out by the eastern gate, they deposited the Blessed One’s body at the Makuṭabandhana Cetiya of the Mallas in the east of the city.

Narration of the Story of Mahākassapatthera
230
<p n="230" rend="bodytext"><hi rend="paranum">230</hi><hi rend="dot">.</hi> Atha <pb ed="V" n="2.0121"/> kho kosinārakā mallā āyasmantaṃ ānandaṃ etadavocuṃ – ‘‘kathaṃ mayaṃ, bhante ānanda, tathāgatassa sarīre paṭipajjāmā’’ti? ‘‘Yathā kho, vāseṭṭhā, rañño cakkavattissa sarīre paṭipajjanti, evaṃ tathāgatassa sarīre paṭipajjitabba’’nti. ‘‘Kathaṃ pana, bhante ānanda, rañño cakkavattissa sarīre paṭipajjantī’’ti? ‘‘Rañño, vāseṭṭhā, cakkavattissa sarīraṃ ahatena vatthena veṭhenti, ahatena vatthena veṭhetvā vihatena kappāsena veṭhenti, vihatena kappāsena <pb ed="T" n="2.0187"/> veṭhetvā ahatena vatthena veṭhenti. Etena upāyena pañcahi yugasatehi rañño cakkavattissa sarīraṃ veṭhetvā āyasāya teladoṇiyā pakkhipitvā aññissā āyasāya doṇiyā paṭikujjitvā sabbagandhānaṃ citakaṃ karitvā rañño cakkavattissa sarīraṃ jhāpenti. Cātumahāpathe rañño cakkavattissa thūpaṃ karonti <pb ed="M" n="2.0133"/>. Evaṃ kho, vāseṭṭhā, rañño cakkavattissa sarīre paṭipajjanti. Yathā kho, vāseṭṭhā, rañño cakkavattissa sarīre paṭipajjanti, evaṃ tathāgatassa sarīre paṭipajjitabbaṃ. Cātumahāpathe tathāgatassa thūpo kātabbo. Tattha ye mālaṃ vā gandhaṃ vā cuṇṇakaṃ vā āropessanti vā abhivādessanti vā cittaṃ vā pasādessanti, tesaṃ taṃ bhavissati dīgharattaṃ hitāya sukhāyā’’ti. Atha kho kosinārakā mallā purise āṇāpesuṃ – ‘‘tena hi, bhaṇe, mallānaṃ vihataṃ kappāsaṃ sannipātethā’’ti.</p> <p rend="bodytext">Atha kho kosinārakā mallā bhagavato sarīraṃ ahatena vatthena veṭhetvā vihatena kappāsena veṭhesuṃ, vihatena kappāsena veṭhetvā ahatena vatthena <pb ed="P" n="2.0162"/> veṭhesuṃ. Etena upāyena pañcahi yugasatehi bhagavato sarīraṃ veṭhetvā āyasāya teladoṇiyā pakkhipitvā aññissā āyasāya doṇiyā paṭikujjitvā sabbagandhānaṃ citakaṃ karitvā bhagavato sarīraṃ citakaṃ āropesuṃ.</p> <pb ed="P" n="2.0162"/> <p rend="subhead">Mahākassapattheravatthu</p>
230. Then the Mallas of Kusinārā said to Venerable Ānanda: “How should we treat the body of the Tathāgata, Venerable Ānanda?”

“Vāseṭṭhas, the body of the Tathāgata should be treated in the same way as the body of a wheel-turning monarch (cakravartin).”

“But how, Venerable Ānanda, is the body of a wheel-turning monarch treated?”

“Vāseṭṭhas, the body of a wheel-turning monarch is wrapped in new linen. Having wrapped it in new linen, they wrap it in teased cotton wool. Having wrapped it in teased cotton wool, they wrap it in new linen. In this way, they wrap the body of the wheel-turning monarch in five hundred layers of linen and cotton. Then they place it in an iron oil-vat, which is enclosed in another iron vat. They build a pyre of all kinds of perfumes and cremate the body of the wheel-turning monarch. They build a stupa (thūpaṃ karonti) for the wheel-turning monarch at a crossroads (cātumahāpathe). This is how, Vāseṭṭhas, the body of a wheel-turning monarch is treated. Vāseṭṭhas, the body of the Tathāgata should be treated in the same way. A stupa should be erected at the crossroads for the Tathāgata. And those who offer garlands, scents, or perfume powders there, or bow down there, or gladden their minds there: that will be for their long-term welfare and happiness.”

Then the Mallas of Kusinārā ordered their men: “In that case, gather the Mallas’ teased cotton wool!”

Then the Mallas of Kusinārā wrapped the Blessed One’s body in new linen and then in teased cotton wool. Having wrapped it in teased cotton wool, they wrapped it in new linen. In this way, having wrapped the Blessed One’s body in five hundred layers, they placed it in an iron oil-vat, covered it with another iron vat, made a pyre of all kinds of perfumes, and placed the Blessed One’s body on the pyre.

The Story of the Elder Mahākassapa
231
<p n="231" rend="bodytext"><hi rend="paranum">231</hi><hi rend="dot">.</hi> Tena kho pana samayena āyasmā mahākassapo pāvāya kusināraṃ addhānamaggappaṭippanno hoti mahatā bhikkhusaṅghena saddhiṃ pañcamattehi <pb ed="T" n="2.0188"/> bhikkhusatehi. Atha kho āyasmā mahākassapo maggā okkamma aññatarasmiṃ rukkhamūle nisīdi. Tena kho pana samayena aññataro ājīvako kusinārāya mandāravapupphaṃ gahetvā pāvaṃ addhānamaggappaṭippanno hoti. Addasā kho āyasmā mahākassapo taṃ ājīvakaṃ dūratova āgacchantaṃ, disvā taṃ ājīvakaṃ etadavoca – ‘‘apāvuso, amhākaṃ satthāraṃ jānāsī’’ti? ‘‘Āmāvuso, jānāmi, ajja sattāhaparinibbuto samaṇo gotamo. Tato me idaṃ mandāravapupphaṃ gahita’’nti. Tattha ye te <pb ed="V" n="2.0122"/> bhikkhū avītarāgā appekacce bāhā paggayha kandanti, chinnapātaṃ papatanti, āvaṭṭanti, vivaṭṭanti – ‘‘atikhippaṃ bhagavā parinibbuto, atikhippaṃ sugato parinibbuto, atikhippaṃ cakkhuṃ loke antarahito’’ti. Ye pana te bhikkhū vītarāgā, te satā sampajānā adhivāsenti – ‘‘aniccā saṅkhārā, taṃ kutettha labbhā’’ti.</p>
At that time the Venerable Mahākassapa was journeying from Pāvā to Kusinārā along the road, together with a large community of monks, about five hundred monks.

Then the Venerable Mahākassapa, leaving the road, sat down at the foot of a certain tree.

At that time a certain Ājīvaka ascetic, carrying a coral-tree flower (mandārava-puṣpa) from Kusinārā, was traveling on the road to Pāvā.

The Venerable Mahākassapa saw that Ājīvaka coming from afar, and having seen him, said to him: “Friend, do you know our teacher (śāstāraṃ)?”

“Yes, friend, I know. The renunciate (śramaṇa) Gotama has been completely passed away (parinirvṛta) for seven days now. That is why I picked this coral-tree flower.”

Thereupon, those monks there who were not free from craving (avītarāgā), some raised their arms and wept, they fell down as if their feet were cut off, rolled around, and writhed, crying: "Too soon has the Blessed One (bhagavān) attained complete extinction (parinirvṛta), too soon has the Well-Gone One (sugato) attained complete extinction, too soon has the Eye disappeared from the world!"

But those monks who were free from craving (vītarāgā), mindful and fully aware, endured, reflecting: "Impermanent (anitya) are conditioned things (saṃskārā); how could it be otherwise?"
<p n="231" rend="bodytext"><hi rend="paranum">231</hi><hi rend="dot">.</hi><hi rend="bold">Pāvāya</hi><pb ed="V" n="2.0170"/><hi rend="bold">kusināra</hi>nti pāvānagare piṇḍāya caritvā ‘‘kusināraṃ gamissāmī’’ti addhānamaggappaṭipanno hoti. <hi rend="bold">Rukkhamūle nisīdī</hi>ti ettha kasmā divāvihāranti na vuttaṃ? Divāvihāratthāya anisinnattā. Therassa hi parivārā bhikkhū sabbe sukhasaṃvaddhitā mahāpuññā. Te majjhanhikasamaye tattapāsāṇasadisāya bhūmiyā padasā gacchantā kilamiṃsu. Thero te disvā – ‘‘bhikkhū kilamanti, gantabbaṭṭhānañca na dūraṃ, thokaṃ vissamitvā darathaṃ paṭippassambhetvā sāyanhasamaye kusināraṃ gantvā dasabalaṃ passissāmī’’ti maggā <pb ed="M" n="2.0190"/> okkamma aññatarasmiṃ rukkhamūle <pb ed="P" n="2.0598"/> saṅghāṭiṃ paññapetvā udakatumbato udakena hatthapāde sītale katvā nisīdi. Parivārabhikkhūpissa rukkhamūle nisīditvā yoniso manasikāre kammaṃ kurumānā tiṇṇaṃ ratanānaṃ vaṇṇaṃ bhaṇamānā nisīdiṃsu. Iti darathavinodanatthāya nisinnattā ‘‘divāvihāra’’nti na vuttaṃ.</p> <p rend="bodytext"><hi rend="bold">Mandāravapupphaṃ gahetvā</hi>ti mahāpātippamāṇaṃ pupphaṃ āgantukadaṇḍake ṭhapetvā chattaṃ viya gahetvā. <hi rend="bold">Addasa kho</hi>ti āgacchantaṃ dūrato addasa. Disvā ca pana cintesi –</p> <hi rend="bold">Mandāravapupphaṃ gahetvā</hi> <hi rend="bold">Addasa kho</hi> <p rend="indent">‘‘Etaṃ ājīvakassa hatthe mandāravapupphaṃ paññāyati, etañca na sabbadā manussapathe paññāyati, yadā pana koci iddhimā iddhiṃ vikubbati, tadā sabbaññubodhisattassa ca mātukucchiokkamanādīsu hoti. Na kho pana ajja kenaci iddhivikubbanaṃ kataṃ, na me satthā mātukucchiṃ okkanto, na kucchito nikkhamanto, nāpissa ajja abhisambodhi, na dhammacakkappavattanaṃ, na yamakapāṭihāriyaṃ, na devorohaṇaṃ, na āyusaṅkhārossajjanaṃ. Mahallako pana me satthā dhuvaṃ parinibbuto bhavissatī’’ti.</p> <p rend="bodytext">Tato – ‘‘pucchāmi na’’nti cittaṃ uppādetvā – ‘‘sace kho pana nisinnakova pucchāmi, satthari agāravo kato bhavissatī’’ti uṭṭhahitvā ṭhitaṭṭhānato apakkamma chaddanto nāgarājā maṇicammaṃ viya dasabaladattiyaṃ meghavaṇṇaṃ paṃsukūlacīvaraṃ pārupitvā dasanakhasamodhānasamujjalaṃ añjaliṃ sirasmiṃ patiṭṭhapetvā satthari katena gāravena ājīvakassa abhimukho hutvā – ‘‘āvuso, amhākaṃ satthāraṃ jānāsī’’ti āha. Kiṃ pana satthu parinibbānaṃ jānanto pucchi ajānantoti? Āvajjanapaṭibaddhaṃ khīṇāsavānaṃ jānanaṃ, anāvajjitattā panesa ajānanto pucchīti <pb ed="V" n="2.0171"/> eke. Thero samāpattibahulo, rattiṭṭhānadivāṭṭhānaleṇamaṇḍapādīsu niccaṃ samāpattibaleneva yāpeti, kulasantakampi gāmaṃ pavisitvā dvāre samāpattiṃ samāpajjitvā samāpattito vuṭṭhitova bhikkhaṃ gaṇhāti. Thero kira iminā pacchimena attabhāvena mahājanānuggahaṃ karissāmi – ‘‘ye mayhaṃ bhikkhaṃ vā denti gandhamālādīhi vā sakkāraṃ karonti, tesaṃ taṃ mahapphalaṃ hotū’’ti evaṃ <pb ed="M" n="2.0191"/> karoti. Tasmā samāpattibahulatāya na jānāti. Iti ajānantova pucchatīti vadanti, taṃ <pb ed="P" n="2.0599"/> na gahetabbaṃ.</p> <pb ed="V" n="2.0171"/> <pb ed="M" n="2.0191"/> <pb ed="P" n="2.0599"/> <p rend="bodytext">Na hettha ajānanakāraṇaṃ atthi. Abhilakkhitaṃ satthu parinibbānaṃ ahosi, dasasahassilokadhātukampanādīhi nimittehi. Therassa pana parisāya kehici bhikkhūhi bhagavā diṭṭhapubbo, kehici na diṭṭhapubbo, tattha yehipi diṭṭhapubbo, tepi passitukāmāva, yehipi adiṭṭhapubbo, tepi passitukāmāva. Tattha yehi na diṭṭhapubbo, te atidassanakāmatāya gantvā ‘‘kuhiṃ bhagavā’’ti pucchantā ‘‘parinibbuto’’ti sutvā sandhāretuṃ nāsakkhissanti. Cīvarañca pattañca chaḍḍetvā ekavatthā vā dunnivatthā vā duppārutā vā urāni paṭipisantā parodissanti. Tattha manussā – ‘‘mahākassapattherena saddhiṃ āgatā paṃsukūlikā sayampi itthiyo viya parodanti, te kiṃ amhe samassāsessantī’’ti mayhaṃ dosaṃ dassanti. Idaṃ pana suññaṃ mahāaraññaṃ, idha yathā tathā rodantesu doso natthi. Purimataraṃ sutvā nāma sokopi tanuko hotīti bhikkhūnaṃ satuppādanatthāya jānantova pucchi.</p> <p rend="bodytext"><hi rend="bold">Ajja sattāhaparinibbuto samaṇo gotamo</hi>ti ajja samaṇo gotamo sattāhaparinibbuto. <hi rend="bold">Tato me ida</hi>nti tato samaṇassa gotamassa parinibbutaṭṭhānato.</p> <hi rend="bold">Ajja sattāhaparinibbuto samaṇo gotamo</hi> <hi rend="bold">Tato me ida</hi>
231. *Pāvāya* *Kusināra*: Having wandered for alms in Pāvā city, he was one who had set out on the road to Kusināra, thinking, "I will go to Kusināra."

*Rukkhamūle nisīdī*: Here, why was it not said "rest by day"? Because he did not sit down for the purpose of resting by day.

The monks who were the retinue of that elder were all nurtured in comfort and were of great merit.

They, going on foot at midday on ground similar to a heated stone, grew weary.

The elder, seeing them, [thought:] "The monks are weary, and the place to go is not far away; having rested a little, having calmed their distress, having gone to Kusināra in the evening, I will see the Ten-Powered One," he left the road at a certain tree root, spread out his Saṃghāṭī robe, and sat down, having made his hands and feet cool with water from a water pot.

The monks of his retinue also, having sat down at the root of the tree, sat down speaking the virtues of the Triple Gem, making the work [that consists in] appropriate attention.

Thus, because he sat down for the sake of allaying distress, it was not said "rest by day."

*Mandāravapupphaṃ gahetvā*: Taking a Mandārava flower, placing a flower of the size of a large bowl on a staff for new arrivals, taking it like an umbrella.

*Addasa kho*: He saw him coming from afar.

And having seen [him], he thought:

*Mandāravapupphaṃ gahetvā* *addasa kho*

"This Mandārava flower appears in the hand of an Ājīvaka; and this does not appear at all times on the path of men; when some powerful one works a miracle, then it is in the events beginning with the entry into the mother's womb of the All-Knowing Bodhisattva.

But today a miracle has not been worked by anyone, my teacher has not entered a mother's womb, nor is he emerging from [it], nor is today his complete awakening, nor the turning of the wheel of the Dharma, nor the twin miracle, nor the descent from the gods, nor the casting off of the life force.

My teacher is old; surely he will be completely extinguished."

Then – producing the thought "Shall I ask or not?" – [he thought:] "If, indeed, I ask while sitting, disrespect to the Teacher will have been done," having risen up, having gone away from the place where he was standing, Chaddanta the Nāga-king, covering himself with a patched-together robe the color of a cloud, like a jeweled skin, having placed his Anjali gesture, radiant with the joining of his ten fingernails, upon his head, having become face to face with the Ājīvaka with reverence done to the Teacher, he said, "Friend, do you know our Teacher?"

What? Knowing the complete extinction of the Teacher, did he ask, or not knowing? The knowing of those whose outflows are ended is bound to reflection; but because he did not reflect, he asked not knowing, some say.

The Elder is one who frequents meditative attainments; constantly he spends [his time] in places for night, places for day, cave shelters, pavilions, etc., only by the force of meditative attainment; having entered even a village that belongs to a family, having achieved meditative attainment at the door, having risen from meditative attainment, he takes alms.

The Elder, it seems, by this final existence of his, [thinks] "I will do a favor to the great multitude of people: 'May that be of great fruit to those who give me alms or do honor with incense, garlands, etc.,'" thus he acts.

Therefore, he does not know due to his abundance of meditative attainments.

Thus, they say, "He asks not knowing"; that is not to be accepted.

There is no cause for not knowing here.

The Teacher's complete extinction was marked, by signs such as the shaking of the ten-thousand world-spheres, etc.

In that Elder's assembly, the Blessed One had been seen previously by some monks, but not seen previously by others; among them, even those by whom he had been seen previously were desirous of seeing [him], and even those by whom he had not been seen previously were desirous of seeing [him].

Among them, those by whom he had not been seen previously, going in their extreme desire to see, asking "Where is the Blessed One?", hearing "He is completely extinguished," will not be able to bear it.

Having cast aside their robes and their bowls, wearing a single garment or badly clothed or poorly covered, striking their breasts, they will wail.

There, people [will say:] "These rag-robe wearers who have come together with the Elder Mahākassapa, even they themselves wail like women; how will they console us?" They will show fault in me.

But this is an empty great forest; here, even if they weep in any way, there is no fault.

Having heard beforehand, grief also becomes thin, he asked knowing, indeed, for the sake of the monks' production of mindfulness.

*Ajja sattāhaparinibbuto samaṇo gotamo*: Today, the ascetic Gotama is one who has been completely extinguished for a week.

*Tato me idaṃ*: From that, from the place of complete extinction of the ascetic Gotama.

*Ajja sattāhaparinibbuto samaṇo gotamo* *tato me idaṃ*
232
<p n="232" rend="bodytext"><hi rend="paranum">232</hi><hi rend="dot">.</hi> Tena kho pana samayena subhaddo nāma vuddhapabbajito tassaṃ parisāyaṃ nisinno hoti. Atha kho subhaddo vuddhapabbajito te <pb ed="M" n="2.0134"/> bhikkhū etadavoca – ‘‘alaṃ, āvuso, mā socittha, mā paridevittha, sumuttā mayaṃ tena mahāsamaṇena. Upaddutā ca homa – ‘idaṃ vo kappati, idaṃ vo na kappatī’ti. Idāni pana mayaṃ yaṃ icchissāma, taṃ karissāma, yaṃ na icchissāma, na taṃ karissāmā’’ti. Atha kho āyasmā mahākassapo <pb ed="T" n="2.0189"/> bhikkhū āmantesi – ‘‘alaṃ, āvuso, mā socittha, mā paridevittha. Nanu etaṃ <pb ed="P" n="2.0163"/>, āvuso, bhagavatā paṭikacceva akkhātaṃ – ‘sabbeheva piyehi manāpehi nānābhāvo vinābhāvo aññathābhāvo’. Taṃ kutettha, āvuso, labbhā. ‘Yaṃ taṃ jātaṃ bhūtaṃ saṅkhataṃ palokadhammaṃ, taṃ tathāgatassāpi sarīraṃ mā palujjī’ti, netaṃ ṭhānaṃ vijjatī’’ti.</p>
232. Now at that time, one Subhadda, who had renounced only in his old age, was seated in the assembly.

Then Subhadda, who had gone forth when old, said to those monks: “Enough, friends! Do not grieve, do not lament! We are well rid of that great ascetic (mahāsamaṇa). We were always bothered by his saying: “It is fitting for you to do this, it is not fitting for you to do that!” But now we will be able to do as we like and we won’t do what we don’t like."

Then the Venerable Mahākāśyapa addressed the monks, saying: “Enough friends! Do not grieve, do not lament! For has not the Blessed One declared that with all that is dear and beloved there must be change (nānābhāva), separation (vinābhāva), and severance (aññathābhāva)? So why all this, friends? Whatever is born (jātaṃ), become (bhūtaṃ), compounded (saṅkhataṃ) is subject to decay (palokadhammaṃ), it cannot be that even the body (śarīraṃ) of the *Tathāgata* does not decay.’; There can be no such state of things."
<p n="232" rend="bodytext"><hi rend="paranum">232</hi><hi rend="dot">.</hi><hi rend="bold">Subhaddo nāma vuḍḍhapabbajito</hi>ti ‘‘subhaddo’’ti tassa nāmaṃ. Vuḍḍhakāle pana pabbajitattā ‘‘vuḍḍhapabbajito’’ti vuccati. Kasmā pana so evamāha? Bhagavati āghātena. Ayaṃ kireso khandhake āgate ātumāvatthusmiṃ nahāpitapubbako vuḍḍhapabbajito bhagavati kusinārato nikkhamitvā aḍḍhateḷasehi bhikkhusatehi saddhiṃ ātumaṃ āgacchante bhagavā āgacchatīti sutvā – ‘‘āgatakāle yāgupānaṃ karissāmī’’ti sāmaṇerabhūmiyaṃ ṭhite dve putte etadavoca – ‘‘bhagavā kira, tātā, ātumaṃ āgacchati mahatā bhikkhusaṅghena saddhiṃ aḍḍhateḷasehi bhikkhusatehi; gacchatha tumhe, tātā, khurabhaṇḍaṃ ādāya nāḷiyāvāpakena anugharakaṃ anugharakaṃ āhiṇḍatha loṇampi telampi taṇḍulampi khādanīyampi <pb ed="P" n="2.0600"/> saṃharatha <pb ed="M" n="2.0192"/> bhagavato āgatassa yāgupānaṃ karissāmā’’ti (mahāva. 303). Te tathā akaṃsu.</p> <p rend="bodytext">Manussā <pb ed="V" n="2.0172"/> te dārake mañjuke paṭibhāneyyake disvā kāretukāmāpi akāretukāmāpi kārentiyeva. Katakāle – ‘‘kiṃ gaṇhissatha tātā’’ti pucchanti. Te vadanti – ‘‘na amhākaṃ aññena kenaci attho, pitā pana no bhagavato, āgatakāle yāgudānaṃ dātukāmo’’ti. Taṃ sutvā manussā aparigaṇetvāva yaṃ te sakkonti āharituṃ, sabbaṃ denti. Yampi na sakkonti, manussehi pesenti. Atha bhagavati ātumaṃ āgantvā bhusāgāraṃ paviṭṭhe subhaddo sāyanhasamayaṃ gāmadvāraṃ gantvā manusse āmantesi – ‘‘upāsakā, nāhaṃ tumhākaṃ santikā aññaṃ kiñci paccāsīsāmi, mayhaṃ dārakehi ābhatāni taṇḍulādīniyeva saṅghassa pahonti. Yaṃ hatthakammaṃ, taṃ me dethā’’ti. ‘‘Idañcidañca gaṇhathā’’ti sabbūpakaraṇāni gāhetvā vihāre uddhanāni kāretvā ekaṃ kāḷakaṃ kāsāvaṃ nivāsetvā tādisameva pārupitvā – ‘‘idaṃ karotha, idaṃ karothā’’ti sabbarattiṃ vicārento satasahassaṃ vissajjetvā bhojjayāguñca madhugoḷakañca paṭiyādāpesi. Bhojjayāgu nāma bhuñjitvā pātabbayāgu, tattha sappimadhuphāṇitamacchamaṃsapupphaphalarasādi yaṃ kiñci khādanīyaṃ nāma sabbaṃ pakkhipati kīḷitukāmānaṃ sīsamakkhanayoggā hoti sugandhagandhā.</p> <pb ed="V" n="2.0172"/> <p rend="bodytext">Atha bhagavā kālasseva sarīrapaṭijagganaṃ katvā bhikkhusaṅghaparivuto piṇḍāya carituṃ ātumanagarābhimukho pāyāsi. Manussā tassa ārocesuṃ – ‘‘bhagavā piṇḍāya gāmaṃ pavisati, tayā kassa yāgu paṭiyāditā’’ti. So yathānivatthapāruteheva tehi kāḷakakāsāvehi ekena hatthena dabbiñca kaṭacchuñca gahetvā brahmā viya dakkhiṇajāṇumaṇḍalaṃ bhūmiyaṃ patiṭṭhapetvā vanditvā – ‘‘paṭiggaṇhātu me, bhante, bhagavā yāgu’’nti āha.</p> <p rend="bodytext">Tato ‘‘jānantāpi tathāgatā pucchantī’’ti khandhake āgatanayena bhagavā pucchitvā ca sutvā ca taṃ vuḍḍhapabbajitaṃ vigarahitvā tasmiṃ vatthusmiṃ akappiyasamādānasikkhāpadañca, khurabhaṇḍapariharaṇasikkhāpadañcāti dve sikkhāpadāni <pb ed="P" n="2.0601"/> paññapetvā – ‘‘bhikkhave, anekakappakoṭiyo bhojanaṃ pariyesanteheva <pb ed="M" n="2.0193"/> vītināmitā, idaṃ pana tumhākaṃ akappiyaṃ adhammena uppannaṃ bhojanaṃ, imaṃ paribhuttānaṃ anekāni attabhāvasahassāni apāyesveva nibbattissanti, apetha mā gaṇhathā’’ti bhikkhācārābhimukho agamāsi. Ekabhikkhunāpi na kiñci gahitaṃ.</p> <pb ed="P" n="2.0601"/> <pb ed="M" n="2.0193"/> <p rend="bodytext">Subhaddo anattamano hutvā ayaṃ ‘‘sabbaṃ jānāmī’’ti āhiṇḍati. Sace na gahitukāmo, pesetvā ārocetabbaṃ. Ayaṃ pakkāhāro nāma sabbaciraṃ tiṭṭhanto sattāhamattaṃ tiṭṭheyya. Idañhi mama yāvajīvaṃ pariyattaṃ assa. Sabbaṃ tena nāsitaṃ, ahitakāmo ayaṃ mayhanti <pb ed="V" n="2.0173"/> bhagavati āghātaṃ bandhitvā dasabale dharante kiñci vattuṃ nāsakkhi. Evaṃ kirassa ahosi – ‘‘ayaṃ uccā kulā pabbajito mahāpuriso, sace kiñci vakkhāmi, maṃyeva santajjessatī’’ti. Svāyaṃ ajja ‘‘parinibbuto bhagavā’’ti sutvā laddhassāso viya haṭṭhatuṭṭho evamāha.</p> <pb ed="V" n="2.0173"/> <p rend="bodytext">Thero taṃ sutvā hadaye pahāradānaṃ viya matthake patitasukkhāsani viya maññi, dhammasaṃvego cassa uppajji – ‘‘sattāhamattaparinibbuto bhagavā, ajjāpissa suvaṇṇavaṇṇaṃ sarīraṃ dharatiyeva, dukkhena bhagavatā ārādhitasāsane nāma evaṃ lahu mahantaṃ pāpakasaṭaṃ kaṇṭako uppanno, alaṃ kho panesa pāpo vaḍḍhamāno aññepi evarūpe sahāye labhitvā sakkā sāsanaṃ osakkāpetu’’nti. Tato thero cintesi –</p> <p rend="bodytext">‘‘Sace kho panāhaṃ imaṃ mahallakaṃ idheva pilotikaṃ nivāsāpetvā chārikāya okirāpetvā nīharāpessāmi, manussā ‘samaṇassa gotamassa sarīre dharamāneyeva sāvakā vivadantī’ti amhākaṃ dosaṃ dassessanti adhivāsemi tāva.</p> <p rend="bodytext">Bhagavatā hi desito dhammo asaṅgahitapuppharāsisadiso. Tattha yathā vātena pahaṭapupphāni yato vā tato vā gacchanti, evameva evarūpānaṃ pāpapuggalānaṃ vasena gacchante gacchante kāle vinaye ekaṃ dve sikkhāpadāni nassissanti, sutte eko dve pañhāvārā nassissanti, abhidhamme ekaṃ dve bhūmantarāni nassissanti, evaṃ anukkamena mūle naṭṭhe pisācasadisā bhavissāma; tasmā dhammavinayasaṅgahaṃ karissāma. Evañhi sati daḷhaṃ <pb ed="M" n="2.0194"/> suttena saṅgahitāni pupphāni viya ayaṃ dhammavinayo niccalo bhavissati.</p> <pb ed="M" n="2.0194"/> <p rend="bodytext">Etadatthañhi bhagavā <pb ed="P" n="2.0602"/> mayhaṃ tīṇi gāvutāni paccuggamanaṃ akāsi, tīhi ovādehi upasampadaṃ adāsi, kāyato apanetvā kāye cīvaraparivattanaṃ akāsi, ākāse pāṇiṃ cāletvā candūpamaṃ paṭipadaṃ kathento maṃ kāyasakkhiṃ katvā kathesi, tikkhattuṃ sakalasāsanadāyajjaṃ paṭicchāpesi. Mādise bhikkhumhi tiṭṭhamāne ayaṃ pāpo sāsane vuḍḍhiṃ mā alattha. Yāva adhammo na dippati, dhammo na paṭibāhiyati. Avinayo na dippati vinayo na paṭibāhiyati. Adhammavādino na balavanto honti, dhammavādino na dubbalā honti; avinayavādino na balavanto honti, vinayavādino na dubbalā honti. Tāva dhammañca vinayañca saṅgāyissāmi. Tato bhikkhū attano attano pahonakaṃ gahetvā kappiyākappiyaṃ <pb ed="V" n="2.0174"/> kathessanti. Athāyaṃ pāpo sayameva niggahaṃ pāpuṇissati, puna sīsaṃ ukkhipituṃ na sakkhissati, sāsanaṃ iddhañceva phītañca bhavissatī’’ti.</p> <pb ed="P" n="2.0602"/> <pb ed="V" n="2.0174"/> <p rend="bodytext">So evaṃ nāma mayhaṃ cittaṃ uppannanti kassaci anārocetvā bhikkhusaṅghaṃ samassāsesi. Tena vuttaṃ – ‘‘atha kho āyasmā mahākassapo…pe… netaṃ ṭhānaṃ vijjatī’’ti.</p>
232 Subhadda by name, an old renunciate, thus: “Subhadda” is his name.

In old age, however, because of having renounced, he is called “old renunciate.”

But why did he say that? Out of contempt for the Blessed One.

It seems that this same Subhadda, when the Khandhaka had come, having gone forth from Kusināra to Ātumā, an old renunciate who formerly was a barber in Ātumā, when the Blessed One was coming to Ātumā together with thirteen hundred monks, having heard, “The Blessed One is coming,” said this to his two sons who were abiding in the state of a novice: “The Blessed One, fathers, is coming to Ātumā together with a great Saṃgha of monks, thirteen hundred monks; go, fathers, taking a razor and a bag with a barber’s implement, wander from house to house collecting salt, oil, rice, and food.” Having gathered it together, “We will prepare rice-gruel and a drink for the Blessed One who has come” (Mahāva.
303).

They did just that.

People, having seen those boys who were charming and clever, being desirous of having [their hair] cut, even when not desiring to have it cut, would have it cut.

At the time of the cutting, they would ask, “What will you take, fathers?”

They would say, “We have no need for anything else, but our father wishes to give rice-gruel as a gift to the Blessed One when he has come.”

Having heard that, people, without reckoning it, whatever they were able to bring, they would give everything.

Whatever they were not able to [bring themselves], they would send by means of people.

Then, when the Blessed One, having come to Ātumā, had entered the storehouse, Subhadda, at the time of the evening, going to the village gate, addressed the people: “Lay followers, I do not expect anything else from your presence, but only the rice and so forth that has been brought by my boys is sufficient for the Saṃgha.

Whatever is manual labor, give that to me.”

“Take this and take that,” having caused all the equipment to be taken, having had the rice removed in the monastery, having dressed in a single blackish-brown robe and having wrapped another just like it, thinking, “Do this, do that,” the whole night, having spent a hundred thousand, he had both edible rice-gruel and honey-cakes prepared.

Edible rice-gruel is called rice-gruel to be drunk after having eaten, in which all edible things such as ghee, honey, molasses, fish, meat, flowers, fruit juice, and so forth are put, and it is suitable for anointing the head of those who desire to play, [and] it is fragrant.

Then the Blessed One, early in the morning, having taken care of his body, surrounded by the Saṃgha of monks, set out towards the city of Ātumā for alms.

People announced to him, “The Blessed One is entering the village for alms; by whom has rice-gruel been prepared?”

He, just as if having dressed in those blackish-brown robes which had already been worn, taking both a ladle and a spoon in one hand, like Brahmā, establishing his right knee on the ground, having bowed down, said, “May the Blessed One accept the rice-gruel from me, O Bhante!”

Then, “Even though knowing, the Tathāgatas ask,” according to the manner come [down] in the Khandhaka, the Blessed One, both having asked and having heard, censuring that old renunciate, in that matter, having made known two precepts: the precept of unallowable acceptance and the precept of not using a razor and bag, “Monks, even though seeking food for countless aeons, it has been rejected, but this food of yours is unallowable, arisen through unrighteousness; for those who have eaten this, many thousands of existences will arise only in the apāyas, go away, do not take [it]!” he went towards the alms round.

Nothing was taken by even one monk.

Subhadda, having become displeased, [thought], “This one wanders about [saying], ‘I know everything.’”

If [one] does not desire to take [it], [one] should send [it back] and announce [it].

This cooked food, indeed, while abiding for a very long time, may abide for only seven days.

This, indeed, would be enough for my whole life.

Everything was destroyed by him; this one is desirous of harm to me,” having bound contempt towards the Blessed One, while the Ten-Powered One was enduring, he was not able to say anything.

Thus it seemed to him: “This one has gone forth from a high family, a great man; if I say anything, he himself will rebuke me.”

Today, having heard, “The Blessed One has attained nirvāṇa,” delighted and pleased, he said thus.

The elder, having heard that, thought, “It is like giving a blow to [my] heart, like a thunderbolt fallen on [my] head,” and agitation about the Dhamma arose in him: “The Blessed One has attained nirvāṇa only seven days [ago], even today his body of golden color endures, in a sāsana brought about with difficulty by the Blessed One, a thorn, a great heap of evil, has arisen so quickly, it is enough, indeed, that this evil one, while growing, having obtained other companions of this sort, is able to cause the sāsana to decline.”

Then the elder thought:

“If, indeed, I, having had this old man settled right here in a dilapidated [dwelling], having had ashes scattered [on him], were to cause [him] to be removed, people will show blame to us, ‘Even while the body of the samaṇa Gotama endures, the disciples are quarreling,’ therefore I will endure for a while.”
[Thus,] the Dharma is taught by the Blessed One, it is like a heap of flowers not held together.

Just as flowers scattered by the wind go here and there, in the same way, because of such evil individuals, as time goes on, one or two precepts (*śikṣāpada*) will be lost from the monastic discipline (*vinaya*), one or two question series (*pañhāvāra*) will be lost from the sūtras, one or two levels of existence (*bhūmantara*) will be lost from the *Abhidhamma*. Thus, gradually, when the root is destroyed, we will become like demons. Therefore, let us make a compilation of the Dharma and the Discipline (*dharma-vinaya-saṅgaha*).

Thus, when that is the case, this *dharma-vinaya*, like flowers held together firmly by a thread (*sūtra*), will be unshakeable.

The Blessed One did these things for me: He came out three *gāvutas* to meet me, he gave me ordination (*upasampada*) with three instructions (*ovāda*), having removed [the robe] from his own body, he made a robe exchange with my body, having moved his hand in the sky, while relating the simile of the moon, having made me a bodily witness (*kāyasakkhi*), he spoke; three times he had me accept the entire inheritance of the teaching (*sakalasāsanadāyajja*).

While a monk like me is standing, may this evil not attain growth in the teaching (*śāsana*).

As long as what is not *dharma* does not shine forth, *dharma* is not rejected.

What is not discipline (*avinaya*) does not shine forth, discipline (*vinaya*) is not rejected.

Those who speak what is not *dharma* are not strong, those who speak *dharma* are not weak; those who speak what is not discipline (*avinaya*) are not strong, those who speak discipline (*vinaya*) are not weak.

So long will I recite the Dharma and the Discipline (*dhammañca vinayañca saṅgāyissāmi*).

Then the monks, having taken what was enough for themselves, will speak of what is allowable (*kappiya*) and what is not allowable (*akappiya*).

Then this evil one will himself attain restraint (*niggaha*), he will not be able to lift his head again, and the teaching (*śāsana*) will be prosperous (*iddha*) and thriving (*phīta*)".

So, without announcing to anyone that such a thought had arisen in my mind, he encouraged the monastic community (*bhikkhusaṅgha*).

Therefore it was said, "Then the venerable Mahākassapa…pe… this is not a valid reason (*ṭhānaṃ vijjatī*)".
233
<p n="233" rend="bodytext"><hi rend="paranum">233</hi><hi rend="dot">.</hi> Tena kho pana samayena cattāro mallapāmokkhā sīsaṃnhātā ahatāni vatthāni nivatthā – ‘‘mayaṃ bhagavato citakaṃ āḷimpessāmā’’ti na sakkonti āḷimpetuṃ. Atha kho kosinārakā mallā āyasmantaṃ anuruddhaṃ etadavocuṃ – ‘‘ko nu kho, bhante anuruddha, hetu ko paccayo, yenime cattāro mallapāmokkhā sīsaṃnhātā ahatāni vatthāni nivatthā – ‘mayaṃ bhagavato citakaṃ āḷimpessāmā’ti na sakkonti āḷimpetu’’nti? ‘‘Aññathā kho, vāseṭṭhā, devatānaṃ adhippāyo’’ti. ‘‘Kathaṃ pana, bhante, devatānaṃ adhippāyo’’ti? ‘‘Devatānaṃ kho, vāseṭṭhā, adhippāyo – ‘ayaṃ āyasmā mahākassapo pāvāya kusināraṃ addhānamaggappaṭippanno mahatā bhikkhusaṅghena saddhiṃ pañcamattehi bhikkhusatehi. Na tāva bhagavato citako pajjalissati, yāvāyasmā mahākassapo bhagavato pāde sirasā na vandissatī’’’ti. ‘‘Yathā, bhante, devatānaṃ adhippāyo, tathā hotū’’ti.</p>
At that time, four leading Mallas, having bathed their heads and wearing new clothes, tried to ignite the Blessed One's pyre, thinking, "We will ignite the Blessed One's pyre," but they were unable to ignite it.

Then the Mallas of Kusinārā said to the Venerable Anuruddha: "What is the reason, Venerable Anuruddha, what is the cause that these four leading Mallas, having bathed their heads and wearing new clothes, try to ignite the Blessed One's pyre, thinking, 'We will ignite the Blessed One's pyre,' but are unable to ignite it?"
